# Separator
group: primitives / Display
Thin horizontal or vertical divider line, solid, dashed or dotted, optionally with a label ("or", "Today") on the line.

Use `Separator` to split groups of content or toolbar items. It is decorative by default (role="none"); set `:decorative="false"` when the divider carries meaning for assistive tech. Vertical separators need a parent with a height (e.g. `flex items-center` with `h-5` on the separator).

**Line style** (`variant`): `solid` (default, filled `bg-border`), `dashed` and `dotted` (1px border; use for "tear-off", optional or secondary regions, receipts). Unknown values fall back to solid.

**Thickness** (`size`): `thin` (1px, default), `md` (2px) and `thick` (3px) for section breaks that need more weight. **Tone**: `default` (border colour), `muted` (half strength, for dense lists), `strong` (the form-control border colour, for dividers that must stay visible on cards) and `primary` (accent). On a labelled separator the tone also sets the text colour (`strong` is foreground, `primary` is the accent, the others stay muted). Unknown values fall back to `thin` and `default`. Thicker and toned filled lines add a border in forced-colors mode.

**Labelled** separators: pass `label="or"` or put any content in the default slot to show text on the line. `align` places it: `center` (line on both sides, default; sign-in forms, "or"), `start` (label first, line after; section headings) or `end` (line first, label last). Unknown `align` values fall back to center. Labelled separators work vertically too (the label sits between two vertical lines). Without `label`/slot the markup is a single element as before. With `asChild` the slot is the element to render and `label` is ignored.

import { Separator } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - Direction of the line. Invalid values fall back to horizontal.
- decorative: boolean = true - true = role="none"; false = role="separator" (+ aria-orientation when vertical). A non-decorative separator with `label` gets aria-label=label (role separator hides its children).
- variant: 'solid' | 'dashed' | 'dotted' = 'solid' - Line style. Unknown values fall back to solid.
- size: 'thin' | 'md' | 'thick' = 'thin' - Line thickness: 1px, 2px or 3px. Applies to plain and labelled separators, in both orientations. Unknown values fall back to thin.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'strong' | 'primary' = 'default' - Colour of the line (and of the label text when `strong` or `primary`). default = border token, muted = half strength, strong = form-control border token, primary = accent. Unknown values fall back to default.
- label: string - Text shown on the line. Empty string = plain separator. Ignored with `asChild`; the default slot takes precedence.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'center' - Label position when a label/slot is present. start = label then line; end = line then label; center = line, label, line. Unknown values fall back to center.
- as: string | Component - Element to render (reka-ui default is a div).
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Label content (replaces `label`, e.g. an icon plus text). With `asChild` it is the element rendered instead of the wrapper.

Rules:
- Give vertical separators an explicit height (`h-5`) or a stretching flex parent.
- Keep `decorative` true unless the divider conveys structure.
- Use `label="or"` for dividers between alternatives instead of hand-rolled flex + two hr.
- Use `variant="dashed"|"dotted"` for style; do not set border classes manually.
- Use `size="md"|"thick"` for section breaks and `tone="muted"` inside dense lists; do not set `h-*` or `bg-*` classes by hand.
- Do not combine `label` with `asChild`.

Accessibility:
- Decorative by default (role="none") so screen readers skip the line; label text stays readable.
- Use `decorative=false` when the line separates regions of a toolbar or menu: it is then a real `separator` that assistive tech can announce.
- `size` and `tone` only change thickness and colour. A thicker or toned filled line adds a border in forced-colors mode, where background colours are replaced, so it stays visible. Tones use the existing border, input and primary tokens; a decorative divider needs no text contrast, a `strong` one meets 3:1 against the page and card surfaces.
- The line is a 1px `border` colour fill. Forced-colors mode replaces background tokens, so a filled line also paints `forced-colors:bg-[CanvasText]` (a system colour keeps its value) and the default hairline, labelled lines included, stays visible. Dashed and dotted variants use borders, so they remain visible too.
- With `decorative=false` it exposes role="separator"; vertical ones also set aria-orientation. Because separator children are presentational, `label` is also set as aria-label (slot content is not; pass aria-label yourself).

Example: Horizontal
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-3">
  <p class="text-sm font-medium">Perfect Design</p>
  <Separator />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">A Vue 3 design system.</p>
</div>
```

Example: Vertical in a toolbar
```vue
<div class="flex h-5 items-center gap-3 text-sm">
  <span>Docs</span>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" />
  <span>Source</span>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" :decorative="false" />
  <span>Releases</span>
</div>
```

Example: Dashed and dotted
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4">
  <Separator />
  <Separator variant="dashed" />
  <Separator variant="dotted" />
  <div class="flex h-6 items-center gap-4 text-sm">
    <span>Left</span>
    <Separator variant="dashed" orientation="vertical" />
    <span>Right</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: With a label (centred)
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-3">
  <Button variant="outline" class="w-full">First sample action</Button>
  <Separator label="or" />
  <Button class="w-full">Second sample action</Button>
</div>
```

Example: Label alignment
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4">
  <Separator label="Start" align="start" />
  <Separator label="Center" align="center" />
  <Separator label="End" align="end" />
</div>
```

Example: Labelled dashed and slot content
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4">
  <Separator label="Optional" variant="dashed" align="start" />
  <Separator variant="dotted"><span class="text-xs">Today</span></Separator>
</div>
```

Example: Thickness
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4">
  <Separator size="thin" />
  <Separator size="md" />
  <Separator size="thick" />
  <Separator size="md" variant="dashed" />
  <Separator size="thick" variant="dotted" />
  <div class="flex h-6 items-center gap-4 text-sm">
    <span>Thin</span>
    <Separator orientation="vertical" size="thin" />
    <span>Medium</span>
    <Separator orientation="vertical" size="md" />
    <span>Thick</span>
    <Separator orientation="vertical" size="thick" />
    <span>End</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4">
  <Separator tone="default" size="md" />
  <Separator tone="muted" size="md" />
  <Separator tone="strong" size="md" />
  <Separator tone="primary" size="md" />
  <Separator tone="strong" label="Strong" />
  <Separator tone="primary" label="Primary" align="start" variant="dashed" />
</div>
```

Example: Vertical with a label
```vue
<div class="flex h-32 items-center gap-6 text-sm">
  <span>Before</span>
  <Separator label="or" orientation="vertical" />
  <span>After</span>
</div>
```

# Skeleton
group: primitives / Display
Placeholder block shown while content loads: text, circle, avatar, pill, rounded, rect and paragraph shapes with a pulse or no animation.

Use `Skeleton` to reserve layout space while data loads. Size it with classes (`h-4 w-40`, `size-12`) and compose several to mimic the final layout. Unknown `shape` / `animation` values fall back to `rect` / `pulse`. Do not use it for in-progress actions (use `Spinner`).

**Shapes**: `text` (one text line, h-4), `circle` and `avatar` (round size-10; `avatar` never shrinks in flex rows), `rect` (default block), `rounded` (block with large radius for cards and images), `pill` (h-6 w-24 for badges, chips and buttons) and `lines` (a paragraph of `lines` text lines, the last one shorter).

**Presets**: `SkeletonText` (paragraph), `SkeletonAvatar` (sm to xl, circle or square), `SkeletonCard` (media + title + lines) and `SkeletonTable` (rows x columns) are ready-made compositions of `Skeleton`, so apps do not hand-build them. They are compound parts rather than a `preset` prop because each has its own props (`rows`, `columns`, `size`) that would not apply to the other shapes. Each part is `aria-hidden`; announce the loading state once from the caller (a region with `aria-busy="true"`, or `LoadingState`).

**Animation**: `pulse` (default), `shimmer` (deprecated alias: it pulses, because a moving highlight needs a gradient) or `none` (static placeholder, e.g. dense tables or when many skeletons would be noisy). The pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion. The older boolean `shimmer` still works and is ignored when `animation` is set.

import { Skeleton, SkeletonText, SkeletonAvatar, SkeletonCard, SkeletonTable } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- shape: 'text' | 'circle' | 'rect' | 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'avatar' | 'lines' = 'rect' - text = h-4 full-width line, circle/avatar = size-10 round, rect = h-20 block, rounded = h-20 block with rounded-xl, pill = h-6 w-24 fully rounded, lines = paragraph wrapper. Unknown values fall back to rect.
- animation: 'none' | 'pulse' | 'shimmer' = 'pulse' - Loading animation. Unknown values fall back to pulse (or shimmer when `shimmer` is set).
- shimmer: boolean = false - Shortcut for animation="shimmer". Ignored when `animation` is set.
- lines: number = 3 - Line count for shape="lines" (floored, 1..20; invalid values give 3). The last line is w-3/4 when there are 2 or more.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render (the wrapper, for shape="lines"; its lines are divs).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; use it to set the size. For shape="lines" it applies to the wrapper (e.g. max-w-sm, gap-3).

Parts:
- SkeletonText - A paragraph placeholder: `lines` text lines, the last one shorter. Same output as `Skeleton shape="lines"` with the part slot name.
    - lines: number = 3 - Line count (floored, 1..20; invalid values give 3).
    - animation: 'none' | 'pulse' | 'shimmer' = 'pulse' - Same as Skeleton.
    - as: string | Component = 'div' - Wrapper element.
- SkeletonAvatar - A round or square avatar placeholder that never shrinks in a flex row.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - 32px, 40px, 48px, 64px. Unknown values fall back to md.
    - shape: 'circle' | 'square' = 'circle' - square is rounded-md, for logos and app icons.
    - animation: 'none' | 'pulse' | 'shimmer' = 'pulse' - Same as Skeleton.
- SkeletonCard - A card placeholder: optional media block, a title line and body lines, inside a bordered card.
    - media: boolean = true - Show the media block above the text.
    - lines: number = 3 - Body lines (0..20); 0 or invalid values drop the body.
    - animation: 'none' | 'pulse' | 'shimmer' = 'pulse' - Same as Skeleton.
- SkeletonTable - A table placeholder: an optional header row and `rows` rows of `columns` cells on a grid.
    - rows: number = 5 - Body rows (floored, 1..50; invalid values give 5).
    - columns: number = 4 - Columns (floored, 1..12; invalid values give 4).
    - header: boolean = true - Render a header row.
    - animation: 'none' | 'pulse' | 'shimmer' = 'pulse' - Same as Skeleton.

Rules:
- Mirror the final layout dimensions to avoid layout shift.
- Put aria-busy on the loading region; the skeleton itself is aria-hidden.
- Do not hard-code colours; the component uses `bg-muted`.
- Use shape="lines" for paragraphs instead of stacking text skeletons; set class on the wrapper.
- Use SkeletonText, SkeletonAvatar, SkeletonCard and SkeletonTable for common shapes instead of hand-building them.
- Use animation="none" for static placeholders; do not use the deprecated `shimmer` flag.

Accessibility:
- aria-hidden="true": the placeholder is invisible to assistive tech, so many skeletons never produce noise. Announce the loading state once on the container with `aria-busy="true"` or a single visually hidden `role="status"` message, and swap both when the data arrives.
- The pulse is disabled with `motion-reduce:animate-none`; the muted fill stays visible, so the placeholder is still perceivable without motion.
- Skeletons are flat `bg-muted` blocks with no border: in forced-colors mode add a `border` class on large placeholders if they must stay visible.
- Size them with `w-full`, `max-w-*` or percentage widths so they reflow at 320px.

Example: Card placeholder
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Skeleton shape="circle" class="size-12" />
  <div class="flex-1 space-y-2">
    <Skeleton shape="text" class="w-1/2" />
    <Skeleton shape="text" class="w-3/4" />
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: Shapes
```vue
<div class="flex max-w-md flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <Skeleton shape="text" class="w-32" />
  <Skeleton shape="circle" />
  <Skeleton shape="avatar" />
  <Skeleton shape="rect" class="h-10 w-24" />
  <Skeleton shape="rounded" class="h-10 w-24" />
  <Skeleton shape="pill" />
</div>
```

Example: Paragraph (lines)
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4">
  <Skeleton shape="lines" />
  <Skeleton shape="lines" :lines="5" />
</div>
```

Example: Animations
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-2">
  <Skeleton animation="pulse" shape="text" />
    <Skeleton animation="none" shape="text" />
</div>
```

Example: Loading card
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-3" aria-busy="true">
  <Skeleton shape="rounded" class="h-40" />
  <div class="flex items-center gap-3">
    <Skeleton shape="avatar" />
    <Skeleton shape="text" class="w-1/3" />
    <Skeleton shape="pill" class="ms-auto" />
  </div>
  <Skeleton shape="lines" :lines="3" />
</div>
```

Example: SkeletonText
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm space-y-4" aria-busy="true">
  <SkeletonText />
  <SkeletonText :lines="5" />
  <SkeletonText :lines="2" animation="none" />

```

Example: SkeletonAvatar

```vue
  <SkeletonAvatar size="sm" />
  <SkeletonAvatar />
  <SkeletonAvatar size="lg" />
  <SkeletonAvatar size="xl" shape="square" />

```

```vue
  <SkeletonTable :rows="3" :columns="3" />
  <SkeletonTable :rows="2" :columns="5" :header="false" animation="none" />
```

# Spinner
group: primitives / Display
Small rotating SVG that shows work in progress, with an accessible label or as a purely visual mark.

Use `Spinner` for an indeterminate wait of unknown length inside a control or next to a label. By default it is a `progressbar` named by `label`. Set `decorative` when the surrounding element already announces the busy state (a loading button, a status region), so the spinner is hidden from assistive tech.

Use `ProgressRing` when the progress is known. Use `LoadingState` for a whole region that is loading. `Button` with `loading` already draws a decorative spinner.

import { Spinner } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- label: string = 'Loading' - Accessible name of the spinner. Ignored when `decorative`.
- decorative: boolean = false - Hide the spinner from assistive tech (`aria-hidden`, no role). Use it when a parent already announces the busy state.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Diameter: 12, 16, 20, 24 or 32px. Unknown values fall back to md.
- variant: 'ring' | 'dots' | 'bars' | 'pulse' | 'orbit' = 'ring' - Animation shape. `ring` is a rotating arc, `dots` three dots fading in turn, `bars` an equaliser of four bars, `pulse` a solid dot with an expanding ring, `orbit` two arcs turning in opposite directions. Unknown values fall back to `ring`. Non-default values add `data-variant`. The names are exported as `SPINNER_VARIANTS`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes. The spinner uses `currentColor`.

Rules:
- Choose `variant` for the look only (`ring`, `dots`, `bars`, `pulse`, `orbit`); semantics and sizes do not change.
- Pass `decorative` when the spinner sits inside a button or a status region that already announces the wait.
- Give a specific `label` when the spinner stands alone.
- Use `ProgressRing` or `Progress` when the amount done is known.

Accessibility:
- Not decorative: `role="progressbar"` with `aria-label` from `label`. Give it a label that says what is loading, not just "Loading".
- Decorative: `aria-hidden="true"` and no role. The parent must announce the busy state, for example with `role="status"` text.
- Every variant keeps the same role, label and `decorative` behaviour.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` no variant moves: the ring, dots, bars and orbit fade gently, and `pulse` shows a static dot with a faint ring.

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-4 text-primary">
  <Spinner size="xs" />
  <Spinner size="sm" />
  <Spinner size="md" />
  <Spinner size="lg" />
  <Spinner size="xl" />
</div>
```

Example: Next to a label
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 text-sm">
  <span class="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><Spinner label="Saving changes" class="text-primary" /></span>
  <span role="status" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 text-muted-foreground"><Spinner decorative size="sm" /> Syncing the sample catalogue</span>
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-6 text-primary">
  <Spinner variant="ring" size="lg" label="Loading ring" />
  <Spinner variant="dots" size="lg" label="Loading dots" />
  <Spinner variant="bars" size="lg" label="Loading bars" />
  <Spinner variant="pulse" size="lg" label="Loading pulse" />
  <Spinner variant="orbit" size="lg" label="Loading orbit" />
</div>
```

Example: Inline next to text
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
  <p role="status" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><Spinner variant="dots" decorative size="sm" /> Fetching the sample report</p>
  <p role="status" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><Spinner variant="bars" decorative size="sm" /> Transcribing the sample recording</p>
</div>
```

# AspectRatio
group: primitives / Layout helpers
Keeps its content at a fixed width-to-height ratio (images, video, maps, placeholders).

Use `AspectRatio` to reserve space for media before it loads and to crop it consistently. The outer wrapper is `width: 100%` and takes its height from `ratio`; your content fills it absolutely. Size it by placing it in a width-constrained container. `class` and attributes go on the inner content element, so `overflow-hidden rounded-lg` clips the media. Where the native `aspect-ratio` CSS fits (a plain box), a Tailwind `aspect-video` class is simpler.

**Rounded** (`rounded`): `none` (default), `md`, `lg` or `full`. A non-`none` value also sets `overflow-hidden`, so media is clipped to the corners; `full` with `:ratio="1"` is a circle. **Variant** (`variant`): `plain` (default), `bordered` (1px border) and `muted` (muted background with muted text, for placeholders and empty media; it keeps a border in forced-colors mode, where backgrounds are replaced). **Fit** (`fit`): `none` (default, nothing is applied), `cover` (crop to fill), `contain` (letterbox) and `fill` (stretch) for a direct `img` or `video` child. Unknown values fall back to the defaults. `aspectRatioVariants` returns the same classes for a plain element.

import { AspectRatio } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- ratio: number = 16 / 9 - Width divided by height (`1`, `4 / 3`, `16 / 9`). Non-finite or <= 0 falls back to 16 / 9.
- rounded: 'none' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' = 'none' - Corner radius of the content element; any value other than none also clips the content (overflow-hidden). Unknown values fall back to none.
- variant: 'plain' | 'bordered' | 'muted' = 'plain' - Surface: plain adds nothing, bordered adds a 1px border, muted adds a muted background (with a forced-colors border). Unknown values fall back to plain.
- fit: 'none' | 'cover' | 'contain' | 'fill' = 'none' - Sizing of a direct img or video child: cover crops, contain letterboxes, fill stretches. none leaves the child alone. Unknown values fall back to none.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Content element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged onto the content element (not the sizing wrapper).

Slots:
- default - Content that fills the ratio box.

Rules:
- Constrain the width with a parent (`w-full max-w-80`, grid column); AspectRatio itself is 100% wide.
- Pass `:ratio="16 / 9"` as a number expression, not a string.
- Use `rounded` (it also clips) and `fit="cover"` instead of `overflow-hidden rounded-* ` plus `object-cover` classes.
- Use `variant="muted"` for placeholders and `variant="bordered"` for media on a page background; keep `plain` when a card already draws the border.

Accessibility:
- Purely presentational: give embedded images alt text and give media containers a role/aria-label when they convey content.
- `rounded`, `variant` and `fit` change the look only: they add no role or name, so an informative image keeps its own `alt`. The `muted` surface uses the muted foreground on the muted background (4.5:1 in every theme) and a border in forced-colors mode. `fit` sets sizing on direct `img` and `video` children only.
- It reserves space with the intrinsic ratio, so there is no layout shift while media loads, and it scales with its container at any zoom level or width.

Example: Default 16:9
```vue
<div class="w-full max-w-80">
  <AspectRatio class="flex items-center justify-center overflow-hidden rounded-lg bg-muted text-sm text-muted-foreground">16 / 9</AspectRatio>
</div>
```

Example: Square and 4:3 with overlay
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
  <div class="w-32">
    <AspectRatio :ratio="1" class="flex items-center justify-center rounded-md bg-accent text-accent-foreground">1 / 1</AspectRatio>
  </div>
  <div class="w-48">
    <AspectRatio :ratio="4 / 3" class="relative overflow-hidden rounded-md bg-muted">
      <Badge class="absolute start-2 top-2">4 / 3</Badge>
    </AspectRatio>
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: Rounded
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
  <div class="w-28"><AspectRatio :ratio="1" rounded="none" variant="muted" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">none</AspectRatio></div>
  <div class="w-28"><AspectRatio :ratio="1" rounded="md" variant="muted" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">md</AspectRatio></div>
  <div class="w-28"><AspectRatio :ratio="1" rounded="lg" variant="muted" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">lg</AspectRatio></div>
  <div class="w-28"><AspectRatio :ratio="1" rounded="full" variant="muted" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">full</AspectRatio></div>
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
  <div class="w-40"><AspectRatio variant="plain" rounded="md" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">plain</AspectRatio></div>
  <div class="w-40"><AspectRatio variant="bordered" rounded="md" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">bordered</AspectRatio></div>
  <div class="w-40"><AspectRatio variant="muted" rounded="md" class="flex items-center justify-center text-sm">muted</AspectRatio></div>
</div>
```

Example: Fit
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
  <div class="w-40">
    <AspectRatio :ratio="1" variant="bordered" rounded="md" fit="cover">
      <img alt="Sample image, cover" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 40 20' preserveAspectRatio='none'%3E%3Crect width='40' height='20' fill='%23888'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='20' cy='10' r='8' fill='%23ddd'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" />
    </AspectRatio>
  </div>
  <div class="w-40">
    <AspectRatio :ratio="1" variant="bordered" rounded="md" fit="contain">
      <img alt="Sample image, contain" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 40 20' preserveAspectRatio='none'%3E%3Crect width='40' height='20' fill='%23888'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='20' cy='10' r='8' fill='%23ddd'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" />
    </AspectRatio>
  </div>
  <div class="w-40">
    <AspectRatio :ratio="1" variant="bordered" rounded="md" fit="fill">
      <img alt="Sample image, fill" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 40 20' preserveAspectRatio='none'%3E%3Crect width='40' height='20' fill='%23888'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='20' cy='10' r='8' fill='%23ddd'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" />
    </AspectRatio>
  </div>
</div>
```

# ScrollArea
group: primitives / Layout helpers
Scrollable region with consistent, themed scrollbars across browsers.

Use `ScrollArea` for bounded lists, logs, code panels and side panels where native scrollbars look inconsistent. Give it a bounded size (`h-64`, `max-h-80` via `class`, or a flex/grid parent). Native keyboard, wheel and touch scrolling are preserved, and the viewport is always keyboard focusable (reka-ui sets `tabindex="0"`). Pass `label` to name it. `type` controls when bars show: `hover` (default), `scroll`, `auto` (only when overflowing) or `always`. For horizontal overflow set `horizontal`. Use `ScrollBar` directly only when composing custom layouts inside a reka ScrollAreaRoot.

**Scrollbar thickness** (`size`): `sm` (6px), `md` (10px, default) and `lg` (16px, easier to grab). **Scrollbar look** (`variant`): `default` (transparent track, faint thumb), `track` (a visible muted track behind a solid thumb, so the scroll extent is readable) and `solid` (a solid thumb with no track, for content where the faint thumb is hard to see). When the bars appear is still `type`; `variant` and `size` only change how they look. Unknown values fall back to `md` and `default`. `scrollBarVariants` returns the bar classes for custom layouts.

import { ScrollArea, ScrollBar } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- type: 'hover' | 'scroll' | 'auto' | 'always' = 'hover' - When scrollbars are visible.
- scrollHideDelay: number = 600 - ms before bars hide again (hover / scroll types).
- vertical: boolean = true - Render the vertical scrollbar.
- horizontal: boolean = false - Render the horizontal scrollbar (for content wider than the area).
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Scrollbar thickness: 6px, 10px or 16px. Applies to both bars. Unknown values fall back to md.
- variant: 'default' | 'track' | 'solid' = 'default' - Scrollbar look: default (faint thumb), track (visible muted track behind a solid thumb) or solid (solid thumb). Unknown values fall back to default.
- dir: 'ltr' | 'rtl' - Text direction of the scrollbars. Defaults to the `ConfigProvider` direction.
- label: string - Accessible name of the viewport. With a label the viewport is exposed as a `region` with that name; it is a tab stop either way.
- viewportClass: string | object | array - Classes for the inner viewport (padding, max-height).
- as: string | Component - Root element (default div).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the root; set the size here (`h-64 w-72`).

Parts:
- ScrollBar - Themed scrollbar with a thumb. Rendered automatically by ScrollArea; must be a descendant of a reka-ui ScrollAreaRoot.
    - orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Axis the bar controls.
    - forceMount: boolean - Keep the bar mounted regardless of overflow state.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Bar thickness: 6px, 10px or 16px. Unknown values fall back to md.
    - variant: 'default' | 'track' | 'solid' = 'default' - Look: faint thumb, visible track plus solid thumb, or solid thumb. Unknown values fall back to default.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Scrollable content.

Rules:
- Always bound the height or width (`class="h-64"`), otherwise nothing scrolls.
- Always pass `label` so the focusable viewport has a name.
- Use `horizontal` (and `:vertical="false"` if needed) only for content wider than the area; use `w-max` on the inner row.
- Use `viewport-class` for padding so scrollbars stay at the edge.
- Use `variant="track"` or `"solid"` when the faint default thumb is too subtle; use `size="lg"` for touch-first panels. Do not add `::-webkit-scrollbar` CSS.
- Prefer `type="auto"` or `always` on touch-first or test pages where hover is unavailable.

Accessibility:
- Uses native scrolling inside the viewport, so wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling keep working.
- Keyboard: the viewport is a Tab stop (`tabindex="0"`, set by reka-ui), so Arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End scroll it; the focus ring is drawn inset so the root `overflow-hidden` does not clip it.
- With `label`, the focusable viewport is exposed as `role="region"` with that name; without it only the tab stop exists, so always pass `label` for content that matters.
- `size` and `variant` only restyle the bars: the viewport stays the focusable, named scroller. The `track` and `solid` thumbs use the muted foreground colour (at least 4.5:1 on the background, card and muted surfaces) and a border in forced-colors mode; the default thumb is `bg-input` (the form-control border colour, 3:1 against the background and card surfaces in light and dark, about 3.1:1 and 3.4:1 measured in Chrome) and darkens to the muted foreground on hover; it is lighter than the solid thumbs but no longer a faint hint, and it is still not the only way to scroll. Use `lg` where a thicker bar is easier to grab; bars never replace the keyboard path.
- Scrollbars are decorative, hidden from assistive tech by reka-ui, and have no motion beyond fade.
- Responsive: size it with `w-full max-w-*` so it never forces horizontal scroll of the page at 320px.

Example: Vertical list
```vue
<ScrollArea type="always" label="Sample item list" class="h-40 w-full max-w-64 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
  <div class="space-y-2">
    <div v-for="n in 20" :key="n" class="flex items-center justify-between text-sm">
      <span>Item {{ n }}</span>
      <Badge variant="secondary">{{ n * 3 }}</Badge>
    </div>
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

Example: Horizontal overflow
```vue
<ScrollArea type="always" label="Sample tag row" horizontal :vertical="false" class="w-full max-w-72 rounded-md border">
  <div class="flex w-max gap-2 p-3">
    <Badge v-for="n in 20" :key="n" variant="outline">Tag {{ n }}</Badge>
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

Example: Scrollbar variants
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Default scrollbar" variant="default" class="h-32 w-40 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Row {{ n }}</p>
  </ScrollArea>
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Track scrollbar" variant="track" class="h-32 w-40 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Row {{ n }}</p>
  </ScrollArea>
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Solid scrollbar" variant="solid" class="h-32 w-40 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Row {{ n }}</p>
  </ScrollArea>
</div>
```

Example: Scrollbar sizes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Small scrollbar" size="sm" variant="track" class="h-32 w-40 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Row {{ n }}</p>
  </ScrollArea>
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Medium scrollbar" size="md" variant="track" class="h-32 w-40 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Row {{ n }}</p>
  </ScrollArea>
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Large scrollbar" size="lg" variant="track" class="h-32 w-40 rounded-md border" viewport-class="p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Row {{ n }}</p>
  </ScrollArea>
  <ScrollArea type="always" label="Large horizontal scrollbar" size="lg" variant="solid" horizontal :vertical="false" class="w-full max-w-72 rounded-md border">
    <div class="flex w-max gap-2 p-3">
      <Badge v-for="n in 20" :key="n" variant="outline">Tag {{ n }}</Badge>
    </div>
  </ScrollArea>
</div>
```

# VisuallyHidden
group: primitives / Layout helpers
Hides content visually while keeping it available to screen readers.

Use `VisuallyHidden` for text that only assistive technology needs: labels for icon-only controls, extra context for links, headings that structure a page without being shown. It keeps the element in the accessibility tree (unlike `display: none`/`hidden`). Prefer a visible label whenever the design allows. Use `as-child` to hide an existing element such as a heading.

import { VisuallyHidden } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- as: string | Component = 'span' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Apply the hiding styles to the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged with the root class.

Slots:
- default - Content read by screen readers only.

Rules:
- Use for accessible names of icon-only controls instead of aria-label when text must be translatable in the DOM.
- Never use it to hide interactive content; keyboard users would focus something they cannot see.
- Use as-child to hide an existing semantic element (h2, label) rather than nesting it.

Accessibility:
- Content stays in the accessibility tree and is read by screen readers.
- Not focusable by default: do not put interactive controls inside unless they are meant to be reached while invisible.

Example: Label for an icon-only button
```vue
<Button size="icon" variant="outline">
  <Icon :icon="faXmark" />
  <VisuallyHidden>Close</VisuallyHidden>
</Button>
```

Example: Hidden heading via asChild
```vue
<section>
  <VisuallyHidden as-child><h2>Account settings</h2></VisuallyHidden>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">The heading above is announced but not shown.</p>
</section>
```

# Link
group: primitives / Links
Inline text link with variants, safe external handling and RouterLink support.

Use `Link` for navigation inside or between text. `external` opens a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, adds an arrow icon and an sr-only "(opens in new tab)" hint. For router navigation pass `as` (or `as-child`) with a RouterLink and give it its `to` as an attribute. For link-looking buttons use `Button variant="link"`; for button-looking links use `Button as="a"`.

Variations:

- `variant`: `default` (primary, underline on hover), `underline` (primary, always underlined), `muted`, `subtle` (foreground colour, always underlined), `plain` (inherits the surrounding text colour, always underlined, for links inside tinted or coloured text) and `destructive` (destructive colour, always underlined, for links to irreversible actions such as a delete page).
- `size`: `inherit` (default, keeps the surrounding text size), `sm` (14px), `md` (16px), `lg` (18px).

Inline links are exempt from the 24px minimum target size (WCAG 2.5.8); a standalone link in a toolbar or list should sit in a row with at least 24px of height.

import { Link } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'underline' | 'muted' | 'subtle' | 'plain' | 'destructive' = 'default' - default = primary, underline on hover; underline = always underlined; muted = grey; subtle = foreground colour with underline; plain = inherits the text colour, underlined; destructive = destructive colour, underlined. Unknown values fall back to default.
- size: 'inherit' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'inherit' - inherit keeps the size of the surrounding text; sm, md, lg set text-sm, text-base, text-lg. Unknown values fall back to inherit.
- href: string - Destination. Omitted while `disabled`.
- external: boolean = false - target="_blank", rel="noopener noreferrer", trailing icon and sr-only hint.
- externalLabel: string = '(opens in new tab)' - Visually hidden hint read after an external link. Use it to translate the text; a `ConfigProvider` label `link.externalHint` sets it for a whole subtree and this prop wins.
- externalIcon: boolean = true - Show the trailing arrow icon on external links.
- disabled: boolean = false - aria-disabled, tabindex -1, no href, clicks blocked.
- as: string | Component = 'a' - Element or component (e.g. RouterLink) to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (no icon or sr-only hint is added).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Link text.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a plain Link (`as="a"`, not disabled) has no `href`, or an `asChild` Link wraps an element without `href`.
- Throws a ContractError when a Link has no accessible name (an icon-only link needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Use `size` only for standalone links; inside a paragraph leave it on `inherit`.
- Use `external` for off-site URLs; never write target="_blank" manually.
- For RouterLink use `as` / `as-child`, not onClick + router.push.
- Do not use Link for actions that do not navigate; use Button.

Accessibility:
- External links announce "(opens in new tab)" via an sr-only span.
- Disabled links use role="link" with aria-disabled="true", drop href and leave the tab order (an `<a>` without `href` would otherwise lose its role).
- Links are distinguishable without colour: `default` and `muted` underline on hover and focus, `underline` and `subtle` are always underlined; use one of those inside running text.
- `plain` and `destructive` are underlined at rest, so the link is not marked by colour alone. `plain` inherits its colour: check contrast against the surface it sits on. `destructive` uses text-destructive on the page background, a tested pair.
- Visible focus ring on keyboard focus.

Example: Variants
```vue
<p class="text-sm">
  Read the <Link href="/guides/getting-started">guide</Link>, the <Link href="/components" variant="underline">component list</Link>,
  the <Link href="/foundations/accessibility" variant="muted">accessibility notes</Link> or the <Link href="/guides/customisation" variant="subtle">customisation guide</Link>.
</p>
```

Example: External and disabled
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
  <Link href="https://vuejs.org" external>Vue.js</Link>
  <Link href="https://vuejs.org" external :external-icon="false">Vue.js without icon</Link>
  <Link href="/guides/testing" disabled>Disabled link</Link>
</div>
```

Example: Plain and destructive variants
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
  <p class="rounded-md bg-muted px-3 py-2 text-muted-foreground">Sample note with a <Link href="/guides/testing" variant="plain">plain link</Link> that keeps the note colour.</p>
  <p>Sample warning: <Link href="/guides/customisation" variant="destructive">delete the sample project</Link> cannot be undone.</p>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-x-4 gap-y-1 text-sm">
  <Link href="/components">inherit</Link>
  <Link href="/components" size="sm">sm</Link>
  <Link href="/components" size="md">md</Link>
  <Link href="/components" size="lg">lg</Link>
</div>
```

# Badge
group: primitives / Status
Small non-interactive label for status, counts and categories.

Use `Badge` to label an item with a short status or category (`Beta`, `Paid`, `3 new`). It is not interactive: for removable or toggleable tags use `Chip`; for presence on an avatar use `Avatar status`.

Variations:

- `variant`: fixed-colour looks `default`, `secondary`, `outline`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, plus the tone-aware `soft`, `solid` and `outline`.
- `tone`: `neutral | primary | success | warning | danger | info`. Pair with `soft` (tinted, the usual choice in tables and lists), `solid` (strong, for counts and "new") or `outline` (bordered). `soft` / `solid` without a tone are neutral. Ignored by the fixed-colour variants.
- `size`: `sm` (dense tables), `md` (default), `lg`.
- `rounded`: `default` (rounded-md), `full` (pill), `none`.
- `dot`: leading status dot in the current text colour, for "Active" / "Offline" style statuses.

When using `badgeVariants` outside the component, wrap the result in `cn()` so tailwind-merge drops overridden neutral colours.

import { Badge } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'secondary' | 'outline' | 'destructive' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'soft' | 'solid' = 'default' - Look. `soft`, `solid` and `outline` are tone-aware. Unknown values fall back to default.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' - Semantic colour for `soft` / `solid` / `outline`. Unset = neutral (soft, solid) or plain outline. Ignored by other variants and when unknown.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and text size. Unknown values fall back to md.
- rounded: 'default' | 'full' | 'none' = 'default' - Corner radius: rounded-md, rounded-full (pill) or none.
- dot: boolean = false - Show a small decorative dot (aria-hidden, current colour) before the content. Not rendered with `asChild`.
- as: string | Component = 'span' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Badge content: text, a count, or an inline icon (svg children are sized to the badge).

Rules:
- Use `variant="soft"` + `tone` for statuses in tables/lists; `solid` for counts; do not colour-code without a text label.
- Use `Chip`, not `Badge`, when the label must be removable or selectable.
- Use `rounded="full"` for pills and `dot` for presence-style statuses; do not hand-roll dots with extra spans.
- Do not pass `tone` expecting it to recolour `default` / `secondary` / `destructive` / `success` / `warning` / `info` variants.

Accessibility:
- Badges are plain text with no role; screen readers read the content in flow.
- Tone colours are tested token pairs (AA contrast in light and dark); the label text, not the colour, carries the meaning.
- Badges never shrink below their content and use `whitespace-nowrap`: keep them to one or two words, and place them in a `flex-wrap` row so they reflow at 320px.
- The `dot` is aria-hidden: never rely on colour alone, always include a text label (e.g. "Offline").
- A dot-only badge (no content) conveys nothing to assistive tech: add `aria-label` / visually hidden text.

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
  <Badge>Default</Badge>
  <Badge variant="secondary">Secondary</Badge>
  <Badge variant="outline">Outline</Badge>
  <Badge variant="destructive">Destructive</Badge>
  <Badge variant="success">Success</Badge>
  <Badge variant="warning">Warning</Badge>
  <Badge variant="info">Info</Badge>
</div>
```

Example: Soft tones
```vue

  <Badge variant="soft">Neutral</Badge>
  <Badge variant="soft" tone="primary">Primary</Badge>
  <Badge variant="soft" tone="success">Paid</Badge>
  <Badge variant="soft" tone="warning">Pending</Badge>
  <Badge variant="soft" tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
  <Badge variant="soft" tone="info">Draft</Badge>

```

```vue

  <Badge variant="solid" tone="warning">Warning</Badge>
```

# CountBadge
group: primitives / Status
Numeric count pill or small dot for unread items and pending work, with a required accessible label.

Use `CountBadge` for a number that sits next to or on top of another element: unread messages, open tasks, items in a cart. A count of 0 renders nothing, a large count is capped (`99+`), and the visible number is hidden from assistive technology in favour of a `label` such as `3 unread messages`. For a status word (`Paid`, `Draft`) use `Badge`; for a status light without a number use `StatusDot`.

Variations:

- `tone`: `neutral | primary | success | warning | danger | info`.
- `appearance`: `solid` (default), `soft` (tinted) or `outline` (border on the page background, readable over other elements).
- `size`: `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), `lg` 28px tall.
- `shape`: `pill` (grows with the text), `circle` (round for one or two digits), `square` (control radius).
- `dot`: a marker without a number. With `count` it hides at 0, without `count` it always shows.
- `max` and `showZero`: the cap before `max+`, and whether `0` is rendered.

Placement: wrap the target and the badge in `CountBadgeAnchor` and put the badge in its `badge` slot. `placement` is `top-end` (default), `top-start`, `bottom-end` or `bottom-start`; start and end flip in right-to-left text. `countBadgePlacement` exposes the same classes for custom wrappers.

Bad input is handled, not thrown: a count that is not a number or is NaN or negative counts as 0, a fraction is truncated, `Infinity` shows `max+`, and an invalid `max` falls back to 99. Wrap `countBadgeVariants(...)` in `cn()` when you use it on a plain element, because a few classes override each other.

import { CountBadge, CountBadgeAnchor } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- count: number - Number to show. Not a number, NaN and negative values count as 0, fractions are truncated, Infinity shows `max+`. In `dot` mode, omit it for an always-visible dot.
- max: number = 99 - Largest number printed; above it the badge shows `max+`. A whole number from 1; anything else falls back to 99.
- showZero: boolean = false - Render the badge when the count is 0. By default a 0 renders nothing.
- dot: boolean = false - Small marker without a number. Still needs `label`. With `count` it hides at 0 (unless `showZero`).
- label: string - Accessible text, read instead of the visible number (visually hidden). Required whenever the badge renders. Example: `3 unread messages`.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - Semantic colour. Unknown values fall back to primary.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height and text size (16px, 20px, 28px); a 6px, 8px or 10px dot in `dot` mode. Unknown values fall back to md.
- shape: 'pill' | 'circle' | 'square' = 'pill' - Corner shape. `circle` stays round up to two digits and widens for `99+`. Unknown values fall back to pill.
- appearance: 'solid' | 'soft' | 'outline' = 'solid' - Fill style. `outline` has a page-background fill so it stays readable over other elements. Unknown values fall back to solid.
- as: string | Component = 'span' - Element to render.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- CountBadgeAnchor - Relative wrapper that places a `CountBadge` (in its `badge` slot) on a corner of the default-slot content, using logical start and end offsets.
    - placement: 'top-end' | 'top-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'bottom-start' = 'top-end' - Corner of the target the badge is centred on. Unknown values fall back to top-end.
    - as: string | Component = 'span' - Element to render.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- badge - On `CountBadgeAnchor`: the badge to place on the corner (usually a `CountBadge`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a rendered badge (a count above 0, `show-zero`, or a dot) has no non-empty `label`.

Rules:
- Always pass `label` with the full phrase a screen reader should hear ("3 unread messages"), not just the number; keep it in sync with `count`.
- Do not guard with `v-if="count > 0"`: `CountBadge` already renders nothing at 0 unless `show-zero` is set.
- Use `max` for a cap (`99+`); do not format the number yourself.
- To attach a badge to another element use `CountBadgeAnchor` with the `badge` slot and `placement`; never position it with physical left/right classes.
- Use `dot` for presence without a number and `Badge` for words. Do not signal state by colour alone: the label or neighbouring text must say it.
- Use `appearance="outline"` when the badge overlaps other content so it keeps its own background.

Accessibility:
- Not interactive and has no role. The visible number is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden `label` (for example `3 unread messages`) carries the meaning, so the count is never colour alone and is read in flow with the element next to it.
- A rendered badge without `label` text throws a ContractError in strict mode. A badge that renders nothing (count 0) is not checked.
- The label does not update itself: when `count` changes, pass a matching `label`. A change is not announced; for live updates keep an existing polite `role="status"` region elsewhere in the page.
- Numbers use tabular figures. Tone colours are Badge token pairs covered by the contrast tests (light and dark). In forced-colors mode the border stays visible.
- Placement uses logical `start` and `end` insets and flips the shift for right-to-left text. The anchor wrapper has `pointer-events-none` on the badge so clicks reach the element underneath.
- The badge is small by design and is not a target. Put the interaction on the element it is attached to.

Example: Count with an accessible label
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <span class="text-sm">Inbox</span>
  <CountBadge :count="3" label="3 unread messages" />
</div>
```

Example: Overflow and zero
```vue

  <CountBadge :count="7" label="7 open tasks" />
  <CountBadge :count="250" label="More than 99 open tasks" />
  <CountBadge :count="250" :max="9" label="More than 9 open tasks" />
  <CountBadge :count="0" show-zero label="0 open tasks" />
  <CountBadge :count="0" label="No open tasks" />
</div>
```

Example: Tones
```vue

  <CountBadge :count="4" tone="neutral" label="4 drafts" />
  <CountBadge :count="4" tone="primary" label="4 mentions" />
  <CountBadge :count="4" tone="success" label="4 approved" />
  <CountBadge :count="4" tone="warning" label="4 pending" />
  <CountBadge :count="4" tone="danger" label="4 failed" />
  <CountBadge :count="4" tone="info" label="4 notes" />
</div>
```

```vue
  <CountBadge :count="12" appearance="soft" label="12 alerts" />
```

```vue
  <CountBadge :count="8" label="8 items, medium" />
```

```vue
  <CountBadge :count="42" shape="circle" label="42 items, circle" />
```

# Progress
group: primitives / Status
Horizontal progress bar with determinate and indeterminate modes, tones, sizes, a pulse animation, inside/top labels and segments.

Use `Progress` to show how far a known task has come (`modelValue` 0..`max`) or that something is working with no known end (omit `modelValue` or pass `null`). Values are clamped: NaN and negatives become 0, values above `max` become `max`, an invalid `max` falls back to 100. Unknown `size`/`tone`/`valuePosition` values fall back to the defaults.

Variations: **size** `xs` (2px) to `xl` (20px); **tone** for meaning (primary, success, warning, danger, info, neutral); **animated** pulses the filled bar (a busy but determinate task; static under prefers-reduced-motion). **variant** picks the indeterminate look: `slide` or `sweep` (two-phase: grows, travels, shrinks). A moving stripe look is not offered because stripes need a gradient. `striped` is deprecated and draws nothing, because stripes need a gradient and the design system uses none; **valuePosition** `end` (percentage beside the bar, default), `inside` (percentage inside the filled bar, needs size `lg`/`xl`, clipped when the value is very small) or `top` (header row with the visible `label` on the left and the percentage on the right); **segments** splits the bar into N steps for wizards, password strength or quotas (each segment fills proportionally). For a circular meter use `ProgressRing`; for tiny inline waits use `Spinner`.

import { Progress } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: number | null - Current value. null/undefined renders the indeterminate animation.
- max: number = 100 - Upper bound. Non-finite or <= 0 falls back to 100.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the filled bar. Unknown values fall back to primary.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Track height: 2px, 4px, 8px, 12px, 20px. Unknown values fall back to md.
- label: string - Accessible name (aria-label). Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set. Also rendered as visible text when `valuePosition="top"`.
- showValue: boolean = false - Show the rounded percentage as text (determinate only). Placement set by `valuePosition`.
- valuePosition: 'end' | 'inside' | 'top' = 'end' - end = beside the bar; inside = in the filled bar (use size lg/xl; segmented bars fall back to end); top = header row above the bar with label + percentage.
- variant: 'slide' | 'sweep' = 'slide' - Indeterminate look: slide = the bar travels across the track; sweep = the bar grows, travels and shrinks. Static half-opacity full bar under prefers-reduced-motion. No effect when determinate or segmented. Unknown values fall back to slide.
- striped: boolean = false - Deprecated, no visual effect (stripes need a gradient).
- animated: boolean = false - Pulses the filled bar; implies nothing else. Static under prefers-reduced-motion and ignored while indeterminate.
- segments: number = 0 - Split the bar into N segments (2..50, floored). Values below 2 or non-finite render a normal bar. Each segment fills proportionally to the value.
- as: string | Component - Root element (default div).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the root wrapper (set width here, e.g. `w-64`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a Progress has none of `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- Omit modelValue (or pass null) for unknown duration; never fake a percentage.
- Always set `label` when more than one progress bar is on the page.
- Control width with the parent (e.g. `max-w-72`); the bar fills its container by default.
- Use tone="danger"/"warning" for thresholds instead of custom colours.
- Use value-position="inside" only with size lg/xl; use value-position="top" when the label should be visible.
- Use `segments` for discrete steps; use `animated` only while work is actually running. Do not use `striped`.

Accessibility:
- role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin/max/now (reka-ui); indeterminate omits aria-valuenow. Segmented bars keep a single progressbar on the root; segments are plain presentation.
- Pass `label` (aria-label) describing what is progressing; a bar without a name throws a ContractError (the rendered fallback is "Progress"). Use `aria-labelledby` to point at visible text instead.
- The percentage text uses `tabular-nums`, so the digits do not jitter while the value changes. Progress updates are not announced as a live region; use a separate `role="status"` message for milestones.
- The indeterminate animation is replaced by a static half-opacity bar and the pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion. In forced-colors mode (where background colours are replaced by system colours) the track gets a 1px border and the fill a 2px border, so the filled length stays readable.
- Responsive: the bar is `w-full` and shrinks with its container; give it a `max-w-*` parent rather than a fixed width.

Example: Determinate and indeterminate
```vue
<div class="w-full max-w-72 space-y-3">
  <Progress :model-value="45" label="Sample upload" />
  <Progress :model-value="80" tone="success" size="lg" show-value label="Sample disk" />
  <Progress label="Loading" />
</div>
```

Example: Interactive with tones
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const value = ref(30)
</script>

<div class="w-full max-w-72 space-y-3">
  <Progress :model-value="value" show-value label="Sample quota" :tone="value > 85 ? 'danger' : value > 60 ? 'warning' : 'primary'" />
  <div class="flex gap-2">
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="value = Math.max(0, value - 10)">-10</Button>
    <Button size="sm" @click="value = Math.min(100, value + 10)">+10</Button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```vue
  <Progress label="Sample slide" />

  <Progress variant="sweep" tone="success" size="lg" label="Sample large sweep" />
</div>
```

```vue
  <Progress :model-value="60" size="xs" label="xs" />
  <Progress :model-value="60" size="sm" label="sm" />
```

Example: Segmented

```vue
  <Progress :model-value="step * 20" :segments="5" label="Sample steps" show-value value-position="top" />
  <Progress :model-value="60" :segments="10" size="sm" tone="success" label="Sample strength" />
  <div class="flex gap-2">
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="step = Math.max(0, step - 1)">Back</Button>
    <Button size="sm" @click="step = Math.min(5, step + 1)">Next</Button>
  </div>
</div>
```

# ProgressRing
group: primitives / Status
Circular SVG meter that fills clockwise from the top, with a centre label.

Use `ProgressRing` for scores, quotas and completion where a compact circular readout fits (dashboards, cards). It is pure and stateless: the arc animates with a CSS transition when `value` changes (disabled for reduced motion). Values are sanitised: NaN and negatives become 0, values above `max` become `max`, an invalid `max` falls back to 100. For linear bars use `Progress`.

Variations:

- `size`: a number of px (default 64) or a preset: `xs` 40, `sm` 48, `md` 64, `lg` 96, `xl` 128. A preset also sets a matching thickness (4, 5, 6, 8, 10px) unless you pass `strokeWidth`.
- `variant`: `default` draws the muted track under the arc; `bare` draws the arc alone, for rings on tinted or busy surfaces.
- `shape`: the line cap of the arc, `round` (default) or `butt` (flat ends, so the arc length is exact).
- `tone`: colour of the arc.

import { ProgressRing } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- label: string - Accessible name of the ring. Required: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` must say what is measured.
- valueText: string - Text for `aria-valuetext`, e.g. `42 of 100 GB`. Defaults to the rounded percent.
- value: number = 0 - Current value, clamped to 0..max.
- max: number = 100 - Upper bound. Non-finite or <= 0 falls back to 100.
- size: number | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 64 - Outer diameter in px, or a preset: xs 40, sm 48, md 64, lg 96, xl 128. Invalid numbers and unknown presets fall back to 64.
- strokeWidth: number = 6 - Ring thickness in px (capped at size / 2). Without it a size preset uses its own thickness (4, 5, 6, 8, 10px) and a numeric size uses 6.
- variant: 'default' | 'bare' = 'default' - `default` draws the muted track under the arc; `bare` draws the arc alone. Unknown values fall back to default.
- shape: 'round' | 'butt' = 'round' - Line cap of the arc (`stroke-linecap`): rounded or flat ends. Unknown values fall back to round.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the value arc (track is always muted).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the root; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- label ({ value: number; percent: number }) - Centre content. Defaults to the rounded percentage.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a ProgressRing has none of `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- Always pass `label` describing the metric.
- Use `size` (px or a preset such as `lg`) and `strokeWidth` props for dimensions, not CSS width/height.
- Put custom centre content in the `label` slot; it receives { value, percent }.
- Stateless: do not expect count-up animation; drive `value` from state.

Accessibility:
- role="meter" with aria-valuenow/min/max and aria-valuetext ("42%"); the SVG itself is aria-hidden.
- The rendered fallback name is "Progress", but a ring without `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`) throws a ContractError: pass `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`) with the real subject.
- The centre text is `tabular-nums`; forced-colors mode keeps the track and arc visible because both are drawn with token strokes.
- Arc transition is removed with motion-reduce.
- Size presets, `variant` and `shape` change only the drawing: role, value, aria-valuetext and the centre percentage are the same. With `variant="bare"` keep the centre percentage (or your `label` slot): without the track the arc alone does not show where the scale ends.

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-4">
  <ProgressRing :value="25" tone="danger" label="Sample metric A" />
  <ProgressRing :value="60" tone="warning" label="Sample metric B" />
  <ProgressRing :value="92" tone="success" label="Sample metric C" />
</div>
```

Example: Custom size and label slot
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-4">
  <ProgressRing :value="7" :max="10" :size="96" :stroke-width="8" label="Sample score">
    <template #label="{ value }">
      <span class="text-lg font-semibold">{{ value }}<span class="text-xs text-muted-foreground">/10</span></span>
    </template>
  </ProgressRing>
  <ProgressRing :value="40" :size="40" :stroke-width="4" tone="info" label="Sample progress" />
</div>
```

Example: Size presets
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <ProgressRing :value="64" size="xs" label="Sample metric xs" />
  <ProgressRing :value="64" size="sm" label="Sample metric sm" />
  <ProgressRing :value="64" size="md" label="Sample metric md" />
  <ProgressRing :value="64" size="lg" label="Sample metric lg" />
  <ProgressRing :value="64" size="xl" label="Sample metric xl" />
</div>
```

Example: Variants and line caps
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <ProgressRing :value="45" label="Sample, track and round cap" />
  <ProgressRing :value="45" variant="bare" label="Sample, bare" />
  <ProgressRing :value="45" shape="butt" label="Sample, butt cap" />
  <ProgressRing :value="45" variant="bare" shape="butt" tone="success" label="Sample, bare and butt" />
</div>
```

# StatusBadge
group: primitives / Status
Badge that maps a raw status string (active, pending, failed...) to a tone, with a leading dot.

Use `StatusBadge` to display backend status values without writing a status-to-colour map in every view. Statuses are matched case-insensitively after trimming and normalising spaces and dashes to underscores, so `In Progress`, `in-progress` and `IN_PROGRESS` all match `in_progress`. Built-in groups: success (active, online, healthy, ok, success, completed, approved, ...), warning (pending, warning, degraded, queued, paused, ...), info (running, in_progress, processing, new, draft, info, ...), danger (error, failed, offline, down, rejected, critical, unhealthy, ...), anything else neutral. `null`/empty renders "Unknown". Override with `tones`, or reuse the logic with the exported `statusTone(status, overrides?)` and `statusBadgeDefaultTones`.

Variations:

- `variant`: `soft` (default: tinted success, warning and info, filled danger, secondary neutral), `outline` (bordered, tone-coloured text), `solid` (filled with the tone colour), `plain` (tone-coloured dot and text with no border, fill or side padding, for dense tables and lists) and `tinted` (every tone tinted, danger and primary included, so a failed row does not outweigh everything else on a busy status screen).
- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`. The dot scales with the text (4px, 6px, 8px).
- `shape`: `rounded` (default, rounded-md), `pill` (fully round), `square` (no radius).

The status text is always rendered, whatever the variant: the tone colour never carries the status alone.

import { StatusBadge } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- status: string | null - Raw status value. null/undefined/empty renders "Unknown" in the neutral tone.
- tones: Record<string, 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info'> - Overrides of the built-in map. Keys are normalised like the status; invalid tones are ignored.
- label: string - Text to show. Defaults to the humanised status (`in_progress` -> `In progress`).
- variant: 'soft' | 'outline' | 'solid' | 'plain' | 'tinted' = 'soft' - Look. soft = the original tinted/filled badges (danger filled); outline = border and tone text; solid = tone fill; plain = text and dot only; tinted = every tone tinted, danger included. Unknown values fall back to soft.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Badge text and padding size; the dot follows (4px, 6px, 8px). Unknown values fall back to md.
- shape: 'pill' | 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corner radius: rounded-full, rounded-md or none. Unknown values fall back to rounded.
- dot: boolean = true - Show the leading status dot.
- pulse: boolean = false - Animate the dot (live / in-progress states; reduced-motion safe).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the badge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ label: string; tone: Tone }) - Replaces the label text.

Rules:
- Pass the raw backend status to `status`; do not pre-map to variants.
- Add app-specific statuses via `tones`, not new components.
- Use `statusTone(status)` when you need the tone outside the badge (row colour, icon).
- Do not use for counts or categories; use Badge.
- Use `variant="plain"` for dense tables, `variant="outline"` on tinted surfaces, `variant="solid"` sparingly; do not drop the text.

Accessibility:
- The status is conveyed by text, not colour; the dot is aria-hidden. Every variant renders the text, including `plain`.
- `solid` keeps a border in forced-colors mode, where fills are dropped. The tone colours are tested token pairs (tinted, outline and plain text on the page background, foreground colours on solid fills).
- Keep the label meaningful when you override it (screen readers read the label only).
- The pulsing halo is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

Example: Built-in statuses
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <StatusBadge status="active" />
  <StatusBadge status="pending" />
  <StatusBadge status="in_progress" pulse />
  <StatusBadge status="failed" />
  <StatusBadge status="draft" />
  <StatusBadge status="archived" />
  <StatusBadge :status="null" />
</div>
```

Example: Overrides, labels and no dot
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
  <StatusBadge status="running" :tones="{ running: 'success' }" label="Live" pulse />
  <StatusBadge status="decommissioned" :tones="{ decommissioned: 'danger' }" :dot="false" />
  <StatusBadge status="quarantined" label="Isolated" />
  <StatusBadge status="CUSTOM-STATE" :tones="{ custom_state: 'primary' }" />
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <StatusBadge status="active" /><StatusBadge status="pending" /><StatusBadge status="failed" /><StatusBadge status="running" /><StatusBadge status="archived" />
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <StatusBadge variant="outline" status="active" /><StatusBadge variant="outline" status="pending" /><StatusBadge variant="outline" status="failed" /><StatusBadge variant="outline" status="running" /><StatusBadge variant="outline" status="archived" />
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <StatusBadge variant="tinted" status="active" /><StatusBadge variant="tinted" status="pending" /><StatusBadge variant="tinted" status="failed" /><StatusBadge variant="tinted" status="running" /><StatusBadge variant="tinted" status="archived" />
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <StatusBadge variant="solid" status="active" /><StatusBadge variant="solid" status="pending" /><StatusBadge variant="solid" status="failed" /><StatusBadge variant="solid" status="running" /><StatusBadge variant="solid" status="archived" />
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
    <StatusBadge variant="plain" status="active" /><StatusBadge variant="plain" status="pending" /><StatusBadge variant="plain" status="failed" /><StatusBadge variant="plain" status="running" /><StatusBadge variant="plain" status="archived" />
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and shapes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <StatusBadge size="sm" status="active" /><StatusBadge status="active" /><StatusBadge size="lg" status="active" />
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <StatusBadge shape="pill" status="pending" /><StatusBadge shape="rounded" status="pending" /><StatusBadge shape="square" status="pending" />
    <StatusBadge shape="pill" variant="outline" size="lg" status="running" pulse />
  </div>
</div>
```

# StatusDot
group: primitives / Status
Small coloured dot that signals a state (online, failing, pending), optionally pulsing.

Use `StatusDot` next to text that already names the state (a table row, a list item, a header). When the dot is the ONLY indicator pass `label` so assistive tech announces it; otherwise it is `aria-hidden`. For a labelled pill use `StatusBadge`. `pulse` adds an animated halo for live/in-progress states and is disabled automatically for users who prefer reduced motion.

Variations:

- `variant`: `solid` (filled, default), `ring` (filled with an outline and a gap, for the current or selected item), `outline` (hollow, for "not started" or "disabled" states) and `soft` (tinted fill with a border). `ring`, `outline` and `soft` draw a border or outline, so they stay visible in forced-colors mode where a fill alone is dropped.
- `size`: `xs` (4px), `sm` (6px), `md` (8px, default), `lg` (10px), `xl` (12px).
- `tone`: `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`.

The shape is not the state: pair every variant with text or a `label`, as before.

import { StatusDot } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'neutral' - Semantic colour. Unknown values fall back to neutral.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Diameter: 4px, 6px, 8px, 10px, 12px. Unknown values fall back to md.
- variant: 'solid' | 'ring' | 'outline' | 'soft' = 'solid' - solid = filled; ring = filled with an outline and a gap; outline = hollow border; soft = 30% tinted fill with a border. Unknown values fall back to solid.
- pulse: boolean = false - Animated halo (animate-ping); removed under prefers-reduced-motion.
- label: string - Accessible name. Sets role="status" and aria-label; without it the dot is aria-hidden.
- as: string | Component = 'span' - Element to render.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Rules:
- Always add visible text next to the dot or pass `label`; colour alone is not accessible.
- Use `tone`, not custom bg-* classes, for state colours.
- Use `pulse` only for live/ongoing states, sparingly.
- Use `variant="outline"` for inactive or not-started states and `variant="ring"` for the current item; keep `solid` for the usual status.

Accessibility:
- Decorative by default (aria-hidden="true"); pair it with visible text.
- With `label` it becomes role="img" with that aria-label (a static image, not a live region, so it does not interrupt screen-reader users when it re-renders). Use `role="status"` on a surrounding element if a state change must be announced.
- The pulse halo is aria-hidden and disabled via motion-reduce.
- Never rely on colour alone: always include text or a label. The `ring`, `outline` and `soft` variants change the shape as well as the colour, but the shape is not a status either.
- `ring`, `outline` and `soft` use an outline or border, which forced-colors mode keeps; a `solid` fill is dropped there, so keep the adjacent text.

Example: Tones and sizes
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <StatusDot tone="neutral" />
  <StatusDot tone="primary" />
  <StatusDot tone="success" />
  <StatusDot tone="warning" />
  <StatusDot tone="danger" />
  <StatusDot tone="info" />
  <StatusDot tone="success" size="sm" />
  <StatusDot tone="success" size="lg" />
</div>
```

Example: Inline with text, pulsing and labelled
```vue
<ul class="space-y-2 text-sm">
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" pulse /> Sample service is live</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" /> Sample database is down</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="warning" label="Degraded" /> <Badge variant="outline">Sample cache</Badge></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<ul class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-6 gap-y-2 text-sm">
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" /> Solid</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" /> Solid</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" variant="ring" /> Ring</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" variant="ring" /> Ring</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" variant="outline" /> Outline</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" variant="outline" /> Outline</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="success" variant="soft" /> Soft</li>
  <li class="flex items-center gap-2"><StatusDot tone="danger" variant="soft" /> Soft</li>
</ul>
```

Example: Sizes and pulse on every variant
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <div class="flex items-center gap-3">
    <StatusDot tone="info" size="xs" /><StatusDot tone="info" size="sm" /><StatusDot tone="info" size="md" /><StatusDot tone="info" size="lg" /><StatusDot tone="info" size="xl" />
    <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">xs to xl</span>
  </div>
  <div class="flex items-center gap-3">
    <StatusDot tone="success" pulse /><StatusDot tone="success" variant="ring" pulse /><StatusDot tone="success" variant="outline" pulse /><StatusDot tone="success" variant="soft" pulse />
    <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sample live indicators</span>
  </div>
</div>
```
