# Toggle
group: primitives / Toggles
Two-state button that stays pressed (bold, mute, pin). Controlled or uncontrolled.

Use `Toggle` for an independent on/off button, typically with an icon (formatting, mute, favourite). Use `v-model` for the pressed state, or `default-pressed` when you only need an initial state. For a set of related toggles use `ToggleGroup`; for settings use `Switch` or `Checkbox`. Icon-only toggles MUST have an `aria-label`.

Variations:

- `variant`: `default` (flat), `outline` (bordered), `soft` (muted fill, primary tint when pressed) and `filled` (secondary fill, solid primary when pressed). `soft` and `filled` read as buttons without a border, for toolbars and filter rows.
- `tone`: `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info` recolours the PRESSED state: tinted for `default`, `outline` and `soft`, solid for `filled`. Unset keeps the neutral accent (primary for `soft` and `filled`).
- `size`: `xs` (28px), `sm` (32px), `md` (36px, default), `lg` (40px), `xl` (44px).
- `shape`: `rounded` (default, rounded-md), `pill`, `square`.

import { Toggle } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: boolean - Pressed state (v-model). Leave undefined for uncontrolled use.
- defaultPressed: boolean = false - Initial pressed state when uncontrolled.
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'soft' | 'filled' = 'default' - Visual style: flat, bordered, muted fill (primary tint when pressed) or secondary fill (solid primary when pressed). Unknown values fall back to default.
- tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' - Colour of the pressed state (tinted, or solid for `filled`). Unset = neutral accent (primary for `soft` and `filled`). Unknown values are ignored.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Height/padding: 28px, 32px, 36px, 40px, 44px. Unknown values fall back to md.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corner radius: rounded-md, rounded-full or none. Unknown values fall back to rounded.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables interaction.
- as: string | Component = 'button' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ pressed: boolean }) - Label and/or icon.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: boolean] - Fired when the pressed state changes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a Toggle has no accessible name (an icon-only Toggle needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Always set aria-label on icon-only toggles.
- Use v-model (boolean) for controlled state; default-pressed for uncontrolled.
- Group related toggles with ToggleGroup instead of laying out several Toggles by hand.
- Reuse `toggleVariants({ variant, tone, size, shape })` (wrapped in `cn()`) to style non-button elements.
- Use `tone` for the pressed colour only; do not use it to mean a status without text.

Accessibility:
- Native <button> with aria-pressed reflecting the state; Space/Enter toggle.
- Icon-only toggles need aria-label; the label names the control and must not change with the state (aria-pressed already says on or off).
- Target size: `xs` is 28px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px, `lg` 40px and `xl` 44px high, all at least 24px; on coarse pointers `xs` and `sm` grow to 40px and `md`, `lg` to 44px.
- Pressed state is shown by a fill and exposed as aria-pressed, so it is not conveyed by colour alone; `outline` adds a border that keeps the shape visible in forced-colors mode; `soft` and `filled` get a border there, and any pressed toggle a 2px border.
- Tones and variants use tested token pairs: tinted text on its tint, primary-foreground on primary, status foregrounds on solid status colours, muted-foreground on muted and secondary-foreground on secondary. The pressed state never depends on the tone: it is aria-pressed, a fill change and, in forced-colors mode, a border.
- Pressed state is also exposed as data-state="on|off" for styling.

Example: Variants and sizes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
  <Toggle aria-label="Bold"><Icon :icon="faBold" /></Toggle>
  <Toggle variant="outline" aria-label="Italic"><Icon :icon="faItalic" /></Toggle>
  <Toggle size="sm" default-pressed>Small</Toggle>
  <Toggle size="lg" variant="outline">Large</Toggle>
  <Toggle disabled>Disabled</Toggle>
</div>
```

Example: v-model
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const pinned = ref(false)
</script>

<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Toggle v-model="pinned" variant="outline">{{ pinned ? 'Pinned' : 'Pin' }}</Toggle>
  <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Pinned: {{ pinned }}</span>
</div>
```

Example: Soft and filled
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
  <Toggle variant="soft">Soft</Toggle>
  <Toggle variant="soft" default-pressed>Soft pressed</Toggle>
  <Toggle variant="filled">Filled</Toggle>
  <Toggle variant="filled" default-pressed>Filled pressed</Toggle>
</div>
```

Example: Pressed tones
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <Toggle default-pressed tone="primary">Primary</Toggle>
    <Toggle default-pressed tone="success">Success</Toggle>
    <Toggle default-pressed tone="warning">Warning</Toggle>
    <Toggle default-pressed tone="danger">Danger</Toggle>
    <Toggle default-pressed tone="info">Info</Toggle>
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <Toggle variant="filled" default-pressed tone="primary">Primary</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="filled" default-pressed tone="success">Success</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="filled" default-pressed tone="warning">Warning</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="filled" default-pressed tone="danger">Danger</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="filled" default-pressed tone="info">Info</Toggle>
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and shapes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <Toggle variant="outline" size="xs">xs</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="outline" size="sm">sm</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="outline" size="md">md</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="outline" size="lg">lg</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="outline" size="xl">xl</Toggle>
  </div>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <Toggle variant="outline" shape="rounded">Rounded</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="outline" shape="pill">Pill</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="outline" shape="square">Square</Toggle>
    <Toggle variant="soft" shape="pill" default-pressed>Pill soft</Toggle>
  </div>
</div>
```

# ToggleGroup
group: primitives / Toggles
Joined set of toggle buttons (default, outline or segmented look) with single or multiple selection and roving keyboard focus.

Use `ToggleGroup` with `ToggleGroupItem` children for segmented choices (alignment, view mode, text formatting). `type="single"` keeps one value (string, pressing the active item clears it); `type="multiple"` keeps an array. `variant` and `size` are provided to every item (items can override). Unknown `variant`/`size` values fall back to `default`/`md`. For a required single choice with radio semantics prefer `RadioGroup`/`Tabs`.

**Variants**: `default` (flat joined buttons; toolbars and formatting), `outline` (bordered joined buttons; filters, alignment) and `segmented` (separate rounded items sitting on a muted track, the active one raised; view switchers like List/Grid or Day/Week/Month, best with `fullWidth`). **Sizes**: `xs` (28px) to `xl` (44px). `fullWidth` stretches the group and shares the width between items.

**Shape** (`shape`): `rounded` (default), `pill` (fully rounded ends or segments) and `square`. **Tone** (`tone`): the colour of the pressed item. `neutral` (default) keeps the accent fill; `primary`, `success`, `danger` and `info` use a solid status fill with its foreground colour. **Gap** (`gap`): `none` (default) joins the items; `sm` (4px) and `md` (8px) turn them into separate buttons. All three can be combined with every `variant`, `size` and `orientation`; items may override `shape` and `tone`. Unknown values fall back to the defaults.

import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- type: 'single' | 'multiple' = 'single' - Selection mode. Value is string (single) or string[] (multiple).
- modelValue: string | string[] - Selected value(s) (v-model). Leave undefined for uncontrolled use.
- defaultValue: string | string[] - Initial value(s) when uncontrolled.
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'segmented' = 'default' - Look shared by all items. segmented puts separate rounded items on a muted track. Unknown values fall back to default.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Size shared by all items: 28px, 32px, 36px, 40px, 44px tall. Unknown values fall back to md.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corner shape shared by all items: rounded-md, fully rounded (pill) or no rounding. Pill and square also change the segmented track. Unknown values fall back to rounded.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'neutral' - Colour of the pressed item. neutral is the accent fill; the others are solid status fills (primary, success, destructive, info) with their foreground colour. Unknown values fall back to neutral.
- gap: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' = 'none' - Space between items. none joins them into one control; sm (4px) and md (8px) render separate buttons, each with its own corners and border. Unknown values fall back to none.
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - Layout and arrow-key direction.
- fullWidth: boolean = false - Stretch the group to its container (w-full) and let horizontal items share the width equally.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables every item.
- loop: boolean = true - Wrap keyboard focus from last to first item.
- dir: 'ltr' | 'rtl' - Reading direction for keyboard navigation.
- as: string | Component - Root element (default div).
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the group root.

Parts:
- ToggleGroupItem - One toggle inside the group. Inherits variant/size/orientation from the group. Renders a button with aria-pressed and data-state="on|off".
    - value: string - Value reported to the group v-model when pressed.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disables this item.
    - variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'segmented' - Overrides the group variant.
    - size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' - Overrides the group size.
    - shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' - Overrides the group shape.
    - tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'info' - Overrides the group pressed-state colour.
    - as: string | Component = 'button' - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - ToggleGroupItem children.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string | string[] | undefined] - Fired when the selection changes. undefined when a single group is cleared.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a ToggleGroup has neither `aria-label` nor `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a ToggleGroupItem has no accessible name (an icon-only item needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when a ToggleGroupItem `value` is blank or used by another item of the same group.

Rules:
- single mode v-model is string | undefined; multiple mode is string[].
- Use `tone` only to colour the pressed item (success = on, danger = destructive filter); do not use it as the only signal of a state.
- Use `gap="sm"|"md"` for separate chips; keep `gap="none"` for one joined control.
- Set variant/size on the group, not per item, unless one item must differ.
- Use variant="segmented" (usually with full-width) for view/range switchers; "outline" for bordered button rows; "default" for toolbars.
- Always label the group (aria-label) and every icon-only item.
- ToggleGroupItem must be a descendant of ToggleGroup.

Accessibility:
- Group has role="group": label it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
- Items are buttons with aria-pressed; roving tabindex gives a single tab stop and arrow keys move between items (Home/End supported, `loop` wraps).
- Icon-only items need aria-label.
- Single groups behave as toggle buttons (aria-pressed), not radios: Arrow keys move focus, Space/Enter press the focused item. Use RadioGroup when exactly one choice is required.
- A toned fill (primary, success, danger, info) uses the status colour with its foreground token, so the label stays readable; in forced-colors mode the pressed item also gets a 2px border, because background colours are replaced there. Tone never replaces `aria-pressed`.
- Shape and gap change corners and spacing only. Joined groups round their outer corners with logical properties, so they mirror in right-to-left layouts.
- Items are 28px to 44px high (at least 24px at every size) and grow on coarse pointers; the pressed fill is paired with aria-pressed so state is not colour only.
- Responsive: the group is `inline-flex`; use `full-width` inside a `max-w-*` container so segments reflow at 320px.

# Markdown
group: typography / Prose
Renders Markdown text (CommonMark plus GFM tables, task lists and strikethrough) as styled, accessible elements without v-html.

Use `Markdown` for text you do not author element by element: README files, release notes, help text, user comments and LLM replies. The source is parsed by a small built-in parser into a tree and drawn with Vue render functions, so raw HTML in the source is shown as literal text and `v-html` is never involved. Use `Prose` when you already have trusted HTML to style, and `Heading`, `Text` and friends for hand-written pages.

Supported: ATX and setext headings, paragraphs, block quotes, ordered and bullet lists (nested, start numbers, tight and loose), task items, fenced and indented code, thematic breaks, GFM tables with alignment, link reference definitions, hard and soft breaks, emphasis, strong, strikethrough (`~~`), inline code, inline and reference links, `<url>` autolinks, bare http and https URLs, images, backslash escapes and character references (numeric plus a small named set). Not supported: raw HTML (shown as text), footnotes, math, emoji shortcodes, single-tilde strikethrough, `www.` autolinks.

Safety: link targets must be http, https, mailto, tel, a relative path or a `#fragment`; images may use http, https, relative paths and `data:image/png|jpeg|gif|webp` (never SVG). Anything else, including obfuscated `javascript:` variants, renders the label as plain text. `allowedProtocols` can only narrow the list. Input longer than `maxLength` renders as plain text and nesting beyond `maxDepth` stays literal.

Streaming: set `streaming` while text is still arriving. The whole source is parsed again on every change (the parser is linear time, a 200 KB document takes a few milliseconds), and in the last block unfinished emphasis, code spans, links, images and table rows are closed or hidden instead of showing raw syntax. Turn it off when the text is complete.

No existing app component was verified as replaced.

import { Markdown } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- source: string - Markdown text. When omitted, the text of the default slot is used (the Vue compiler collapses whitespace in slot text, so use `source` for multi-line documents).
- headingOffset: number = 0 - Added to every heading level, clamped to 0..5 (integers; invalid values count as 0). `3` renders `#` as h4. Levels above 6 clamp at h6.
- headingIds: boolean = true - Give headings stable, unique slug ids (`-1`, `-2` suffix on duplicates, `section` for empty headings).
- headingAnchors: boolean = false - Add a keyboard-focusable link named "Link to this section" beside each heading. Needs `headingIds`.
- idPrefix: string = '' - Prefix for heading ids (`doc` gives `doc-install`). Use it when several documents share one page.
- linkTarget: '_self' | '_blank' - Target for internal links. Only `_blank` sets the attribute.
- externalTarget: '_self' | '_blank' - Target for external (absolute http/https or protocol-relative) links. `_blank` adds `target`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a screen-reader-only "(opens in a new tab)". External links always get `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- baseUrl: string - Resolves relative link and image URLs. Fragments and absolute URLs are left alone. The result is checked again.
- allowedProtocols: string[] - Narrows the allowed schemes (subset of `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel`; images also `data`). Names outside the built-in list are ignored. An empty array allows only relative URLs and fragments.
- highlight: boolean = true - Use CodeViewer for fences tagged json, yaml/yml, go/golang, toml, shell/sh/bash/zsh or plain/text. Other languages, and everything when false, render a plain labelled region.
- codeFold: boolean = false - Show line numbers and fold toggles in highlighted code.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Body text 14px, 16px or 18px; headings scale with it.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' = 'default' - `muted` uses the muted foreground colour for body text.
- inline: boolean = false - Parse and render only inline syntax inside a `span`: no paragraphs, headings or lists. For one-line UI strings.
- streaming: boolean = false - The text is still arriving. Closes or hides unfinished syntax in the last block, hides a table header until its delimiter row exists, and sets `aria-busy`.
- components: MarkdownComponents - Custom renderers by node type: `link` (props href, title, external, target, rel; label as default slot), `image` (src, alt, title) and `code` (code, language, info, filename, closed). Each is a component or an element name and only receives checked values.
- maxDepth: number = 32 - Maximum nesting of block quotes, lists and inline emphasis (clamped to 1..100). Deeper markers stay literal text.
- maxLength: number = 1000000 - Longer sources render as one unformatted plain-text paragraph.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge. The default measure is `max-w-prose`; override it with e.g. `max-w-none`.

Slots:
- default - Markdown text used when `source` is not set. Only text nodes count; elements are ignored.

Events:
- headings [headings: { level: number; text: string; id: string }[]] - The heading outline when it first renders and whenever it changes (text, ids, or levels after `headingOffset`). Feed it to TableOfContents.

Rules:
- Render LLM-written or user-written Markdown with Markdown, never with v-html or a separate parser.
- Pass the text as `source`; slot text is whitespace-collapsed by the Vue compiler.
- Set headingOffset so the page keeps one h1: `:heading-offset="1"` makes # an h2.
- Set `streaming` while a reply is arriving and remove it when the reply is complete.
- Wire a table of contents with `@headings` and TableOfContents `items` (`{ id, label: text, level }`).
- Use `inline` for one-line UI strings; it never renders block elements.
- Do not widen `allowedProtocols`; it only narrows. Put custom link or image components in `components`, they receive already-checked URLs.
- Raw HTML, footnotes, math and emoji shortcodes are not supported; tell users to write plain Markdown.
- Give each document on a page distinct heading text or an idPrefix so ids and region names stay unique.

Accessibility:
- Renders native elements only: h1 to h6, p, ul/ol/li, blockquote, table with th scope="col", figure/figcaption, hr, a, img, code and pre. No ARIA roles are added to prose.
- Headings keep their order; use headingOffset so the page has one h1. Heading ids are stable and unique, and headingAnchors adds a real link named "Link to this section" that is reached with Tab.
- Tables and code blocks that can overflow are scroll regions (role="region", tabindex="0") named by the nearest heading, the file name or the language, with a number added when a name repeats so landmark names stay unique. Scroll them with the arrow keys once focused.
- Task list items are disabled native checkboxes whose accessible name is the item text and whose state is the checked attribute. They are display only.
- Links are underlined, show a focus ring that survives forced-colors mode, and wrap long URLs. A link that opens a new tab says so to screen readers.
- Images always carry alt (empty only when the markdown alt is empty), load lazily and never exceed the container width. A sole image with a title becomes a figure with a caption.
- While streaming the root has aria-busy="true"; there is no live region, so screen readers read the finished text. Reflows at 320px: text wraps and only tables and code scroll, inside their own regions.

Example: Streaming simulation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const pieces = text.match(/[\s\S]{1,14}/g) ?? []
const shown = ref('')
const count = ref(0)
function next() {
  if (count.value < pieces.length) shown.value += pieces[count.value++]
}
function reset() {
  shown.value = ''
  count.value = 0
}
</script>

<div class="space-y-4">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" :disabled="count >= total" @click="next">Receive next chunk</Button>
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" :disabled="count === 0" @click="reset">Start over</Button>
    <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground" role="status">Chunk {{ count }} of {{ total }}</span>
  </div>
  <Markdown :source="shown" :heading-offset="3" :streaming="count < total" />
</div>
```

# Prose
group: typography / Prose
Wrapper that styles raw HTML content (headings, lists, links, code, tables, images) with design tokens.

Use `Prose` around content you do not control element-by-element: rendered Markdown, CMS HTML or long-form articles. Styles apply to descendants via Tailwind arbitrary variants, so it works without any plugin. Set `measure` for a readable line length (`max-w-prose`, 65ch). For individual, hand-authored elements prefer `Heading`, `Text` and friends.

Sizes: `xs` 13px (dense help panels), `sm` 14px (app UI), `base`/`md` 16px (default reading size), `lg` 18px (articles), `xl` 20px (landing copy). Tones: `default` follows the page; `inverted` swaps foreground and background tokens for a high-contrast block in either theme; `dark` forces the dark palette for the block regardless of page theme. Both non-default tones add a padded rounded surface (override with `class`, e.g. `p-0`).

Density sets the vertical rhythm: `compact` (tight margins for help panels and changelogs), `default`, `relaxed` (generous margins and `leading-relaxed` for long-form reading). Density overrides descendant margins through tailwind-merge, so use `Prose` (or wrap `proseVariants` in `cn()`).

import { Prose } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'base' - Base font size: xs text-sm (13px), sm text-base (14px), base and md text-md (16px), lg text-lg, xl text-xl.
- tone: 'default' | 'inverted' | 'dark' = 'default' - `inverted` = bg-foreground/text-background surface with re-coloured links, code, tables and rules; `dark` = forced dark palette (`dark` class) on a bordered surface. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- density: 'compact' | 'default' | 'relaxed' = 'default' - Vertical rhythm. `compact`: smaller heading, paragraph, list, code, table and media margins. `relaxed`: larger margins plus `leading-relaxed`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- measure: boolean = false - Limit width to max-w-prose (65ch).
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render (`article`, `section`...).
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child instead of rendering a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes. Override a descendant rule with e.g. `[&_h1]:text-2xl`.

Slots:
- default - Raw HTML or markup to style.

Rules:
- Start headings inside Prose one level below the page outline (no jumps).
- Wrap rendered Markdown/CMS HTML in Prose; do not use it around Vue components that already style themselves.
- Use `measure` for long-form reading.
- Use `tone="inverted"` or `tone="dark"` for a contrasting block; they add padding and a radius, remove with `class="p-0 rounded-none"`.
- `size="md"` equals `base`.
- Use `density="compact"` for help panels and changelogs, `density="relaxed"` for long articles.
- Override a descendant with `class="[&_h2]:text-2xl"`.

Accessibility:
- Does not change semantics; the underlying HTML structure is what assistive tech sees.
- Link colour relies on underline as well as colour.
- Rendered `pre` blocks that overflow get `tabindex="0"` automatically (and a focus ring) so keyboard users can scroll them; the attribute is removed again when they stop overflowing. Elements that already have a `tabindex` are left alone.
- Lists and quotes use logical properties (`ps`, `border-s`) and table headers use `text-start`, so right-to-left content mirrors.
- `inverted` and `dark` use token pairs (foreground/background) so contrast follows the theme.
- `density` only changes margins and line height (WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing stays user-adjustable); `compact` never shrinks the font size.

Example: Article
```vue
<Prose as="article" measure>
  <h4>Sample article</h4>
  <p>Install the package and import the <code>theme.css</code> file. See the <a href="/guides/getting-started">guide</a> for details.</p>
  <h5>Steps</h5>
  <ol><li>Install</li><li>Import the theme</li><li>Add <strong>@source</strong></li></ol>
  <blockquote>Sample quotation text.</blockquote>
  <pre><code>pnpm add @perfect-design/ui</code></pre>
</Prose>
```

Example: Density
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <Prose density="compact"><h4>Compact</h4><p>Sample paragraph one.</p><p>Sample paragraph two.</p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li></ul></Prose>
  <Prose><h4>Default</h4><p>Sample paragraph one.</p><p>Sample paragraph two.</p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li></ul></Prose>
  <Prose density="relaxed"><h4>Relaxed</h4><p>Sample paragraph one.</p><p>Sample paragraph two.</p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li></ul></Prose>
</div>
```

Example: Table and list, large size
```vue
<Prose size="lg">
  <h4>Sizes</h4>
  <ul><li>Small</li><li>Base<ul><li>Default</li></ul></li><li>Large</li></ul>
  <table>
    <thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Size</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody><tr><td>sm</td><td>14px</td></tr><tr><td>base</td><td>16px</td></tr></tbody>
  </table>
  <hr />
  <p>Sample closing paragraph.</p>
</Prose>
```

Example: Size: xs and sm
```vue
<div class="space-y-6">
  <Prose size="xs"><p>Extra small (13px): terse help text with a <a href="/guides/getting-started">link</a>.</p></Prose>
  <Prose size="sm"><p>Small (14px): matches the dense app UI scale.</p></Prose>
</div>
```

Example: Size: md and xl
```vue
<div class="space-y-6">
  <Prose size="md"><p>Medium (16px): the default reading size.</p></Prose>
  <Prose size="xl"><p>Extra large (20px): intro copy.</p></Prose>
</div>
```

Example: Tone: inverted
```vue
<Prose tone="inverted">
  <h4>Sample notes</h4>
  <p>See the <a href="/guides/getting-started">changelog</a> and run <code>pnpm up</code>.</p>
  <ul><li>Sample item</li><li>Another item</li></ul>
  <pre><code>pnpm add @perfect-design/ui</code></pre>
  <table>
    <thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody><tr><td>tone</td><td>inverted</td></tr></tbody>
  </table>
</Prose>
```

Example: Tone: dark
```vue
<Prose tone="dark" size="sm">
  <h4>Always dark</h4>
  <p>Uses the dark tokens: <a href="/guides/getting-started">links</a>, <code>code</code> and <strong>emphasis</strong>.</p>
  <blockquote>Sample quotation text.</blockquote>
</Prose>
```

# Blockquote
group: typography / Text
Quoted passage in five variants (left border, tinted, card, pull-quote) with a citation footer or an author row (avatar, name, role).

Use `Blockquote` for quotations. Pass `citation` (or the `citation` slot for rich markup) to show an attribution footer, and `cite` for the machine-readable source URL. Not for generic callouts (use an Alert).

Variants: `default` and `primary` (inline-start border, neutral or primary) for quotes inside articles; `tinted` (soft surface with a hairline border) for emphasised excerpts; `card` for quotes in grids; `pull` (large display type, combine with `align="center"`) for pull-quotes. Attribution: `citation` renders a plain muted footer; `author` / `role` / `avatar` (or their slots) render an author row and take precedence over `citation`. Only quote real, attributed text.

import { Blockquote } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'primary' | 'tinted' | 'card' | 'pull' = 'default' - Visual style. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'base' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' - Text size of the quote. Not set by default (inherits; `pull` is 2xl). Wins over the variant size.
- align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - Centres the quote and the author row.
- citation: string - Attribution text shown in a muted footer. Overridden by the `citation` slot; ignored when an author row is rendered.
- author: string - Author name; renders the author row. Overridden by the `author` slot.
- authorRole: string - The author's job title or company, under the author name. Overridden by the `role` slot.
- role: string - Deprecated: use `authorRole`. Still shown when `authorRole` is not set, and logs one development warning per instance.
- avatar: string - Avatar image URL (decorative, `alt=""`). Use the `avatar` slot for an `Avatar` component.
- cite: string - Source URL, rendered as the native `cite` attribute.
- as: string | Component = 'blockquote' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child; no footer is rendered.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - The quoted text.
- citation - Attribution content; overrides the `citation` prop.
- author - Author name; overrides the `author` prop.
- role - Author role; overrides the `role` prop.
- avatar - Avatar element (e.g. `<Avatar>`); overrides the `avatar` URL.

Rules:
- The author avatar image blur when a surrounding `ConfigProvider` sets `blurMedia` (privacy, not decoration); there is no prop on this component.
- Put the quote in the default slot and the author in `citation`.
- Use `cite` only for a real URL.
- Use `author` (+ `authorRole`, `avatar`; `role` is a deprecated alias) for attributed quotes, `citation` for plain sources; do not pass both.
- Only use real quotes with a real source. Never invent a quote, person or company.
- Use `variant="pull"` for at most one highlighted quote per section.

Accessibility:
- Native <blockquote> element; the `cite` attribute is not announced, so show the attribution visibly via `citation` or `author`.
- The avatar image is decorative (`alt=""`) because the author name is rendered as text next to it.
- Borders use logical properties (`border-s`, `ps`), so the quote rule flips in right-to-left layouts.
- Text wraps and reflows at 320px; no fixed widths.

Example: Basic
```vue
<Blockquote>Sample quotation text.</Blockquote>
```

Example: With citation
```vue
<div class="space-y-6">
  <Blockquote citation="Sample source" cite="https://example.com/source">Sample quotation text with a machine-readable source.</Blockquote>
  <Blockquote variant="primary">
    Sample quotation text in the primary colour.
    <template #citation><cite>Sample publication</cite>, sample date</template>
  </Blockquote>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: tinted
```vue
<Blockquote variant="tinted" citation="Sample source">Sample excerpt that deserves emphasis.</Blockquote>
```

Example: Variant: card with author row
```vue
<Blockquote variant="card" author="Sample author" author-role="Sample role">
  Sample quotation text inside a card.
</Blockquote>
```

Example: Variant: pull-quote
```vue
<Blockquote variant="pull" align="center" author="Sample author" author-role="Sample role">
  Sample pull-quote text in display size.
</Blockquote>
```

Example: Size
```vue
<div class="space-y-4">
  <Blockquote size="sm">Small quote.</Blockquote>
  <Blockquote size="xl" variant="primary">Extra large quote.</Blockquote>
</div>
```

Example: Author row with slots
```vue
<Blockquote variant="tinted">
  Sample quotation text with a slotted author row.
  <template #avatar><Avatar name="Sample author" /></template>
  <template #author>Sample author</template>
  <template #role>Sample role, <a class="underline" href="/guides/getting-started">sample link</a></template>
</Blockquote>
```

# Eyebrow
group: typography / Text
Small plain label placed above a heading.

Use `Eyebrow` only when the label adds information the heading lacks, such as the product area or document type above a title. If the label repeats the heading, leave it out. It renders normal-case text (a `p` by default); use `as="span"` inline. Not a replacement for a form label.

Variations:

- `variant`: `plain` (default, text only), `rule` (a hairline after the text that fills the row, for section labels in a wide column) or `dot` (a small dot before the text, for a status-style label). The rule and dot are decorative and hidden from assistive technology; they are not rendered with `asChild`.
- `size`: `xs`, `sm` (default), `md`.
- `tone`: `primary` (default), `muted`, `foreground`.

Never tracked or all-caps: sentence case only.

import { Eyebrow } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'plain' | 'rule' | 'dot' = 'plain' - `plain`: text only. `rule`: flex row with a decorative hairline (`bg-border`, `bg-current` in forced-colors mode) after the label. `dot`: decorative dot before the label in the text colour. Not rendered with `asChild`. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' = 'sm' - Text size: xs text-xs, sm text-sm, md text-base. Unknown values fall back to `sm`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'muted' | 'foreground' = 'primary' - Text colour: primary, muted-foreground or foreground. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- as: string | Component = 'p' - Element to render (`span`, `div`...).
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child instead of rendering a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Label text.

Rules:
- Use only when it adds information the heading lacks; otherwise omit it.
- Place directly above a Heading and keep it to a few words.
- Do not add uppercase or letter-spacing classes.
- Use `variant="rule"` only above a heading in a wide column; use `variant="dot"` for short status-style labels.

Accessibility:
- Plain text in a paragraph; no role. Keep it short so the heading stays the main landmark for navigation.
- Primary, muted and foreground tones use token pairs tested for AA contrast on the page background and cards.
- The `rule` and `dot` decorations are `aria-hidden` spans: the label text carries the meaning, so a dot never stands in for a status word. The rule falls back to the text colour in forced-colors mode and keeps a minimum length, so a long label wraps instead of overflowing at 320px.

Example: Above a heading
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Eyebrow>Component reference</Eyebrow>
  <Heading :level="4" size="2xl">Eyebrow</Heading>
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="max-w-md space-y-4">
  <Eyebrow>Plain label</Eyebrow>
  <Eyebrow variant="rule">Section label with a rule</Eyebrow>
  <Eyebrow variant="dot" tone="muted">Label with a dot</Eyebrow>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and tones
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Eyebrow size="xs">Extra small, primary</Eyebrow>
  <Eyebrow size="sm" tone="muted">Small, muted</Eyebrow>
  <Eyebrow size="md" tone="foreground">Medium, foreground</Eyebrow>
  <Eyebrow variant="rule" size="md" tone="foreground">Medium with a rule</Eyebrow>
</div>
```

Example: Tones and inline use
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Eyebrow tone="muted">Typography</Eyebrow>
  <Eyebrow as="span">Plain label</Eyebrow>
  <div class="flex items-center gap-2"><Badge>Stable</Badge><Eyebrow as="span" tone="muted">Added in the first release</Eyebrow></div>
</div>
```

# FormattedNumber
group: typography / Text
A locale-aware number, percentage, currency amount, unit or compact figure rendered with Intl.NumberFormat, with tabular figures and bidi isolation.

Use `FormattedNumber` wherever a figure is shown to people: prices, deltas, counts, durations, table cells. It wraps `Intl.NumberFormat`, accepts numbers, bigints and numeric strings (formatted exactly, no float rounding), and never throws on bad input.

The number-format "style" is the prop `format` (`decimal`, `percent`, `currency`, `unit`, `compact`), not `style`: in Vue `style` is the inline-style attribute, and a static `style="percent"` is compiled into an empty style object before the component sees it. A dynamic `:style="'percent'"` string that names one of the five formats is still accepted as an alias (for code written against the Intl option name), but write `format`. `format="compact"` is decimal style with compact notation ("1.2K"); an explicit `notation` wins over it.

`locale` defaults to `en`, not the browser locale, so server and client render identical text; pass the app locale explicitly. Safe fallbacks (nothing throws): a value that is NaN, Infinity, blank or non-numeric renders `fallback` (default `n/a`); `format="currency"` without a valid `currency`, or `format="unit"` without `unit`, renders plain decimal (and throws a ContractError in strict mode, see `requires`); a malformed `currency` code renders plain decimal; an unknown `unit` renders the plain number followed by the unit text; a malformed `locale` falls back to `en`; fraction digits are clamped to 0 to 20 and `maximumFractionDigits` is raised to `minimumFractionDigits` when smaller. `-0` is shown as `0`. A small negative that rounds to zero ("-0") needs `signDisplay="negative"`.

`tone="positive"`, `"negative"` and `"auto"` (from the sign of the value) add colour AND a visible sign (`signDisplay` defaults to `exceptZero` for them), so colour is never the only signal. Use `formatNumber(value, options)` (exported next to the component) for plain strings such as chart labels or `aria-label`s.

import { FormattedNumber } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- value*: number | bigint | string - The figure. Numeric strings (`"1234.5"`, `"1e3"`) and bigints are formatted exactly. NaN, Infinity, blank and non-numeric values render `fallback`.
- format: 'decimal' | 'percent' | 'currency' | 'unit' | 'compact' = 'decimal' - Number-format style (the Intl `style` option; named `format` because `style` is the Vue inline-style attribute). `percent` multiplies by 100 (0.25 is 25%). `currency` needs `currency`, `unit` needs `unit`. `compact` is decimal with compact notation. Unknown values fall back to `decimal`.
- currency: string - ISO 4217 code such as `EUR` (any case). Required for `format="currency"`. A malformed code renders plain decimal.
- unit: string - Intl sanctioned unit such as `kilometer`, `liter`, `kilometer-per-hour`. Required for `format="unit"`. An unknown unit renders the number then the unit text.
- notation: 'standard' | 'compact' | 'scientific' | 'engineering' - Notation. Defaults to `compact` for `format="compact"`, else `standard`. Unknown values are ignored.
- minimumFractionDigits: number - Fewest fraction digits, 0 to 20 (clamped).
- maximumFractionDigits: number - Most fraction digits, 0 to 20 (clamped); raised to `minimumFractionDigits` when smaller.
- signDisplay: 'auto' | 'always' | 'never' | 'exceptZero' | 'negative' - When to show a sign. Defaults to `auto`, or `exceptZero` for the tones `positive`, `negative` and `auto` so the sign backs up the colour.
- locale: string = 'en' - BCP 47 tag (`de-DE`, `ar-EG`). Malformed tags fall back to `en`. Never defaults to the runtime locale, so SSR and hydration agree.
- fallback: string = 'n/a' - Text for an invalid value. Sets `data-invalid="true"` on the root.
- tabular: boolean = true - Equal-width figures (`tabular-nums`) so numbers in a column line up.
- isolate: boolean = true - Wrap the text in a `<bdi>` so a number or its sign never reorders inside right-to-left or mixed-direction text.
- variant: 'plain' | 'mono' | 'outline' = 'plain' - `plain` inherits the font, `mono` uses the monospace font, `outline` draws a hairline box. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- size: 'inherit' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' = 'inherit' - Font size; `inherit` keeps the surrounding size. Unknown values fall back to `inherit`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'positive' | 'negative' | 'auto' = 'default' - `muted` secondary colour. `positive` (success) and `negative` (destructive) colour the text and show a sign. `auto` picks positive, negative or default from the sign of the value. An invalid value never gets a status colour.
- weight: 'normal' | 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold' - Font weight. Unset inherits.
- as: string = 'span' - Root element tag (`span`, `strong`, `div`, `td`...).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `format` is 'currency' and `currency` is missing or blank (the value would otherwise render as a bare number).
- Throws a ContractError when `format` is 'unit' and `unit` is missing or blank.

Rules:
- The number-format style prop is `format`, never `style` (a static `style="percent"` is compiled to an empty style object).
- Always pass `currency` with `format="currency"` and `unit` with `format="unit"`.
- `format="percent"` expects a ratio: 0.25 renders 25%. Pass 25 and you get 2,500%.
- Pass `locale` from app state; the default is `en`, not the browser locale.
- Use `tone="auto"` or `tone="positive"` for deltas, not a hand-written `text-green-*` class; the sign is added for you.
- Use `formatNumber(value, options)` for strings (chart labels, `aria-label`). It takes the same options with `style` instead of `format`, and returns `fallback` for invalid input.
- Do not format a number yourself with `toLocaleString` in templates: server and browser locales differ and cause hydration mismatches.

Accessibility:
- Renders plain text, so screen readers read the formatted string. Prefer a locale that matches the page language.
- Tone is never the only signal: `positive`, `negative` and `auto` also show a sign (`signDisplay` defaults to `exceptZero` for them). Do not set `signDisplay="never"` with a status tone.
- The invalid fallback text ("n/a" by default) is read as written; use a more specific `fallback` such as "No data" where it helps.
- The `<bdi>` wrapper keeps numbers and signs in order in right-to-left and mixed text. Digits follow the locale (`ar-EG` uses Arabic-Indic digits).
- Tabular figures change width only, not meaning. Colours use `text-success`, `text-destructive` and `text-muted-foreground`, covered by the contrast tests; forced-colors mode keeps the sign and the outline variant border.

Example: Formats
```vue
<dl class="grid grid-cols-[max-content_auto] gap-x-4 gap-y-1">
  <dt>Decimal</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="1234567.891" /></dd>
  <dt>Percent</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="0.256" format="percent" :maximum-fraction-digits="1" /></dd>
  <dt>Currency</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="1499.5" format="currency" currency="EUR" /></dd>
  <dt>Unit</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="42.5" format="unit" unit="kilometer-per-hour" /></dd>
  <dt>Compact</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="1234567" format="compact" /></dd>
</dl>
```

Example: Locales
```vue
<dl class="grid grid-cols-[max-content_auto] gap-x-4 gap-y-1">
  <dt>de-DE</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="1234567.891" locale="de-DE" format="currency" currency="EUR" /></dd>
  <dt>ja-JP</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="1234567" locale="ja-JP" format="currency" currency="JPY" /></dd>
  <dt>fr-FR</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="0.075" locale="fr-FR" format="percent" :maximum-fraction-digits="1" /></dd>
  <dt>ar-EG</dt><dd dir="rtl"><FormattedNumber :value="-1234.5" locale="ar-EG" /></dd>
</dl>
```

Example: Notation and fraction digits
```vue
<dl class="grid grid-cols-[max-content_auto] gap-x-4 gap-y-1">
  <dt>Compact</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="1500000" notation="compact" :maximum-fraction-digits="1" /></dd>
  <dt>Scientific</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="123456" notation="scientific" /></dd>
  <dt>Engineering</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="123456" notation="engineering" /></dd>
  <dt>Fixed 2 digits</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="3" :minimum-fraction-digits="2" /></dd>
  <dt>Rounded</dt><dd><FormattedNumber :value="3.14159" :maximum-fraction-digits="0" /></dd>
</dl>
```

Example: Deltas with sign and tone
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
  <FormattedNumber :value="0.124" format="percent" tone="auto" :maximum-fraction-digits="1" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="-0.087" format="percent" tone="auto" :maximum-fraction-digits="1" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="0" format="percent" tone="auto" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="42" sign-display="always" tone="muted" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="-42" sign-display="never" />
</div>
```

Example: Variants, sizes and weight
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-4">
  <FormattedNumber :value="2048" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="2048" variant="mono" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="2048" variant="outline" size="sm" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="2048" size="2xl" weight="semibold" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="2048" size="xs" tone="muted" />
</div>
```

Example: Bigint and numeric strings
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-1">
  <FormattedNumber value="12345678901234567890" />
  <FormattedNumber value="12345678901234567890" format="compact" />
  <FormattedNumber value="1e6" />
</div>
```

Example: Invalid values and fallback
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
  <FormattedNumber :value="NaN" />
  <FormattedNumber value="" />
  <FormattedNumber value="12 apples" fallback="No data" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="1" format="currency" currency="not-a-code" />
  <FormattedNumber :value="7" format="unit" unit="parsec" />
</div>
```

Example: Right-to-left page
```vue
<p dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <span>الرصيد:</span>
  <FormattedNumber :value="-1234.5" locale="ar" format="currency" currency="USD" />
</p>
```

# Heading
group: typography / Text
Semantic h1-h6 heading with independent visual size, underline/divider decoration and optional eyebrow and description.

Use `Heading` for every title. `level` decides the semantic element (h1-h6, invalid values fall back to 2) and drives the default visual size; `size` overrides the look without changing the document outline. Use `as` only when the element must not be a heading tag. Do not use for body copy (use `Text`).

Variants: `default` for ordinary titles; `underline` for a short accent bar under section titles; `divider` for a full-width rule under a title that opens a section. Alignment: `align` left/center/right. Eyebrow + description: pass `eyebrow` and/or `description` (or the same-named slots) and the heading is wrapped in a `heading-group` block (eyebrow above, paragraph below); `class` and attributes still go to the heading element itself, `groupClass` to the wrapper. Use that for page and section headers.

import { Heading } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | '1'..'6' = 2 - Semantic level. Renders h1-h6. Invalid values fall back to 2.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' | '4xl' | '5xl' | '6xl' = by level (1: 4xl, 2: 3xl, 3: 2xl, 4: xl, 5: lg, 6: md) - Visual size, independent of level. Unknown values fall back to the level default.
- weight: 'normal' | 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold' = 'semibold' - Font weight.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'default' - Text colour. `default` inherits.
- variant: 'default' | 'underline' | 'divider' = 'default' - Decoration. `underline` adds a short accent bar (override with `after:bg-*`), `divider` adds a full-width bottom border. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' - Text alignment. With an eyebrow/description it aligns the whole group and keeps the underline bar aligned. Not set by default.
- eyebrow: string - Small plain label above the heading (use only when it adds information the heading lacks); wraps the heading in a `heading-group`. The `eyebrow` slot overrides it.
- eyebrowTone: 'primary' | 'muted' = 'primary' - Colour of the eyebrow.
- description: string - Muted supporting paragraph below the heading; wraps it in a `heading-group`. Size scales with the heading size. The `description` slot overrides it.
- groupClass: string | object | array - Classes for the `heading-group` wrapper (only rendered with an eyebrow/description). Merged last, e.g. `gap-4`.
- balance: boolean = false - Applies text-wrap: balance for even line lengths.
- as: string | Component - Element to render instead of h1-h6; styling is kept.
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child instead of rendering a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Heading content.
- eyebrow - Eyebrow content (overrides the `eyebrow` prop).
- description - Description content (overrides the `description` prop); may contain links or inline markup.

Rules:
- Choose `level` for document structure, `size` for looks.
- One h1 per page.
- Do not set font sizes with raw classes; use `size`.
- Use `description` instead of stacking Heading + Text by hand.
- Use `eyebrow` only when it adds information the heading lacks.

Accessibility:
- Renders real h1-h6 elements; keep one h1 per page and do not skip levels.
- Use `size` rather than a different `level` to change appearance.
- The eyebrow and description are separate elements (p) next to the heading, so the heading text itself stays the accessible name.
- Heading text always uses solid token colours; `tone="warning"` switches to the dark warning ink in light mode so it stays AA.
- In examples and pages, start nested headings one level below the surrounding section so the outline never jumps (h2 then h3, not h2 then h4).

Example: Levels
```vue
<div class="space-y-3">
  <Heading :level="1">Heading 1</Heading>
  <Heading :level="2">Heading 2</Heading>
  <Heading :level="3">Heading 3</Heading>
  <Heading :level="4">Heading 4</Heading>
  <Heading :level="5">Heading 5</Heading>
  <Heading :level="6">Heading 6</Heading>
</div>
```

Example: Semantic level vs visual size
```vue
<div class="space-y-3">
  <Heading :level="4" size="xl" tone="muted">Quiet title</Heading>
  <Heading :level="5" size="5xl" weight="bold" balance>Balanced display statement that wraps evenly</Heading>
  <Heading as="div" size="lg" tone="primary">Not a heading element</Heading>
</div>
```

Example: Underline accent
```vue
<div class="space-y-6">
  <Heading variant="underline">Section title</Heading>
  <Heading variant="underline" align="center" class="after:bg-success">Centered title</Heading>
</div>
```

Example: Divider
```vue
<Heading :level="4" variant="divider">Sample section</Heading>
```

Example: Alignment
```vue
<div class="space-y-3">
  <Heading align="left">Left</Heading>
  <Heading align="center">Center</Heading>
  <Heading align="right">Right</Heading>
</div>
```

Example: Eyebrow and description
```vue
<Heading :level="4" size="4xl" eyebrow="Typography" description="Eyebrow above, description below, both optional.">
  Sample heading
</Heading>
```

Example: Centered header with slots
```vue
<Heading :level="4" size="5xl" align="center" eyebrow-tone="muted" group-class="gap-4">
  <template #eyebrow>Sample label</template>
  Sample centered heading
  <template #description>Sample description with a <a class="underline" href="/guides/getting-started">sample link</a>.</template>
</Heading>
```

# InlineCode
group: typography / Text
Inline <code> snippet with a muted background and monospace font.

Use `InlineCode` for short identifiers, commands and file names inside running text. Font size is `text-sm`; use `size` or a `text-*` class to change it. For multi-line code use a code block component, not this.

Variations: `variant` `default` (muted chip), `outline` (hairline border, no fill), `plain` (monospace text only); `size` `xs`, `sm` (default), `md`, `lg`; `tone` `neutral` (default) or `primary`, `success`, `danger`, `info`, which tints the chip, colours the outline or colours the text depending on `variant`. Tinted pairs are the tested status token pairs. When using `inlineCodeVariants` outside the component, wrap the result in `cn()` so tailwind-merge drops the overridden neutral fill.

import { InlineCode } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'plain' = 'default' - `default`: bg-muted chip. `outline`: hairline border, transparent fill. `plain`: monospace text with no chip or padding. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'sm' - Font size: xs text-xs, sm text-sm, md text-base, lg text-md. Unknown values fall back to `sm`.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'neutral' - Status colour. `default`: tinted chip (`bg-X/10 text-X`). `outline`: coloured border and text. `plain`: coloured text. Unknown values fall back to `neutral`.
- as: string | Component = 'code' - Element to render (e.g. `kbd`).
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child instead of rendering a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Code text.

Rules:
- Inline only; never wrap multi-line blocks.
- Keep it to short identifiers; long strings wrap with `break-words` instead of overflowing.
- Use `tone` only to mark a status or role, with the meaning also in the surrounding text.

Accessibility:
- Uses the native <code> element, which conveys code semantics to assistive technology.
- Long identifiers wrap (`break-words`) instead of forcing horizontal scroll at 320px.
- Tone is never the only signal: write the status in the sentence (for example "returns 500"). The `outline` variant keeps a visible border in forced-colors mode; `default` relies on the system text colour there.

Example: In a sentence
```vue
<Text>Run <InlineCode>pnpm install</InlineCode> before starting the dev server.</Text>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<Text>Chip <InlineCode>--radius</InlineCode>, outline <InlineCode variant="outline">--radius</InlineCode> and plain <InlineCode variant="plain">--radius</InlineCode>.</Text>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Text>Extra small <InlineCode size="xs">pnpm test</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text>Small <InlineCode>pnpm test</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text>Medium <InlineCode size="md">pnpm test</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text>Large <InlineCode size="lg">pnpm test</InlineCode></Text>
</div>
```

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Text>Chip: <InlineCode tone="primary">primary</InlineCode> <InlineCode tone="success">200 OK</InlineCode> <InlineCode tone="danger">500</InlineCode> <InlineCode tone="info">204</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text>Outline: <InlineCode variant="outline" tone="primary">primary</InlineCode> <InlineCode variant="outline" tone="success">200 OK</InlineCode> <InlineCode variant="outline" tone="danger">500</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text>Plain: <InlineCode variant="plain" tone="primary">primary</InlineCode> <InlineCode variant="plain" tone="info">204</InlineCode></Text>
</div>
```

Example: In different text sizes
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Text size="xs">Small: <InlineCode>--radius</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text size="xl">Large: <InlineCode>--radius</InlineCode></Text>
  <Text>Keyboard: <InlineCode as="kbd">Ctrl</InlineCode> + <InlineCode as="kbd">K</InlineCode></Text>
</div>
```

# Lead
group: typography / Text
Large muted intro paragraph that follows a page or section title.

Use `Lead` once under a `Heading` to introduce a page or section. For regular paragraphs use `Text`.

Variations: `size` `md` (16px), `lg` (default, 18px), `xl` (20px); `tone` `muted` (default) or `foreground` for a lead that carries the argument and should read at full contrast; `align` `start` (default) or `center` (short display leads only).

import { Lead } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- size: 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'lg' - Font size: md text-md (16px), lg text-lg, xl text-xl. Unknown values fall back to `lg`.
- tone: 'muted' | 'foreground' = 'muted' - Text colour: muted-foreground or foreground. Unknown values fall back to `muted`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - Text alignment: `center` adds text-center. Unknown values fall back to `start`.
- as: string | Component = 'p' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child instead of rendering a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Intro text.

Rules:
- One Lead per page or section.
- Use `tone="foreground"` instead of a colour class when the lead needs full contrast.
- Use `align="center"` only for short display leads, never for paragraphs.

Accessibility:
- Plain paragraph semantics; no special roles.
- Muted and foreground text use tested token pairs (AA contrast on the page background).
- Centred text is a visual choice only; keep centred leads to one or two lines.
- It wraps with `text-pretty` and has no fixed width, so it reflows at 320px and at 200% zoom.

Example: Under a heading
```vue
<div class="max-w-xl space-y-2">
  <Heading :level="4">Sample page title</Heading>
  <Lead>Sample introduction that explains what the page covers in one or two sentences.</Lead>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes, tones and alignment
```vue
<div class="max-w-xl space-y-4">
  <Lead size="md">Medium lead in the muted tone.</Lead>
  <Lead tone="foreground">Large lead at full contrast.</Lead>
  <Lead size="xl" align="center">Extra large, centred.</Lead>
</div>
```

Example: Extra large with actions
```vue
<div class="max-w-xl space-y-4">
  <Lead size="xl">Sample introduction in the extra large size.</Lead>
  <Button>Open the component list</Button>
</div>
```

# Price
group: typography / Text
A locale-aware price with an optional period, a struck-through previous price and a label for free or missing amounts.

Use `Price` wherever an amount of money is shown: plan cards, rate lists, order summaries. It formats with `Intl.NumberFormat` (through `formatPrice`), uses tabular figures, and never throws on bad input.

Digits: whole amounts show no fraction digits, other amounts show two, unless `minimumFractionDigits` or `maximumFractionDigits` say otherwise. `locale` defaults to the `ConfigProvider` locale, else `en-US`, never the browser locale, so server and client render the same text.

Safe fallbacks: a missing, NaN or infinite `amount` renders `fallback` (default a dash, announced as "No price"); an invalid `currency` code renders a plain number; a malformed `locale` falls back to `en-US`. `freeLabel` replaces a zero amount ("Free"). With `compareAt` the old price is struck through for sighted users and screen readers hear "Was X, now Y". The default slot replaces the amount text. For plain strings (chart labels, `aria-label`) use `formatPrice(amount, options)` exported next to the component; `significantFractionDigits` picks the digits for metered rates such as 0.0004.

Not for percentages or counts: use `FormattedNumber`. Not for a whole plan: use `PricingCard`.

import { Price } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- amount: number | null - Amount in major units (49.5 is 49.50). null, undefined, NaN and Infinity render `fallback`.
- currency: string = 'USD' - ISO 4217 code (any case). An invalid code renders a plain number instead of throwing.
- locale: string = ConfigProvider locale, else 'en-US' - BCP 47 tag such as `de-DE`. Malformed tags fall back to `en-US`.
- period: string - Text after the amount, smaller and muted, such as "/month".
- compareAt: number - Previous price. Struck through before the amount; screen readers read "Was X, now Y". Ignored when `amount` is missing or `compareAt` is not finite.
- notation: 'standard' | 'compact' = 'standard' - `compact` shortens large amounts ("$1.2M"). Unknown values mean `standard`.
- minimumFractionDigits: number - Fewest fraction digits. Default 0 for whole amounts and 2 otherwise.
- maximumFractionDigits: number - Most fraction digits. Default 0 for whole amounts and 2 otherwise.
- freeLabel: string - Text shown when `amount` is exactly 0, such as "Free". Unset formats the zero.
- fallback: string = '—' - Text for a missing or non-finite amount. The default dash is announced as "No price".
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Amount scale; the period and previous price scale with it. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' = 'default' - Amount colour. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- as: string = 'span' - Root element tag.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces the formatted amount text, for example a range such as "from" plus a number. The period and previous price still render.

Rules:
- Pass the amount as a number in major units; never pre-format it, `Price` formats it.
- Pass `locale` from app state, or wrap the app in `ConfigProvider`; the fallback is `en-US`, not the browser locale.
- Use `free-label` for zero amounts and `:compare-at` for a previous price; never hand-roll a strike-through.
- Use `period` for "/month" style suffixes instead of a sibling span.
- For metered rates under one cent pass `minimum-fraction-digits` and `maximum-fraction-digits` (or `significantFractionDigits`), otherwise 0.0004 renders as $0.00.
- Use `formatPrice()` for strings such as chart labels and `aria-label`.

Accessibility:
- Renders plain text, so screen readers read the formatted string. With `compareAt` they read "Was $30, now $20"; the visual strike-through is `aria-hidden`.
- A missing amount with the default dash is exposed as an image named "No price" so the dash is not read as "dash" or skipped.
- Strike-through is not the only signal: the "Was" text exists for assistive technology, and the previous price is also muted.
- Tabular figures change width only. Colours are `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground` and `text-primary`, covered by the contrast tests.
- Use `locale` that matches the page language so digits and separators read correctly.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-2">
  <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sample plan A</span>
  <Price :amount="20" period="/month" />
</div>
```

Example: Previous price and free label
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-6">
  <Price :amount="20" :compare-at="30" period="/month" />
  <Price :amount="0" free-label="Free" />
  <Price :amount="null" />
</div>
```

Example: Size
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-6">
  <Price :amount="12" size="sm" period="/month" />
  <Price :amount="12" size="md" period="/month" />
  <Price :amount="12" size="lg" period="/month" />
  <Price :amount="12" size="xl" period="/month" />
</div>
```

Example: Tone
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-6">
  <Price :amount="40" tone="default" />
  <Price :amount="40" tone="muted" />
  <Price :amount="40" tone="primary" />
</div>
```

Example: Locales and currencies
```vue
<dl class="grid grid-cols-[max-content_auto] gap-x-4 gap-y-1">
  <dt>en-US, USD</dt><dd><Price :amount="1234.5" size="sm" /></dd>
  <dt>de-DE, EUR</dt><dd><Price :amount="1234.5" currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" size="sm" /></dd>
  <dt>ja-JP, JPY</dt><dd><Price :amount="1500" currency="JPY" locale="ja-JP" size="sm" /></dd>
</dl>
```

Example: Compact notation and metered digits
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-6">
  <Price :amount="1200000" notation="compact" size="sm" />
  <Price :amount="0.0004" :minimum-fraction-digits="4" :maximum-fraction-digits="4" size="sm" period="per sample unit" />
</div>
```

Example: Slot override
```vue
<Price :amount="20" period="/month"><span>From $20</span></Price>
```

# RelativeTime
group: typography / Text
A `<time>` element that writes a moment as relative text ("3 minutes ago", "in 2 days") with the absolute date in the tooltip, optionally kept fresh by one shared timer.

Use `RelativeTime` for timestamps in feeds, tables and activity lists. It renders a real `<time datetime="...">` with text from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, so the machine-readable value and the localised text always agree. Past and future moments both work ("3 minutes ago", "in 3 minutes"); units step from seconds through minutes, hours, days, weeks and months to years, truncating toward zero so 59 minutes never reads as an hour. Use `minUnit` and `maxUnit` to limit the units (`maxUnit="day"` gives "400 days ago").

Hydration safety: the component never reads the clock while setting up or rendering. Without `now`, the first render (server and client) is the absolute date, formatted in UTC unless `timeZone` is given, and the relative text appears right after mount. With `now` (a Date, epoch milliseconds or ISO string) the output is fully pinned and identical everywhere, which also makes tests, docs and screenshots deterministic. `locale` defaults to `en`, not the browser locale, for the same reason: pass the app locale. After mount the tooltip date uses the browser time zone unless `timeZone` is set.

Live updates: `updateInterval` (milliseconds, 250 to 2147483647, default 0 = off) refreshes the text. Every instance shares ONE module-level timer that runs at the smallest requested period and is created with the first subscriber and cleared with the last, or when the interval changes to 0. A pinned `now` disables updates. Avoid intervals below 1000 ms for lists: text only changes when a unit count changes.

Input handling: strings must be ISO 8601 (`2025-06-15`, `2025-06-15T09:30:00Z`, with an offset or a space instead of `T`); other date strings are treated as invalid because engines parse them differently. Dates and numbers outside the JavaScript Date range, NaN, Infinity, blank or non-date values render `fallback` (default "Unknown time") in a `<time>` without a `datetime` attribute and with `data-state="invalid"`. Nothing throws. `data-state` is `relative`, `absolute` (before mount without `now`) or `invalid`.

The name is `unitStyle` because `style` is the Vue inline-style attribute; it maps to the Intl `style` option. For a plain string use `formatRelative(datetime, now, options)` exported next to the component.

import { RelativeTime } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- datetime*: Date | number | string - The moment: a Date, epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 string. Anything invalid renders `fallback`.
- now: Date | number | string - Reference moment. Pins the output (no clock read, `updateInterval` ignored). Without it the first render is the absolute date and relative text follows after mount.
- locale: string = 'en' - BCP 47 tag (`de`, `ar`, `ja-JP`). Malformed tags fall back to `en`. Also written to `lang` on the element.
- numeric: 'auto' | 'always' = 'auto' - `auto` writes words where the language has them ("yesterday", "tomorrow", "now"), `always` writes counts ("1 day ago"). Unknown values fall back to `auto`.
- unitStyle: 'long' | 'short' | 'narrow' = 'long' - Width of unit names: "3 minutes ago", "3 min. ago", "3m ago". Maps to the Intl `style` option. Unknown values fall back to `long`.
- minUnit: 'second' | 'minute' | 'hour' | 'day' | 'week' | 'month' | 'year' = 'second' - Smallest unit used. Closer moments read as 0 of this unit ("this minute").
- maxUnit: 'second' | 'minute' | 'hour' | 'day' | 'week' | 'month' | 'year' = 'year' - Largest unit used. `day` gives "400 days ago". Raised to `minUnit` when smaller.
- updateInterval: number = 0 - Milliseconds between live updates, 250 to 2147483647. 0, negative or non-numeric turns updates off. All instances share one timer. Ignored when `now` is set.
- showTitle: boolean = true - Put the absolute date in the `title` attribute. A `title` you pass yourself wins.
- dateStyle: 'full' | 'long' | 'medium' | 'short' = 'medium' - Intl date style for the absolute date.
- timeStyle: 'full' | 'long' | 'medium' | 'short' | 'none' = 'short' - Intl time style for the absolute date; `none` leaves the time of day out.
- timeZone: string - IANA zone for the absolute date (`UTC`, `Europe/Warsaw`). Unknown zones are ignored. Before mount it is UTC when not given.
- fallback: string = 'Unknown time' - Text for an invalid `datetime`.
- variant: 'plain' | 'muted' | 'dotted' = 'plain' - `plain` inherits, `muted` uses the secondary colour, `dotted` adds a dotted underline that hints at the tooltip. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- size: 'inherit' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'inherit' - Font size; `inherit` keeps the surrounding size.
- tone: 'default' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'default' - Text colour. Colour never carries meaning alone: keep the words in surrounding text.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Rules:
- Always pass `now` in docs, tests and server-rendered pages that must be deterministic; without it the first render is the absolute date.
- The Intl style option is the prop `unitStyle`, not `style`.
- Pass `datetime` as ISO 8601 (or a Date or epoch ms); other date strings are invalid and render the fallback.
- Use `updateInterval` (for example 60000) only on pages that stay open; all instances share one timer, so many rows are cheap.
- Do not format times in templates with `new Date()` or `Date.now()`: it breaks hydration. Use RelativeTime.
- Use `formatRelative(datetime, now, options)` for plain strings (`aria-label`, chart tooltips).

Accessibility:
- Renders a native `<time>` element with a machine-readable `datetime`; the visible text is the accessible name and is read as written ("3 minutes ago").
- The `title` tooltip is supplemental: it is not reachable by keyboard or touch. Show the absolute date as text where it matters (receipts, audit logs).
- `lang` is set to the resolved locale and `dir="auto"` lets right-to-left text such as `ar` resolve its own direction inside a left-to-right page.
- Live updates replace the text in place without a live region, so screen readers are not interrupted every tick. Do not wrap the element in `aria-live`.
- Tone and the dotted variant are never the only signal. Colours use `text-success`, `text-warning-foreground`, `text-destructive`, `text-info` and `text-muted-foreground`, covered by the contrast tests; the dotted underline survives forced-colors mode.

Example: Past and future
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:57:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T09:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-01T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T12:03:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-18T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2023-06-15T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Numeric auto and always
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" numeric="always" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-16T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-16T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" numeric="always" /></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Unit style
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:57:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" unit-style="long" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:57:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" unit-style="short" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:57:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" unit-style="narrow" /></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Locales and right to left
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:57:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" locale="de" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T09:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" locale="ja-JP" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T09:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" locale="ar" /></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Limit the units
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-04-01T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-04-01T12:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" max-unit="day" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:59:40Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" min-unit="minute" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:59:40Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Absolute date in the title
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T09:30:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" time-zone="UTC" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T09:30:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" time-zone="UTC" date-style="full" time-style="long" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T09:30:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" time-zone="UTC" date-style="short" time-style="none" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-14T09:30:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" :show-title="false" /></li>
</ul>
```

Example: Variants, sizes and tones
```vue
<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" variant="muted" size="sm" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:00:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" variant="dotted" time-zone="UTC" /></li>

  <li>Synced <RelativeTime datetime="2025-06-15T11:59:00Z" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" tone="success" size="lg" /></li>

```

Example: Date objects, epoch numbers and invalid input

<ul class="space-y-1">
  <li><RelativeTime :datetime="1749988800000" :now="1750000000000" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="not a date" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime datetime="" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" fallback="No date" /></li>
  <li><RelativeTime :datetime="1e20" now="2025-06-15T12:00:00Z" /></li>
</ul>
