# Text
group: typography / Text
Body text with variant presets, size, tone, weight, leading, transform, wrapping, alignment and truncation or line clamping.

Use `Text` for paragraphs, captions and inline labels instead of raw `<p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">`. `truncate` gives a single ellipsised line (needs a width-constrained parent); `lines` clamps to 1-6 lines and wins over `truncate`. Do not use for headings (use `Heading`).

Variants are presets that fill only the `size` / `tone` / `weight` you leave unset: `default` plain body copy; `caption` (xs, muted) for helper text under media or inputs; `label` (sm, medium, tight leading) for form-like labels and metadata keys (render with `as="label"`/`span`); `overline` (xs, muted, medium weight, normal case) for small labels that are not headings; `mono` (sm, monospace) for IDs, hashes and numbers. Tones: `muted` secondary copy, `subtle` (same colour as `muted`; a dimmer grey cannot meet AA contrast), `foreground` to reset inside muted parents, `primary` accent, and `success`/`warning`/`danger`/`info` for status.

import { Text } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- as: string | Component = 'p' - Element to render (`span`, `div`, `label`...).
- asChild: boolean = false - Style the single slot child instead of rendering a wrapper.
- variant: 'default' | 'caption' | 'label' | 'overline' | 'mono' = 'default' - Preset. Fills `size`/`tone`/`weight` only when they are not given. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' = variant size, else 'base' - Font size. Unknown values fall back to base.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'subtle' | 'foreground' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = variant tone, else 'default' - Text colour. `default` inherits.
- weight: 'light' | 'normal' | 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold' = variant weight, else unset - Font weight.
- align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | 'justify' | 'start' | 'end' - Text alignment.
- leading: 'none' | 'tight' | 'snug' | 'normal' | 'relaxed' | 'loose' - Line height.
- transform: 'uppercase' | 'lowercase' | 'capitalize' - Text transform. Discouraged: write the text in the case it should read and prefer sentence case.
- italic: boolean = false - Italic style.
- wrap: 'balance' | 'pretty' | 'nowrap' - Wrapping strategy: even lines, avoid orphans, or never wrap.
- truncate: boolean = false - Single line with ellipsis. Ignored when `lines` is valid.
- lines: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | '1'..'6' - Clamp to N lines with ellipsis. Other values are ignored.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Text content.

Rules:
- Use `tone="muted"` for secondary copy, not a custom grey.
- `lines` accepts only 1-6; `lines` beats `truncate`.
- Truncate needs a parent with constrained width (e.g. `min-w-0` in flex).
- Do not use `transform="uppercase"` or letter-spacing for labels.
- Prefer `variant` presets (`caption`, `label`, `overline`, `mono`) over hand-written class combinations; pass `size`/`tone` only to deviate.
- Use `Heading` (not `Text variant="overline"`) when the text names a section for the document outline.

Accessibility:
- Truncated or clamped text is still fully present in the DOM for screen readers; expose the full text with a `title` attribute or tooltip where it matters.
- Do not rely on tone colour alone to convey status.
- `variant="label"` is only styling: use `as="label"` with `for` when it labels a control.
- `transform` changes only how text is drawn; screen readers read the original text.
- `warning` uses the dark warning ink in light mode and the warning token in dark mode so it meets AA; it is never the only signal, so keep the words ("Almost full") in the text.

Example: Tones and sizes
```vue
<div class="space-y-1">
  <Text size="lg" weight="semibold">Large semibold</Text>
  <Text>Default body text.</Text>
  <Text size="sm" tone="muted">Small muted caption.</Text>
  <Text size="sm" tone="success">Saved</Text>
  <Text size="sm" tone="warning">Almost full</Text>
  <Text size="sm" tone="danger">Something went wrong</Text>
  <Text size="sm" tone="info">Heads up</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Truncation and line clamp
```vue
<div class="w-64 space-y-3">
  <Text truncate>A very long single line that will be cut off with an ellipsis at the container edge.</Text>
  <Text :lines="2" tone="muted">A longer paragraph that is clamped to two lines. Everything beyond the second line is hidden and replaced by an ellipsis so cards keep an even height.</Text>
  <Text align="center" as="span" class="block">Centered span</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: caption
```vue
<div class="space-y-1">
  <Text>Sample metric name</Text>
  <Text variant="caption">Sample helper text</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: label
```vue
<div class="space-y-1">
  <Text as="span" variant="label" class="block">Sample label</Text>
  <Text variant="caption">Sample helper text for the field.</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: overline
```vue
<div class="space-y-1">
  <Text variant="overline">Sample label</Text>
  <Text>Sample paragraph under the label.</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: mono
```vue
<Text variant="mono" tone="muted">req_sample_id</Text>
```

Example: Preset overrides
```vue
<Text variant="overline" size="sm" tone="primary" weight="bold">Overridden label</Text>
```

Example: Subtle, foreground and primary tones
```vue
<div class="space-y-1">
  <Text tone="subtle">Subtle tertiary copy</Text>
  <Text tone="muted"><Text as="span" tone="foreground" weight="medium">Foreground</Text> inside muted copy</Text>
  <Text tone="primary" weight="light" size="xl">Light primary</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Leading, transform and italic
```vue
<div class="w-full max-w-72 space-y-3">
  <Text leading="relaxed">Relaxed leading gives long paragraphs more air to breathe between lines.</Text>
  <Text leading="tight" transform="capitalize">tight leading and capitalised words</Text>
  <Text italic>Italic emphasis</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Wrapping
```vue
<div class="w-64 space-y-3">
  <Text wrap="balance" size="lg" weight="semibold">Balanced lines are even and pleasant for short statements</Text>
  <Text wrap="pretty" tone="muted">Pretty wrapping avoids a single orphaned word on the last line of a paragraph.</Text>
  <Text wrap="nowrap" class="overflow-hidden">A line that never wraps and is clipped by the parent</Text>
</div>
```

Example: Larger sizes
```vue
<div class="space-y-1">
  <Text size="2xl" weight="semibold">2xl display text</Text>
  <Text size="3xl" weight="bold" leading="tight">3xl display text</Text>
</div>
```

# ConfigProvider
group: layout / Configuration
Sets text direction, locale, time zone, motion override, default size and density, and translated built-in strings for everything inside it.

Wrap an app or a region once instead of passing `locale`, `size` or translated labels to every component. `dir` and `locale` are set as `dir` and `lang` on the wrapper and passed to the headless primitives (menus, tabs, sliders), which read them even in portalled content. `labels` translates the strings a component ships with, keyed `<component>.<string>`: `pagination.nav|first|previous|next|last|page|summary`, `datePicker.placeholder|clear|required|dialog`, `confirmDialog.confirm|cancel|defaultTitle|error`, `fileDropzone.prompt|dragging|remove|added|addedMany|removed|typeNotAllowed|tooLarge|onlyOne|atMost|accepts|upTo|maxFiles`, `multiSelect.more|clearSelection|selectAll|clear|options`, `colorPicker.swatches|input|invalid`, `passwordInput.show|revealWarning`, `textarea.count|limit`, `combobox.clearSelection|toggleOptions|empty`, `modelPicker.clearSelection|toggleOptions|empty`, `link.externalHint`, `heatmap.less|more`. Pagination, DatePicker, ConfirmDialog, FileDropzone, MultiSelect, ColorPicker, PasswordInput, Textarea, Combobox, ModelPicker, Link, Heatmap and CalendarHeatmap read them today. Placeholders such as `{count}`, `{name}`, `{size}`, `{max}` and `{types}` are replaced where a label uses them. Precedence per value is the component prop, then the nearest provider, then the English default, so a component with no provider behaves exactly as before. Providers nest: an inner provider overrides an outer one per key and `labels` merge per key. Invalid values (an unknown `dir`, a bad locale or time zone, a label that is not a non-blank string) are ignored, and labels are always rendered as text, never as HTML. Read the merged result in your own components with `useConfig()` (a computed with `dir`, `locale`, `timeZone`, `reducedMotion`, `size`, `density`, `labels`) and give them the same translation hook with `useConfigLabels(prefix, defaults)`. `reducedMotion` is an app-level override for code that asks; CSS `motion-reduce:` rules still follow the operating system. `dir` and `lang` are attributes of the wrapper, so portalled content (dialogs, popovers) does not inherit them from the DOM: use the same `dir` on `<html>` for those, or rely on the primitives that read it from the provider. `blurMedia` is the privacy switch: it blurs avatars and photos in the subtree, and each component's own `blurred` prop wins. Use `asChild` to render no extra element, or `class="contents"` to keep layout unchanged.

import { ConfigProvider } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- dir: 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'auto' - Text direction of the subtree. Unset keeps the surrounding direction; unknown values are ignored.
- locale: string - BCP 47 tag such as `de-DE`, set as `lang`. DatePicker uses it as its default `locale`. Invalid tags are ignored.
- timeZone: string - IANA time zone such as `Europe/Berlin`, for components that read `useConfig().timeZone`. Invalid names are ignored.
- reducedMotion: 'user' | 'reduce' | 'no-preference' = 'user' - `user` follows the operating system. The other two are exposed as `data-reduced-motion` and `useConfig().reducedMotion`; CSS media queries are not changed.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' - Default size for Pagination and DatePicker when they have no `size` of their own. Sizes a component does not support fall back to its default. Set as `data-size`.
- density: 'default' | 'compact' | 'comfortable' - Default density hint for components that read `useConfig().density`. Set as `data-density`.
- labels: Record<string, string> - Translations of built-in strings keyed `<component>.<string>`. Merged per key with outer providers. Non-string, blank and unknown-key entries are ignored.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render no wrapper: attributes go onto the single child element.
- blurMedia: boolean - Privacy blur for every avatar and photo in the subtree (Avatar, AvatarGroup, TeamGrid, ImageGrid, Lightbox, MediaFrame, BeforeAfter, and the images of BlogCard, Blockquote, Testimonial and ChatMessage). A component's own `blurred` prop wins, true or false. Unset keeps the surrounding value, then false. Exposed as `useConfig().blurMedia`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last.

Slots:
- default - Content that receives the configuration.

Rules:
- `blurMedia` is for privacy (screen sharing, demos, sensitive uploads), not decoration. A component prop `blurred` still wins.
- Put one ConfigProvider near the root for `dir`, `locale` and `labels`; nest another only where a region differs.
- Label keys are `<component>.<string>`: pagination.*, datePicker.*, confirmDialog.*. Unknown keys are harmless and ignored by the components.
- A prop on the component still beats the provider: use the prop for one-off text, the provider for the whole app.
- Never pass HTML in labels: they are plain text. Blank and non-string values are ignored.
- Read the config in your own component with `useConfig()` (a computed ref) and `useConfigLabels(prefix, defaults)`; it works without a provider and returns your defaults.
- Use `asChild` or `class="contents"` when the wrapper div would disturb a flex or grid layout.

Accessibility:
- `blurMedia` is visual only: alt text, names and roles are unchanged and nothing is removed from the accessibility tree. The affected elements get `data-blurred`.
- Renders a plain element with no role or name; it does not change the accessibility tree except through `dir` and `lang`.
- `lang` lets screen readers pick the right voice and lets the browser hyphenate correctly; set `locale` on the part of the page that is in another language.
- Translated labels replace the accessible names of the navigation landmark, the page and arrow buttons, the clear button and the dialog. A blank label is ignored, so a name never disappears.
- `dir="rtl"` mirrors logical spacing and the arrow icons of Pagination; `dir="auto"` lets the browser decide from the content.
- `reducedMotion` does not change the operating-system preference: CSS rules that honour `prefers-reduced-motion` keep doing so.

Example: Translate built-in strings
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const page = ref(3)
const labels = { 'pagination.nav': 'Seitennavigation', 'pagination.first': 'Erste Seite', 'pagination.previous': 'Vorherige Seite', 'pagination.next': 'Nächste Seite', 'pagination.last': 'Letzte Seite', 'pagination.page': 'Seite', 'pagination.summary': 'Seite {page} von {total}' }
</script>

<ConfigProvider locale="de-DE" :labels="labels">
  <Pagination v-model:page="page" :total="120" :page-size="10" />
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: Locale for dates
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const date = ref(new Date(2025, 2, 14))
const labels = { 'datePicker.clear': 'Datum entfernen', 'datePicker.dialog': 'Datum wählen', 'datePicker.placeholder': 'Datum wählen' }
</script>

<ConfigProvider locale="de-DE" :labels="labels">
  <div class="min-h-96 max-w-xs">
    <DatePicker v-model="date" clearable aria-label="Fälligkeitsdatum" />
  </div>
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: Translated confirmation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
const labels = { 'confirmDialog.confirm': 'Löschen', 'confirmDialog.cancel': 'Abbrechen' }
function remove() { /* delete it */ }
</script>

<ConfigProvider :labels="labels">
  <Button variant="destructive" @click="open = true">Projekt löschen</Button>
  <ConfirmDialog v-model:open="open" title="Projekt löschen?" description="Das Projekt und seine Daten werden entfernt." destructive @confirm="remove" />
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: Right-to-left region
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const page = ref(2)
const labels = { 'pagination.nav': 'ترقيم الصفحات', 'pagination.summary': 'صفحة {page} من {total}', 'pagination.page': 'صفحة' }
</script>

<ConfigProvider dir="rtl" locale="ar" :labels="labels" class="rounded-lg border p-4">
  <Pagination v-model:page="page" :total="60" :page-size="10" />
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: Nested providers
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const outer = { 'pagination.nav': 'Seiten, außen', 'pagination.next': 'Weiter', 'pagination.previous': 'Zurück' }
const inner = { 'pagination.nav': 'Seiten, innen', 'pagination.next': 'Vor' }
</script>

<ConfigProvider size="lg" :labels="outer" class="space-y-3">
  <Pagination :total="40" :page-size="10" variant="compact" />
  <ConfigProvider size="sm" :labels="inner">
    <Pagination :total="40" :page-size="10" variant="compact" />
  </ConfigProvider>
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: Default size hint
```vue
<ConfigProvider size="sm" class="space-y-3">
  <Pagination :total="50" :page-size="10" variant="compact" :labels="{ nav: 'Pages, provider size' }" />
  <Pagination :total="50" :page-size="10" variant="compact" size="lg" :labels="{ nav: 'Pages, own size' }" />
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: No wrapper element
```vue
<ConfigProvider as-child dir="ltr" locale="en-GB" reduced-motion="reduce">
  <section aria-label="Sample region" class="rounded-lg border p-4">
    <p class="text-sm">Language, direction and the motion override are set on this section.</p>
  </section>
</ConfigProvider>
```

Example: Blur media in a region
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const blur = ref(false)
</script>

<ConfigProvider :blur-media="blur" class="space-y-4 rounded-lg border p-4">
  <Switch v-model="blur" label="Blur people and photos" />
  <AvatarGroup aria-label="Meeting participants">
    <Avatar name="Author One" />
    <Avatar name="Author Two" :blurred="false" />
    <Avatar name="Author Five" />
  </AvatarGroup>
  <ImageGrid :images="images" :columns="3" :lightbox="false" />
</ConfigProvider>
```

# Container
group: layout / Containers
Constrains content to a max width, centres it and adds responsive horizontal padding.

Wrap page content in `Container` instead of hand-writing `mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`. Pick a `size` preset (`sm` … `7xl`, `prose` for a readable text measure, or `full`). Horizontal padding is `padded` (default responsive gutter) or, for explicit control, a `gutter` preset (`none` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`, replaces `padded`). `paddingY` (`none` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`) adds vertical padding so you do not need a wrapping `Section`. Use `padded=false` when the parent already pads, and `centered=false` to left-align. Not for vertical rhythm (use `Section`) or spacing between children (use `Stack`).

import { Container } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' | '4xl' | '5xl' | '6xl' | '7xl' | 'prose' | 'full' = '7xl' - Max-width preset (Tailwind max-w-*; `prose` = max-w-prose). Unknown values fall back to 7xl.
- padded: boolean = true - Responsive horizontal padding: px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8. Ignored when `gutter` is set.
- gutter: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Horizontal gutter preset (none px-0, sm px-3 sm:px-4, md = default responsive, lg px-6 sm:px-8 lg:px-12). Replaces `padded`; unknown values are ignored.
- paddingY: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Vertical padding preset (py-0, py-4 md:py-6, py-8 md:py-12, py-12 md:py-20). Unset or unknown adds none.
- centered: boolean = true - Horizontally centre with mx-auto.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render, e.g. `main`.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Page content.

Rules:
- Use Container for page-level width; do not hand-write mx-auto max-w-* px-* wrappers.
- Pass `as="main"` only once per page.
- Use size="prose" for long-form text; use `gutter` instead of `padded` when you need a specific gutter scale.
- Use `paddingY` for simple vertical padding; use Section when you also need backgrounds or dividers.
- Nest a Container inside a Section for full-bleed backgrounds with constrained content.

Accessibility:
- Renders a plain div by default; use `as="main"` for the primary landmark (only one per page) and `as="section"` with an `aria-label` for a named region.
- Responsive: `padded` adds 16px gutters (24px from `sm`, 32px from `lg`), the container is `w-full`, so content reflows at 320px and at 200% zoom without horizontal scroll.
- No interactive behaviour, no focus handling.

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Container size="sm" class="bg-muted py-2 text-sm">sm</Container>
  <Container size="3xl" class="bg-muted py-2 text-sm">3xl</Container>
  <Container size="full" class="bg-muted py-2 text-sm">full</Container>
</div>
```

Example: Page wrapper
```vue
<Container as="section" aria-label="Sample page" size="5xl" class="py-8">
  <h4 class="text-2xl font-semibold">Sample page title</h4>
  <p class="text-muted-foreground">Content is centred and padded.</p>
</Container>
```

Example: Prose measure
```vue
<Container size="prose" class="bg-muted py-3 text-sm">A readable measure of roughly 65 characters per line, ideal for articles, docs and legal copy.</Container>
```

Example: Gutter presets
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Container size="2xl" gutter="none" class="bg-muted py-2 text-sm">gutter none</Container>
  <Container size="2xl" gutter="sm" class="bg-muted py-2 text-sm">gutter sm</Container>
  <Container size="2xl" gutter="lg" class="bg-muted py-2 text-sm">gutter lg</Container>
</div>
```

Example: Vertical padding
```vue
<div class="space-y-2">
  <Container size="2xl" padding-y="sm" class="bg-muted text-sm">paddingY sm</Container>
  <Container size="2xl" padding-y="lg" class="bg-muted text-sm">paddingY lg</Container>
</div>
```

Example: No padding, left-aligned
```vue
<Container size="2xl" :padded="false" :centered="false" class="bg-muted p-3 text-sm">Left-aligned, own padding</Container>
```

# Section
group: layout / Containers
Page section with vertical padding presets, optional tinted background and borders.

Use `Section` to stack bands of content on landing and docs pages. It owns vertical rhythm (`padding`: `none` | `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`) and full-bleed background (`tone`: `none` transparent, `muted` for quiet alternating bands, `card` for bands on the card surface, `primary` for a single band that needs emphasis; all flat token colours, no gradients or patterns). `divider` (`top` | `bottom` | `both`) draws a border on chosen edges, e.g. `top` for footers and `bottom` for headers; `bordered` is the shorthand for both. Put a `Container` inside to constrain width. For a labelled region give it `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading. Not for card-like boxed content (use Card).

import { Section } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- padding: 'none' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' = 'md' - Vertical padding preset (responsive): xs py-3/md:py-4, sm py-6/md:py-8, md py-10/md:py-14, lg py-14/md:py-20, xl py-20/md:py-28. Unknown values fall back to md.
- tone: 'none' | 'muted' | 'card' | 'primary' = 'none' - Flat background using semantic tokens only. The former `gradient` and `pattern` tones were removed and fall back to none. Unknown values fall back to none.
- divider: 'none' | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'both' - Border on the top, bottom or both edges (border-t / border-b / border-y). Takes precedence over `bordered`; unknown values are ignored.
- bordered: boolean = false - Adds top and bottom borders (border-y). Ignored when a valid `divider` is set.
- as: string | Component = 'section' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Section content, usually a Container.

Rules:
- Section handles vertical padding and background; Container handles width. Nest them.
- Give Section an aria-labelledby when it has a heading.
- Tones are flat token colours only; do not add gradients or patterns with classes.
- Use divider="top|bottom|both" for one-sided borders; bordered is shorthand for both and loses to divider.
- Use tone="primary" sparingly (one emphasised band per page).

Accessibility:
- Renders a <section>, which is only exposed as a region landmark when it has an accessible name: set `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`.
- Tones are token pairs (`bg-*` with its `*-foreground`), so text contrast follows the tested AA pairs in light and dark.
- Responsive: padding steps down on small screens (`py-*` then `md:py-*`); no fixed widths.

Example: Tones
```vue
<div>
  <Section padding="sm"><Container size="3xl">Plain</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="sm" tone="muted" bordered><Container size="3xl">Muted + bordered</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="sm" tone="primary"><Container size="3xl">Primary</Container></Section>
</div>
```

Example: Dividers
```vue
<div>
  <Section padding="xs" divider="top"><Container size="3xl">Top divider</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="xs" divider="bottom"><Container size="3xl">Bottom divider</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="xs" divider="both" tone="card"><Container size="3xl">Both dividers</Container></Section>
</div>
```

Example: Padding sizes
```vue
<div>
  <Section padding="none" tone="muted"><Container size="3xl">none</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="xs" tone="card"><Container size="3xl">xs</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="sm" tone="muted"><Container size="3xl">sm</Container></Section>
  <Section padding="md" tone="card"><Container size="3xl">md</Container></Section>
</div>
```

Example: Labelled band
```vue
<Section padding="lg" tone="card" aria-labelledby="sample-band-title">
  <Container size="4xl">
    <VStack :gap="3">
      <h4 id="sample-band-title" class="text-2xl font-semibold">Sample band heading</h4>
      <p class="text-muted-foreground">Sample text inside a labelled section.</p>
      <HStack><Button>Open the component list</Button></HStack>
    </VStack>
  </Container>
</Section>
```

# AppShell
group: layout / Page structure
Application frame with header, collapsible sidebar (drawer on mobile), main content and footer slots.

Use `AppShell` as the root layout of dashboards and admin apps. Pick a `layout`: `top-nav-sidebar` (default; full-width header above sidebar and content), `sidebar-left` / `sidebar-right` (full-height sidebar, header over the content column only), `top-nav` (header and content, no sidebar) or `dual-sidebar` (`sidebar` slot on the start side plus a `sidebar-end` slot, e.g. a details panel). Sidebars render in `<aside>` landmarks with the `sidebar-*` tokens; their content is yours. From the drawer breakpoint up (`md` by default, `lg` via `drawerBreakpoint`) a sidebar is always visible and collapses to an icon rail (`railWidth` sm/md/lg, `collapseMode="rail"`) or disappears (`collapseMode="hidden"`) with `v-model:collapsed` (`v-model:collapsed-end` for the end sidebar); `sidebarWidth` sets the expanded width. Below the breakpoint the sidebar is an off-canvas drawer: hidden unless `v-model:open` (`v-model:open-end`) is true, then it is a modal dialog over the page above a backdrop that closes on click and Escape: everything behind it is `inert` (so focus cannot leave the drawer), page scrolling is locked (`lockScroll`), focus moves into the drawer and returns on close, and closes by itself when the viewport grows past the breakpoint. `contentMaxWidth` centres and constrains the page content (`sm` … `7xl`, `prose`, `full`) with responsive padding. Slot props `{ collapsed, open, toggle, sidebarId, expanded, triggerProps, collapsedEnd, openEnd, toggleEnd }` are available in every slot; `toggle` collapses on desktop and opens/closes the drawer on mobile, and `v-bind="triggerProps"` on the menu button adds `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`. The default slot is the `<main>` content (set `:main="false"` to render a `div` when the shell is embedded in a page that already has a `main`). No extra dependencies: it is plain CSS classes plus a media query listener.

import { AppShell } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- layout: 'top-nav-sidebar' | 'sidebar-left' | 'sidebar-right' | 'top-nav' | 'dual-sidebar' = 'top-nav-sidebar' - `top-nav-sidebar`: header spans the full width above sidebar + content. `sidebar-left` / `sidebar-right`: full-height (sticky h-dvh) sidebar on that side, header over the content column. `top-nav`: no sidebar (slots ignored). `dual-sidebar`: `sidebar` at the start + `sidebar-end` at the end. Unknown values fall back to the default. Sets `data-layout` when not default.
- collapsed: boolean = false - v-model:collapsed. Primary sidebar becomes a rail (or hides, see collapseMode) on desktop when true. Works uncontrolled.
- open: boolean = false - v-model:open. Primary sidebar drawer visibility below the drawer breakpoint. Works uncontrolled.
- collapsedEnd: boolean = false - v-model:collapsedEnd. Collapsed state of the `sidebar-end` (dual-sidebar).
- openEnd: boolean = false - v-model:openEnd. Drawer visibility of the `sidebar-end` (dual-sidebar).
- sidebarWidth: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Expanded sidebar width (and drawer width): w-56 / w-64 / w-72. Unknown values fall back to md.
- railWidth: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Collapsed rail width: w-12 / w-14 / w-16. Unknown values fall back to md.
- collapseMode: 'rail' | 'hidden' = 'rail' - `rail` shrinks to an icon rail; `hidden` removes the sidebar on desktop while collapsed. Unknown values fall back to rail.
- drawerBreakpoint: 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Viewport below which sidebars are off-canvas drawers (768px / 1024px). Unknown values fall back to md.
- contentMaxWidth: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' | '4xl' | '5xl' | '6xl' | '7xl' | 'prose' | 'full' - Wrap the page content in a centred, max-width container (same presets as Container). Unset renders the content edge to edge. Unknown values are ignored.
- contentPadded: boolean = true - With contentMaxWidth: responsive horizontal padding (px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8).
- lockScroll: boolean = true - Set overflow:hidden on <body> while a drawer is open (below the breakpoint only); the previous value is restored on close and unmount.
- mainId: string = 'main-content' - id of the <main> element (skip-link target).
- sidebarLabel: string = 'Sidebar' - aria-label of the primary sidebar <aside>.
- sidebarEndLabel: string = 'Secondary sidebar' - aria-label of the end sidebar <aside> (dual-sidebar).
- main: boolean = true - Render the page region as a `<main>` landmark. Set `false` to render a `div` when the shell is embedded in a page that already has a main landmark (live demos, nested apps).
- skipLink: boolean = false - Render a skip link to the main content (visible on focus).
- skipLinkLabel: string = 'Skip to main content' - Text of the skip link.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Root element.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- header ({ collapsed: boolean, open: boolean, toggle: () => void, sidebarId: string, expanded: boolean, triggerProps: { 'aria-controls': string, 'aria-expanded': 'true' | 'false' }, collapsedEnd: boolean, openEnd: boolean, toggleEnd: () => void }) - Sticky top bar (<header>). Not rendered when empty.
- sidebar ({ collapsed: boolean, open: boolean, toggle: () => void, sidebarId: string, expanded: boolean, triggerProps: { 'aria-controls': string, 'aria-expanded': 'true' | 'false' }, collapsedEnd: boolean, openEnd: boolean, toggleEnd: () => void }) - Primary sidebar content inside <aside> (start side; end side with layout sidebar-right). Not rendered when empty or with layout top-nav (and no drawer/backdrop).
- sidebar-end ({ collapsed: boolean, open: boolean, toggle: () => void, sidebarId: string, expanded: boolean, triggerProps: { 'aria-controls': string, 'aria-expanded': 'true' | 'false' }, collapsedEnd: boolean, openEnd: boolean, toggleEnd: () => void }) - Second sidebar for layout dual-sidebar, on the end side. Ignored in other layouts.
- default ({ collapsed: boolean, open: boolean, toggle: () => void, sidebarId: string, expanded: boolean, triggerProps: { 'aria-controls': string, 'aria-expanded': 'true' | 'false' }, collapsedEnd: boolean, openEnd: boolean, toggleEnd: () => void }) - Main page content inside <main>.
- footer ({ collapsed: boolean, open: boolean, toggle: () => void, sidebarId: string, expanded: boolean, triggerProps: { 'aria-controls': string, 'aria-expanded': 'true' | 'false' }, collapsedEnd: boolean, openEnd: boolean, toggleEnd: () => void }) - Footer (<footer>) under main. Not rendered when empty.

Events:
- update:collapsed [value: boolean] - Sidebar collapsed state changed (v-model:collapsed).
- update:open [value: boolean] - Primary drawer opened/closed, including backdrop click, Escape and growing past the drawer breakpoint (v-model:open).
- update:collapsedEnd [value: boolean] - End sidebar collapsed state changed (v-model:collapsedEnd).
- update:openEnd [value: boolean] - End drawer opened/closed (v-model:openEnd).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a rendered sidebar has a blank `sidebarLabel` (or `sidebarEndLabel` for the end sidebar).
- Throws a ContractError when `skipLink` is set and `mainId` or `skipLinkLabel` is blank.
- Throws a ContractError when `main` is false and the page has no `<main>` (or `role="main"`) landmark elsewhere.

Rules:
- Sidebar content is the consumer's; AppShell only provides the frame, width, drawer behaviour and tokens.
- Bind both v-model:collapsed and v-model:open if you need to persist state; otherwise they work uncontrolled.
- Use the slot prop `toggle` for the hamburger button (`toggleEnd` for the end sidebar).
- Choose layout by structure: top-nav-sidebar (header over everything), sidebar-left/right (full-height sidebar), top-nav (no sidebar), dual-sidebar (two sidebars; use the sidebar-end slot).
- Use contentMaxWidth instead of wrapping the default slot in a Container; use drawerBreakpoint="lg" for dense sidebars that need more room.
- Do not mix collapsed with `open`: collapsed is desktop-only (rail/hidden), open is the mobile drawer.
- Pair with PageHeader inside the default slot for page titles.

Accessibility:
- Sidebar is an <aside> landmark with `aria-label` (sidebarLabel); header, main and footer are native landmarks.
- <main> has an id and tabindex="-1" so skip links and programmatic focus work; enable `skipLink` for a built-in skip link.
- Mobile drawer: while open the sidebar is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` and its `aria-label`; the header, content and the other sidebar are `inert`, so Tab cannot leave the drawer and screen readers cannot reach the page behind it. The backdrop is aria-hidden and closes on click; Escape closes it; focus moves into the drawer on open and returns to the previously focused control on close; page scroll is locked while it is open.
- Menu button: give it an `aria-label` and spread the `triggerProps` slot prop on it (`aria-controls` points at the sidebar id, `aria-expanded` follows the drawer on mobile and the collapsed state on desktop).
- Responsive: below the drawer breakpoint the content column is full width (no sidebar column), so nothing scrolls horizontally at 320px; the drawer is capped to the viewport width.
- Only one `<main>` per page: pass `:main="false"` when the shell is embedded.
- Give each sidebar a distinct accessible name (`sidebarLabel`, `sidebarEndLabel`) when there are two.
- With `layout="sidebar-right"` or `dual-sidebar` the end sidebar comes after the main content in the DOM, which is its reading and tab order.
- Collapsing only changes width; make sure collapsed sidebar items keep accessible names (aria-label on icon-only links).

Example: Basic shell
```vue
<div class="h-72 overflow-hidden rounded-md border">
  <AppShell :main="false" class="min-h-full" sidebar-label="Basic shell sidebar">
    <template #header><div class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium">App</div></template>
    <template #sidebar><div class="p-3 text-sm">Sidebar nav</div></template>
    <div class="p-4 text-sm">Main content</div>
  </AppShell>
</div>
```

Example: Layout: sidebar-left
```vue
<div class="h-72 overflow-hidden rounded-md border">
  <AppShell :main="false" layout="sidebar-left" class="min-h-full" sidebar-label="Left sidebar">
    <template #header><div class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium">Page header</div></template>
    <template #sidebar><div class="p-3 text-sm">Left nav</div></template>
    <div class="p-4 text-sm">Main content</div>
  </AppShell>
</div>
```

```vue

    <template #header><div class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium">Page header</div></template>
    <template #sidebar><div class="p-3 text-sm">Details panel</div></template>
```

# CenteredLayout
group: layout / Page structure
Full-height page that centres a narrow column, for sign-in, empty and error pages.

Use `CenteredLayout` for pages with a single focused task: login, sign-up, password reset, 404, onboarding. Fills the dynamic viewport height (`min-h-dvh`) and centres an inner column of `width` sm … 4xl. Slots: `logo`, `header` (title/subtitle), default content, `footer` (links), `illustration`. Layouts: `default` (plain centred column, for empty/error/onboarding pages), `card` (the column becomes a bordered card on a muted page, the classic auth card), `split` (form on one side and an `illustration` panel on the other from `lg`, hidden on mobile; `illustrationPosition` picks the side). Use `width="xl"`/`"2xl"`/`"4xl"` for wide pages such as multi-step onboarding. Not for dashboards (use AppShell).

import { CenteredLayout } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- width: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '4xl' = 'md' - Inner column max width (max-w-sm … max-w-4xl). Unknown values fall back to md.
- layout: 'default' | 'card' | 'split' = 'default' - `card` wraps the column in a card surface on a muted page; `split` adds an illustration panel (needs the `illustration` slot, otherwise it renders like default). Unknown values fall back to default. Sets `data-layout` when not default.
- illustrationPosition: 'start' | 'end' = 'end' - Split layout: side of the illustration panel from `lg` up (start = left in LTR). Unknown values fall back to end.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Root element, e.g. `main`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- logo - Centred brand mark above the header.
- header - Centred title/subtitle block.
- default - Main content (form, empty-state, message).
- footer - Muted, centred footer text/links.
- illustration - Split layout only: decorative or marketing panel next to the form; hidden below `lg`. Mark purely decorative content aria-hidden.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `layout="split"` is used without an `illustration` slot.

Rules:
- Use layout="card" for sign-in/sign-up forms and layout="split" + #illustration for branded auth pages; plain default for empty/error pages.
- The illustration slot only renders with layout="split" and is hidden below lg, so never put essential content in it.
- Use for auth and empty pages; it already provides min-h-dvh, padding and background.
- Put the form/content in the default slot; logo/header/footer are optional wrappers.

Accessibility:
- On a real page use `as="main"` so the page has a main landmark. The live examples keep the default `div` because the docs page already has a `main` (a page must not have two).
- Put the page heading (h1) in the `header` slot; in examples, use the heading level that follows the surrounding section so the outline does not skip levels.
- The illustration panel is hidden below `lg` (`display: none`), so it is removed from the accessibility tree there; never put essential content in it.
- Responsive: the column is `w-full` with a `max-w-*` cap and the page pads 16px (24px from `sm`), so it reflows at 320px without horizontal scroll. `min-h-dvh` follows the mobile browser UI.

Example: Sign-in page
```vue
<div class="h-96 overflow-auto rounded-md border" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Sign-in page demo">
  <CenteredLayout width="sm" class="min-h-full">
    <template #logo><Badge>Sample logo</Badge></template>
    <template #header><h4 class="text-xl font-semibold">Sample sign-in</h4><p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sample subtitle.</p></template>
    <VStack :gap="3">
      <Input type="email" placeholder="Email" aria-label="Email" />
      <Button>Continue</Button>
    </VStack>
    <template #footer>Sample footer text.</template>
  </CenteredLayout>
</div>
```

Example: Auth card
```vue
<div class="h-96 overflow-auto rounded-md border" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Auth card demo">
  <CenteredLayout layout="card" width="sm" class="min-h-full">
    <template #header><h4 class="text-xl font-semibold">Sample sign-up</h4><p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sample subtitle.</p></template>
    <VStack :gap="3">
      <Input type="email" placeholder="Email" aria-label="Email" />
      <Button>Create sample account</Button>
    </VStack>
    <template #footer>Sample footer text.</template>
  </CenteredLayout>
</div>
```

Example: Side illustration
```vue

  <CenteredLayout layout="split" width="sm" class="min-h-full">
    <template #header><h4 class="text-xl font-semibold">Sample split page</h4></template>
    <VStack :gap="3">
      <Input type="email" placeholder="Email" aria-label="Email" />

    </VStack>
```


# PageHeader
group: layout / Page structure
Page title block with description, breadcrumb, back link, tabs, actions, centered / compact / hero variants and optional sticky mode.

Put one `PageHeader` at the top of every page view. The title renders in an `h1` (change with `titleAs`), the description below it, a `breadcrumb` slot above, and `actions` on the right (stacked below on small screens). Set `sticky` to pin it to the top of the scroll container with an opaque background and bottom border. Variants: `default` (heading left, actions right), `centered` (everything centred, e.g. marketing and empty states; `align="center"` centres any variant), `compact` (tighter spacing and a smaller title for dense or nested pages) and `hero` (banner with a flat `background`: `muted`, `primary` or an `image` via `backgroundImage`, plus a `background` slot for custom art). Add a back link with `backHref` (or the `back` slot for a router link) and sub-navigation with the `tabs` slot. For app-wide top bars use the `header` slot of AppShell instead.

import { PageHeader } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- title: string - Title text. Use the `title` slot for rich content.
- description: string - Supporting text under the title. Use the `description` slot for rich content.
- titleAs: 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6' | 'div' | 'p' = 'h1' - Element for the title. Keep h1 unless the page already has one.
- variant: 'default' | 'centered' | 'compact' | 'hero' = 'default' - `centered` centres everything; `compact` = gap-2, pb-2 and a text-lg title; `hero` = rounded bordered banner with larger padding and a text-3xl/4xl title. Unknown values fall back to default. Sets `data-variant` when not default.
- align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - Centre the content for any variant (same as `variant="centered"`). Unknown values fall back to start.
- background: 'muted' | 'primary' | 'image' = 'muted' - Hero only. `muted` = flat muted surface; `primary` = solid primary with primary-foreground text; `image` = `backgroundImage` under an overlay (falls back to muted without an image). Defaults to `image` when only `backgroundImage` is set. The former `gradient` value was removed and falls back to `muted`. Ignored by other variants.
- backgroundImage: string - Hero only: image URL drawn behind the content (an `img` with empty alt, `object-cover`, under a bg-background/70 overlay so text stays readable).
- backHref: string - Renders a back link (chevron + label) above the breadcrumb pointing here. Empty values render nothing; the `back` slot wins.
- backLabel: string = 'Back' - Text of the back link.
- sticky: boolean = false - sticky top-0 with z-sticky, an opaque bg-background, border-b and padding.
- tabsLabel: string = 'Tabs' - Accessible name of the `tabs` row while it overflows and scrolls: then it is a focusable `region` with this name.
- as: string | Component = 'header' - Root element.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- title - Overrides the `title` prop.
- description - Overrides the `description` prop.
- breadcrumb - Rendered above the title (e.g. a Breadcrumb).
- actions - Right-aligned buttons (centred in centered mode); wraps under the heading below the sm breakpoint.
- back - Custom back link (e.g. a RouterLink). Replaces the `backHref` link.
- tabs - Sub-navigation (e.g. TabsList) rendered under the heading; scrolls horizontally when it overflows.
- background - Hero only: custom background art, absolutely positioned behind the content (decorative; mark aria-hidden).

Rules:
- Use variant="hero" once per landing page; use compact for sub-pages and dense dashboards.
- Use backHref for simple links and the #back slot for router links; use the #tabs slot for page sub-navigation (Tabs/TabsList).
- Hero backgrounds are flat tokens: `muted`, `primary` or an image. There are no gradients.
- background and backgroundImage only apply to variant="hero"; backgroundImage is decorative (empty alt).
- Use exactly one PageHeader (with the h1) per page; set titleAs="h2" (or the next level down) for nested ones so the outline never skips a level.
- Put primary page actions in the `actions` slot; at most one `default` Button.
- The sticky mode sticks to the nearest scroll container.

Accessibility:
- Title is an h1 by default: one per page.
- Root is a <header>; breadcrumb should be its own labelled <nav>.
- Sticky mode keeps the header in the tab order position; it does not trap focus. The background is opaque so scrolled content never shows through the title.
- The `tabs` row is a focusable, labelled region (`tabsLabel`) only while it overflows horizontally, so it is never an empty Tab stop.
- Responsive: actions wrap under the heading below `sm`; the title uses `text-balance` and the heading block has `min-w-0`, so long titles wrap at 320px instead of overflowing.
- The back link is a real <a> with visible focus ring; the chevron is aria-hidden. Hero background images have an empty alt and are aria-hidden: do not put information in them.
- Give the tabs slot content its own accessible name (e.g. `aria-label` on TabsList).

Example: Title and description
```vue
<PageHeader title-as="h4" title="Sample title" description="Sample description under the title." />
```

Example: With actions and breadcrumb
```vue
<PageHeader title-as="h4" title="Sample list" description="Sample description">
  <template #breadcrumb><span>Section / Sample list</span></template>
  <template #actions>
    <Button variant="outline">Export</Button>
    <Button><Icon :icon="faPlus" /> New item</Button>
  </template>
</PageHeader>
```

```vue
  <template #actions><Button>Primary action</Button><Button variant="outline">Secondary action</Button></template>

```

# ResizablePanels
group: layout / Page structure
Two or more panels separated by draggable, keyboard-accessible handles; sizes are percentages that always add up to 100.

Use `ResizablePanels` for IDE-style layouts: a file tree next to an editor, a master/detail view, a console under a preview. Put `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` as alternating direct children (panel, handle, panel, ...). Sizes are percentages with `defaultSize` / `minSize` / `maxSize` per panel; they are always normalised to sum 100 and clamped, whatever you pass (NaN, negative, sums other than 100). Bind `v-model:sizes` to read or control the layout, or set `storageKey` to remember it in localStorage. A panel can be `collapsible`. Dragging uses pointer events (mouse, touch and pen); the handle is a focusable `separator` with arrow-key, Shift, Home / End and Enter support. For a fixed, non-resizable split use `SplitLayout`. The root fills its parent (`h-full w-full`): give it a height with `class`. For an exact server-rendered first paint give every panel a `defaultSize`; sizes are finalised right after mount.

import { ResizablePanels, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - `horizontal` lays panels in a row (the handles are vertical bars); `vertical` stacks them. Unknown values fall back to horizontal.
- sizes: number[] - Controlled sizes in percent (`v-model:sizes`), one per panel in DOM order. Ignored while its length differs from the panel count; normalised and clamped.
- storageKey: string - localStorage key. Layout is restored after mount and saved after each completed resize. Missing / throwing storage and corrupt JSON are ignored.
- step: number = 5 - Arrow-key step in percent. Invalid values fall back to 5.
- largeStep: number = 20 - Step in percent while Shift is held. Invalid values fall back to 20.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disable every handle.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes (e.g. `h-64`).

Parts:
- ResizablePanel - A sized region. Direct child of `ResizablePanels`; its content scrolls / clips independently (`overflow-hidden` by default, override with `class`).
    - defaultSize: number - Initial size in percent. Missing or invalid values (NaN, negative) share the remaining space equally.
    - minSize: number = 0 - Minimum size in percent.
    - maxSize: number = 100 - Maximum size in percent (never below minSize).
    - collapsible: boolean = false - Collapses to `collapsedSize` when dragged below half of `minSize`, or with Enter on an adjacent handle. Sets `data-collapsed`.
    - collapsedSize: number = 0 - Size in percent while collapsed (0 .. minSize).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.
- ResizableHandle - The draggable divider (`role="separator"`) between two panels. Exposes `aria-valuenow` (size of the preceding panel), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`.
    - variant: 'line' | 'bar' = 'line' - `line` = hairline with a wide hit area; `bar` = thicker muted track.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Visible thickness. `line`: sm and md 1px, lg 2px. `bar`: sm 4px, md 8px, lg 12px. The 24px hit area never changes. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - label: string - Accessible name of the separator. Required: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` must say which panels it resizes.
    - grip: boolean = false - Show a small grip in the middle. The default slot replaces it.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disable this handle only: leaves the tab order, gets `aria-disabled`, ignores pointer and keys.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - ResizablePanel and ResizableHandle children, alternating.

Events:
- update:sizes [sizes: number[]] - Layout changed by the user (drag, keyboard, collapse) or via `setSizes`.
- resizeStart - A pointer drag started.
- resizeEnd [sizes: number[]] - A pointer drag ended (also on cancel).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when ResizablePanels has no ResizablePanel, starts or ends with a ResizableHandle, or has two panels or two handles in a row.
- Throws a ContractError when a ResizableHandle has none of `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a ResizablePanel or ResizableHandle is used outside ResizablePanels.

Rules:
- Children of ResizablePanels must alternate ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel ...; never put two handles in a row.
- Give ResizablePanels an explicit height (`class="h-64"`) or a sized parent; the root is `h-full w-full`.
- Sizes are percentages summing to 100; do not compute pixel widths yourself.
- Use `v-model:sizes` with an array whose length equals the panel count, or `storage-key` for persistence; not both.
- Add `aria-label` to every ResizableHandle.
- For a static split use SplitLayout instead.

Accessibility:
- Each handle is `role="separator"` with `tabindex="0"`, `aria-orientation` (a horizontal row of panels has VERTICAL separators), `aria-valuenow` (size % of the preceding panel), `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.
- Keyboard: Arrow keys along the layout axis resize by `step` (Shift = `largeStep`); Home / End jump to the smallest / largest size reachable; Enter toggles a collapsible neighbour. Arrows flip in right-to-left containers.
- Always give handles an `aria-label` that says what they resize (the `label` prop; default "Resize panels"). Disabled handles leave the tab order and set `aria-disabled`.
- Pointer target: the 1px line handle has a 24px-wide invisible hit area (WCAG 2.5.8); the keyboard alternative to dragging is the Arrow/Home/End map above (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Focus shows as a ring-coloured handle plus a transparent outline, so it is visible in forced-colors mode. The `line` handle fills with `CanvasText` there (hover, focus and drag included) and the `bar` handle draws a border, because forced-colors mode drops background tokens; the idle outline that `outline-hidden` would add is removed so the divider stays a clean line. Panels stay side by side at every width; give the root a sensible `min-w-0` parent so it does not overflow at 320px.
- Handle `size` changes the visible thickness only: the 24px hit area, keyboard map and `aria-value*` attributes are identical at every size. Prefer `lg` when the divider is the main control of the layout.
- Handle transitions and hover colours respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Example: Side by side
```vue
<ResizablePanels class="h-40 rounded-md border">
  <ResizablePanel :default-size="30" :min-size="15" :max-size="60"><div class="p-3 text-sm">Sidebar</div></ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize sidebar" />
  <ResizablePanel :default-size="70"><div class="p-3 text-sm">Sample content</div></ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanels>
```

Example: Vertical with a grip
```vue
<ResizablePanels orientation="vertical" class="h-56 rounded-md border">
  <ResizablePanel :default-size="65"><div class="p-3 text-sm">Preview</div></ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle grip aria-label="Resize console" />
  <ResizablePanel :default-size="35" :min-size="10"><div class="p-3 text-sm">Console</div></ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanels>
```

Example: Three panels, v-model:sizes
```vue

</script>

    <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize B and C" />

  </ResizablePanels>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ sizes.map((s) => Math.round(s)).join(' / ') }}</p>

```

Example: Collapsible and persisted

Example: Handle sizes

```vue
  <ResizablePanels class="h-16 rounded-md border">
    <ResizablePanel><div class="p-2 text-sm">line lg</div></ResizablePanel>
```

```vue
    <ResizablePanel><div class="p-2 text-sm">line</div></ResizablePanel>
```

# SplitLayout
group: layout / Page structure
Two-pane layout (start / end) with ratio presets, fixed-width pane and responsive stacking.

Use `SplitLayout` for master/detail views, settings with a side panel, or content next to a preview. Choose a `ratio` preset (`1:1`, `1:2`, `2:1`, `1:3`, `3:1` as start:end; the older `equal`, `1/3`, `2/3` still work as aliases of `1:1`, `1:2`, `2:1`) or pin one pane to a CSS length with `fixed-start` / `fixed-end` + `fixedWidth`. Below the `stackBelow` breakpoint the panes stack vertically. Use `sticky="start"` or `"end"` to keep one pane (filters, summary, table of contents) in view while the other scrolls, and `reverseOnMobile` to show the end pane first when stacked (e.g. a summary above the form). Panes do not scroll by themselves; add `overflow-auto` and a height via `class` on the content you slot in. For resizable panes use a dedicated Resizable component.

import { SplitLayout } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- ratio: 'equal' | '1:1' | '1/3' | '1:2' | '2/3' | '2:1' | '1:3' | '3:1' | 'fixed-start' | 'fixed-end' = 'equal' - Column split, start:end. `1:1` = `equal`; `1:2` = `1/3` (start gets a third); `2:1` = `2/3` (start gets two thirds); `1:3` and `3:1` quarter splits. Unknown values fall back to equal.
- fixedWidth: string = '16rem' - CSS length of the fixed pane, set through the `--split-fixed` CSS variable. Only used by fixed-start / fixed-end.
- stackBelow: 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Breakpoint below which the panes stack vertically.
- gap: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 = 0 - Gap between panes.
- divider: boolean = false - Border between the panes (horizontal when stacked, vertical when side by side).
- sticky: 'start' | 'end' - Makes that pane sticky (self-start, top = stickyOffset) once side by side. Unknown values are ignored. Sets `data-sticky`.
- stickyOffset: string = '1rem' - CSS length for the sticky pane top offset, set through the `--split-sticky-top` CSS variable. Empty values fall back to 1rem.
- reverseOnMobile: boolean = false - While stacked, show the end pane first (max-md:order-first / max-lg:order-first). DOM order is unchanged. Sets `data-reverse-mobile`.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Root element.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- start - First pane (left in LTR).
- end - Second pane (right in LTR).

Rules:
- Slots are named `start` and `end`.
- The ratio, fixedWidth and stickyOffset are applied as CSS variables (the only inline styles); pass any valid CSS length.
- Prefer a:b ratios (`1:2`, `2:1`) in new code; `1/3` and `2/3` are legacy aliases.
- Use sticky + stickyOffset for side summaries/filters; the sticky pane sticks to the nearest scroll container and only once side by side.
- reverseOnMobile changes visual order only; keep the important pane first in the DOM for screen readers.
- Panes use min-w-0 so wide content does not overflow; set overflow on your own content.

Accessibility:
- Presentational grid; DOM order (start, then end) is the reading and tab order, including when stacked. With `reverseOnMobile` the visual order differs from the DOM order, so only use it when both orders make sense.
- Use `as` with a landmark (`section`) and aria-label when a pane is a distinct region.
- Responsive: panes stack in one column below `stackBelow` (`md` by default, 768px; `lg` = 1024px) and both panes have `min-w-0`, so nothing overflows at 320px. A scrolling container around a sticky pane must be focusable and labelled (see the live example).
- Ratios and the fixed width are applied through CSS variables (`--split-cols`, `--split-fixed`) so they follow the same breakpoint as the stack.

Example: Ratios
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <SplitLayout ratio="1/3" :gap="4">
    <template #start><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">1/3</div></template>
    <template #end><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">2/3</div></template>
  </SplitLayout>
  <SplitLayout ratio="equal" :gap="4">
    <template #start><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">50%</div></template>
    <template #end><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">50%</div></template>
  </SplitLayout>
</div>
```

Example: Fixed sidebar with divider
```vue
<SplitLayout ratio="fixed-start" fixed-width="12rem" divider class="rounded-md border">
  <template #start><div class="p-3 text-sm">Fixed 12rem</div></template>
  <template #end><div class="p-3 text-sm">Fluid remainder</div></template>
</SplitLayout>
```

Example: Quarter ratios
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <SplitLayout ratio="1:3" :gap="4">
    <template #start><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">1</div></template>
    <template #end><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">3</div></template>
  </SplitLayout>
  <SplitLayout ratio="2:1" :gap="4">
    <template #start><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">2</div></template>
    <template #end><div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">1</div></template>
  </SplitLayout>
</div>
```

Example: Sticky pane
```vue
<div class="h-48 overflow-auto rounded-md border p-2" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Sticky pane demo">
  <SplitLayout ratio="2:1" :gap="4" sticky="end" sticky-offset="0.5rem">
    <template #start><div class="h-96 rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">Long sample content, scroll the box</div></template>
    <template #end><div class="rounded-md border bg-card p-3 text-sm">Sample sticky pane</div></template>
```

```vue
  <template #start><div class="p-3 text-sm">Sample form (first in the DOM)</div></template>

```

Example: Stack below lg
```vue

  <template #start><Badge>Start pane</Badge></template>
  <template #end><Badge variant="secondary">End pane</Badge></template>
</SplitLayout>
```

# Affix
group: layout / Scrolling
Pins content with `position: sticky` and reports whether it is currently stuck.

Wrap a toolbar, table of contents or summary card in `Affix` so it stays visible while the page (or a scroll container, via `root`) scrolls. Positioning is pure CSS (`sticky` plus an inline `top` / `bottom` from `offsetTop` / `offsetBottom` in px); an `IntersectionObserver` watching a 1px sentinel placed next to the content drives the `change` event, the `data-stuck` attribute and the `stuck` slot prop (a scroll-listener fallback is used when IntersectionObserver is unavailable). The `variant` prop adds a shadow or border only while stuck. Sticky only works while the nearest scrolling ancestor and the parent are taller than the content: do not put `overflow: hidden` on ancestors. The sentinel is a zero-net-height inline-block sibling next to the content, so avoid parents that add `gap` between children. For two-column layouts use `SplitLayout` with `sticky`.

import { Affix } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- offsetTop: number - Pixels from the top of the scroll container where the content sticks. Defaults to 0 unless only `offsetBottom` is given. Non-finite values are ignored; negative values are allowed.
- offsetBottom: number - Pixels from the bottom edge (pins to the bottom). Drives stuck detection only when `offsetTop` is not set; both are applied inline when both are set.
- zIndex: number | string = 'var(--z-sticky)' token - A number or any CSS value such as `var(--z-overlay)`. Invalid values fall back to the `--z-sticky` token.
- variant: 'plain' | 'elevated' | 'bordered' = 'plain' - Look while stuck: `elevated` adds background + shadow, `bordered` background + edge border. Unknown values fall back to plain.
- disabled: boolean = false - Render as a normal block: not sticky, no observer, never stuck.
- root: HTMLElement | string | null = null - Scroll container as an element or CSS selector. `null` or not found = the viewport.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge (e.g. `z-10`, `bg-card`); wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ stuck: boolean }) - The pinned content.

Events:
- change [stuck: boolean] - The stuck state flipped. Not emitted for the initial not-stuck state.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `root` is a selector that matches no element (or is not a valid selector), because the Affix would silently watch the viewport.

Rules:
- Use `offset-top` / `offset-bottom` numbers (px), not inline style, for the sticky distance.
- Use `z-index` with a CSS variable such as `var(--z-overlay)` rather than magic numbers when layering.
- Sticky fails if an ancestor has overflow hidden/auto without a height; point `root` at the real scroll container.
- Attributes (id, aria-label, data-*) land on the pinned element, not on a wrapper; the component renders a sentinel sibling before/after it.

Accessibility:
- Affix adds no role or label of its own: put landmarks (`role="toolbar"`, `<nav aria-label>`) on the content or pass `aria-*` attributes, which fall through to the pinned element.
- The sentinel is `aria-hidden` and not focusable. Stuck styling never hides content; ensure the pinned element does not cover focused elements below it (use scroll-padding on the container).
- Transitions are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- When `root` is a scrolling box, that box must itself be keyboard reachable: give it `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and an `aria-label` (the live example does), or axe reports scrollable-region-focusable.
- The `elevated` variant also gets the opaque `bg-background`, and a border in forced-colors mode (shadows disappear there), so stuck content is distinguishable from the scrolled content without relying on the shadow alone.

Example: Sticky toolbar with stuck state
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const stuck = ref(false)
</script>

<div id="affix-demo-scroll" class="h-48 overflow-auto rounded-md border" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Sticky toolbar demo">
  <Affix root="#affix-demo-scroll" variant="elevated" class="px-3 py-2" @change="stuck = $event">
    <span class="text-sm font-medium">Toolbar ({{ stuck ? 'stuck' : 'in flow' }})</span>
  </Affix>
  <div class="grid gap-2 p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="text-sm">Paragraph {{ n }}</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: Offset below a header and a bottom bar
```vue
<div id="affix-offset-scroll" class="relative h-64 overflow-auto rounded-md border" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Offset demo">
  <div class="sticky top-0 z-40 flex h-12 items-center border-b bg-card px-3 text-sm text-card-foreground">Header, 48px</div>
  <Affix root="#affix-offset-scroll" :offset-top="48" :z-index="30" variant="bordered" class="px-3 py-2 text-sm">Pins 48px from the top</Affix>
  <div class="grid gap-2 p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 8" :key="n" class="text-sm">Paragraph {{ n }}</p>
  </div>
  <Affix root="#affix-offset-scroll" :offset-bottom="40" :z-index="30" variant="bordered" class="px-3 py-2 text-sm">Pins 40px from the bottom</Affix>
  <div class="grid gap-2 p-3">
    <p v-for="n in 8" :key="n" class="text-sm">Paragraph {{ n + 8 }}</p>
  </div>
  <div class="sticky bottom-0 z-40 flex h-10 items-center border-t bg-card px-3 text-sm text-card-foreground">Bottom bar, 40px</div>
</div>
```

Example: Bordered variant and disabled
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <Affix variant="bordered" class="px-3 py-2 text-sm">Border appears when stuck</Affix>
  <Affix disabled class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">Disabled: behaves like a plain block</Affix>
</div>
```

# InfiniteScroll
group: layout / Scrolling
Fires `load` when the end of a list scrolls into view; handles loading, end-of-list and error-with-retry states.

Wrap the items of a feed, table or list in `InfiniteScroll`. A hidden sentinel after the content is watched with `IntersectionObserver` (with a scroll-listener fallback when it is unavailable); when it comes within `rootMargin` of the viewport (or of your scroll container via `root`) the component emits `load` once. Set `loading` synchronously in your handler and clear it when the page arrived: the sentinel is re-checked after every loading cycle, so a still-visible sentinel loads the next page. Set `finished` when no more data exists and `error` to show a retry affordance. Do not use it for page-numbered data (use pagination) or for rendering thousands of rows (pair it with VirtualList).

import { InfiniteScroll } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- loading: boolean = false - A page is being fetched: shows the loading slot and blocks `load`. Set it synchronously inside `@load`.
- finished: boolean = false - No more data: shows the end slot and stops observing.
- error: boolean | string = false - Last fetch failed: shows the error slot with a retry button and stops auto-loading. A string is used as the message.
- disabled: boolean = false - Pause loading (no observer, no `load`).
- root: HTMLElement | string | null = null - Scroll container as an element or CSS selector (resolved after mount). `null` or not found = the viewport.
- rootMargin: string = '200px' - IntersectionObserver rootMargin: how early `load` fires. Invalid values fall back to the scroll-listener path.
- variant: 'default' | 'compact' = 'default' - Footer density for the loading, end and error blocks. `default`: py-4, error message above the retry button. `compact`: py-2, message and retry on one wrapping row. Sets `data-variant` when not default. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Footer text and spinner size: sm text-xs with a 12px spinner, md text-sm with 16px, lg text-base with 20px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - The loaded items.
- loading - Shown while `loading` (default: spinner + "Loading…").
- end - Shown when `finished` (default: "No more results.").
- error ({ retry: () => void, error: boolean | string }) - Shown when `error` (default: message + "Try again" button). Call `retry` to emit `retry` + `load`.

Events:
- load - Fetch the next page. Emitted once per intersection; never while `loading`, `finished`, `error` or `disabled`.
- retry - The retry button was used; `load` follows immediately.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when nothing listens for `load` (unless `finished` is set), because no page would ever be fetched.
- Throws a ContractError when `root` is a selector that matches no element (or is not a valid selector).

Rules:
- Set `loading` to true synchronously in the `@load` handler and false when done; set `finished` when the API returns no more pages.
- On failure set `error` (not `finished`) so the user can retry; clear it on `@retry`/`@load`.
- Inside a scrolling div pass `root` (element or selector); otherwise the viewport is observed.
- Do not emit your own scroll listeners; the component already falls back when IntersectionObserver is missing.

Accessibility:
- The status area is a polite live region (`role="status"`); the loading and end messages are announced when they appear. The root gets `aria-busy` while loading.
- The error block is `role="alert"`; the default retry is a real `button`. Custom error slots must provide a keyboard-reachable retry control.
- The sentinel is `aria-hidden`. Consider also offering a manual "Load more" button for keyboard users on very long feeds.
- Spinner animation is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- `variant` and `size` change spacing and text size only; the live region, `role="alert"` error block and retry button are the same in every combination. The compact error row wraps, so it does not overflow at 320px.
- The default retry button is at least 24px high (44px on coarse pointers) and has the shared focus ring.
- When `root` is a scrolling box, give that box `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and an `aria-label` so keyboard users can scroll it.

Example: Load pages on demand
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = ref(Array.from({ length: 5 }, (_, i) => i + 1))
const loading = ref(false)
const finished = ref(false)
async function load() {
  loading.value = true
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))
  items.value.push(...Array.from({ length: 5 }, (_, i) => items.value.length + i + 1))
  loading.value = false
  finished.value = items.value.length >= 20
}
</script>

<InfiniteScroll :loading="loading" :finished="finished" class="grid gap-2" @load="load">
  <div v-for="n in items" :key="n" class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">Sample row {{ n }}</div>
</InfiniteScroll>
```

Example: Inside a scroll container with an error state
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const failed = ref(true)
</script>

<div id="infinite-demo-scroll" class="h-40 overflow-auto rounded-md border p-2" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Infinite scroll demo">
  <InfiniteScroll root="#infinite-demo-scroll" root-margin="0px 0px 40px 0px" :error="failed ? 'Could not reach the server.' : false" @load="failed = false">
    <div v-for="n in 8" :key="n" class="border-b py-2 text-sm">Item {{ n }}</div>
    <template #error="{ retry, error }">
      <p class="text-sm">{{ error }}</p>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="retry">Retry</Button>
    </template>
  </InfiniteScroll>
</div>
```

Example: Footer variants and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
  <div class="rounded-md border"><InfiniteScroll loading finished><p class="px-3 pt-3 text-sm">Default, loading</p></InfiniteScroll></div>
  <div class="rounded-md border"><InfiniteScroll loading finished variant="compact"><p class="px-3 pt-3 text-sm">Compact, loading</p></InfiniteScroll></div>
  <div class="rounded-md border"><InfiniteScroll finished size="sm"><p class="px-3 pt-3 text-sm">Small, end</p></InfiniteScroll></div>
  <div class="rounded-md border"><InfiniteScroll finished size="lg"><p class="px-3 pt-3 text-sm">Large, end</p></InfiniteScroll></div>
  <div class="rounded-md border"><InfiniteScroll finished error="Could not reach the server."><p class="px-3 pt-3 text-sm">Default, error</p></InfiniteScroll></div>
  <div class="rounded-md border"><InfiniteScroll finished error="Could not reach the server." variant="compact"><p class="px-3 pt-3 text-sm">Compact, error</p></InfiniteScroll></div>
</div>
```

Example: Finished with a custom end slot
```vue
<InfiniteScroll finished class="grid gap-2">
  <div class="rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">Only sample item</div>
  <template #end><p class="text-center text-xs text-muted-foreground">No more items.</p></template>
</InfiniteScroll>
```

# Grid
group: layout / Stacks & grids
CSS grid with 1-12 columns, per-breakpoint column counts and a gap scale.

Use `Grid` for card galleries, stat rows and form layouts. Set `cols` for the base (mobile) count and `sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl` to change it from that breakpoint upwards (mobile-first). All class names come from fixed maps so Tailwind generates them. Invalid column numbers fall back to 1 (base) or are ignored (breakpoints). For content-driven grids set `minItemWidth` (e.g. `16rem`): the grid fits as many columns as possible, each at least that wide (`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr))`), so no breakpoints are needed. Add `autoFill` to keep empty tracks. `gapSm` / `gapMd` / `gapLg` grow the gap responsively. `variant` draws each direct child as a `bordered` or `card` cell and `layout` sets emphasis: `lead` makes the first item span the whole row, `feature` makes it span 2 columns and 2 rows from `md` up (use at least 3 columns from `md`). For other span control apply your own classes on the children.

import { Grid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- cols: 1 | 2 | … | 12 = 1 - Base column count. Invalid values fall back to 1.
- sm: 1 | 2 | … | 12 - Columns from the `sm` breakpoint up.
- md: 1 | 2 | … | 12 - Columns from the `md` breakpoint up.
- lg: 1 | 2 | … | 12 - Columns from the `lg` breakpoint up.
- xl: 1 | 2 | … | 12 - Columns from the `xl` breakpoint up.
- gap: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 = 4 - Gap on both axes. Invalid values fall back to 4.
- gapSm: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Gap from the `sm` breakpoint up (sm:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.
- gapMd: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Gap from the `md` breakpoint up (md:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.
- gapLg: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Gap from the `lg` breakpoint up (lg:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.
- minItemWidth: string | number - Auto-fit mode: columns are at least this wide and as many as fit. Number = px, string = CSS length (`16rem`, `240px`, `20ch`, `30%`). Set through the `--grid-min` CSS variable; replaces base `cols`; breakpoint props (`sm`/`md`/...) still override it. Invalid values are ignored.
- autoFill: boolean = false - With `minItemWidth`: use `auto-fill` (keeps empty tracks) instead of `auto-fit` (collapses empty tracks so items stretch).
- gapX: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Column gap. Wins over `gap` and over `gapSm`/`gapMd`/`gapLg` horizontally at every breakpoint.
- gapY: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Row gap. Wins over `gap` and over `gapSm`/`gapMd`/`gapLg` vertically at every breakpoint.
- variant: 'plain' | 'bordered' | 'card' = 'plain' - Cell look for every direct child. `plain`: none. `bordered`: rounded-lg, border, p-4. `card`: bordered bg-card cell with text-card-foreground. Cells get min-w-0. Applied with child selectors, so override with `class` on the grid (e.g. `[&>*]:p-6`). Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- layout: 'uniform' | 'lead' | 'feature' = 'uniform' - `uniform`: equal cells. `lead`: the first item spans the full row at every width. `feature`: from `md` up the first item spans 2 columns and 2 rows (needs 3 or more columns from `md`); below `md` it is a normal cell. Unknown values fall back to `uniform`.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render, e.g. `ul`.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Grid items.

Rules:
- Write numbers as bound props: `:cols="3" :md="4"` (not cols="3" md="4").
- Mobile-first: `cols` is the smallest screen; sm/md/lg/xl only override upwards.
- Only 1-12 are valid for cols. For card galleries prefer `min-item-width="16rem"` (auto-fit) over breakpoint columns.
- minItemWidth takes a number (px) or a plain CSS length string; calc()/var() are rejected and ignored.
- Use gapSm/gapMd/gapLg for responsive spacing (mobile-first).
- Use `variant="card"` for card galleries instead of styling every child; put the most important item first and use `layout="lead"` or `"feature"` so it gets more room than the rest.

Accessibility:
- Presentational. Source order = reading order; do not reorder items with CSS in a way that breaks it.
- Use `as="ul"` with `<li>` children for lists of cards.
- Responsive: `cols` is the mobile (320px) layout, so start at 1 and add columns with `sm`/`md`/`lg`. `minItemWidth` clamps each track with `min(100%, width)`, so a track never exceeds the container and the grid cannot overflow at 320px.
- Item content that must be able to shrink needs `min-w-0` (grid items default to `min-width: auto`); cells drawn by `variant` already have it.
- `lead` and `feature` only change spans, not source order, so reading order is unchanged. `feature` applies from `md` up, so the layout is a single column at 320px.

Example: Responsive columns
```vue
<Grid :cols="1" :sm="2" :lg="4" :gap="3">
  <div v-for="n in 8" :key="n" class="rounded-md border bg-card p-4 text-sm">Sample item {{ n }}</div>
</Grid>
```

Example: Different row and column gaps
```vue
<Grid :cols="3" :gap-x="6" :gap-y="2">
  <Badge v-for="n in 6" :key="n" variant="secondary">Cell {{ n }}</Badge>
</Grid>
```

Example: Auto-fit with minItemWidth
```vue
<Grid min-item-width="12rem" :gap="3">
  <div v-for="n in 6" :key="n" class="rounded-md border bg-card p-4 text-sm">Sample card {{ n }}</div>
</Grid>
```

Example: Auto-fill and numeric width
```vue
<Grid :min-item-width="160" auto-fill :gap="3">
  <div v-for="n in 2" :key="n" class="rounded-md border bg-card p-4 text-sm">Sample card {{ n }}</div>
</Grid>
```

Example: Responsive gaps
```vue
<Grid :cols="2" :gap="2" :gap-md="4" :gap-lg="8">
  <Badge v-for="n in 4" :key="n" variant="secondary">Cell {{ n }}</Badge>
</Grid>
```

Example: Cell variants
```vue
<div class="space-y-4">
  <Grid :cols="1" :sm="3" :gap="3" variant="bordered">
    <div v-for="n in 3" :key="n" class="text-sm">Bordered cell {{ n }}</div>
  </Grid>
  <Grid :cols="1" :sm="3" :gap="3" variant="card">
    <div v-for="n in 3" :key="n" class="text-sm">Card cell {{ n }}</div>
  </Grid>
</div>
```

Example: Lead and feature layouts
```vue
<div class="space-y-6">
  <Grid :cols="1" :sm="3" :gap="3" layout="lead" variant="card">
    <div class="text-sm font-medium">First item spans the row</div>
    <div v-for="n in 3" :key="n" class="text-sm">Sample item {{ n }}</div>
  </Grid>
  <Grid :cols="1" :md="3" :gap="3" layout="feature" variant="card">
    <div class="text-sm font-medium">First item spans two columns and two rows</div>
    <div v-for="n in 4" :key="n" class="text-sm">Sample item {{ n }}</div>
  </Grid>
</div>
```

Example: Two-column form
```vue
<Grid :cols="1" :md="2" :gap="4" class="max-w-xl">
  <Input placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
  <Input placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
  <Input placeholder="Email" aria-label="Email" class="md:col-span-2" />
</Grid>
```
