# Spacer
group: layout / Stacks & grids
Flexible (flex-1) or fixed-size empty space for use inside flex layouts.

Without `size`, `Spacer` grows to fill free space in a flex container, pushing siblings apart (e.g. logo left, actions right). With `size` it becomes a fixed gap along `axis`. Sizes run 0-6, 8, 10, 12 and the section-level steps 14, 16, 20 and 24; `sizeMd` and `sizeLg` change the size from a breakpoint up (mobile-first), for example tight on a phone and 24 units between page sections on a desktop. Prefer the `gap` prop of Stack/Grid for uniform spacing and use Spacer for one-off gaps or push-apart behaviour. Always `aria-hidden`.

import { Spacer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- size: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 20 | 24 - Fixed size from the spacing scale. Omit (or pass an invalid value) for flexible flex-1.
- sizeMd: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 20 | 24 - Size from the `md` breakpoint up (md:h-* / md:w-*). Ignored without a valid `size`; invalid values are ignored.
- sizeLg: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 20 | 24 - Size from the `lg` breakpoint up (lg:h-* / lg:w-*). Ignored without a valid `size`; invalid values are ignored.
- axis: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Which dimension `size` sets: vertical = height, horizontal = width.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Rules:
- A Spacer without `size` only works inside a flex container.
- Do not use Spacer for uniform spacing; use the gap prop of Stack/Grid.
- sizeMd / sizeLg need a `size`; set `size` to the smallest-screen value.

Accessibility:
- Rendered with aria-hidden="true"; contains no content.
- Large fixed sizes (16 to 24 units = 64 to 96px) are fixed lengths: use `sizeMd` / `sizeLg` and start small so the spacing does not crowd a 320px screen.

Example: Push items apart
```vue
<HStack class="rounded-md border p-2">
  <Badge>Start</Badge>
  <Spacer />
  <Button size="sm">End</Button>
</HStack>
```

Example: Fixed sizes
```vue
<div>
  <Badge>Above</Badge>
  <Spacer :size="8" />
  <Badge>Below (8 units later)</Badge>
</div>
<HStack class="mt-4">
  <Badge>Left</Badge>
  <Spacer :size="6" axis="horizontal" />
  <Badge>Right</Badge>
</HStack>
```

Example: Section spacing that grows with the screen
```vue
<div>
  <Badge>First section</Badge>
  <Spacer :size="8" :size-md="16" :size-lg="24" />
  <Badge>Second section</Badge>
</div>
<HStack class="mt-4">
  <Badge>Left</Badge>
  <Spacer axis="horizontal" :size="4" :size-md="12" />
  <Badge>Right</Badge>
</HStack>
```

# Stack
group: layout / Stacks & grids
Flex container that lays children out in a row or column with consistent gaps.

Use `Stack` for one-dimensional layout with a gap scale instead of `flex flex-col gap-4` snippets. `HStack` (row, vertically centred) and `VStack` (column) are thin wrappers that preset `direction`. Responsive gaps (`gapSm` / `gapMd` / `gapLg`) grow the gap from a breakpoint up, `collapse` turns a horizontal stack into a column on small screens, and `divided` draws separators between children. `variant` gives the stack itself a surface (`bordered`, `card`, `muted`) and `padding` sets its inner padding, so a card-like panel needs no wrapper. For two-dimensional layouts use `Grid`; for pushing items apart inside a stack add a `Spacer`.

import { Stack, HStack, VStack } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- direction: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Main axis (flex-col / flex-row).
- gap: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 = 4 - Gap between children (Tailwind spacing scale). Invalid values fall back to 4.
- gapSm: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Gap from the `sm` breakpoint up (sm:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.
- gapMd: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Gap from the `md` breakpoint up (md:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.
- gapLg: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 - Gap from the `lg` breakpoint up (lg:gap-*). Invalid values are ignored.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' | 'baseline' - Cross-axis alignment (align-items). Unset keeps the browser default (stretch).
- justify: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'between' | 'around' | 'evenly' - Main-axis distribution (justify-content).
- wrap: boolean = false - Allow children to wrap (flex-wrap).
- collapse: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Horizontal stacks only: column below this breakpoint, row from it up (flex-col md:flex-row). Unknown values are ignored.
- divided: boolean = false - Border between children: divide-y (vertical) or divide-x (horizontal) with the border token.
- variant: 'plain' | 'bordered' | 'card' | 'muted' = 'plain' - Surface of the stack. `plain`: none. `bordered`: rounded-lg with a border. `card`: bordered bg-card panel (text-card-foreground). `muted`: rounded filled panel (secondary token pair). Surfaces add p-4 unless `padding` is set. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- padding: 'auto' | 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'auto' - Inner padding: `auto` = none for `plain`, p-4 for the surfaces; `none` p-0, `sm` p-3, `md` p-4, `lg` p-6. Works on `plain` too. Unknown values fall back to `auto`.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render, e.g. `ul` or `nav`.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- HStack - Stack with `direction="horizontal"` and `align="center"` by default. Accepts every Stack prop except `direction`. Root has `data-slot="h-stack"`.
    - align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' | 'baseline' = 'center' - Cross-axis alignment.
    - gap: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 = 4 - Gap scale.
- VStack - Stack with `direction="vertical"`. Accepts every Stack prop except `direction`. Root has `data-slot="v-stack"`.
    - gap: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 = 4 - Gap scale.

Slots:
- default - Children to lay out.

Rules:
- Use Stack/HStack/VStack instead of ad-hoc flex + gap classes.
- gap accepts only 0-6, 8, 10, 12; other values fall back to 4.
- Use gapSm/gapMd/gapLg for responsive spacing (mobile-first: `gap` is the smallest screen).
- Use `collapse="md"` on a horizontal Stack to stack it on mobile; it has no effect on vertical stacks.
- Use `divided` with `:gap="0"` and padded children for list rows; the separator uses the border token.
- HStack centres items vertically by default; Stack and VStack do not set align.
- Use `variant="card"` instead of wrapping a Stack in a bordered div; set `padding="none"` when rows bring their own padding.
- Put a Spacer inside an HStack to push following items to the end.

Accessibility:
- Purely presentational; use `as="ul"` / `as="nav"` with proper child elements when the content is a list or navigation.
- Visual order follows DOM order; do not rely on flex reordering for reading order.
- Surface variants are decorative boxes with no role; use `as="section"` with an `aria-label` or `as="ul"` when the box is a landmark or list. `card` and `muted` use the tested card and secondary token pairs.
- Responsive: use `collapse` so a horizontal toolbar becomes a column below the breakpoint (mobile first), or `wrap` to let items flow onto new lines; both avoid horizontal overflow at 320px.

Example: Vertical and horizontal
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-6">
  <Stack :gap="2">
    <Badge>One</Badge>
    <Badge variant="secondary">Two</Badge>
  </Stack>
  <Stack direction="horizontal" :gap="2" align="center">
    <Badge>One</Badge>
    <Badge variant="secondary">Two</Badge>
  </Stack>
</div>
```

Example: HStack toolbar and VStack form
```vue
<VStack :gap="4" class="max-w-sm">
  <Input placeholder="Email" aria-label="Email" />
  <HStack justify="between">
    <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </HStack>
</VStack>
```

Example: Responsive gap
```vue
<VStack :gap="2" :gap-md="4" :gap-lg="8">
  <Badge>One</Badge>
  <Badge variant="secondary">Two</Badge>
  <Badge variant="outline">Three</Badge>
</VStack>
```

Example: Collapse to a column on mobile
```vue
<Stack direction="horizontal" collapse="md" :gap="3" align="start">
  <Input placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
  <Button variant="outline">Filter</Button>
  <Button>Apply</Button>
</Stack>
```

Example: Divided list
```vue
<div class="space-y-4">
  <VStack divided :gap="0" class="rounded-md border">
    <div class="p-3 text-sm">Row one</div>
    <div class="p-3 text-sm">Row two</div>
    <div class="p-3 text-sm">Row three</div>
  </VStack>
  <HStack divided :gap="0" class="rounded-md border">
    <div class="flex-1 p-3 text-sm">Col one</div>
    <div class="flex-1 p-3 text-sm">Col two</div>
  </HStack>
</div>
```

Example: Surface variants
```vue
<Grid min-item-width="12rem" :gap="3">
  <VStack :gap="2"><Badge>plain</Badge><span class="text-sm">Plain stack</span></VStack>
  <VStack variant="bordered" :gap="2"><Badge>bordered</Badge><span class="text-sm">Bordered stack</span></VStack>
  <VStack variant="card" :gap="2"><Badge>card</Badge><span class="text-sm">Card stack</span></VStack>
  <VStack variant="muted" :gap="2"><Badge>muted</Badge><span class="text-sm">Muted stack</span></VStack>
</Grid>
```

Example: Card with divided rows and padding
```vue
<VStack variant="card" padding="none" divided :gap="0" class="max-w-sm">
  <div class="p-3 text-sm">Sample row one</div>
  <div class="p-3 text-sm">Sample row two</div>
  <div class="p-3 text-sm">Sample row three</div>
</VStack>
<HStack variant="muted" padding="lg" justify="between" class="mt-4 max-w-sm">
  <span class="text-sm">Large padding</span>
  <Button size="sm">Action</Button>
</HStack>
```

Example: Wrapping chips
```vue
<HStack wrap :gap="2" class="max-w-xs">
  <Badge v-for="n in 8" :key="n" variant="outline">Tag {{ n }}</Badge>
</HStack>
```

# StyleScope
group: layout / Style packs
Applies one style pack (density, corners, depth, type) to everything inside it.

A style pack restyles the whole system by overriding tokens (`--spacing`, `--radius`, shadows, text sizes, fonts, borders), so every component follows without changing its markup. `StyleScope` sets `data-style` on a wrapper, which lets one page mix looks: a dense `workbench` data panel next to the core `quiet` marketing page, or an `editorial` article inside an app. The pack CSS must be imported once (`@perfect-design/ui/packs.css` or a single `@perfect-design/ui/packs/<name>.css`). To switch the whole app, use `useThemeStore().setStyle()` or `StylePicker`, which set `data-style` on `<html>`. The packs are: `quiet` (core), `workbench` (dense, hairlines), `tactile` (raised surfaces), `editorial` (serif, square, reading-first), `raw` (hard shadows, ink borders), `contrast` (7:1 text, bold focus) and `terminal` (mono, dense). Each one is justified in DESIGN.md.

import { StyleScope } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- look*: 'quiet' | 'workbench' | 'tactile' | 'editorial' | 'raw' | 'contrast' | 'terminal' - Style pack for the subtree. `quiet` restores the core look inside another pack.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last.

Slots:
- default - Content styled by the pack.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `look` is not one of the known packs.

Rules:
- Pick a pack for the product (workbench for tools, editorial for reading, quiet for most apps), never per component.
- Do not restyle with inline colours or shadows to imitate a pack; wrap in `StyleScope` or set the pack on `<html>`.
- Import the pack CSS once; without it `StyleScope` has no visible effect.

Accessibility:
- Renders a plain element: no role, no name, no effect on the accessibility tree.
- The `contrast` pack keeps text pairs at 7:1 or better and draws a 3px focus outline; `workbench` and `terminal` restore normal spacing on coarse pointers so touch targets stay at least 44px.
- Motion in `tactile` only runs under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

Example: Workbench panel
```vue
<StyleScope look="workbench" class="rounded-lg border p-4">
  <Stack :gap="3">
    <Input aria-label="Filter" placeholder="Filter rows" />
    <HStack><Button size="sm">Apply</Button><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Reset</Button></HStack>
  </Stack>
</StyleScope>
```

Example: Editorial article
```vue
<StyleScope look="editorial" class="rounded-lg border p-5">
  <h3 class="text-2xl">Reading comes first</h3>
  <p class="mt-2 text-base">Long text sits in a serif face at a comfortable size and line height, with rules instead of shadows.</p>
  <Button class="mt-4" variant="outline">Read the full report</Button>
</StyleScope>
```

Example: Tactile controls
```vue
<StyleScope look="tactile" class="rounded-lg border p-4">
  <HStack><Button>Save</Button><Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button><Badge>Draft</Badge></HStack>
</StyleScope>
```

Example: Raw
```vue
<StyleScope look="raw" class="border-2 p-4">
  <Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Plain facts</CardTitle></CardHeader><CardContent>No softening, no tricks.</CardContent></Card>
</StyleScope>
```

Example: Contrast
```vue
<StyleScope look="contrast" class="rounded-lg border p-4">
  <Stack :gap="3"><Input aria-label="Reference number" placeholder="Reference number" /><Button>Check status</Button></Stack>
</StyleScope>
```

Example: Terminal
```vue
<StyleScope look="terminal" class="rounded-lg border p-4">
  <Stack :gap="3"><Input aria-label="Command" placeholder="deploy --env staging" /><HStack><Button size="sm">Run</Button><Badge variant="outline">exit 0</Badge></HStack></Stack>
</StyleScope>
```

# FormActions
group: forms / Actions
Aligned row of form actions (submit and cancel) with an optional sticky bottom bar and stacking on small screens.

Place `FormActions` at the end of a form. For the common case pass `submitLabel` (and `cancelLabel`) and it renders a primary `type="submit"` Button plus an outline cancel Button; the native form submit still fires, and `submit` / `cancel` are emitted on click. For anything else (extra buttons, links, destructive actions) fill the default slot, which replaces the built-in buttons. `sticky` pins the bar to the bottom of the scroll container for long forms, on an opaque background.

import { FormActions } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- layout: 'stacked' | 'inline' | 'split' = 'stacked' - `stacked`: full-width buttons in a column below `sm`, a row from `sm`. `inline`: a wrapping row at every width. `split`: as `stacked`, but from `sm` the first action sits at the start and the others at the end (a secondary or destructive action apart from the primary one). Every layout keeps DOM order. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'between' = 'end' - Horizontal alignment (applies from `sm` up when stacked). Ignored by `layout="split"`. Invalid values fall back to `end`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Gap between actions (6 / 8 / 12 px), padding of a `bar`, `boxed` or `sticky` surface, and the size of the built-in buttons. Buttons you put in the default slot keep their own size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'plain' | 'bar' | 'boxed' = 'plain' - `plain`: no surface. `bar`: a full-width footer with a top border on an opaque background. `boxed`: a bordered, rounded panel on an opaque background. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- sticky: boolean = false - Stick to the bottom of the scroll container. A `plain` sticky bar gets the `bar` surface (top border, opaque background) so content never shows through.
- stacked: boolean = true - Kept for compatibility: `false` is the same as `layout="inline"` and applies to the default layout only.
- submitLabel: string - Renders the primary `type="submit"` Button with this label.
- cancelLabel: string - Renders an outline Button with this label that emits `cancel`.
- loading: boolean = false - Spinner + aria-busy on the submit button, blocks submit clicks.
- submitDisabled: boolean = false - Disables the submit button.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Custom actions; replaces the `submitLabel` / `cancelLabel` buttons.

Events:
- submit [event: MouseEvent] - Click on the built-in submit button (the native form submit still happens).
- cancel [event: MouseEvent] - Click on the built-in cancel button.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when it renders no actions: no default slot content and neither `submitLabel` nor `cancelLabel`.

Rules:
- Put FormActions last in the <form> so the submit button submits it.
- Exactly one primary (default variant) button per form.
- Do not use flex order utilities on the buttons; keep DOM order equal to visual order.
- Use `layout="split"` to keep a destructive or secondary action (first in DOM order) apart from the primary one; `variant="bar"` for a footer inside a card or dialog.
- Use the default slot for custom/extra actions; then `submitLabel` / `cancelLabel` are ignored.

Accessibility:
- The wrapper is a plain container. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` and it becomes a named `role="group"`; an unnamed group would only add noise.
- Built-in cancel is `type="button"` so it never submits; submit is `type="submit"`. Tab visits Cancel then Submit, the same order they appear.
- Stacked layout keeps DOM order (no `flex-col-reverse`), so focus order always matches the visual order. Buttons are full width below `sm` and wrap at 320px.
- `sticky` uses an opaque `bg-background` and a top border (no blur, no transparency), so text behind it never reduces contrast. A sticky bar can cover a focused field: give the scroll container `scroll-pb-20` or similar.
- `layout` and `variant` change only layout and surface, never DOM order, roles or labels. `split` moves the first action to the start with a margin, not `order`, so focus order still matches the visual order. `bar` and `boxed` use an opaque `bg-background` and a border (no blur, no transparency).
- Loading uses Button `aria-busy` and blocks activation. Buttons are 44px tall on touch pointers.

Example: Submit and cancel
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const last = ref('')
</script>

<form class="grid max-w-md gap-3" @submit.prevent="last = 'Saved'">
  <Field label="Project name"><Input name="project" /></Field>
  <FormActions submit-label="Save changes" cancel-label="Cancel" @cancel="last = 'Cancelled'" />
  <p role="status" class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Last action: {{ last || 'none' }}</p>
</form>
```

Example: Custom slot, spread layout, loading
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const saving = ref(false)
const result = ref('')
function publish() {
  saving.value = true
  result.value = 'Publishing'
  setTimeout(() => { saving.value = false; result.value = 'Published' }, 600)
}
</script>

<form @submit.prevent="publish">
  <FormActions align="between" aria-label="Publish actions">
    <Button variant="outline" class="text-destructive" type="button" @click="result = 'Draft deleted'">Delete draft</Button>
    <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline" type="button" @click="result = 'Draft saved'">Save draft</Button>
      <Button type="submit" :loading="saving">Publish</Button>
    </div>
  </FormActions>
  <p role="status" class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ result }}</p>
</form>
```

Example: Layouts
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <FormActions aria-label="Stacked actions" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
  <FormActions aria-label="Inline actions" layout="inline" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
  <FormActions aria-label="Split actions" layout="split" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
</div>
```

Example: Surfaces and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <FormActions aria-label="Plain actions" submit-label="Save" />
  <FormActions aria-label="Bar actions" variant="bar" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
  <FormActions aria-label="Boxed actions" variant="boxed" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
  <FormActions aria-label="Small actions" size="sm" variant="boxed" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
  <FormActions aria-label="Large actions" size="lg" variant="boxed" submit-label="Save" cancel-label="Cancel" />
</div>
```

# Checkbox
group: forms / Choice
Boolean (or indeterminate) checkbox with optional label and description, sizes, tones, shapes, invalid state and Field wiring.

Use `Checkbox` for an independent yes/no choice, for selecting several items from a list, or as a "select all" control (bind the indeterminate state when only some children are checked). Pass `label` (or the `label` slot) to render a clickable `<label>` beside the box; without it ALWAYS provide `aria-label`. Add `description` for a line of helper text under the label, `labelPosition="start"` to put the label before the box, `tone` to recolour the checked state and `shape` for a square or circular box. For a bordered or filled tile around the choice use `CheckboxCard`; `Checkbox` has no `variant` because the card components already cover that look. Use `Switch` for settings that apply immediately, `RadioGroup` when exactly one option can be chosen. The model is `true | false | 'indeterminate'`; clicking an indeterminate box turns it on. Works controlled (`v-model`) and uncontrolled (`default-value`).

import { Checkbox } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: boolean | 'indeterminate' | null - v-model value. Uncontrolled when omitted; `null` renders as unchecked.
- defaultValue: boolean | 'indeterminate' - Initial state when uncontrolled.
- label: string - Text rendered in a `<label for>` beside the box. Use the `label` slot for rich content.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Box size (14 / 16 / 20 px); the hit area is always at least 24px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the checked and indeterminate surface. `neutral` uses the foreground colour with background-coloured glyph. The check or minus glyph is always drawn, so state never rests on colour. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' | 'circle' = 'rounded' - Corner shape of the box: slightly rounded, sharp, or fully round. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- labelPosition: 'end' | 'start' = 'end' - Side of the label in reading order. `start` puts it before the box and flips in right-to-left layouts. Only has an effect when a label is shown.
- description: string - Helper text under the label, referenced from the box through `aria-describedby` (merged with Field hint and error ids). Shown only together with a label. Use the `description` slot for rich content.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the checkbox and dims the label. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- required: boolean = false - Sets `aria-required`. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.
- name: string - Form field name; a hidden input is rendered when inside a `<form>`.
- value: string - Value submitted with the form when checked.
- id: string - Control id. Falls back to the Field id, then a generated one. The label `for` always matches.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the box (`data-slot="checkbox"`); wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- label - Rich label content; replaces the `label` prop text.
- description - Rich helper text under the label; replaces the `description` prop. Needs a label to be shown.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: boolean | 'indeterminate'] - Emitted when the user toggles the checkbox.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the checkbox has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, or `label` (prop or slot).

Rules:
- Always give a Checkbox either `label`/`label` slot or `aria-label`.
- Use `v-model` (boolean | "indeterminate"); drive "select all" with a computed that returns "indeterminate".
- Use `description` for helper text instead of a sibling paragraph: it is wired to the box with aria-describedby. It needs a label.
- Use `tone` (primary, success, danger, neutral, info) for the checked colour and `shape` (rounded, square, circle) for the box; do not recolour with classes.
- Use `label-position="start"` to put the label first; never reorder with left/right classes.
- Use CheckboxCard, not a Checkbox variant, when the whole option needs a bordered tile.
- Use Switch for immediate on/off settings, Checkbox for form choices submitted later.
- Put layout classes (`mt-1`) on the Checkbox via `class`; it targets the box, not the label wrapper.

Accessibility:
- Button with `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked` (`true`, `false` or `mixed` for indeterminate); Space toggles it, Tab moves on.
- Clicking the `<label for>` toggles the box. Without a label always set `aria-label`. A required checkbox with a label shows a visible asterisk.
- Inside a Field it receives `id`, `aria-describedby` (hint and error), `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and disabled state.
- `invalid` sets `aria-invalid="true"`; the destructive ring never appears without it. Forced-colors mode draws a dashed border for invalid and keeps the check or dash glyph for state.
- `description` is a `<p>` whose id is added to the box `aria-describedby`, after any Field hint and error ids and an explicit `aria-describedby`; it is rendered only with a label. `labelPosition` changes visual order only: the box stays first in the DOM, so reading and tab order are unchanged.
- Tones and shapes change colour and corner radius only. Role, name, keyboard and the check or minus glyph are identical, and forced-colors mode keeps the glyph and a dashed invalid border for every tone.
- Hit area is at least 24px even for the 14px box (and about 40px on touch pointers) through an invisible ::after; a multi-line label aligns to the first line.
- A group of checkboxes needs a name: wrap them in `Fieldset` with a legend, or give the container `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby`.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const accepted = ref(false)
</script>

<div class="grid gap-2">
  <Checkbox v-model="accepted" label="I accept the terms" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Accepted: {{ accepted }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <Checkbox tone="primary" label="Primary" default-value />
  <Checkbox tone="success" label="Success" default-value />
  <Checkbox tone="danger" label="Danger" default-value />
  <Checkbox tone="neutral" label="Neutral" default-value />
  <Checkbox tone="info" label="Info" default-value />
</div>
```

Example: Shapes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <Checkbox shape="square" label="Square" default-value />
  <Checkbox shape="rounded" label="Rounded" default-value />
  <Checkbox shape="circle" label="Circle" default-value />
  <Checkbox shape="circle" tone="success" label="Circle, indeterminate" default-value="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

Example: Description and label position
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
  <Checkbox label="Sample option A" description="Sample description text under the label." default-value />
  <Checkbox label="Sample option B" description="Sample description, with the label shown first." label-position="start" tone="info" />
</div>
```

Example: Select all with indeterminate state
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = ref([{ id: 1, label: 'Email', on: true }, { id: 2, label: 'SMS', on: false }, { id: 3, label: 'Push', on: false }])
const all = computed(() => {
  const n = items.value.filter((i) => i.on).length
  return n === 0 ? false : n === items.value.length ? true : 'indeterminate'
})
function toggleAll(v) { items.value.forEach((i) => (i.on = v === true)) }
</script>

<div class="grid gap-2">
  <Checkbox :model-value="all" label="All channels" @update:model-value="toggleAll" />
  <div class="grid gap-2 pl-6">
    <Checkbox v-for="i in items" :key="i.id" v-model="i.on" :label="i.label" size="sm" />
  </div>
</div>
```

Example: In a Field with validation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const agreed = ref(false)
</script>

<Field label="Consent" hint="Required to continue." :error="agreed ? '' : 'You must accept'" orientation="horizontal">
  <Checkbox v-model="agreed" />
</Field>
```

Example: Sizes and states
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <Checkbox size="sm" label="Small" default-value />
  <Checkbox label="Medium" default-value />
  <Checkbox size="lg" label="Large" default-value />
  <Checkbox label="Disabled" disabled default-value />
  <Checkbox label="Invalid" invalid />
</div>
```

# CheckboxCard
group: forms / Choice
Selectable card tile backed by a native checkbox, with title, description, icon slots, variants, tones, a stacked layout and a group for multi-select lists.

Use `CheckboxCard` when a boolean (or multi-select) choice deserves more room than a plain `Checkbox`: plan add-ons, notification channels, feature toggles with an explanation. Standalone it works with `v-model` (boolean). Wrap several in `CheckboxCardGroup` and give each a `value` to bind a `string[]`. The native `<input type="checkbox">` is visually hidden (sr-only) so keyboard, screen readers, form submission and `:focus-visible` rings all work natively; the whole card is the click target. Use `RadioCard` when exactly one option can be chosen, and `Checkbox` for compact lists. Any extra attribute (`aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`, listeners) is forwarded to the native input, not the label root.

import { CheckboxCard, CheckboxCardGroup } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: boolean - v-model checked state. Omit for uncontrolled use. Ignored when inside a `CheckboxCardGroup` and `value` is set.
- defaultValue: boolean = false - Initial state when uncontrolled.
- value: string - Value used by a surrounding `CheckboxCardGroup` (and submitted with the form). Required for group membership.
- title: string - Title text. Use the `title` slot for rich content.
- description: string - Description text. Use the `description` slot for rich content.
- icon: IconDefinition - Icon shown before the text. Use the `icon` slot for anything else.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' = 'outline' - Surface style. Inherits the group variant when unset; unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and text size. Inherits the group size when unset.
- tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the checked state: border, tint, icon and indicator. `neutral` uses foreground on background. Inherits the group tone when unset; unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- layout: 'default' | 'stacked' = 'default' - `default` puts the icon, text and indicator in one row; `stacked` puts the icon above the text and the indicator in the top end corner. Inherits the group layout when unset.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the native input and dims the card. Also inherited from a group or Field.
- required: boolean = false - Sets `required` on the native input. Also inherited from a Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and a destructive border. Also inherited from a group or Field error.
- name: string - Form field name. Inherits the group name when unset.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root `<label data-slot="checkbox-card">`; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- CheckboxCardGroup - Grid wrapper (`role="group"`) that owns a `string[]` v-model for its cards (match by `value`), propagates `disabled`, `invalid`, `variant`, `size`, `tone`, `layout`, `name` and lays cards out in 1-4 columns. Label it with `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` or wrap it in a `Field`.
    - modelValue: string[] - Selected values. Omit for uncontrolled use. Non-arrays are treated as empty; duplicates and non-strings are dropped.
    - defaultValue: string[] = [] - Initial selection when uncontrolled.
    - columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 1 - Grid columns from the `sm` breakpoint up (2 on `sm`, 3-4 on `lg`). Invalid values fall back to 1.
    - variant: 'outline' | 'filled' - Default variant for cards.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Default size for cards.
    - tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' - Default tone for cards. A card with its own `tone` wins.
    - layout: 'default' | 'stacked' - Default layout for cards. A card with its own `layout` wins.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disables every card.
    - invalid: boolean = false - Marks the group and every card invalid.
    - name: string - Form field name shared by all cards.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last on the group root.

Slots:
- default ({ checked: boolean }) - Extra content below the description (e.g. a price).
- title ({ checked: boolean }) - Rich title; replaces the `title` prop text.
- description ({ checked: boolean }) - Rich description; replaces the `description` prop text.
- icon ({ checked: boolean }) - Custom leading icon/illustration; replaces the `icon` prop.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: boolean] - Emitted when the user toggles the card (also inside a group, alongside the group update).
- CheckboxCardGroup: update:modelValue [value: string[]] - Emitted by the group with the new array of selected values.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `CheckboxCard` has no accessible name: no title, description or slot text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (an icon alone does not count).
- Throws a ContractError when `CheckboxCardGroup` has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `Fieldset` legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `CheckboxCard` inside a `CheckboxCardGroup` has a missing or empty `value`, or a `value` another card in the group already uses.

Rules:
- Use CheckboxCard for rich multi-select options; use Checkbox for plain compact ones.
- Always set `value` on each card inside CheckboxCardGroup; bind a string[] to the group, not to the cards.
- Label the group with aria-label/aria-labelledby (or wrap in Field); pass aria-label on cards that have no title.
- Extra attrs (aria-*, id, data-*) land on the native input, not on the label root; use `class` for root styling.
- Use `variant` (outline|filled), `size` (sm|md|lg), `tone` (primary|success|danger|neutral|info) and `layout` (default|stacked); on the group they cascade to cards unless a card overrides.
- Use `tone="danger"` for choices with a cost or risk, not for validation errors: errors use `invalid`.

Accessibility:
- The native `<input type="checkbox">` carries the semantics (role checkbox, checked state, form submission); it is visually hidden but focusable and the whole card is its label.
- Space toggles when focused; `:focus-visible` shows a ring on the card via `has-focus-visible`.
- The input is `aria-labelledby` the title and `aria-describedby` the description when present. With no title, pass `aria-label` (forwarded to the input).
- `CheckboxCardGroup` has `role="group"`: give it `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`, or wrap it in a `Field`, whose label then names the group through `aria-labelledby` (hint and error go to `aria-describedby`). `aria-invalid` is not allowed on a group, so the invalid state is on each card input.
- Tones and the stacked layout change only classes: the native input, its name and description wiring and the keyboard behaviour are identical. The check mark in the indicator carries the state, the tone colour is an addition.
- Forced-colors mode: the focus ring becomes an outline, the checked card gets a system-colour border and the indicator a system-colour fill, and an invalid card a dashed border.
- The check indicator is `aria-hidden`; state is exposed through the native `checked` property and `data-state`.

Example: Basic (boolean v-model)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const newsletter = ref(false)
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <CheckboxCard v-model="newsletter" title="Newsletter" description="Product news, once a month." />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Subscribed: {{ newsletter }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Group with icons (string[] v-model)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const channels = ref(['email'])
const icons = { email: faEnvelope, sms: faPhone, app: faUser }
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-2xl gap-2">
  <CheckboxCardGroup v-model="channels" :columns="3" aria-label="Notification channels">
    <CheckboxCard value="email" title="Email" description="Once a day" :icon="icons.email" />
    <CheckboxCard value="sms" title="SMS" description="Urgent only" :icon="icons.sms" />
    <CheckboxCard value="app" title="In-app" description="As it happens" :icon="icons.app" />
  </CheckboxCardGroup>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ channels.join(', ') || 'none' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: filled
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const on = ref(true)
</script>

<div class="max-w-sm">
  <CheckboxCard v-model="on" variant="filled" title="Filled card" description="Muted surface instead of a bordered one." />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <CheckboxCard size="sm" title="Small" description="Compact padding" />
  <CheckboxCard size="md" title="Medium" description="Default padding" />
  <CheckboxCard size="lg" title="Large" description="Roomy padding" />
```

# MultiSelect
group: forms / Choice
Dropdown checkbox list with chips summary, search filter, select all / clear, max selections and full keyboard support.

Use `MultiSelect` when the user picks several values from a known list of 5-10 000 options and the selection should stay visible as compact chips (first `maxVisible` chips, then "+N more"). It is dependency-free: the panel is rendered inline below the trigger (absolute, `z-(--z-dropdown)`), so avoid placing it inside an `overflow-hidden` ancestor that would clip it. The model is `string[]` of option values; options are `{ value, label, disabled? }`. Use `Select` for a single value, `Combobox` for async/free-text lookups, `TagsInput` for free-form tags, `CheckboxCard` for a few rich options. Works controlled (`v-model`) and uncontrolled (`default-value`); the open state can be controlled with `v-model:open`. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `data-*`) go to the trigger button; an `aria-label` is rendered as a hidden name and combined with the visible chips, so the accessible name always contains the visible text. `class` goes to the root.

import { MultiSelect } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string[] - Selected option values (v-model). Omit for uncontrolled use. Non-arrays are treated as empty; duplicates and non-strings are dropped.
- defaultValue: string[] = [] - Initial selection when uncontrolled.
- open: boolean - Open state (v-model:open). Omit for uncontrolled use. Never open while disabled.
- options: { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }[] = [] - Available options. Entries without a string `value` are ignored. Disabled options cannot be toggled (a selected disabled option stays selected, also on Clear).
- placeholder: string = 'Select...' - Trigger text when nothing is selected.
- searchable: boolean = true - Show the search box (case-insensitive label filter). When false the listbox takes focus and typing jumps to the first option starting with the typed text.
- searchPlaceholder: string = 'Search...' - Placeholder and accessible name of the search input.
- emptyText: string = 'No results found' - Shown when no option matches or there are no options. Overridable with the `empty` slot.
- max: number - Maximum number of selected values. Remaining options become `aria-disabled`, a "n / max selected" counter replaces "Select all". Non-positive, NaN or non-numeric values mean unlimited; fractions are floored.
- maxVisible: number = 3 - Chips shown in the trigger before the rest collapse into "+N more". 0 shows only the count; invalid values fall back to 3.
- actions: boolean = true - Show the "Select all" (enabled, filtered options) and "Clear" actions row.
- clearable: boolean = false - Show a clear (x) button (24px, 32px on touch devices) in the trigger while something is selected.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Trigger min height (28 / 32 / 36 / 40 px). Text is 16px on small screens and 14px from the `md` breakpoint (`lg` stays 16px); on touch devices the trigger is at least 44px tall.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of the trigger. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens on focus, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of the trigger. `underline` is always square-cornered. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon before the chevron; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the trigger and blocks all changes. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- required: boolean = false - Sets `aria-required` on the trigger. Also inherited from a Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and a destructive border. Also set by a Field with an error.
- name: string - Form field name; one hidden input per selected value is rendered.
- id: string - Trigger id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id, then a generated one.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root (`data-slot="multi-select"`); use it to set the width.

Slots:
- chip ({ value: string; label: string }) - Content of each chip in the trigger.
- option ({ option: MultiSelectOption; selected: boolean }) - Content of each option row (next to the checkbox).
- empty - Content of the empty state.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string[]] - Emitted with the new selection whenever the user changes it (toggle, select all, clear).
- update:open [open: boolean] - Emitted when the panel opens or closes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the trigger has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (the chips and the placeholder do not count).
- Throws a ContractError when an option `value` is missing, not a string, empty or used twice.

Rules:
- Bind a string[] with v-model; options are { value, label, disabled? } with unique string values.
- Always give the trigger an accessible name: wrap in Field, or pass aria-label (it lands on the trigger button). The chips and placeholder do not count; without a name it raises a ContractError.
- Use `max` to cap selections (it hides Select all); use `max-visible` to control chip overflow.
- Set width with `class` on the root (e.g. class="w-72"); the panel matches the trigger width (min 12rem).
- The panel is inline (not portalled): do not place it inside overflow-hidden containers.
- Look props are `variant`, `shape`, `status` and `size`. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
- Use Select for a single value; use name="field" to submit one hidden input per selected value.

Accessibility:
- The trigger is a `<button aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded aria-controls>`; label it with a `Field` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (attrs go to the trigger). An author name is combined with the visible chips or placeholder through `aria-labelledby` (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name), so the trigger never has an `aria-label` that hides its visible text.
- The panel contains a search input (focused on open) and a `role="listbox" aria-multiselectable` of `role="option" aria-selected` rows. The active option is announced via `aria-activedescendant` while DOM focus stays on the input (or on the listbox when `searchable=false`). The check box in each row is decorative and drawn only for selected rows, so it also shows in forced-colors mode.
- `status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon before the chevron. Success and warning also add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the trigger references from `aria-describedby`; error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours.
- Trigger: ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Enter / Space open the panel; typing a character opens it and seeds the search.
- In the panel: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (skipping disabled, wrapping); Enter toggles it; Space toggles it while the search is empty (otherwise it is a normal character); Ctrl/Cmd+A selects all enabled options (unless text is typed in the search box); Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; Tab closes. With `searchable=false`, Home/End jump and typing performs a type-ahead jump. The "Select all" and "Clear" buttons are for pointer use (`tabindex=-1`); Ctrl/Cmd+A is the keyboard equivalent of "Select all".
- A visually hidden `role="status"` region announces the filtered option count ("3 options available") and the empty message while searching. Disabled and limit-blocked options are `aria-disabled`; the "n / max selected" counter is `aria-live="polite"` and uses tabular numbers.
- Target sizes: the clear button is 24px (32px on touch devices), action buttons are at least 24px, options and the search input are 44px tall on touch devices. The trigger and search input use 16px text on small screens so iOS does not zoom.
- Focus and the active option keep an outline in forced-colors mode; chips get a border. The trigger text wraps and the panel is at least 12rem wide, so nothing overflows at 320px. Layout uses logical properties (RTL safe). Animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Clicking outside or moving focus outside closes the panel.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const picked = ref(['apple', 'cherry'])
const fruit = [{ value: 'apple', label: 'Apple' }, { value: 'banana', label: 'Banana' }, { value: 'cherry', label: 'Cherry' }, { value: 'date', label: 'Date', disabled: true }, { value: 'elder', label: 'Elderberry' }, { value: 'fig', label: 'Fig' }]
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <MultiSelect v-model="picked" :options="fruit" placeholder="Pick fruit" aria-label="Fruit" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ picked.join(', ') || 'none' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Chips overflow (+N more)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const picked = ref(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry', 'elder', 'fig'])
</script>

<div class="max-w-sm">
  <MultiSelect v-model="picked" :options="fruit" :max-visible="2" aria-label="Many fruit" />
</div>
```

Example: Maximum selections
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const picked = ref(['apple'])
</script>

<div class="max-w-sm">
  <MultiSelect v-model="picked" :options="fruit" :max="2" clearable aria-label="Up to two fruit" placeholder="Choose up to 2" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" size="xs" placeholder="Extra small" aria-label="Extra small" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" size="sm" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" size="md" placeholder="Medium" aria-label="Medium" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" size="lg" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large" />
</div>
```

Example: Variants and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" placeholder="Outline" aria-label="Outline" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" variant="filled" placeholder="Filled" aria-label="Filled" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" variant="underline" placeholder="Underline" aria-label="Underline" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" variant="ghost" placeholder="Ghost" aria-label="Ghost" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" shape="pill" :default-value="['apple', 'fig']" placeholder="Pill" aria-label="Pill" />
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" shape="square" placeholder="Square" aria-label="Square" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
  <Field label="Fruit for the box" hint="Sample message: all of these are in stock."><MultiSelect :options="fruit" status="success" :default-value="['apple']" /></Field>
  <Field label="Fruit for the stall" hint="Sample message: one of these is almost sold out."><MultiSelect :options="fruit" status="warning" :default-value="['fig']" clearable /></Field>
  <Field label="Fruit for the pie" error="Sample message: choose at least one fruit."><MultiSelect :options="fruit" status="error" placeholder="Choose fruit" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Without search, without actions
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm">
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" :searchable="false" :actions="false" placeholder="Type to jump" aria-label="Plain list" />
</div>
```

Example: In a Field: invalid and disabled
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
  <Field label="Fruit" error="Choose at least one fruit.">
    <MultiSelect :options="fruit" invalid placeholder="Choose fruit" />
  </Field>
  <MultiSelect :options="fruit" disabled :default-value="['fig']" aria-label="Disabled" />
</div>
```

# PlanPicker
group: forms / Choice
One column of selectable plans with the price at the end, for checkout, upgrade and settings screens.

Use `PlanPicker` when a person chooses one plan inside a form or a settings page: each plan is a radio card with a name, an optional description and a few short points, and its price at the end of the row. It is built on a reka-ui radio group, so the arrow keys move and select, and the whole group is one tab stop. Use `PricingGrid` or `PricingCard` for the marketing page that compares plans side by side, `RadioCardGroup` when the options are not priced, and `UsageEstimator` for usage-based pricing. The model is the selected plan `id`. Set `name` to submit the id in a native form. Prices render through `Price`; a `price` of `null` shows `customLabel`. `billing` switches every plan between `price` and `yearlyPrice` (a plan without `yearlyPrice` keeps its monthly price), and `showBillingToggle` adds the toggle.

import { PlanPicker } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- plans*: PlanPickerPlan[] - Plans in display order: `{ id, name, description?, price, yearlyPrice?, period?, yearlyPeriod?, badge?, disabled?, features? }`. `id` is a unique non-empty string, `price` is in major units or `null`. Keep `features` to about three short points. A value that is not an array renders no plans.
- modelValue: string - v-model: the selected plan `id`. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultValue: string - Initial plan `id` when uncontrolled.
- billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' - v-model:billing. Uncontrolled when omitted. Unknown values count as `monthly`.
- defaultBilling: 'monthly' | 'yearly' = 'monthly' - Initial billing when uncontrolled.
- showBillingToggle: boolean = false - Show the monthly and yearly toggle above the plans.
- billingLabels: { group?: string; monthly?: string; yearly?: string } - Text of the toggle and its accessible name. Defaults are "Billing period", "Monthly" and "Yearly".
- yearlyNote: string = 'Billed yearly' - Small text under a price that is a yearly price. An empty string hides it.
- customLabel: string = 'Custom' - Shown instead of the price when `price` is `null`.
- currency: string - ISO 4217 currency code. Default `USD`. An invalid code renders a plain number.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for prices, such as `de-DE`. Defaults to the ConfigProvider locale, else `en-US`.
- name: string - Form field name. A hidden input with the selected `id` is rendered while a plan is selected, so a native form submits it.
- required: boolean = false - Sets `aria-required` on the group. Also inherited from a Field. Native form validation does not check it.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables every plan and the toggle. Also inherited from a Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid` on the group and a destructive border on every plan. Also set by a Field with an error.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap and text size of the plans. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'cards' | 'list' = 'cards' - `cards` are separate bordered radio cards; `list` is one bordered list with dividers between rows. Unknown values fall back to `cards`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root element; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted when the user selects a plan.
- update:billing [value: 'monthly' | 'yearly'] - Emitted when the user switches the billing toggle.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the picker has no accessible name (no Field label, Fieldset legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when a plan has an empty `id` or two plans share an `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when a plan has an empty `name`.

Rules:
- Use PlanPicker for choosing a plan inside a form or settings screen; use PricingGrid for the marketing comparison.
- Always name the picker: wrap it in Field with a label, or set `aria-label`.
- Give every plan a unique non-empty `id` and a `name`; the model is the plan `id`.
- Pass prices as numbers in major units and set `currency` and `locale`; never pass formatted strings.
- Keep `features` to about three short points; put the full comparison on a pricing page.
- Use `v-model:billing` with `show-billing-toggle` for monthly and yearly prices; give `yearlyPrice` and `yearlyPeriod` on each plan that has them.
- Set `name` when the selected plan must be submitted by a native form.
- In examples, label plans as samples ("Sample plan A") and use round numbers.

Accessibility:
- The group has `role="radiogroup"` and each plan `role="radio"`. Name the group with a Field label, a Fieldset legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Each plan is named by its `name`, and described by its description, points and price.
- Keyboard: Tab enters the group at the selected plan (or the first one) and leaves it; the arrow keys move to the next enabled plan and select it; Space selects the focused plan. Disabled plans are skipped.
- The selected plan shows a filled radio dot as well as a primary border and tint, so selection never relies on colour. The focus ring uses `focusRing` and an outline in forced-colors mode.
- Each row stacks no further than one column, so the layout reflows at 320px: the name wraps, and the price stays at the end of the row.
- The billing toggle is a named radio group of its own. Prices are tabular figures.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const plans = [
  { id: 'a', name: 'Sample plan A', description: 'Sample description for the smallest plan.', price: 0, period: '/month' },
  { id: 'b', name: 'Sample plan B', description: 'Sample description for the middle plan.', price: 10, yearlyPrice: 100, period: '/month', yearlyPeriod: '/year', features: ['Sample feature one', 'Sample feature two'] },
  { id: 'c', name: 'Sample plan C', description: 'Sample description for the largest plan.', price: 40, yearlyPrice: 400, period: '/month', yearlyPeriod: '/year', badge: 'Sample badge' },
]
const plan = ref('b')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-lg gap-3">
  <PlanPicker v-model="plan" :plans="plans" aria-label="Plan" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ plan }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: In a Field, with billing toggle and form value
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

  { id: 'a', name: 'Sample plan A', description: 'Sample description for the smallest plan.', price: 0, period: '/month' },
  { id: 'b', name: 'Sample plan B', description: 'Sample description for the middle plan.', price: 10, yearlyPrice: 100, period: '/month', yearlyPeriod: '/year', features: ['Sample feature one', 'Sample feature two'] },
  { id: 'c', name: 'Sample plan C', description: 'Sample description for the largest plan.', price: 40, yearlyPrice: 400, period: '/month', yearlyPeriod: '/year', badge: 'Sample badge' },

```

Example: List variant
```vue

```

Example: Sizes
```vue

  { id: 'a', name: 'Sample plan A', description: 'Sample description for the smallest plan.', price: 0, period: '/month' },

  { id: 'b', name: 'Sample plan B', description: 'Sample description for the middle plan.', price: 10, yearlyPrice: 100, period: '/month', yearlyPeriod: '/year', features: ['Sample feature one', 'Sample feature two'] },
  { id: 'c', name: 'Sample plan C', description: 'Sample description for the largest plan.', price: 40, yearlyPrice: 400, period: '/month', yearlyPeriod: '/year', badge: 'Sample badge' },

```

# RadioCard
group: forms / Choice
Selectable card tile backed by a native radio input, used inside RadioCardGroup for single-choice options with tones, a stacked layout and roving arrow-key navigation.

Use `RadioCard` + `RadioCardGroup` when exactly one option can be chosen and each option needs a title, description or icon: billing plans, shipping methods, deployment targets. The group owns `v-model` (a string); each card has a `value`. Native radios are visually hidden (sr-only) so form submission and screen readers behave natively, while the group adds roving keyboard navigation (arrows move focus AND selection, Home/End jump, disabled cards are skipped). A `RadioCard` rendered outside a group throws a ContractError and is inert and disabled. Use `RadioGroup` for compact radios, `SegmentedControl` for short inline switches, `CheckboxCard` for multiple selection. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`) are forwarded to the native input; use `class` for the card root.

import { RadioCard, RadioCardGroup } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- value*: string - Value this card represents. Must be a non-empty string.
- title: string - Title text. Use the `title` slot for rich content.
- description: string - Description text. Use the `description` slot for rich content.
- icon: IconDefinition - Icon shown before the text. Use the `icon` slot for anything else.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' = 'outline' - Surface style. Inherits the group variant when unset.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and text size. Inherits the group size when unset.
- tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the selected state: border, tint, icon and indicator dot. `neutral` uses foreground on background. Inherits the group tone when unset; unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- layout: 'default' | 'stacked' = 'default' - `default` puts the icon, text and indicator in one row; `stacked` puts the icon above the text and the indicator in the top end corner. Inherits the group layout when unset.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables this card (skipped by arrow keys).
- invalid: boolean = false - Marks this card invalid. Also inherited from the group.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root `<label data-slot="radio-card">`.

Parts:
- RadioCardGroup - Grid wrapper (`role="radiogroup"`) that owns the selected value, shares one native radio `name`, propagates state/variant/size/tone/layout to cards and implements roving keyboard navigation.
    - modelValue: string - Selected value (v-model). Omit for uncontrolled use.
    - defaultValue: string - Initial value when uncontrolled.
    - columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 1 - Grid columns from the `sm` breakpoint up (2 on `sm`, 3-4 on `lg`). Invalid values fall back to 1.
    - variant: 'outline' | 'filled' - Default variant for cards.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Default size for cards.
    - tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' - Default tone for cards. A card with its own `tone` wins.
    - layout: 'default' | 'stacked' - Default layout for cards. A card with its own `layout` wins.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disables every card and blocks keyboard changes.
    - required: boolean = false - Sets `aria-required` on the group and `required` on the radios.
    - invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid` on the group and a destructive border on every card.
    - name: string - Native radio name. Defaults to a generated unique name.
    - loop: boolean = true - Wrap arrow-key focus from last to first and back.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last on the group root.

Slots:
- default ({ checked: boolean }) - Extra content below the description (e.g. a price).
- title ({ checked: boolean }) - Rich title; replaces the `title` prop text.
- description ({ checked: boolean }) - Rich description; replaces the `description` prop text.
- icon ({ checked: boolean }) - Custom leading icon/illustration; replaces the `icon` prop.

Events:
- RadioCardGroup: update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted by the group when the user selects a different card (click or arrow keys).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `RadioCard` is not inside a `RadioCardGroup`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `RadioCard` has no accessible name: no title, description or slot text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (an icon alone does not count).
- Throws a ContractError when `RadioCardGroup` has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `Fieldset` legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `RadioCard` has a missing or empty `value`, or a `value` another card in the group already uses.

Rules:
- Always wrap RadioCard in RadioCardGroup; a bare RadioCard is inert and raises a ContractError.
- Bind v-model on the group (string), never on the cards; every card needs a unique non-empty `value`.
- Label the group with aria-label/aria-labelledby or wrap it in Field.
- Use `columns` (1-4) on the group for grids; use `variant` (outline|filled), `size` (sm|md|lg), `tone` (primary|success|danger|neutral|info) and `layout` (default|stacked) on the group so all cards match.
- Extra attrs (aria-*, id, data-*) land on the native input; use `class` for root styling.

Accessibility:
- The group has `role="radiogroup"`; name it with `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`, or wrap it in a `Field`, whose label then names the group through `aria-labelledby`.
- Each card is a native `<input type="radio">` (visually hidden, focusable) inside a `<label>`; cards share one `name`, so browsers and form submission treat them as one group.
- ArrowDown/ArrowRight select and focus the next enabled card, ArrowUp/ArrowLeft the previous (looping unless `loop=false`); Home/End jump to the first/last enabled card; disabled cards are skipped.
- Tab enters the group at the checked card (native radio behaviour) and leaves it with the next Tab.
- Inputs are `aria-labelledby` the title and `aria-describedby` the description; `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on the group and on each input.
- Tones and the stacked layout change only classes: the radios, names, roving keyboard behaviour and description wiring are identical. The filled dot in the indicator carries the state, the tone colour is an addition.
- Forced-colors mode: the focus ring becomes an outline, the checked card gets a system-colour border and the indicator a system-colour fill.
- Responsive: one column below `sm`, so cards never overflow at 320px.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const plan = ref('pro')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <RadioCardGroup v-model="plan" aria-label="Plan">
    <RadioCard value="free" title="Sample plan A" description="Short description of plan A." />
    <RadioCard value="pro" title="Sample plan B" description="Short description of plan B." />
    <RadioCard value="enterprise" title="Sample plan C" description="Short description of plan C." />
  </RadioCardGroup>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Plan: {{ plan }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Columns with icons
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

const icons = { email: faEnvelope, phone: faPhone, chat: faUser }
</script>

<div class="max-w-2xl">
  <RadioCardGroup v-model="contact" :columns="3" aria-label="Contact method">
    <RadioCard value="email" title="Email" description="Written reply" :icon="icons.email" />
    <RadioCard value="phone" title="Phone" description="Spoken reply" :icon="icons.phone" />
    <RadioCard value="chat" title="Chat" description="Live reply" :icon="icons.chat" />

```

# RadioGroup
group: forms / Choice
Single-choice group of radio items with roving keyboard focus, labels, descriptions, sizes, tones and Field wiring.

Use `RadioGroup` with `RadioGroupItem` children when exactly one of a small set (2-6) of options must be chosen and all options should be visible. Use `Select`/`NativeSelect` for longer lists, `SegmentedControl` for compact view switches and `Checkbox` when several can be chosen. Each item takes a `value` (non-empty string) and either a `label` prop or default-slot content that is rendered in a `<label>` beside the radio. `size`, `tone` and `labelPosition` set on the group apply to every item (an item can override them); `description` on an item adds helper text under its label. The model is the selected item value as a string. Works controlled (`v-model`) and uncontrolled (`default-value`).

import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string - v-model: the selected item value. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultValue: string - Initial value when uncontrolled.
- orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Layout and arrow-key axis. Unknown values fall back to vertical.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Size of every radio and its label text. An item `size` wins. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the checked border and dot of every item. An item `tone` wins. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- labelPosition: 'end' | 'start' = 'end' - Side of the label in reading order for every item; `start` flips in right-to-left layouts. An item `labelPosition` wins.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables every item. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- required: boolean = false - Sets `aria-required` on the group. Also inherited from a Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the group. Also set by a Field with an error.
- name: string - Form field name; hidden inputs are rendered when inside a `<form>`.
- loop: boolean = true - Arrow-key focus wraps from last to first item.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the group; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- RadioGroupItem - One radio. Renders a button with `role="radio"`; with a label (prop or slot) it is wrapped with a `<label for>`.
    - value: string - Value this item represents. Must be a non-empty string.
    - label: string - Label text; use the default slot for rich content.
    - description: string - Helper text under the label, referenced from the radio through `aria-describedby`. Shown only together with a label. Use the `description` slot for rich content.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Radio size (14 / 16 / 20 px, hit area at least 24px) and label text size. Inherits the group `size`, then `md`. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' - Colour of the checked border and dot. Inherits the group `tone`, then `primary`. The dot is always drawn, so state never rests on colour.
    - labelPosition: 'end' | 'start' - Side of the label in reading order. Inherits the group `labelPosition`, then `end`.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disables this item only (the label dims too).
    - id: string - Item id; generated when omitted. The label `for` always matches.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last on the radio button; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - RadioGroupItem children. Each item also has a `description` slot for rich helper text under its label.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted when the user selects an item.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `RadioGroup` has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `Fieldset` legend, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `RadioGroupItem` has a missing or empty `value`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `RadioGroupItem` has no accessible name: no `label` prop, default slot text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- Always pair RadioGroup with a visible Field label or `aria-label`.
- Set `size`, `tone` and `label-position` once on the group; override on an item only when one option must differ. Use `description` on an item for helper text (needs a label).
- Item `value` must be a non-empty string; put the label on the item (`label` prop), not outside it.
- Use `v-model` on the group, never on items. 2-6 options only; otherwise use Select.

Accessibility:
- Group has `role="radiogroup"`, items are `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`. Name the group with `aria-label`, or put it in a Field: the Field label then names it through `aria-labelledby`.
- Keyboard: Tab enters the group once (roving tabindex, on the selected item or the first), Arrow keys move and select (wrapping when `loop`), Space selects the focused item, Shift+Tab leaves.
- A `description` is a `<p>` whose id is set as the radio `aria-describedby` (after an explicit one); it is rendered only with a label. `labelPosition` changes visual order only: the radio stays first in the DOM, so reading and tab order are unchanged.
- Size and tone change the look only. Roles, names and keyboard are identical for every variation, and the checked dot and dashed invalid border survive forced-colors mode for every tone.
- Clicking a label selects its radio. Inside a Field the group receives `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`.
- Each radio has an at-least-24px hit area (about 40px on touch pointers) through an invisible ::after; forced-colors mode keeps the dot visible with a system colour.
- Responsive: the horizontal layout wraps, so it never overflows at 320px.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const plan = ref('pro')
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <RadioGroup v-model="plan" aria-label="Plan">
    <RadioGroupItem value="free" label="Sample plan A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="pro" label="Sample plan B" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="team" label="Sample plan C" disabled />
  </RadioGroup>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ plan }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Horizontal in a Field with an error
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const size = ref('')
</script>

<Field label="T-shirt size" :error="size ? '' : 'Choose a size'" required>
  <RadioGroup v-model="size" orientation="horizontal">
    <RadioGroupItem value="s" label="S" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="m" label="M" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="l" label="L" />
  </RadioGroup>
</Field>
```

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <RadioGroup default-value="a" tone="success" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Success tone">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Success A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Success B" />
  </RadioGroup>
  <RadioGroup default-value="a" tone="danger" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Danger tone">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Danger A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Danger B" />
  </RadioGroup>
  <RadioGroup default-value="a" tone="info" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Info tone">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Info A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Info B" />
  </RadioGroup>
  <RadioGroup default-value="a" tone="neutral" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Neutral tone">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Neutral A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Neutral B" />
  </RadioGroup>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue

  <RadioGroup default-value="a" size="sm" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Small">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Small A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Small B" />
  </RadioGroup>
  <RadioGroup default-value="a" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Medium">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Medium A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Medium B" />
  </RadioGroup>
  <RadioGroup default-value="a" size="lg" orientation="horizontal" aria-label="Large">
    <RadioGroupItem value="a" label="Large A" />
    <RadioGroupItem value="b" label="Large B" />
  </RadioGroup>
</div>
```

Example: Descriptions and label position
```vue

  <RadioGroup default-value="monthly" aria-label="Billing period">
    <RadioGroupItem value="monthly" label="Sample option A" description="Sample description for the first option." />
    <RadioGroupItem value="yearly" label="Sample option B" description="Sample description for the second option." />
  </RadioGroup>
  <RadioGroup default-value="email" label-position="start" tone="info" aria-label="Contact method">
    <RadioGroupItem value="email" label="Sample option C" description="Sample description for the third option." />
    <RadioGroupItem value="phone" label="Sample option D" description="Sample description for the fourth option." />
  </RadioGroup>

```

Example: Rich label content
```vue

  <RadioGroupItem value="a">
    <span>Monthly <Badge variant="secondary">Sample badge</Badge></span>
  </RadioGroupItem>
  <RadioGroupItem value="b">
    <span>Yearly <Badge>Sample badge</Badge></span>
  </RadioGroupItem>
```
