# Field
group: forms / Field wrappers
Form-field wrapper: label, control, hint and error with automatic id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid wiring.

Wrap one form control in `Field`. It generates an id (or uses `id`), renders a `Label` with `for`, a hint and an error message, and provides a context that `Input`, `Textarea`, `PasswordInput`, `SearchInput` and other form controls read to set `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `required` and `disabled`. Use `orientation="horizontal"` for checkbox/switch rows. Group several fields with `FieldGroup` / `Fieldset`. Custom controls can opt in with `useFieldControl()` exported from the package. When a control fails a native constraint (`required`, `pattern`, `minlength`) after the user has interacted with it, the browser message is shown as the error, so the message, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` appear together.

import { Field } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- label: string - Label text. Use the `label` slot for rich content.
- hint: string - Helper text under the control; referenced by aria-describedby.
- error: string - Error message; marks the control invalid and is announced through a polite live region. Wins over the native validation message.
- invalid: boolean = false - Mark invalid without a message.
- required: boolean = false - Shows the required indicator and sets `required` on the control.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the control and dims the label.
- id: string - Control id. Generated with `useId()` when omitted.
- orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Label above the control, or beside it.
- hintPlacement: 'below' | 'above' = 'below' - `above` puts the hint between the label and the control. Ignored when horizontal. Both placements are linked by `aria-describedby`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size of the label, hint and error (12px, 14px, 16px) and the gap between them. Pair it with the same `size` on the control. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge.

Slots:
- default - The control.
- label - Rich label content (overrides `label`).
- hint - Rich hint content (overrides `hint`).
- error - Rich error content (overrides `error`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the Field wraps a control that has no accessible name and the Field has no `label` (prop or slot) and no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when the Field has a label and wraps a native input, textarea or select whose `id` differs from the id the label points at (pass that id to `Field` instead of the control).

Rules:
- Wrap every form control in `Field`; one control per Field.
- Show errors through the `error` prop, not custom markup. Do not validate on every keystroke; validate on blur or submit.
- Native `required`, `pattern` and `minlength` messages are shown automatically after interaction; `error` overrides them.
- Use `orientation="horizontal"` for Checkbox/Switch rows.
- For several related controls (radio set, date range) use `Fieldset` with a legend instead.

Accessibility:
- The `<label for>` matches the control id. Group controls (RadioGroup, SegmentedControl, CheckboxCardGroup, RadioCardGroup) are named through `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label, because a `for` attribute cannot label a `div`.
- The hint and the error are referenced by `aria-describedby`; the error is referenced only while it exists. `aria-invalid="true"` is set only when the field is invalid; a required control that is valid reports `aria-invalid="false"` so Firefox and Safari do not announce it as invalid on page load.
- The error text sits in one polite live region that is always in the page. An error that appears or changes after the user leaves a field is announced; an error already present at load is not. After a failed submit, move focus to the first invalid field so its error is read through `aria-describedby`.
- Required is exposed by the native `required` attribute on the control plus a visible asterisk (decorative, `aria-hidden`).
- Browser constraint failures are surfaced only after interaction (`:user-invalid`), never while typing in a pristine field.
- Controls that ignore the context (third-party inputs) need `:id` bound manually. The error is never colour-only: it is text.

Example: Label and hint
```vue
<Field class="max-w-sm" label="Username" hint="Letters and numbers only.">
  <Input name="username" autocomplete="username" />
</Field>
```

Example: Error state with live validation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const bio = ref('')
</script>

<Field class="max-w-sm" label="Bio" required :error="bio.length < 10 ? 'At least 10 characters' : ''" hint="Tell us about yourself.">
  <Textarea v-model="bio" />
</Field>
```

Example: Hint above the control
```vue
<Field class="max-w-sm" label="Display name" hint="Shown next to your comments." hint-placement="above">
  <Input name="display-name" autocomplete="nickname" />
</Field>
```

Example: Native validation and submit handling
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const status = ref('')
</script>

<form class="grid max-w-sm gap-4" @submit.prevent="status = 'Submitted without errors.'">
  <Field label="Email" hint="Format: name@example.com." required>
    <Input type="email" name="email" autocomplete="email" />
  </Field>
  <Button type="submit">Send</Button>
  <p role="status" class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ status }}</p>
</form>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
  <Field size="sm" label="Small" hint="12px text."><Input size="sm" /></Field>
  <Field label="Medium" hint="14px text."><Input /></Field>
  <Field size="lg" label="Large" hint="16px text." error="Needs a value."><Input size="lg" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Horizontal (switch row)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const on = ref(true)
</script>

<Field orientation="horizontal" label="Email notifications" hint="Weekly summary.">
  <Switch v-model="on" />
</Field>
```

# Label
group: forms / Field wrappers
Accessible form label with optional required indicator and disabled style.

Renders a `<label>` (reka-ui) pointing at a control via `for`. Prefer `Field`, which renders and wires the Label for you; use `Label` directly for custom layouts, checkbox/switch rows, or standalone captions. The asterisk is decorative (`aria-hidden`); also set `required` on the control so assistive tech announces it.

import { Label } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- for: string - Id of the labelled control.
- required: boolean = false - Appends a destructive-coloured `*` (aria-hidden).
- disabled: boolean = false - Dims the label and sets `data-disabled`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'default' | 'muted' = 'default' - `muted` renders the label in the muted text colour for secondary captions. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- as: string | Component = 'label' - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge.

Slots:
- default - Label text.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the label has no `for` and no control nested inside it.
- Throws a ContractError when `for` does not match the id of any element in the document (the label rendered by `Field` is exempt, since it names group controls through `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Prefer `Field` over bare `Label`.
- Always set `for` to the control id.
- Do not nest interactive controls inside Label except via `as-child` patterns.

Accessibility:
- Renders a native `<label>`: clicking it focuses or activates the control through `for`, and the text becomes the control name.
- The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`; the native `required` attribute on the control is what assistive tech announces.
- `for` only labels labelable elements (input, select, textarea, button). For a radio group or other `div` widget use `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label `id` (Field does this).
- `muted` uses the muted-foreground colour, which meets 4.5:1 on the page and card backgrounds; every size stays real text that zooms with the page.
- Text wraps (`leading-snug`) so a long label stays readable at 320px and at 200% zoom.

Example: Basic
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-1.5">
  <Label for="demo-label-email">Email</Label>
  <Input id="demo-label-email" type="email" />
</div>
```

Example: Required and disabled
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <div class="grid gap-1.5"><Label for="demo-label-req" required>Full name</Label><Input id="demo-label-req" required /></div>
  <div class="grid gap-1.5"><Label for="demo-label-dis" disabled>Locked</Label><Input id="demo-label-dis" disabled /></div>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and muted
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <div class="grid gap-1.5"><Label for="demo-label-sm" size="sm">Small label</Label><Input id="demo-label-sm" size="sm" /></div>
  <div class="grid gap-1.5"><Label for="demo-label-md">Medium label</Label><Input id="demo-label-md" /></div>
  <div class="grid gap-1.5"><Label for="demo-label-lg" size="lg">Large label</Label><Input id="demo-label-lg" size="lg" /></div>
  <div class="grid gap-1.5"><Label for="demo-label-muted" variant="muted">Muted label</Label><Input id="demo-label-muted" /></div>
</div>
```

# FilterBar
group: forms / Filtering
A row of applied filters as removable chips with an "Add filter" popover, "Clear all", a polite live region and URL-query helpers.

Use `FilterBar` above a table, list or board when the user narrows results by several fields at once. `v-model` is an array of `{ id, field, operator?, value, label? }`; `fields` describes what can be filtered (`text`, `number`, `select`, `multi-select`, `date`, `boolean`) and drives the field, condition and value pickers in the popover. Each applied filter is a `FilterChip` ("Status is In transit") with its own remove button; "Clear all" removes everything. Additions, removals and clearing are announced in a polite live region, and focus moves to a neighbouring chip (or "Add filter") after a removal so the keyboard user never loses their place. `variant` (`default`, `compact`, `inline`) and `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) change density and shape; the bar wraps instead of scrolling, down to 320px. `filtersToQuery` and `queryToFilters` turn the model into a plain object for the URL and back; they skip anything malformed, refuse keys like `__proto__` and never throw. The bar only edits the list: applying it to data is the app's job. Use `SearchInput` for one free-text box, `MultiSelect` for one field with many values, and `DataTable` column filters when each column already has its own control.

import { FilterBar, FilterChip } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: FilterItem[] - Applied filters (v-model). Entries without a string `id` and `field`, with no value, or with a repeated `id` are ignored. Omit for uncontrolled use.
- defaultValue: FilterItem[] = [] - Initial filters when uncontrolled.
- fields: FilterField[] = [] - What can be filtered: `{ id, label, type?, options?, operators?, placeholder?, min?, max?, step? }`. `type` defaults to `text`; `select` and `multi-select` need `options` (`{ value, label, disabled? }`); `operators` restricts the conditions to a subset of the known ids (`eq`, `neq`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `starts`, `ends`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `before`, `after`, `in`, `nin`). Fields with a blank or repeated `id` are ignored.
- open: boolean - Open state of the "Add filter" popover (v-model:open). Omit for uncontrolled use.
- variant: 'default' | 'compact' | 'inline' = 'default' - `default` has 8px gaps and bordered chips with a muted fill; `compact` has 4px gaps, tighter padding and smaller corners; `inline` has flat chips with only a bottom rule and link-style buttons, for use inside a toolbar or a sentence. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size of the chips (12 / 14 / 16px) and height of the buttons (24 / 32 / 36px; 44px on touch devices). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- clearable: boolean = true - Show "Clear all" while at least one filter is applied.
- max: number - Most filters that can be applied. At the limit "Add filter" is disabled. Non-positive or non-numeric values mean unlimited; fractions are floored.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables adding, removing and clearing.
- labels: Partial<FilterBarLabels> - Text overrides: `group`, `add`, `clear`, `field`, `operator`, `value`, `apply`, `cancel`, `remove` (uses `{filter}`), `yes`, `no`, `choose`, `valueRequired`, the live region sentences `added`, `removed` (use `{filter}`) and `cleared`, and `operators` (a map from operator id to wording). Blank or missing keys keep the English default.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root (`data-slot="filter-bar"`, `role="group"`).

Parts:
- FilterChip - One applied filter: text plus a remove button. Rendered by `FilterBar` as a list item, usable alone (for example in a summary line). Emits `remove`; Delete and Backspace on the remove button remove it too.
    - label: string - Chip text. Required (or default slot text): it also names the remove button, "Remove filter: <label>".
    - variant: 'default' | 'compact' | 'inline' = 'default' - Same looks as `FilterBar.variant`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - removable: boolean = true - Show the remove button.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disables the remove button.
    - removeLabel: string - Full accessible name of the remove button, replacing "Remove filter: <label>".
    - as: string | Component = 'span' - Element to render. `FilterBar` uses `li`.

Slots:
- chip ({ filter: FilterItem; label: string }) - Content of a chip, replacing the generated text. The remove button keeps naming the chip after its generated text.

Events:
- update:modelValue [filters: FilterItem[]] - The list changed: a filter was added, removed or cleared.
- update:open [open: boolean] - The "Add filter" popover opened or closed.
- add [filter: FilterItem] - A filter was added through the popover.
- remove [filter: FilterItem] - A filter was removed with its chip button.
- clear [filters: FilterItem[]] - "Clear all" removed these filters.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `fields` has no usable entry, when a field has no `id` or a repeated `id`, or when a field has no `label`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `select` or `multi-select` field has no `options`.
- Throws a ContractError when an applied filter has no `id` or a repeated `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `FilterChip` has no label text (the prop or the default slot).

Rules:
- Always pass `fields` with unique `id` and a `label`; give `select` and `multi-select` fields `options`.
- Bind `v-model` to an array of `{ id, field, operator?, value }`. `value` is a string, number, boolean or string[] matching the field type; keep `id` unique.
- The bar edits the list only. Apply the filters to your data yourself; do not build another filter UI beside it.
- Store filters in the URL with `filtersToQuery(filters)` and read them with `queryToFilters(route.query, { fields })`. Always pass `fields` when reading so unknown or malformed entries are dropped.
- Use `variant="compact"` in dense toolbars and `variant="inline"` inside a sentence. Do not restyle chips with colours to encode meaning.
- Pass `labels` to translate the bar; do not wrap it to rename buttons.
- Use `FilterChip` alone only for read-only summaries or custom lists; always give it a `label`.

Accessibility:
- The bar is `role="group"` named "Filters" (override with `labels.group` or `aria-label`). Applied filters are a `<ul>` of `<li>` chips; each chip has a real `<button>` named "Remove filter: Status is In transit".
- Keyboard: Tab reaches each remove button, then "Add filter", then "Clear all". Enter or Space activates a button; Delete and Backspace on a focused remove button remove that chip. "Add filter" opens a popover that moves focus inside, closes with Escape and returns focus to the button.
- After a removal focus moves to the remove button now at the same position (or the last one), and to "Add filter" when no chip is left; after "Clear all" it moves to "Add filter".
- The popover is a form: Field (`<select>`), Condition (`<select>`, hidden for `boolean` and for fields with one operator) and a value editor by type: text input, number input with steppers, date input, `<select>`, a group of checkboxes with a legend for `multi-select`. Enter submits from any single-line input. An empty or out-of-range value shows an error linked to the editor and returns focus to it; nothing is added.
- A visually hidden `role="status"` region (polite, atomic) says "Added filter: Status is Booked.", "Removed filter: ..." or "All filters cleared.". It is always in the DOM, so the first announcement is not lost.
- State is never colour alone: a filter is text plus an "x" button; the `inline` variant keeps a bottom rule (a border in forced-colors mode). Every control keeps the focus ring (an outline in forced-colors mode).
- Targets are at least 24px (the remove button is 24px, 32px on touch devices; buttons are 44px tall on touch devices). Popover form text is 16px on small screens. Chips wrap their text and the bar wraps its rows, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px or at 200% zoom. Logical properties keep the layout correct in right-to-left text.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const fields = [{ id: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'select', options: [...] }, { id: 'weight', label: 'Weight (kg)', type: 'number' }, { id: 'carrier', label: 'Carrier', type: 'multi-select', options: [...] }, ...]
const filters = ref([{ id: 'f1', field: 'status', operator: 'eq', value: 'in-transit' }, ...])
</script>

<FilterBar v-model="filters" :fields="fields" />
```

Example: Empty and uncontrolled
```vue
<FilterBar :fields="fields" />
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6">
  <FilterBar variant="default" :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
  <FilterBar variant="compact" :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
  <FilterBar variant="inline" :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6">
  <FilterBar size="sm" :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
  <FilterBar size="md" :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
  <FilterBar size="lg" :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
</div>
```

Example: URL query round trip
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { filtersToQuery, queryToFilters } from '@perfect-design/ui'
const filters = ref(queryToFilters(route.query, { fields }))
const query = computed(() => filtersToQuery(filters.value))
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <FilterBar v-model="filters" :fields="fields" />
  <pre class="overflow-x-auto rounded-md bg-muted p-3 text-xs" tabindex="0" aria-label="Query object">{{ JSON.stringify(query, null, 2) }}</pre>
</div>
```

Example: Limit, disabled and custom wording
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6">
  <FilterBar :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" :max="3" />
  <FilterBar :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" disabled />
  <FilterBar :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" :labels="labels" />
</div>
```

Example: Narrow container and long values
```vue
<div class="max-w-64">
  <FilterBar :default-value="filters" :fields="fields" />
</div>
```

Example: FilterChip on its own
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
  <FilterChip label="Status is Booked" @remove="removed = 'Status'" />
  <FilterChip label="Insured is Yes" variant="compact" size="sm" />
  <FilterChip label="Read only" :removable="false" variant="inline" />
  <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground" role="status">{{ removed ? removed + ' removed' : 'Nothing removed' }}</span>
</div>
```

# FieldGroup
group: forms / Layout
Layout wrapper that stacks or grids several Fields with a consistent gap.

Use `FieldGroup` to space a set of `Field`s evenly instead of hand-writing gap utilities. `orientation="horizontal"` makes a wrapping row (each child is at least 12rem wide, so a row reflows to one column at 320px), `columns` 2 or 3 makes a responsive grid that collapses to one column on small screens. Give it a `label` to expose it as a named `role="group"`. For a visually bordered group with a legend, or to disable a whole section, use `Fieldset`.

import { FieldGroup } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Stack vertically or lay out in a wrapping row. Ignored when `columns` > 1.
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 = 1 - Responsive grid column count (one column below `sm`). Invalid values fall back to a single column.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between fields: 12px, 20px or 32px when stacked (smaller in a wrapping row). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- label: string - Accessible name. When set, the wrapper gets `role="group"` and `aria-label`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes (e.g. override the gap).

Slots:
- default - The Fields (or any form content) to lay out.

Rules:
- Wrap sibling Fields in FieldGroup instead of adding gap/space-y utilities.
- Use `columns` (1-3), not custom grid classes; it is responsive already.
- Use Fieldset, not FieldGroup, when the group needs a visible legend or must be disabled as a whole.

Accessibility:
- With `label` the wrapper is a `role="group"` named by `aria-label`; without it there is no role and no extra tab stop.
- Layout only: DOM order is the reading and focus order at every width.
- Responsive: one column below `sm`; `horizontal` wraps at 12rem per child, so nothing overflows at 320px.
- A group of related answers (radios, checkboxes) needs a visible name: use `Fieldset` with a legend.

Example: Stacked fields
```vue
<FieldGroup>
  <Field label="First name"><Input autocomplete="given-name" /></Field>
  <Field label="Last name"><Input autocomplete="family-name" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

Example: Two-column grid with an accessible name
```vue
<FieldGroup :columns="2" label="Shipping address">
  <Field label="Street"><Input autocomplete="address-line1" /></Field>
  <Field label="City"><Input autocomplete="address-level2" /></Field>
  <Field label="Postcode" hint="No spaces"><Input autocomplete="postal-code" /></Field>
  <Field label="Country"><Input autocomplete="country-name" /></Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

Example: Gap
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6">
  <FieldGroup gap="sm"><Field label="Tight A"><Input /></Field><Field label="Tight B"><Input /></Field></FieldGroup>
  <FieldGroup gap="lg" :columns="2"><Field label="Loose A"><Input /></Field><Field label="Loose B"><Input /></Field></FieldGroup>
</div>
```

# Fieldset
group: forms / Layout
Native fieldset with legend and description that groups related controls and can disable them all at once.

Use `Fieldset` for a set of related controls that needs a visible title (shipping address, notification preferences, a radio set). It renders a real `<fieldset>` + `<legend>`, so screen readers announce the group name, and `disabled` natively disables every descendant control. `variant="card"` draws a bordered panel, `filled` a panel on the secondary surface, `divided` a single rule above the group, and `plain` has no chrome. Use `FieldGroup` when you only need spacing.

import { Fieldset } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- legend: string - Legend text. Use the `legend` slot for rich content.
- description: string - Helper text under the legend; linked to the fieldset through `aria-describedby`.
- variant: 'plain' | 'card' | 'filled' | 'divided' = 'plain' - `card` adds border, radius, padding and card background; `filled` uses the secondary surface without a border; `divided` adds a top rule and padding only. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Legend and description text size and the gap between fields (12px, 20px, 24px). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- disabled: boolean = false - Native `disabled`: disables every control inside and dims the section.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - The controls, stacked with a consistent gap.
- legend - Rich legend content (replaces the `legend` prop).
- description - Rich description content (replaces the `description` prop).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the Fieldset has no `legend` (prop or slot) and no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- Use Fieldset (not a div + heading) for groups of related inputs that need a title; always set `legend` (a missing one throws a ContractError).
- Use `disabled` on the Fieldset to disable a whole section; do not disable each control.
- Put Fields directly inside; the default slot already applies the gap.

Accessibility:
- Native `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` (legend first): the legend is announced as the group name when focus enters the group. A fieldset without a legend has no name, so it throws a ContractError (set `aria-label` when a visible legend is not wanted).
- `description` is referenced by `aria-describedby` on the fieldset.
- `filled` pairs `bg-secondary` with `text-secondary-foreground` for the legend, description and content, so contrast follows the tested pair; the legend and description stay real text at every size.
- Native `disabled` removes all descendant controls from the tab order and from form submission.
- Responsive: `min-w-0` lets the fieldset shrink inside flex and grid parents, so wide content never forces horizontal scrolling at 320px.

Example: Plain fieldset
```vue
<Fieldset legend="Contact" description="How we reach you about your order.">
  <Field label="Email"><Input type="email" autocomplete="email" /></Field>
  <Field label="Phone"><Input type="tel" autocomplete="tel" /></Field>
</Fieldset>
```

Example: Card variant, disabled section
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const locked = ref(true)
</script>

<div class="space-y-3">
  <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="locked = !locked">{{ locked ? 'Enable section' : 'Disable section' }}</Button>
  <Fieldset variant="card" legend="Billing" description="Locked while the invoice is processing." :disabled="locked">
    <Field label="Company name"><Input autocomplete="organization" /></Field>
    <Field label="Tax id"><Input /></Field>
  </Fieldset>
</div>
```

Example: Variants and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-6">
  <Fieldset variant="filled" legend="Filled" description="Secondary surface."><Field label="One"><Input /></Field></Fieldset>
  <Fieldset variant="divided" legend="Divided" size="lg"><Field label="Two"><Input /></Field></Fieldset>
  <Fieldset variant="card" legend="Compact card" size="sm"><Field label="Three" size="sm"><Input size="sm" /></Field></Fieldset>
</div>
```

# FormSection
group: forms / Layout
Titled form section landmark with description, optional aside actions, divider and a responsive 1-4 column fields grid.

Use `FormSection` to break a long form into named chunks ("Profile", "Billing address") with a heading, help text and a grid of fields. It renders a `<section>` labelled by its heading (a named region landmark) and lays its default slot out as a responsive grid (`columns` 1-4: one column on mobile, two from `sm`, three/four from `lg`). The `split` variant puts the header beside the fields on large screens (settings pages). Use `Fieldset` when you need a native `<fieldset>/<legend>` grouping a set of related controls (radio/checkbox groups) and `FieldGroup` for vertical spacing only; `FormSection` can wrap either. Make a field span the whole row with `class="col-span-full"`.

import { FormSection } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- title: string - Heading text; also names the landmark via `aria-labelledby`. Use the `title` slot for rich content.
- description: string - Help text under the title; referenced by `aria-describedby`. Use the `description` slot for rich content.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of the title (`h1`-`h6`). Invalid values fall back to 3. Pick the level that fits the page outline.
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 1 - Field grid columns: 1 on mobile; 2 from `sm`; the full count (3 or 4) from `lg`. Invalid values fall back to 1.
- variant: 'stacked' | 'split' | 'card' = 'stacked' - `stacked`: header above the fields. `split`: header on the left (1/3) and fields on the right (2/3) from `lg`. `card`: stacked inside a bordered, padded panel. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Title size (14px, 16px, 18px) and the gaps between header, rows and columns. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- divider: boolean = false - Adds a bottom border and padding to separate consecutive sections.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the `<section data-slot="form-section">` root; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - The fields. Direct children become grid items.
- title - Rich heading content; replaces the `title` prop.
- description - Rich description content; replaces the `description` prop.
- aside - Actions aligned to the end of the header (e.g. an Edit or Reset button).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the FormSection has no `title` (prop or slot) and no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- Wrap related Fields in FormSection with a title; do not nest FormSections.
- Use `columns` (1-4) for the field grid; it collapses on small screens automatically. Use class="col-span-full" for wide fields.
- Set `level` to fit the page heading outline (default h3).
- Use `variant="split"` for settings pages; `divider` to separate stacked sections.
- Put section-level actions in the `aside` slot, not inside the fields grid.

Accessibility:
- Renders a `<section>` named by its title via `aria-labelledby`, which exposes it as a region landmark; without a title it has no name, so pass `aria-label` (attrs fall through to the section).
- The description is linked with `aria-describedby`.
- The heading level is configurable (`level`, h1-h6): pick one that continues the page outline without skipping levels.
- Layout changes are purely visual; DOM order (header, then fields) is the reading order at every breakpoint.
- Responsive: the header row wraps when the `aside` actions do not fit, and the field grid is one column below `sm`, so nothing overflows at 320px.
- Use `Fieldset` inside a section for radio or checkbox sets that need a legend.

Example: Basic
```vue
<FormSection title="Profile" description="Shown on your public page." class="max-w-2xl">
  <Field label="First name"><Input autocomplete="given-name" /></Field>
  <Field label="Last name"><Input autocomplete="family-name" /></Field>
</FormSection>
```

Example: Three columns with divider and aside action
```vue
<div class="max-w-4xl">
```

```vue
    <Field label="C"><Input /></Field>
  </FormSection>
</div>
```

# Combobox
group: forms / Selection
Type-to-filter single select over an options array with clear button, empty state and Field wiring.

Use `Combobox` when the user picks one value from a long list (countries, users, tags) and benefits from typing to filter. It opens on focus or click, filters options case-insensitively on their label, supports arrow-key navigation, Enter to select and Escape to close, and shows `emptyText` (or the `empty` slot) when nothing matches or `options` is empty. Use `Select` for short lists or rich items, `NativeSelect` for the platform picker. The model is the selected option `value` (string); clearing sets `""`. A model value that matches no option shows an empty input. Server-side search is not built in: filter `options` yourself. `class` is applied to the root (use it for width); other attributes go to the `<input>`.

import { Combobox } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- options: Array<{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }> = [] - Selectable options. `label` is displayed and filtered.
- modelValue: string | null - v-model: the selected option value. `""`/`null` mean nothing selected. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultValue: string - Initial value when uncontrolled.
- placeholder: string - Input placeholder.
- emptyText: string = 'No results' - Message when no option matches. Use the `empty` slot for rich content.
- clearable: boolean = false - Shows a clear button while a value is selected; clearing emits `""`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Input height: 28px, 32px, 36px or 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of the input. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens on focus, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of the input. `underline` is always square-cornered. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon left of the buttons; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables input, toggle and clear. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- required: boolean = false - Native required on the input. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.
- name: string - Form field name; a hidden input is rendered when inside a `<form>`.
- open: boolean - Controlled open state (`v-model:open`).
- id: string - Input id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root element (width/layout); wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- option ({ option: ComboboxOption }) - Custom content for each option (default: its label).
- empty - Content shown when no option matches (default: `emptyText`).

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted when an option is selected (or `""` when cleared).
- update:open [value: boolean] - Emitted when the list opens or closes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder does not count).
- Throws a ContractError when an option `value` is missing, empty or used twice.

Rules:
- Pass `options` as data ({ value, label }); do not nest item components.
- Bind `v-model` to a string; treat `""` as empty. Use `clearable` for optional fields.
- Wrap in Field with a label or pass `aria-label`; width goes in `class`, other attributes reach the input.
- Look props are `variant`, `shape`, `status` and `size`. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
- For async search, filter and replace `options` yourself; the built-in filter only matches labels.

Accessibility:
- Input has `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `autocomplete="off"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the list is a `role="listbox"` of `role="option"` items. DOM focus stays on the input.
- Keyboard: focus or click opens the list, type to filter, Arrow Up/Down move the highlight, Enter selects, Escape closes; blur restores the selected label. Clear the value by emptying the input (Ctrl/Cmd+A, Backspace).
- The toggle and clear buttons are pointer shortcuts: they are removed from the tab order (`tabindex=-1`), named ("Toggle options", "Clear selection") and 24px (36px on touch devices) with a focus ring. Clear is only rendered while a value exists.
- The empty message is a polite `role="status"` region, so "No results" is announced when typing filters everything out. The disabled state is read from the native `disabled` attribute.
- Inside a Field the input receives `id` (label `for`), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` (only when invalid), `required`; otherwise set `aria-label`.
- `status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon left of the buttons. Success and warning also add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the input references from `aria-describedby`; error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours. The input keeps end padding so text never runs under the icon or the buttons.
- The input is 16px on small screens (no iOS zoom) and 14px from `md`, at least 44px tall on touch devices; the list is capped to the available width and scrolls inside. Highlighted options keep an outline in forced-colors mode. Layout uses logical properties (RTL safe).

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const lang = ref('')
const languages = [{ value: 'ts', label: 'TypeScript' }, { value: 'go', label: 'Go' }, { value: 'rs', label: 'Rust' }, { value: 'py', label: 'Python', disabled: true }]
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
  <Combobox v-model="lang" :options="languages" placeholder="Search language" aria-label="Language" clearable />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ lang || 'nothing' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: In a Field with custom empty text
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const country = ref('')
const countries = [{ value: 'pl', label: 'Poland' }, { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' }, { value: 'fr', label: 'France' }]
</script>

<Field class="max-w-xs" label="Country" hint="Start typing to filter." :error="country ? '' : 'Pick a country'" required>
  <Combobox v-model="country" :options="countries" placeholder="Country" empty-text="No such country" />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
  <Combobox aria-label="Outline" placeholder="Outline" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox variant="filled" aria-label="Filled" placeholder="Filled" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox variant="underline" aria-label="Underline" placeholder="Underline" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost" placeholder="Ghost" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
  <Combobox size="xs" aria-label="Extra small" placeholder="xs" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox size="sm" aria-label="Small" placeholder="sm" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox size="lg" aria-label="Large" placeholder="lg" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox shape="pill" aria-label="Pill" placeholder="pill" clearable default-value="a" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
  <Combobox shape="square" aria-label="Square" placeholder="square" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Option A' }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-3">
  <Field label="Country" hint="Sample message: shipping is available."><Combobox status="success" default-value="a" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Poland' }]" /></Field>
  <Field label="Language" hint="Sample message: translation is incomplete."><Combobox status="warning" default-value="a" clearable :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'German' }]" /></Field>
  <Field label="Timezone" error="Sample message: pick a timezone."><Combobox status="error" placeholder="Search timezone" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Europe/Warsaw' }]" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Custom option and empty slots
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const user = ref('u1')
</script>

<Combobox v-model="user" class="max-w-xs" aria-label="Assignee" :options="[{ value: 'u1', label: 'Sample user A' }, { value: 'u2', label: 'Sample user B' }]">
  <template #option="{ option }"><span>{{ option.label }}</span> <Badge variant="secondary">user</Badge></template>
  <template #empty>Nobody found. <Button variant="link" size="xs">Invite</Button></template>
</Combobox>
```

# ModelPicker
group: forms / Selection
Searchable, grouped single choice over plain option data with a description and text badges per option.

Use `ModelPicker` when people choose one entry from a list of engines, presets, modes or plans and each entry needs a sentence of explanation. It is a `Combobox` with richer rows: type to filter on the label and the description, move with the arrow keys, Enter picks, Escape closes. The options are plain data, so the same component works for any list. `v-model` is the option `id` (a string); `""` means nothing selected, and a model value that matches no option shows an empty input. Groups: pass entries of `{ label, options }`, or give flat options a `group` key and they are gathered under one heading in order of first appearance; the two forms can be mixed, and options without a group stay ungrouped. Badges are short words ("Fast", "Preview") rendered as text, so they do not rely on colour; they are not searched. A disabled option is shown dimmed, skipped by the keyboard and cannot be chosen. Use `Select` for a short list without search, `Combobox` when options need only a label. Server-side search is not built in: filter `options` yourself. `class` goes on the root; other attributes go to the `<input>`.

import { ModelPicker } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- options: Array<ModelPickerOption | ModelPickerGroup> = [] - Plain data. `ModelPickerOption` is `{ id: string; label: string; description?: string; badges?: string[]; disabled?: boolean; group?: string }`, `ModelPickerGroup` is `{ label: string; options: ModelPickerOption[] }`. Ids are unique across all groups.
- modelValue: string | null - v-model: the selected option `id`. `""`/`null` mean nothing selected. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultValue: string - Initial id when uncontrolled.
- placeholder: string - Input placeholder.
- emptyText: string = 'No matching options' - Message when nothing matches the search. Use the `empty` slot for rich content.
- clearable: boolean = false - Shows a clear button while an option is selected; clearing emits `""`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Input height: 28px, 32px, 36px or 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of the input. `outline` is bordered, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens on focus, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of the input. `underline` is always square-cornered. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon left of the buttons; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables input, toggle and clear. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- required: boolean = false - Native required on the input. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.
- name: string - Form field name; a hidden input is rendered when inside a `<form>`.
- open: boolean - Controlled open state (`v-model:open`).
- id: string - Input id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root element (width/layout); wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- option ({ option: ModelPickerOption }) - Replaces the content of each row (default: label, badges and description).
- empty - Content shown when nothing matches (default: `emptyText`).

Events:
- update:modelValue [id: string] - Emitted when an option is chosen (or `""` when cleared).
- update:open [value: boolean] - Emitted when the list opens or closes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder does not count).
- Throws a ContractError when an option `id` is missing, empty or used twice.
- Throws a ContractError when an option has no `label`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `{ label, options }` group has no `label`.

Rules:
- Pass `options` as data: `{ id, label, description?, badges?, disabled?, group? }`, or `{ label, options }` groups. Do not nest item components.
- Bind `v-model` to a string id; treat `""` as empty. Use `clearable` for optional fields.
- Wrap in Field with a label or pass `aria-label`; width goes in `class`, other attributes reach the input.
- Every option needs a unique non-empty `id` and a `label`; every group needs a `label`.
- Badges are short words, not icons or colours. Search matches the label and the description only.
- Look props are `variant`, `shape`, `status` and `size`. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.

Accessibility:
- The input has `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the list is a `role="listbox"` of `role="option"` rows, with `role="group"` and a heading for each labelled group. DOM focus stays on the input.
- Keyboard: focus or click opens the list, type to filter by label and description, Arrow Up/Down move the highlight across groups, Enter chooses, Escape closes; blur restores the selected label. Disabled options are skipped. Empty the input (Ctrl/Cmd+A, Backspace) to clear.
- The toggle and clear buttons are pointer shortcuts removed from the tab order, named ("Toggle options", "Clear selection") and 24px (36px on touch devices) with a focus ring.
- Each row reads as one option: label, badges, then description. Badges are words, never a colour only. The chosen row shows a check mark, and a disabled row is dimmed and marked `aria-disabled`.
- The empty message is a polite `role="status"` region, so "No matching options" is announced when typing filters everything out.
- Inside a Field the input receives `id` (label `for`), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `required`; otherwise set `aria-label`. `status` adds an icon, and success and warning add hidden text; `error` sets `aria-invalid`.
- The input is 16px on small screens (no iOS zoom) and at least 44px tall on touch devices. Rows wrap long text instead of overflowing, the list is capped to the available width and scrolls inside, highlighted rows keep an outline in forced-colors mode, and layout uses logical properties (RTL safe).

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const preset = ref('')
const presets = [{ id: 'draft', label: 'Draft - fast', description: 'Quick first pass for short texts.', badges: ['Fast'] }, ...]
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <ModelPicker v-model="preset" :options="presets" aria-label="Preset" placeholder="Choose a preset" clearable />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ preset || 'nothing' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Groups as data
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const preset = ref('review')
</script>

<ModelPicker v-model="preset" class="max-w-sm" :options="groups" aria-label="Preset" />
```

Example: Groups with a group key
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const preset = ref('')
</script>

<ModelPicker v-model="preset" class="max-w-sm" :options="items" aria-label="Preset" placeholder="Choose a preset" />
```

Example: Uncontrolled with a default
```vue
<ModelPicker class="max-w-sm" :options="options" default-value="summary" aria-label="Preset" />
```

Example: In a Field with an empty state
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const preset = ref('')
</script>

<Field class="max-w-sm" label="Preset" hint="Search by name or description." required>
  <ModelPicker v-model="preset" :options="options" placeholder="Search presets" empty-text="No preset matches that search" />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <ModelPicker aria-label="Outline" placeholder="Outline" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker variant="filled" aria-label="Filled" placeholder="Filled" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker variant="underline" aria-label="Underline" placeholder="Underline" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost" placeholder="Ghost" :options="options" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <ModelPicker size="xs" aria-label="Extra small" placeholder="xs" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker size="sm" aria-label="Small" placeholder="sm" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker size="lg" aria-label="Large" placeholder="lg" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker shape="pill" aria-label="Pill" placeholder="pill" clearable default-value="draft" :options="options" />
  <ModelPicker shape="square" aria-label="Square" placeholder="square" :options="options" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <Field label="Reviewer" hint="Sample message: this preset is available."><ModelPicker status="success" default-value="review" :options="options" /></Field>
  <Field label="Drafter" hint="Sample message: this preset is slow today."><ModelPicker status="warning" default-value="draft" :options="options" /></Field>
  <Field label="Summariser" error="Sample message: choose a preset."><ModelPicker status="error" placeholder="Choose a preset" :options="options" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Custom row
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const preset = ref('draft')
</script>

<ModelPicker v-model="preset" class="max-w-sm" aria-label="Preset" :options="options">
  <template #option="{ option }"><span>{{ option.label }}</span></template>
</ModelPicker>
```

# NativeSelect
group: forms / Selection
Styled native <select> with chevron, options array or slot content, placeholder, variants, sizes, shapes, status and Field wiring.

Use `NativeSelect` for simple option lists where the platform picker is a feature (mobile, long lists, forms that must work without JS-heavy widgets). Provide options through the `options` array, or through the default slot with `<option>` / `<optgroup>` for grouping; both can be combined. Use `Select` for custom-styled dropdowns with rich items, `Combobox` for type-to-filter. `placeholder` renders a disabled, hidden first option with an empty value shown while nothing is selected. `class` is applied to the wrapper (use it for width such as `w-48`); every other attribute (`name`, `autocomplete`, `aria-*`) goes to the `<select>`.

import { NativeSelect } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - v-model value. `null`/`undefined` render as empty. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- options: Array<{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }> - Options rendered as `<option>` before any slot content.
- placeholder: string - Disabled hidden first option (value `""`) shown while no value is selected; text is muted.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`, the chevron sits flush at the end), border on hover and fill on focus (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is fully rounded and moves the chevron in; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon left of the chevron. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the select. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- required: boolean = false - Native required. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the wrapper element; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - `<option>` / `<optgroup>` elements, rendered after the `options` array.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted on the native change event.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the select has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder option does not count).

Rules:
- Use `options` for simple lists, the default slot for `<optgroup>`. Do not mix a placeholder with a pre-selected value.
- Bind with `v-model`; the value is always a string.
- Put width classes (`w-48`) in `class` (applied to the wrapper); pass `name`/`autocomplete` as plain attributes.
- Wrap in Field with a label; never rely on the placeholder as the label.
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The chevron and the status icon are decorative and ignore pointer events.
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours.
- Native `<select>` semantics: platform picker, full keyboard (Arrow keys, type-ahead, Space or Alt+Down to open) and screen-reader support.
- Inside a Field it receives `id` (label `for`), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `required` and disabled state; otherwise give it `aria-label`.
- The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden` SVG) and ignores pointer events. Options use popover colours, so they stay readable in dark mode.
- The placeholder is a disabled, hidden first option; with `required` the browser reports the empty choice as invalid after interaction.
- Responsive: `w-full min-w-0`; 16px text below `md` prevents iOS focus zoom; 44px tall on touch pointers. The chevron uses `end-3`, so RTL works.

Example: Options array with placeholder
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const country = ref('')
const countries = [{ value: 'pl', label: 'Poland' }, { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' }, { value: 'fr', label: 'France', disabled: true }]
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
  <NativeSelect v-model="country" :options="countries" placeholder="Choose a country" aria-label="Country" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Value: {{ country || '(none)' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Slot options with optgroups in a Field
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const city = ref('')
</script>

<Field class="max-w-xs" label="City" hint="Where we ship from." :error="city ? '' : 'Choose a city'" required>
  <NativeSelect v-model="city" placeholder="Select city">
    <optgroup label="Poland">
      <option value="waw">Warsaw</option>
      <option value="krk">Krakow</option>
    </optgroup>
    <optgroup label="Germany">
      <option value="ber">Berlin</option>
    </optgroup>
  </NativeSelect>
</Field>
```

Example: Variants and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-3">
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" variant="outline" aria-label="Outline" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Outline' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" variant="filled" aria-label="Filled" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Filled' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" variant="underline" aria-label="Underline" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Underline' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Ghost' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" shape="pill" aria-label="Pill" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Pill' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" shape="square" aria-label="Square" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Square' }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-3">
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" status="success" aria-label="Valid choice" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Available' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" status="warning" aria-label="Choice with a warning" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Limited stock' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" status="error" aria-label="Invalid choice" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Unavailable' }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" size="xs" aria-label="Extra small" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Extra small' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" size="sm" aria-label="Small" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Small' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" aria-label="Medium" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Medium' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" size="lg" aria-label="Large" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Large' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" disabled aria-label="Disabled" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Disabled' }]" />
  <NativeSelect model-value="a" invalid aria-label="Invalid" :options="[{ value: 'a', label: 'Invalid' }]" />
</div>
```

# Select
group: forms / Selection
Custom single-select dropdown with groups, labels, keyboard typeahead and Field wiring.

Use `Select` (compound: `Select`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectLabel`, `SelectSeparator`) when you need a styled, accessible dropdown for 4+ options, with grouping or rich item content. Use `NativeSelect` for the best mobile UX and simple option lists, `Combobox` when the user needs to filter a long list by typing, `RadioGroup`/`SegmentedControl` for 2-5 visible options. The model is the selected item value (string). Item values must be NON-EMPTY strings (use a `Placeholder` on `SelectValue` for the empty state, not an item with value `""`). The content is portalled, so style it through `SelectContent`'s `class`, not through the parent. Wrap in `Field` for label, hint and error; the trigger receives `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and disabled state.

import { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectValue, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectGroup, SelectLabel, SelectSeparator } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string - v-model: the selected item value. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultValue: string - Initial value when uncontrolled.
- open: boolean - Controlled open state (`v-model:open`).
- defaultOpen: boolean - Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the trigger.
- required: boolean = false - Marks the select required for forms and `aria-required`.
- name: string - Form field name; a hidden native select is rendered inside a `<form>`.

Parts:
- SelectTrigger - The button that shows the value and opens the list. Applies the shared field surface and a chevron. It carries the look props (`size`, `variant`, `shape`, `status`) because the trigger is the field surface; the `Select` root is a compound root with no element of its own. `selectTriggerVariants` returns the same classes for a plain element.
    - size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height: 28px, 32px, 36px or 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens on focus, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
    - shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `underline` is always square-cornered, so `shape` does not change it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
    - status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon before the chevron; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Disables the trigger. Also inherited from the Select root and a surrounding Field.
    - invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.
    - id: string - Trigger id. Falls back to the surrounding Field id.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.
- SelectValue - Displays the selected item text or the placeholder. Place inside SelectTrigger.
    - placeholder: string - Text shown while no value is selected.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged onto the value element.
- SelectContent - Portalled floating list with scroll buttons. Contains SelectItem/SelectGroup/SelectSeparator.
    - position: 'popper' | 'item-aligned' = 'popper' - `popper` anchors under the trigger and matches its width; `item-aligned` overlays the selected item.
    - side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' = 'bottom' - Preferred side (popper only).
    - align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'start' - Alignment against the trigger (popper only).
    - sideOffset: number = 4 - Gap in px between trigger and content (popper only).
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Row density of every item: `sm` is compact (12px text), `md` the standard row, `lg` a roomy 16px row. A `size` on a `SelectItem` wins. Items stay 44px tall on touch devices. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last on the floating surface; wins over internal classes.
- SelectItem - One option with a check indicator when selected.
    - value: string - Item value. Must be a non-empty string.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Prevents selecting this item.
    - textValue: string - Text for typeahead and the trigger display when the slot content is not plain text.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Row density. Defaults to the `size` of the surrounding `SelectContent`, then `md`.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.
- SelectGroup - Groups items under a SelectLabel (`role="group"`).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged onto the group.
- SelectLabel - Non-selectable heading for a SelectGroup.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- SelectSeparator - Thin divider between groups.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.

Slots:
- default - SelectTrigger and SelectContent.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted when an item is selected.
- update:open [value: boolean] - Emitted when the list opens or closes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `SelectTrigger` has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (the selected value and the placeholder do not count).
- Throws a ContractError when `Select` has no `SelectTrigger`, no `SelectValue` or no `SelectContent`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `SelectItem` has a missing or empty `value` (the item is not rendered).

Rules:
- Always compose Select > SelectTrigger(SelectValue) + SelectContent(SelectItem...). Put `placeholder` on SelectValue.
- SelectItem `value` must be a non-empty string (an empty one raises a ContractError and the item is not rendered); never use "" for "none" - use a placeholder or a "none" sentinel value.
- Wrap in Field for label/error; otherwise give SelectTrigger an `aria-label`.
- Style the dropdown via SelectContent `class` (it is portalled out of the parent).
- Look props go on SelectTrigger (`variant`, `shape`, `status`, `size`), not on Select. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
- Prefer NativeSelect for simple lists or when native mobile pickers are desirable.

Accessibility:
- Trigger is a `role="combobox"` button with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`; the list is a `role="listbox"` with `role="option"` items and `aria-selected`.
- Keyboard: Enter/Space/Arrow Up/Arrow Down opens, Arrow keys move, Home/End jump, type-ahead jumps, Enter or Space selects, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- Inside a Field the trigger receives `id` (label `for`), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` (only when invalid); without Field set `aria-label` on SelectTrigger.
- Content is portalled and focus moves into the list while it is open; Tab does not leave it. Disabled items are skipped by keyboard navigation.
- The trigger is 16px text on small screens (no iOS zoom) and 14px from `md` (`lg` stays 16px); trigger and items are at least 44px tall on touch devices. The content is capped to the available width and scrolls with the scroll buttons or the keyboard.
- `status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon before the chevron. Success and warning also add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the trigger references from `aria-describedby`; error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours.
- The highlighted item keeps an outline in forced-colors mode and the selected item shows a check icon (not colour alone). Layout uses logical properties (RTL safe).

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const fruit = ref('')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
  <Select v-model="fruit">
    <SelectTrigger aria-label="Fruit">
      <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a fruit" />
    </SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectItem value="apple">Apple</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="banana">Banana</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="cherry" disabled>Cherry (sold out)</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ fruit || 'nothing' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Groups in a Field with an error
```vue

</script>

<Field class="max-w-xs" label="Timezone" hint="Used for schedules." :error="tz ? '' : 'Choose a timezone'" required>
  <Select v-model="tz">
    <SelectTrigger>
      <SelectValue placeholder="Select timezone" />
    </SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectGroup>
        <SelectLabel>Europe</SelectLabel>
        <SelectItem value="cet">Central European (CET)</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="gmt">Greenwich Mean (GMT)</SelectItem>
      </SelectGroup>
      <SelectSeparator />
      <SelectGroup>
        <SelectLabel>Americas</SelectLabel>
        <SelectItem value="est">Eastern (EST)</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="pst">Pacific (PST)</SelectItem>
      </SelectGroup>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
</Field>
```

# Slider
group: forms / Selection
Pick a number or a numeric range by dragging a thumb or using the keyboard.

Use `Slider` for approximate numeric choices where the exact value matters less than the position (volume, price range, opacity). The `v-model` is ALWAYS an array of numbers (reka-ui convention): `[40]` for one thumb, `[20, 80]` for a range, one thumb is rendered per value. Use `NumberInput` when the user must type or read an exact value. Name each thumb with `aria-label` or `thumb-labels`, or wrap the slider in a `Field` with a label.

import { Slider } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: number[] | null - Controlled values, one per thumb. Always an array, even for a single thumb.
- defaultValue: number[] = [min] - Initial values when uncontrolled.
- min: number = 0 - Lowest selectable value.
- max: number = 100 - Highest selectable value.
- step: number = 1 - Snap increment for drag and keyboard. Fractional steps are float-safe.
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - Layout direction. Vertical needs a parent with a height, or it falls back to a minimum of 11rem. Unknown values fall back to horizontal.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Track thickness (4 / 6 / 10 px). The thumb is 24px in `sm` and `md` and 28px in `lg`, so the target size rule holds in every size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'neutral' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the filled range and the thumb border. `neutral` uses the foreground colour. `invalid` always wins and uses the destructive colour, so an error never depends on the tone. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- marks: boolean | number[] | Array<{ value: number; label?: string }> = false - Tick marks under the track (beside it when vertical). `true` marks every step, or only the two ends when there would be more than 50 intervals. Numbers mark those values; objects also print `label`. Values outside `min`..`max` and duplicates are dropped. Marks are decorative (`aria-hidden`); a thumb that sits exactly on a labelled mark announces that label as its value text.
- showValue: boolean = false - Shows the current value in a bubble above each thumb (beside it when vertical). The bubble is decorative: the thumb already carries `aria-valuenow`. Thumbs that sit close together overlap their bubbles, so use it for single values or well separated ranges.
- formatValue: (value: number) => string - Formats the bubble text and sets `aria-valuetext` on the thumb, e.g. `(v) => v + '%'`. `aria-valuenow` stays the raw number.
- disabled: boolean = false - Blocks pointer and keyboard interaction and removes thumbs from the tab order.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets aria-invalid on thumbs and applies destructive styling.
- required: boolean = false - Marks the hidden form input as required.
- inverted: boolean = false - Flips the direction (max at the start edge).
- dir: 'ltr' | 'rtl' - Reading direction. In `rtl` the minimum is at the right edge: thumbs, fill, marks and the value bubble mirror, and ArrowLeft moves the thumb towards the maximum. Unset follows the nearest ancestor `dir` (or the document `dir`) once mounted and tracks later changes; set it explicitly in server-rendered pages, whose first paint cannot know the ancestor. Unknown values are ignored.
- minStepsBetweenThumbs: number = 0 - Minimum distance between range thumbs, measured in steps.
- name: string - Form field name. Inside a native form hidden inputs `name[0]`, `name[1]`... are rendered.
- ariaLabel: string - Accessible name for every thumb. With several thumbs the index is appended ("Price 1 of 2").
- thumbLabels: string[] - Per-thumb accessible names, e.g. `["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]`. Wins over `ariaLabel`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: number[]] - Fires on every change while dragging or keying.
- valueCommit [value: number[]] - Fires once when an interaction finishes. Use it for expensive work such as requests or filtering.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a thumb has no accessible name: no `aria-label`, `thumb-labels` entry or `Field` label.
- Throws a ContractError when `modelValue` or `defaultValue` is set but is not an array of numbers (use `ref([40])`, not `ref(40)`).

Rules:
- v-model is ALWAYS number[]: use `v-model="vol"` with `ref([40])`, never `ref(40)`.
- Always set `aria-label` (single) or `thumb-labels` (range), or wrap in `Field` with a label; an unnamed thumb raises a ContractError.
- Use @value-commit, not update:modelValue, for network requests.
- Use NumberInput when users need to type an exact number.
- Use `tone` for meaning (success, danger) and `size` for density; `invalid` always paints destructive, whatever the tone.
- Set `dir="rtl"` (or put the slider inside a `dir="rtl"` container) on right-to-left pages; do not mirror it with CSS transforms. In server-rendered pages pass `dir` explicitly.
- Use `marks` for ticks (numbers) or labelled stops (`{ value, label }`) and `show-value` with `format-value` to show units; both are decorative, so keep the value in a visible label too when it matters.

Accessibility:
- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-orientation`.
- Keyboard: in left-to-right, ArrowRight/ArrowUp raise the value and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown lower it by `step`; in right-to-left the arrows follow the thumb on screen, so ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers (ArrowUp/ArrowDown are unchanged). Shift+Arrow and PageUp/PageDown take larger steps, Home/End jump to the bounds. Tab moves between thumbs of a range.
- Name each thumb with `aria-label` or `thumb-labels`. Inside a `Field` with a label, thumbs without their own label are named by the Field label through `aria-labelledby` (a `label for` cannot name a slider); range thumbs add reka-ui's "Minimum"/"Maximum".
- Inside `Field` the first thumb receives the field id and aria-describedby; invalid sets aria-invalid on every thumb.
- Targets: thumbs are 24px, and on coarse pointers the whole track area is at least 44px tall, so a tap anywhere on it moves the nearest thumb.
- Marks and the value bubble are `aria-hidden` and decorative. `formatValue` and labelled marks set `aria-valuetext`; `aria-valuenow` always stays the number. Every size keeps a 24px thumb, and the bubble and marks never take pointer events.
- The tone is not the only signal of state: the thumb position, the filled range length and `aria-valuenow` carry the value, and `invalid` adds `aria-invalid`. The slider follows the reading direction: `dir="rtl"` (the prop, or the nearest ancestor and then the document `dir`) puts the minimum at the right edge and mirrors the thumbs, the fill, the marks and the value bubble. `inverted` flips it again.
- Forced-colors: track, range and thumb keep their token colours (`forced-color-adjust: none`) and the focus ring falls back to an outline. `disabled` dims the slider and removes the thumbs from the tab order.

Example: Single value
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const volume = ref([40])
</script>

<div class="flex w-64 max-w-full flex-col gap-2">
  <Slider v-model="volume" aria-label="Volume" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">Volume: {{ volume[0] }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Price range
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<Field label="Price range" :hint="`From ${price[0]} to ${price[1]}`" class="w-72 max-w-full tabular-nums">
  <Slider v-model="price" :min="0" :max="1000" :step="50" :thumb-labels="['Minimum price', 'Maximum price']" />
</Field>
```

Example: Value bubble and formatted value
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<div class="w-64 max-w-full">
  <Slider v-model="opacity" show-value :format-value="(v) => v + '%'" aria-label="Opacity" />
</div>
```

Example: Tick marks and labelled marks
```vue

</script>

  <Slider v-model="level" :step="25" marks aria-label="Sample level with ticks" />
  <Slider v-model="level" :step="25" :marks="labelled" aria-label="Sample level with labels" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue

  <Slider size="sm" :default-value="[30]" aria-label="Small" />
  <Slider size="md" :default-value="[50]" aria-label="Medium" />
  <Slider size="lg" :default-value="[70]" aria-label="Large" />
</div>
```

Example: Tones
```vue

  <Slider tone="primary" :default-value="[40]" aria-label="Primary tone" />
  <Slider tone="success" :default-value="[55]" aria-label="Success tone" />
  <Slider tone="danger" :default-value="[70]" aria-label="Danger tone" />
  <Slider tone="neutral" :default-value="[45]" aria-label="Neutral tone" />
  <Slider tone="info" :default-value="[60]" aria-label="Info tone" />

```

Example: Vertical
```vue

</script>

  <Slider v-model="gain" orientation="vertical" show-value :marks="[{ value: 0, label: '0' }, { value: 50, label: '50' }, { value: 100, label: '100' }]" aria-label="Sample gain" />
  <Slider :default-value="[70]" orientation="vertical" tone="success" size="lg" aria-label="Sample level" />
```

