# UsageEstimator
group: forms / Selection
Usage-based cost calculator: a slider and number field per metered dimension, a live cost per line and an estimated total.

Use `UsageEstimator` on a pricing page or a plan screen when the price depends on how much is used. Each dimension has a `rate` per unit (or per `per` units), optional free `included` units, bounds, and optionally graduated `tiers` that replace the flat rate. The estimate is computed by the exported pure helpers `lineCost` and `estimateTotal`, which never round: amounts are rounded only when displayed. Quantities are clamped to `min` and `max`; NaN and negative values count as 0. Tier bounds `upTo` count billable units (after `included`), and units above the last bounded tier are billed at that tier rate. Use `PlanPicker` to choose a plan and `RateCard` or `TieredPricing` to show the rates as a table. Always say that the figures are an estimate with `note`.

import { UsageEstimator } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- dimensions*: UsageDimension[] - Metered dimensions, one row each: `{ id, label, unit, unitSingular?, rate, per?, included?, min?, max, step?, tiers? }`. `id` and `label` are required and unique, `max` is a finite number above `min`, `rate` is at least 0. `tiers` is `{ upTo: number | null, rate: number }[]` in ascending order.
- modelValue: Record<string, number> - v-model: quantity per dimension id. A missing id counts as that dimension's `min` (or 0). Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultValue: Record<string, number> - Initial quantities when uncontrolled.
- currency: string - ISO 4217 currency code. Default `USD`.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for money and quantities. Defaults to the ConfigProvider locale, else `en-US`.
- period: string - Text after the total, such as "/month". It is also spoken with the total.
- input: 'slider' | 'number' | 'both' = 'both' - Controls in each row. With `slider` alone the quantity is shown as text. Unknown values fall back to `both`.
- showBreakdown: boolean = true - Show the cost of each row and its rate hint. The total is always shown.
- totalLabel: string = 'Estimated total' - Label of the total line, also used in the spoken update.
- note: string - Disclaimer under the total, such as "Sample rates. Estimate only." Use the `note` slot for rich content.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Spacing, text size and control size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'card' | 'plain' = 'card' - `card` is a bordered panel; `plain` has no surface. Unknown values fall back to `card`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root element; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- note - Rich disclaimer under the total. Overrides the `note` prop.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: Record<string, number>] - Emitted with the full quantity map when a slider or number field changes a quantity.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a dimension has an empty `id` or two dimensions share an `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when a dimension has an empty `label`, which names its controls.
- Throws a ContractError when a dimension `max` is not a finite number above its `min`.
- Throws a ContractError when a dimension `rate` (or a tier `rate`) is not a finite number of at least 0.

Rules:
- Use UsageEstimator for usage-based pricing; use PlanPicker to choose a plan and RateCard or TieredPricing to list the rates.
- Give every dimension a unique `id`, a `label`, a `unit`, a `rate` and a `max`; set `step` so the slider moves in useful jumps.
- Set `unitSingular` ("seat") when `unit` is plural, so a per-unit rate reads "$5 / seat".
- Use `per` for rates quoted per 1,000 units and `included` for free units; use `tiers` for graduated pricing (`upTo` counts billable units, `null` means no limit).
- Compute the figure with `lineCost` and `estimateTotal`, never by hand; they do not round.
- Always set `note` to say the figure is an estimate, and `period` for the billing period.
- In examples, use labelled sample rates and round numbers ("Sample requests"), never real prices.

Accessibility:
- Every slider thumb and number field is named from the dimension `label` and `unit` ("Sample requests, requests"). The visible label is contained in that name.
- Keyboard: the slider takes the arrow keys, Home, End and Page Up/Down; the number field takes the arrow keys and typed digits, and commits on Enter or blur.
- The total is announced through one polite `role="status"` region, once the quantities stop changing (about 600ms), not on every slider step.
- Rows stack at 375px: the label and cost on one line, the slider above the number field. Numbers use tabular figures and logical properties, so right-to-left layouts mirror.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const dimensions = [{ id: 'requests', label: 'Sample requests', unit: 'requests', rate: 0.5, per: 1000, max: 100000, step: 1000 }]
</script>

<UsageEstimator :dimensions="dimensions" :default-value="{ requests: 20000 }" period="/month" note="Sample rate. Estimate only." class="max-w-xl" />
```

Example: Included units, tiers and a shown model
```vue

```

# CopyField
group: forms / Text fields
Read-only value (API key, URL, token) with a joined copy-to-clipboard button, copied feedback, variants, sizes, shapes and status.

Use `CopyField` to show a value the user should copy rather than type: API keys, share links, connection strings. The input selects its whole text on focus; the button copies using the async Clipboard API with an `execCommand` fallback (so it also works on plain-http origins), shows a check and "Copied" for `copiedDuring` ms and announces it through a polite live region; a failed copy shows and announces "Copy failed" the same way. `mask` hides the value but still copies the real one. Not for editable fields.

import { CopyField } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- value: string | null - Text shown and copied.
- modelValue: string | null - Alias of `value` (wins when both are set) so the field works with `v-model`. Never emits.
- label: string = 'Copy' - Copy button text.
- copiedLabel: string = 'Copied' - Button text and live-region message in the copied state.
- failedLabel: string = 'Copy failed' - Button text and live-region message when copying fails.
- copiedDuring: number = 2000 - Milliseconds the copied state lasts. Read once when the component is created.
- mask: boolean = false - Render the value as password dots (the real value is still copied).
- iconOnly: boolean = false - Visually hide the button text (kept for assistive tech).
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables input and button.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid`. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of the input and the joined button: muted fill (`filled`), a line with a text button (`underline`), borderless until hover with a text button (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height of the input and the button: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of the whole control. `pill` rounds the start of the input and the end of the button; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour on the input and the button, with an icon at the end of the input. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- inputClass: string | object | array - Classes for the inner <input>.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the wrapper element.

Events:
- copy [value: string] - The value was copied.
- copy-error [error: unknown] - Copying threw (e.g. no clipboard access at all).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when the copy button has no text, that is when `label` is blank.

Rules:
- Use CopyField for read-only copyable values; use Input for editable ones.
- Always label it (Field label or `aria-label`); with `icon-only` also pass a descriptive `label`.
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`. The copy button follows `variant`, `shape` and `size`.
- Handle failures with `@copy-error`; `@copy` fires only after a successful copy.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The icon is not focusable and does not cover the button.
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator on the input and the button (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours. The button text and its copied and failed states are the same in every variant.
- Input is `readonly` (focusable and selectable) and selects all text on focus. `autocomplete="off"` and no spellcheck.
- Copy button is `type="button"` with visible text (or screen-reader-only text with `iconOnly`) that changes to the copied or failed label; icons are decorative. It is not disabled while feedback shows, so keyboard focus is kept and a failed copy can be retried.
- A `role="status"` region outside the button announces "Copied" or "Copy failed" and is cleared after `copiedDuring` ms, so no stale message stays in browse mode.
- Button is disabled only when the value is empty or the field is disabled. It is 36px tall (44px on touch pointers); text is 16px below `md`.
- Use a descriptive `label` (for example "Copy token") when several copy buttons share a page.

Example: API key
```vue
<CopyField value="sample-api-key-0000" aria-label="Sample API key" />
```

Example: In a Field, masked, with feedback
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const copies = ref(0)
</script>

<Field label="Secret token" hint="Shown once. Store it somewhere safe.">
  <CopyField value="sample-token-0000" mask icon-only label="Copy token" @copy="copies++" />
</Field>
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Copied {{ copies }} time(s)</p>
```

Example: Variants, shapes and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-3">
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" variant="outline" aria-label="Outline value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" variant="filled" aria-label="Filled value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" variant="underline" aria-label="Underline value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" shape="pill" aria-label="Pill value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" shape="square" aria-label="Square value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" size="xs" aria-label="Extra small value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" size="lg" aria-label="Large value" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-3">
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" status="success" aria-label="Verified value" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" status="warning" aria-label="Value that expires soon" />
  <CopyField value="sample-value-0000" status="error" aria-label="Revoked value" />
</div>
```

# DateInput
group: forms / Text fields
Styled native date, time, datetime-local or month input with min/max validation messaging, variants, sizes, shapes and status.

Wraps the browser-native picker (`type="date" | "time" | "datetime-local" | "month"`) in the shared field surface. `v-model` is the ISO string the native input produces (`2024-05-01`, `13:30`, `2024-05-01T13:30`, `2024-05`; empty string when cleared). When the value falls outside `min`/`max` (compared as ISO strings) the field gets `aria-invalid`, an inline message is shown and `invalid` / `validate` events fire. The value is still emitted, so the parent decides whether to block submission. Build a custom calendar popover if you need ranges or presets; use this for fast, accessible, mobile-friendly entry.

import { DateInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - ISO value matching `type`. Empty string / null = no value.
- type: 'date' | 'time' | 'datetime-local' | 'month' = 'date' - Native input type; also determines the ISO format of value, min and max.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`), border on hover and fill on focus (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Text stays 16px below `md` and touch pointers get a 44px target. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is fully rounded; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon after the native picker button. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`. An out-of-range value is still invalid whatever the status.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- min: string - Lowest allowed ISO value. Forwarded natively and used for validation messaging.
- max: string - Highest allowed ISO value.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the input; changes are ignored.
- readonly: boolean = false - Shows the value but blocks changes.
- required: boolean = false - Native required attribute.
- invalid: boolean = false - Marks the field invalid regardless of min/max (no message is shown).
- messages: { min?: string; max?: string } = 'Must be on or after {min}' / 'Must be on or before {max}' - Custom out-of-range messages; `{min}` and `{max}` are replaced with the limits.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the <input>; wins over internal classes. Other attributes (name, id, aria-*) go to the <input>.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Fires on every user change with the ISO string (even when outside min/max).
- validate [result: { valid: boolean; reason: 'min' | 'max' | null; message: string | null; value: string }] - Fires after every user change with the validation result. Empty values are valid.
- invalid [result: { valid: false; reason: 'min' | 'max'; message: string; value: string }] - Fires only when the value is outside min/max.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- v-model is an ISO string matching `type`, never a Date object.
- min/max must use the same ISO format as `type` (e.g. `08:00` for time, `2024-05` for month).
- Out-of-range values are still emitted. Block submission yourself using @invalid or the `validate` event.
- Attributes (name, id, aria-label) land on the inner <input>.
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`. The min/max message stays automatic.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The icon is not focusable and does not cover the native picker button.
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours.
- Native picker: keyboard entry (Arrow keys move between segments, typing fills them, Backspace clears one) and screen-reader semantics come from the browser. Give it a label through `Field` or `aria-label`.
- The out-of-range message lives in one persistent `role="status"` region that is empty and visually hidden while the value is valid, so the text is announced when it appears. While it has text, the input gets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` points at it, appended to any `Field` description or your own `aria-describedby`.
- Inside `Field` the field id, hint/error description and invalid/disabled state are applied.
- Responsive: text is 16px below `md` (no iOS zoom) and 14px from `md`, with a 44px minimum height on touch pointers. The input is `min-w-0` and fills its container, so it never overflows at 320px. The control follows the dark colour-scheme.

Example: Date with range
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const date = ref('2024-06-15')
</script>

<Field label="Start date" class="w-56">
  <DateInput v-model="date" min="2024-01-01" max="2024-12-31" />
</Field>
```

Example: Custom message and validation event
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const when = ref('2023-01-01')
const status = ref('')
</script>

<div class="flex w-56 flex-col gap-2">
  <DateInput
    v-model="when"
    min="2024-01-01"
    :messages="{ min: 'Pick a date from {min} onwards' }"
    aria-label="Event date"
    @validate="status = $event.valid ? 'valid' : $event.reason"
  />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Last validation: {{ status || 'n/a' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Variants, shapes and sizes
```vue
<div class="flex w-56 flex-col gap-3">
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" variant="outline" aria-label="Outline date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" variant="filled" aria-label="Filled date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" variant="underline" aria-label="Underline date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" shape="pill" aria-label="Pill date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" shape="square" aria-label="Square date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" size="xs" aria-label="Extra small date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" size="lg" aria-label="Large date" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="flex w-56 flex-col gap-3">
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" status="success" aria-label="Valid date" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-12-31" status="warning" aria-label="Date near the end of the range" />
  <DateInput model-value="2024-05-01" status="error" aria-label="Unavailable date" />
</div>
```

Example: Time and month
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const time = ref('09:30')
const month = ref('2024-05')
</script>

<div class="flex w-56 flex-col gap-3">
  <DateInput v-model="time" type="time" min="08:00" max="18:00" aria-label="Meeting time" />
  <DateInput v-model="month" type="month" aria-label="Billing month" />
</div>
```

# Editable
group: forms / Text fields
Inline editable text: click to edit, Enter saves, Escape cancels, blur saves (configurable).

Use `Editable` for titles, names and short notes that should look like plain text until the user wants to change them (rename a project, edit a caption). The preview is a focusable button-like element: click (or double-click / focus via `activationMode`), Enter, Space or F2 starts editing; the input is focused and its text selected. `submitMode` controls what commits: `both` (Enter and blur, default), `enter` (blur cancels) or `blur` (Enter ignored). Escape always cancels. With `multiline` a textarea is used and Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+Enter commits. Not for forms that need always-visible fields: use `Input` / `Textarea` there.

import { Editable } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - v-model text. `null` renders as empty. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- placeholder: string - Muted text shown in preview while empty, and the control placeholder.
- submitMode: 'both' | 'enter' | 'blur' = 'both' - `both`: Enter and blur commit. `enter`: Enter commits, blur cancels. `blur`: only blur commits, Enter is ignored. Escape always cancels.
- activationMode: 'click' | 'dblclick' | 'focus' = 'click' - How the preview enters edit mode with the pointer / focus. Enter, Space and F2 always work on the focused preview. In `focus` mode a keyboard commit still returns focus to the preview without re-entering edit mode.
- multiline: boolean = false - Edit in a `<textarea>`; Enter inserts a newline, Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+Enter commits.
- rows: number = 3 - Textarea rows (multiline only).
- disabled: boolean = false - Not editable, dimmed, `aria-disabled`. Also inherited from a Field.
- readonly: boolean = false - Not editable and not interactive; renders as plain text.
- required: boolean = false - Native required on the editing control. Also inherited from a Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid` on the editing control. Also set by a Field with an error.
- variant: 'plain' | 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' = 'plain' - Look of the preview before editing. `plain` reads as text until hovered, `outline` always shows a border, `filled` shows a muted fill, `underline` shows only a bottom rule. The editing control keeps a visible border (a thicker bottom rule for `underline`). Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size of preview and control (12px, 14px, 16px or 18px from the `md` breakpoint; `lg` is always 18px). 16px below the `md` breakpoint (no iOS focus zoom). On coarse pointers both are at least 44px high.
- ariaLabel: string - Accessible name of the editing control. The preview button is named `<ariaLabel>: <visible text>`, which contains its visible text.
- savedLabel: string = 'Saved' - Spoken after a commit through a polite live region (`Saved: <text>`).
- cancelledLabel: string = 'Changes discarded' - Spoken after the draft is discarded.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted on commit when the text changed.
- submit [value: string] - Emitted on every commit, even when unchanged.
- cancel [value: string] - Emitted when the draft is discarded; payload is the unchanged value.
- edit - Emitted when edit mode starts.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the control has no accessible name: no `ariaLabel` (or `aria-label`) and no `Field` label.

Rules:
- Use Editable for inline rename/caption patterns, not for regular form fields (use Input/Textarea).
- Always provide `aria-label` or a Field label (an `aria-labelledby` on the root does not reach the control); add `placeholder` so empty values stay clickable.
- Use `v-model`; listen to `submit`/`cancel` for side effects like API calls.
- Use `variant="plain"` for titles that should read as text, `outline` or `filled` when the value must look editable at rest, `underline` inside dense forms. `size` also takes `xs`.
- Use `multiline` for long text: plain Enter inserts a newline, Shift/Ctrl+Enter saves.

Accessibility:
- Preview is `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`; Enter, Space or F2 starts editing. Disabled/readonly previews are not interactive.
- The preview button is named `<ariaLabel>: <visible text>` (or the Field label plus its text through `aria-labelledby`), so the visible text is always part of the name. The editing control gets `ariaLabel`, `aria-invalid`, `required`, `autocomplete="off"`, `enterkeyhint="done"` and Field wiring.
- Escape cancels; after a keyboard commit/cancel focus returns to the preview (also in `activationMode="focus"`) so keyboard users keep their place.
- A commit or cancel is announced through a polite `role="status"` region ("Saved: <text>", "Changes discarded").
- Responsive: preview and control are at least 32px high (44px on coarse pointers) and 16px text on small screens; the preview wraps long text and never overflows at 320px. Hover adds a border, so the editable state does not rely on background alone.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible way to tell it is editable and a visible focus indicator: `outline`, `filled` and `underline` show their edge at rest, `plain` shows a border on hover and focus. Forced-colors mode draws the border of every variant in system colours. `variant` never changes the keyboard map or the accessible name.
- IME composition Enter does not commit.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const title = ref('Quarterly report')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Editable v-model="title" placeholder="Untitled" aria-label="Title" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Saved: {{ title }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Multiline
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const note = ref('First line\nSecond line')
</script>

<Editable class="max-w-sm" v-model="note" multiline :rows="4" placeholder="Add a note" aria-label="Note" />
```

Example: Submit modes
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const a = ref('Enter only (blur cancels)')
const b = ref('Blur only (Enter ignored)')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Editable v-model="a" submit-mode="enter" aria-label="Enter mode" />
  <Editable v-model="b" submit-mode="blur" aria-label="Blur mode" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Editable size="xs" model-value="Extra small" aria-label="Extra small" />
  <Editable size="sm" model-value="Small" aria-label="Small" />
  <Editable size="md" model-value="Medium" aria-label="Medium" />
  <Editable size="lg" model-value="Large" aria-label="Large" />
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Editable model-value="Plain preview" aria-label="Plain" />
  <Editable variant="outline" model-value="Outline preview" aria-label="Outline" />
  <Editable variant="filled" model-value="Filled preview" aria-label="Filled" />
  <Editable variant="underline" model-value="Underline preview" aria-label="Underline" />
</div>
```

Example: Disabled and readonly
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Editable disabled model-value="Disabled" aria-label="Disabled" />
  <Editable readonly model-value="Read only" aria-label="Read only" />
</div>
```

Example: Events
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const name = ref('Sample project')
const log = ref('')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Editable v-model="name" aria-label="Project name" @edit="log = 'editing'" @submit="log = 'saved'" @cancel="log = 'cancelled'" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Last event: {{ log || 'none' }}</p>
</div>
```

# Input
group: forms / Text fields
Single-line text field with v-model, variants (outline, filled, underline, ghost), sizes, shapes, status, prefix and suffix slots and automatic Field wiring.

Use `Input` for short free text (name, email, URL, number). Wrap it in `Field` to get a label, hint and error message wired through `id`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`. Use `Textarea` for multi-line, `PasswordInput` / `SearchInput` / `NumberInput` / `DateInput` for specialised inputs. Standard attributes (`placeholder`, `name`, `autocomplete`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) fall through to the `<input>`. With `type="number"` the model is a `number` (or `""` when cleared); prefer `NumberInput` when you need clamping or steppers. `email`, `url` and `tel` inputs turn off autocorrect, autocapitalise and spellcheck. Set `autocomplete` and `inputmode` for the data you collect. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` change the look; `status` adds an icon (and screen reader text for `success` and `warning`), so state is never colour alone. The `prefix` and `suffix` slots hold an inset icon or one or two characters; use `InputGroup` for longer content or buttons. `inputVariants` gives a plain `<input>` the same look. Text is 16px below `md` (iOS Safari does not zoom on focus) and 44px tall on touch pointers.

import { Input } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | number | null - v-model value. `null`/`undefined` render as empty. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- type: string = 'text' - Native input type (`text`, `email`, `url`, `tel`, `number`, ...).
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface. `filled` uses a muted fill (the card colour in dark mode, at least 1.15:1 away from the outline fill there, 1.25:1 measured in Chrome on the page background), `underline` keeps only a bottom border (thicker on focus), `ghost` shows the border on hover and fills on focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Text stays 16px below `md` and touch pointers get a 44px target (except `lg`, already 44px). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is fully rounded, `square` has no radius. `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon at the end. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Anything but `default` wraps the input in a `span`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the input. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- readonly: boolean = false - Prevents editing but keeps the value focusable and submittable.
- required: boolean = false - Native required. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- prefix - Inset icon or one or two characters at the start (a currency symbol, `@`). Decorative (`aria-hidden`) and not clickable: say what it means in the label. Wraps the input in a `span`. Use `InputGroup` for text or buttons.
- suffix - Inset icon or one or two characters at the end (a unit, `%`). Decorative and not clickable. The status icon moves left of it.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string | number] - Emitted on every input event.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder does not count; `type="hidden"` is exempt).

Rules:
- Wrap every Input in `Field` with a label; never use placeholder as the only label.
- Use `v-model`, never mutate the prop. Use `invalid` or `Field error` for error state, not custom red classes.
- Pass `type`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode`, `name` as plain attributes.
- Pick one `variant` per form and keep it. Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.
- Use the `prefix` and `suffix` slots only for an icon or one or two characters; use `InputGroup` for text addons or buttons. Never rely on the slot to name the field.
- Import `inputVariants` to give a plain `<input>` the same look.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`).
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours for every variant.
- `prefix` and `suffix` are decorative: the field name must come from the label, not from the slot content.
- Native `<input>`: Tab focuses it, there are no custom key bindings. Always provide a visible label (via Field) or `aria-label`; a placeholder is not a label.
- Inside a Field the input receives the label `for` and `id`, `aria-describedby` (hint and error) and `aria-invalid` automatically.
- `invalid` sets `aria-invalid="true"`; visual and assistive state never diverge. A required, valid input reports `aria-invalid="false"`.
- `readonly` stays focusable and submittable; `disabled` leaves the tab order.
- Invalid state is not colour-only: the text error is linked, and forced-colors mode draws a dashed border.
- Responsive: `w-full min-w-0`, so it never overflows at 320px. 16px text below `md` prevents iOS focus zoom; `pointer-coarse:min-h-11` gives a 44px target on touch.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const name = ref('')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Input v-model="name" placeholder="Your name" aria-label="Name" autocomplete="name" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Hello, {{ name || 'stranger' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: In a Field with validation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const email = ref('nope')
</script>

<Field class="max-w-sm" label="Email" hint="We never share it." :error="email.includes('@') ? '' : 'Enter a valid email'" required>
  <Input v-model="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <Input variant="outline" placeholder="Outline" aria-label="Outline" />
  <Input variant="filled" placeholder="Filled" aria-label="Filled" />
  <Input variant="underline" placeholder="Underline" aria-label="Underline" />
  <Input variant="ghost" placeholder="Ghost" aria-label="Ghost" />
</div>
```

Example: Shapes and extra small
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <Input shape="rounded" placeholder="Rounded" aria-label="Rounded" />
  <Input shape="pill" placeholder="Pill" aria-label="Pill" />
  <Input shape="square" placeholder="Square" aria-label="Square" />
  <Input size="xs" placeholder="Extra small" aria-label="Extra small" />
  <Input variant="filled" shape="pill" size="lg" placeholder="Filled pill, large" aria-label="Filled pill, large" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <Input status="success" model-value="ada@example.com" aria-label="Valid email" />
  <Input status="warning" model-value="ada@example" aria-label="Email with a warning" />
  <Input status="error" model-value="ada" aria-label="Invalid email" />
  <Input status="success" variant="underline" model-value="Underline" aria-label="Success underline" />
  <Input status="error" shape="pill" model-value="Pill" aria-label="Error pill" />
</div>
```

Example: Prefix and suffix
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <Input aria-label="Price in dollars" placeholder="0.00" inputmode="decimal"><template #prefix>$</template></Input>
  <Input aria-label="Weight in kilograms" placeholder="0" inputmode="decimal"><template #suffix>kg</template></Input>
  <Input aria-label="Handle" placeholder="handle"><template #prefix>@</template></Input>
  <Input aria-label="Discount in percent" status="success" model-value="15"><template #suffix>%</template></Input>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and states
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <Input size="sm" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small" />
  <Input placeholder="Medium" aria-label="Medium" />
  <Input size="lg" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large" />
  <Input disabled model-value="Disabled" aria-label="Disabled" />
  <Input readonly model-value="Read only" aria-label="Read only" />
  <Input invalid model-value="Invalid" aria-label="Invalid" />
</div>
```

# InputGroup
group: forms / Text fields
Puts a prefix, a suffix or joined buttons around an Input, Textarea or NativeSelect so they share one field surface.

Use `InputGroup` with `InputGroupAddon` when a field needs fixed text ("https://", ".com", a currency sign), an icon, or an attached button ("Subscribe", "Apply"). `layout="inset"` (default) draws one surface around everything: the addons sit inside the border and the Input inside loses its own border, background and ring, so focus is shown once, on the group. `layout="joined"` keeps every child as its own control and only squares the touching edges, which suits an attached `Button` or `Select`. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` take the same values as every text field. Put the group inside `Field` for the label, hint and error: the Input inside still receives `id`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` from the Field. Give the inner Input the same `size` as the group, and a Button inside a joined group the matching Button size. Use the Input `prefix` and `suffix` slots instead when a single icon is all you need.

import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- layout: 'inset' | 'joined' = 'inset' - `inset`: one shared surface with the addons inside. `joined`: separate controls attached edge to edge. Unknown values fall back to `inset`.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of an inset group (a joined group draws no surface of its own). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Minimum height and text size: `xs` 28px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px, `lg` 44px (44px minimum on touch pointers except `lg`, which is already 44px). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of the group (inset) or of the outer edges of the row (joined). Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Inset only. Colours the border and adds a status icon; `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text. In a joined group give the Input its own `status`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string - Hidden text of the success and warning icons. Defaults to the English text (translate it).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the group; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- InputGroupAddon - A prefix, suffix or action next to the control. Text is muted; in a `joined` group it gets its own border and fill. A Button inside an inset addon is pulled toward the edge.
    - as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render. Use `span` or `label` when the addon should be associated with the control.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single child element (for example a `label`) with the addon attributes and classes merged into it, instead of a wrapper.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - InputGroupAddon parts and one Input, Textarea or NativeSelect, in visual order.

Rules:
- Wrap the whole group in `Field` with a label; never rely on the addon text as the label.
- Use `layout="joined"` for an attached Button, the default inset layout for text and icon addons.
- Give the inner Input the same `size` as the group; do not restyle the Input border, the group draws it.
- Put the addons and the control in visual order; `InputGroupAddon` before the Input is a prefix, after it a suffix.

Accessibility:
- The group is a plain container: it adds no role and no name. The control inside keeps its own label (use `Field`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), and addon text is read in document order with it.
- An addon that holds only an icon must keep the icon decorative (`aria-hidden`, the default of `Icon`); a Button inside an addon needs its own name like any Button.
- Focus shows once, as a border and ring on the whole group (`:has(:focus-visible)`), so keyboard users see which field is active (a `class` on the group can override the inner focus border); an invalid control inside turns the group border destructive. The group border stays visible in forced-colors mode, and an invalid group gets a dashed one.
- `status` is never colour only: an icon sits at the inline end, and `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text.
- Responsive: the group is `w-full min-w-0`, text is 16px below `md` and the minimum height is 44px on touch pointers.

Example: Prefix and suffix text
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const site = ref('')
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
  <Field label="Website">
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroupAddon>https://</InputGroupAddon>
      <Input v-model="site" placeholder="example" autocomplete="url" />
      <InputGroupAddon>.com</InputGroupAddon>
    </InputGroup>
  </Field>
  <Field label="Amount" hint="Sample amount in dollars.">
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroupAddon>$</InputGroupAddon>
      <Input type="number" inputmode="decimal" placeholder="0.00" />
      <InputGroupAddon>USD</InputGroupAddon>
    </InputGroup>
  </Field>
</div>
```

Example: Icon and attached button
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
  <Field label="Search the docs">
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroupAddon><Icon :icon="faMagnifyingGlass" size="sm" /></InputGroupAddon>
      <Input placeholder="Search" />
    </InputGroup>
  </Field>
  <Field label="Email" hint="One message a month.">
    <InputGroup layout="joined">
      <Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.test" autocomplete="email" />
      <Button type="submit">Subscribe</Button>
    </InputGroup>
  </Field>
  <Field label="Voucher code">
    <InputGroup>
      <Input placeholder="SAMPLE-CODE" />
      <InputGroupAddon><Button size="xs" variant="ghost" type="button">Apply</Button></InputGroupAddon>
    </InputGroup>
  </Field>
  <Field label="Reply-to address">
    <InputGroup layout="joined">
      <InputGroupAddon><Icon :icon="faEnvelope" size="sm" /></InputGroupAddon>
      <Input type="email" autocomplete="email" />
    </InputGroup>
  </Field>
</div>
```

Example: Variants, shapes and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <InputGroup variant="filled"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Filled" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup variant="underline"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Underline" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup variant="ghost"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Ghost" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup shape="pill"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Pill" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup shape="square"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Square" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup size="xs"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input size="xs" aria-label="Extra small" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup size="sm"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input size="sm" aria-label="Small" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup size="lg"><InputGroupAddon>@</InputGroupAddon><Input size="lg" aria-label="Large" /></InputGroup>
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <InputGroup status="success"><InputGroupAddon>https://</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Success" model-value="example" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup status="warning"><InputGroupAddon>https://</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Warning" model-value="example" /></InputGroup>
  <InputGroup status="error"><InputGroupAddon>https://</InputGroupAddon><Input aria-label="Error" invalid model-value="example" /></InputGroup>
</div>
```

# NumberInput
group: forms / Text fields
Numeric text field with -/+ steppers, clamping, keyboard stepping, float-safe arithmetic, variants, sizes, shapes and status.

A native `<input inputmode="decimal">` (deliberately NOT `type="number"`, which has inconsistent locale, scroll-wheel and validation behaviour) wrapped with stepper buttons. The value is committed on blur, Enter or a stepper/keyboard step: it is clamped to `min`/`max`, non-numeric drafts are rejected and the field reverts to the last valid value. `v-model` is `number | null` (`null` = empty). `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` style the whole control (the steppers follow); `status` adds an icon left of the increment stepper, plus screen reader text for `success` and `warning`. `numberInputVariants` gives a wrapper element the same surface. Use `Slider` for approximate picks, `Input` for free text and identifiers (zip codes, phone numbers) that merely look numeric.

import { NumberInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: number | null - Current value; `null` (or NaN/Infinity) means empty.
- min: number - Lower bound applied on commit and when stepping.
- max: number - Upper bound applied on commit and when stepping.
- step: number = 1 - Increment for steppers and ArrowUp/ArrowDown. PageUp/PageDown move by 10 steps. Stepping is float-safe (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3).
- precision: number - Fixed decimals: values are rounded and displayed padded (`1.50`). Omit to keep typed decimals.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the input and both steppers.
- readonly: boolean = false - Value is visible and focusable but cannot be changed by typing, keys or steppers.
- required: boolean = false - Native required attribute.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets aria-invalid and destructive styling.
- placeholder: string - Placeholder shown when empty.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`), border on hover and fill while focused (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height and stepper width: 28, 32, 36 and 44px tall. Text stays 16px below `md` and touch pointers get a 44px target. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is fully rounded and clips the steppers to it; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon left of the increment stepper. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- showSteppers: boolean = true - Render the -/+ buttons.
- decrementLabel: string = 'Decrease' - aria-label of the minus button (use for i18n or context: "Fewer guests").
- incrementLabel: string = 'Increase' - aria-label of the plus button.
- invalidLabel: string = 'Not a number, value restored' - Spoken through the polite live region when typed text is not a number and the previous value comes back.
- adjustedLabel: string = 'Adjusted to' - Spoken when `min`, `max` or `precision` changes what was typed (`Adjusted to 10`).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the wrapper; wins over internal classes. Other attributes (name, id, aria-*) go to the inner input.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: number | null] - Fires on commit (blur, Enter, stepper, arrow/page/home/end keys) with the clamped value, or null when emptied. Not fired while typing or when the value is unchanged.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. A wrapping `<label>` only counts without steppers, because the first button inside it is labelled instead.
- Throws a ContractError when a rendered stepper has no name, that is when `decrementLabel` or `incrementLabel` is blank while `showSteppers` is on.

Rules:
- v-model is number | null, never a string.
- Set `min`/`max` rather than validating after the fact; the value is clamped on commit.
- Give an `aria-label` or wrap in `Field` with a label.
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.
- Use `precision` for money-like fixed decimals; use `step` for fractional increments.
- Use Input (not NumberInput) for identifiers such as postcodes or phone numbers.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`).
- The surface is a wrapper, so the variants react to `focus-within`: `underline` thickens its bottom border and `ghost` fills while the input or a stepper has focus, and forced-colors mode keeps the outline.
- The input exposes role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow/min/max (omitted when empty or unbounded), aria-valuetext with the formatted value (`1.50`) and aria-readonly when `readonly`.
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown step, PageUp/PageDown step x10, Home/End jump to min/max when defined, Enter commits.
- Stepper buttons have aria-labels (`incrementLabel`/`decrementLabel`) and sit outside the tab order; the keyboard works on the input itself. A stepper click speaks the new value through a polite `role="status"` region.
- Rejected input is announced: non-numeric text restores the previous value ("Not a number, value restored") and clamping or rounding says "Adjusted to <value>".
- inputmode is `decimal` (`numeric` when `precision` is 0) and enterkeyhint is `done`. Inside `Field` the input gets the id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
- Responsive: 16px text below `md`, 44px height and stepper width on coarse pointers, tabular numerals, logical (RTL-safe) stepper borders and a forced-colors focus outline on the whole control.

Example: Quantity
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const qty = ref(2)
</script>

<div class="flex w-40 flex-col gap-2">
  <NumberInput v-model="qty" :min="1" :max="10" aria-label="Quantity" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Quantity: {{ qty }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Decimals with precision
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const amount = ref(9.9)
</script>

<Field label="Amount" hint="Step 0.1, two decimals" class="w-48">
  <NumberInput v-model="amount" :step="0.1" :precision="2" :min="0" />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants, shapes and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid w-48 gap-3">
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" variant="outline" aria-label="Outline quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" variant="filled" aria-label="Filled quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" variant="underline" aria-label="Underline quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" shape="pill" aria-label="Pill quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" shape="square" aria-label="Square quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" size="xs" aria-label="Extra small quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" size="lg" aria-label="Large quantity" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid w-48 gap-3">
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" status="success" aria-label="Valid quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="9" status="warning" aria-label="Quantity close to the limit" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="0" status="error" aria-label="Invalid quantity" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="4" status="success" :show-steppers="false" aria-label="Valid quantity without steppers" />
</div>
```

Example: Disabled and read-only
```vue
<div class="flex w-40 flex-col gap-3">
  <NumberInput :model-value="3" disabled aria-label="Disabled" />
  <NumberInput :model-value="3" readonly aria-label="Read only" />
</div>
```

# PasswordInput
group: forms / Text fields
Password field with an accessible show/hide toggle, variants, sizes, shapes and status.

Use `PasswordInput` for every password entry. It defaults to `autocomplete="current-password"` (set `new-password` on sign-up and change-password forms) so password managers work. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` style the input and the toggle stays inside it; `status` adds an icon left of the toggle (plus screen reader text for `success` and `warning`). `passwordInputVariants` gives a plain `<input>` the same look. The toggle button is disabled when the field is disabled and stays usable when readonly. `visible` is optional controlled state (`v-model:visible`). The toggle keeps one name and exposes its state with `aria-pressed`, and a screen-reader-only warning (`revealWarning`) says the password will be shown on screen.

import { PasswordInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - Current value (v-model). Uncontrolled when omitted.
- visible: boolean = false - Show the password as text. Supports `v-model:visible`; uncontrolled when omitted.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the input and the toggle.
- readonly: boolean = false - Prevents editing; toggle still works.
- required: boolean = false - Native required.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid` and destructive styling. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`), border on hover and fill on focus (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Control height: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is fully rounded; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon left of the toggle. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- autocomplete: string = 'current-password' - Native autocomplete token.
- showLabel: string = 'Show password' - Accessible name of the toggle in both states (localise here); the state is `aria-pressed`.
- hideLabel: string = 'Hide password' - Deprecated: kept so existing code compiles. The toggle name no longer changes with the state.
- revealWarning: string = 'Shows the password as plain text on screen.' - Screen-reader description of the toggle.
- inputClass: string | object | array - Classes for the inner <input>.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the wrapper element.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted on every input.
- update:visible [value: boolean] - Emitted when the toggle is pressed.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when the show/hide toggle has no name, that is when `showLabel` is set to a blank string.

Rules:
- Use PasswordInput, never `<Input type="password">`, so users can reveal what they typed.
- Set `autocomplete="new-password"` on registration/change forms.
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.
- Localise by overriding `showLabel` and `revealWarning`, or once for the app with `passwordInput.show` and `passwordInput.revealWarning` in a ConfigProvider. `hideLabel` has no effect: the toggle name must not change with the state.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The icon is not focusable and does not cover the toggle.
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator on the input; forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours.
- Toggle is a real `<button type="button">`: Tab reaches it after the input, Enter or Space toggles it. It has a constant `aria-label` (`showLabel`), `aria-pressed` for the state, `aria-controls` pointing at the input and a described-by warning.
- Input turns off autocapitalize, autocorrect and spellcheck; `autocomplete` defaults to `current-password` (use `new-password` when creating one). Pasting is never blocked.
- Needs an accessible name: Field label or `aria-label`.
- The toggle is 24px (36px on touch pointers); the input reserves room for it with logical padding, so RTL works.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const password = ref('')
</script>

<PasswordInput v-model="password" aria-label="Password" />
```

Example: Sign-up field with validation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const password = ref('short')
const visible = ref(true)
</script>

<Field label="New password" hint="At least 12 characters." :error="password.length < 12 ? 'Too short' : undefined" required>
  <PasswordInput v-model="password" v-model:visible="visible" autocomplete="new-password" />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants, shapes and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <PasswordInput variant="outline" placeholder="Outline" aria-label="Outline password" />
  <PasswordInput variant="filled" placeholder="Filled" aria-label="Filled password" />
  <PasswordInput variant="underline" placeholder="Underline" aria-label="Underline password" />
  <PasswordInput variant="ghost" placeholder="Ghost" aria-label="Ghost password" />
  <PasswordInput shape="pill" placeholder="Pill" aria-label="Pill password" />
  <PasswordInput shape="square" placeholder="Square" aria-label="Square password" />
  <PasswordInput size="xs" placeholder="Extra small" aria-label="Extra small password" />
  <PasswordInput size="lg" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large password" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <PasswordInput status="success" model-value="sample-password" aria-label="Strong password" />
  <PasswordInput status="warning" model-value="sample" aria-label="Weak password" />
  <PasswordInput status="error" model-value="sample" aria-label="Rejected password" />
</div>
```

# PinInput
group: forms / Text fields
Segmented one-character-per-cell input for verification codes and PINs.

Use `PinInput` for OTP / verification codes and short PINs. **`v-model` is a single string** (`"123"` while typing a 6-digit code), unlike reka-ui which uses an array; the component converts internally. `complete` fires with the full joined string once every cell is filled. Submit there. Focus advances automatically, Backspace/Delete/arrow keys work per cell and pasting a whole code fills all cells. Gaps are preserved visually but collapse in the string (`"1_3"` becomes `"13"`), so rely on `complete` for validity. Use `Input` for variable-length codes.

import { PinInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - The code as one string. Characters beyond `length` are dropped; in `number` mode non-digits are dropped.
- length: number = 6 - Number of cells (minimum 1).
- type: 'text' | 'number' = 'text' - `number` restricts to digits and opens a numeric keypad.
- mask: boolean = false - Hide entered characters (password-style cells).
- otp: boolean = false - One-time-code mode: the first cell gets autocomplete="one-time-code" (SMS autofill) and cells must be filled in order.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables every cell.
- required: boolean = false - Marks the hidden form input as required.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets aria-invalid on every cell and destructive styling.
- placeholder: string - Placeholder for each empty cell, e.g. "○".
- name: string - Form field name; a hidden input carries the joined code.
- cellLabel: string - Accessible-name prefix of each cell ("Digit 1 of 6"). Defaults to "Digit" in number mode, "Character" otherwise.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Cell size: 32, 36, 40 or 48 px square (44px on coarse pointers below `lg`). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of every cell. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps only a bottom rule per cell (it thickens on focus), `ghost` shows the border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of every cell. `pill` makes each cell a circle. `underline` cells are always square-cornered. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status of the whole code. Colours every cell border and adds ONE icon after the last cell; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that the group's `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"` on every cell. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- cellClass: string | object | array - Extra classes for every cell, merged last (e.g. `size-14 text-2xl`).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root group; wins over internal classes. Other attributes go to the root.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Fires on every change with the joined string (may be shorter than `length`).
- complete [value: string] - Fires with the joined code when all cells are filled.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the group has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (the named cells do not name the group).
- Throws a ContractError when `cellLabel` is set to a blank string.

Rules:
- v-model is ONE string, not an array. Do not pass arrays.
- Submit on `@complete`, not on every update.
- Use `type="number"` for numeric codes and `otp` for SMS codes.
- Always provide `aria-label` or a Field label for the group.
- Look props apply per cell: `variant`, `shape`, `size`; `status` colours all cells and adds one icon. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.

Accessibility:
- The root has role="group". Name it with `aria-label`, or put it in a `Field` with a label: the Field label then names the group through `aria-labelledby` (the Field `label for` points at a hidden input, which cannot name a group).
- Each cell is a text input named "Digit n of N" (or "Character n of N", or your `cellLabel`), with `autocapitalize="none"`.
- `type="number"` sets `inputmode="numeric"` and `pattern="[0-9]*"` on every cell so touch devices show a numeric keypad.
- Keyboard: typing advances focus, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End move between cells, Backspace clears and steps back, Delete clears the cell. Pasting a code into any cell distributes it across the cells. With `otp`, focus cannot skip an empty cell.
- `otp` sets autocomplete="one-time-code" on the first cell, so mobile keyboards offer the SMS code there; the other cells use autocomplete="off".
- Inside `Field`, aria-describedby (hint and error) is set on the group and aria-invalid on every cell.
- `status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw one icon after the last cell, and success and warning add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the group references from `aria-describedby`. Error sets `aria-invalid` on every cell.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill per cell and the focus ring (a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` cells in system colours.
- Targets and reflow: cells are 40px by default (`size` sets 32 to 48px), 44px on coarse pointers below `lg`, use 16px text or larger (no iOS zoom on focus) and shrink with `min-w-0` when the row is wider than the screen, so the code never overflows at 320px.

Example: Verification code
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const code = ref('')
const verified = ref('')
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <PinInput v-model="code" type="number" otp aria-label="Verification code" @complete="verified = $event" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">Entered: {{ code || 'nothing yet' }}. Completed: {{ verified || 'not yet' }}.</p>
</div>
```

Example: In a Field with an error
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const pin = ref('1234')
</script>

<Field label="Enter your PIN" error="Incorrect PIN, try again">
  <PinInput v-model="pin" :length="4" type="number" mask />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3">
  <PinInput :length="4" model-value="1234" aria-label="Outline cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" model-value="1234" variant="filled" aria-label="Filled cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" model-value="1234" variant="underline" aria-label="Underline cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" model-value="1234" variant="ghost" aria-label="Ghost cells" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3">
  <PinInput :length="4" size="xs" aria-label="Extra small cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" size="sm" aria-label="Small cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" aria-label="Medium cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" size="lg" aria-label="Large cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" shape="pill" aria-label="Circular cells" />
  <PinInput :length="4" shape="square" aria-label="Square cells" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <Field label="Backup code" hint="Sample message: code accepted."><PinInput :length="4" model-value="1234" status="success" /></Field>
  <Field label="Recovery code" hint="Sample message: this code expires soon."><PinInput :length="4" model-value="5678" status="warning" /></Field>
  <Field label="Access code" error="Sample message: the code does not match."><PinInput :length="4" model-value="0000" status="error" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Disabled
```vue
<PinInput :length="4" model-value="ABCD" disabled aria-label="Locked code" />
```

# PromptInput
group: forms / Text fields
Auto-growing message box for chat style interfaces: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, a Stop button replaces Send while a reply is running.

Use `PromptInput` at the bottom of a conversation or a command panel where one block of text is sent at a time. It grows with its text up to `maxRows`, then scrolls. `submitOn="enter"` (default) sends on Enter and inserts a line break on Shift+Enter; `submitOn="mod-enter"` sends on Ctrl or Cmd with Enter and keeps Enter for line breaks, which suits long prompts. An Enter that confirms an IME candidate never sends. Text that is empty or only whitespace never sends; the `submit` event carries the trimmed text and the field clears afterwards unless `clearOnSubmit` is off. While `loading` the Send button becomes a Stop button (emits `stop`) and sending is blocked, but the field stays editable so the next prompt can be drafted. `maxLength` shows a `count / limit` counter in code points; typing past the limit is allowed so pasted text is not cut, but the over-limit state is shown in text and an icon, `aria-invalid` is set and sending is blocked. The component renders no `<form>` and no messages: the app owns the conversation. Use `Textarea` for ordinary form fields and `Input` for one-line text. `class` goes on the root; every other attribute reaches the `<textarea>`.

import { PromptInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - v-model text. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- placeholder: string - Hint text while the field is empty. It is not the accessible name.
- submitOn: 'enter' | 'mod-enter' = 'enter' - Key that sends. `enter`: Enter sends, Shift+Enter (or Alt+Enter) adds a line. `mod-enter`: Ctrl or Cmd with Enter sends, Enter adds a line. Never sends while an IME is composing.
- loading: boolean = false - A reply is in progress. Shows the Stop button instead of Send, sets `aria-busy` and `data-loading` on the root, and blocks sending. The field stays editable.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the field and both buttons. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- readonly: boolean = false - Blocks editing and sending. The Stop button keeps working while `loading`.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid="true"` and destructive styling. Also set by a Field with an error, and by being over `maxLength`.
- variant: 'default' | 'filled' | 'minimal' = 'default' - Surface of the box. `default` is bordered, `filled` uses a muted fill, `minimal` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, text size (14px, 14px, 16px from `md`; 16px below it) and button size (32px, 36px, 44px; 44px on touch). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- rows: number = 1 - Rows shown while the text is short.
- maxRows: number = 8 - Rows the field grows to before the text scrolls inside it.
- maxLength: number - Character limit in code points (an emoji counts as one). Adds the counter and the limit states. It is not the native `maxlength`, so typing past it is allowed.
- clearOnSubmit: boolean = true - Empties the field after a successful submit and emits `update:modelValue` with `""`. Turn off to keep the text until the app decides.
- submitLabel: string = 'Send' - Accessible name of the Send button. Set it when the app is not in English.
- stopLabel: string = 'Stop' - Accessible name of the Stop button.
- limitNearLabel: string = 'Close to the character limit' - Announced politely once when the text reaches 90% of `maxLength`.
- limitOverLabel: string = 'Over the character limit' - Shown beside the counter and announced politely once when the text is over `maxLength`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the root (the prompt box); wins over internal classes. Other attributes go to the `<textarea>`.

Slots:
- header - Above the text, for attachment chips or a quoted message.
- attach - Start of the toolbar under the text: the attach button, mode toggles. Give every icon-only button a label.
- actions - End of the toolbar, before Send or Stop: a voice button, a model picker.
- footer - Below the toolbar, in small muted text: a keyboard hint or a notice.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted on every input event, and with `""` after a submit when `clearOnSubmit` is on.
- submit [value: string] - The trimmed text. Not emitted when the text is empty or whitespace, over `maxLength`, `loading`, `disabled` or `readonly`.
- stop - The Stop button was pressed while `loading`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the textarea has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder does not count).

Rules:
- Always set `aria-label` (or use Field); a placeholder is not a name.
- Listen to `@submit` (trimmed text, never empty) and `@stop`; the component renders no messages and no form.
- Set `loading` while a reply streams so Send turns into Stop; wire `@stop` to cancel the request.
- Use `max-length` for a limit: it allows typing past it and blocks sending. It is not the native `maxlength`.
- Put the attach button in the `attach` slot and give icon-only buttons a label. Do not wrap the component in a form just to catch Enter.
- Look props are `variant` and `size`; width goes in `class`, other attributes (`name`, `autofocus`, `autocomplete`) reach the textarea.

Accessibility:
- The `<textarea>` is the only tab stop for typing and carries the accessible name; buttons are native `<button>` elements named "Send" and "Stop" (`submitLabel`, `stopLabel`). Name the field with `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a `Field` label; a placeholder is not a name.
- Keyboard: Enter sends (Shift+Enter inserts a line) or, with `submitOn="mod-enter"`, Ctrl or Cmd with Enter sends and Enter inserts a line. An Enter that confirms an IME candidate (`isComposing`, keyCode 229) is ignored, so Japanese, Chinese and Korean input is not cut off. Tab moves from the field to the toolbar buttons.
- With `maxLength` the counter is read once when the field gets focus (`aria-describedby`). A separate polite `role="status"` region stays empty until the text reaches 90% of the limit or goes over it, then says one fixed sentence, so a screen reader does not read the count on every key.
- The over-limit state is never colour alone: the counter gains an icon and the words in `limitOverLabel`, the field gets `aria-invalid="true"` and the Send button is disabled. The Stop button is a named button, and the root carries `aria-busy` while `loading`.
- The focus ring surrounds the whole box while the field has keyboard focus; forced-colors mode draws an outline. Targets: 32, 36 and 44px buttons by `size`, 44px on touch devices, never below 24px in the dense style packs. Text is 16px below `md`. The toolbar wraps at 320px and layout uses logical properties (RTL safe).
- Auto-grow reads the layout and does nothing when there is none (hidden container, tests). It follows width changes through a `ResizeObserver`, so it re-measures when the box is narrowed.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('')
const sent = ref('')
function onSubmit(v) { sent.value = v }
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-xl gap-2">
  <PromptInput v-model="text" aria-label="Message" placeholder="Write a message" @submit="onSubmit" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Last sent: {{ sent || 'nothing yet' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Streaming with a Stop button
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('Summarise the sample notes')
const busy = ref(false)
function start() { busy.value = true }
function stop() { busy.value = false }
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-xl gap-2">
  <PromptInput v-model="text" aria-label="Message" :loading="busy" @submit="start" @stop="stop" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ busy ? 'Reply running. Press Stop to end it.' : 'Idle.' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Character limit
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('This sample text is already over the limit of twenty characters.')
</script>

<PromptInput v-model="text" class="max-w-xl" aria-label="Note" :max-length="20" />
```

Example: Send with Ctrl or Cmd and Enter
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('')
</script>

<PromptInput v-model="text" class="max-w-xl" aria-label="Long prompt" submit-on="mod-enter" :rows="3" placeholder="Press Enter for a new line, Ctrl or Cmd with Enter to send">
  <template #footer>Ctrl or Cmd with Enter sends.</template>
</PromptInput>
```

Example: Attach button, actions and footer
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('')
</script>

<PromptInput v-model="text" class="max-w-xl" aria-label="Message">
  <template #header><Badge variant="outline">notes.txt</Badge></template>
  <template #attach><IconButton label="Attach a file" variant="outline" shape="circle" :icon="faPlus" /></template>
  <template #actions><Badge variant="secondary">Draft - fast</Badge></template>
  <template #footer>Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.</template>
</PromptInput>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xl gap-3">
  <PromptInput variant="default" aria-label="Default" placeholder="Default" />
  <PromptInput variant="filled" aria-label="Filled" placeholder="Filled" />
  <PromptInput variant="minimal" aria-label="Minimal" placeholder="Minimal" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xl gap-3">
  <PromptInput size="sm" aria-label="Small" placeholder="Small" />
  <PromptInput size="md" aria-label="Medium" placeholder="Medium" />
  <PromptInput size="lg" aria-label="Large" placeholder="Large" />
</div>
```

Example: Auto-grow and max rows
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('First line\nSecond line\nThird line\nFourth line\nFifth line')
</script>

<PromptInput v-model="text" class="max-w-xl" aria-label="Draft" :rows="2" :max-rows="4" />
```

Example: Disabled and read-only
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-xl gap-3">
  <PromptInput disabled aria-label="Disabled" model-value="Not available right now" />
  <PromptInput readonly loading aria-label="Read-only while running" model-value="Draft is locked" />
</div>
```

Example: In a Field
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('')
</script>

<Field class="max-w-xl" label="Message" hint="Sample hint: keep it short.">
  <PromptInput v-model="text" :max-length="200" />
</Field>
```
