# SearchInput
group: forms / Text fields
Text field with a search icon, a clear button, Esc-to-clear and an optional debounced `search` event.

Use `SearchInput` for filtering lists, tables and command-style lookups. `update:modelValue` fires on every keystroke; `search` fires with the current value after `debounce` ms (immediately when `0`), or at once on Enter. Esc and the clear button empty the field, emit `clear` and `search("")`. When `disabled` or `readonly` the clear button is hidden and Esc is ignored. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` style the input; the search icon and clear button stay inside it, and `status` adds an icon left of the clear button (plus screen reader text for `success` and `warning`). `searchInputVariants` gives a plain `<input type="search">` the same look. Not for password or numeric entry.

import { SearchInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - Current text (v-model). Uncontrolled when omitted.
- debounce: number = 0 - Milliseconds to wait after typing before emitting `search`. Negative/NaN behave as 0.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the input and hides the clear button.
- readonly: boolean = false - Prevents editing and clearing; Enter still emits `search`.
- required: boolean = false - Native required.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets `aria-invalid` and destructive styling. Also inherited from a surrounding Field.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`, the icon sits flush at the start), border on hover and fill on focus (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Control height: 28, 32, 36 and 44px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is fully rounded and moves the icon in; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon left of the clear button. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- clearLabel: string = 'Clear search' - Accessible name of the clear button.
- landmark: boolean = false - Give the wrapper `role="search"`. Use once per page region.
- landmarkLabel: string = 'Search' - Accessible name of the search landmark (with `landmark`). Make it unique when a page has several.
- inputClass: string | object | array - Classes for the inner <input>.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the wrapper element (use for width/layout).

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Every input change, immediately.
- search [value: string] - Debounced value after typing, immediately on Enter, and `""` after a clear.
- clear - Emitted when the field is cleared by button or Esc.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder does not count).
- Throws a ContractError when `clearLabel` is blank, or `landmarkLabel` is blank while `landmark` is set.

Rules:
- Use `@search` (not `@update:modelValue`) for network/expensive filtering; set `debounce` for type-ahead.
- Attributes such as `placeholder`, `name`, `aria-label` go to the inner input; `class` styles the wrapper.
- Always provide an accessible name (Field label or aria-label).
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`). The icon is not focusable and does not cover the clear button.
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator on the input; forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours.
- Native `type="search"` input with `enterkeyhint="search"`; autocorrect, autocapitalize and spellcheck are off. The browser clear button is hidden in favour of the labelled one.
- Keyboard: Enter emits `search` at once; Esc clears and does not bubble, so enclosing dialogs stay open; Tab reaches the clear button after the input, and focus returns to the input after clearing.
- The clear button is `type="button"`, named by `clearLabel`, 24px (36px on touch pointers), and only exists while there is text and the field is editable.
- Give the input an accessible name: wrap in Field with a label, or pass `aria-label`.
- `landmark` adds `role="search"` with `aria-label` (`landmarkLabel`) for a real site or section search; use it once per region.
- Icon and button use logical offsets (`start`, `end`), so RTL works. 16px text below `md` avoids iOS focus zoom.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const query = ref('')
</script>

<SearchInput v-model="query" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Query: {{ query || '(empty)' }}</p>
```

Example: Debounced search inside a Field
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const query = ref('')
const searched = ref('')
</script>

<Field label="Find a customer" hint="Search runs 300 ms after you stop typing, or on Enter.">
  <SearchInput v-model="query" :debounce="300" placeholder="Name or email" @search="searched = $event" @clear="searched = ''" />
</Field>
<p class="mt-2 text-sm">Last search: <Badge variant="secondary">{{ searched || 'none' }}</Badge></p>
```

Example: Variants, shapes and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <SearchInput variant="outline" placeholder="Outline" aria-label="Outline search" />
  <SearchInput variant="filled" placeholder="Filled" aria-label="Filled search" />
  <SearchInput variant="underline" placeholder="Underline" aria-label="Underline search" />
  <SearchInput variant="ghost" placeholder="Ghost" aria-label="Ghost search" />
  <SearchInput shape="pill" placeholder="Pill" aria-label="Pill search" />
  <SearchInput shape="square" placeholder="Square" aria-label="Square search" />
  <SearchInput size="xs" placeholder="Extra small" aria-label="Extra small search" />
  <SearchInput size="lg" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large search" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-3">
  <SearchInput status="success" model-value="sample query" aria-label="Search with results" />
  <SearchInput status="warning" model-value="sample query" aria-label="Search with a warning" />
  <SearchInput status="error" model-value="sample query" aria-label="Search with an error" />
</div>
```

# TagsInput
group: forms / Text fields
Free-form list of short strings entered as removable chips.

Type text and press Enter or the delimiter (comma by default) to turn it into a tag; remove tags with their delete button, or Backspace/Delete once the caret is at the start. Tags are trimmed, empty tags are ignored, duplicates (case-sensitive) are rejected and `max` limits the count. Additions, removals and rejections are spoken through a polite live region, and rejections also surface through the `duplicate` and `reject` events so you can show a visible message. `v-model` is a `string[]`. Use `Combobox` when tags must come from a fixed list, `Input` for a single value.

import { TagsInput } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string[] | null - Controlled tags.
- defaultValue: string[] = [] - Initial tags when uncontrolled.
- placeholder: string - Shown only while there are no tags.
- max: number - Maximum number of tags; extra additions are rejected with reason `max`. Unlimited when omitted or 0.
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables typing and removal.
- required: boolean = false - Marks the hidden form input as required.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets aria-invalid on the text input and destructive styling on the field.
- delimiter: string | RegExp = ',' - Typing this character commits the text as a tag. Enter always commits. Also splits pasted text with `addOnPaste`.
- addOnBlur: boolean = false - Add the pending text when the input loses focus.
- addOnPaste: boolean = false - Split pasted text on the delimiter and add every part.
- name: string - Form field name; inside a native form hidden inputs `name[0]`, `name[1]`... are rendered.
- ariaLabel: string - Accessible name of the text input when there is no Field label.
- removeLabel: string = 'Remove' - Prefix of each remove button name, e.g. "Remove react".
- addedLabel: string = 'Added' - Spoken after a tag is added through the polite live region (`Added react`).
- removedLabel: string = 'Removed' - Spoken after a tag is removed (`Removed react`).
- duplicateLabel: string = 'Already added' - Spoken when the text matches an existing tag (`Already added: react`).
- maxLabel: string = 'Tag limit reached' - Spoken when `max` blocks an addition (`Tag limit reached: react`).
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Minimum height of the field (28 / 32 / 36 / 44 px) and text size of the typing input. Tags wrap and grow the field. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface. `outline` is the bordered default, `filled` uses a muted fill, `underline` keeps a bottom rule that thickens while focus is inside, `ghost` shows its border on hover and focus. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is a large radius box (not a full pill) so wrapped tags are never clipped. `underline` is always square-cornered. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon in the first row; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that the text input's `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes. Other attributes (id, aria-*, data-*) go to the text input.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string[]] - Fires when tags are added or removed.
- add [tag: string] - A tag was added.
- remove [tag: string] - A tag was removed.
- duplicate [tag: string] - The (trimmed) text already exists and was not added.
- reject [payload: { value: string; reason: 'duplicate' | 'max' }] - Any rejected addition. Also fires after `duplicate`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the text input has no accessible name: no `Field` label, `for` label, `ariaLabel` or `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- v-model is string[]; tags are trimmed and case-sensitive unique.
- Surface `reject` (reason duplicate | max) with a visible Field error. A screen reader already hears the rejection through the built-in status region.
- Attributes such as id/aria-label land on the inner text input, class lands on the root.
- Look props are `variant`, `shape`, `status` and `size`. `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
- Use Combobox, not TagsInput, when values must come from a fixed set.

Accessibility:
- The text input keeps native input semantics; tags are listed before it and each remove button is named "Remove <tag>" (the button labels itself, because the library part otherwise names it with the bare tag text). Remove buttons are 24px square (36px on coarse pointers).
- Additions, removals, duplicates and `max` rejections are announced through a polite `role="status"` region. After a tag is removed with its button, focus moves back to the text input.
- Backspace (or ArrowLeft) at the start of an empty input highlights the last tag (aria-current); Backspace/Delete again removes it.
- Inside `Field` the text input gets the field id (so the Field label names it), aria-describedby and aria-invalid; pass `aria-label` otherwise.
- The field wraps tags onto new lines, is at least 44px high on coarse pointers, uses 16px text on small screens and shows a forced-colors outline while focused. The selected chip has a ring and, in forced-colors mode, an outline.
- `status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon, and success and warning add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") that the text input references from `aria-describedby`. Error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus indicator on the container (a ring, or a thicker bottom border for `underline`); forced-colors mode draws the border of `underline` and `ghost` in system colours.
- Enter never submits the surrounding form while text is pending.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const skills = ref(['vue', 'typescript'])
</script>

<div class="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
  <TagsInput v-model="skills" placeholder="Add a skill" aria-label="Skills" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ skills.length }} tags</p>
</div>
```

Example: Limit with feedback
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const tags = ref(['one', 'two'])
const error = ref('')
function onReject({ value, reason }) {
  error.value = reason === 'max' ? 'At most 3 tags.' : `"${value}" is already added.`
}
</script>

<Field label="Keywords" hint="Press Enter or comma to add" :error="error" class="w-80">
  <TagsInput v-model="tags" :max="3" @reject="onReject" @add="error = ''" />
</Field>
```

Example: Variants and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid w-80 max-w-full gap-2">
  <TagsInput :default-value="['outline']" aria-label="Outline" />
  <TagsInput variant="filled" :default-value="['filled']" aria-label="Filled" />
  <TagsInput variant="underline" :default-value="['underline']" aria-label="Underline" />
  <TagsInput variant="ghost" :default-value="['ghost']" aria-label="Ghost" />
  <TagsInput shape="pill" :default-value="['pill']" aria-label="Pill" />
  <TagsInput shape="square" :default-value="['square']" aria-label="Square" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid w-80 max-w-full gap-2">
  <TagsInput size="xs" :default-value="['xs']" aria-label="Extra small" />
  <TagsInput size="sm" :default-value="['sm']" aria-label="Small" />
  <TagsInput :default-value="['md']" aria-label="Medium" />
  <TagsInput size="lg" :default-value="['lg']" aria-label="Large" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid w-80 max-w-full gap-3">
  <Field label="Approved keywords" hint="Sample message: every keyword is accepted."><TagsInput status="success" :default-value="['one']" /></Field>
  <Field label="Draft keywords" hint="Sample message: two keywords are very similar."><TagsInput status="warning" :default-value="['two', 'too']" /></Field>
  <Field label="Required keywords" error="Sample message: add at least one keyword."><TagsInput status="error" placeholder="Add a keyword" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Disabled
```vue
<TagsInput class="w-80" :model-value="['locked', 'read-only']" disabled aria-label="Locked tags" />
```

# Textarea
group: forms / Text fields
Multi-line text field with v-model, variants, sizes, shapes, status, optional autosize and character counter.

Use for free-form text longer than one line. `autosize` grows the field with its content (optionally capped by `maxRows`). `maxlength` + `showCount` renders a `n / max` counter (counts UTF-16 code units, the unit `maxlength` enforces, so an emoji is 2); the counter is linked by `aria-describedby` and a polite status announces only when the limit is reached. Inside a `Field` it receives id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid automatically. `variant`, `size`, `shape` and `status` change the look; a `pill` shape is `rounded-xl` because a full pill would clip several lines, and `status` adds an icon at the top end (plus screen reader text for `success` and `warning`). `textareaVariants` gives a plain `<textarea>` the same look. Attributes (`placeholder`, `name`, `aria-*`) go to the `<textarea>`; `class` is merged onto it.

import { Textarea } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: string | null - v-model value. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'underline' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface: muted fill (`filled`), bottom border only (`underline`), border on hover and fill on focus (`ghost`). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Minimum height (48, 56, 64, 80px), text size and padding. Text stays 16px below `md`. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners. `pill` is `rounded-xl`; `square` has no radius; `underline` has no corners and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Status colour with an icon. `success` and `warning` add visually hidden text linked through `aria-describedby`; `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- statusLabel: string = 'Valid' or 'Warning' - Screen reader text of the `success` and `warning` status. Set it when the app is not in English.
- rows: number = 3 - Visible rows when not autosizing.
- autosize: boolean = false - Grow with content; disables manual resizing.
- maxRows: number - Cap for autosize; further content scrolls.
- maxlength: number - Native maxlength; drives the counter.
- showCount: boolean = false - Show `count / maxlength` (needs maxlength).
- limitLabel: string = 'Character limit reached' - Message announced once when the limit is reached (localise here, or with `textarea.limit` in a ConfigProvider; the counter text is `textarea.count`, `{count} / {max}`).
- disabled: boolean = false - Disables the field (also from Field).
- readonly: boolean = false - Prevents editing.
- required: boolean = false - Native required (also from Field).
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets aria-invalid and destructive styling (also from Field error).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the <textarea>.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Emitted on every input event.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the textarea has no accessible name: no `Field` label, wrapping or `for` label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (a placeholder does not count).

Rules:
- Use `Textarea` for multi-line only; use `Input` otherwise.
- Set `maxlength` together with `show-count`.
- Pass `class` for width/height; it lands on the textarea.
- Use `status` for validation feedback (it adds the icon) and still show the message through `Field error` or `hint`.
- Use `shape="pill"` sparingly on a textarea: it is `rounded-xl`, not a full pill.

Accessibility:
- Status is never colour alone: an icon appears for `success`, `warning` and `error`; `success` and `warning` add screen reader text referenced by `aria-describedby`, and `error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` (pair it with a visible message in `Field`).
- `underline` and `ghost` keep a visible focus indicator (a thicker bottom border, or a border and ring); forced-colors mode draws borders in system colours.
- Native `<textarea>`; Tab focuses it. It needs a label (Field) or `aria-label`.
- The counter is not a live region (that would announce every keystroke). It is part of `aria-describedby` and is read when the field gets focus; a separate `role="status"` announces only when the limit is reached.
- Inside a Field: described by hint and error, `aria-invalid` on error. A consumer `id` or `aria-describedby` is kept and merged.
- Resizable vertically (`resize-y`) unless `autosize`. 16px text below `md` prevents iOS focus zoom; the counter uses `tabular-nums`.

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const text = ref('')
</script>

<Textarea v-model="text" class="max-w-md" placeholder="Write something" aria-label="Message" />
```

Example: Autosize with counter
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const note = ref('Grows as you type.')
</script>

<Textarea v-model="note" class="max-w-md" autosize :max-rows="6" :maxlength="140" show-count aria-label="Note" />
```

Example: Variants and shapes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-3">
  <Textarea variant="outline" placeholder="Outline" aria-label="Outline" />
  <Textarea variant="filled" placeholder="Filled" aria-label="Filled" />
  <Textarea variant="underline" placeholder="Underline" aria-label="Underline" />
  <Textarea variant="ghost" placeholder="Ghost" aria-label="Ghost" />
  <Textarea shape="pill" placeholder="Pill" aria-label="Pill" />
  <Textarea shape="square" placeholder="Square" aria-label="Square" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-3">
  <Textarea size="xs" :rows="1" placeholder="Extra small" aria-label="Extra small" />
  <Textarea size="sm" :rows="1" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small" />
  <Textarea size="md" :rows="1" placeholder="Medium" aria-label="Medium" />
  <Textarea size="lg" :rows="1" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-3">
  <Textarea status="success" model-value="Looks good." aria-label="Success" />
  <Textarea status="warning" model-value="This is close to the limit." aria-label="Warning" />
  <Textarea status="error" model-value="Too short." aria-label="Error" />
</div>
```

# FileDropzone
group: forms / Upload
Drag-and-drop or click-to-browse file picker with type, size and count validation. Selection only, no upload.

Collects `File` objects; **it never uploads anything**. Send the `v-model` files to your own endpoint. Validation runs on drop and on pick: `accept` (native syntax: `image/*`, `.pdf`, `text/csv`), `maxSize` (bytes), `maxFiles` (with `multiple`). Accepted files go to `v-model` (always `File[]`); rejected ones are reported through `reject` (`[{ file, reason: "type" | "size" | "count" }]`) and a human-readable `error` message, which is also shown inline. In single mode a new file replaces the old one. Duplicates (same name, size and modified time) are ignored. The whole area is a native `<button>` (Enter and Space open the picker); customise its content with the default slot, which receives `{ dragging }`. `variant`, `size` and `status` change the look of the area. There is no `shape`: the area is a tall panel and a pill or square corner adds nothing to it. There is no `underline`: a bottom rule alone does not read as a place to drop files, so `solid` and `filled` cover the quieter looks.

import { FileDropzone } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: File[] | null - Accepted files. Always an array, also without `multiple`.
- accept: string - Comma separated MIME types, wildcards or extensions, e.g. `image/*,.pdf`. Case-insensitive. Everything is accepted when omitted.
- maxSize: number - Maximum size per file in bytes. Larger files are rejected with reason `size`.
- maxFiles: number - Maximum total files (requires `multiple`; single mode always allows one). Extra files are rejected with reason `count`.
- multiple: boolean = false - Allow several files; new files are appended instead of replacing.
- disabled: boolean = false - Blocks click, keyboard, drag/drop and file removal.
- required: boolean = false - Native required on the hidden input.
- invalid: boolean = false - Sets aria-invalid and destructive styling. Also applied automatically while a rejection message is shown.
- name: string - Form field name of the hidden file input.
- showFiles: boolean = true - Render the list of accepted files with remove buttons.
- ariaLabel: string - Extra name text, rendered visually hidden inside the button so the visible prompt always stays part of the accessible name. A surrounding Field label is added to the name as well.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height of the drop area: 64, 96, 128 or 192 px minimum. The default icon scales with it. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'outline' | 'solid' | 'filled' | 'ghost' = 'outline' - Surface of the drop area. `outline` is the dashed border, `solid` draws the border as a continuous line, `filled` replaces it with a muted fill, `ghost` shows the border on hover, focus and while dragging. Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- status: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' = 'default' - Validation status. Colours the border and adds an icon in the top corner; `success` and `warning` also add hidden text that `aria-describedby` points at. `error` also sets `aria-invalid="true"`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root wrapper (dropzone + list); wins over internal classes. Other attributes go to the dropzone area.

Slots:
- default ({ dragging: boolean }) - Content of the dropzone area. Replaces the default icon, prompt and constraints hint.

Events:
- update:modelValue [files: File[]] - Fires when accepted files are added or one is removed.
- reject [rejections: { file: File; reason: 'type' | 'size' | 'count' }[]] - Fires when any file was not accepted.
- error [message: string] - Human-readable summary of the rejection (also shown inline with role="alert").

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the drop area has no accessible name: custom slot content without text, and no `ariaLabel`, `aria-label` or `Field` label.

Rules:
- v-model is File[] (even in single mode). The component never uploads: send files yourself.
- Handle `reject`/`error` or rely on the inline message; set `max-size` in BYTES.
- Look props are `variant`, `size` and `status`; there is no `shape` or `underline` (see the description). `status="error"` already sets aria-invalid; still show a visible error message in a Field.
- `max-files` only applies together with `multiple`.
- Custom slot content must be phrasing content (spans, icons) and must not contain interactive elements: the area is itself a button.
- Do not pass `aria-label` through attrs: it would replace the visible prompt in the accessible name. Use the `ariaLabel` prop.

Accessibility:
- The drop area is a native `<button type="button">`: Tab focuses it, Enter and Space open the file picker, and disabled removes it from the tab order. Clicking or pressing the button is the keyboard and touch alternative to dragging files in.
- The accessible name is the visible prompt text. `ariaLabel` adds hidden text inside the button instead of replacing the name (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name). Inside a `Field`, the Field label and the prompt are combined with `aria-labelledby`.
- A hidden native file input does the real work, stays out of the tab order and is `aria-hidden`.
- Rejections render in a `role="alert"` paragraph, linked with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` on the button. Accepted and removed files are announced politely through a visually hidden `role="status"` region ("report.pdf added").
- Each accepted file has a remove button named "Remove <file name>"; it is 24px square and grows to 44px on coarse pointers.
- Dragging adds `data-dragging` to the root and the area and changes the text to "Drop to upload". In forced-colors mode the dragging state adds an outline, so it does not depend on colour alone.
- `status` is never colour alone: success, warning and error draw an icon in the top corner, and success and warning add visually hidden text ("Valid", "Warning") outside the button that the button references from `aria-describedby` (so it does not change the accessible name). Error sets `aria-invalid` and relies on the Field error message.
- Every `variant` keeps a visible edge or fill and the focus ring; `filled` and `ghost` draw a system-colour border in forced-colors mode, so the area never disappears.
- Responsive: the area and file names shrink with `min-w-0` and truncate, so nothing overflows at 320px.

Example: Images up to 2 MB
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const files = ref([])
</script>

<div class="w-96 max-w-full">
  <FileDropzone v-model="files" accept="image/*" :max-size="2 * 1024 * 1024" aria-label="Upload an image" />
  <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">{{ files.length }} file(s) selected</p>
</div>
```

Example: Multiple with limits and custom content
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const docs = ref([])
const message = ref('')
</script>

<Field label="Attachments" hint="PDF only, up to 3 files" class="w-96 max-w-full">
  <FileDropzone v-model="docs" multiple accept=".pdf" :max-files="3" @error="message = $event">
    <template #default="{ dragging }">
      <Icon :icon="faFilePdf" size="xl" />
      <span>{{ dragging ? 'Release to add' : 'Drop PDFs or click to browse' }}</span>
    </template>
  </FileDropzone>
  <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">{{ docs.length }} file(s) kept. Last rejection: {{ message || 'none' }}</p>
</Field>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid w-96 max-w-full gap-3">
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Outline dropzone" size="sm" />
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Solid dropzone" size="sm" variant="solid" />
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Filled dropzone" size="sm" variant="filled" />
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Ghost dropzone" size="sm" variant="ghost" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid w-96 max-w-full gap-3">
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Extra small dropzone" size="xs" />
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Small dropzone" size="sm" />
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Medium dropzone" />
  <FileDropzone aria-label="Large dropzone" size="lg" />
</div>
```

Example: Status
```vue
<div class="grid w-96 max-w-full gap-4">
  <Field label="Signed copy" hint="Sample message: the file was verified."><FileDropzone status="success" size="sm" /></Field>
  <Field label="Photo" hint="Sample message: the image is lower resolution than advised."><FileDropzone status="warning" size="sm" /></Field>
  <Field label="Contract" error="Sample message: attach the contract."><FileDropzone status="error" size="sm" /></Field>
</div>
```

Example: Disabled
```vue
<FileDropzone class="w-96 max-w-full" disabled aria-label="Uploads disabled" />
```

# ConfirmDialog
group: feedback / Confirmation
Confirm / cancel dialog with destructive styling and async-aware confirm, plus a promise-based useConfirm() host.

Two ways to use it. (1) Declarative: render `<ConfirmDialog v-model:open="open" title=... @confirm="handler" />`. The handler may be async: the dialog stays open with a spinner while it runs, closes on success, and shows the error (and emits `error`) if it throws. (2) Imperative: mount `<ConfirmHost />` once (requires Pinia) and call `const { confirm } = useConfirm(); if (await confirm({ title, destructive: true })) ...`. Concurrent confirm() calls queue and resolve one at a time. Escape, outside click and the cancel button resolve `false`; while busy the dialog cannot be dismissed. `@confirm` is declared as an `onConfirm` handler prop so its returned promise can be awaited.

import { ConfirmDialog, ConfirmHost } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- open: boolean = false - v-model:open. Works controlled or uncontrolled.
- title*: string - Question naming the action. A blank value throws a ContractError (in production it shows "Are you sure?").
- description: string - Consequence text. A screen-reader-only description is used when omitted.
- confirmLabel: string = 'Confirm' - Confirm button text. Name the action ("Delete project").
- cancelLabel: string = 'Cancel' - Cancel button text.
- destructive: boolean = false - Destructive confirm button.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'danger' | 'warning' | 'success' | 'info' = 'neutral' - Tone of the prompt. Non-neutral tones tint the panel border and show a status icon above the title; `danger` also makes the confirm button destructive. Unknown values fall back to `neutral`. Adds `data-tone` on the panel.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'sm' - Maximum panel width from the `sm` breakpoint (xs 20rem, sm 24rem, md 32rem, lg 42rem). Unknown values fall back to `sm`.
- variant: 'default' | 'centered' = 'default' - `centered` centres the icon, text and buttons, for short confirmations. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- loading: boolean = false - External busy state; blocks confirm, cancel and dismissal.
- onConfirm: () => unknown | Promise<unknown> - The `@confirm` handler. Awaited; rejection keeps the dialog open.
- class: string | object | array - Merged onto the dialog content.

Parts:
- ConfirmHost - Mount once near the app root; renders the queue of useConfirm() requests. Takes no props.

Slots:
- default - Extra content between the description and the buttons (e.g. a "type the name to confirm" input).

Events:
- update:open [value: boolean] - v-model:open. Set to false after success or cancel.
- cancel [] - Dismissed without confirming (Cancel button or Escape; a click outside does not dismiss it).
- error [error: unknown] - The confirm handler threw or rejected.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `ConfirmDialog` has a blank `title`, no `open` (use `v-model:open`) or no `@confirm` handler.
- Throws a ContractError when `useConfirm().confirm()` is called with a blank `title` or while no `ConfirmHost` is mounted (the promise would never settle).

Rules:
- Use destructive for irreversible actions and name the action in confirmLabel.
- Prefer useConfirm() + one <ConfirmHost /> for "are you sure?" checks in scripts.
- Return the promise from @confirm so the dialog can show progress and errors.
- Set `tone="danger"` for irreversible actions (it also styles the confirm button); use `warning`, `info` or `success` for other prompts. Keep `tone` and `title` in agreement.
- Do not nest ConfirmDialog inside another dialog.

Accessibility:
- Built on AlertDialog (reka-ui): role="alertdialog", focus is trapped, Escape cancels, focus returns to the trigger.
- Initial focus goes to Cancel, the safe action, also for non-destructive confirmations.
- Clicking outside does not dismiss it: an explicit choice is required.
- Title and description are wired with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. An sr-only description is added when none is given.
- While busy the confirm button exposes aria-busy, Cancel is disabled, and the dialog cannot be dismissed.
- Errors from the handler render in a role="alert" paragraph.
- The tone icon is decorative (aria-hidden) and the tint is a border only: the title, description and button label say what the tone says. Every size and tone keeps the Title, Description and Cancel parts.
- The panel is capped at the viewport width minus 2rem and scrolls inside itself when the content is taller than the viewport.

Example: Destructive confirmation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
function remove() { /* delete it */ }
</script>

<Button variant="destructive" @click="open = true">Delete project</Button>
<ConfirmDialog
  v-model:open="open"
  title="Delete this project?"
  description="This permanently removes the project and its data."
  confirm-label="Delete"
  destructive
  @confirm="remove"
/>
```

Example: Tone, size and centred layout
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
const tone = ref('warning')
function show(next) { tone.value = next; open.value = true }
function apply() { /* save it */ }
</script>

<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Button variant="outline" @click="show('danger')">Danger</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" @click="show('warning')">Warning</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" @click="show('info')">Info</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" @click="show('success')">Success</Button>
</div>
<ConfirmDialog
  v-model:open="open"
  :tone="tone"
  size="xs"
  variant="centered"
  title="Apply this change?"
  description="It takes effect for everyone in the workspace."
  confirm-label="Apply change"
  @confirm="apply"
/>
```

Example: Async confirm
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
const save = () => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1000))
</script>

<Button @click="open = true">Publish</Button>
<ConfirmDialog v-model:open="open" title="Publish changes?" description="Visitors will see them immediately." confirm-label="Publish" @confirm="save" />
```

Example: Promise-based with useConfirm()
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const { confirm } = useConfirm()
async function run() { if (await confirm({ title: 'Reset settings?', destructive: true })) result.value = 'reset' }
</script>

<Button variant="outline" @click="run">Reset settings</Button>
<span class="ml-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ result }}</span>
<ConfirmHost />
```

# PageLoadingBar
group: feedback / Loading
A thin bar fixed to the top of the viewport that shows a route change or page load, with a delay so fast navigations never flash.

Mount `PageLoadingBar` once in the app shell and drive `active` from your router. While `active` is true it shows an indeterminate sweep; when `active` turns false it fills to 100% and fades. `delay` (default 150ms) keeps navigations that finish quickly from flashing the bar, and `minDuration` (default 300ms) keeps a bar that did show from blinking away. Turning `active` back on during the finish or fade resumes the sweep without a flash.

The bar is `position: fixed` at `z-(--z-toast)` and ignores the pointer. It is idle and `aria-hidden` until it shows; then it is a `progressbar` named by `label` (default "Loading page") with no value while loading. Under prefers-reduced-motion the sweep becomes a static full-width bar while active and the fade is instant.

Use it for route and page level waits. For a bar inside a layout use `Progress`; for a region use `LoadingState`.

vue-router:

```ts
const loading = ref(false)
router.beforeEach(() => { loading.value = true })
router.afterEach(() => { loading.value = false })
router.onError(() => { loading.value = false })
```

```vue
<PageLoadingBar :active="loading" />
```

import { PageLoadingBar } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- active: boolean = false - True while a navigation or load is in flight.
- delay: number = 150 - Milliseconds before the bar shows. 0 shows at once. Negative or invalid values give 150.
- minDuration: number = 300 - Minimum milliseconds the bar stays once shown. Negative or invalid values give 300.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the bar. Unknown values fall back to primary.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' = 'sm' - Thickness: 2px, 4px, 6px. Unknown values fall back to sm.
- label: string = 'Loading page' - Accessible name of the progressbar while it is visible.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the fixed root; use it to move the bar or change its stacking.

Rules:
- Mount one PageLoadingBar in the app shell; drive `active` from router.beforeEach / afterEach / onError.
- Keep the default `delay`; do not set it to 0 outside demos.
- Do not use it for in-component loading; use Progress, Spinner or LoadingState.
- Announce route changes separately (focus or title); the bar is visual only.

Accessibility:
- Idle: `aria-hidden="true"` and invisible, so it adds nothing to the accessibility tree.
- Visible: `role="progressbar"` with `aria-label` (default "Loading page"); no `aria-valuenow` while loading (indeterminate), `aria-valuenow="100"` while it finishes.
- A progress bar is not announced on its own. For a route change also move focus or update the document title; this bar is a visual cue.
- prefers-reduced-motion: a static full-width bar while active, no sweep, no fade.
- The bar never takes pointer events and is not focusable.

Example: Toggle with a button
```vue
<div class="space-y-3">
  <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="loading = !loading">{{ loading ? 'Finish loading' : 'Start loading' }}</Button>
  <PageLoadingBar :active="loading" :delay="0" :min-duration="600" label="Loading sample page" />
</div>
```

Example: Tone and thickness
```vue
<div>
  <PageLoadingBar active :delay="0" size="xs" tone="info" label="Loading sample xs" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">The info-toned bar sits at the top of the viewport.</p>
</div>
```

# Alert
group: feedback / Messages
Inline, in-flow status message with optional icon, title, description and dismiss button.

Use `Alert` for a message that belongs to a section of the page (form-level errors, "saved" confirmations, notices above a table). Compose it with `AlertTitle` and `AlertDescription`. Tone (`variant`) and surface (`appearance`) are independent: `soft` (default, tinted) for most in-page messages, `solid` for high-emphasis notices that must not be missed, `outline` for low-key bordered notices on busy backgrounds, `minimal` for unobtrusive inline text with just an icon. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) scales padding and type. Use `Banner` for page-wide notices, `Toast` for transient confirmations, `InlineMessage` for one line under a field and `Callout` for documentation notes.

import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'destructive' = 'default' - Tone. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- appearance: 'soft' | 'solid' | 'outline' | 'minimal' = 'soft' - Surface treatment, independent of `variant`. Unknown values fall back to `soft`. Non-default values add a `data-appearance` attribute.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap and type scale. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add a `data-size` attribute.
- layout: 'default' | 'inline' = 'default' - Body layout. `default` stacks title, description and actions; `inline` puts title, description and the `actions` slot in one wrapping row with the actions pushed to the end. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.
- icon: IconDefinition - Optional FontAwesome icon. Nothing is rendered when omitted.
- dismissible: boolean = false - Shows a dismiss (X) button. Dismissing hides the alert, moves focus to the next focusable sibling (else the parent region) and emits `dismiss` once. To show it again, change its `:key`.
- dismissLabel: string = 'Dismiss' - Accessible label of the dismiss button.
- role: 'alert' | 'status' | 'note' - Overrides the computed role: `alert` for warning/destructive, `status` otherwise.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- AlertTitle - Bold heading line of the alert.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- AlertDescription - Muted body text of the alert.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.

Slots:
- default - Usually `AlertTitle` + `AlertDescription`, or plain text.
- actions - Buttons or links for the next step. Placed under the text, or at the end of the row with `layout="inline"`.

Events:
- dismiss [] - The dismiss button was used. Fires once; the alert then removes itself.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an `Alert` is empty (no title or text) or is `dismissible` with a blank `dismissLabel`.

Rules:
- A dismissed Alert stays gone until its `:key` changes; bind `:key` to the message id to show a new message.
- Always give an Alert a title or text; do not render empty alerts.
- Use variant="destructive" for errors and "warning" for recoverable problems.
- Use Alert for in-page messages only; use Toaster for transient feedback.
- Choose the tone with `variant` and the surface with `appearance`; default to `soft`, use `solid` only for one critical notice per view.
- Use `appearance="minimal"` or `size="sm"` for messages inside cards, tables and forms.
- Pass FontAwesome IconDefinition objects to `icon`, never inline SVG.

Accessibility:
- Warning and destructive use role="alert" (assertive). Other variants use role="status" (polite). Override with `role`.
- The dismiss button is a real <button> with an aria-label (`dismissLabel`). It is 28px square, 40px on coarse pointers.
- Solid appearance pairs each tone with its `*-foreground` token for contrast. Icon and dismiss button follow the text colour.
- The icon is decorative (aria-hidden). Colour is never the only signal: always include text.
- Every appearance keeps a border, so the alert stays visible in forced-colors mode. Text wraps and the body has `min-w-0`, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px.

Example: Variants
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faCircleCheck, faCircleInfo, faTriangleExclamation } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Alert>
    <AlertTitle>Changes are not saved</AlertTitle>
    <AlertDescription>Save the form before leaving this page.</AlertDescription>
  </Alert>
  <Alert variant="info" :icon="faCircleInfo">
    <AlertTitle>New version available</AlertTitle>
    <AlertDescription>Reload the page to load it.</AlertDescription>
  </Alert>
  <Alert variant="success" :icon="faCircleCheck">
    <AlertTitle>Saved</AlertTitle>
  </Alert>
  <Alert variant="destructive" :icon="faTriangleExclamation">
    <AlertTitle>Payment failed</AlertTitle>
    <AlertDescription>Your card was declined.</AlertDescription>
  </Alert>
</div>
```

Example: Soft appearance (default)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faCircleInfo, faTriangleExclamation } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Alert variant="info" appearance="soft" :icon="faCircleInfo"><AlertTitle>Soft info</AlertTitle><AlertDescription>Tinted surface, readable body text.</AlertDescription></Alert>
  <Alert variant="warning" appearance="soft" :icon="faTriangleExclamation"><AlertTitle>Soft warning</AlertTitle></Alert>
</div>
```

```vue
</script>

  <Alert appearance="solid" variant="info" :icon="faCircleInfo" dismissible><AlertTitle>Solid info</AlertTitle><AlertDescription>Icon and dismiss follow the text colour.</AlertDescription></Alert>
  <Alert appearance="solid" variant="success" :icon="faCircleCheck"><AlertTitle>Solid success</AlertTitle></Alert>
  <Alert appearance="solid" variant="warning" :icon="faTriangleExclamation"><AlertTitle>Solid warning</AlertTitle></Alert>
```

```vue
  <Alert appearance="outline" variant="info" :icon="faCircleInfo"><AlertTitle>Outline info</AlertTitle><AlertDescription>Border carries the tone.</AlertDescription></Alert>
```

```vue
</div>
```

Example: Layout and actions

Example: Dismissible

# Banner
group: feedback / Messages
Full-width, page-level notice with optional sticky position, action slot and remembered dismissal.

Use `Banner` at the very top of a page or layout for global announcements: maintenance windows, upgrade prompts, degraded service. Set `storageKey` so a dismissed banner stays dismissed across visits. Use `Alert` for messages inside the page content.

Placements: `top` (default strip at the top of a layout), `bottom` (strip at the bottom, e.g. cookie notices), `floating` (fixed, centred rounded card near the bottom of the viewport for announcements that should not shift layout) and `inline` (rounded block inside the content flow, e.g. above a table). Appearance: `solid` (filled, loud) or `soft` (tinted, calmer). Add a call to action with `actionLabel` (+ `actionHref` for a link) or the `action` slot.

import { Banner } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'destructive' = 'default' - Solid tone. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- placement: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'floating' | 'inline' = 'top' - Where the banner sits. `floating` is `position: fixed` (centred, bottom of the viewport); `inline` is a rounded in-flow block. Unknown values fall back to `top`. Non-default values add `data-placement`.
- appearance: 'solid' | 'soft' = 'solid' - Filled tone or tinted background with a tone border. Unknown values fall back to `solid`. `soft` adds `data-appearance`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap and type scale. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- layout: 'default' | 'centered' = 'default' - `centered` centres the message and the actions (announcement strips). Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.
- sticky: boolean = false - Sticks to the top of the scroll container (z-sticky); with `placement="bottom"` it sticks to the bottom. Ignored for `floating` and `inline`.
- actionLabel: string - Built-in call-to-action label (small outlined button, or a link with `actionHref`). Blank values render nothing. The `action` slot overrides it.
- actionHref: string - Turns the built-in call-to-action into a link.
- icon: IconDefinition - Optional leading FontAwesome icon.
- dismissible: boolean = false - Shows a dismiss button.
- dismissLabel: string = 'Dismiss' - Accessible label of the dismiss button.
- storageKey: string - Remember dismissal in localStorage under `pd-banner:<storageKey>`; the banner is hidden after mount next time (the first render always shows it, so server and client markup match). Storage errors are ignored.
- role: 'alert' | 'status' | 'note' - Overrides the computed role: `alert` for warning/destructive, `status` otherwise.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Message text.
- action - Right-aligned actions, usually a small Button or link. Overrides `actionLabel`.

Events:
- dismiss [] - The dismiss button was used (fires once).
- action [] - The built-in call-to-action (`actionLabel`) was clicked. Not emitted for content in the `action` slot.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `Banner` is empty (no text) or is `dismissible` with a blank `dismissLabel`. A dismissible banner without `storageKey` is allowed: it comes back on the next page load.

Rules:
- Place one Banner at the top of the layout, outside the main content.
- Always set `storageKey` on dismissible marketing/upgrade banners so they do not reappear.
- Pick the placement by context: `top`/`bottom` for layout-level strips, `floating` for announcements, `inline` inside content.
- Prefer `actionLabel`/`actionHref` for a single call to action; use the `action` slot only for custom controls.
- Use `size="sm"` for dense app shells and `layout="centered"` for short announcements with a single action.
- Keep banner text to one or two lines; put actions in the `action` slot.

Accessibility:
- role="status" (polite) by default. Warning and destructive use role="alert".
- Dismiss is a labelled <button> with a visible focus ring (28px square, 40px on coarse pointers). The call to action is a real button or link.
- Every size and layout keeps the 24px dismiss target (40px on coarse pointers); the centred layout still wraps at 320px.
- Colour pairs use the *-foreground tokens for contrast in light and dark mode.
- Content wraps (`break-words`, `min-w-0`), the floating placement is capped at the viewport width minus 2rem, so it reflows at 320px.

Example: Announcement
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { faBullhorn, faTriangleExclamation } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<Banner variant="info" :icon="faBullhorn">Scheduled maintenance on Saturday 02:00-04:00 UTC.</Banner>
```

Example: Action, dismissible and remembered
```vue
<Banner variant="default" dismissible storage-key="docs-demo-upgrade">
  The workspace storage is almost full.
  <template #action><Button size="xs" variant="secondary">Upgrade</Button></template>
</Banner>
```

Example: Size and layout
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Banner variant="info" size="sm" placement="inline">Small strip with one line of text.</Banner>
  <Banner variant="info" size="lg" placement="inline">Large strip with room for longer text.</Banner>
  <Banner variant="warning" layout="centered" placement="inline" action-label="View status" action-href="#status">Some builds are delayed.</Banner>
</div>
```

Example: Placement: bottom
```vue
<div class="flex h-40 flex-col overflow-auto rounded-md border">
  <div class="min-h-24 flex-1 p-4 text-sm">Page content.</div>
  <Banner placement="bottom" variant="info" sticky>This site stores one cookie to remember your theme.</Banner>
</div>
```

Example: Placement: floating
```vue
<div class="relative h-40 overflow-hidden rounded-md border transform-gpu">
  <p class="p-4 text-sm text-muted-foreground">App content behind the banner.</p>
  <Banner placement="floating" variant="default" action-label="Open appearance settings" action-href="/foundations/themes">Dark mode is available.</Banner>
</div>
```

Example: Placement: inline
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faTriangleExclamation } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Banner placement="inline" variant="warning" :icon="faTriangleExclamation">Showing cached data from 10 minutes ago.</Banner>
  <div class="rounded-md border p-4 text-sm">Table content</div>
</div>
```

Example: Soft tones
```vue
<div class="grid gap-2">
  <Banner appearance="soft" placement="inline">Default</Banner>
  <Banner appearance="soft" placement="inline" variant="info">Info</Banner>
  <Banner appearance="soft" placement="inline" variant="success">Success</Banner>
  <Banner appearance="soft" placement="inline" variant="warning">Warning</Banner>
  <Banner appearance="soft" placement="inline" variant="destructive">Destructive</Banner>
</div>
```

Example: Call to action
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

const clicks = ref(0)
</script>

<div class="grid gap-2">
  <Banner variant="info" action-label="Upgrade plan" dismissible @action="clicks++">Storage is almost full.</Banner>
  <Banner variant="success" appearance="soft" action-label="Read the migration guide" action-href="/guides/migration">A new major version is available.</Banner>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">CTA clicked {{ clicks }} time(s)</p>
</div>
```

Example: Sticky warning
```vue

  <Banner variant="warning" sticky>Service is degraded.</Banner>
  <div class="h-64 p-4 text-sm">Scroll me; the banner stays on top.</div>
</div>
```

# Callout
group: feedback / Messages
Documentation-style note, tip, important, warning, caution, danger, success, quote or example block with a tinted surface and a status icon.

Use `Callout` inside long-form content (docs, articles, settings help) to highlight information. Pick the type by intent: `note` (neutral extra information), `tip` (helpful advice), `important` (must-know information), `warning` (risk of problems), `caution` and `danger` (risk of data loss or breakage; `caution` is a softer-looking icon, same tone), `success` (positive outcome or best practice), `quote` (cited text, rendered in italics) and `example` (worked sample). `appearance` sets the surface (`soft` tinted by default, `solid` filled, `outline` border only, `minimal` icon and text only) and `size` the padding and type scale (`sm`, `md`, `lg`). `dismissible` adds a close button and the `actions` slot puts buttons or links under the text. It is static content, not a status message; it does not announce itself. Use `Alert` for dynamic status messages.

import { Callout } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- type: 'note' | 'tip' | 'important' | 'warning' | 'caution' | 'danger' | 'success' | 'quote' | 'example' = 'note' - Semantic kind; picks colour and default icon. Unknown values fall back to `note`. `data-type` reflects the resolved type.
- title: string - Heading line. Use the `title` slot for rich content.
- icon: IconDefinition - Replaces the default icon of the type.
- hideIcon: boolean = false - Hides the icon.
- appearance: 'soft' | 'solid' | 'outline' | 'minimal' = 'soft' - Surface, independent of `type`. `solid` fills with the type colour and its foreground; `outline` keeps a coloured border on a transparent surface; `minimal` removes border, fill and side padding. Unknown values fall back to `soft`. Non-default values add `data-appearance`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap, type scale and icon size. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- dismissible: boolean = false - Shows a dismiss (X) button. Dismissing hides the callout and emits `dismiss` once.
- dismissLabel: string = 'Dismiss' - Accessible name of the dismiss button. A blank value throws a ContractError when `dismissible`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Body content (text, paragraphs, lists, code).
- title - Rich title; overrides the `title` prop.
- actions - Buttons or links shown under the text (for example a `Button` with `size="xs"`).

Events:
- dismiss [] - The dismiss button was used. Fires once; the callout then removes itself.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `Callout` is empty (no `title` and no content).
- Throws a ContractError when a `dismissible` `Callout` has a blank `dismissLabel`.

Rules:
- Choose `type` by intent: note, tip, important, warning, caution, danger, success, quote, example.
- Use Callout for static documentation notes; use Alert for runtime status.
- Give warning/danger callouts a title that names the consequence.
- Pick `appearance` for emphasis: soft (default), solid (must not be missed), outline (busy backgrounds), minimal (inline hint).
- Use `dismissible` only for notes the reader can safely hide; give the `dismissLabel` a specific name.

Accessibility:
- Rendered with role="note" so assistive tech identifies it as supplementary content.
- The type is conveyed by the icon and the title text, not by colour. The surface keeps a full border for forced-colors mode.
- Long words wrap (`break-words`); the body has `min-w-0`.
- Every appearance keeps a border or a filled surface, so the callout stays visible in forced-colors mode; `minimal` relies on the icon and the title text.
- The dismiss button is a native button named by `dismissLabel` (24px, 40px on coarse pointers) with a visible focus ring; the actions slot content stays in the tab order after the text.

Example: Types
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Callout title="Note">Tokens are defined in theme.css.</Callout>
  <Callout type="tip" title="Tip">Use the <code>class</code> prop to override anything.</Callout>
  <Callout type="warning" title="Warning">Changing the accent preset affects every component.</Callout>
  <Callout type="danger" title="Danger">Deleting a workspace cannot be undone.</Callout>
</div>
```

Example: Type: important
```vue
<Callout type="important" title="Important">Rotate API keys before the migration window.</Callout>
```

Example: Type: caution
```vue
<Callout type="caution" title="Caution">Running this migration locks the table for several minutes.</Callout>
```

Example: Type: success
```vue
<Callout type="success" title="Best practice">Pin dependency versions in production builds.</Callout>
```

Example: Type: quote
```vue
<Callout type="quote" title="Sample source">Quoted text from the source goes here.</Callout>
```

Example: Type: example
```vue
<Callout type="example" title="Example">Calling <code>retry(3)</code> retries the request up to three times.</Callout>
```

Example: Custom icon, no title
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faBell } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Callout :icon="faBell">Notifications are batched every 5 minutes.</Callout>
  <Callout type="tip" hide-icon>Compact variant without an icon.</Callout>
</div>
```

Example: Appearance
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Callout type="note" appearance="soft" title="Soft">Tinted surface, the default.</Callout>
  <Callout type="note" appearance="solid" title="Solid">Filled with the type colour.</Callout>
  <Callout type="warning" appearance="outline" title="Outline">Border only, for busy backgrounds.</Callout>
  <Callout type="tip" appearance="minimal" title="Minimal">Icon and text with no surface.</Callout>
</div>
```

Example: Size
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3">
  <Callout size="sm" title="Small">Dense notes beside form fields.</Callout>
  <Callout size="md" title="Medium">The default scale.</Callout>
  <Callout size="lg" title="Large">Lead note at the top of a page.</Callout>
</div>
```

Example: Dismissible with actions
```vue

  New projects are blocked until a plan is chosen.
  <template #actions>
    <Button size="xs">Choose a plan</Button>
    <Button size="xs" variant="outline">Remind me later</Button>
  </template>
</Callout>
```

# InlineMessage
group: feedback / Messages
One-line, field-level message with a tone-coloured icon.

Use `InlineMessage` for short validation or helper feedback directly under a field or next to a control ("Username is taken", "Looks good"). Give it an `id` and reference it from the control with `aria-describedby`. For longer or section-level messages use `Alert`.

import { InlineMessage } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- tone: 'neutral' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' = 'neutral' - Colour and default icon. Unknown values fall back to `neutral`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text and icon size (text-xs, text-sm, text-base). Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- variant: 'plain' | 'soft' | 'outline' = 'plain' - `plain` is coloured text with an icon; `soft` adds a tinted box; `outline` adds a bordered box. Use the boxed forms for a message that stands alone (above a form, beside a toolbar). Unknown values fall back to `plain`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- icon: IconDefinition - Replaces the tone icon.
- live: 'polite' | 'assertive' | 'off' = 'assertive' for danger, else 'polite' - Live-region behaviour: `polite` is role=status, `assertive` is role=alert, `off` renders no live role. Use `off` for field hints and messages present on first render.
- hideIcon: boolean = false - Hides the icon.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Message text.

Rules:
- Use `variant="soft"` or `"outline"` only for a message that stands alone; under a field use the plain default.
- Set `live="off"` on a field hint or a message that is already there at first render; live roles are for messages that appear after an action.
- Always give the message an id and link it with aria-describedby.
- Keep it to a single short sentence.

Accessibility:
- role="alert" for danger (announced immediately), role="status" otherwise.
- Pair it with `aria-describedby` on the control. The icon is decorative.
- The tone is carried by the icon and the message text in every variant. `outline` keeps a border for forced-colors mode; `soft` is tinted text on a tinted fill (the same pairs as a soft Badge).
- The box variants shrink to the text (`w-fit`) and wrap at `max-w-full`, so long messages reflow at 320px.

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="grid gap-2">
  <InlineMessage>Use at least 8 characters.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="info">We will never share your email.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="success">Username is available.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="warning">This password is easy to guess.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="danger">Username is already taken.</InlineMessage>
</div>
```

Example: Variant and size
```vue
<div class="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
  <InlineMessage tone="success" variant="soft">Saved to the draft folder.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="warning" variant="soft" size="sm">Two fields were trimmed.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="danger" variant="outline">The key could not be verified.</InlineMessage>
  <InlineMessage tone="info" variant="outline" size="lg">Changes apply on the next sign in.</InlineMessage>
</div>
```

Example: Small, custom icon, wired to a field
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faBell } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-xs gap-1.5">
  <label for="docs-im-email" class="text-sm font-medium">Email</label>
  <input id="docs-im-email" class="h-9 rounded-md border bg-transparent px-3 text-sm" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="docs-im-email-msg" />
  <InlineMessage id="docs-im-email-msg" size="sm" tone="danger" :icon="faBell">Enter a valid address.</InlineMessage>
</div>
```

# NotificationList
group: feedback / Notifications
Inbox-style list of notifications with unread dots, relative times, mark-as-read, grouping and a collapsible tail.

Use `NotificationList` for an in-app inbox, a bell dropdown or an activity panel. Each item is `{ id, title, description?, time?, read?, icon?, tone?, href?, group? }`. Times (Date, epoch ms or ISO string) render as relative text via `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with the absolute date in the tooltip; any other string (e.g. "just now") is shown as provided and invalid values render nothing. Clicking a row marks it read and emits `select`; "Mark all as read" and per-row dismiss are built in. The list is usable uncontrolled (it updates itself and emits `update:items`) or controlled (`v-model:items` / handle `read`, `read-all`, `dismiss`). Items with a `group` are rendered under headings in order of first appearance. `maxItems` collapses the tail behind Show more; `loading` shows skeleton rows. For transient messages use `Toaster`; for page-level status use `Alert` or `Banner`.

import { NotificationList } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: NotificationItem[] = [] - Notifications (v-model:items). Every item needs a unique string or number `id` and a non-empty `title` (otherwise a ContractError; in production such entries are not shown). Never mutated.
- appearance: 'card' | 'flush' = 'card' - `card` is a bordered, rounded surface. `flush` removes the border, radius and fill so the list sits inside a popover, a sheet or another card that already has one. Unknown values fall back to `card`. Non-default values add `data-appearance`.
- shape: 'circle' | 'square' = 'circle' - Shape of the icon bubble: round, or square with the control radius. Unknown values fall back to `circle`. Non-default values add `data-shape`.
- variant: 'default' | 'compact' = 'default' - Density. `compact` uses tighter rows, a smaller icon and single-line descriptions. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- loading: boolean = false - Show skeleton rows instead of the list and set `aria-busy`.
- loadingCount: number = 3 - Skeleton rows (clamped 0-50).
- maxItems: number - Collapse to this many rows with a Show more button. Non-positive, NaN or Infinity mean unlimited; fractions are floored.
- dismissible: boolean = false - Show a dismiss (X) button on each row.
- markReadOnSelect: boolean = true - Clicking an unread row marks it read.
- showMarkAll: boolean = true - Show Mark all as read while something is unread.
- now: number | Date - Reference time for relative text. Without it the first render shows absolute UTC times (server and client match), then relative text appears after mount and refreshes every 30 s. Set it for fixed output (tests, docs).
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for relative times; defaults to the `ConfigProvider` locale, then the browser default. Invalid locales fall back to the default.
- markAllLabel: string = 'Mark all as read' - Header button label.
- showMoreLabel: string = 'Show more' - Label before the hidden count, e.g. "Show more (5)".
- showLessLabel: string = 'Show less' - Label when expanded.
- emptyLabel: string = 'No notifications' - Default empty-state text (the `empty` slot overrides it).
- label: string = 'Notifications' - Accessible name of the list region. Give each list on a page its own name.
- dismissLabel: string = 'Dismiss' - Prefix of the dismiss button aria-label ("Dismiss: <title>").
- loadingLabel: string = 'Loading notifications' - Screen-reader text while loading.
- unreadItemLabel: string = 'Unread' - Screen-reader prefix on unread titles.
- unreadLabel: (count: number) => string = n => n ? `${n} unread` : 'All caught up' - Text of the live unread count.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root.

Slots:
- icon ({ item: NotificationItem }) - Custom leading icon/avatar per row (replaces the `icon` field).
- empty - Empty state shown when there is nothing to list.

Events:
- update:items [items: NotificationItem[]] - New list after mark-read, mark-all or dismiss (v-model:items).
- read [id: string | number] - A single notification was marked read (row click).
- read-all [ids: (string | number)[]] - Mark all as read pressed; payload lists the ids that were unread.
- dismiss [id: string | number] - A notification was dismissed.
- select [item: NotificationItem] - A row was clicked / activated (also fires for read rows).
- show-more - The list was expanded with Show more.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `NotificationList` has a blank `label`, or an item has no `id`, repeats an `id` or has a blank `title`.

Rules:
- Give every item a unique `id`; bind `v-model:items` for the simplest working inbox.
- Use `time` as Date, epoch ms or ISO string; pass `now` for deterministic output.
- Use `group` for headings (e.g. Today / Earlier) and `maxItems` to cap long lists.
- Use `tone` + `icon` for status colour; never colour rows with hard-coded classes.
- Use `appearance="flush"` inside popovers and sheets so the border is not doubled; keep `card` on the page.
- Handle `select` to navigate or open details; `href` items render as real links.

Accessibility:
- The root is a labelled `region` (override with `aria-label`); each group is a `ul role="list"` of `li role="listitem"`, labelled by its heading.
- Rows are native `<button>` (or `<a>` when `href` is set), so Enter and Space activate them; unread rows carry a screen-reader "Unread:" prefix in addition to the visual dot.
- The unread count is an `aria-live="polite"` region and updates as items are read, dismissed or marked all read.
- `appearance="flush"` removes the list border, so place it inside a container that keeps one (popover, sheet, card); rows keep their dividers. `shape` changes only the radius of the decorative icon bubble.
- Dismiss buttons are labelled "Dismiss: <title>"; `loading` sets `aria-busy` and announces a status message; times use `<time datetime>` with an absolute-date tooltip.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [
  { id: 1, title: 'Deploy finished', description: 'Build #42 is live.', time: Date.now() - 5 * 60_000, read: false },
  { id: 2, title: 'New comment', time: Date.now() - 3 * 3600_000, read: true },
]
</script>

<NotificationList label="Notifications, basic" :items="items" class="max-w-md" />
```

Example: Inbox with icons, links, dismiss and events
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { faBell, faCircleCheck, faTriangleExclamation } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
const items = ref([
  { id: 1, title: 'Deploy finished', description: 'Build #42 is live.', time: Date.now() - 5 * 60_000, read: false, tone: 'success', icon: faCircleCheck },
  { id: 2, title: 'New comment on your report', time: Date.now() - 3 * 3600_000, read: false, icon: faBell, href: '/components/feedback/alert' },
  { id: 3, title: 'Invoice overdue', time: Date.now() - 2 * 86400_000, read: true, tone: 'danger', icon: faTriangleExclamation },
])
const log = ref('')
</script>

<NotificationList label="Notifications, with dismiss" v-model:items="items" dismissible class="max-w-md"
  @read="log = 'read ' + $event" @read-all="log = 'read all (' + $event.length + ')'" @dismiss="log = 'dismissed ' + $event" />
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ log || 'No events yet' }}</p>
```

Example: Variant: compact with groups
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [
  { id: 1, title: 'Build passed', time: Date.now() - 60_000, read: false, group: 'Today' },
  { id: 2, title: 'Review requested', time: Date.now() - 7200_000, read: false, group: 'Today' },
  { id: 3, title: 'Weekly report', time: Date.now() - 4 * 86400_000, read: true, group: 'Earlier' },
]
</script>

<NotificationList label="Notifications, compact" variant="compact" :items="items" class="max-w-sm" />
```

Example: Appearance: flush, shape: square
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

const items = [{ id: 1, title: 'Deploy finished', time: Date.now() - 5 * 60_000, read: false, tone: 'success', icon: faCircleCheck }]
</script>

<div class="max-w-md rounded-lg border bg-popover p-1">
  <NotificationList label="Notifications, flush" appearance="flush" shape="square" :items="items" :show-mark-all="false" />
</div>
```

Example: Show more
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<NotificationList label="Notifications, collapsed" :items="items" :max-items="2" class="max-w-md" />
```

Example: Loading and empty
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
  <NotificationList label="Notifications, loading" loading class="max-w-md" />
  <NotificationList label="Notifications, empty" :items="[]" class="max-w-md"><template #empty>You are all caught up.</template></NotificationList>
</div>
```
