# AsyncBoundary
group: feedback / States
Shows the right state for async content: loading, error with retry, empty or the content itself.

Wrap anything that is fetched. Drive it with `state` (`idle`, `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `success`) or hand it a `promise` and it follows the promise: pending is loading, rejected is the error, fulfilled is the content (or the empty state when the result has nothing in it). The built-in states are `LoadingState`, `ErrorState` and `EmptyState`; replace any of them with the `loading`, `error`, `empty` or `idle` slot. `delay` holds the loading state back so a fast load never flashes it, and `minDuration` keeps it up long enough to read. A promise that is swapped for a newer one, or that settles after the component is gone, is ignored. Use it for a region of a page. For a whole failed page use `ErrorState` with `variant="page"`; for content that only needs a skeleton while it loads, `LoadingState` alone is enough.

import { AsyncBoundary } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- state: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'error' | 'empty' | 'success' - The state to show. Wins over `promise` when set. Unknown values fall back to `success`. With neither `state` nor `promise` the default slot shows.
- promise: PromiseLike<unknown> | null - Follow a promise: pending is `loading`, rejected is `error`, fulfilled is `success` or `empty`. `null` means not started (`idle`). A newer promise replaces the old one, whose result is then ignored.
- error: unknown - What went wrong: a string, an Error, an object with a `message`, a number. Rendered as plain text (never HTML), control characters removed, cut at 300 characters. Overrides the reason of a rejected promise.
- variant: 'default' | 'card' | 'compact' = 'default' - `default` has no surface. `card` draws a bordered surface with padding for the content. `compact` swaps in the dense forms of the built-in states: an inline loader, a single-row error, a compact empty state. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Scale of the built-in loading, error and empty states. Your own content is not affected. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- delay: number = 0 - Milliseconds to wait before the loading state appears. Finished content stays on screen meanwhile. A load that ends sooner never shows the loader. Negative, NaN and Infinity count as 0; the maximum is 60000.
- minDuration: number = 0 - Milliseconds the loading state stays once it has appeared, so it does not flash. Counted from the moment it appeared. The same limits as `delay`.
- loadingLabel: string = 'Loading…' - Text of the built-in loading state. Also announced when you supply your own `loading` slot.
- loadingVariant: 'spinner' | 'text' | 'card' | 'table' | 'list' | 'avatar-text' | 'kpi-grid' | 'form' = 'spinner' - Look of the built-in loading state (the `variant` of `LoadingState`): a spinner or a skeleton that matches the content.
- errorTitle: string - Heading of the built-in error state. Defaults to "Something went wrong".
- errorMessage: string - Your own wording for the built-in error state. The real error then moves into the collapsible technical details. Without it the error text is shown, or a generic sentence when there is none.
- retryable: boolean = true - Show the retry button in the built-in error state. It needs an `@retry` handler.
- retryLabel: string = 'Try again' - Text of the retry button.
- emptyTitle: string = 'Nothing to show' - Heading of the built-in empty state. Say what is empty ("No invoices yet"). Also announced when loading ends with nothing.
- emptyDescription: string - Supporting text of the built-in empty state.
- emptyIcon: IconDefinition - Icon of the built-in empty state.
- isEmpty: (value: unknown) => boolean - Decides whether a fulfilled promise value is empty. The default treats null, undefined, an empty array, a blank string and an empty Set or Map as empty. A function that throws counts as not empty.
- successLabel: string = 'Loaded.' - Announced politely when a load ends with content. An empty string turns the announcement off, for the empty state as well.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ data: unknown }) - The content. `data` is the value a followed promise fulfilled with.
- loading - Replaces the built-in loading state.
- error ({ error: unknown, message: string, retry: () => void }) - Replaces the built-in error state. `message` is the safe text; call `retry` to emit `retry`.
- empty ({ data: unknown }) - Replaces the built-in empty state.
- empty-action - Button or link shown under the built-in empty state (the `action` slot of `EmptyState`).
- idle - Shown before anything was requested (`state="idle"` or `:promise="null"`). Renders nothing when omitted.

Events:
- retry [] - The retry button of the built-in error state was pressed, or `retry()` was called from the `error` slot. Start the load again.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `AsyncBoundary` has no default slot (the content to show once loading succeeds).
- Throws a ContractError when the retry button is on (`retryable`, the default) but there is no `@retry` handler and no `error` slot, because the button would do nothing.

Rules:
- Give the boundary one source of truth: `state` or `promise`, not both. `state` wins when both are set.
- Always handle `@retry` (start the load again) or set `:retryable="false"`.
- Create the promise once per load (in an event handler or a watcher). A promise created in the template runs on every render.
- Use `delay` (about 200 ms) for fast endpoints and `minDuration` (about 500 ms) when a flash of loader is worse than waiting. Both default to 0.
- Name what is empty in `emptyTitle` ("No invoices yet"); say what failed in `errorTitle`. Do not rely on the defaults in shipped screens.
- Pass the raw error to `error`; the component shortens it and never renders HTML. Use `errorMessage` for friendlier wording.
- Timers and the promise callback are cleaned up on unmount; do not add your own.

Accessibility:
- The root carries `aria-busy="true"` while loading, including the time before a delayed loader appears.
- Announcements: the built-in loading state is a polite `role="status"` region and the built-in error state is `role="alert"` (assertive, because the person has to act). A separate visually hidden polite status region announces the end of a load ("Loaded." or the empty title), a custom `loading` slot and a custom `error` slot. Regions are siblings, never nested.
- Nothing is announced on first render with finished content, and a load that ended before its `delay` produces one short announcement, not a loading and a loaded pair.
- The retry button is a labelled native button with a 24px minimum target (44px on coarse pointers) and a visible focus ring. When the loader replaces the error, focus is not moved; the retry button leaves the DOM, so put your own focus management in the `retry` handler when needed.
- Error text is rendered as text only, long words wrap (`break-words`), and the technical details are a labelled, focusable region. Colour is never the only signal: the error has an icon and a heading, the empty state a title.
- Motion: the skeleton pulse is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Borders keep the card surface visible in forced-colors mode. Layout uses logical properties and wraps at 320px.

Example: Move through the states
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const current = ref('success')
const states = ['loading', 'error', 'empty', 'success']
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
    <Button v-for="s in states" :key="s" size="sm" :variant="current === s ? 'default' : 'outline'" :aria-pressed="current === s" @click="current = s">{{ s }}</Button>
  </div>
  <AsyncBoundary :state="current" error="The sample server did not answer." empty-title="No invoices yet" empty-description="Invoices appear here once one is issued." @retry="current = 'loading'">
    <p>Three sample invoices are listed here.</p>
  </AsyncBoundary>
</div>
```

Example: Follow a promise
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const promise = ref(null)
let attempt = 0
function load() {
  attempt += 1
  const ok = attempt % 2 === 0
  promise.value = new Promise((resolve, reject) => setTimeout(() => (ok ? resolve(['Sample row']) : reject(new Error('Sample request failed'))), 700))
}
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <div><Button size="sm" @click="load">Load sample rows</Button></div>
  <AsyncBoundary :promise="promise" loading-label="Loading sample rows" empty-title="No sample rows" @retry="load">
    <template #idle><p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Nothing requested yet.</p></template>
    <template #default="{ data }"><p>Loaded {{ data ? data.length : 0 }} sample row.</p></template>
  </AsyncBoundary>
</div>
```

Example: No flash: delay and minimum time
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const current = ref('success')
function run(ms) {
  current.value = 'loading'
  setTimeout(() => (current.value = 'success'), ms)
}
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3">
  <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="run(150)">Quick load (150 ms)</Button>
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="run(1500)">Slow load (1.5 s)</Button>
  </div>
  <AsyncBoundary :state="current" :delay="400" :min-duration="800" loading-label="Loading sample report" :retryable="false">
    <p>Sample report is ready.</p>
  </AsyncBoundary>
</div>
```

Example: Skeleton loading and an empty state with an action
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faFileInvoice } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
  <AsyncBoundary state="loading" loading-variant="list" :rows="3" loading-label="Loading sample list" :retryable="false">
    <p>List</p>
  </AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary state="empty" :empty-icon="faFileInvoice" empty-title="No invoices yet" empty-description="Issue the first one to see it here." :retryable="false">
    <p>List</p>
    <template #empty-action><Button size="sm">Issue an invoice</Button></template>
  </AsyncBoundary>
</div>
```

Example: Error text is shown safely
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const failure = new Error('Request to /sample/reports timed out after 30 seconds')
const hostile = '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)> ' + 'long text '.repeat(80)
</script>

<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
  <AsyncBoundary state="error" :error="hostile" error-title="Could not load the report" @retry="() => {}">
    <p>Report</p>
  </AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary state="error" :error="failure" error-title="Could not load the report" error-message="The report service is slow. Try again in a minute." @retry="() => {}">
    <p>Report</p>
  </AsyncBoundary>
</div>
```

Example: Variants and sizes
```vue
<div class="grid items-start gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
  <AsyncBoundary variant="card" state="success" :retryable="false"><p>Content on a card surface.</p></AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary variant="card" size="sm" state="empty" empty-title="No sample items" :retryable="false"><p>Items</p></AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary variant="compact" state="loading" loading-label="Loading sample items" :retryable="false"><p>Items</p></AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary variant="compact" state="error" error="The sample list could not be loaded." @retry="() => {}"><p>Items</p></AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary variant="compact" state="empty" empty-title="No sample items" :retryable="false"><p>Items</p></AsyncBoundary>
  <AsyncBoundary size="lg" state="loading" loading-label="Loading a large sample" :retryable="false"><p>Items</p></AsyncBoundary>
</div>
```

Example: Your own states in slots
```vue
<AsyncBoundary state="error" error="Sample failure" loading-label="Loading" @retry="() => {}">
  <template #loading><p>Fetching the sample list</p></template>
  <template #error="{ message, retry }">
    <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 rounded-md border p-3 text-sm">
      <span>{{ message }}</span>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="retry">Fetch again</Button>
    </div>
  </template>
  <p>Sample list</p>
</AsyncBoundary>
```

# EmptyState
group: feedback / States
Centred placeholder for lists, tables and views that have no content yet.

Use `EmptyState` when a collection is empty (first run, no search results, cleared filters). Variants: `default` (centred, full page or large region), `card` (self-contained bordered surface), `bordered-dashed` (dashed outline, good for upload/drop zones and "add the first item" slots), `compact` (dense, for popovers, side panels and small widgets), `inline` (single row with icon, text and action, for table footers and list ends) and the `illustration` slot for custom artwork. Always say what is missing and offer the next step in the `action` slot. For failed loads use `ErrorState`; for loading use `LoadingState`.

import { EmptyState } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- icon: IconDefinition - FontAwesome icon in a muted circle. Use the `icon` slot for custom artwork.
- title: string - Heading. Omitted when empty.
- description: string - Supporting text (max-w-md).
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and type scale. `sm` for cards/popovers, `lg` for full pages.
- layout: 'center' | 'start' = 'center' - `start` aligns the icon, text and action to the start edge (logical, so it follows the writing direction). Use it in panels, forms and tables where a centred block looks lost. `inline` is already a start-aligned row and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `center`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' = 'neutral' - Tint of the icon bubble. The title and description say what is empty; the tone is only a cue. Unknown values fall back to `neutral`. Non-default values add `data-tone`.
- variant: 'default' | 'card' | 'bordered-dashed' | 'compact' | 'inline' = 'default' - Layout and surface. `compact` and `inline` ignore the padding of `size`. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- titleAs: 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'p' | 'div' = 'h3' - Element used for the title so the heading outline stays correct.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- illustration - Large custom artwork (SVG/img) rendered above everything else; can be combined with `icon`.
- icon - Custom icon/illustration; overrides the `icon` prop.
- title - Rich title.
- description - Rich description.
- action - Buttons/links for the next step.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an `EmptyState` has no `title` (or `title` slot).

Rules:
- Use `layout="start"` inside left-aligned panels (LLMSlop L7: not everything centred); use `tone` only when the empty state has a status meaning.
- Pick `variant` by context: card/bordered-dashed for sections, compact in popovers, inline for table footers.
- Pass decorative artwork through the `illustration` slot (give it aria-hidden or alt).
- Always include a title; add an action when the user can fix the emptiness.
- Use `titleAs` to keep heading levels sequential.

Accessibility:
- The title renders as a heading. Choose the level with `titleAs` (`h2`, `h3` by default, `h4`) or use `p`/`div` when a heading would break the outline.
- The icon is decorative. The message is text. A tone only tints the icon bubble, so the title and description carry the meaning.
- `layout="start"` uses logical alignment (`items-start`, `text-start`), so it follows right-to-left writing; the text wraps and the illustration scales down at 320px.
- Actions are whatever you slot in, so give them real button or link semantics.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faInbox } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<EmptyState :icon="faInbox" title="No messages" description="New messages appear here." />
```

Example: With action and sizes
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faFolderOpen } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
  <EmptyState size="sm" :icon="faFolderOpen" title="No projects" description="Create a project to see it listed here.">
    <template #action><Button size="sm">New project</Button></template>
  </EmptyState>
  <EmptyState size="sm" title="No projects match this filter" description="Clear the filters to see all projects.">
    <template #action><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Clear filters</Button></template>
  </EmptyState>
</div>
```

Example: Variant: card
```vue

</script>

<EmptyState variant="card" :icon="faFolderOpen" title="No projects" description="Create a project to see it listed here."><template #action><Button size="sm">New project</Button></template></EmptyState>
```

Example: Variant: bordered-dashed
```vue

</script>

<EmptyState variant="bordered-dashed" :icon="faInbox" title="Drop files here" description="Or pick them from your computer."><template #action><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Browse files</Button></template></EmptyState>
```


# ErrorState
group: feedback / States
Failed-load placeholder with a message, retry button and collapsible technical details.

Use `ErrorState` where content could not be loaded (a list, a page, a widget). Keep `message` short and actionable; put stacks, request ids and response bodies in `details`. The parent owns the retry logic: handle `retry` and toggle `retrying`. Variants: `default` (centred block inside a region), `card` (bordered surface), `inline` (one row for widgets, list items and table cells) and `page` (full-viewport 404/500/403/503 layout with an `h1`). Use `status` for ready-made HTTP copy (`404` and `403` hide the retry button, `500` and `503` keep it). For form-level errors use `Alert`; for one-line field errors use `InlineMessage`.

import { ErrorState } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap, icon, title, message and code size of the `default` and `card` variants (`inline` is a fixed compact row and `page` fills the viewport). Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- layout: 'center' | 'start' = 'center' - `start` aligns the icon, text and actions to the start edge (follows the writing direction). It applies to `default`, `card` and `page`. Unknown values fall back to `center`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.
- tone: 'danger' | 'warning' | 'neutral' = 'danger' - Colour of the icon (and of the `inline` row). Use `warning` for degraded service and `neutral` for not found or no access. The title and message still say what happened. Unknown values fall back to `danger`. Non-default values add `data-tone`.
- variant: 'default' | 'card' | 'inline' | 'page' = 'default' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- status: number | string - HTTP status preset: 403, 404, 500 or 503 fill `code`, title, message and the default of `retryable`. Other values only show the code.
- code: number | string - Large code shown instead of the icon (defaults to `status`). Blank values are ignored.
- title: string = 'Something went wrong' - Heading. Blank values fall back to the `status` preset title, then to the default.
- message: string - Human-readable explanation. Falls back to the `status` preset message. The default slot overrides it.
- titleAs: 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'p' | 'div' = 'h3' ('h1' for page) - Heading element of the title. Invalid values fall back to the default.
- details: string - Technical detail in a collapsible <details> block (closed by default). Hidden when blank.
- retryable: boolean = true - Show the retry button. When omitted it follows the `status` preset (false for 403/404), otherwise true.
- retryLabel: string = 'Try again' - Retry button text.
- retrying: boolean = false - Spinner + disabled retry button with aria-busy (the alert root is not marked busy).
- detailsLabel: string = 'Technical details' - Summary text of the details block.
- icon: IconDefinition = faTriangleExclamation - Icon in the destructive-tinted circle. Hidden when a `code` is shown.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Rich message; overrides `message`.
- actions - Extra buttons next to the retry button.

Events:
- retry [] - Retry button clicked (not emitted while `retrying`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an `ErrorState` has no message: a `message`, a known `status` preset or the default slot is required.

Rules:
- Use `tone="warning"` for degraded service and `"neutral"` for 403/404; keep `danger` for failures the person can retry.
- Handle @retry and drive `retrying` from the request state.
- Never put secrets in `details`.
- Use ErrorState for failed loads, not for validation errors.
- For route-level 404/500 screens use `variant="page"` with `status` and provide a link home in the `actions` slot.
- Use `variant="inline"` for failed widgets and list rows, `card` for failed panels.

Accessibility:
- The root has role="alert" so the failure is announced when it appears.
- The title is an `h3` by default and an `h1` for the page variant. Change it with `titleAs` to keep heading levels in order.
- Technical details use native <details>/<summary>. The scrollable details block is keyboard focusable and labelled by `detailsLabel`.
- Every size, layout and tone keeps role="alert", the title, the message and the retry button. The tone changes only the icon and row colour: warning icons use the warning foreground token and the words carry the meaning.
- The retry button exposes aria-busy while retrying. The status code uses the muted foreground token, which keeps 3:1 contrast.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<ErrorState message="We could not load your projects." />
```

Example: Retry with details
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const retrying = ref(false)
function retry() { retrying.value = true; setTimeout(() => (retrying.value = false), 1500) }
</script>

<ErrorState
  title="Could not load users"
  message="The server did not respond in time."
  details="GET /api/users -> 504 Gateway Timeout (request id 7f3a)"
  :retrying="retrying"
  @retry="retry"
/>
```

Example: Variant: card
```vue
<ErrorState variant="card" title="Could not load chart" message="The analytics service did not respond." details="GET /api/stats -> 504" />
```

Example: Variant: inline
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const retrying = ref(false)
function retry() { retrying.value = true; setTimeout(() => (retrying.value = false), 1500) }
</script>

<ErrorState variant="inline" title="Could not load comments" message="Check your connection." :retrying="retrying" @retry="retry" />
```

Example: Variant: page (404)
```vue
<ErrorState variant="page" status="404" title-as="h4" class="min-h-80 py-8"><template #actions><Button size="sm" as="a" href="/components">Back to the component list</Button></template></ErrorState>
```

Example: Variant: page (500)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const retrying = ref(false)
function retry() { retrying.value = true; setTimeout(() => (retrying.value = false), 1500) }
</script>

<ErrorState variant="page" status="500" title-as="h4" class="min-h-80 py-8" details="Request id 7f3a9c" :retrying="retrying" @retry="retry" />
```

Example: Custom code
```vue
<ErrorState variant="card" code="E_TIMEOUT" title="Request timed out" message="The server took too long to answer." :retryable="false" />
```

Example: Size, layout and tone
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <ErrorState variant="card" size="sm" layout="start" title="Could not load the list" message="The server did not answer. Try again." />
  <ErrorState variant="card" size="lg" tone="warning" status="503" />
  <ErrorState variant="inline" tone="neutral" title="No access" message="Ask an admin for the viewer role." :retryable="false" />
</div>
```

# LoadingState
group: feedback / States
Loading placeholder: spinner with label, or text / card / table / list / avatar-text / kpi-grid / form skeletons; optional full-page layout.

Use `LoadingState` while data is on its way. Use `variant="spinner"` for short or unknown waits and the skeleton variants when the final layout is predictable, so the page does not jump: `text` (article lines), `card` (media + lines), `table` (header + rows x columns), `list` (rows with a marker, a line and a trailing value), `avatar-text` (people/comments/activity feeds), `kpi-grid` (dashboard metric tiles) and `form` (label + field pairs and a submit button). `rows` and `columns` are clamped to sensible limits.

import { LoadingState } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'spinner' | 'text' | 'card' | 'table' | 'list' | 'avatar-text' | 'kpi-grid' | 'form' = 'spinner' - Placeholder shape. Unknown values fall back to `spinner`.
- label: string = 'Loading…' - Visible next to the spinner, screen-reader-only for skeletons. The default slot overrides it.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Scale of the `spinner` variant: spinner, label and padding. Skeleton variants ignore it. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- layout: 'stacked' | 'inline' = 'stacked' - `inline` puts the spinner and the label in one start-aligned row (buttons-adjacent status, table footers, toolbars). Spinner variant only. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' | 'pill' = 'rounded' - Corner shape of the skeleton placeholders: small radius, none, or fully rounded. Match the shape of the content that will replace them. The spinner variant ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Non-default values add `data-shape`.
- indicator: 'ring' | 'dots' | 'bars' | 'pulse' | 'orbit' = 'ring' - Spinner shape of the `spinner` variant (see `Spinner` `variant`). Skeleton variants ignore it. Unknown values fall back to `ring`.
- fullPage: boolean = false - Fill the viewport height and centre the content.
- rows: number = 3 - Skeleton text lines, table body rows, list rows, avatar rows or form fields, clamped to 1-50.
- columns: number = 4 - Skeleton table columns, or the number of `kpi-grid` tiles, clamped to 1-12.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces the label text.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `LoadingState` has a blank `label` and no default slot (the label is what screen readers announce, also for skeletons).

Rules:
- Use `layout="inline"` for loading status inside toolbars and footers; use `shape` to match the skeleton to the final content.
- Match the skeleton variant to the final layout: kpi-grid for metric tiles, avatar-text for people/comment lists, list for plain rows, form for settings forms.
- Always render exactly one of LoadingState / ErrorState / EmptyState / content for a data region.

Accessibility:
- role="status" (a polite live region). It has no aria-busy: the region exists only while loading.
- Skeleton blocks are aria-hidden. The label is announced through an sr-only element.
- Size, layout and shape only change geometry: every combination keeps the same status region and the announced label. The inline layout keeps the label visible next to the spinner.
- The pulse animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

Example: Spinner
```vue
<LoadingState label="Loading projects…" />
```

Example: Skeletons
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6">
  <LoadingState variant="text" :rows="4" label="Loading article" />
  <LoadingState variant="card" :rows="2" label="Loading card" />
  <LoadingState variant="table" :rows="4" :columns="3" label="Loading table" />
</div>
```

Example: Indicator shapes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-2">
  <LoadingState layout="inline" size="sm" indicator="dots" label="Loading comments" />
  <LoadingState layout="inline" size="sm" indicator="bars" label="Loading charts" />
  <LoadingState layout="inline" size="sm" indicator="orbit" label="Loading files" />
</div>
```

Example: Size and layout (spinner)
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4">
  <LoadingState size="sm" label="Loading comments" />
  <LoadingState layout="inline" size="sm" label="Saving changes" />
  <LoadingState size="lg" label="Loading the report" />
</div>
```

Example: Skeleton shape
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <LoadingState variant="list" shape="square" :rows="2" label="Loading rows" />
  <LoadingState variant="avatar-text" shape="pill" :rows="2" label="Loading people" />
</div>
```

Example: Skeleton: list
```vue
<LoadingState variant="list" :rows="4" label="Loading files" />
```

Example: Skeleton: avatar-text
```vue
<LoadingState variant="avatar-text" :rows="3" label="Loading members" />
```

Example: Skeleton: kpi-grid
```vue
<LoadingState variant="kpi-grid" :columns="4" label="Loading metrics" />
```

Example: Skeleton: form
```vue
<LoadingState variant="form" :rows="3" label="Loading form" class="max-w-md" />
```

# OfflineIndicator
group: feedback / States
Shows a warning message while the browser is offline; renders nothing visible when online.

Place `OfflineIndicator` once near the top of the layout. It uses `useOnline()` from the library helpers (navigator.onLine plus online/offline events). The live-region wrapper is always mounted so screen readers announce the message when it appears. Use the `offline` prop to drive it from your own connectivity check.

import { OfflineIndicator } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'banner' | 'pill' | 'inline' = 'default' - Look while offline. `default` is a bordered, tinted box; `banner` a full-width filled strip for the top of a layout; `pill` a small chip for headers and toolbars; `inline` icon and text only. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- label: string = 'You are offline. Changes may not be saved.' - Message while offline. The default slot overrides it.
- icon: IconDefinition = faWifi - Leading icon.
- offline: boolean - Force the state instead of reading the browser. Leave undefined for automatic detection.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces the label text.

Rules:
- Pick `variant="banner"` for the top of a layout, `pill` for a header or toolbar, `inline` inside a form footer.
- Mount once in the app shell.
- Use the `offline` prop only for previews or custom connectivity checks.

Accessibility:
- role="status" with aria-live="polite" on an always-mounted wrapper, so the message is announced when it appears.
- The message is text with an icon, never colour alone. The text wraps and has `min-w-0`.
- Every variant keeps the same live region. `default` and `pill` keep a border and `banner` a filled strip, so they stay visible in forced-colors mode; `inline` relies on the icon and the words. The banner uses the warning fill with its foreground token.

Example: Forced offline (preview)
```vue
<OfflineIndicator offline />
```

Example: Custom message
```vue
<OfflineIndicator offline label="No connection. We will retry automatically." />
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
  <OfflineIndicator offline variant="banner" class="justify-self-stretch" />
  <OfflineIndicator offline variant="default" />
  <OfflineIndicator offline variant="pill" label="Offline" />
  <OfflineIndicator offline variant="inline" label="You are offline. Edits are kept on this device." />
</div>
```

Example: Automatic (hidden while online)
```vue
<OfflineIndicator />
```

# StaleNotice
group: feedback / States
Shows when data was last updated, turns into a warning once it is stale, with optional refresh button.

Use `StaleNotice` on dashboards and cached views. Pass the time of the last successful fetch; the relative time ("5 minutes ago") re-renders on an interval and the notice switches to the warning style after `staleAfter`. A missing or unparsable timestamp is a mistake: it throws a ContractError (see `requires`); in production it renders "unknown" and counts as stale. The pure helper `formatRelativeTime(date, now?, locale?)` is exported too.

import { StaleNotice } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- timestamp*: Date | number | string - Last update time (Date, epoch ms or parsable date string). Missing or invalid values throw a ContractError.
- variant: 'default' | 'inline' | 'banner' | 'pill' = 'default' - Look. `default` is a bordered box; `inline` is icon and text only; `banner` a full-width strip with top and bottom borders; `pill` a small rounded chip. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- tone: 'auto' | 'neutral' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' = 'auto' - `auto` is `warning` once stale and `neutral` while fresh. Any other value forces that colour in both states; the stale wording still appears when stale. Unknown values fall back to `auto`. An explicit tone adds `data-tone`.
- staleAfter: number = 300000 - Age in ms after which the data is stale (strictly greater than).
- interval: number = 30000 - Re-render interval in ms. 0 disables ticking.
- label: string = 'Last updated' - Text before the relative time.
- staleLabel: string = 'Data may be out of date.' - Text shown while stale.
- hideWhenFresh: boolean = false - Render nothing until the data is stale.
- refreshable: boolean = false - Show a refresh button.
- refreshLabel: string = 'Refresh' - Refresh button text.
- refreshing: boolean = false - Spinner + disabled refresh button.
- locale: string = ConfigProvider locale, then `en` - BCP 47 tag for Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. Invalid tags fall back to `en`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- refresh [] - Refresh button clicked (not emitted while `refreshing`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `StaleNotice` has a missing or unparsable `timestamp`.

Rules:
- Leave `tone` on `auto` unless the product has a reason to force a colour; use `variant="banner"` for a page-level strip and `pill` for a header.
- Pass the timestamp of the last SUCCESSFUL fetch, not of the last attempt.
- Handle @refresh and drive `refreshing` from the request state.
- The interval timer is cleaned up on unmount.

Accessibility:
- role="status" (polite). The text only changes when the relative time rolls over, not on every tick.
- The time is a <time datetime> element with the absolute time as title, set in tabular figures.
- Every variant and tone keeps the icon and the same text. `default`, `banner` and `pill` keep a border for forced-colors mode; `inline` relies on the icon and the words. Tinted surfaces use `text-foreground`.
- The stale state is conveyed by text, not colour alone. The refresh button is a labelled <button> and is disabled while refreshing.

Example: Fresh
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const updated = Date.now() - 90_000
</script>

<StaleNotice :timestamp="updated" />
```

Example: Stale with refresh
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const updated = Date.now() - 20 * 60_000
const busy = ref(false)
function refresh() { busy.value = true; setTimeout(() => (busy.value = false), 1000) }
</script>

<StaleNotice :timestamp="updated" refreshable :refreshing="busy" @refresh="refresh" />
```

Example: Variants and tone
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const updated = Date.now() - 20 * 60_000
const fresh = Date.now() - 60_000
</script>

<div class="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
  <StaleNotice :timestamp="updated" variant="banner" class="justify-self-stretch" refreshable />
  <StaleNotice :timestamp="fresh" variant="pill" tone="success" label="Synced" />
  <StaleNotice :timestamp="updated" variant="inline" />
  <StaleNotice :timestamp="fresh" tone="info" />
  <StaleNotice :timestamp="updated" tone="danger" stale-label="Data could not be refreshed." />
</div>
```

# TypingIndicator
group: feedback / States
Three softly pulsing dots in a compact bubble that show someone or something is writing, with the label announced once.

Use `TypingIndicator` at the end of a conversation while a person or an assistant is composing a reply. It is a polite `role="status"` whose visually hidden `label` ("Mira is typing") is the only thing a screen reader announces; the dots are decoration. `ChatThread` draws one for its `typing` prop. Use `Spinner` or `LoadingState` for a wait that is not a reply being written, and `Progress` when the amount done is known.

import { TypingIndicator } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- label: string = 'Typing' - Visually hidden text announced politely once. Name who is typing when it is known. Empty or blank falls back to `Typing`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' = 'md' - Dot size and padding: 4px or 6px dots. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Non-default values add `data-size`.
- variant: 'bubble' | 'plain' = 'bubble' - `bubble` is a muted rounded chip; `plain` is the dots only, in the surrounding text colour. Unknown values fall back to `bubble`. Non-default values add `data-variant`.
- decorative: boolean = false - Hide it from assistive tech (no role, no label text). Use when a parent region already announces the state, as `ChatThread` does.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Rules:
- Put one at the end of a conversation while a reply is being written; in `ChatThread` set `typing` instead of placing it by hand.
- Set `label` to say who is typing ("Mira is typing"); do not leave generic text when the name is known.
- Use `decorative` only when a parent already announces the state.
- Use `Spinner` or `LoadingState` for waits that are not a reply being composed.

Accessibility:
- `role="status"` (polite live region) with a visually hidden label; the three dots are `aria-hidden`, so the label is announced once and the animation is never read.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the dots are static and slightly faded: nothing moves.
- The dots use `currentColor` on the muted token pair, so contrast follows the theme. State is never colour alone: the label carries the meaning.
- With `decorative` it has no role and no text; give the surrounding region the announcement.

Example: Default
```vue
<TypingIndicator />
```

Example: Named, sizes and looks
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
  <TypingIndicator label="Mira is typing" />
  <TypingIndicator size="sm" label="Sample assistant is writing" />
  <p class="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sample assistant <TypingIndicator variant="plain" size="sm" label="Sample assistant is typing" /></p>
</div>
```

# Toaster
group: feedback / Toasts
Fixed-position, screen-reader-announced stack that renders the global toast store.

Mount `<Toaster />` ONCE near the app root (requires Pinia). Choose one of six position presets: `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-right` (default; also exported as `TOASTER_POSITIONS`). Top positions render the newest toast nearest the top edge, bottom positions nearest the bottom. Use `showProgress` for visible countdown bars and `hideIcons` for text-only toasts. Push from anywhere with `useToastStore()`: `push({ title, description, variant, duration, action, key })` or the shortcuts `success/error/warning/info(title, description?)`. At most 5 toasts are visible; a `key` replaces an existing toast instead of stacking. Duration 0 or Infinity makes a toast sticky. With `pauseOnHover` the stack stays visible while hovered or focused (the store timers keep running, so a toast that expired meanwhile lingers until about one second after the pointer leaves).

import { Toaster } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- position: 'top-left' | 'top-center' | 'top-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-center' | 'bottom-right' = 'bottom-right' - Screen corner/edge. Newest toast is nearest the anchored edge. Unknown values fall back to `bottom-right`.
- pauseOnHover: boolean = true - Keep toasts visible while the pointer is over or focus is inside the stack.
- showProgress: boolean = false - Show a countdown bar on every toast with a finite duration. It freezes while the stack is hovered or focused and is hidden under reduced motion.
- hideIcons: boolean = false - Render toasts without their leading status icon.
- layout: 'default' | 'compact' | 'inline' = 'default' - Card layout of every toast: `compact` is dense, `inline` puts the action at the end of the row. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-layout` to the region.
- appearance: 'default' | 'soft' | 'solid' = 'default' - Surface of every toast: popover with a tone border, tinted, or filled with the tone colour. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-appearance` to the region.
- label: string = 'Notifications' - Accessible name of the region.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `Toaster` has a blank `label` (the toast store already throws for a blank toast title).

Rules:
- Mount <Toaster /> exactly once and install Pinia.
- Never create toasts by rendering ToastItem; call useToastStore().
- Use `key` to dedupe repeating messages (e.g. connection errors).
- Choose `position` from the six presets (top|bottom x left|center|right); default is bottom-right.
- Enable `showProgress` only when users benefit from seeing the remaining time; it respects reduced motion.
- Toast titles must be non-empty; the store throws otherwise.

Accessibility:
- The stack is one labelled region (`label`, default "Notifications"). Give every Toaster on a page its own label.
- New toasts are announced once through two persistent hidden live regions inside it: polite for default, success and info, assertive (role="alert") for warning and danger. Only the visible text is read, plus "Actions available" when a toast has an action.
- Toasts never take focus when they appear. Dismiss buttons and actions are real buttons in the tab order.
- Hover or focus inside the stack keeps toasts on screen (WCAG 2.2.1). Escape on a focused toast dismisses it. Dismissing a focused toast moves focus to the next toast, or back to where it was.
- Entry animation and the countdown bar are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. The stack is full width up to `max-w-sm`, so it fits 320px.

Example: Push toasts from the store
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { useToastStore } from '@perfect-design/ui'
const toasts = useToastStore()
</script>

<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.success('Saved', 'Everything is up to date')">Success</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.error('Request failed')">Error</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.push({ title: 'Archived', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} } })">With action</Button>
</div>
<Toaster label="Notifications, basic demo" />
```

Example: Position and sticky toast
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const toasts = useToastStore()
</script>

<Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.push({ title: 'Needs your attention', variant: 'warning', duration: 0, key: 'attention' })">Show sticky warning</Button>
<Toaster label="Notifications, top centre demo" position="top-center" />
```

Example: Six position presets
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const position = ref('bottom-right')
const positions = ['top-left', 'top-center', 'top-right', 'bottom-left', 'bottom-center', 'bottom-right']
</script>

<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Button v-for="p in positions" :key="p" size="sm" :variant="position === p ? 'default' : 'outline'" @click="position = p; toasts.push({ title: p, description: 'Toast position', duration: 3000, key: 'pos-demo' })">{{ p }}</Button>
</div>
<Toaster label="Notifications, position demo" :position="position" />
```

Example: Compact and solid toasts
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const toasts = useToastStore()
</script>

<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.push({ title: 'Copied', variant: 'success', duration: 4000, key: 'copied' })">Compact toast</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.push({ title: 'Archived', duration: 6000, key: 'archived', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} } })">Toast with action</Button>
</div>
<Toaster label="Notifications, compact demo" layout="compact" appearance="solid" position="top-right" />
```

Example: Progress bars
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const toasts = useToastStore()
</script>

<Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.push({ title: 'Report exported', description: 'Closing in 6 seconds', variant: 'success', duration: 6000 })">Show toast with countdown</Button>
<Toaster label="Notifications, countdown demo" show-progress />
```

Example: Without icons
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const toasts = useToastStore()
</script>

<Button variant="outline" @click="toasts.push({ title: 'Copied to clipboard', duration: 3000 })">Show text-only toast</Button>
<Toaster label="Notifications, text-only demo" hide-icons position="top-right" />
```

# ToastItem
group: feedback / Toasts
Presentational toast card: icon, title, description, optional action and dismiss button.

You normally do not render `ToastItem` yourself: push toasts with `useToastStore()` and mount `<Toaster />` once. Use `ToastItem` directly to build a custom toast host or to show a static preview of a toast. Options: leave the status icon on (default), replace it with `icon`, or remove it with `hideIcon`; add a draining countdown bar with `progress` + `duration` (frozen by `paused`, hidden under reduced motion; it only visualises time, dismissal is owned by the store/Toaster). Note that `Toast` is the store item type, which is why the component is named `ToastItem`.

import { ToastItem } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- title*: string - Main message.
- description: string - Secondary text.
- variant: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'default' - Tone (same names as the toast store). Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- layout: 'default' | 'compact' | 'inline' = 'default' - `default` puts the action under the text; `compact` is a dense card with smaller type and padding; `inline` keeps the size and moves the action to the end of the row. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-layout`.
- appearance: 'default' | 'soft' | 'solid' = 'default' - `default` is the popover surface with a tone border; `soft` is tinted; `solid` is filled with the tone colour and its foreground token (icon, text, progress bar and dismiss follow the text colour). Unknown values fall back to `default`. Non-default values add `data-appearance`.
- action: { label: string; onClick: () => void } - Action button. Clicking it runs `onClick`, then emits `action` and `dismiss`.
- icon: IconDefinition - Replaces the default status icon of the variant (colour still follows the variant).
- hideIcon: boolean = false - Render without the leading icon. Wins over `icon`.
- progress: boolean = false - Show a countdown bar along the bottom edge that drains over `duration`. Needs a finite `duration` > 0; otherwise no bar is rendered.
- duration: number - Countdown length in ms for the progress bar. The component never dismisses itself; keep it in sync with the store duration.
- announce: boolean = true - Make the toast its own live region (role status or alert). Toaster sets it to false and announces through one persistent region.
- paused: boolean = false - Freezes the progress bar (Toaster sets it while the stack is hovered or focused).
- dismissLabel: string = 'Dismiss notification' - Accessible label of the close button.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- dismiss [] - Close button or action was used.
- action [] - Action button clicked (after `action.onClick`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `ToastItem` has a blank `title`, a blank `dismissLabel` or an `action` with a blank `label`.

Rules:
- Use `layout="compact"` for dense UIs and `appearance="solid"` only for toasts that must not be missed.
- Prefer useToastStore().push()/success()/error() over rendering ToastItem manually.
- Use `hideIcon` for terse confirmations and `progress` only when users benefit from seeing the remaining time (undo windows).
- Keep toast titles short; put detail in `description`.

Accessibility:
- Standalone, it is its own live region: role="status" for default, success and info, role="alert" for warning and danger. Inside a `Toaster`, `announce` is off and the Toaster announces instead.
- The dismiss button has an aria-label, is 28px square and 40px on coarse pointers. The action is a real <button>.
- Every layout and appearance keeps the title, the action and the dismiss button as real buttons with names; the status icon and the title carry the tone, the border or fill only supports it. Solid uses each tone with its foreground token.
- The progress bar is aria-hidden decoration (time is never the only cue). It is hidden under prefers-reduced-motion and its animation is cancelled on unmount.

Example: Variants
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <ToastItem title="Settings saved" description="Your changes are live." variant="success" />
  <ToastItem title="Connection lost" variant="danger" />
  <ToastItem title="Update available" variant="info" />
</div>
```

Example: With action
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { faBell } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
const undone = ref(false)
</script>

<div class="max-w-sm">
  <ToastItem title="Item archived" :action="{ label: 'Undo', onClick: () => (undone = true) }" />
  <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Undone: {{ undone }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Layout and appearance
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const clicks = ref(0)
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <ToastItem title="Copied" layout="compact" variant="success" />
  <ToastItem title="Item archived" layout="inline" :action="{ label: 'Undo', onClick: () => clicks++ }" />
  <ToastItem title="Draft saved" description="Soft surface." appearance="soft" variant="info" />
  <ToastItem title="Upload failed" description="Solid surface, text follows the tone foreground." appearance="solid" variant="danger" :action="{ label: 'Retry', onClick: () => clicks++ }" />
</div>
```

Example: Without icon
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2"><ToastItem title="Copied to clipboard" hide-icon /><ToastItem title="Export finished" description="3 files, 12 MB." variant="success" hide-icon /></div>
```

Example: Custom icon
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faBell } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<div class="max-w-sm"><ToastItem title="New reminder" variant="info" :icon="faBell" /></div>
```

Example: Progress countdown
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const paused = ref(false)
</script>

<div class="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
  <ToastItem title="Message sent" description="Undo within 8 seconds." variant="success" progress :duration="8000" :paused="paused" />
  <ToastItem title="Sync failed" variant="danger" progress :duration="8000" :paused="paused" />
  <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="paused = !paused">{{ paused ? 'Resume' : 'Pause' }} countdown</Button>
</div>
```

# HoverCard
group: overlays / Floating
Rich preview card that appears when hovering or focusing a link or element.

Compose `HoverCard` + `HoverCardTrigger` + `HoverCardContent`. Use for previews of the thing a link points at (user profile, repo summary). Opens after `openDelay` (700ms) and stays open while the pointer is over the card. It is supplementary and hover-driven, so it must never be the only way to reach information (touch devices do not open it). Width and padding come from `size` on `HoverCardContent` (`sm` w-52, `md` w-64 default, `lg` w-80, `xl` w-96, `auto` fits the content; all capped to the viewport width). `variant` (`neutral` | `inverted`) sets the colours and `showArrow` adds an arrow that points at the trigger (off by default). `hoverCardContentVariants` is exported for reuse. Use `Popover` for click-driven interactive panels and `Tooltip` for one-line hints.

import { HoverCard, HoverCardTrigger, HoverCardContent } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- enableTouch: boolean - Also open the card on touch input (reka-ui). Off by default because hover cards have no touch equivalent.
- open: boolean - Controlled open state (v-model:open).
- defaultOpen: boolean = false - Initial state when uncontrolled.
- openDelay: number = 700 - Delay in ms before opening on hover.
- closeDelay: number = 300 - Delay in ms before closing after leaving.

Parts:
- HoverCardTrigger - Element that triggers the card; renders an <a> by default.
- HoverCardContent - Portalled floating surface. Attributes fall through.
    - side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' = 'bottom' - Preferred side.
    - align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'center' - Alignment along the side axis.
    - sideOffset: number = 6 - Gap in px between trigger and card.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'auto' = 'md' - Width and padding preset (unknown values fall back to md).
    - variant: 'neutral' | 'inverted' = 'neutral' - Surface colours (unknown values fall back to neutral). Adds data-variant when inverted.
    - showArrow: boolean = false - Render an arrow that points at the trigger (decorative, aria-hidden).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged onto the surface (wins over the size preset).

Slots:
- default - HoverCardTrigger and HoverCardContent.

Events:
- update:open [value: boolean] - Open state changed.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the element a `HoverCardTrigger` renders is not keyboard focusable (a link needs `href`) or has no accessible name.

Rules:
- Hover cards are supplementary previews only; the trigger link must work on its own.
- Use Popover when the user needs to interact with the content.
- HoverCardTrigger renders <a>; pass as-child to wrap your own element.
- Choose width with size (sm/md/lg/xl/auto) instead of w-* classes; unknown size/variant values fall back to md/neutral. show-arrow is off by default.

Accessibility:
- Also opens on keyboard focus of the trigger. Esc dismisses it.
- The card is hoverable: the pointer can move onto it without it closing (WCAG 1.4.13).
- Touch devices do not open it. Do not hide essential content here, and keep the trigger a real link or button.
- The inverted variant uses foreground and background colours: keep the content to plain text. The arrow is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- The card is capped at the available height and the viewport width, and scrolls when it has to.

Example: Profile preview
```vue
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger href="/components" class="text-sm font-medium underline underline-offset-4">Sample user</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent class="space-y-1">
    <p class="text-sm font-semibold">Sample user</p>
    <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Profile preview text appears here.</p>
    <Badge>Admin</Badge>
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

Example: Sizes, variants and arrow
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
  <HoverCard v-for="size in ['sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', 'auto']" :key="size">
    <HoverCardTrigger href="#sizes" class="text-sm underline underline-offset-4">size {{ size }}</HoverCardTrigger>
    <HoverCardContent :size="size"><p class="text-sm">Hover card size {{ size }}.</p></HoverCardContent>
  </HoverCard>
  <HoverCard>
    <HoverCardTrigger href="#inverted" class="text-sm underline underline-offset-4">inverted</HoverCardTrigger>
    <HoverCardContent variant="inverted" size="sm"><p class="text-sm">Inverted surface.</p></HoverCardContent>
  </HoverCard>
  <HoverCard>
    <HoverCardTrigger href="#arrow" class="text-sm underline underline-offset-4">with arrow</HoverCardTrigger>
    <HoverCardContent show-arrow size="sm"><p class="text-sm">Arrow points at the trigger.</p></HoverCardContent>
  </HoverCard>
</div>
```

Example: Custom delays and placement
```vue
<HoverCard :open-delay="100" :close-delay="100">
  <HoverCardTrigger as-child><Button variant="link">Quick preview</Button></HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent side="right" align="start" class="w-80">
    <p class="text-sm">Opens fast, to the right of the trigger.</p>
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

# Popover
group: overlays / Floating
Non-modal floating panel anchored to a trigger. Compound component built on reka-ui.

Compose `Popover` + `PopoverTrigger` + `PopoverContent` (+ `PopoverAnchor`, `PopoverClose`). Use for small interactive content (quick forms, pickers, option lists) that should stay in context. Width is set with `size` on `PopoverContent`: `xs` (w-48, tiny menus), `sm` (w-60, short option lists), `md` (w-72, default, quick forms), `lg` (w-96, pickers and richer forms), `xl` (w-lg, previews, dense panels), `auto` (fits content; for chips or short summaries); every size is capped to the viewport width and `class` can still override it. `variant` (`neutral` | `inverted`) sets the colours: `neutral` is the popover surface, `inverted` is the foreground colour with background-coloured text, like the default tooltip. `showArrow` draws an arrow that points at the trigger (off by default). `popoverContentVariants` is exported for reuse. Placement is controlled with `side`, `align` and `sideOffset` on `PopoverContent`; it flips automatically near viewport edges. Use `Tooltip` for plain text hints, `HoverCard` for hover previews, `DropdownMenu` for action lists and `Dialog` for modal flows.

import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, PopoverAnchor, PopoverClose } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- open: boolean - Controlled open state (v-model:open).
- defaultOpen: boolean = false - Initial state when uncontrolled.
- modal: boolean = false - Trap focus and block outside interaction.

Parts:
- PopoverTrigger - Toggles the popover (use as-child on a Button).
- PopoverContent - Portalled floating surface. Attributes fall through.
    - side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' = 'bottom' - Preferred side of the trigger.
    - align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'center' - Alignment along the side axis.
    - sideOffset: number = 6 - Gap in px between trigger and content.
    - alignOffset: number = 0 - Offset in px along the alignment axis.
    - size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'auto' = 'md' - Width and padding preset (unknown values fall back to md).
    - variant: 'neutral' | 'inverted' = 'neutral' - Surface colours (unknown values fall back to neutral). Adds data-variant when inverted.
    - showArrow: boolean = false - Render an arrow that points at the trigger (decorative, aria-hidden).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged onto the surface (wins over the size preset).
- PopoverAnchor - Optional element to position against instead of the trigger.
- PopoverClose - Closes the popover; use as-child on a Button.

Slots:
- default - PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent and optionally PopoverAnchor.

Events:
- update:open [value: boolean] - Open state changed.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the element a `PopoverTrigger` renders has no accessible name (an icon-only button needs `aria-label`).

Rules:
- Use PopoverTrigger as-child on a Button so it stays a real button.
- Popover content is interactive; use Tooltip for non-interactive text.
- Choose width with size (xs/sm/md/lg/xl/auto) instead of hand-written w-* classes; unknown values fall back to md.
- A class on PopoverContent (class="w-96") still overrides the preset.
- variant="inverted" suits short summaries; put interactive forms on the neutral surface. show-arrow is off by default; unknown variants fall back to neutral.

Accessibility:
- Trigger gets aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- Esc and an outside press close it. Focus moves into the content and returns to the trigger.
- Content is role=dialog: give it an aria-label when it has no visible heading.
- The inverted variant uses foreground and background colours: keep the content to plain text and do not use muted text colours inside it. The arrow is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- The content keeps 8px from the viewport edges, never exceeds the viewport width and scrolls when taller than the available space.

Example: Basic
```vue
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">Dimensions</Button></PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent class="space-y-3">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium">Set dimensions</p>
    <Input placeholder="Width" aria-label="Width" />
    <Input placeholder="Height" aria-label="Height" />
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Popover v-for="size in ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', 'auto']" :key="size">
    <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">{{ size }}</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent :size="size">
      <p class="text-sm">Popover size {{ size }}</p>
    </PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
</div>
```

Example: Variants and arrow
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">Neutral</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent size="sm"><p class="text-sm">Neutral surface, no arrow.</p></PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">Neutral with arrow</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent size="sm" show-arrow><p class="text-sm">Neutral surface with an arrow.</p></PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">Inverted</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent size="sm" variant="inverted"><p class="text-sm">Inverted surface, no arrow.</p></PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">Inverted with arrow</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent size="sm" variant="inverted" show-arrow><p class="text-sm">Inverted surface with an arrow.</p></PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
</div>
```

Example: Placement and controlled state
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
</script>

<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Popover v-model:open="open">
    <PopoverTrigger as-child><Button>Options</Button></PopoverTrigger>
    <PopoverContent side="right" align="start" :side-offset="10">
      <p class="mb-2 text-sm">Opens to the right, aligned to the top.</p>
      <PopoverClose as-child><Button size="sm" variant="secondary">Close</Button></PopoverClose>
    </PopoverContent>
  </Popover>
  <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">open = {{ open }}</span>
</div>
```

# Tooltip
group: overlays / Floating
Short text hint shown on hover or keyboard focus. Compound component plus a one-line `SimpleTooltip`.

Use `SimpleTooltip` with a `content` prop for the common case, or compose `TooltipProvider` + `Tooltip` + `TooltipTrigger` + `TooltipContent` for full control. Wrap the app (or a region) in one `TooltipProvider` to share the open delay and get instant hand-off between neighbouring tooltips; `SimpleTooltip` includes its own provider. Variations: `variant` (`dark` inverted bubble, the default and best contrast on light pages; `light` popover-coloured bubble with border and shadow, for dark surfaces or when an inverted bubble feels heavy) and `size` (`sm` compact labels for dense toolbars, `md` default, `lg` roomier text for longer hints). Both are props of `TooltipContent` and `SimpleTooltip`; `tooltipVariants` is exported for reuse. Tooltips are for supplementary, non-interactive text only; never hide essential information in one. Use `Popover` or `HoverCard` for interactive content.

import { Tooltip, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent, SimpleTooltip } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- disableClosingTrigger: boolean - Keep the tooltip open when the trigger is clicked (reka-ui).
- ignoreNonKeyboardFocus: boolean - Open on keyboard focus only, not on pointer focus (reka-ui).
- open: boolean - Tooltip root: controlled open state (v-model:open).
- defaultOpen: boolean = false - Tooltip root: initial state when uncontrolled.
- delayDuration: number - Tooltip root: hover delay in ms; overrides the provider value.
- disabled: boolean = false - Tooltip root: never show the tooltip.
- disableHoverableContent: boolean = false - Tooltip root: close when the pointer leaves the trigger even if it moves onto the content.

Parts:
- TooltipProvider - Shares timing between tooltips; mount once near the app root.
    - delayDuration: number = 400 - Hover delay in ms before opening.
    - skipDelayDuration: number = 300 - Window in ms after closing during which the next tooltip opens instantly.
    - disableHoverableContent: boolean = false - Prevent the pointer from entering the content.
- TooltipTrigger - Element that triggers the tooltip (use as-child on the target).
- TooltipContent - Portalled bubble with arrow. Attributes fall through.
    - side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' = 'top' - Preferred side.
    - align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'center' - Alignment along the side axis.
    - sideOffset: number = 6 - Gap in px between trigger and bubble.
    - showArrow: boolean = true - Render the arrow.
    - variant: 'dark' | 'light' = 'dark' - Bubble look (unknown values fall back to dark). The arrow follows the variant.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, text size and max width (unknown values fall back to md).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged onto the bubble (wins over variant classes).
- SimpleTooltip - Wraps its default slot (a single element) with a tooltip showing `content`. Has its own provider.
    - content: string - Tooltip text. Without content (and without the `content` slot) the tooltip is disabled.
    - side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' = 'top' - Preferred side.
    - align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'center' - Alignment.
    - delayDuration: number = 400 - Hover delay in ms.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Never show the tooltip.
    - variant: 'dark' | 'light' = 'dark' - Bubble look.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Bubble size.
    - showArrow: boolean = true - Render the arrow that points at the trigger.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged onto the bubble.

Slots:
- default - TooltipTrigger and TooltipContent.

Events:
- update:open [value: boolean] - Tooltip root: open state changed.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `Tooltip` has no `TooltipProvider` around it (use `SimpleTooltip` or mount one provider near the app root). It still renders with a fallback provider.
- Throws a ContractError when `TooltipTrigger` or `TooltipContent` is not inside a `Tooltip`.
- Throws a ContractError when the element a `TooltipTrigger` renders cannot be reached with the keyboard (a span or div without `tabindex="0"`) or has no accessible name (an icon-only button without `aria-label`).

Rules:
- Use variant="light" on dark or busy surfaces where the inverted bubble blends in; keep the default dark elsewhere.
- Use size="sm" for dense toolbars and size="lg" only for longer hints; unknown variant/size values fall back to dark/md.
- Prefer <SimpleTooltip content="..."> for plain text.
- The trigger must be a single focusable element; tooltips on disabled buttons need a wrapper element.
- Do not use a tooltip as the only label of an icon-only button; add aria-label as well.
- TooltipContent must be inside Tooltip; Tooltip must be inside TooltipProvider (SimpleTooltip handles this itself).

Accessibility:
- Trigger gets aria-describedby pointing at the tooltip (role=tooltip).
- Opens on keyboard focus as well as hover and Esc dismisses it. The tooltip stays open while the pointer is on it (WCAG 1.4.13).
- Never put interactive controls or essential information in a tooltip. Icon-only buttons still need an aria-label.
- The bubble gets a border in forced-colors mode and keeps 8px from the viewport edges.

Example: SimpleTooltip
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <SimpleTooltip content="Save your changes"><Button>Save</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="Shown on the right" side="right"><Button variant="outline">Right</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="Never shown" disabled><Button variant="ghost">Disabled</Button></SimpleTooltip>
</div>
```

Example: Variants: dark and light
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <SimpleTooltip content="Dark (default) bubble" variant="dark"><Button variant="outline">Dark</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="Light bubble with border" variant="light"><Button variant="outline">Light</Button></SimpleTooltip>
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <SimpleTooltip content="Small" size="sm"><Button variant="outline" size="sm">sm</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="Medium (default)" size="md"><Button variant="outline">md</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="Large tooltips fit longer explanatory text comfortably" size="lg"><Button variant="outline" size="lg">lg</Button></SimpleTooltip>
</div>
```

Example: Without an arrow
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
  <SimpleTooltip content="Arrow (default)"><Button variant="outline">With arrow</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="No arrow" :show-arrow="false"><Button variant="outline">No arrow</Button></SimpleTooltip>
  <SimpleTooltip content="Light, no arrow" variant="light" :show-arrow="false"><Button variant="outline">Light, no arrow</Button></SimpleTooltip>
</div>
```

Example: Compound with variant and size
```vue
<TooltipProvider>
  <Tooltip>
    <TooltipTrigger as-child><Button variant="ghost">Compound</Button></TooltipTrigger>
    <TooltipContent variant="light" size="lg" side="bottom">Light, large, below the trigger.</TooltipContent>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipProvider>
```

Example: Compound with shared provider
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { faCircleInfo } from '@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons'
</script>

<TooltipProvider :delay-duration="200">
  <div class="flex items-center gap-3">
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger as-child>
        <Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Help"><Icon :icon="faCircleInfo" /></Button>
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent side="bottom">Opens the help centre</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger as-child><Button variant="outline">Custom</Button></TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent :show-arrow="false" class="max-w-sm">No arrow, wider bubble.</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  </div>
</TooltipProvider>
```

# Tour
group: overlays / Guided tours
Step-by-step coach marks that spotlight page elements and explain them in a positioned card.

Use `Tour` for first-run onboarding and feature announcements. Each step points at an element (`target`: CSS selector, element or getter); a spotlight dims the page around it and a card with title, description, progress and Back/Next/Skip/Finish controls is placed on the requested side, flipping and clamping to stay inside the viewport. Steps whose target element is missing or hidden show a centred card without a spotlight, so a tour never breaks when the UI changes; pass `target: null` for a step that is centred on purpose. The tour renders nothing while closed. Control it with `v-model:open` and `v-model:step`, or leave both uncontrolled and call the exposed `start()`. The overlay is teleported to `body` (disable with `:teleport="false"`). It does not lock page scroll. `variant` changes the card: `compact` tightens the padding and gap and sets the description in small text; `dots` replaces the "2 / 5" text with one dot per step (the text stays for screen readers). For a single anchored hint use `Popover`; for blocking decisions use `Dialog`.

import { Tour } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- steps: TourStep[] = [] - Ordered steps: `{ target, title, description?, placement? }`. `title` is required. `target` is a selector string, HTMLElement or `() => HTMLElement | null`, or `null` for a step that is meant to be centred. An empty list renders nothing.
- open: boolean - Whether the tour shows (v-model:open). Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultOpen: boolean = false - Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- step: number - Zero-based current step (v-model:step). Clamped into range; NaN becomes 0. Uncontrolled when omitted.
- defaultStep: number = 0 - Initial step when uncontrolled.
- placement: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' = 'bottom' - Default card side. A step `placement` overrides it. Flips to the opposite side when it does not fit.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Card width (16, 20 or 24rem, capped to the viewport). Unknown values fall back to md.
- variant: 'default' | 'compact' | 'dots' = 'default' - Card look: compact is tighter, dots shows one dot per step instead of the progress text (unknown values fall back to default). Adds data-variant when not default.
- offset: number = 12 - Gap in px between spotlight and card.
- padding: number = 6 - Extra px of spotlight around the target.
- showProgress: boolean = true - Show the "2 / 5" progress text.
- showSkip: boolean = true - Show Skip (hidden on the last step).
- closeOnEscape: boolean = true - Esc skips the tour.
- closeOnOverlayClick: boolean = false - Clicking the dimmed backdrop skips the tour.
- scrollIntoView: boolean = true - Scroll the target to the centre when its step shows (instant under reduced motion).
- teleport: boolean = true - Teleport the overlay to `body`; false renders in place.
- nextLabel: string = 'Next' - Next button label.
- prevLabel: string = 'Back' - Back button label.
- skipLabel: string = 'Skip' - Skip button label.
- finishLabel: string = 'Finish' - Label of the Next button on the last step.
- progressFormat: (current: number, total: number) => string = `${current} / ${total}` - Builds the progress text (1-based). Use it to localise.
- cardClass: string | object | array - Extra classes for the card, merged last.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the overlay root (`data-slot="tour"`).

Slots:
- title ({ step: TourStep, index: number, total: number }) - Replace the step title content.
- description ({ step: TourStep, index: number, total: number }) - Replace the step description content (rendered even when the step has none).

Events:
- update:open [value: boolean] - Open state changed (v-model:open).
- update:step [value: number] - Step changed (v-model:step). Reset to 0 on skip/finish.
- next [index: number] - Moved forward; payload is the new index.
- prev [index: number] - Moved back; payload is the new index.
- skip [index: number] - Dismissed early (Skip, Esc, backdrop); payload is the step it was skipped at.
- finish - Next pressed on the last step.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a step has no `title` (or a `title` slot), when a step has no `target` (use `target: null` for a deliberately centred step), or when the tour dialog ends up without an accessible name. It is checked each time the tour opens.

Rules:
- Bind `v-model:open` (and optionally `v-model:step`); the tour renders nothing until open.
- Give targets stable ids or pass a getter; a `target` that does not match an element degrades to a centred card, never an error; a step with no `target` key at all throws, so use `target: null` for a centred step.
- Keep titles short and put detail in `description`; do not put interactive content in the card.
- Use variant="compact" for short steps and variant="dots" for long tours where the count matters less than position; unknown size/variant values fall back to md/default.
- Prefer `placement` on the step for tricky layouts; the card auto-flips and clamps to the viewport.
- Tour does not lock scroll and does not block keyboard shortcuts of the page other than Esc/Arrow keys while open.

Accessibility:
- The card is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` (title) and `aria-describedby` (description and the progress text).
- Focus moves to the card on open and on every step change, so the new step is announced. Tab and Shift+Tab are trapped inside the card and focus returns to the previously focused element on close.
- Esc skips, ArrowRight goes next (Finish on the last step), ArrowLeft goes back.
- With `variant="dots"` the dots are `aria-hidden` and the progress text stays in the DOM for assistive technology (the active dot is also filled, not only coloured).
- The spotlight and the opaque scrim panels are `aria-hidden`. The spotlight outline stays visible in forced-colors mode. Motion is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion` and smooth scrolling falls back to instant.
- The page is not scroll-locked and no body styles are touched. Listeners are removed on close and unmount. The card is capped at the viewport width minus 1rem.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const open = ref(false)
const step = ref(0)
const steps = [
  { target: '#tour-demo-search', title: 'Search', description: 'Find anything in your workspace.' },
  { target: '#tour-demo-create', title: 'Create', description: 'Start a new project from here.', placement: 'right' },
  { target: '#tour-demo-missing', title: 'All set', description: 'This step has no target, so the card is centred.' },
]
</script>

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <Button size="sm" @click="open = true">Take the tour</Button>
  <input id="tour-demo-search" class="min-w-0 rounded-md border px-2 py-1 text-sm" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
  <Button id="tour-demo-create" size="sm" variant="outline">Create</Button>
</div>
<Tour v-model:open="open" v-model:step="step" :steps="steps" />
```

Example: Events and custom labels
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

const log = ref('')
const steps = [
  { target: '#tour-demo-badge', title: 'New badge', description: 'Marks fresh features.', placement: 'top' },
  { target: null, title: 'Welcome', description: 'A step with target null is centred.' },
]
</script>

<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Button size="sm" @click="tour.start()">Start</Button>
  <span id="tour-demo-badge" class="rounded-full bg-muted px-2 py-0.5 text-xs">New</span>
  <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ log || 'No events yet' }}</span>
</div>
<Tour ref="tour" :steps="steps" next-label="Continue" prev-label="Previous" finish-label="Done" skip-label="Not now"
  :progress-format="(c, t) => 'Step ' + c + ' of ' + t"
  @next="log = 'next ' + $event" @prev="log = 'prev ' + $event" @skip="log = 'skipped at ' + $event" @finish="log = 'finished'" />
```

Example: Size: sm
```vue

</script>

<Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="open = true">Small card</Button>
<span id="tour-demo-sm" class="ml-3 text-sm">Anchor</span>

```

```vue
</script>

<Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="open = true">Compact card</Button>
<span id="tour-demo-compact" class="ml-3 text-sm">Anchor</span>
```
