# Breadcrumb
group: navigation / Wayfinding
Shows the path to the current page. Items-array API or compound parts, with middle-item truncation.

Pass `items` (the last item is the current page) for the common case, or compose `BreadcrumbList` / `BreadcrumbItem` / `BreadcrumbLink` / `BreadcrumbSeparator` / `BreadcrumbPage` / `BreadcrumbEllipsis` for full control. `maxItems` collapses middle items behind an ellipsis button that expands on click. For client-side routing pass `link-as` a RouterLink (it receives `to`) or use `BreadcrumbLink as-child` in compound mode. Do not use for step flows (`Stepper`) or in-page sections (`TableOfContents`).

import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbSeparator, BreadcrumbPage, BreadcrumbEllipsis } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: BreadcrumbItemData[] - Items `{ label, href?, to?, icon? }`. Last item renders as the current page. Malformed entries are skipped.
- maxItems: number = 0 - Collapse middle items when there are more than this many (first item + ellipsis + last maxItems-1). 0 disables; 1 is raised to 2.
- linkAs: string | Component - Component/element for links, e.g. RouterLink (receives `to`).
- label: string = 'Breadcrumb' - aria-label of the nav landmark.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size and gap of the trail. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- separator: 'chevron' | 'slash' | 'dot' = 'chevron' - Glyph between entries. Compound `BreadcrumbSeparator` parts follow it too. The `separator` slot replaces it. Unknown values fall back to `chevron`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged onto the nav.

Parts:
- BreadcrumbList - `<ol>` wrapper for items and separators.
- BreadcrumbItem - `<li>` wrapper for one link, page or ellipsis.
- BreadcrumbLink - Link to an ancestor.
    - href: string - URL.
    - to: string | object - Router target, forwarded when `as` is a component.
    - as: string | Component = 'a' - Element or component.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single child.
- BreadcrumbSeparator - Decorative `<li role="presentation" aria-hidden>`; shows the glyph chosen with `separator` on `Breadcrumb` (chevron by default), accepts a slot.
- BreadcrumbPage - Current page: `aria-current="page"`, not a link.
- BreadcrumbEllipsis - Button standing in for hidden items.
    - label: string = 'Show hidden items' - Accessible name.

Slots:
- default - Compound parts, used when `items` is empty.
- separator - Replaces the chevron between items.
- link ({ item: BreadcrumbItemData, index: number }) - Custom link rendering per non-current item.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `label` is blank, because it names the nav landmark.
- Throws a ContractError when no `BreadcrumbPage` (the current page) is rendered; in `items` mode the last item is the current page, so an empty `items` throws too.
- Throws a ContractError when a `BreadcrumbLink` has no `href` or `to` (unless `as-child` or a non-anchor `as` is used).
- Throws a ContractError when a `BreadcrumbLink` has no accessible name (text or `aria-label`).

Rules:
- The last entry of `items` is the current page and is not a link.
- For RouterLink use `link-as`, never onClick + router.push.
- Use `max-items` (not CSS) to handle long trails.

Accessibility:
- `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` containing an ordered list. Pass a distinct `label` when a page holds more than one trail.
- `size` and `separator` only change the look: the separators stay `aria-hidden` for every glyph, so a slash or dot is never read out, and the current page is still marked with aria-current.
- Current page has aria-current="page"; separators are aria-hidden and flip in RTL.
- The ellipsis is a real button whose label states how many items are hidden; it is 24px (40px on coarse pointers). Links show an underline on hover and sit on a wrapping list, so long trails reflow at 320px.

Example: Items API
```vue
<div @click.prevent>
  <Breadcrumb label="Items breadcrumb" :items="[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/', icon: faHouse },
    { label: 'Components', href: '/components' },
    { label: 'Breadcrumb' },
  ]" />
</div>
```

Example: Truncated trail
```vue
<div @click.prevent>
  <Breadcrumb label="Truncated breadcrumb" :max-items="4" :items="[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Components', href: '/components' },
    { label: 'Navigation', href: '/components/navigation' },
    { label: 'Level four', href: '/components/navigation' },
    { label: 'Level five', href: '/components/navigation' },
    { label: 'Breadcrumb' },
  ]" />
</div>
```

Example: Separators
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3" @click.prevent>
  <Breadcrumb v-for="kind in ['chevron', 'slash', 'dot']" :key="kind" :label="'Separator ' + kind" :separator="kind" :items="[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Components', href: '/components' },
    { label: kind },
  ]" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-3" @click.prevent>
  <Breadcrumb v-for="size in ['sm', 'md', 'lg']" :key="size" :label="'Size ' + size" :size="size" separator="slash" :items="[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Components', href: '/components' },
    { label: 'Size ' + size },
  ]" />
</div>
```

Example: Compound parts
```vue
<div @click.prevent>
  <Breadcrumb label="Compound breadcrumb">
    <BreadcrumbList>
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbSeparator />
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/components">Components</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbSeparator />
      <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
    </BreadcrumbList>
  </Breadcrumb>
</div>
```

# BoardCard
group: data-display / Boards
Draggable card for a BoardColumn, with a keyboard alternative (Alt + arrow keys) to dragging.

Presentational card that starts a native HTML5 drag. On `dragstart` it writes `{ id, from }` (JSON, custom MIME type) to `dataTransfer` and marks itself `dragging`; `BoardColumn` reads that on drop. Inside a `BoardColumn` it learns its source column automatically, or set `columnId` yourself. Because dragging is pointer-only, a focused card also emits `move` with a direction when you press Alt + an arrow key: apply it to your data (left/right = other column, up/down = reorder). `disabled` blocks both. The card has no drag logic beyond this and no state of its own: you keep the board data.

import { BoardCard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- id*: string - Unique card id, sent in the drag payload and `move` events.
- columnId: string - Column the card lives in. Defaults to the id of the enclosing `BoardColumn`.
- title: string - Optional heading above the default slot.
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'flat' = 'default' - Card surface.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and text size.
- disabled: boolean = false - Not draggable, no keyboard move, dimmed, `aria-disabled`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ dragging: boolean }) - Card body; `dragging` is true between dragstart and dragend.

Events:
- dragstart [cardId: string] - Drag started (not emitted when disabled).
- dragend [cardId: string] - Drag finished, dropped or cancelled.
- move [request: { cardId: string; direction: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right"; from?: string }] - Alt + Arrow key pressed on the focused card (keyboard alternative to dragging). Not emitted when disabled or when the key comes from a nested control.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `BoardCard` has a blank `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `BoardCard` is not inside a list: use a `BoardColumn`, or a parent with `role="list"` (a `ul` or `ol` also counts).
- Throws a ContractError when two cards on the same board share an `id` (the board is the element that holds the columns).

Rules:
- Always handle the `move` event (Alt+Arrow) in addition to the column `move`, otherwise keyboard users cannot reorder.
- Card ids must be unique across the whole board, not just within a column.
- Place BoardCard only inside BoardColumn (or another `role="list"`).
- Put interactive content (buttons, links) in the body freely; keyboard shortcuts only fire when the card itself is focused.

Accessibility:
- Each card is a focusable `listitem` (`tabindex="0"`) that must live inside a list: `BoardColumn` provides `role="list"`, and a standalone card needs a `role="list"` parent (axe `aria-required-parent`).
- Keyboard alternative to dragging: Alt + Arrow keys emit `move`; `aria-keyshortcuts` advertises it and a visually hidden description ("Hold Alt and press an arrow key to move this card.") is linked with `aria-describedby`. Keys typed inside nested inputs/buttons are ignored.
- After applying a move, return focus to the card (cards re-mount when they change column) and announce the result with the column `announce(message)` method.
- Disabled cards set `draggable="false"` and `aria-disabled`.
- Dragging is indicated with `data-dragging` plus opacity, shadow and ring, not colour alone.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<BoardColumn id="todo" title="To do" class="w-64">
  <BoardCard id="a" title="Write docs">Cover the keyboard flow.</BoardCard>
</BoardColumn>
```

Example: Keyboard move requests
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const last = ref('none')
function onMove(r) { last.value = r.direction + ' from ' + r.from }
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <BoardColumn id="todo" title="To do" class="w-64">
    <BoardCard id="k1" title="Focus me" @move="onMove" />
  </BoardColumn>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Last request: {{ last }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<div role="list" aria-label="Card variants" class="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
  <BoardCard id="v1" variant="default" title="Default" class="w-40" />
  <BoardCard id="v2" variant="outline" title="Outline" class="w-40" />
  <BoardCard id="v3" variant="flat" title="Flat" class="w-40" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div role="list" aria-label="Card sizes" class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-3">
  <BoardCard id="s1" size="sm" title="Small" class="w-36" />
  <BoardCard id="s2" size="md" title="Medium" class="w-40" />
  <BoardCard id="s3" size="lg" title="Large" class="w-44" />
</div>
```

Example: Disabled and dragging slot prop
```vue
<div role="list" aria-label="Disabled and movable cards" class="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
  <BoardCard id="d1" title="Locked" disabled class="w-44">Cannot be moved.</BoardCard>
  <BoardCard id="d2" title="Movable" class="w-44">
    <template #default="{ dragging }">{{ dragging ? 'Moving...' : 'Drag me' }}</template>
  </BoardCard>
</div>
```

# BoardColumn
group: data-display / Boards
Kanban-style column that accepts dragged BoardCards and reports where they were dropped.

Presentational drop zone built on native HTML5 drag events. `BoardColumn` shows a title, a count badge, optional header/footer and an empty state, highlights while a card hovers over it and emits `move` with `{ cardId, from, to, index }`. It never mutates anything: you own the data and apply the move. Pair it with `BoardCard`, which is the draggable part and also provides a keyboard alternative. Cards dragged from a column know their source column automatically, so `acceptFrom` can restrict flows (for example "Done" only accepts from "In progress"). Drops of files, text or any foreign data are ignored. For sortable lists without columns use a plain list; for touch-first drag and drop add your own pointer-based layer, native HTML5 drag is mouse/desktop oriented.

import { BoardColumn } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- id*: string - Unique column id. Sent as `to` in `move` and provided to child cards as their `from`.
- title: string - Column heading (also labels the group for assistive tech). Required unless the column has `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- count: number - Number in the badge. Defaults to the number of cards in the default slot; negative/NaN values fall back to that. Set it when the list is paginated or virtualised.
- showCount: boolean = true - Show the count badge.
- emptyText: string = 'No cards' - Empty-state text; override with the `empty` slot.
- acceptFrom: string[] - Only accept cards coming from these column ids. Cards already in this column (reordering) are always accepted; cards of unknown origin are rejected when this is set. Empty/undefined accepts everything.
- disabled: boolean = false - Reject every drop, never highlight, dim the column.
- variant: 'default' | 'muted' | 'outline' = 'default' - Column surface.
- headingLevel: number = 3 - Heading level of the column title, 2 to 6. Other values fall back to 3.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap and text size.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes (set the column width here, e.g. `w-72`).

Slots:
- default - `BoardCard` children.
- header ({ title: string | undefined; count: number; over: boolean }) - Replaces the title and count badge.
- footer ({ count: number; over: boolean }) - Rendered below the cards (e.g. an "Add card" button). Omitted when not provided.
- empty ({ over: boolean }) - Replaces the empty-state text.

Events:
- move [event: { cardId: string; from?: string; to: string; index: number }] - A card was dropped on this column. `from` is the source column when the card knew it; `index` is the final insertion index among the column cards, excluding the dragged card itself, so `splice(index, 0, card)` after removal is correct.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `BoardColumn` has a blank `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when `BoardColumn` has no `title` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`) to name its group.

Rules:
- BoardColumn only reports drops; always update your own state in the `move` handler, nothing moves by itself.
- Give every column a unique `id` and every card a unique `id` across the whole board.
- Use `index` with splice after removing the card from its source: `target.splice(index, 0, card)`.
- Set the column width via `class` (e.g. `w-72`); the column itself is fluid.
- Handle the BoardCard `move` event (Alt+Arrow) too so the board is keyboard accessible.
- Use `acceptFrom` for workflow rules and `disabled` for locked columns; do not filter inside the move handler only.

Accessibility:
- Root is `role="group"` labelled by the title; the card area is `role="list"` (cards are `listitem`s) once it has cards.
- Native drag and drop is pointer-only. The keyboard alternative lives on `BoardCard`: Alt + Arrow keys emit a `move` request that you apply to your data (see the board example).
- The count badge is followed by visually hidden text ("cards"), so it reads "3 cards"; a disabled column sets `aria-disabled`.
- Drops are announced after the move is applied: every column holds a polite `role="status"` region that says "Moved <card title> to <column>, position n" once the card renders at the dropped position in this column. A drop your `move` handler ignores is not announced (the request expires after 10 s). Call the exposed `announce(message)` from your keyboard `move` handler to announce keyboard moves the same way.
- Columns are fluid and wrap in a grid on a phone; set a fixed width only on wide layouts.
- The highlight uses `data-over` plus a ring and background change, not colour alone, and transitions are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<BoardColumn id="todo" title="To do" class="w-64">
  <BoardCard id="a" title="Write docs" />
  <BoardCard id="b" title="Fix login bug" />
</BoardColumn>
```

Example: Drag and drop board
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = reactive([
  { id: 'todo', title: 'To do', cards: [{ id: 'c1', title: 'Write docs' }, { id: 'c2', title: 'Fix login bug' }] },
  { id: 'doing', title: 'In progress', cards: [{ id: 'c3', title: 'Review PR' }] },
  { id: 'done', title: 'Done', cards: [] },
])
// `index` is the card's final position in the target column
function onMove({ cardId, to, index }) {
  const source = columns.find((c) => c.cards.some((card) => card.id === cardId))
  const card = source.cards.find((c) => c.id === cardId)
  source.cards.splice(source.cards.indexOf(card), 1)
  columns.find((c) => c.id === to).cards.splice(index, 0, card)
}
</script>

<div class="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-3">
  <BoardColumn v-for="col in columns" :key="col.id" :id="col.id" :title="col.title" @move="onMove">
    <BoardCard v-for="card in col.cards" :key="card.id" :id="card.id" :title="card.title" @move="onNudge" />
  </BoardColumn>
</div>
```

```vue
  <BoardColumn id="done" title="Done" :accept-from="['doing']" empty-text="Only finished work lands here" />
```

```vue
  </template>
```

# BarChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG bar chart: grouped or stacked, vertical or horizontal, rounded or square bars, optional value labels and grid styles, with axis, legend and per-bar tooltips.

Use `BarChart` to compare values across categories. Pass `labels` (categories) and `series` (`{ name, data, tone? }`; `data[i]` belongs to `labels[i]`). The value domain always includes 0 and uses nice ticks; negative bars extend below (vertical) or left of (horizontal) the zero line. `variant="stacked"` (or the `stacked` boolean) stacks positives up and negatives down separately; `rounded`, `gap`, `size`, `showValues` and `grid` change the look without changing the data or the text alternatives. Non-finite values draw no bar and read "n/a" in the tooltip. Mismatched lengths are tolerated (category count = longest of labels and series; missing labels are empty). Crowded category labels are thinned and long ones truncated with the full text in a `<title>`; horizontal bars size their label gutter from an estimate of the rendered width of the widest label (per-glyph width classes, wide letters count more), so labels do not clip at the left edge. More than 5 series cycle through chart-1..5. For trends over time use `LineChart`; for parts of a whole use `DonutChart`. Size with `class` (`w-full`, `max-w-xl`); `width`/`height` only set the viewBox proportions.

import { BarChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- labels*: string[] - Category labels, one per group of bars.
- series*: { name: string; data: number[]; tone?: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' }[] - One entry per series. Unnamed series get "Series N".
- orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - Bar direction. Horizontal charts list categories down the left.
- variant: 'grouped' | 'stacked' = 'grouped' - Series side by side (`grouped`) or stacked per category (`stacked`). When omitted, the `stacked` boolean decides.
- stacked: boolean = false - Stack series per category instead of grouping them side by side. Same as `variant="stacked"`; `variant` wins when both are set.
- rounded: 'auto' | 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'full' = 'auto' - Bar corner radius: `none` 0, `sm` 2px, `md` 4px, `full` a pill (half the shorter side). `auto` keeps the original look: 2px for grouped bars, square for stacked segments.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between categories: bars fill 85% (`sm`), 70% (`md`) or 50% (`lg`) of each category band.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Chart height when `height` is not set: 160 / 240 / 320 viewBox units.
- showValues: boolean = false - Print the value at the end of each bar (the category total when stacked), using the axis formatter. Labels that do not fit their bar are left out; the tooltip and the hidden data table still carry every value.
- grid: 'none' | 'value' | 'dashed' | 'full' - Gridline style: `value` lines at each tick, `dashed` dashed value lines, `full` value lines plus a separator between categories, `none` no lines. When omitted, `showGrid` decides (`value` when on).
- showGrid: boolean = true - Gridlines at each tick.
- showAxis: boolean = true - Value ticks, category labels and the zero baseline.
- integerTicks: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Value axis ticks on whole numbers only. `auto` does this when every value is an integer (counts, so no 0.5 tick); `true` forces it; `false` always allows fractional ticks.
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend of series swatches. `auto` shows it when there is more than one series.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats axis ticks and tooltips (default: compact on the axis, grouped numbers in tooltips).
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary ("Bar chart: 3 categories, 2 series, values from 1 to 9") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to plot.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so axis text keeps its real size at 320px.
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 240).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `labels` is not an array, `series` is not an array, or a series has no `data` array. Empty arrays are valid and show `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Use `labels` for categories and `series[].data` for values (same index); never pass objects per bar.
- Use `stacked` only when series are parts of a total; otherwise group them.
- Provide a `valueFormatter` for currency, percentages and units.
- Only chart-N / semantic tones are available; do not pass colours. Set a `label` describing the insight.
- Size with `class`, not `width`/`height` (viewBox units); pick the height with `size` (sm, md, lg).
- Prefer `variant="stacked"` over the `stacked` boolean in new code. Use `showValues` for few bars; labels that do not fit are dropped, so never rely on them as the only source of values.
- `rounded="full"` suits grouped bars; keep stacked segments `none` unless `gap="lg"` separates them.

Accessibility:
- The chart is `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` (category/series counts and value range); override with `label`.
- Every bar has a native `<title>` tooltip: "Category, Series: value" ("n/a" for missing values).
- A visually hidden data table (caption, category rows, one column per series) follows the chart, so every value is readable as text. It is cut at 200 rows.
- Axis text is 12px with tabular figures and the SVG is sized to its container, so labels stay legible at 320px; the horizontal label gutter grows with the widest label (up to 40% of the width, then labels are cut with an ellipsis), so wide letters such as W and M are not clipped. Series are distinguished by legend, position and the data table, not by colour alone.
- The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
- Colour is never the only carrier: the HTML legend names every series and tooltips give exact values.
- Variants change only the drawing: `variant`, `rounded`, `gap`, `size` and `grid` leave the image name, the tooltips and the hidden data table identical. `showValues` adds the values as text inside the image; gridlines are decoration inside the labelled image.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<BarChart class="max-w-md" label="Sample data: bar chart" :labels="['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri']" :series="[{ name: 'Orders', data: [12, 19, 8, 24, 16] }]" />
```

Example: Whole-number ticks for counts
```vue

```

# BulletChart
group: data-display / Charts
Bullet chart: one thin measure bar against a target marker and qualitative range bands, for one or several stacked measures.

Use `BulletChart` to compare a measure with its goal and with bands such as poor, fair and good, in the space of a single row. It replaces a gauge or a set of progress bars when several measures share one scale. Each entry of `bullets` is `{ label, value, target?, ranges?, max?, tone?, unit? }`. `ranges` are ascending upper bounds (`[50, 75, 100]`); unsorted, duplicate and non-finite bounds are cleaned up. The bands are tonal steps of the muted colour (the lowest is the darkest) and the two darkest also carry a diagonal hatch, so the bands never rely on shade alone; `showRangeLabels` prints the bounds. The target is a tick with a diamond cap: a shape, not a colour. `variant` lays the measures out as rows (`horizontal`) or columns (`vertical`); `size` sets the band thickness. With `sharedScale` (default) every measure uses one axis, so lengths compare; turn it off when the measures have different units, and each measure then fills its own scale (no common axis is drawn). A value beyond the end of the scale is clamped and marked with an arrow head; a value that is not a number is listed as "n/a" and drawn without a bar. Not for time series (use `LineChart`) or part-to-whole data (use `DonutChart`). At most 60 measures are drawn.

import { BulletChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- bullets*: BulletInput[] - Measures: `{ label, value, target?, ranges?, max?, tone?, unit? }`. `ranges` are ascending upper bounds of the bands (up to 5); `max` is the upper end of that measure's scale; `unit` is appended to its value. An empty array shows `emptyText`.
- variant: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - Rows (`horizontal`) or side-by-side columns (`vertical`). A vertical chart with many measures scrolls inside a focusable, named region.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Band thickness and spacing: 16, 24 or 32 px bands (vertical: 18, 26 or 35 px wide, 120, 180 or 240 px tall).
- tone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'chart-1' - Colour token of the measure bar for bullets without their own `tone`.
- showTarget: boolean = true - Draw the target marker: a tick with a diamond cap. The table alternative always lists the target.
- showValues: boolean = true - Print each value (with its `unit`) beside the measure.
- showAxis: boolean = true - Draw the scale (ticks and grid lines). Only with `sharedScale`.
- showRangeLabels: boolean = false - Print the upper bound of every range band. Adds spacing so the labels do not collide with the next measure.
- showLegend: boolean = false - Legend for the measure, the target marker and the ranges.
- sharedScale: boolean = true - One scale for all measures (comparable lengths, one axis). Off: each measure fills its own scale and no axis is drawn.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats axis ticks, values, targets and range bounds. Defaults to compact numbers on the axis and grouped numbers for values.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- title: string - Visible heading text above the chart. Also names the chart when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible supporting text under the title.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown when there are no measures.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).
- height: number - Total viewBox height. Overrides the height that follows `size` and the number of measures: bands thicken (up to twice the size) and rows spread to fill it.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when `bullets` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.
- Throws a ContractError when a measure has no `label` text.

Rules:
- Give every BulletChart a `label` or a `title`; give every measure a `label`.
- Pass `ranges` as ascending upper bounds (`[50, 75, 100]`); the lowest band is drawn darkest.
- Use the same unit for all measures when `sharedScale` is on; set `sharedScale` to false for mixed units.
- Use `variant="vertical"` for a few measures side by side, `horizontal` for a list.
- Use `max` on a measure to fix its scale end; a larger value is clamped and marked.
- Do not use a BulletChart for a time series (LineChart) or a share of a whole (DonutChart).

Accessibility:
- The chart is one `role="img"` SVG named by `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; an automatic summary ("Bullet chart: 3 measures") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- A visually hidden table lists every measure with its value, target and range bounds, so no number depends on seeing the picture.
- The target marker is a tick with a diamond cap (a shape). The range bands are tonal steps of the muted colour, the two darkest are hatched, and `showRangeLabels` prints their bounds: no meaning rests on colour alone. Shapes keep an outline in forced-colors mode.
- Each band, bar and marker has a native tooltip (`<title>`); values and labels are 12px text with tabular figures.
- The SVG fills its container (1 unit is 1 CSS px) and never widens the page; a vertical chart with many columns scrolls horizontally inside a focusable `role="region"` named like the chart.
- No animation. Empty and invalid data show an inline message; NaN and Infinity never reach the SVG.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<BulletChart label="Sample data: orders shipped" :bullets="[{ label: 'Orders shipped', value: 78, target: 85, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }]" />
```

Example: Several measures on one scale
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const bullets = [
    { label: 'Orders shipped', value: 78, target: 85, ranges: [50, 75, 100], unit: 'k' },
    { label: 'Returns handled', value: 42, target: 60, ranges: [40, 70, 100], unit: 'k' },
    { label: 'Dock utilisation', value: 91, target: 80, ranges: [60, 85, 100], unit: '%' },
  ]
</script>

<BulletChart
  title="Warehouse measures"
  description="Sample data, thousands of units and percent"
  :bullets="bullets"
  :value-formatter="(n) => String(n)"
/>
```

Example: Variant: horizontal and vertical

```vue
  <BulletChart variant="horizontal" label="Sample data: rows" :bullets="[{ label: 'Orders', value: 78, target: 85, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }, { label: 'Returns', value: 42, target: 60, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }]" />
  <BulletChart variant="vertical" label="Sample data: columns" :bullets="[{ label: 'Orders', value: 78, target: 85, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }, { label: 'Returns', value: 42, target: 60, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }, { label: 'Dock', value: 91, target: 80, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }]" />

```

Example: Size: sm, md and lg
```vue

  <BulletChart size="md" label="Sample data: medium" :bullets="[{ label: 'Orders', value: 78, target: 85, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }]" />
  <BulletChart size="lg" label="Sample data: large" :bullets="[{ label: 'Orders', value: 78, target: 85, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }]" />
```

Example: Tone
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-6">
  <BulletChart tone="success" label="Sample data: success tone" :bullets="[{ label: 'On time', value: 88, target: 90, ranges: [60, 80, 100] }]" />
  <BulletChart tone="danger" label="Sample data: danger tone" :bullets="[{ label: 'Errors', value: 35, target: 20, ranges: [20, 40, 100] }]" />

```

# CalendarHeatmap
group: data-display / Charts
Contribution-style calendar: one cell per day, weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, with month labels, a legend and a month table for assistive technology.

Use `CalendarHeatmap` to show activity per day over weeks or years (commits, deploys, support tickets, visits). `data` is `{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", value }` per day; entries of the same day are summed, a date-time is read up to its date, and entries with an invalid date or a negative or non-numeric value are skipped and counted in an inline message. The range is `start` to `end`; without them it is the span of the data (at most 1830 days, the latest are kept). All date maths is UTC, and the component never reads the current date, so server and browser render the same grid. A day without an entry is drawn as an outlined "no data" cell, a day with value 0 as the faint level 0 cell, and the rest in `levels` (3 to 7) steps of the `tone` from the domain `min` (default 0) to `max` (default the largest value). Month names sit above the first week of each month (the year at the first label and every January), and Mon, Wed and Fri label the rows. The grid keeps its cell size and scrolls inside a focusable, named region instead of shrinking. For a rows-by-columns matrix of anything else use `Heatmap`.

import { CalendarHeatmap } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- data*: CalendarEntry[] - `{ date, value }` per day. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, an ISO date-time or a `Date` (its UTC date). `value` is a number >= 0. The same day is summed. An empty array with `start` and `end` draws empty days; without them it shows `emptyText`.
- start: string - First day shown, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Default: the earliest day in `data` (or 364 days before `end`).
- end: string - Last day shown, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Default: the latest day in `data` (or `start` when the data ends earlier).
- weekStart: 'sun' | 'mon' = 'sun' - First row of each week column: Sunday or Monday. The Mon, Wed and Fri labels follow.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Cell size: 10, 12 or 16 px.
- shape: 'square' | 'circle' = 'square' - Rounded squares or circles. The legend uses the same shape.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between cells: 1, 2 or 4 px.
- levels: number = 5 - Number of intensity steps above zero, clamped to 3 to 7 (a non-number gives 5).
- tone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'chart-1' - Colour token of the intensity ramp.
- min: number - Value where the ramp starts (default 0). Values below it are the faintest step.
- max: number - Value of the strongest step (default: the largest value in the range). Set it to compare several calendars on one scale.
- fit: boolean = false - Stretch the grid to the width of the container instead of the fixed `size`. The cell side is the width left after the weekday labels divided by the weeks, kept between 8 and 40px, so a year fills a wide card. Month, weekday and legend text stay 12px and the legend keeps the `size` swatches. Under 8px a cell the grid scrolls in its region as before. `size` is the fallback until the container is measured.
- showLegend: boolean = true - Less ... More legend with the no-activity cell and every step.
- legendLabels: { less?: string; more?: string } - Text of the legend ends, for translation. Wins over the `ConfigProvider` labels `heatmap.less` and `heatmap.more`; the English words "Less" and "More" are the default. The legend layout measures the translated text.
- showMonthLabels: boolean = true - Month names above the weeks (the year at the first label and every January).
- showWeekdayLabels: boolean = true - Mon, Wed and Fri beside the rows.
- cellTitle: (date: string, value: number | null) => string - Custom native tooltip per day. Receives the `YYYY-MM-DD` date and the summed value, or `null` for a day without data.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- title: string - Visible heading text above the chart. Also names the chart when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible supporting text under the title.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown when there is nothing to draw: no valid data and no `start` or `end`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when `data` is not an array. An empty array is valid.
- Throws a ContractError when `start` or `end` is set but is not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date.

Rules:
- Give every CalendarHeatmap a `label` or a `title`.
- Pass `data` as `{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", value }`; use `start` and `end` so a quiet period still shows its empty days.
- Never compute `start` or `end` from the current date inside a server-rendered page without passing it in; the component itself never reads the clock.
- Use `max` to compare several calendars on one scale; use `levels` (3 to 7) for a coarser or finer ramp.
- Use `weekStart="mon"` for locales that start the week on Monday.
- Use `fit` when the calendar sits in a wide card or a fluid layout; keep the fixed `size` for a compact widget.
- Translate the legend with `legendLabels` or the `ConfigProvider` labels `heatmap.less` / `heatmap.more`.
- Do not use it for a rows-by-columns matrix of unrelated labels (use Heatmap).

Accessibility:
- The grid is one `role="img"` SVG named by `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (an automatic summary with the range and the total is the fallback when strict mode is off). It sits in a focusable `role="region"` with the same name, so a keyboard user can scroll a wide calendar.
- A visually hidden table gives the text alternative by month: total, active days, busiest day and days without data. No value depends on colour.
- Every day cell has a native tooltip with the weekday, date and value ("Mon 3 Mar 2025: 12", or "no data"). Cells keep an outline in forced-colors mode and the legend shows every step.
- Month and weekday names are 12px text. Weekday labels show Mon, Wed and Fri only; all seven days are in each cell tooltip.
- No animation. Invalid entries are counted in an inline message; NaN and Infinity never reach the SVG.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<CalendarHeatmap
  label="Sample data: deploys per day"
  start="2025-03-03"
  end="2025-03-23"
  :data="[{ date: '2025-03-03', value: 2 }, { date: '2025-03-05', value: 6 }, { date: '2025-03-12', value: 1 }, { date: '2025-03-18', value: 9 }]"
/>
```

```vue
</script>

<CalendarHeatmap
  title="Deploys in 2025"
  description="Sample data, one cell per day"
  tone="success"
  :data="year"
/>
```

# DonutChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG donut or half donut showing parts of a whole, with a centre total and a legend of values and percentages that sits beside or under the ring.

Use `DonutChart` for a handful (2–6) of parts that add up to a meaningful total. Segments are proportional to their values; negative, NaN and Infinity values count as 0. One non-zero segment is a full ring; a zero total shows a muted ring and the centre reads "0" with the `emptyText` caption while the legend still lists every label at 0%. The centre shows the formatted total plus `centerText`; replace it with the scoped `center` slot. `variant="half"` draws a semicircle with the total in its hollow, which suits a single headline split (passed / failed) in less height; `layout` moves the legend (beside the ring, always beside, or always under it). Use `BarChart` for many categories or precise comparison.

import { DonutChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- data*: { label: string; value: number; tone?: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' }[] - Segments in draw order (clockwise from 12 o'clock). Tones cycle chart-1..5 when omitted.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Rendered width: 7rem / 10rem / 14rem (`size-28` / `size-40` / `size-56` for `full`).
- variant: 'full' | 'half' = 'full' - `full` is a ring, `half` a semicircle opening downwards at half the height (`h-14` / `h-20` / `h-28`), with the centre text at the bottom of its hollow.
- layout: 'auto' | 'inline' | 'stacked' = 'auto' - Legend placement: `auto` beside the ring and wrapping below it when narrow, `inline` always beside it (long labels truncate), `stacked` always under it at full width. Use `showLegend` to remove the legend.
- thickness: number = 14 - Ring thickness in viewBox units (100×100 box), clamped to 2–40.
- showLegend: boolean = true - List swatch, label, formatted value and percentage (max one decimal) per segment.
- centerText: string - Small caption under the total in the centre.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats the total, legend values and tooltips.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary ("Donut chart: 3 segments, total 100") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown when `data` is empty (and as the centre caption when the total is 0).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Slots:
- center ({ total: number }) - Replaces the default centre content (total + caption).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `data` is not an array, or a segment lacks a non-empty string `label` or a finite number `value`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Use for 2–6 parts of a whole; prefer BarChart beyond that.
- Pass `{ label, value }` objects; tones auto-cycle chart-1..5 or set `tone` per segment.
- Put the headline in the `center` slot only when the default total is not what you want to say.
- Use `variant="half"` for a single split or a progress-like total; keep full rings for three or more parts.
- Use `layout="stacked"` in narrow cards and `layout="inline"` only with short labels.
- Keep the legend on (default) so values are available as text, not only as arcs.

Accessibility:
- The ring is `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` (segment count and total); override with `label`.
- Each segment has a native `<title>` tooltip "Label: value (pct%)"; the HTML legend repeats every value and percentage as real text.
- The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
- `variant` and `layout` change only the drawing and where the legend sits: the image name, the tooltips and the legend text are the same. The half ring is still one labelled image and the total stays real text in its hollow.
- The ring has a fixed size (`size-28`, `size-40` or `size-56`) and the legend wraps beside or under it, so it fits a 320px screen. Values and percentages use `tabular-nums`; the legend text is the non-colour alternative to the segment colours.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<DonutChart
  center-text="items"
  label="Sample data: three segments"
  :data="[
    { label: 'Segment A', value: 420 },
    { label: 'Segment B', value: 310 },
    { label: 'Segment C', value: 130 },
  ]"
/>
```

Example: Custom centre and tones
```vue
<DonutChart
  size="lg"
  label="Sample data: test results"
  :thickness="18"
  :data="[
    { label: 'Passed', value: 86, tone: 'success' },
    { label: 'Flaky', value: 9, tone: 'warning' },
    { label: 'Failed', value: 5, tone: 'danger' },
  ]"
  :value-formatter="(n) => n + ' tests'"
>
  <template #center="{ total }">
    <span class="text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums">{{ total }}</span>
    <Badge variant="success">Passed</Badge>
  </template>
</DonutChart>
```

Example: Variant: full and half
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-8">
  <DonutChart variant="full" size="sm" label="Sample data: full ring" center-text="items" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 30 }, { label: 'Segment C', value: 10 }]" />
  <DonutChart variant="half" size="sm" label="Sample data: half ring" center-text="items" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 30 }, { label: 'Segment C', value: 10 }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Layout: legend placement
```vue
<div class="grid gap-8 md:grid-cols-3">
  <DonutChart layout="auto" size="sm" label="Sample data: legend wraps when narrow" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 40 }]" />
  <DonutChart layout="inline" size="sm" label="Sample data: legend always beside" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B with a long name', value: 40 }]" />
  <DonutChart layout="stacked" size="sm" label="Sample data: legend below" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 40 }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Thickness
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-8">
  <DonutChart :thickness="6" size="sm" :show-legend="false" label="Sample data: thin ring" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 40 }]" />
  <DonutChart :thickness="14" size="sm" :show-legend="false" label="Sample data: default ring" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 40 }]" />
  <DonutChart :thickness="28" size="sm" :show-legend="false" label="Sample data: thick ring" :data="[{ label: 'Segment A', value: 60 }, { label: 'Segment B', value: 40 }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Empty and zero total
```vue

  <DonutChart label="Budget split" :data="[]" empty-text="No budget set" />
  <DonutChart size="sm" label="Budget with nothing spent" :data="[{ label: 'Spent', value: 0 }, { label: 'Left', value: 0 }]" />
</div>
```

# FunnelChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG funnel chart with funnel, pyramid, bars and steps variants, vertical or horizontal layout, conversion rates, labels inside or beside the shapes and non-monotone data.

Use `FunnelChart` for a sequence of stages where each one is (usually) a subset of the one before: a sales pipeline, a sign-up flow, an order process. Pass `stages` as `{ label, value, tone? }`. `variant` picks the shape: `funnel` joins the stages into one tapering shape (the edge facing the next stage has the next value), `pyramid` is the same shape stacked the other way round (the first stage is the base), `steps` centres a rectangle per stage and `bars` aligns the rectangles to the start like a bar chart. `orientation` runs the stages top to bottom or start to end. `showConversion` prints the share of the previous stage next to each value (the first stage has none; a previous value of 0 or a missing value reads "n/a"). Text sits `beside` the shapes (a label column, or underneath when horizontal) or `inside` them; text that does not fit inside moves beside its stage. The data does not have to fall: a stage larger than the one before is drawn as it is (and its conversion is above 100%). Negative values draw no shape; missing values read "n/a". At most 50 stages are drawn; the hidden table lists up to 200. Use `BarChart` to compare unrelated categories and `Gauge` or `StatBar` for one value against a target.

import { FunnelChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- stages*: { label: string; value: number; tone?: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' }[] - Stages in order. `value` sizes the shape (negative or non-finite values draw nothing and non-finite ones read "n/a"); `tone` overrides the chart `tone` for one stage. An empty array shows `emptyText`.
- variant: 'funnel' | 'pyramid' | 'bars' | 'steps' = 'funnel' - `funnel` tapering shape, `pyramid` the same shape upside down (first stage at the base), `bars` rectangles aligned to the start (left, or bottom when horizontal), `steps` rectangles centred on the axis.
- orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - `vertical` stacks the stages top to bottom with a label column; `horizontal` runs them from start to end with text underneath each stage.
- labelPlacement: 'inside' | 'beside' = 'beside' - `beside` prints label, value and conversion next to the shapes; `inside` prints them on a small plate inside each shape when it fits (the label moves beside the stage when it does not; when horizontal only the value and conversion go inside).
- showConversion: boolean = false - Show the percent of the previous stage next to each value. The first stage has none. A previous value of 0 or a missing value reads "n/a".
- showValues: boolean = true - Show the value of each stage. With it off only the label (and the conversion, if on) is printed; the values stay in the table and tooltips.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height of one stage when vertical (32 / 44 / 56), height of the shapes when horizontal (96 / 144 / 200), and the spacing of the figure.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between neighbouring stages: 2, 4 or 8 viewBox units.
- tone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'chart-1' - Tone of the stages that set none.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats values and tooltips. Defaults to compact (labels) / grouped (tooltip) numbers.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it.
- title: string - Visible heading above the chart. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there are no stages.
- loading: boolean = false - Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.
- loadingText: string = 'Loading chart' - Message of the loading placeholder.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides the height derived from `size` and the number of stages.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `stages` is not an array or a stage has no `label` or no numeric `value`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `stages` in the order of the process, each as `{ label, value }`; do not pre-compute percentages, use `showConversion`.
- Set `label` (or `title`) to say what the funnel measures and use `valueFormatter` for units.
- Use `variant="pyramid"` only when the first stage is the broadest and should sit at the base; for a normal funnel use `funnel`.
- Use `orientation="horizontal"` for few stages (up to about 6) in wide containers; vertical for long lists and narrow screens.
- Use `labelPlacement="inside"` for wide shapes; narrow stages move their text beside them automatically.
- Size with `class`, `size` and `gap`, not `width` / `height`. At most 50 stages are drawn.

Accessibility:
- The chart is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (stage count, first and last stage).
- A visually hidden data table (stages as rows) lists the value, the percent of the previous stage and the percent of the first stage of every stage, so no number depends on the picture; missing rates read "n/a".
- Meaning never rests on colour: every stage carries its label, and its value and conversion are text (on a plate in the page background when drawn inside a shape, so the text keeps the normal text contrast). Each shape has a native `<title>` tooltip.
- The SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px): text keeps its size, labels are shortened (full text in a tooltip) and horizontal labels are thinned when columns get narrow, so nothing overflows at 320px.
- In forced-colors mode the shapes use the system text colour and the plates keep their border. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<FunnelChart class="max-w-xl" label="Sample data: sign-up flow" :stages="[{ label: 'Visited', value: 12400 }, { label: 'Signed up', value: 5200 }, { label: 'Activated', value: 2900 }, { label: 'Subscribed', value: 840 }]" />
```

```vue
</div>
```

# Heatmap
group: data-display / Charts
Accessible grid heatmap (commit calendar, activity by hour) with intensity levels, labels, legend and cell tooltips.

Use `Heatmap` for a rows × columns matrix of magnitudes: activity calendars, usage by weekday/hour, correlation-style grids. It is a real `<table>`: row/column labels are `<th>`, every cell is a `<td>` with a visually hidden value and the colour in an inner span. Intensity is one of `levels` (1–5) opacity steps of the tone; `null`, NaN, missing and zero cells are the muted "empty" colour. The domain defaults to the data min/max (override with `min`/`max`). Ragged rows are padded. For long column label lists use `colLabelStep` to show every n-th label visibly. `heatLevel(value, min, max, levels)` is exported as a pure helper.

import { Heatmap } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- values*: (number | null)[][] - Rows × columns of values. Empty array → `emptyText`.
- rowLabels: string[] - Row headers (`<th scope="row">`).
- colLabels: string[] - Column headers (`<th scope="col">`).
- tone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'chart-1' - Colour token of the intensity ramp.
- min: number - Domain minimum (default: smallest value in the data).
- max: number - Domain maximum (default: largest value in the data).
- levels: number = 5 - Number of intensity steps, clamped to 1–5.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Cell size: size-3 / size-4 / size-6.
- shape: 'square' | 'circle' = 'square' - Cell shape: slightly rounded square, or a circle (`rounded-full`) for a dot matrix. Applies to the legend swatches too.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between cells: 1px, 2px or 4px (`border-spacing`).
- showLegend: boolean = true - Less … More swatch legend.
- colLabelStep: number = 1 - Show every n-th column label visibly; the others stay screen-reader only. With `fit` the step also grows automatically so labels never overlap.
- fit: boolean = false - Stretch the columns to the width of the container. Cells stay square and grow up to 40px (`size` is ignored; `shape` and `gap` still apply). The table keeps its semantics through ARIA roles. Each column label is centred over its column. The first and last labels always show; the ones between are thinned so none overlap, and a first or last label wider than its cell hugs the grid edge so it stays inside.
- fill: boolean = false - Only with `fit`: cells grow past the 40px cap until the grid fills the container width (columns are `minmax(0, 1fr)`). Cells stay square, so the heatmap gets taller as it gets wider; label thinning uses the uncapped cell width.
- legendLabels: { less?: string; more?: string } - Text of the legend ends, for translation. Wins over the `ConfigProvider` labels `heatmap.less` and `heatmap.more`; the English words "Less" and "More" are the default. With `fit` and row labels the legend starts at the first cell column.
- label: string - Accessible name of the region and its visually hidden table caption. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown when there are no cells.
- formatValue: (value: number) => string - Formats numbers in the visually hidden table cells, the default cell tooltip and the summary range, e.g. as a percentage. Empty cells stay "no data". Unset keeps plain number formatting.
- cellTitle: (value: number | null, rowLabel: string, colLabel: string) => string - Custom native tooltip per cell (default "Row, Col: value").
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `values` is not an array of rows (each row an array). An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `values` as rows × columns; use null for missing cells (zero is also drawn as empty).
- Provide `rowLabels`/`colLabels` so the table is understandable to screen readers.
- Use `shape="circle"` for sparse matrices and `gap="lg"` to separate cells further; keep squares for dense calendars. `levels` already sets the number of intensity steps (1 to 5), so there is no separate `scale` prop.
- Use `formatValue` for units (percent, bytes); it changes text only, not the intensity.
- Use `colLabelStep` for wide calendars instead of removing labels.
- Use `fit` to fill a container up to 40px cells and `fit fill` when the grid must reach the container edge; `fill` alone does nothing.
- Translate the legend with `legendLabels` or the `ConfigProvider` labels `heatmap.less` / `heatmap.more`; never leave English legend text in a localised app.
- Pick one `tone`; do not mix colours. Use `min`/`max` to compare several heatmaps on one scale.

Accessibility:
- Native table semantics: row and column labels are `<th scope>`, cells are `<td>`; a visually hidden `<caption>` carries `label` or an automatic summary.
- Each cell contains its value as visually hidden text ("no data" for empty cells), so colour is never the only carrier; the swatch has a native tooltip.
- The grid sits in a focusable `role="region"` (named by `label` or the summary) that scrolls horizontally, so a wide heatmap never widens the page and keyboard users can scroll it. Text is 12px; the legend uses tabular figures.
- The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
- `shape` and `gap` change only the swatches: the table, the hidden values and the intensity steps are identical. Circles are not read differently from squares.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<Heatmap
  label="Sample data: three rows by four columns"
  :row-labels="['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed']"
  :col-labels="['9', '12', '15', '18']"
  :values="[[0, 3, 5, 1], [2, 8, 9, 4], [null, 1, 6, 2]]"
/>
```

Example: Commit calendar (7 × 26)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const days = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun']
const weeks = Array.from({ length: 26 }, (_, i) => 'W' + (i + 1))
const grid = days.map((_, r) => weeks.map((_, c) => ((r * 7 + c * 13) % 11 < 3 ? 0 : (r * 31 + c * 17) % 9)))
</script>

<Heatmap
  size="sm"
  label="Sample data: activity by weekday and week"
  tone="success"
  :row-labels="days"
  :col-labels="weeks"
  :col-label-step="4"
  :values="grid"
  :cell-title="(v, r, c) => (v ? v + ' commits' : 'No commits') + ' on ' + r + ', ' + c"
/>
```

Example: Fit the container
```vue
<Heatmap fit label="Sample data: requests by hour" :row-labels="['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed']" :col-labels="Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => String(i).padStart(2, '0') + ':00')" :values="Array.from({ length: 3 }, (_, r) => Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, c) => (r * 7 + c * 3) % 11))" />
```

Example: Fill the container
```vue
<Heatmap fit fill label="Sample data: requests by hour, full width" :legend-labels="{ less: 'Fewer', more: 'More' }" :row-labels="['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed']" :col-labels="Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => String(i).padStart(2, '0'))" :values="Array.from({ length: 3 }, (_, r) => Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, c) => (r * 7 + c * 3) % 11))" />
```

Example: Shape: square and circle
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-8">
  <Heatmap shape="square" label="Sample data: square cells" :row-labels="['Mon', 'Tue']" :col-labels="['9', '12', '15']" :values="[[0, 3, 5], [2, 8, 9]]" />
  <Heatmap shape="circle" size="lg" label="Sample data: circle cells" :row-labels="['Mon', 'Tue']" :col-labels="['9', '12', '15']" :values="[[0, 3, 5], [2, 8, 9]]" />
</div>
```

Example: Gap
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-8">
  <Heatmap gap="sm" label="Sample data: tight cells" :values="[[1, 4, 7], [3, 6, 9]]" :show-legend="false" />
  <Heatmap gap="md" label="Sample data: default cells" :values="[[1, 4, 7], [3, 6, 9]]" :show-legend="false" />
  <Heatmap gap="lg" shape="circle" label="Sample data: wide spacing" :values="[[1, 4, 7], [3, 6, 9]]" :show-legend="false" />
</div>
```

Example: Formatted values
```vue
<Heatmap label="Sample data: success rate by weekday" :row-labels="['Mon', 'Tue']" :col-labels="['9', '12', '15']" :values="[[0.5, 0.75, 1], [0.25, null, 0.9]]" :format-value="(v) => Math.round(v * 100) + '%'" />
```

Example: Empty
```vue
<Heatmap label="Activity by weekday" :values="[]" empty-text="No activity yet" />
```

# LineChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG line chart with multiple series, nice y ticks, linear, smooth or step curves, optional area fill and markers, grid styles, gaps for missing values and tooltips on dots.

Use `LineChart` for trends over an ordered axis (time, steps). Pass `labels` (x categories) and `series` (`{ name, data, tone? }`). The y domain is the nice-tick extent of the data. NaN / Infinity values break the line into separate segments; a point with no neighbours is drawn as a dot even when `showDots` is false. `curve` joins points with straight segments, a smooth curve that never overshoots the data, or steps that hold each value until the next point. Dots are on automatically up to 60 points (`showDots="auto"`); each dot has a native `<title>` tooltip. Crowded x labels are thinned. Renders 10,000 points quickly (dots stay off by default). Use `Sparkline` for tiny inline trends and `BarChart` for category comparison. Size with `class`; `width`/`height` set the viewBox proportions.

import { LineChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- labels*: string[] - X-axis labels, one per point.
- series*: { name: string; data: number[]; tone?: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' }[] - One line per entry. More than 5 series cycle through chart-1..5.
- variant: 'line' | 'area' = 'line' - Lines only, or lines with a soft fill under each. When omitted, the `area` boolean decides.
- area: boolean = false - Soft fill under each line. Same as `variant="area"`; `variant` wins when both are set.
- curve: 'linear' | 'smooth' | 'step' = 'linear' - How points are joined. `smooth` is a monotone curve (it never dips below the lowest or above the highest neighbour); `step` holds each value until the next point. Gaps still break the line. The area follows the curve.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Chart height when `height` is not set: 160 / 240 / 320 viewBox units.
- showDots: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - `auto` draws dots when there are at most 60 points.
- markerShape: 'circle' | 'square' | 'diamond' | 'triangle' | 'series' = 'circle' - Shape of the point markers. `series` gives each series its own shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), which the legend repeats, so series differ by shape and dash pattern as well as colour. Markers still follow `showDots`.
- grid: 'none' | 'horizontal' | 'dashed' | 'full' - Gridline style: `horizontal` solid lines at each y tick, `dashed` dashed ones, `full` horizontal lines plus a vertical line at each labelled x position, `none` no lines. When omitted, `showGrid` decides (`horizontal` when on).
- showGrid: boolean = true - Horizontal gridlines at each y tick.
- showAxis: boolean = true - Y tick labels and x labels.
- integerTicks: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Value axis ticks on whole numbers only. `auto` does this when every value is an integer (counts, so no 0.5 tick); `true` forces it; `false` always allows fractional ticks.
- yMin: number - Lower bound of the y axis, rounded down to a tick. Without it the axis starts below the lowest value, which makes a narrow series look like a large swing. Values below it are drawn on the bottom edge. Non-finite values are ignored.
- yMax: number - Upper bound of the y axis, rounded up to a tick. Values above it are drawn on the top edge. Non-finite values are ignored.
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend of series swatches; `auto` shows it for more than one series.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats y ticks and tooltips.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary ("Line chart: 12 points per series, 2 series, values from 1 to 9") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to plot.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so axis text keeps its real size at 320px.
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 240).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `labels` is not an array, `series` is not an array, or a series has no `data` array. Empty arrays are valid and show `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Use `labels` for the x axis and `series[].data` for y values (same index).
- Use NaN (or a non-finite number) for missing points: the line breaks instead of interpolating.
- Provide `valueFormatter` for units and a `label` that states the takeaway.
- Large series: leave `showDots` on `auto` (off above 60 points).
- Use Sparkline, not LineChart, for tiny inline trends.
- Use `curve="step"` for values that hold between readings and `curve="smooth"` only for continuous measurements; never smooth counts that jump.
- Prefer `variant="area"` over the `area` boolean in new code. Use `markerShape="series"` when several series share a chart and must be told apart without colour.

Accessibility:
- The chart is `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` (points, series, value range); override with `label`.
- Dots carry native `<title>` tooltips: "Label, Series: value". Isolated points are always drawn so no data is invisible.
- A visually hidden data table (caption, one row per point, one column per series) follows the chart, so every value is readable as text. It is cut at 200 rows.
- Series differ by dash pattern as well as colour (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot); the legend draws the same line sample. Axis text is 12px with tabular figures and the SVG is sized to its container, so labels stay legible at 320px.
- The empty state is a `role="img"` element labelled with `emptyText`.
- The HTML legend names every series so colour is not the only identifier.
- Variants change only the drawing: `curve`, `variant`, `grid` and `size` leave the image name, the tooltips and the hidden data table identical. `markerShape="series"` adds a third cue (shape) next to colour and dash pattern, and the legend repeats it.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<LineChart class="max-w-md" label="Sample data: line chart" :labels="['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May']" :series="[{ name: 'Series A', data: [120, 180, 150, 240, 310] }]" />
```

Example: Fixed y domain
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
  <LineChart label="Sample data: automatic domain" :labels="['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']" :series="[{ name: 'Reading', data: [172.0, 172.6, 172.2, 172.4] }]" />
  <LineChart label="Sample data: domain 150 to 200" :y-min="150" :y-max="200" :labels="['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']" :series="[{ name: 'Reading', data: [172.0, 172.6, 172.2, 172.4] }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Whole-number ticks and edge labels
```vue
<LineChart class="max-w-md" label="Sample data: queue length" :labels="['13:00:00', '13:00:05', '13:00:10']" :series="[{ name: 'Queued', data: [0, 2, 1] }]" />
```

Example: Multi-series with area and gaps
```vue
<LineChart
  area
  label="Sample data: two series"
  :labels="['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun']"
  :series="[
    { name: 'Requests', data: [320, 410, 380, 520, 470, 300, 280] },
    { name: 'Errors', data: [12, 18, Number.NaN, 30, 22, 9, 7], tone: 'danger' },
  ]"
  :value-formatter="(n) => n.toLocaleString()"
/>
```

Example: Curve: linear, smooth, step
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <LineChart curve="linear" size="sm" label="Sample data: straight segments" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9, 5] }]" />
  <LineChart curve="smooth" size="sm" label="Sample data: smooth curve" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9, 5] }]" />
  <LineChart curve="step" size="sm" label="Sample data: steps" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9, 5] }]" />
</div>
```

```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
  <LineChart variant="line" size="sm" label="Sample data: line" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9, 5] }]" />
  <LineChart variant="area" curve="smooth" size="sm" label="Sample data: smooth area" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9, 5] }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Marker shape
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
  <LineChart marker-shape="diamond" size="sm" label="Sample data: diamond markers" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9] }]" />
  <LineChart marker-shape="series" size="sm" label="Sample data: a shape per series" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']" :series="[{ name: 'Series A', data: [3, 8, 4, 9] }, { name: 'Series B', data: [6, 5, 7, 2] }, { name: 'Series C', data: [1, 3, 2, 4] }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Grid: none, horizontal, dashed, full
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <LineChart grid="none" size="sm" label="Sample data: no grid" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9] }]" />
  <LineChart grid="horizontal" size="sm" label="Sample data: horizontal grid" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9] }]" />
  <LineChart grid="dashed" size="sm" label="Sample data: dashed grid" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9] }]" />
  <LineChart grid="full" size="sm" label="Sample data: full grid" :labels="['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']" :series="[{ name: 'Series', data: [3, 8, 4, 9] }]" />
</div>
```

# NetworkGraph
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free node-link diagram with four deterministic layouts, group colours with marker shapes, arrowheads, hulls and a text alternative.

Use `NetworkGraph` to show how things connect: services that call each other, sites on a route, people in a team. Pass `nodes` (`{ id, label?, group?, size? }`) and `edges` (`{ from, to, weight?, directed?, label? }`). `layout` places the nodes: `force` (a spring simulation with a fixed number of steps and no randomness, so the same data always gives the same picture), `circular`, `grid` or `layered` (left to right along the edge direction; cycles are broken deterministically). `variant` sets how much is drawn: `plain`, `labelled` (node and connection labels, up to 120 nodes) or `grouped` (a dashed hull around every group). Nodes grow with their weighted degree (the sum of the weights of their connections) unless `size` is set, so mix `size` on all nodes or on none. Group is told by colour and by marker shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), and listed in a legend. Hover or focus a node to keep it and its neighbours at full strength and dim the rest. Bad data is handled in place: duplicate ids are ignored, connections to unknown ids are skipped, more than `maxNodes` nodes (default 300) are cut, and a short message under the graph says what happened. Do not use it for more than a few hundred nodes or for a tree; use `Tree` for hierarchies.

import { NetworkGraph } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- nodes*: { id: string; label?: string; group?: string; size?: number }[] - The nodes. `id` is unique and required; a repeated id is ignored. `label` defaults to the id. `group` sets colour, marker shape and hull. `size` is a relative size (positive number).
- edges: { from: string; to: string; weight?: number; directed?: boolean; label?: string }[] = [] - Connections between node ids. `weight` (positive) widens the line and enlarges both nodes; `directed` draws an arrowhead at `to`; `label` shows on the line in the `labelled` variant. Unknown ids are skipped and counted; `from` equal to `to` draws a loop.
- layout: 'force' | 'circular' | 'grid' | 'layered' = 'force' - Placement. `force` is a spring simulation with fixed steps, `circular` puts the nodes on a ring grouped by group, `grid` fills rows, `layered` stacks columns along the edge direction.
- variant: 'plain' | 'labelled' | 'grouped' = 'plain' - `plain` draws nodes and lines; `labelled` adds node labels (cut at 12 characters) and connection labels, up to 120 nodes; `grouped` outlines every group with a dashed hull.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Drawing height when `height` is not set: 200 / 300 / 420 viewBox units. Also the gap between title, drawing, legend and messages.
- edgeStyle: 'straight' | 'curved' = 'straight' - `curved` bends every line to one side of its direction, so a connection A to B and one B to A no longer overlap.
- directed: boolean = false - Draw an arrowhead on every connection that does not set its own `directed`.
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend of groups with their colour and marker. `auto` shows it when any node has a group; `false` hides it.
- maxNodes: number = 300 - Most nodes drawn, 1 to 5000. The first nodes are kept; a message says how many were left out. Connections to left-out nodes are skipped.
- title: string - Visible title above the drawing (plain text, not a heading). Also names the graph when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible description under the title.
- label: string - Accessible name of the graph. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set; an automatic summary ("Network graph: 6 nodes, 7 connections, 3 groups") is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to draw.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The graph then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so text keeps its size at 320px.
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when `nodes` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows the empty state.
- Throws a ContractError when a node has no `id` (a non-empty string).
- Throws a ContractError when `edges` is given and is not an array.
- Throws a ContractError when a connection has no `from` or no `to`.

Rules:
- Always pass `label` or `title`; give every node a unique `id` and use those ids in `edges`.
- Use `group` for categories: it sets colour, marker shape, the legend and the `grouped` hulls. Do not add a second colour prop.
- Pick `layout="layered"` with `directed` for flows and dependencies, `circular` for small symmetric sets, `grid` for lists, `force` (the default) for general networks.
- Use `variant="labelled"` for fewer than about 30 nodes; larger graphs stay `plain` and rely on hover, focus and the legend.
- Do not pass random or time-based data to force a different picture: the layout is deterministic by design.
- Raise `maxNodes` only when you must; the default of 300 keeps the drawing readable and fast.

Accessibility:
- The drawing is a `role="group"` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`). Every node is a focusable `role="img"` named with its label, group, number of connections and up to five neighbours.
- Keyboard: Tab enters the graph on one node (a roving tab stop); Arrow Right and Down move to the next node, Arrow Left and Up to the previous one, Home and End jump to the first and last. The order follows the layout (grouped for circular and grid, by column for layered). Tab leaves the graph. Hover and focus highlight the node, its neighbours and their lines; the rest dims. Focus also draws a ring.
- Group is never colour alone: each group has a marker shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), the legend shows both, and the node name includes the group. Direction is an arrowhead, not a colour. Nodes keep an outline in forced-colors mode.
- A visually hidden text alternative follows the drawing: a table of nodes (name, group, connections written as "A to B (weight 3)") and a table of connections (pair, weight, label), each cut at 200 rows with the cut stated in the caption.
- Messages about cut or skipped data are plain text under the graph. The empty state is a `role="img"` with `emptyText`.
- The drawing scales to the container (1 unit = 1 CSS px) and reflows at 320px. Highlight changes use opacity only, with a transition under `motion-safe`; nothing moves on its own.
