# RadarChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG radar (spider) chart with three or more axes, several series, line, area or dots variants, polygon or circular rings, 3 to 6 levels and a configurable scale.

Use `RadarChart` to compare a few profiles over the same 3 to about 10 measures (a skills matrix, a product comparison). Pass `axes` (names, clockwise from the top) and `series` (`{ name, data, tone? }`, one value per axis). `variant` draws each series as an outline (`line`), an outline with a soft fill (`area`) or only markers (`dots`); every series has its own dash pattern and marker shape, so series differ by more than colour. `shape` sets the rings: straight segments (`polygon`) or circles; `levels` sets how many rings, 3 to 6. The scale starts at 0 (or the lowest value when negative) and ends at a round number that covers the data; set `min` and `max` to compare charts on the same scale. The radius is chosen so every axis label stays inside the chart, also at 320px; long names are shortened (the full name is in a tooltip). Missing or non-finite values sit at the centre and read "n/a" in the table. At most 40 axes are drawn. Use `BarChart` when there are fewer than 3 measures or when exact comparison matters: areas and angles are hard to read precisely.

import { RadarChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- axes*: string[] - Axis names, at least 3, clockwise from the top. An empty array shows `emptyText`; 1 or 2 names are an error (and show `emptyText` outside strict mode).
- series*: { name: string; data: number[]; tone?: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' }[] - One shape per entry; `data` has one value per axis in the order of `axes`. More than 5 series cycle through chart-1..5, dash patterns and marker shapes.
- variant: 'line' | 'area' | 'dots' = 'line' - `line` outlines each series, `area` adds a soft fill under the outline, `dots` draws only the markers (a larger marker per axis).
- shape: 'polygon' | 'circle' = 'polygon' - Shape of the rings: straight segments between the axes, or circles. The series outline is always a polygon.
- levels: 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 4 - Number of rings. Other numbers are rounded and clamped to 3..6.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Chart height 220 / 300 / 380 viewBox units (the radar is as large as the width and the axis labels allow) and the spacing of the figure.
- min: number - Value at the centre. Defaults to 0, or the lowest value when that is negative. A `min` above `max` is swapped.
- max: number - Value at the outer ring. Defaults to a round number (1, 2, 2.5, 5 times a power of ten per ring) that covers the data. Values above it sit on the rim.
- showValues: boolean = false - Print the value of each point outside it. Values that would overlap or leave the chart are left out; none are drawn beyond 48 points.
- showScale: boolean = true - Print the value of each ring along the first axis (thinned when the rings are close together).
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend with the dash pattern and marker of each series; `auto` shows it for more than one series.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats ring labels, values and tooltips. Defaults to compact (rings) / grouped (tooltip) numbers.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it.
- title: string - Visible heading above the chart. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there is nothing to plot.
- loading: boolean = false - Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.
- loadingText: string = 'Loading chart' - Message of the loading placeholder.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 300).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `axes` is not an array or has 1 or 2 names, `series` is not an array, or a series has no `data` array. Empty arrays are valid and show `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Use at least 3 axes and keep it to about 10; give each series one value per axis, in the order of `axes`.
- Set `label` (or `title`) to say what is compared. Name the unit in `valueFormatter` and set `min` / `max` when several charts must share a scale.
- Limit the chart to 2 or 3 series; with `variant="area"` the fills overlap.
- Use `shape="circle"` for a softer look and `levels` for the number of rings; neither changes the data.
- Do not use a radar chart to read exact values; show `showValues` or use `BarChart`.
- Size with `class` and `size`, not `width` / `height`.

Accessibility:
- The chart is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (axis and series counts, value range and scale).
- A visually hidden data table (axes as rows, one column per series) follows the chart, so every value is readable as text; missing values read "n/a".
- Series are told apart by dash pattern and marker shape (and by the legend), not by colour alone; `dots` uses marker shapes only. Each marker has a native `<title>` tooltip with the axis, series and value.
- The radius is computed so that every axis label stays inside the viewBox. The SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so text keeps its size and nothing overflows at 320px. Long names are shortened and keep their full text in a tooltip.
- In forced-colors mode lines and markers use the system text colour; dash patterns and marker shapes carry the series, and the area fill is dropped. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<RadarChart class="max-w-md" label="Sample data: product profile" :axes="['Speed', 'Range', 'Cost', 'Comfort', 'Safety']" :series="[{ name: 'Model A', data: [7, 5, 8, 6, 9] }]" />
```

Example: Two series
```vue
<RadarChart
  class="max-w-md"
  label="Sample data: two models compared"
  :axes="['Speed', 'Range', 'Cost', 'Comfort', 'Safety']"
  :series="[
    { name: 'Model A', data: [7, 5, 8, 6, 9] },
    { name: 'Model B', data: [4, 8, 5, 9, 6], tone: 'chart-2' },
  ]"
/>
```

Example: Variant: line, area, dots

```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <RadarChart v-for="v in ['line', 'area', 'dots']" :key="v" :variant="v" size="sm" :label="'Sample data: ' + v" :axes="['Speed', 'Range', 'Cost', 'Comfort', 'Safety']" :series="[{ name: 'Model A', data: [7, 5, 8, 6, 9] }, { name: 'Model B', data: [4, 8, 5, 9, 6] }]" />
</div>
```

```vue

  <RadarChart shape="polygon" size="sm" label="Sample data: polygon rings" :axes="['Speed', 'Range', 'Cost', 'Comfort', 'Safety']" :series="[{ name: 'Model A', data: [7, 5, 8, 6, 9] }]" />
  <RadarChart shape="circle" size="sm" label="Sample data: circular rings" :axes="['Speed', 'Range', 'Cost', 'Comfort', 'Safety']" :series="[{ name: 'Model A', data: [7, 5, 8, 6, 9] }]" />
```

# Sankey
group: data-display / Charts
Flow diagram: nodes in layers joined by ribbons whose width is the amount that flows, with a table of flows as the text alternative.

Use `Sankey` to show how a quantity moves and splits across stages (orders to outcomes, budget to spending lines, traffic to pages), when the paths matter as much as the totals. Pass `links` of `{ source, target, value }`; nodes are created from the ids, and an optional `nodes` list sets labels. The layout is layered and deterministic: a node sits one layer after its latest source, nodes that nothing leaves line up on the right edge, and a fixed number of relaxation passes places nodes near the nodes they exchange flow with. Repeated source and target pairs are added up. Flows with a value that is not above zero, flows from a node to itself and flows that close a loop are left out and reported in a message. `variant` chooses solid nodes with tinted ribbons or outlined nodes with hairline-edged ribbons; ribbon opacity comes from tokens (`linkOpacity`), never a gradient. Do not use it for a few categories without stages (use `DonutChart` or `BarChart`), for flows that loop back, or for more than a few dozen nodes.

import { Sankey } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- links*: SankeyLink[] - `{ source, target, value }` flows between node ids. Repeated pairs are added up. An empty array shows `emptyText`.
- nodes: SankeyNode[] - `{ id, label? }` entries to set labels. Ids that only appear in `links` become nodes labelled with the id; nodes that no flow touches are left out.
- variant: 'flat' | 'outline' = 'flat' - `flat` solid nodes and tinted ribbons; `outline` empty nodes with a tone coloured edge and ribbons with a hairline edge.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height of the drawing: 220, 320 or 440 (an explicit `height` wins).
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Vertical space between the nodes of one layer: 6, 12 or 22 px.
- tone: 'auto' | 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'auto' - `auto` gives each node the next chart colour and colours a ribbon like its source; any other value paints the whole diagram in that token.
- linkOpacity: 'soft' | 'medium' | 'strong' = 'medium' - Ribbon opacity: 15, 30 or 45 percent of the tone. Labels stay readable over all three.
- showValues: boolean = true - Print the node value after its label.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats values in labels, tooltips and the table. Default: grouped number with up to two decimals.
- label: string - Accessible name of the diagram. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- title: string - Visible heading above the diagram; also the name when there is no `label`.
- description: string - Visible sentence under the title.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown when there is no flow to draw.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width until the container is measured. The diagram then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel).
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when `links` is not an array of flows. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `links` as `{ source, target, value }` with ids that name the nodes; add `nodes` only to set labels.
- Values must be numbers above zero. Do not pass flows that loop back (A to B to A); they are dropped.
- Always set `label` or `title`; use `valueFormatter` for units.
- Use `variant="outline"` for dense pages, `tone` for one-colour diagrams, `linkOpacity` to tune ribbon weight. Never add gradients.
- Do not use a Sankey for categories without stages, or for more than a few dozen nodes. Use BarChart, DonutChart or Treemap.

Accessibility:
- The drawing is one SVG `role="img"` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by an automatic summary (nodes, flows, layers).
- A visually hidden table lists every flow as From, To and Value (first 200 rows). It is the text alternative; the nodes and ribbons also carry native tooltips ("Shipped to Lost: 10").
- Colour is never the only signal: every node that has room is labelled with its name and value, ribbons are matched to their ends by position and tooltip, and the table names every flow. Ribbon tints stay at 45 percent or less so labels over them keep their contrast in light and dark.
- The `outline` variant adds a hairline edge to ribbons and an edge to nodes, so shapes remain visible in forced-colors mode.
- The diagram is not interactive and has no motion. It scales to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel), so text keeps its real size and nothing overflows at 320px.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<Sankey
  label="Sample order outcomes"
  :links="[
    { source: 'Orders', target: 'Shipped', value: 80 },
    { source: 'Orders', target: 'Returned', value: 20 },
    { source: 'Shipped', target: 'Delivered', value: 70 },
    { source: 'Shipped', target: 'Lost', value: 10 }
  ]"
/>
```

Example: Variant: flat and outline
```vue

</script>

  <Sankey variant="flat" size="sm" label="Sample outcomes, flat" :links="flows" />
  <Sankey variant="outline" size="sm" label="Sample outcomes, outline" :links="flows" />
</div>
```

# ScatterChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG scatter, bubble and connected-scatter chart with several series, marker shapes per series, nice numeric axes, grid styles, axis titles and an optional linear trend line.

Use `ScatterChart` to show how two numbers relate across many items (price against rating, load against latency). Pass `points` as `{ x, y, size?, label?, series? }`; points with the same `series` name form one series. `variant` picks the mark: `scatter` plots markers, `bubble` scales the area of each marker with `size`, `connected` also joins the points of a series in the order given (a path over time). Series differ by marker shape as well as colour (`markerShape="series"`, the default), so the chart never relies on colour alone. Both axes are numeric with nice ticks, negative values draw a zero line, and the plot never leaves the container: the chart fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px) and thins tick labels instead of overflowing at 320px. `trend` adds the least squares line of each series (dotted) and states its equation in the text summary. Points with a non-finite x or y are skipped and counted in the summary. Every point is available to assistive technology through the hidden data table (cut at 200 rows); each marker also has a native tooltip. Use `LineChart` when x is an ordered category, `Heatmap` for dense two-dimensional counts and `Sparkline` for a tiny inline trend.

import { ScatterChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- points*: { x: number; y: number; size?: number; label?: string; series?: string }[] - The data. `series` groups points (points without one form the series `Points`), `label` names a point in the tooltip, the table and `showValues`, `size` is the bubble area. Non-finite coordinates are skipped; an empty array shows `emptyText`.
- variant: 'scatter' | 'bubble' | 'connected' = 'scatter' - `scatter` markers of one size, `bubble` markers whose area follows `size` (points without a size get the smallest), `connected` also draws a line per series in data order.
- markerShape: 'circle' | 'square' | 'diamond' | 'triangle' | 'series' = 'series' - Marker shape. `series` gives each series its own shape (circle, square, diamond, triangle), which the legend repeats; a single series is drawn with circles. A fixed shape applies to every series.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Plot height 200 / 280 / 360 viewBox units, marker radius 3.5 / 4.5 / 6 (bubbles 3 to 12, 4 to 18, 5 to 24) and the spacing of the figure.
- grid: 'none' | 'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'full' | 'dashed' = 'full' - `horizontal` a line at each y tick, `vertical` at each x tick, `full` both, `dashed` both dashed, `none` no lines.
- xTitle: string - Title of the x axis, printed under the plot (cut to the plot width, the full text is in a tooltip).
- yTitle: string - Title of the y axis, printed rotated at the start edge (cut to the plot height).
- trend: boolean = false - Draw the least squares line of each series as a dotted line across its x range, cut where it leaves the plot. A series needs two points with different x. The equation and R squared are in the text summary and the tooltip.
- showValues: boolean = false - Print the label of each point (or `x, y`) next to it. Labels that would overlap, or fall outside the chart, are left out; none are drawn beyond 60 points.
- showAxis: boolean = true - Tick labels and the two axis lines.
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend of series with their marker shape; `auto` shows it for more than one series. A trend adds a "Linear trend" entry.
- tones: Record<string, 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted'> - Tone per series name, e.g. `{ Errors: "danger" }`. Series without an entry cycle through chart-1..5.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats y ticks, sizes and tooltips (and x when `xFormatter` is not set).
- xFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats x ticks, x values in tooltips and in the data table.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it; an auto-generated summary is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- title: string - Visible heading above the plot. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there is no valid point.
- loading: boolean = false - Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.
- loadingText: string = 'Loading chart' - Message of the loading placeholder.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size` (default height 280).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `points` is not an array or an entry has a non-numeric `x` or `y`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `points` as flat `{ x, y }` objects and group them with `series`, never as nested arrays per series.
- Always set `label` (or `title`) to say what the chart shows, and `xTitle` / `yTitle` with the units.
- Use `variant="bubble"` only when a third number matters and give every point a `size`; use `connected` only for points that have an order.
- Leave `markerShape` on `series` when there is more than one series, so series do not differ by colour alone.
- Use `trend` for a straight-line relation; it needs at least two different x values per series.
- Provide `valueFormatter` and `xFormatter` for units and currency. Size with `class` and `size`, not `width` / `height`.

Accessibility:
- The plot is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (point and series counts, x and y ranges, trend equations, skipped points).
- A visually hidden data table follows the chart with one row per point (label, x, y and size), so every value is readable as text; it is cut at 200 rows and says so in its caption.
- Series are told apart by marker shape (and by dash pattern when connected), not by colour alone; the HTML legend repeats the shapes. A trend line is dotted and listed in the legend.
- Each marker has a native `<title>` tooltip with the series, label, x, y and size. Individual points are not tab stops: the data table is the keyboard and screen reader alternative.
- Axis text is 12px with tabular figures and the SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px), so labels keep their size and thin out instead of overflowing at 320px. Tick labels are kept inside the viewBox.
- In forced-colors mode markers, lines and trend lines use the system text colour; shapes and dash patterns carry the series. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<ScatterChart class="max-w-xl" label="Sample data: score against hours" x-title="Hours" y-title="Score" :points="[   { x: 12, y: 31, label: 'Alder' }, { x: 18, y: 38, label: 'Birch' }, { x: 25, y: 44, label: 'Cedar' },   { x: 31, y: 41, label: 'Dogwood' }, { x: 39, y: 58, label: 'Elm' }, { x: 47, y: 61, label: 'Fir' },   { x: 55, y: 70, label: 'Gum' }, { x: 63, y: 66, label: 'Hazel' }, ]" />
```

```vue
  <ScatterChart variant="bubble" size="sm" label="Sample data: bubble" :points="[{ x: 1, y: 3, size: 4 }, { x: 2, y: 5, size: 9 }, { x: 4, y: 4, size: 2 }, { x: 5, y: 8, size: 16 }, { x: 7, y: 6, size: 6 }]" />
```

```vue
  y-title="Revenue"
  :value-formatter="(n) => '$' + n"
  :points="[   { x: 12, y: 31, label: 'Alder' }, { x: 18, y: 38, label: 'Birch' }, { x: 25, y: 44, label: 'Cedar' },   { x: 31, y: 41, label: 'Dogwood' }, { x: 39, y: 58, label: 'Elm' }, { x: 47, y: 61, label: 'Fir' },   { x: 55, y: 70, label: 'Gum' }, { x: 63, y: 66, label: 'Hazel' }, ]"
/>
```

Example: Size
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <ScatterChart v-for="s in ['sm', 'md', 'lg']" :key="s" :size="s" variant="bubble" :label="'Sample data: size ' + s" :points="[{ x: 1, y: 3, size: 4 }, { x: 2, y: 5, size: 9 }, { x: 4, y: 4, size: 2 }, { x: 5, y: 8, size: 16 }]" />
</div>
```

Example: Negative values and custom tones
```vue
<ScatterChart
  class="max-w-xl"
  label="Sample data: change against baseline"
  x-title="Change in input"
  y-title="Change in output"
  :tones="{ Gains: 'success', Losses: 'danger' }"
  :points="[
    { x: 4, y: 6, series: 'Gains' }, { x: 8, y: 9, series: 'Gains' }, { x: 2, y: 3, series: 'Gains' },
    { x: -3, y: -5, series: 'Losses' }, { x: -7, y: -8, series: 'Losses' }, { x: -5, y: -2, series: 'Losses' },
  ]"
/>
```

Example: Empty, loading and bad values
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <ScatterChart label="Orders" :points="[]" empty-text="No orders yet" />
  <ScatterChart label="Orders" :points="[]" loading />
  <ScatterChart size="sm" label="Sample data: skipped points" :points="[{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: Number.NaN, y: 4 }, { x: 3, y: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY }, { x: 4, y: 5 }]" />
</div>
```

# Sparkline
group: data-display / Charts
Tiny inline trend (pure SVG) as a line, area, bar or win/loss strip, for tables, KPI tiles and lists.

Use `Sparkline` to show the shape of a short series next to a number. It has no axes, grid or tooltips: use `LineChart` when readers need values. The rendered size is controlled with `class` (default `w-24`, height follows the viewBox aspect ratio); `width`/`height` only set the viewBox proportions. `variant` picks the form: `line`, `area`, `bar` (one bar per value from a zero baseline) or `winloss` (equal squares above the centre line for positive values, below it for negative ones; a short tick on the line for zero). NaN, Infinity and null values become gaps, a single point is drawn as a dot and a flat series is a horizontal line.

import { Sparkline } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- data*: number[] - Series values. Non-finite entries are skipped (gap in the line).
- tone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'chart-1' - Colour token of the line, area and dots. Unknown values fall back to chart-1.
- variant: 'line' | 'area' | 'bar' | 'winloss' = 'line' - Form of the sparkline. `line` and `area` join the points (see `curve`); `bar` draws a bar per value from a zero baseline; `winloss` draws equal squares above (positive) or below (negative) a centre line. When omitted, `area` decides between `line` and `area`.
- area: boolean = false - Soft fill under the line. Same as `variant="area"`; `variant` wins when both are set.
- curve: 'linear' | 'smooth' | 'step' = 'linear' - How `line` and `area` join points: straight, a monotone smooth curve that never overshoots the data, or steps. Ignored by `bar` and `winloss`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Rendered width: `w-16`, `w-24` or `w-32`. `class` overrides it.
- negativeTone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'danger' - Colour token of negative values in `bar` and `winloss`. Position below the baseline is the primary cue; colour only repeats it.
- strokeWidth: number = 1.5 - Line width in viewBox units. Invalid values fall back to the default.
- width: number = 96 - ViewBox width (aspect ratio only; size the element with `class`).
- height: number = 32 - ViewBox height.
- label: string - Accessible label of the image. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); an auto-generated summary of the numbers is only the fallback when strict mode is off.
- showLast: boolean = false - Emphasise the last value with a dot (`line` and `area` only).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; use it to set the rendered size (`w-32`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `data` is not an array. An empty array draws nothing.

Rules:
- Use Sparkline for inline trends only; use LineChart when axes or tooltips are needed.
- Set the rendered size with `class` (`w-32 h-auto`), not with `width`/`height` (those are viewBox units).
- Always pair it with the actual number; pass a descriptive `label` when the trend matters.
- Use `variant="winloss"` for outcomes per period (pass/fail, up/down), `bar` for discrete counts and `line` or `area` for continuous trends.
- Choose `tone` semantically (success for good, danger for bad) rather than decoratively.

Accessibility:
- Renders `<svg role="img">` with an automatic `aria-label` summary (point count, first/last value, min and max); override with `label`.
- Empty data is announced as "No data". The `winloss` variant is announced as "Wins and losses: N wins, N losses, N even" and shows the sign by position (above or below the centre line), not by colour; `bar` negatives sit below a visible baseline.
- It is a small inline image (default `w-24`) that never widens its container; put several in a `flex-wrap` row so a phone does not scroll sideways. The trend is always paired with the number in text.
- Purely visual: never rely on the sparkline alone to convey a value: show the number next to it.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <Sparkline :data="[3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 7, 10]" label="Sample data: steady rise" />
  <Sparkline :data="[3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 7, 10]" tone="success" area show-last label="Sample data: rise with last value marked" />
  <Sparkline :data="[10, 8, 9, 5, 6, 3]" tone="danger" class="w-32" label="Sample data: decline" />
</div>
```

Example: Variant: line, area, bar, winloss
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-6">
  <Sparkline variant="line" :data="[3, -2, 5, 4, -1, 6, 2]" label="Sample data: line" />
  <Sparkline variant="area" :data="[3, -2, 5, 4, -1, 6, 2]" label="Sample data: area" />
  <Sparkline variant="bar" :data="[3, -2, 5, 4, -1, 6, 2]" label="Sample data: bars with negatives" />
  <Sparkline variant="winloss" :data="[1, -1, 1, 1, 0, -1, 1]" label="Sample data: wins and losses" />
</div>
```

Example: Curve and size
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-6">
  <Sparkline curve="linear" size="sm" :data="[3, 8, 4, 9, 5]" label="Sample data: linear" />
  <Sparkline curve="smooth" size="md" :data="[3, 8, 4, 9, 5]" label="Sample data: smooth" />
  <Sparkline curve="step" variant="area" size="lg" :data="[3, 8, 4, 9, 5]" label="Sample data: step area" />
</div>
```

Example: In a card
```vue
<Card class="max-w-xs">
  <CardContent class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
    <div>
      <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sample metric</p>
      <p class="text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums">30</p>
      <Badge variant="success">+12%</Badge>
    </div>
    <Sparkline :data="[12, 15, 14, 18, 22, 21, 26, 30]" tone="success" area show-last class="w-28" label="Sample metric rose from 12 to 30 over 8 points" />
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

Example: Gaps and edge cases
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <Sparkline :data="[1, 4, Number.NaN, 6, 3, 7]" label="Sample data: series with a gap" />
  <Sparkline :data="[5]" label="Sample data: one point" />
  <Sparkline :data="[2, 2, 2, 2]" tone="muted" label="Sample data: flat series" />
  <Sparkline :data="[]" label="Sample data: no points" />
</div>
```

# Treemap
group: data-display / Charts
Hierarchical tile chart: area follows value, tiles are squarified, groups can be shown as nested containers, and every tile is keyboard reachable.

Use `Treemap` to show how a total splits into parts and parts of parts (disk use by folder, stock by category, spend by team), when the share matters more than the exact value. Tile area is proportional to the value; the layout is squarified so tiles stay close to square, and it is deterministic (same data, same picture). A node with `children` takes the sum of them as its value, a node without children needs a positive number. `variant` chooses flat tinted tiles, nested containers with a header per group, or soft outlined tiles. `colorBy="depth"` paints everything in one `tone` and makes deeper levels denser; `colorBy="series"` gives every top-level group its own chart colour (with a legend). Labels are written only into tiles that are big enough (`labels="auto"`); every tile keeps its full name in `aria-label` and a native tooltip. Do not use it for exact comparison of many values (use `BarChart`), for time series, or for more than a few hundred visible tiles; tiles smaller than 2px are skipped and counted in a message. No drill-down: it is a static picture with a text alternative.

import { Treemap } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- data*: TreemapDatum[] - `{ label, value?, children? }` nodes. A node with children takes the sum of them; a leaf needs a number above zero. Other entries are left out and counted in a message. An empty array shows `emptyText`.
- variant: 'flat' | 'nested' | 'outline' = 'flat' - `flat` tinted tiles with a seam, `nested` draws every group as a container with a header and puts its tiles inside, `outline` soft tiles with a tone coloured edge.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height of the drawing: 200, 300 or 420 (an explicit `height` wins).
- gap: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between tiles: 0, 1, 2 or 4 px.
- tone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'chart-1' - Colour token of the tiles with `colorBy="depth"`. Tiles are a 15 to 45 percent tint so the label keeps its contrast.
- colorBy: 'depth' | 'series' = 'depth' - `depth` uses `tone` for everything and makes deeper levels denser; `series` gives each top-level group its own chart colour (cycling chart-1 to chart-5, in input order).
- labels: 'auto' | 'none' = 'auto' - `auto` writes the label into every tile that is wide and tall enough (long labels are cut with an ellipsis); `none` leaves tiles unlabelled. Names and tooltips are always there.
- showValues: boolean = true - Print the value under the label when the tile is tall enough and the value fits.
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend of the top-level groups. `auto` shows it with `colorBy="series"` and two or more groups.
- maxDepth: number = 4 - Levels that are drawn, 1 to 8. Deeper nodes are folded into the node at this level, so totals stay right.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats values in labels, names, tooltips and the table. Default: grouped number with up to two decimals.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- title: string - Visible heading above the chart; also the name when there is no `label`.
- description: string - Visible sentence under the title.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown when there is nothing to draw.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel).
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when `data` is not an array of nodes. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `data` as `{ label, value?, children? }`; give leaves a positive number, never give a group a `value` (it is the sum of its children).
- Always set `label` or `title`; label values and units with `valueFormatter`.
- Use `variant="nested"` when groups matter, `flat` for a plain share picture, `outline` on dense pages. Use `colorBy="series"` only when the top-level groups are the story; otherwise keep one tone.
- Use `maxDepth` to cut deep trees. Tiny tiles are skipped automatically; do not pre-filter just to keep the picture clean, tell readers where the rest is.
- Do not use a treemap for exact comparison, negative values or time series. Use BarChart, LineChart or DonutChart.

Accessibility:
- The drawing is an SVG `role="group"` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by an automatic summary (item count, top-level groups, total). It is a group, not an image, because its tiles are focusable.
- Every tile is `role="img"` with an `aria-label` of its full path, value and share of the total ("Cables / Fibre: 20 (20% of total)"), even when its text label is hidden or cut.
- Keyboard: one tile is in the tab order (roving tabindex). Arrow Right/Down move to the next tile, Arrow Left/Up to the previous, Home and End to the first and last, in layout order (largest first). Focus shows a thick ring in the `ring` token, also in forced-colors mode.
- The full name of the focused or hovered tile is written below the chart (hidden from assistive technology, which reads the tile name itself). Tiles also carry a native tooltip.
- A visually hidden data table lists every group and leaf with its value (first 200 rows). It is the text alternative for the whole chart.
- Colour is never the only signal: tiles are labelled, groups have header text, and the table names every item. Tints stay at 45 percent or less so the foreground label keeps its contrast in light and dark.
- There is no motion. The SVG scales to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS pixel) so labels keep their real size and nothing overflows at 320px.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<Treemap
  label="Sample stock by category"
  :data="[
    { label: 'Cables', value: 68 },
    { label: 'Racks', value: 30 },
    { label: 'Tools', value: 10 },
    { label: 'Spares', value: 6 }
  ]"
/>
```

Example: Variant: flat, nested and outline

```vue
  { label: 'Cables', children: [{ label: 'Copper', value: 40 }, { label: 'Fibre', value: 20 }, { label: 'Patch leads', value: 8 }] },

  <Treemap variant="nested" size="sm" label="Sample stock, nested" :data="stock" />
  <Treemap variant="outline" size="sm" label="Sample stock, outline" :data="stock" />
</div>
```

```vue
  <Treemap size="md" label="Sample, medium" :data="[{ label: 'A', value: 5 }, { label: 'B', value: 3 }, { label: 'C', value: 2 }]" />
```

# WaterfallChart
group: data-display / Charts
Dependency-free SVG waterfall chart: a start value, increases and decreases, subtotals and a total, as bars, steps or lollipops, vertical or horizontal, with connectors and a pattern or marker for decreases.

Use `WaterfallChart` to show how a value gets from one total to another through a series of changes (a budget, a revenue bridge, a stock movement). Pass `items` as `{ label, value?, type? }`: the first item is the `start` by default, the others are `delta`s, and `subtotal` / `total` items show the running total at that point (their `value` is not used). `variant` picks the drawing: `bars` floats a bar between the old and the new level, `steps` draws a staircase of the running total, `lollipop` a stem with a head at the new level. Increases and decreases never differ by colour alone: decreases are hatched (`bars`), dashed (`steps`) or hollow (`lollipop`), values carry a sign (`+30`, `−12` with a real minus sign) and the data table names each bar. `connectors` draws a thin line from the end of one bar to the start of the next at the running total. A running total below zero is drawn below the baseline. Items without a finite value read "n/a" and change nothing. Use `BarChart` for independent categories and `LineChart` for a trend over time.

import { WaterfallChart } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items*: { label: string; value?: number | null; type?: 'start' | 'delta' | 'subtotal' | 'total' }[] - Bars in order. `start` sets the running total (default for the first item), `delta` changes it (default for the others), `subtotal` and `total` show it (their `value` is ignored). A start or delta without a finite value reads "n/a". An empty array shows `emptyText`.
- variant: 'bars' | 'steps' | 'lollipop' = 'bars' - `bars` floating bars (decreases hatched), `steps` a staircase of treads and risers (decreases dashed), `lollipop` stems with a head at the new level (increase filled, decrease hollow, total square).
- orientation: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - `vertical` puts the bars side by side along the x axis; `horizontal` stacks them as rows with the labels at the start.
- connectors: boolean = true - Thin dotted lines from the end of each bar to the start of the next, at the running total.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Chart height 160 / 240 / 320 when vertical, height of a row 24 / 32 / 40 when horizontal (at most 960 in total).
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between neighbouring bars: `sm` is wide bars, `lg` is narrow bars.
- showValues: boolean = false - Print the change (`+80`, `−25`) or the total at the end of each bar. Labels that do not fit are left out; they are also in the table.
- showGrid: boolean = true - Gridlines at each tick of the value axis.
- showAxis: boolean = true - Tick labels, category labels and the zero line.
- integerTicks: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Value axis ticks on whole numbers only. `auto` does this when every value is an integer (counts, so no 0.5 tick); `true` forces it; `false` always allows fractional ticks.
- showLegend: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - Legend of increase, decrease and total with the marking of the variant; `auto` shows it when more than one kind of bar is present.
- positiveTone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'success' - Tone of increases.
- negativeTone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'danger' - Tone of decreases.
- totalTone: 'chart-1' | 'chart-2' | 'chart-3' | 'chart-4' | 'chart-5' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'muted' = 'primary' - Tone of the start, subtotal and total bars.
- valueFormatter: (n: number) => string - Formats axis ticks, values and tooltips. Defaults to compact (axis) / grouped (tooltip) numbers.
- label: string - Accessible name of the chart image. Required unless `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it.
- title: string - Visible heading above the chart. It also names the chart when `label` is not set.
- description: string - Visible description under the title. The image points to it with `aria-describedby`, next to the generated summary.
- emptyText: string = 'No data' - Shown (as role="img") when there are no items.
- loading: boolean = false - Show a busy placeholder (`role="status"`, `aria-busy`) with `loadingText` instead of the chart.
- loadingText: string = 'Loading chart' - Message of the loading placeholder.
- width: number = 480 - ViewBox width used until the container is measured. The chart then fills its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px).
- height: number - ViewBox height. Overrides `size`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element (`<figure>`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `items` is not an array, an item has no `label`, an unknown `type`, or a `start` / `delta` has no numeric `value`. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `items` in order: the opening value first, then the changes (negative numbers for decreases), then `{ label, type: "total" }`; do not compute running totals yourself.
- Use `type: "subtotal"` for an intermediate sum and `type: "total"` for the closing bar; their `value` is ignored.
- Set `label` (or `title`) to say what the bridge shows and use `valueFormatter` for currency or units; `showValues` prints signed changes.
- Use `variant="steps"` or `"lollipop"` for many items, `orientation="horizontal"` for long labels.
- Keep the default tones (increase `success`, decrease `danger`, total `primary`) unless the data has a different meaning; the hatch, dash and hollow head carry the sign regardless of tone.
- Size with `class`, `size` and `gap`, not `width` / `height`.

Accessibility:
- The chart is one `<svg role="img">` named by `label` (or `title`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) and described by the visible `description` and a generated text summary (bar count, start and end level, number of increases and decreases).
- A visually hidden data table lists every bar as a row named with its kind ("Refunds (decrease)") with the signed change and the running total, so no number depends on the picture.
- Increase and decrease are never told apart by colour alone: decreases are hatched (bars), dashed (steps) or hollow (lollipop), values carry a plus or minus sign, and the legend repeats the markings. Each mark has a native `<title>` tooltip.
- The SVG is sized to its container (1 unit = 1 CSS px): category labels are shortened (full text in a tooltip) and thinned when crowded, value labels that do not fit are left out, so nothing overflows at 320px.
- In forced-colors mode marks and the hatch use the system text colour; the hatch, dashes and shapes carry the meaning. The loading placeholder is a polite `role="status"` region marked busy; it does not animate.

Example: Minimal

```vue
<WaterfallChart class="max-w-xl" label="Sample data: balance bridge" :items="[{ label: 'Opening', value: 120 }, { label: 'Sales', value: 80 }, { label: 'Refunds', value: -25 }, { label: 'Hosting', value: -40 }, { label: 'Services', value: 35 }, { label: 'Closing', type: 'total' }]" />
```

# ChatMessage
group: data-display / Chat
One chat message with a role, a bubble, plain or card surface, an avatar, a header, a status written as text and hover or focus actions.

Use `ChatMessage` for each turn in a conversation: a person writing, a reply, a system notice or a tool result. It knows nothing about who the participants are (no vendor or model is baked in) and renders whatever you put in the default slot, or a `markdown` string through the library `Markdown` component. Put messages in a `ChatThread` for the scrolling log, follow behaviour and announcements.

**Role** (`user`, `assistant`, `system`, `tool`) picks the colours and the default side (`user` sits at the end, the rest at the start). Role is also spoken: a visually hidden phrase ("You said", "Assistant said", "System message", "Tool result") is placed before the content, so it is not carried by alignment or colour alone. Set `role-label` to name the speaker ("Ada said").

**Status** is text with an icon where one fits: `sending`, `sent`, `error` (failed to send) and `streaming` (responding). The text is not a live region by default, because a thread of fifty messages would announce all of them; let `ChatThread` summarise, or set `live` for a single stand-alone message.

**Actions** (copy, retry) sit in the `actions` slot. They fade in on hover and when anything inside the message has focus, they are always visible on touch screens and in forced-colors mode, and they stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree while faded, so a keyboard or screen reader user never loses them.

**Markdown** goes through the same sanitising renderer as `Markdown`: raw HTML is never parsed, `javascript:` links and unsafe image sources are dropped, external links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Remote images are shown as links, not loaded, unless you set `show-images`. Inline `data:` pictures are shown.

import { ChatMessage } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system' | 'tool' = 'assistant' - Author kind. Sets the surface colours, the default side and the hidden speaker phrase. Unknown values fall back to `assistant`.
- variant: 'bubble' | 'plain' | 'card' = 'bubble' - `bubble` is a tinted box, `plain` has no box (transcripts, wide text), `card` is a bordered panel. Unknown values fall back to `bubble`.
- align: 'start' | 'end' - Side of the thread. Defaults to `end` for `user` and `start` otherwise; sets `data-align`. The row uses logical direction, so it mirrors in right-to-left. Unknown values use the default.
- name: string - Participant or tool name shown in the header.
- datetime: string | number | Date - When the message was sent. A valid value renders `<time datetime>` with the ISO string; an invalid value is ignored.
- timeLabel: string - Visible time text that replaces the formatted time ("Just now"). Shown as plain text when `datetime` is missing or invalid.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for the formatted time. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `en` (not the runtime locale), so server and client print the same text. A bad value falls back to the runtime default.
- timeZone: string - IANA time zone for the formatted time, for example `UTC`. Set it when the page is server-rendered so both renders print the same text. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `UTC` (not the runtime zone). A bad value falls back to local time.
- roleLabel: string - Visually hidden speaker phrase read before the content ("Ada said"). A trailing colon is added for you. Defaults to a phrase for the role.
- status: 'sending' | 'sent' | 'error' | 'streaming' - Delivery or generation state, written as text ("Sending", "Sent", "Failed to send", "Responding"). `sending` and `streaming` set `aria-busy` on the message. Unknown values show nothing.
- statusLabel: string - Status text that replaces the default, for translation or a more specific message ("Could not reach the server").
- live: boolean = false - Make the status text a polite `role="status"` region. Leave off inside a `ChatThread`.
- markdown: string - Markdown source rendered with `Markdown` (size sm, streaming-aware while `status="streaming"`). Wins over the default slot, an empty string renders an empty body.
- showImages: boolean = false - Load http(s) images found in `markdown`. Off by default: they become links.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Root element, for example `li` inside a list or `article`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Message content. Ignored when `markdown` is set.
- avatar - Avatar or icon beside the message. Decorative unless it carries text; the hidden role phrase already names the speaker.
- header ({ author?: string; datetime: Date | null }) - Replaces the default header (name and time).
- actions - Copy, retry or other buttons. Every control needs an accessible name.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a button, link or `role="button"` element in the `actions` slot has no accessible name (give icon-only buttons an `aria-label`).

Rules:
- Inline images blur when a surrounding `ConfigProvider` sets `blurMedia` (privacy, not decoration); there is no prop on this component.
- Use `role` for who wrote it and keep the default `role-label` unless a name reads better ("Ada said"); never rely on alignment or colour to say who spoke.
- Give every icon-only control in the `actions` slot an `aria-label`; use `IconButton` with `label`.
- Pass streamed Markdown through `markdown` with `status="streaming"`; do not build HTML strings and never use `v-html`.
- Leave `live` off inside a `ChatThread`; the thread announces a short summary instead of each status.
- Set `time-zone` (and `locale`) when the page is server-rendered; a `time` element needs a valid `datetime`.
- Do not name a vendor or a model in the component; pass names through `name` and `role-label`.

Accessibility:
- The speaker is named in text, not by side or colour: a visually hidden phrase ("You said", "Assistant said", "System message", "Tool result", or `role-label`) comes first in the content.
- A valid `datetime` renders a native `<time datetime>`; the visible text can be changed with `time-label`.
- Status is visible text (plus an icon for `error` and `sent`). It is not a live region unless `live` is set, so a thread does not announce every message; `ChatThread` owns one polite summary region. `sending` and `streaming` set `aria-busy`.
- Actions are ordinary buttons that fade in on `:hover` and `:focus-within`. They are never `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`, so they keep their place in the tab order and the accessibility tree; touch (coarse pointer) and forced-colors modes show them all the time. Every control needs an accessible name.
- Markdown output uses real lists, headings, links and code; external links announce that they open in a new tab. Long words and URLs wrap; code scrolls inside its own region, so the message reflows at 320px.
- The row uses logical properties and a reversed flex direction, so `dir="rtl"` mirrors it. Bubble surfaces get a transparent border that forced-colors mode draws. Colour pairs are the ones the contrast test covers.

Example: A short exchange
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <ChatMessage role="user">Which environment did the last deploy go to?</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="assistant">Staging. Production still runs the previous release.</ChatMessage>
</div>
```

```vue
  <ChatMessage role="assistant">Checking the queue now.</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="tool" name="queue_depth">{ "queue": "kestrel-freight", "depth": 0 }</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="system">The session moved to the staging workspace.</ChatMessage>
</div>
```

```vue

  <ChatMessage variant="bubble" role="assistant">Bubble: a tinted box.</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage variant="plain" role="assistant">Plain: no box, for transcripts and long text that should use the full width.</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage variant="card" role="assistant">Card: a bordered panel.</ChatMessage>
</div>
```

```vue

  <ChatMessage role="assistant" align="end">An assistant message pushed to the end.</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="user" align="start">A user message kept at the start.</ChatMessage>
```

```vue
  <ChatMessage role="user" status="sent">Report uploaded.</ChatMessage>
```

# ChatThread
group: data-display / Chat
Scrolling conversation log that follows the latest message, with day separators, a typing indicator, a jump button, older-message loading and one polite announcement region.

Use `ChatThread` around `ChatMessage` items. It is a labelled, focusable `role="log"` scroll region. Give the root a height (`class="h-96"`, or let a flex parent size it); the log fills it and scrolls.

**Two ways to fill it.** Pass `messages` and draw each one in the `message` slot (day separators, unread count and announcements need the data), or put `ChatMessage` elements in the default slot for a short, static transcript.

**Follow.** While the reader is at the bottom, new and growing messages keep the view at the bottom. Scrolling up stops following and shows a "Jump to latest" button (with the number of messages that arrived meanwhile). The button is a normal focusable button; using it scrolls down, resumes following and moves focus back to the log. `follow-change` reports the state.

**Announcements.** The log is `aria-live="off"`, so assistive technology never reads a streamed reply token by token. A single sibling `role="status"` region carries a short summary ("2 new messages", or the typing label when it appears), collected for one second so a burst is one sentence, and cleared after a few seconds. Set `announcement` to supply your own text. Nothing is announced for the first render or for older messages added at the top.

**Days.** `item-date` (a property name or a function) groups messages by calendar day in `time-zone`; labels use `Intl` in `locale` and say "Today" and "Yesterday" once mounted. All rows are rendered, which is fine for thousands of simple messages; for very large histories load older pages with `load-older` instead of rendering everything.

Attributes you pass (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `id`, `data-*`) land on the log element; `class` and `style` land on the root.

import { ChatThread } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- messages: readonly T[] - Messages as data, each drawn by the `message` slot. `null` counts as empty. Omit it to use the default slot.
- itemKey: string | ((item: T, index: number) => string | number) - Stable key per message (property name or function). Needed to tell appended from prepended messages and for stable DOM. Defaults to the index.
- itemDate: string | ((item: T, index: number) => string | number | Date) - When a message was sent, for day separators (property name or function). Items without a valid date join the day before them. Without it there are no separators.
- label: string - Accessible name of the log. Required: set `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- follow: boolean = true - Stay at the bottom while the reader is at the bottom; scrolling up stops it and shows the jump button. Off makes a plain scrolling list with no button.
- typing: boolean | string = false - Show the typing or streaming indicator at the end (a `TypingIndicator` plus its text). A string names who is typing ("Mira" reads "Mira is typing"). Sets `aria-busy` and announces once when it appears.
- density: 'compact' | 'default' | 'relaxed' = 'default' - Spacing between messages and around the thread. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- canLoadOlder: boolean = false - More history exists: shows the load-older control above the first message.
- loadingOlder: boolean = false - A load is running: disables the control and blocks repeated requests.
- autoLoadOlder: boolean = false - Also emit `load-older` once when the reader scrolls to the top. It fires again only after `loadingOlder` ends or `canLoadOlder` changes, so it cannot loop.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for day labels. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `en` (not the runtime locale), so server and client print the same text.
- timeZone: string - IANA time zone that decides which day a message belongs to (Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `UTC` (not the runtime zone).).
- now: string | number | Date - The current time, for "Today" and "Yesterday". Defaults to the clock after mount (so a server render prints plain dates); pass it for tests or server rendering.
- announcement: string - Text to announce politely (collected for one second) instead of the automatic "N new messages". Use it with the default slot, which cannot be counted.
- labels: Partial<ChatThreadLabels> - Replace any built-in text: `jump`, `unread(count)`, `loadOlder`, `loadingOlder`, `typing`, `typingBy(name)`, `empty`, `newMessages(count)`. Use it to translate.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge on the root; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Static `ChatMessage` elements, used when `messages` is not set.
- message ({ message: T; index: number; id: string | number }) - Draws one message from `messages`. Required when `messages` is set.
- empty - Shown when there are no messages (default "No messages yet").
- typing - Replaces the typing indicator content.
- load-older ({ loading: boolean; load: () => void }) - Replaces the load-older button. Call `load` to emit `load-older`.
- day ({ label: string; date: string }) - Replaces the text of a day separator. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Events:
- load-older - More history is wanted: the button was pressed, or the top was reached with `autoLoadOlder`.
- follow-change [following: boolean] - The reader started or stopped following the latest message.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the log has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `messages` is set but there is no `message` slot to draw each item.

Rules:
- Always name the thread with `label` and give the root a height (`class="h-96"`), otherwise nothing scrolls.
- Use `messages` with a `message` slot and set `item-key` to a stable id, so appended and prepended messages are told apart; set `item-date` for day separators.
- Do not add your own live region and never put streamed text in `announcement`; the thread announces counts only.
- Use `follow-change` to show your own state; do not scroll the log by hand (call the exposed `scrollToBottom()` if you must).
- Emit-driven history: set `can-load-older`, handle `load-older`, toggle `loading-older`, then prepend items with keys that are not reused.
- Pass `time-zone` and `now` when server rendering, so the first client render matches the server render.

Accessibility:
- The log is one element with `role="log"`, `tabindex="0"` and a required accessible name, so keyboard users can scroll it: arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down scroll natively; Home and End jump to the first and last message (and End resumes following).
- `aria-live="off"` keeps screen readers from reading the log as it grows. One sibling `role="status"` region announces a short summary at most once per second ("2 new messages", the typing label, or `announcement`), is cleared after a few seconds, and never contains message text.
- The jump button is an ordinary focusable button after the log. Pressing it scrolls to the latest message, resumes following and returns focus to the log, so focus is never lost when the button disappears.
- Day separators are text (`<time datetime>` with a localised label) between two rules drawn as borders, so they survive forced-colors mode. The typing indicator is text beside decorative `TypingIndicator` dots (hidden from assistive tech, so the thread status region is the only announcement); the dots stay still under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Scrolling is instant, with no smooth-scroll animation. The thread is `min-w-0` and wraps, so it reflows at 320px; spacing uses logical properties and mirrors in right-to-left.
- Message actions inside the log are ordinary buttons in the tab order; the log does not trap focus.

Example: A short transcript in the default slot
```vue
<ChatThread label="Export questions" class="h-64 rounded-md border">
  <ChatMessage role="user">Did the Orchard Mill export finish?</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="assistant">Yes. The file is on the reports page.</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="user">Thanks.</ChatMessage>
</ChatThread>
```

Example: Messages as data with day separators
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const messages = [
  { id: 1, role: 'user', text: 'Did the Orchard Mill export finish?', at: '2026-03-01T16:20:00Z' },
  // ...
]
</script>

<ChatThread :messages="messages" item-key="id" item-date="at" label="Export conversation" time-zone="UTC" locale="en" now="2026-03-02T12:00:00Z" class="h-96 rounded-md border">
    <template #message="{ message }">
      <ChatMessage :role="message.role" :datetime="message.at" time-zone="UTC" locale="en">{{ message.text }}</ChatMessage>
    </template>
</ChatThread>
```

Example: Follow the latest message
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const messages = ref(many(12))
const add = () => { messages.value = [...messages.value, { id: messages.value.length + 1, role: 'assistant', text: 'Sample message', at: '2026-03-02T09:05:00Z' }] }
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Button size="sm" variant="outline" class="self-start" @click="add">Add a message</Button>
  <ChatThread :messages="messages" item-key="id" label="Live conversation" class="h-48 rounded-md border">
    <template #message="{ message }">
      <ChatMessage :role="message.role" :datetime="message.at" time-zone="UTC" locale="en">{{ message.text }}</ChatMessage>
    </template>
  </ChatThread>
</div>
```

Example: Typing and streaming
```vue
<ChatThread label="Streaming reply" typing class="h-64 rounded-md border">
  <ChatMessage role="user">List the open invoices for Brightwater Co.</ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessage role="assistant" status="streaming" markdown="There are **three** open invoices:" />
</ChatThread>
```

Example: Who is typing

# CodeBlock
group: data-display / Code
Monospace code panel with copy button, line numbers, titled header and terminal frames, filename header and tabs, diff marks and line highlighting.

Use `CodeBlock` to show snippets, commands and config. It is plain monospace text: there is NO syntax highlighting and no dependency on a highlighter. Pass the source via `code` (preferred: exact whitespace) or as plain slot text (the Vue template compiler condenses whitespace in templates, so multi-line slot text loses indentation). Variations: `variant="default"` plain panel for docs; `variant="window"` plain panel that always shows the titled header bar; `variant="terminal"` the same header on an inverted console surface for shell sessions (neither draws window dots); `filename` shows the file name in the header (use it for config/source files); `tabs` (+ `v-model:activeTab`) shows several files in one block (install per package manager, multi-file examples); `diff` renders unified-diff lines (`+` added, `-` removed, `@@` hunk) with coloured backgrounds and a gutter marker; `highlight-lines` emphasises chosen lines (`[2, 4]` or `"1,3-5"`). All combine with `line-numbers`, `wrap`, `max-height`. Add `language` for the header label, `line-numbers` for a gutter, `wrap` to wrap long lines and `max-height` to cap tall blocks (the block scrolls). For a short inline value with a copy button use `DescriptionItem copyable`; for inline code in prose use the typography `Code` component.

import { CodeBlock } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- code: string - Source text. When omitted the default slot text is used.
- language: string - Header label and `data-language`. No highlighting is applied.
- variant: 'default' | 'window' | 'terminal' | 'plain' | 'flush' = 'default' - Frame: plain panel, `window` (always shows the titled header bar with the file name), `terminal` (the same header on an inverted console surface), `plain` (no frame or fill, for use inside another surface) or `flush` (full-bleed, top and bottom rules only). No variant draws window dots. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px. The line-number gutter, diff markers and header follow. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- filename: string - File name in the header, left-aligned. In `window`/`terminal` it replaces the language label; in `default` it is shown before the language label. Also the default accessible name of the code region.
- tabs: CodeBlockTab[] - `{ label: string; code: string; id?: string; language?: string }[]`. Renders a tablist and shows the active tab code; overrides `code`/slot. Invalid entries are ignored.
- activeTab: string - `v-model:activeTab`. Id (or label) of the active tab; defaults to the first tab. Unknown ids fall back to the first tab.
- diff: boolean = false - Unified-diff styling: `+` lines green, `-` lines red (the marker char moves to an aria-hidden gutter and screen readers get "Added:/Removed:"), `@@` lines muted. Copy keeps the original text including `+`/`-`.
- highlightLines: number[] | string - 1-based lines to emphasise: `[2, 4]` or `"1,3-5"`. Invalid tokens are ignored, ranges are clamped to the line count.
- lineNumbers: boolean = false - Show a line-number gutter (excluded from copy and selection).
- wrap: boolean = false - Wrap long lines instead of scrolling horizontally.
- maxHeight: string - CSS length (e.g. `16rem`). Content scrolls vertically beyond it.
- copyable: boolean = true - Show the copy button.
- label: string - Accessible name of the scrollable code region. Defaults to `filename`, else `"<language> code"`, else `"Code"`. Give blocks on one page distinct names so the regions are distinguishable.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Plain text source used when `code` is not set.

Events:
- copy [text: string] - Emitted after the code was copied to the clipboard.
- update:activeTab [id: string] - The active tab changed (`v-model:activeTab`).

Rules:
- Pass code via the `code` prop (not slot) when it contains indentation or blank lines.
- Do not expect syntax highlighting; do not add a highlighter dependency.
- Use `max-height` for long listings instead of overflow classes on a wrapper.
- Content is rendered as text, never as HTML.
- Use `variant="window"|"terminal"` for showcase/shell snippets, `filename` for files, `tabs` for multi-file or per-package-manager snippets.
- Use `diff` only with unified-diff text (+/-/@@ prefixes); use `highlight-lines` to point at lines in normal code.
- Tabs: pass `code` inside each tab; give tabs stable `id`s when using `v-model:activeTab`.

Accessibility:
- The scrollable `pre` is focusable (`tabindex=0`, shared focus ring) and is a `role="region"` named by `label`, the file name or `"<language> code"`, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys. Give blocks on one page distinct names.
- Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `select-none`, so they are neither read out nor copied.
- The copy button is named "Copy code" and keeps that name; the result ("Code copied" or "Copy failed") is announced by a sibling `role="status"` element. It is a 24px target.
- Tabs follow the ARIA tabs pattern: `tablist`/`tab`/`tabpanel`, roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End keys; the panel is labelled by the active tab.
- Diff markers are `aria-hidden`; added/removed lines get an sr-only "Added:"/"Removed:" prefix and highlighted lines an sr-only "Highlighted:" prefix, so neither relies on colour. Highlight is a background tint, never an edge stripe.
- `plain` and `flush` change only the surface (`window` and `terminal` additionally force the header bar); `size` changes text size only, so the contrast pairs stay the same as the default. The `flush` rules and the focus ring stay visible in forced-colors mode.
- The header is plain text on a bar: no window dots. Header text is 12px at full contrast. Long lines scroll inside the region (or wrap with `wrap`), so the page never scrolls sideways.

Example: Basic
```vue
<CodeBlock language="bash" label="Install command" code="pnpm add @perfect-design/ui" />
```

Example: Line numbers, wrapping and max height
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const snippet = Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, i) => `const value${i} = compute(${i})`).join('\n')
</script>

<CodeBlock language="ts" label="Generated constants" :code="snippet" line-numbers max-height="12rem" />
<CodeBlock class="mt-4" language="json" label="Wrapped JSON" wrap :copyable="false" code='{"name": "perfect-design", "description": "A very long description that wraps instead of scrolling sideways when wrap is enabled"}' />
```


```vue
  <CodeBlock variant="plain" language="bash" code="pnpm install" label="Plain frame" />
  <CodeBlock variant="flush" language="bash" code="pnpm install" label="Flush frame" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue

  <CodeBlock size="sm" language="ts" code="const small = 1" label="Small" />
  <CodeBlock size="md" language="ts" code="const medium = 2" label="Medium" />
  <CodeBlock size="lg" language="ts" code="const large = 3" label="Large" />

```

Example: Terminal

```vue
  { label: 'pnpm', id: 'pnpm', code: 'pnpm add @perfect-design/ui', language: 'bash' },
```

# CodeViewer
group: data-display / Code
Read-only code viewer with built-in tokenizers for JSON, YAML, Go, TOML and shell, foldable regions, line numbers, line highlighting and a copy button.

Use `CodeViewer` to display code or config that people read, scan and copy: config files, API payloads, scripts. It is the engine behind `YamlViewer` and `GoViewer`. Highlighting is done by small pure-TypeScript tokenizers (no highlighter dependency) and uses only semantic tokens: keywords and keys `text-primary`, strings `text-success`, numbers and types `text-info`, comments `text-muted-foreground`, functions and constants `text-foreground font-medium`.

Folding regions are computed per language: indentation for YAML, tables and brackets for TOML, brackets for JSON and Go (functions, structs, `import (...)`, `const (...)`, switch blocks), brackets plus `if/fi`, `do/done`, `case/esac` for shell, and multi-line block comments. Folded lines are not rendered at all, so folding a large file is cheap; sources above 400 visible lines also use `content-visibility: auto` per row.

Use `CodeBlock` instead for short snippets in prose (tabs, diff marks, terminal frame, no folding), `JsonViewer` to explore a live JS value as a tree, and `YamlViewer` / `GoViewer` when you want to pass a JS value rather than text. This is not an editor: there is no cursor, selection model or editing.

Parts (all carry `data-slot`): `code-viewer`, `code-viewer-header`, `code-viewer-title`, `code-viewer-scroll`, `code-viewer-code`, `code-viewer-line`, `code-viewer-gutter`, `code-viewer-fold-cell`, `code-viewer-fold`, `code-viewer-line-number`, `code-viewer-text`, `code-viewer-token`, `code-viewer-placeholder`, plus the shared `copy-button` and `copy-button-status`. Exposed methods: `expandAll()` and `collapseAll()`.

import { CodeViewer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- source: string = '' - The text to show; required, but an empty string is valid. LF, CRLF and lone CR line endings are accepted; one trailing newline is ignored. The copy button copies this exact string.
- language: 'json' | 'yaml' | 'go' | 'toml' | 'shell' | 'plain' = 'plain' - Tokenizer and folding rules. Unknown values render as `plain` (no colours, no folds).
- filename: string - Shown in the header and used as the accessible name of the code region. Set `filename` or `label`: one of them is required, so viewers on one page have distinct names.
- lineNumbers: boolean = true - Show a line-number gutter. It is `aria-hidden`, not selectable and uses `tabular-nums`, so copying selects clean code.
- foldable: boolean = true - Show fold toggles for the regions the language defines.
- defaultFoldDepth: number - Regions nested this deep (0 = outermost) or deeper start folded. Unset starts fully expanded. Changing `source` or `language` resets the folds.
- highlightLines: number[] | string - Lines to mark, by displayed number: `[2, 5]` or `"3-5,9"`. Reversed ranges are swapped, ranges are clamped to the visible lines and invalid parts are ignored. Marked lines get a bar on the start edge, a tint and visually hidden text "Highlighted line".
- startLine: number = 1 - Number shown for the first line, for excerpts. Fold names and `highlightLines` use the displayed numbers. Values below 1 or non-numbers fall back to 1.
- wrap: boolean = false - Wrap long lines (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) instead of scrolling sideways.
- maxHeight: string - CSS length such as `20rem`. The code scrolls vertically beyond it.
- copy: boolean = true - Show the copy button with a status live region.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Rows stay at least 24px tall (28px for `lg`) so fold toggles keep a 24px target. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'bordered' | 'plain' | 'flush' = 'bordered' - `bordered` is a bordered card surface; `plain` has no frame so the viewer can sit inside another surface; `flush` is full-bleed with top and bottom rules only. Unknown values fall back to `bordered`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the code region. Required unless `filename` is set; give viewers on the same page distinct names.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- copy [text: string] - The source was copied to the clipboard.
- fold [event: { start: number; end: number; collapsed: boolean }] - A region was folded or unfolded. `start` and `end` are the displayed line numbers of the region.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when neither `filename` nor `label` is set, so the code region has a distinct name.
- Throws a ContractError when `source` is not passed as a string. An empty string is valid content.

Rules:
- Use CodeViewer for read-only display of JSON, YAML, Go, TOML or shell text with folding and highlighting. It is not an editor.
- Use CodeBlock for short snippets inside prose, tabs, diffs and terminal sessions; use JsonViewer to explore a JS value as a tree.
- Pass the exact text in `source` (a prop, not slot text) so whitespace survives. For a JS value use YamlViewer or GoViewer.
- Always set `filename` or `label` so the scroll region has a distinct accessible name when a page shows several viewers.
- Do not hard-code colours around it: token colours come from semantic tokens, or from a code theme. Override layout with `class` only.
- For an editor look, import `@perfect-design/ui/code-themes.css` and set `data-code-theme` to a name from `CODE_THEMES` (pair a light and a dark theme with the colour mode yourself); never restyle tokens with your own colours.
- Use `default-fold-depth` to open long files collapsed; use `start-line` for excerpts and `highlight-lines` with displayed numbers.
- Unknown `language` falls back to plain text. Tokenizers are line oriented and approximate: they do not validate the syntax.

Accessibility:
- The code is a scroll region: `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"` and an `aria-label` from `label`, else `filename`, else "<Language> source". Keyboard users reach it with Tab and scroll with the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down; it reflows at 320px with scrolling only inside the region.
- Fold toggles are real `<button>` elements with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` (the code list) and a name such as "Fold lines 3 to 9". Tab to reach them, Enter or Space to toggle. Targets are 24px, 44px on coarse pointers.
- A folded region shows a "… N lines" button (plain text, with an accessible name such as "6 lines hidden. Unfold lines 3 to 9"). Activating it unfolds and returns focus to the fold toggle.
- Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `user-select: none`, so selecting and copying yields clean code. The copy button has a fixed name ("Copy code") and a sibling `role="status"` announces "Code copied" or "Copy failed".
- `size` changes text size only; rows keep a 24px minimum height so fold toggles stay 24px targets (44px on coarse pointers). `flush` keeps its top and bottom rules in forced-colors mode.
- Highlighted lines use a start-edge bar and visually hidden "Highlighted line" text in addition to the tint. Borders are kept for forced-colors mode; fold buttons keep a transparent border that becomes visible there. No animation is used, so reduced motion needs no special handling.

Example: JSON with folding
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

  "name": "sample-service",
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "build": "vite build",
    "test": "vitest run"
  },
  "files": ["dist", "README.md"],
  "engines": { "node": ">=20" }
}`
</script>

<CodeViewer :source="json" language="json" filename="package.json" />
```

