# DiffViewer
group: data-display / Code
Read-only diff of two texts or a unified diff string, in unified, split or inline layout, with word highlights, folded unchanged lines and change-to-change navigation.

Use `DiffViewer` to show what changed between two versions of a text: a config file, a document, generated output, a pull request excerpt. Pass `oldText` and `newText` (the viewer computes the diff in the browser with a Myers line diff and a word diff inside changed lines) or a `patch` string in unified diff format. `variant` is `unified` (default, one column), `split` (old and new side by side; below `splitMinWidth` of the viewer's own width it renders as unified) or `inline` (a changed line is one row with removed and added words marked in place). Added and removed lines carry a "+" or "-" marker, a distinct edge and hidden text, and changed words use underline and strike-through as well as a tint, so colour is never the only signal. Unchanged lines between changes fold behind "N unchanged lines" buttons. Long diffs render only the rows in view. All text is rendered as text, never as HTML. It is not an editor and does not merge or apply changes.

import { DiffViewer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- oldText: string - The original text. A missing side counts as an empty text.
- newText: string - The changed text.
- patch: string - A unified diff (`git diff` output, one or several files). When it is not blank it is shown instead of `oldText` and `newText`. Lines between hunks are not in a patch, so they cannot be revealed. A "\ No newline at end of file" line is ignored. Text that is not a diff shows a message instead.
- label: string - Accessible name of the diff (the scroll region and the table caption). Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- variant: 'unified' | 'split' | 'inline' = 'unified' - `unified` one column, `split` side by side (falls back to unified when the viewer is narrower than `splitMinWidth`; the root carries `data-effective-variant`), `inline` changed lines merged into one row. Unknown values render `unified`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size and row height (24, 28 or 32px). Unknown values render `md`.
- wrap: boolean = false - Wrap long lines inside the viewer instead of scrolling sideways.
- lineNumbers: boolean = true - Show the line number columns (old and new in unified and inline, one per side in split).
- collapse: boolean = true - Fold unchanged lines between changes. `false` shows them all.
- context: number = 3 - Unchanged lines kept around each change. Changes closer than twice this value share one hunk. Ignored for `patch`.
- copy: boolean = true - Show the copy button. It copies the diff as unified text (the `patch` itself when one is given).
- oldLabel: string = 'Original' - Heading of the old side (toolbar title, split column header, copied file header).
- newLabel: string = 'Modified' - Heading of the new side.
- splitMinWidth: number = 640 - Width of the viewer in px under which `split` renders as `unified`. It is measured on the viewer, not on the viewport, so a narrow column on a wide screen falls back too.
- height: number | string - Fixed height of the scrolling area (px or any CSS length).
- maxHeight: number | string - Largest height of the scrolling area. Without `height` or `maxHeight` the area stops at 24rem.
- maxCost: number = 1000 - Largest edit distance the line diff searches. Beyond it the viewer settles for an approximate result and says so in a visible note.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- empty - Shown when there is nothing to show (identical texts or an unreadable patch). Defaults to "No differences." or a message about the patch.

Events:
- copy [text: string] - The diff text was copied to the clipboard.
- hunk [event: { index: number; total: number }] - The current change moved by button or key. `index` is 1-based.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when no accessible name is given (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), so the diff region has a distinct name.
- Throws a ContractError when none of `oldText`, `newText` or `patch` is passed as a string. An empty string is valid.

Rules:
- Use DiffViewer to compare two versions of a text. Use CodeViewer to show one text, and do not use it as an editor or merge tool.
- Pass the exact texts as props (`old-text`, `new-text`) so whitespace survives, or a `patch` string for ready-made unified diffs.
- Always set `label` so the diff region has a distinct accessible name when a page shows several diffs.
- Choose `variant="split"` for wide containers and `unified` for narrow ones; `split` already falls back by itself below `split-min-width`.
- Keep `collapse` on for long files. The line diff is approximate beyond `max-cost` and the viewer says so; do not raise the cost for very different 10k-line files.
- Never pass HTML: all content is rendered as text. Override layout with `class`, not colours.

Accessibility:
- The diff is a `<table>` with a visually hidden caption (the `label`) inside a scroll region (`role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, named by `label`), so keyboard users reach it with Tab and scroll with the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down. It reflows at 320px: wide lines scroll inside the region, or wrap with `wrap`.
- Added, removed and changed lines have a "+", "-" or "~" marker plus visually hidden "Added", "Removed", "Changed" or "Unchanged" text, and a distinct start edge (solid for added, dashed for removed) that survives forced-colors mode. Changed words are also underlined (added) or struck through (removed), so tint is never the only signal. Line numbers and marker glyphs are `aria-hidden` and not selectable, so copying yields clean text.
- Press n for the next change and p for the previous one while the diff area has focus (also the "Next change" and "Previous change" buttons). Focus moves to the hunk header, the current one is highlighted, and a polite `role="status"` says "Change 2 of 5". Navigation wraps around.
- Each fold is a button with the visible text "N unchanged lines" and the name "Expand N unchanged lines" (`aria-expanded="false"`). It reveals up to 100 lines and keeps focus on the next fold button, or on the diff area when nothing is left to reveal. Targets are 24px or more, 44px on coarse pointers.
- Long diffs (over 400 rows) render only the rows near the viewport with `aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`; the spacer rows are `aria-hidden`. `split` falls back to unified from the width of the viewer itself, not the viewport. No animation is used, so reduced motion needs no special handling.

Example: Unified (default)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

const after = `name = "sample-service"
port = 8080

retries = 3
timeout = "5s"`
</script>
```

# GoViewer
group: data-display / Code
Read-only Go viewer: show Go source with highlighting and folds, or render a JS value as a Go composite literal.

Use `GoViewer` to display Go code that people read and copy: handlers, type definitions, examples in docs, or a JS value as a ready-to-paste `map[string]any{...}` literal. Pass `source` for Go text (it wins) or `value` for a JS value rendered by the built-in `goLiteral`. It is a `CodeViewer` with the Go tokenizer, so every `CodeViewer` prop works except `language`.

Highlighted: keywords, predeclared types (`string`, `int64`, `error`, `any`, `byte`, `rune`...), builtins when called (`make`, `len`, `append`, `panic`...), constants (`nil`, `true`, `false`, `iota`), interpreted and raw strings (also across lines), runes, `//` and `/* */` comments including `//go:build` and `//nolint` directives, every number form (hex, octal, binary, underscores, floats, hex floats, imaginary), operators (`:=`, `<-`, `...`, `&^` and the compound forms), function names (after `func` and before `(`), type names (after `type` and in `type (...)` blocks), the package name and import paths, and struct tags in backticks. Folding covers functions, `type` and `struct` and `interface` blocks, `import (...)`, `const (...)` and `var (...)`, `switch` and `select` blocks, composite literals and multi-line comments.

Rendering a `value`: objects and Maps become `map[string]any{...}`, arrays and Sets `[]any{...}`, `null` and `undefined` `nil`, strings are quoted with Go escapes (multi-line text without backticks becomes a raw literal), dates become their ISO 8601 string, bigint becomes `int64(n)`, `NaN` and infinities become `math.NaN()` and `math.Inf(...)`. Output follows gofmt style: tabs, trailing commas and aligned map values. Numbers are written naturally (`42` is an `int`, `3.5` a `float64` once stored in `any`); `numbers="float64"` writes `float64(42)` the way `encoding/json` decodes. `package="name"` wraps the literal in `package name`, an `import "math"` when needed and `var data = ...`. Circular values show a `// Cannot render ...` comment line in the component; calling `goLiteral` directly throws a `TypeError` that names the path.

This is a viewer, not an editor, and it does not parse Go: highlighting is line oriented and does not validate. Use `CodeViewer` for other languages and `JsonViewer` to explore a live value as a tree.

import { GoViewer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- source: string - Go source text. Takes precedence over `value`, including when it is an empty string.
- value: unknown - Any JS value, rendered as a Go composite literal. Replace it (do not mutate) to update the view. Ignored when `source` is a string. With neither prop the view shows `nil`.
- package: string - With `value`: wrap the literal in `package <name>` and `var data = ...`. Invalid identifiers fall back to `main`. No effect with `source`.
- numbers: 'natural' | 'float64' = 'natural' - With `value`: `natural` writes `42` and `3.5`; `float64` writes `float64(42)` for every number.
- filename: string - Header title and accessible name of the code region. Set `filename` or `label`: one of them is required.
- lineNumbers: boolean = true - Show a non-selectable, `aria-hidden` line-number gutter.
- foldable: boolean = true - Show fold toggles for functions, types, import and const groups, switch blocks and comments.
- defaultFoldDepth: number - Regions nested this deep (0 = outermost) or deeper start folded. Unset starts expanded.
- highlightLines: number[] | string - Displayed line numbers to mark: `[2, 5]` or `"3-5,9"`. Invalid parts are ignored; ranges are clamped.
- startLine: number = 1 - Number shown for the first line, for excerpts.
- wrap: boolean = false - Wrap long lines instead of scrolling sideways.
- maxHeight: string - CSS length such as `24rem`; the code scrolls vertically beyond it.
- copy: boolean = true - Show the copy button. It copies the full text, including folded lines.
- variant: 'bordered' | 'plain' | 'flush' = 'bordered' - Framed card surface, no frame (`plain`) or full-bleed with top and bottom rules (`flush`). Unknown values fall back to `bordered`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Rows keep a 24px minimum so fold toggles stay 24px targets. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the code region. Required unless `filename` is set.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- copy [text: string] - The Go text was copied to the clipboard.
- fold [event: { start: number; end: number; collapsed: boolean }] - A region was folded or unfolded, with displayed line numbers.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when neither `filename` nor `label` is set.
- Throws a ContractError when neither `source` (a string, empty is fine) nor `value` is passed. `value` may be any value, including `null`.

Rules:
- Use GoViewer for read-only Go display, not an editor. It does not parse or compile Go.
- Pass Go text in `source` exactly as written (tabs included); pass `value` to show a JS value as a `map[string]any{...}` literal. `source` wins when both are set.
- Use `package="name"` only with `value`; it adds `import "math"` automatically when NaN or an infinity appears.
- Set `filename` (or `label`) so the scroll region has a distinct accessible name.
- Use `default-fold-depth` to open long files as an outline of declarations; use `start-line` for excerpts.
- Circular values render a `// Cannot render ...` comment instead of throwing; `goLiteral` itself throws a TypeError.

Accessibility:
- The Go code is a scroll region: `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, labelled by `label`, else `filename`, else "Go source". Tab reaches it; arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down scroll it. At 320px width only the region scrolls, never the page.
- Fold toggles are `<button>` elements with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and names like "Fold lines 12 to 20". Tab to focus, Enter or Space to toggle. A folded region shows a "… N lines" button that unfolds it and returns focus to the toggle.
- Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `user-select: none`, so selection and copy give clean Go code. Copy has a constant name ("Copy code") and a `role="status"` region announces the result.
- Highlighted lines have a start-edge bar and hidden "Highlighted line" text as well as a tint. Targets are at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers); borders keep controls visible in forced-colors mode; nothing animates. Tabs render 4 columns wide.

Example: HTTP handler
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const handler = `package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"time"
)

// Item is the JSON shape returned by the sample endpoint.
type Item struct {
	ID      int       \`json:"id"\`
	Name    string    \`json:"name"\`
	Created time.Time \`json:"created"\`
}

func itemsHandler(logger *slog.Logger) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		items := []Item{{ID: 1, Name: "first", Created: time.Unix(0, 0).UTC()}}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(items); err != nil {
			logger.Error("encode failed", "err", err)
			http.Error(w, "internal error", http.StatusInternalServerError)
			return
		}
		path := r.URL.Path
		go func() {
			logger.Info("served", "path", path, "count", len(items))
		}()
	}
}

func main() {
	logger := slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(os.Stderr, nil))
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /items", itemsHandler(logger))
	srv := &http.Server{Addr: ":8080", Handler: mux, ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}
	logger.Info("listening", "addr", srv.Addr)
	if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil {
		logger.Error("server stopped", "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}`
</script>

<GoViewer :source="handler" filename="main.go" highlight-lines="29" />
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const operators = `//go:build linux && amd64

package sample

import "sync"

const (
	KB = 1 << (10 * (iota + 1))
	MB
	GB
)

const mask uint8 = 0xF0 &^ 0b0011_0000

//nolint:gocritic // sample directive
func fanIn(inputs ...<-chan int) <-chan int {
	out := make(chan int)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for _, in := range inputs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func(c <-chan int) {
			defer wg.Done()
			for v := range c {
				out <- v
			}
		}(in)
	}
	go func() { wg.Wait(); close(out) }()
	return out
}

func classify(r rune) string {
	switch {
	case r >= '0' && r <= '9':
		return "digit"
	case r == '\\n':
		return "newline"
	}
	return \`other\`
}`
</script>
```

# LogViewer
group: data-display / Code
Searchable, filterable log pane with level badges, ANSI colours, line selection, copy and a tail mode.

Use for build output, job logs and service logs that grow while the page is open. Lines are plain strings (a leading level word such as `ERROR` becomes the badge, ANSI colour codes are rendered) or `{ time, level, message, source }` objects. Only the rows near the viewport are in the DOM, so thousands of lines stay quick. The toolbar searches (`filter` hides other lines, `highlight` marks matches and Enter / Shift+Enter jump between them), filters by level and copies the selected lines. `follow` sticks to the newest line; scrolling up pauses it and shows "Jump to latest". Times given as numbers or Dates are formatted with `locale` and `timeZone`, which fall back to `ConfigProvider`, then `en` and `UTC`, so server and client print the same text. For source code with folding use `CodeViewer`; for a chat transcript use `ChatThread`.

import { LogViewer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- lines*: (string | LogLine)[] - The lines: strings or `{ time?, level?, message, source? }`. An empty array is fine.
- label: string - Accessible name of the log. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- follow: boolean = false - Tail mode: stick to the newest line. Scrolling up pauses it (`pause` event); "Jump to latest" or reaching the end resumes (`resume`).
- wrap: boolean = false - Wrap long lines instead of scrolling sideways.
- lineNumbers: boolean = true - Show line numbers. They are also the buttons that select a line for copying.
- timestamps: boolean = true - Show the time of lines that have one.
- query: string = '' - Search text, case-insensitive. Supports `v-model:query`.
- queryMode: 'filter' | 'highlight' = 'filter' - `filter` hides lines without a match; `highlight` keeps every line and only marks matches.
- levelFilter: LogLevel[] - Levels to show (default all). Lines without a level always show. Supports `v-model:levelFilter`.
- maxLines: number - Keep only the newest N lines; older ones are dropped and the line numbers keep counting from the dropped ones.
- variant: 'plain' | 'panel' | 'terminal' = 'panel' - `plain` has no frame, `panel` a bordered card, `terminal` a heavier ink frame. Unknown values fall back to `panel`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text and row size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- density: 'compact' | 'default' | 'comfortable' = 'comfortable' - Row spacing. Unknown values fall back to `comfortable`.
- toolbar: boolean = true - Show the search, level and copy controls.
- announce: boolean = true - While following, announce new lines to screen readers as one throttled polite summary, never the lines themselves.
- announceInterval: number = 2000 - Minimum milliseconds between announcements.
- height: number | string = '20rem' - Height of the whole viewer: a number (px) or any CSS length. `class` can set another.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for numbers and times. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `en` (not the runtime locale).
- timeZone: string - IANA time zone for times given as Date or epoch milliseconds. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `UTC`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- empty - Shown when there are no lines, or none match the search and level filter.

Events:
- update:query [query: string] - The search text changed.
- update:levelFilter [levels: LogLevel[]] - The shown levels changed.
- copy [text: string] - Lines were copied.
- pause [] - Following paused because the reader scrolled up.
- resume [] - Following resumed (scrolled to the end, or "Jump to latest").

Rules:
- Always give `label` (or `aria-label`): the log is a named region.
- Pass `lines` as an array and replace or append to it; cap growth with `maxLines`.
- Set `time-zone` and `locale` (or a `ConfigProvider`) when giving numeric or Date times and the page is server-rendered.
- Use `follow` only for logs that grow while open; never auto-scroll a static log.
- Use `v-model:query` and `v-model:levelFilter` only when the page needs to own the filters; the toolbar works without them.

Accessibility:
- The line area is `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` and is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so keyboard users can scroll it; it is named by `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- New lines are announced through a separate polite `role="status"` region as a throttled summary while following, never as a stream of lines. A second status region reports search results and copying.
- Press `n` and `p` with the line area focused to move between matches. In the search box, Enter and Shift+Enter move to the next and previous match and Escape clears the search.
- Level buttons use `aria-pressed`; line numbers are buttons named "Select line N" with `aria-pressed`. Level and match state also show as text or a badge, not colour alone.
- Targets are at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers). The focus ring survives forced-colors mode.

Example: Build output with levels and sources
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const lines = [

  { time: '2026-03-04T10:00:09Z', level: 'error', source: 'test', message: 'Case "parses empty input" failed: expected 0, received 1' },
  { time: '2026-03-04T10:00:10Z', level: 'info', source: 'test', message: '41 passed, 1 failed' },
]
</script>

<LogViewer label="Sample build output" :lines="lines" :height="260" locale="en" time-zone="UTC" />
```

# YamlViewer
group: data-display / Code
Read-only YAML viewer: show raw YAML text or serialise a JS value to YAML, with highlighting, indentation folds, line numbers and copy.

Use `YamlViewer` to display YAML that people read and copy: Kubernetes manifests, compose files, CI configs, or a JS value shown as YAML. Pass `source` for raw text (it wins) or `value` for a JS value that is serialised by the built-in `yamlStringify`. It is a `CodeViewer` with the YAML tokenizer, so every `CodeViewer` prop works except `language`.

Highlighted: keys, scalars, numbers, `true`/`false`/`null`/`~`, comments, anchors `&a` and aliases `*a`, merge keys `<<`, tags `!!str`, block scalars `|` and `>` with chomping and indentation indicators, flow collections `[a, b]` and `{k: v}`, quoted strings with escapes (also across lines), multi-document streams (`---`, `...`) and `%YAML` directives. Folding is by indentation, so every mapping or sequence item with children folds, and each document is folded separately.

Serialising a `value`: block style, two or four spaces (`indent`), key order as in the object, strings quoted only when plain text would change meaning (`yes`, `null`, `12`, `a: b`, a leading `-` or `#`), multi-line strings as `|` blocks with the right chomping indicator, empty containers as `{}` and `[]`, `NaN` as `.nan`, infinities as `.inf`, dates as ISO 8601, `undefined`, functions and symbols skipped in maps and written as `null` in lists. Circular values do not throw in the component: it shows a `# Cannot render this value as YAML: ...` comment line. Calling `yamlStringify` directly throws a `TypeError` that names the path of the cycle.

This is a viewer, not an editor, and it does not parse YAML: highlighting is line oriented and does not validate. Use `JsonViewer` to explore a live value as a tree and `CodeViewer` for other languages.

import { YamlViewer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- source: string - Raw YAML text. Takes precedence over `value`, including when it is an empty string.
- value: unknown - Any JS value, serialised to YAML. Replace it (do not mutate) to update the view. Ignored when `source` is a string. With neither prop the view shows `null`.
- indent: 2 | 4 = 2 - Spaces per nesting level when serialising `value`. Other values fall back to 2.
- filename: string - Header title and accessible name of the code region. Set `filename` or `label`: one of them is required.
- lineNumbers: boolean = true - Show a non-selectable, `aria-hidden` line-number gutter.
- foldable: boolean = true - Show fold toggles for indented regions.
- defaultFoldDepth: number - Regions nested this deep (0 = outermost) or deeper start folded. Unset starts expanded.
- highlightLines: number[] | string - Displayed line numbers to mark: `[2, 5]` or `"3-5,9"`. Invalid parts are ignored; ranges are clamped.
- startLine: number = 1 - Number shown for the first line.
- wrap: boolean = false - Wrap long lines instead of scrolling sideways.
- maxHeight: string - CSS length such as `24rem`; the code scrolls vertically beyond it.
- copy: boolean = true - Show the copy button. It copies the full text, including folded lines.
- variant: 'bordered' | 'plain' | 'flush' = 'bordered' - Framed card surface, no frame (`plain`) or full-bleed with top and bottom rules (`flush`). Unknown values fall back to `bordered`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Rows keep a 24px minimum so fold toggles stay 24px targets. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the code region. Required unless `filename` is set.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- copy [text: string] - The YAML text was copied to the clipboard.
- fold [event: { start: number; end: number; collapsed: boolean }] - A region was folded or unfolded, with displayed line numbers.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when neither `filename` nor `label` is set.
- Throws a ContractError when neither `source` (a string, empty is fine) nor `value` is passed. `value` may be any value, including `null`.

Rules:
- Use YamlViewer for read-only YAML display, not an editor. It does not parse or validate YAML.
- Pass raw text in `source` to show a real file exactly as written; pass `value` to show a JS value as YAML. `source` wins when both are set.
- Set `filename` (or `label`) so the scroll region has a distinct accessible name.
- Use `default-fold-depth` to open large manifests as an outline; use `highlight-lines` with displayed line numbers.
- Circular values render a `# Cannot render ...` comment instead of throwing; `yamlStringify` itself throws a TypeError.
- Use JsonViewer to explore a live JS value as a tree, CodeBlock for short snippets in prose.

Accessibility:
- The YAML is a scroll region: `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, labelled by `label`, else `filename`, else "YAML source". Tab reaches it; arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down scroll it. At 320px width only the region scrolls, never the page.
- Fold toggles are `<button>` elements with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and names like "Fold lines 7 to 28". Tab to focus, Enter or Space to toggle. A folded region shows a "… N lines" button that unfolds it and returns focus to the toggle.
- Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and `user-select: none`, so selection and copy give clean YAML. Copy has a constant name ("Copy code") and a `role="status"` region announces the result.
- Highlighted lines have a start-edge bar and hidden "Highlighted line" text as well as a tint. Targets are at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers); borders keep controls visible in forced-colors mode; nothing animates.

Example: Kubernetes Deployment
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-web
  labels:
    app: sample-web

    matchLabels:
      app: sample-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.27
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          env:
            - name: LOG_LEVEL
              value: "info"

              cpu: 500m
              memory: 128Mi`
</script>

<YamlViewer :source="deployment" filename="deployment.yaml" highlight-lines="19" />
```

# JsonViewer
group: data-display / Code and data
Collapsible, keyboard-navigable tree for inspecting any JS/JSON value with type-coloured leaves and copy-path.

Use `JsonViewer` to inspect API responses, config objects, logs and debug state. It renders objects, arrays, Map, Set, Date, BigInt, functions, symbols, `undefined` and `null`, marks circular references with `[Circular]` instead of looping, truncates huge arrays (`maxItems`, with a "Show N more" row) and long strings (`maxStringLength`), and caps total output at 10 000 rows. Every row has a copy-path button (`$.users[0].name`). Replace `value` to update the view (in-place mutation of a non-reactive object is not detected). It is a read-only viewer: for editable JSON use a code editor, for syntax highlighted source text use `CodeBlock`.

import { JsonViewer } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- value: unknown - Any value to display. Replace it (do not mutate) to update.
- defaultExpandDepth: number = 1 - Levels open initially: 0 = collapsed, 1 = root only, 2 = root and its children... Capped at 32; invalid values fall back to 1. Ignored once `v-model:expanded` holds a list.
- expanded: string[] - `v-model:expanded`: JSON paths of open containers (`"$"` is the root). Controlled when bound, uncontrolled otherwise.
- maxItems: number = 100 - Children shown per container before a "Show N more" row (each click reveals up to this many more). Invalid values fall back to 100.
- maxStringLength: number = 120 - Longer strings are cut with an ellipsis; the full text (up to 1000 chars) is in the tooltip. Invalid values fall back to 120.
- rootLabel: string - Label shown before the root value.
- showCopy: boolean = true - Show a copy-path button on each row (the `c` key copies the focused row's path either way).
- variant: 'default' | 'plain' | 'flush' = 'default' - `default` is a bordered card surface, `plain` has no chrome, `flush` is full-bleed with top and bottom rules only. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: 12px, 14px or 16px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- label: string = 'JSON' - Accessible name of the tree (`aria-label`).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:expanded [paths: string[]] - Open containers changed (click or keyboard).
- copy [event: { path: string; ok: boolean }] - A path copy finished; `ok` is false when the clipboard was unavailable or rejected.

Rules:
- Pass the raw value (object/array/anything), not a JSON string; call JSON.parse first for strings.
- Replace `value` with a new object to refresh; in-place mutation of non-reactive data will not re-render.
- Use `v-model:expanded` with JSON paths such as `$` and `$.items[0]` to control or persist expansion.
- Raise `maxItems` only when needed: rows are capped at 10 000 regardless.
- It is read-only; do not use it as an editor.
- Set `aria-label` when several viewers are on one page.

Accessibility:
- Follows the ARIA tree pattern: `role="tree"` with flat `treeitem`s carrying `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize` and `aria-expanded` (containers with children only). Name the tree with `label` or `aria-label` (defaults to "JSON"; falls through to the root).
- Roving tabindex: one tab stop. Up/Down move, Home/End jump, Right expands or enters, Left collapses or goes to the parent, Enter/Space toggle (or reveal more), `c` copies the path of the focused row.
- Copy buttons are mouse/touch affordances (`tabindex="-1"`, 24px, labelled "Copy path ..."); keyboard users use the `c` key. They appear on hover and focus-within.
- Value types are distinguished by colour and by their text (quotes, `n` suffix, `ƒ`, `[Circular]`), never by colour alone. Chevron animation is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const data = { id: 'sample-1', paid: true, total: 129.9, note: null, tags: ['tag-a', 'tag-b'] }
</script>

<JsonViewer :value="data" class="max-w-lg" />
```

Example: Expand depth and v-model:expanded
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const order = { /* ... */ }
const open = ref(['$', '$.customer'])
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 max-w-lg">
  <JsonViewer :value="order" v-model:expanded="open" root-label="order" />
  <p class="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Open paths: {{ open.join(', ') }}</p>
  <JsonViewer :value="order" :default-expand-depth="3" size="sm" variant="plain" />
</div>
```

Example: Exotic and unsafe values
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const node = { name: 'root', when: new Date(Date.UTC(2024, 1, 29)), big: 9007199254740993n, run() {}, tags: new Set(['a', 'b']), meta: new Map([['k', 1]]), text: 'sample '.repeat(60) }
node.self = node // circular
</script>

<JsonViewer :value="node" :default-expand-depth="2" :max-string-length="60" class="max-w-lg" />
```

Example: Huge arrays are truncated
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<JsonViewer :value="big" :max-items="25" class="max-w-lg" />
```

Example: Copy path feedback
```vue

</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2 max-w-lg">
  <JsonViewer :value="order" :default-expand-depth="3" @copy="onCopy" />

</div>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
  <JsonViewer :value="{ a: 1 }" size="sm" />
  <JsonViewer :value="{ a: 1 }" size="md" />
  <JsonViewer :value="{ a: 1 }" size="lg" />
</div>
```

```vue

  <JsonViewer :value="{ a: [1, 2] }" variant="plain" />

</div>
```

# Card
group: data-display / Containers
Surface that groups related content, with header, content and footer parts.

Use `Card` to frame a self-contained chunk of information (a stat, a form section, a list item with actions). Compose with `CardHeader` (`CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction`), `CardContent` and `CardFooter`. Surface variants: `default` (border + shadow), `outline` (border only), `elevated` (shadow, no border), `interactive` (hover + focus styles; render it as a link/button with `as="a"` or `as-child`), `ghost` (no surface, for grouping inside an already-framed area), `filled` (flat muted surface for secondary panels), `with-image-header` (flush `CardMedia` on top, corners clipped). `layout="horizontal"` puts `CardMedia` beside a `CardBody` from the `sm` breakpoint (stacked below). `selectable` turns the whole card into a checkbox-like toggle (plan pickers, multi-select galleries) with `v-model`/`checked`. Do not nest cards inside cards; for a KPI use `KpiTile`.

import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardAction, CardContent, CardFooter, CardMedia, CardBody } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'elevated' | 'interactive' | 'ghost' | 'filled' | 'with-image-header' = 'default' - Surface style. Unknown values render only the base layout classes.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and gap: `sm` 1rem, `md` 1.5rem (the original), `lg` 2rem. `CardHeader`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter` and `CardBody` take their horizontal and vertical padding from the card, so one prop sizes the whole composition. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- layout: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical' - `horizontal` lays `CardMedia` + `CardBody` side by side from `sm` up (no padding/gap on the card itself); unknown values fall back to `vertical`.
- selectable: boolean = false - Whole card toggles on click / Space / Enter. Adds `role="checkbox"`, `aria-checked`, `data-state="checked|unchecked"` and `tabindex=0`. Clicks on inner links, buttons and inputs do not toggle.
- modelValue: boolean - Selected state (`v-model`). When neither `modelValue` nor `checked` is given the card keeps its own state.
- checked: boolean - Alias of `modelValue` for `v-model:checked`.
- disabled: boolean = false - Selectable cards only: dims the card, sets `aria-disabled`, removes it from the tab order and blocks toggling.
- as: string | Component - Element to render.
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- CardHeader - Grid header; places `CardAction` top-right automatically.
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardTitle - Heading (renders `h3`; change with `as`).
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardDescription - Muted supporting text (`p`).
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardAction - Slot for a header action such as a Button or menu.
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardContent - Main body with horizontal padding.
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardFooter - Footer row (flex) for actions or meta.
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardMedia - Image/illustration area (`img` children fill it with object-cover). Takes 40% of the row inside a horizontal card; override with `class`.
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- CardBody - Content column (padding + gap) for horizontal cards, where the card itself has no padding.
    - as: string | Component - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper (reka-ui).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Card parts or arbitrary content.

Events:
- update:modelValue [value: boolean] - Selectable cards: the new selected state.
- update:checked [value: boolean] - Same payload, for `v-model:checked`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `selectable` card (role checkbox) has no accessible name from its text, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, or when a card given `role="region"` has no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. A plain card needs nothing.

Rules:
- Compose Card from its parts; do not hand-roll padding.
- Use `variant="interactive"` together with `as="a"` or `as-child`, never on a bare div with @click only.
- Use `selectable` (with v-model) for pick-one/pick-many cards instead of wrapping a Card in a checkbox label; do not put `variant="interactive"` and `selectable` together.
- For an image on top use `variant="with-image-header"` + `CardMedia` as the first child; for side-by-side use `layout="horizontal"` with `CardMedia` + `CardBody`.
- Do not nest Card inside Card; use `variant="outline"` sections or DescriptionList inside CardContent.
- Put the single header action in CardAction, not inside CardTitle.

Accessibility:
- `selectable` cards expose `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`; give them an accessible name (heading text or `aria-label`). Space and Enter toggle, `disabled` sets `aria-disabled` and drops the card from the tab order.
- Plain card is a presentational div; add `role="region"` + `aria-labelledby` if it must be a landmark.
- `CardMedia` is a plain div: `aria-label` is only valid on it with a role, so a decorative placeholder gets `role="img"` plus a label (or `aria-hidden`), and a real image carries its own `alt`.
- No variant uses a gradient, glow, edge stripe or hover movement: a card is a bordered surface; `elevated` and `interactive` only change the shadow and border colour.
- A checked `selectable` card keeps a visible keyboard focus indicator: besides the focus ring it draws a 2px solid outline, because its primary ring and border would otherwise hide the ring.
- `interactive` only styles the card: render it as `a`/`button` (`as`) so it is focusable and announced correctly.
- CardTitle renders an h3; set `as` to match the page heading hierarchy.

Example: Basic card
```vue
<Card class="max-w-sm">
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Sample project</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Sample data</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Card content goes here.</CardContent>
</Card>
```

---

# FlowCanvas
group: data-display / Diagrams
Interactive node and edge canvas: drag nodes, connect ports with the pointer or the keyboard, pan, zoom, undo, auto layout and a text alternative, drawn as one SVG with no extra dependency.

Use `FlowCanvas` when people build or edit a graph: a workflow, a pipeline, a routing table. For a picture of a graph nobody edits, use `MermaidDiagram` or `NetworkGraph`. Bind `v-model:nodes` (`{ id, label?, x, y, width?, height?, shape?, tone?, ports? }`) and `v-model:edges` (`{ id, from, to, label?, fromPort?, toPort?, style? }`); without a binding the canvas keeps its own copy.

**Interaction.** Drag the background to pan (touch: one finger; two fingers pinch). Zoom with Ctrl or Command plus the wheel, the toolbar or the keys. Drag a node to move it (`grid` snaps). Drag from a port to another node to connect, or click a port and then a node. Shift plus drag, or the "Select area" toggle, draws a selection box. Every one of these has a keyboard path, see the accessibility notes. Undo and redo keep up to `historyLimit` steps.

**Exposed methods** (template ref): `autoLayout()` arranges the nodes with the layered layout of `MermaidDiagram` in `direction`, `fit()`, `zoomIn()`, `zoomOut()`, `zoomTo(n)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `deleteSelected()`, `selectAll()`, `clearSelection()`, `getViewport()` and `setViewport()`. They also work when `readonly` (the caller asked for them); `readonly` blocks the user only.

**Limits.** No nested groups. Custom nodes go through the `node` slot, which draws SVG in the node's own coordinates (no HTML inside the canvas). Undo works on the data this component changed; edits you make elsewhere are not tracked. With more than 120 nodes only the nodes and connections near the visible area are drawn (300 nodes stay interactive). The canvas keeps left to right coordinates in right to left pages; the toolbar and labels follow the page direction. The canvas captures touch gestures, so scroll the page from outside it.

import { FlowCanvas } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- nodes: FlowNode[] = [] - `v-model:nodes`. `{ id, label?, x, y, width?, height?, shape?, tone?, ports? }`. `x` and `y` are the top-left corner in canvas units; size defaults to 148 by 52; `shape` is any Mermaid node shape; `tone` is neutral, primary, success, info, warning or danger; `ports` defaults to one port per side and `[]` makes the node impossible to connect.
- edges: FlowEdge[] = [] - `v-model:edges`. `{ id, from, to, label?, fromPort?, toPort?, style? }`. `from` and `to` are node ids, `style` is `solid`, `dashed` or `dotted`. A connection to an unknown node is not drawn and a note says so.
- label: string - Accessible name of the canvas. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- readonly: boolean = false - No editing by the user: nodes cannot be moved, connected, deleted or laid out, ports are hidden, undo and redo are off. Selecting, panning and zooming still work.
- grid: number | boolean = false - Snap positions to this many canvas units while dragging and moving by keyboard. `true` is 20. It also sets the spacing of the `dots` and `grid` backgrounds.
- variant: 'plain' | 'dots' | 'grid' = 'plain' - Background: a flat surface, a dot grid or grid lines. Both patterns move and scale with the canvas and fade out when they would be denser than 6 pixels.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Height of the canvas: 288, 384 or 512 px (and the gap to the toolbar and list).
- edgeStyle: 'straight' | 'curved' | 'orthogonal' = 'curved' - Shape of connections: a line, a smooth curve that leaves each port outward, or right angles with rounded corners.
- direction: 'TB' | 'LR' | 'BT' | 'RL' = 'LR' - Direction of `autoLayout()` and the toolbar button: top to bottom, left to right, bottom to top or right to left.
- toolbar: boolean = true - Show the toolbar above the canvas (zoom, fit, auto layout, undo, redo, delete, select area). The `toolbar` slot replaces its content.
- minimap: boolean = false - Show a small overview in the bottom corner with the visible area; press or drag on it to move there. It is a pointer shortcut and hidden from assistive technology.
- minZoom: number = 0.25 - Lowest zoom factor, at most 1.
- maxZoom: number = 2 - Highest zoom factor, at least 1.
- historyLimit: number = 50 - Most undo steps kept, 1 to 500. Keyboard moves of the same nodes within one second count as one step.
- autoFit: boolean = true - Fit all nodes into view once, when the canvas first has a size and nodes. Turn it off to keep the canvas origin at the top-left corner.
- emptyText: string = 'No nodes yet' - Text shown while there are no nodes.

Slots:
- node ({ node, selected, active, connecting, width, height }) - Replaces the label of a node. SVG content in the node's own coordinates (0,0 is its top-left corner); the outline, selection ring and ports stay. Text is rendered as text, never as markup.
- toolbar ({ zoom, readonly, canUndo, canRedo, hasSelection, zoomIn, zoomOut, fit, autoLayout, undo, redo, deleteSelected }) - Replaces the default toolbar content. Use the scoped functions so your buttons share the canvas history.

Events:
- update:nodes [nodes: FlowNode[]] - The node array changed (move, delete, layout, undo, redo).
- update:edges [edges: FlowEdge[]] - The connection array changed (connect, delete, undo, redo).
- node-move [{ nodes: { id, x, y }[] }] - Nodes were moved by drag, keyboard or auto layout. Fires once per gesture with every moved node.
- connect [{ edge: FlowEdge }] - A connection was made by the pointer or the keyboard.
- disconnect [{ edge: FlowEdge }] - A connection was removed, including those removed with their node.
- select [{ nodes: string[], edges: string[] }] - The selection changed.
- change [{ reason: 'move' | 'connect' | 'disconnect' | 'delete' | 'layout' | 'undo' | 'redo', nodes, edges }] - The data changed, with the new arrays.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when `nodes` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows the empty state.
- Throws a ContractError when a node has no `id` (a non-empty string).
- Throws a ContractError when two nodes share an `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when a node has no numeric `x` and `y`.
- Throws a ContractError when `edges` is not an array.
- Throws a ContractError when a connection has no `id`, `from` or `to`.
- Throws a ContractError when two connections share an `id`.

Rules:
- Always pass `label`, give every node a unique `id` and numeric `x` and `y`, and every connection a unique `id` with `from` and `to` node ids.
- Use `v-model:nodes` and `v-model:edges`; handle `connect` or `change` only to react (save, validate), not to re-add what the model already holds.
- Text drawn in the `node` slot is the node's visible text, and the accessible name is `node.label`: draw the label itself (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name) and show extra state with shapes, not a second text.
- Do not put HTML or components inside nodes: use the `node` slot with SVG elements, in the node's own coordinates.
- Use `readonly` for display. Use `grid` (or `grid="20"`) when tidy alignment matters; use `autoLayout()` on a template ref to arrange imported data with no positions.
- Pick `edge-style="orthogonal"` for flowcharts, `curved` for graphs, `straight` for dense maps. Pick `direction` for auto layout, not for display.
- Keep `ports` omitted unless the data has named inputs and outputs; then give each port an `id` and reference it with `fromPort` and `toPort`.
- For a static picture of a graph use `MermaidDiagram` or `NetworkGraph`; do not use FlowCanvas for charts.
- Give the canvas room: it needs a width, and `size` sets its height. Do not wrap it in another scroll container.

Accessibility:
- The canvas is a `role="application"` element named by `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`) and described by a visually hidden paragraph that states the keyboard model. It is focusable (Tab) and the page keeps its own scrolling outside it.
- Keyboard on the canvas: arrow keys pan (Shift for larger steps), + and - zoom, 0 fits the view, Ctrl or Command plus A selects everything, Delete removes the selection, Ctrl or Command plus Z undoes and Shift plus Ctrl or Command plus Z (or Ctrl plus Y) redoes, Escape clears the selection or abandons a drag.
- Nodes are `role="button"` elements named by their label with `aria-pressed` for the selection; one node is the tab stop (roving). Arrow keys move focus to the nearest node in that direction, Home and End jump to the first and last in reading order, Enter or Space selects, Shift plus Enter adds to the selection. Alt plus an arrow key moves the selection (by `grid` or 10 units, Shift for 5 times as far); each move is announced.
- Connections by keyboard: focus a node and press C. Focus moves to the nearest other node; arrow keys choose a target in that direction, Tab and Shift plus Tab cycle through all targets, Enter or Space confirms, Escape cancels. Every step is announced. With the pointer, a click on a port followed by a click on a node works without dragging.
- Connections are `role="button"` elements named "Edge A to B" (plus the label), also one tab stop; arrow keys move between them, Enter selects and Delete removes. A selected node has a dashed outline ring and a selected connection a thicker line, never colour alone; forced-colors mode uses system colours.
- One polite `role="status"` region announces moves, connections, deletions, undo, redo, layout and selection counts. Delete reports how many nodes and connections went; Undo and Redo name the step.
- A visually hidden list of every node (with its connection count) and every connection ("Edge A to B") is always in the page; "Show as list" reveals it in a focusable, labelled, scrollable region. Lists are cut at 500 entries with a note.
- Touch: the canvas sets `touch-action: none` so one finger pans and two fingers pinch; ports have a 24 pixel hit area. Pointer dragging always has a keyboard or click alternative. The page can be scrolled from outside the canvas.
- No motion except the user's own pan and zoom. Colours come from tokens; outlines are system colours in forced-colors mode. The toolbar, list and messages follow the page direction (right to left); the canvas itself stays left to right so coordinates and arrow keys keep their meaning.
- Labels are text only (never markup) and long labels are wrapped and cut with the full text in a tooltip and in the accessible name.

```vue
  { id: 'split', label: 'Split the load', x: 500, y: 130, tone: 'warning' },

])
const edges = ref([
  { id: 'e1', from: 'booking', to: 'check' },
  { id: 'e2', from: 'check', to: 'driver', label: 'Yes' },
  { id: 'e3', from: 'check', to: 'split', label: 'No' },
  { id: 'e4', from: 'split', to: 'driver', style: 'dashed' },

<FlowCanvas v-model:nodes="nodes" v-model:edges="edges" label="Sample workflow with custom nodes" size="sm">
```

```vue
    <circle :cx="14" cy="26" r="4" :class="selected ? 'fill-primary' : 'fill-muted-foreground'" />

    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" :disabled="!canUndo" @click="undo">Undo last change</Button>
  </template>
</FlowCanvas>
```

---

# MermaidDiagram
group: data-display / Diagrams
Draws Mermaid text (flowchart, sequence, pie, state, entity relationship, class, gantt, mindmap, timeline, journey) as an accessible SVG, with its own parser and layout and no extra dependency.

Use `MermaidDiagram` when a diagram lives as text next to the code or content it explains. Pass the Mermaid source in `source`; the component parses it, lays it out (layered layout for graphs, custom layouts for the rest) and draws SVG with design tokens, so light, dark and accent presets work. Everything is drawn by Vue templates: the source is never inserted as HTML, so hostile text stays inert text.

A source that cannot be drawn never throws and never leaves a blank area. A syntax error shows an inline alert with the line, the column, the offending source line and what to write instead; an unsupported diagram type shows a message that names the type. Both emit `error`. A diagram that is larger than `maxNodes` or `maxEdges` shows a size message instead of hanging the page.

**Supported syntax**

- `flowchart` / `graph` (TB TD BT LR RL): shapes rectangle, rounded, stadium, subroutine, cylinder, circle, double circle, rhombus, hexagon, parallelograms, trapezoids and the asymmetric flag (`A[text]`, `A(text)`, `A([text])`, `A[[text]]`, `A[(text)]`, `A((text))`, `A(((text)))`, `A{text}`, `A{{text}}`, `A[/text/]`, `A[\text\]`, `A[/text\]`, `A[\text/]`, `A>text]`, plus `A@{ shape: cyl, label: "text" }` for the common shapes); edges `-->` `---` `-.->` `==>` `--o` `--x` `<-->` `o--o` `x--x` `~~~`, longer arrows (`---->`), labels `-->|text|` and `-- text -->`; chains (`A --> B --> C`) and groups (`A & B --> C & D`); nested `subgraph ... end` with `direction`; `classDef`, `class`, `:::class`, `style`, `linkStyle`; edge ids (`e1@-->`, with `e1@{ animate: true }` lines) are read and ignored; `click` lines are accepted and ignored.
- `sequenceDiagram`: `participant` and `actor` with `as` aliases, messages `->>` `-->>` `->` `-->` `-x` `--x` `-)` `--)`, activation (`+` `-`, `activate`, `deactivate`), self messages, `Note left of|right of|over`, `loop` `alt`/`else` `opt` `par`/`and` `critical`/`option` `break` blocks, `autonumber`, `title`.
- `pie`: `title`, `showData`, `"Label" : value` lines.
- `stateDiagram` / `stateDiagram-v2`: states, `state "text" as id`, `id : description`, transitions with labels, `[*]` start and end, composite states (nested), concurrent regions separated by `--` (side by side with a dashed divider), `<<choice>>` `<<fork>>` `<<join>>`, `note left of|right of`, `direction`.
- `erDiagram`: entities with attributes (type, name, PK FK UK, comment), aliases, relationships with all cardinality marks (`||` `|o` `o|` `}o` `o{` `}|` `|{`) and the word forms, identifying `--` and non-identifying `..` lines, labels.
- `classDiagram`: classes with attributes and methods, visibility `+ - # ~`, annotations (`<<interface>>`), generics (`Name~T~`), inheritance, composition, aggregation, association, link, dependency, realisation, cardinalities, labels, namespaces, notes.
- `gantt`: `title`, `dateFormat`, sections, tasks with ids, `after`, `until`, durations in ms s m h d w (calendar months `M` and years `y` as whole numbers), tags `done` `active` `crit` `milestone`.
- `mindmap`: indentation tree with node shapes (square, rounded, circle, bang, cloud, hexagon).
- `timeline`: `title`, sections, periods with several events.
- `journey`: `title`, sections, tasks with a 1 to 5 score and actors.
- `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram` and `classDiagram` accept `;` between statements on one line (write `#59;` for a literal semicolon in text). In flowcharts `;` already works outside brackets and quotes.
- All types: `%%` comment lines and `%%` comments after a statement (not inside quotes or brackets), `accTitle` and `accDescr` (one line or a `{ }` block), `---` front matter with `title:`, and `%%{init: ...}%%` directives (read and ignored: configure the look with props instead).

**Not supported** (it draws what it can, or shows an error that says so): other Mermaid diagram types (git graph, quadrant, xy chart, sankey, block, packet, architecture, kanban, C4, requirement, radar, treemap), icons, images and markdown strings in nodes (`<br>` breaks a line, other HTML tags are dropped and their text is kept), interactive `click` handlers, themes and custom CSS from the source, `:::` styling beyond tones.

**Colour.** The source cannot set arbitrary colours. A `classDef` or `style` fill or stroke colour is mapped to the nearest tone of the design system by hue (red to danger, green to success, blue to info, yellow and orange to warning, teal to primary, greys to neutral); a class named like a tone (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `primary`) picks that tone; `tone:success` in a declaration sets it explicitly; `stroke-dasharray` makes the outline dashed and a `stroke-width` of 3px or more makes it thick. Dashes and weight carry meaning, so state is never shown by colour alone.

**Size and reflow.** With `fit="width"` (default) the SVG scales down to its container, so on a 320px screen a wide diagram gets small text. `fit="scroll"` keeps the natural size inside a focusable, named, scrollable region. `fit="auto"` measures the container and behaves like `width` until the scale would drop below 0.6 (text of 14px would be under about 8px), then switches to `scroll`; the choice is made after mount, so the server render is always `width`. Use `auto` for content you do not control and `width` for small, known diagrams.

Use `Markdown` for prose with code fences, `CodeViewer` to show plain source, and a chart component (`LineChart`, `DonutChart`, `BarChart`) when the data is numeric and should be formatted and interactive.

import { MermaidDiagram } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- source*: string - Mermaid source text. Required: a blank value throws a ContractError in strict mode (and shows a "Nothing to draw" message otherwise).
- variant: 'outline' | 'filled' | 'mono' | 'soft' = 'outline' - `outline` bordered nodes on a card, `filled` tinted nodes, `soft` borderless nodes on a muted panel, `mono` single-colour ink with a heavier border (tones are ignored). Unknown values fall back to `outline`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text and spacing scale: 12, 14 and 16 px base text inside the drawing, and the caption and control text around it.
- density: 'compact' | 'comfortable' | 'spacious' = 'comfortable' - Space between nodes and ranks, node padding, and the padding of the frame.
- edgeStyle: 'curved' | 'straight' | 'orthogonal' = 'curved' - How graph edges are drawn: S-curves, straight segments, or right angles with rounded corners. Applies to flowchart, state, class, ER and mindmap.
- direction: 'TB' | 'LR' | 'BT' | 'RL' - Overrides the direction of graph diagrams (flowchart, state, class, ER). Without it the direction written in the source is used.
- rounded: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'full' = 'md' - Corner radius of rectangular nodes and boxes. `full` makes pills. Shapes that are round by definition (stadium, circle) are not affected.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'danger' = 'neutral' - Accent of nodes that the source does not style itself: the outline colour (outline), the tint (filled, soft). Ignored by `mono`. Pie slices use the categorical chart colours.
- fit: 'width' | 'scroll' | 'auto' = 'width' - `width` scales the SVG down to the container (viewBox); `scroll` keeps the natural size inside a focusable, named scroll region; `auto` is `width` until the scale would fall below 0.6 (`MERMAID_AUTO_MIN_SCALE`), then `scroll`. The resolved value is on the root as `data-fit`.
- showSource: boolean = false - Show the Mermaid source below the diagram (read-only, with a copy button). Readers can also toggle it with the "Show source" button.
- showCode: boolean = false - Alias of `showSource`.
- showTable: boolean = false - Show the text version (nodes and connections, participants and messages, slices with values) as visible content. It is always in the page for screen readers; this makes it visible too. Readers can toggle it with the "Show as text" button.
- title: string - Caption above the diagram and the accessible name. Wins over `accTitle`, the front matter `title` and the title written in the diagram.
- description: string - Longer accessible description. Wins over `accDescr`. Without either, an automatic summary such as "Flowchart with 6 nodes and 7 connections, top to bottom" describes the image.
- maxNodes: number = 300 - Largest diagram that is drawn, counted in nodes (states, classes, entities, tasks, participants, slices...). Above it an inline error is shown instead of laying out the graph.
- maxEdges: number = 600 - Largest number of connections (edges, messages, relations) that is drawn.
- maxSourceLength: number = 100000 - Longest source, in characters, that is parsed. Longer text shows a size error before any parsing.
- maxLineLength: number = 2000 - Longest single source line, in characters, that is parsed. A longer line shows a size error naming the line.
- as: string = 'figure' - Root element. With `figure` the title is a `figcaption`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Events:
- error [event: { message: string; line: number; column: number }] - The source could not be drawn (syntax error, unsupported type, empty input, size limit). Line and column are 1-based; they are 1 for errors without a position.
- rendered [event: { type: string; nodes: number; edges: number }] - The diagram was drawn, on mount and after every change of the source or the options. `type` is `flowchart`, `sequence`, `pie`, `state`, `er`, `class`, `gantt`, `mindmap`, `timeline` or `journey`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `source` is missing or blank (a non-empty string of Mermaid text is required).

Rules:
- Pass Mermaid text in `source`; build it with a template literal or a constant, never by concatenating untrusted markup (the component is safe, but the text must be valid Mermaid).
- Always set `title` (or `accTitle` in the source) so the diagram has a meaningful accessible name; add `description` for the takeaway.
- Pick the diagram type with the first line: `flowchart TD`, `sequenceDiagram`, `pie`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `erDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `gantt`, `mindmap`, `timeline`, `journey`.
- Do not put colours in the source: use `classDef name tone:success` or a class named `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `primary`; fills and strokes are mapped to tones.
- Use `fit="auto"` when the diagram size is not known (user content): it scrolls instead of shrinking text below 60%. Use `fit="scroll"` for wide or dense diagrams and `fit="width"` (default) for small ones. Prefer `direction="TB"` for wide diagrams in narrow columns.
- Use `variant="mono"` for print-like output and `variant="soft"` inside cards that already have a border.
- Handle `@error` when the source comes from users; read `line` and `column` to point at the mistake.
- Import `parseMermaid` and `renderModel` to validate or inspect a source without mounting the component.
- Keep diagrams under the default 300 nodes; raise `maxNodes` deliberately.

Accessibility:
- The drawing is one `<svg role="img">` named by `aria-labelledby` (a `<title>` and a `<desc>`): the `title` prop, then `accTitle`, then the title written in the diagram, then an automatic summary such as "Flowchart with 6 nodes and 7 connections, top to bottom". The description comes from `description`, `accDescr` or the summary.
- A text version is always in the page: an ordered list of nodes (in reading order) and a list of connections "A to B: label" for graphs, participants and messages in order for sequence diagrams, slices with values for pie charts, tasks with dates for gantt charts. It is visually hidden until `showTable` or the "Show as text" button reveals it (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`).
- A syntax error is a `role="alert"` panel naming the line and column, with the offending line; "unsupported" and "nothing to draw" are `role="status"`. Nothing is announced on every redraw.
- With `fit="scroll"` the viewport is `role="region"`, focusable (`tabindex="0"`, visible focus ring) and named "<title>, scrollable diagram", so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys.
- State is not shown by colour alone: dotted and thick edges differ by pattern and weight, shapes differ by outline, gantt status is written as text and drawn as outline, check or diamond, journey scores are printed, actors differ by marker shape, pie slices list value and percentage in the legend.
- Text inside the drawing is at least 12px at natural size (`size="md"` is 14px); with `fit="width"` it shrinks with the container, so use `fit="auto"` (scrolls below a 0.6 scale) or `fit="scroll"` for wide diagrams on narrow screens. Colours are tokens only (ink, muted ink, tones) so dark mode, accent presets and forced-colors mode (system colours replace the tokens) keep working. The component has no animation.
- The source is only ever rendered as Vue text nodes inside SVG `<text>` elements. Markup, `<script>`, event handlers and `javascript:` text in the source can never be executed or inserted as HTML: tags inside labels are dropped (their text stays), and the title, description and the source panel show the text literally. `click` lines are ignored, so no link or handler is ever created.

Example: Large diagram
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const lines = ['flowchart TD']
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) lines.push(`  n${i}[Step ${i + 1}]`)
for (let i = 1; i < 60; i++) lines.push(`  n${Math.floor((i - 1) / 2)} --> n${i}`)
for (let i = 1; i * 4 + 3 < 60; i += 3) lines.push(`  n${i} -.-> n${i * 4 + 3}`)
const large = lines.join('\n')
</script>

<MermaidDiagram :source="large" fit="scroll" title="Sixty sample steps" :max-nodes="200" />
```

Example: Source visible
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const flow = `flowchart TD
  A[Booking received] --> B{Pallets fit the truck?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Assign driver]
  B -->|No| D[Split the load]
  D --> C
  C --> E([Depart depot])
  E --> F[(Delivery log)]`
</script>

<MermaidDiagram :source="flow" show-source show-table title="Booking flow with source and text version" />
```

# Tree
group: data-display / Hierarchy
Keyboard-navigable expandable tree with single selection, sizes, compact density, checkboxes, connector lines and a boxed variant.

Use `Tree` for hierarchical data such as file explorers, category pickers and nested navigation inside a page. Items are `{ id, label, children?, icon?, disabled? }`. Expansion (`v-model:expanded`, array of ids) and selection (`v-model:selected`, one id or null) both work controlled and uncontrolled. Clicking a branch row selects and toggles it; clicking its chevron only toggles. Customise rows with the `item` slot. Variations: `density="compact"` for dense sidebars and file explorers; `checkboxes` (+ `v-model:checked`, ids of checked leaves) for pickers where several nodes are chosen: branches show checked / indeterminate derived from their leaves and toggling a branch toggles all its enabled leaves; `lines` draws connector lines (vertical rules with elbows) to make deep hierarchies easier to scan. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the type scale, toggle and checkbox size and indentation, while `density` sets the vertical rhythm; `compact` alone still means the small scale. `variant` is `default`, `lines` (the same as the `lines` prop) or `boxed` (a bordered card surface; the selected row is also set in a heavier weight). They combine. For site navigation use the navigation components; for tabular data use `Table`.

import { Tree } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items*: TreeItem[] - Root nodes: `{ id: string; label: string; children?: TreeItem[]; icon?: IconDefinition; disabled?: boolean }`. Ids must be non-empty and unique across the whole tree; a missing or repeated id throws a ContractError (rendering drops later duplicates when strict mode is off).
- expanded: string[] = [] - `v-model:expanded`. Ids of expanded branches; unknown ids are ignored.
- selected: string | null = null - `v-model:selected`. Id of the selected node.
- density: 'default' | 'compact' = 'default' - Row height, indentation, toggle size and font size. Unknown values fall back to default.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Type scale (12px, 14px, 16px), toggle and checkbox size and indentation step. Defaults to `md`, or `sm` when `density="compact"`. An explicit value wins. Unknown values behave as unset.
- variant: 'default' | 'lines' | 'boxed' = 'default' - `lines` draws connector lines (same as the `lines` prop); `boxed` frames the tree in a bordered card surface and sets the selected row in a heavier weight. Combine `boxed` with `lines`. Unknown values fall back to default.
- checkboxes: boolean = false - Show a visual checkbox per node (aria-hidden; the treeitem exposes `aria-checked` true/false/mixed). Space toggles the focused node; Enter still selects/expands.
- checked: string[] = [] - `v-model:checked`. Ids of checked LEAF nodes (branches derive their state). Unknown ids are ignored. Only used with `checkboxes`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the tree (`aria-label`). Required: set `label`, or pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` as an attribute.
- lines: boolean = false - Draw connector lines (also set by `variant="lines"`): a vertical rule per ancestor level that ends in an elbow at the last child.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- item ({ item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean; selected: boolean }) - Replace the icon + label inside a row.

Events:
- update:expanded [ids: string[]] - Expanded ids changed.
- update:selected [id: string | null] - Selection changed.
- update:checked [ids: string[]] - Checked leaf ids changed (`checkboxes` only).
- select [item: TreeItem] - A node was activated (click / Enter / Space).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the tree has no name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when a node has no non-empty string `id`, or two nodes anywhere in the tree (collapsed branches included) share an `id`.

Rules:
- Always give nodes stable unique string ids; v-model values are ids, not objects.
- Always set `aria-label` on Tree.
- Use `checkboxes` + `v-model:checked` for multi-pick trees; checked values are leaf ids only, branch state is derived.
- Use `size` for the type scale and `variant="boxed"` for a framed tree; `variant="lines"` is the same as `lines`.
- Use `density="compact"` for sidebars and `lines` for deep hierarchies; they combine with checkboxes.
- Use the `item` slot for badges/actions, not extra buttons that steal keyboard focus.

Accessibility:
- Follows the ARIA tree pattern: `role="tree"` with flat `treeitem`s carrying `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-expanded` (branches only) and `aria-selected`.
- Roving tabindex: one tab stop; Up/Down move, Home/End jump, Right expands or enters, Left collapses or goes to the parent, Enter/Space select.
- With `checkboxes` every treeitem has `aria-checked` (`mixed` for partially checked branches); the visual box and the connector lines are `aria-hidden`.
- Give the tree a name with `label` or `aria-label` (falls through to the root). The selected node also gets an outline in forced-colors mode, and the chevron rotation respects reduced motion.
- Rows use logical padding, so RTL mirrors the indentation. Long labels truncate inside the row instead of widening the page.
- Disabled nodes stay focusable but cannot be selected or toggled.
- `size`, `variant` and `density` change only appearance: the roles, `aria-*` attributes, roving tabindex and the key map are the same in every combination. In `boxed` the selected row keeps `aria-selected` and the forced-colors outline and is also set in a heavier weight, so selection is not shown by tint alone.

Example: Uncontrolled
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [{ id: 'src', label: 'src', children: [{ id: 'main', label: 'main.ts' }] }, { id: 'pkg', label: 'package.json' }]
</script>

<Tree aria-label="Project files" :items="items" class="max-w-xs" />
```

Example: Controlled with icons
```vue

const selected = ref('main')
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">

  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ selected ?? 'none' }}</p>
  <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="expanded = []">Collapse all</Button>
</div>
```

```vue

</script>

```

# ActivityFeed
group: data-display / Lists
Chronological list of who did what to which thing and when, with relative times, day groups, expandable details and a load more button.

Use `ActivityFeed` for audit trails, deploy history and "what changed" panels where each event has an actor, an action, an optional target and a time. `variant` sets the layout: `list` (default, ruled rows with initials avatars), `timeline` (round markers joined by a line), `compact` (one tight line per event, no avatars) and `grouped` (the list under a heading per calendar day, or per `group` you set). `size` sets the text size and `density` the row spacing. Times render with `Intl`: relative ("2 hours ago") up to a week old, absolute after that, with the full date in the `title`. Pass `now` for output that is identical on the server and the client; without it the first render shows absolute times and the relative text appears after mount. Events with `details` get a "Show details" button (controlled with `v-model:expanded` or left uncontrolled). All text is rendered as text, never as HTML. For a single process log use `LogViewer`; for a plain sequence of steps use `Timeline`.

import { ActivityFeed } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- events: ActivityEvent[] = [] - The events in display order. Each has `id`, `action` and `time`; `actor`, `target`, `icon`, `tone`, `group` and `details` are optional. `null` is treated as empty.
- label: string - Accessible name of the feed. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- variant: 'list' | 'timeline' | 'compact' | 'grouped' = 'list' - `list` ruled rows with avatars, `timeline` markers joined by a line, `compact` one tight line per event, `grouped` list under a heading per day or `group`. Unknown values fall back to `list`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size, marker and avatar size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- density: 'comfortable' | 'compact' = 'comfortable' - Row spacing. Unknown values fall back to `comfortable`.
- showAvatars: boolean = true - Initials avatar for events with an `actor` in `list` and `grouped`. Other variants always use the marker.
- now: Date | string | number - Reference time for relative text. Set it for server-safe output; without it the current time is read after mount and refreshed every minute.
- relative: boolean = true - Show relative text for events up to a week from `now`. Off: always the absolute date and time.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for dates and relative text. Unknown values fall back to the runtime default. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `en` (not the runtime locale), so server and client print the same text.
- timeZone: string - IANA time zone for dates and day groups, for example `UTC`. Unknown values fall back to the runtime zone. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `UTC` (not the runtime zone).
- headingLevel: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of the group headings in `grouped`.
- hasMore: boolean = false - More events exist: shows the load more button or the `load-more` slot.
- loading: boolean = false - The next page is loading: the button is disabled, the feed is `aria-busy` and a polite status says so.
- loadMoreLabel: string = 'Load more activity' - Text of the load more button.
- expanded: (string | number)[] - Ids of the events whose details are open (`v-model:expanded`). Leave it unset for uncontrolled use.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- empty - Shown instead of the list when there are no events. Default: "No activity yet."
- load-more ({ loading: boolean }) - Replaces the load more button. Shown while `hasMore` is true.
- details ({ event: ActivityEvent }) - Content of the details panel. With this slot every event gets a "Show details" button.

Events:
- load-more - The load more button was pressed.
- toggle [event: { id: string | number; expanded: boolean }] - An event's details were opened or closed.
- update:expanded [ids: (string | number)[]] - New list of open ids, for `v-model:expanded`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the feed has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when an event has no `id` (a non-empty string or a number) or two events share an id.
- Throws a ContractError when an event has a blank `action`.

Rules:
- Actor avatars blur when a surrounding `ConfigProvider` sets `blurMedia` (privacy, not decoration); there is no prop on this component.
- Always set `label`; give every event a unique, stable `id` and a non-blank `action`.
- Pass `now` (and `time-zone`) for server-rendered pages so the output matches on the client.
- Use generic actors ("Deploy bot", "Reviewer 1"); never invent real people. Put the outcome in `action` or `tone`, not only in colour.
- Use `variant="grouped"` for long histories, `compact` for side panels, `timeline` when order is the point. Use `hasMore` with `@load-more` for paging.
- Details and `empty` text are plain text. Use the `details` slot for richer content you have already made safe.

Accessibility:
- The root is `role="group"` named by `label` (required). Events are one ordered list (`ol` / `li`); in `grouped` each day is a `role="group"` named by its heading, and the heading level is `headingLevel`.
- Times use `<time datetime>` with the ISO value; relative text carries the full absolute date and time in `title`. A value that is not a date is shown as given, without `datetime`.
- Tone is never colour alone: non-neutral tones add an icon and a visually hidden word ("Success.", "Warning.", "Error.", "Info.") before the text.
- Avatars are decorative (`alt=""`) because the actor is named in the text. Initials are derived from the generic actor name.
- Details: a real `button` ("Show details" / "Hide details" plus the event as hidden text) with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` while open. Enter and Space toggle it. 24px minimum height, 44px on coarse pointers, shared focus ring.
- `loading` sets `aria-busy` and a polite `role="status"` says "Loading more activity." The feed never announces new items by itself. Layout uses logical properties and wraps at 320px, so RTL mirrors it.

Example: Basic list
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const now = '2026-03-04T12:00:00Z'
const events = [
  { id: 'e1', actor: 'Deploy bot', action: 'deployed', target: 'Orchard Mill web 1.4', time: '2026-03-04T11:42:00Z', tone: 'success', details: 'Rolled out to 3 of 3 instances.' },
  { id: 'e2', actor: 'Reviewer 1', action: 'approved', target: 'Change 128', time: '2026-03-04T10:05:00Z' },
  { id: 'e3', actor: 'Scheduler', action: 'skipped the nightly export for', target: 'Kestrel Freight', time: '2026-03-04T03:00:00Z', tone: 'warning', details: 'The previous run was still active.' },
  { id: 'e4', actor: 'Reviewer 2', action: 'requested changes on', target: 'Change 127', time: '2026-03-03T16:20:00Z', tone: 'danger' },
  { id: 'e5', actor: 'Deploy bot', action: 'opened', target: 'Change 129', time: '2026-03-03T09:15:00Z', tone: 'info' },
  { id: 'e6', action: 'Maintenance window ended', time: '2026-02-20T22:00:00Z' },
]
</script>

<ActivityFeed class="max-w-xl" label="Sample data: project activity" :events="events.slice(0, 4)" :now="now" time-zone="UTC" locale="en" />
```
