```vue
  { id: 'e4', actor: 'Reviewer 2', action: 'requested changes on', target: 'Change 127', time: '2026-03-03T16:20:00Z', tone: 'danger' },
  { id: 'e5', actor: 'Deploy bot', action: 'opened', target: 'Change 129', time: '2026-03-03T09:15:00Z', tone: 'info' },
  { id: 'e6', action: 'Maintenance window ended', time: '2026-02-20T22:00:00Z' },
]
const shown = ref(events.slice(0, 3))
const hasMore = ref(true)
function more() {
  shown.value = events
  hasMore.value = false
}
</script>

<ActivityFeed class="max-w-xl" label="Sample data: paged activity" :events="shown" :has-more="hasMore" :now="now" time-zone="UTC" locale="en" @load-more="more" />
```

Example: Custom icon, absolute times and empty state
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

const release = [{ id: 'r1', actor: 'Deploy bot', action: 'released', target: 'Brightwater Co app 2.0', time: '2026-03-04T08:00:00Z', icon: faRocket, tone: 'primary' }]
</script>

<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">

  <ActivityFeed label="Sample data: empty feed" :events="[]"><template #empty>Nothing has happened in this project yet.</template></ActivityFeed>

```

Example: Right-to-left

# DescriptionList
group: data-display / Lists
Semantic term/definition pairs (`dl`) for showing record details, with optional copy buttons.

Use `DescriptionList` with `DescriptionItem` children to show key/value details of one record (a user, a deployment, an API key). Pick a `variant`: `stacked` (default) for narrow detail panels, `inline` for compact key-on-left/value-on-right rows (settings summaries, receipts), `grid` for wide overview sections that show many short facts in 1-4 responsive columns, `striped` for long lists of facts that need row tracking (framed, alternate rows tinted). `orientation` (stacked/horizontal) applies inside `stacked`, `grid` and `striped`: `stacked` (default) puts the term above the value and `horizontal` aligns them in two columns from the `sm` breakpoint. Set `copyable` on an item to show a copy button for IDs, URLs and tokens. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the type scale and `density` (`compact`, `default`, `comfortable`) the space between items (row gaps, and the padding of divided or striped items). For a single standalone pair use `DetailField` (it takes `size` too). For tabular comparisons of many records use `Table`.

import { DescriptionList, DescriptionItem, DetailField } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'stacked' | 'inline' | 'grid' | 'striped' = 'stacked' - Layout: `stacked` default; `inline` term left / value right on one row; `grid` responsive columns; `striped` framed list with alternate row tint. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`.
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Column count for `variant="grid"` (always 1 on mobile, 2 from `sm`, N from `lg`). Ignored by other variants.
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'stacked' = 'stacked' - Term above value (stacked) or side by side (horizontal, from `sm`).
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Type scale of terms and values: 12px, 14px or 16px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- density: 'compact' | 'default' | 'comfortable' = 'default' - Space between items: row gaps (6px, 12px, 20px; grid row gaps 8px, 16px, 24px) and the vertical padding of divided and striped items. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- divided: boolean = false - Draw a divider between items instead of a gap. Ignored by `grid`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- DescriptionItem - One term + definition pair rendered as `div > dt + dd` (valid inside `dl`).
    - term: string - Term text. Required: set `term` or use the `term` slot for rich content.
    - copyable: boolean = false - Show a copy button next to the definition.
    - copyText: string - Text to copy; defaults to the rendered text of the definition.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- DetailField - A single standalone label/value pair (its own `dl`).
    - label: string - Label text.
    - value: string | number | null - Value; the default slot wins when given.
    - copyable: boolean = false - Show a copy button (hidden when the value is empty).
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Type scale of the label and value. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - emptyText: string = '–' - Placeholder for empty values.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - `DescriptionItem` children.

Events:
- copy [text: string] - Emitted by DescriptionItem/DetailField after the text was copied.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `DescriptionItem` has no `term` text (prop or `term` slot).
- Throws a ContractError when a `DescriptionItem` is rendered outside a `DescriptionList`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `DetailField` has a blank `label`.

Rules:
- Put only `DescriptionItem` elements directly inside `DescriptionList`.
- Use `copyable` for IDs, URLs, tokens; copyText for masked values.
- Use horizontal orientation inside wide cards, stacked in narrow columns.
- Use DetailField, not DescriptionList, for a lone label/value pair.
- Choose `variant`: stacked for narrow panels, inline for compact key/value rows, grid for wide overviews with many short facts, striped for long fact lists.
- `columns` only applies to `variant="grid"`; `divided` is ignored by grid.
- Use `size` for text and `density` for spacing on DescriptionList (not per item); `density` has an effect on gaps, `divided` and `striped` rows.
- Items adapt to the list `variant` automatically; do not style DescriptionItem per variant yourself.

Accessibility:
- Renders native `dl`/`dt`/`dd` so screen readers announce term/definition relationships.
- The copy button is named after what it copies ("Copy Region"; "Copy value" without a term) and keeps that name. The result ("Copied" or "Copy failed") is announced by a sibling `role="status"` element, not inside the button. It is a 24px target.
- `size` and `density` change type scale and spacing only; the `dl`, `dt`, `dd` structure and copy buttons are the same in every combination. The copy button stays a 24px target at every size.
- Inline values align to the end edge (logical), so RTL mirrors the layout. Items stack on narrow screens; `horizontal` orientation only applies from the `sm` breakpoint.

Example: Stacked details
```vue
<DescriptionList class="max-w-sm">
  <DescriptionItem term="Region">eu-west-1</DescriptionItem>
  <DescriptionItem term="Status"><Badge variant="success">Healthy</Badge></DescriptionItem>
  <DescriptionItem term="Owner">Platform team</DescriptionItem>
</DescriptionList>
```

# List
group: data-display / Lists
Vertical list of rows with leading/trailing slots, dividers and optional interactivity.

Use `List` + `ListItem` for simple vertical collections: files, members, recent activity, settings rows. Each item has `leading` (icon/avatar), default (title), `description` and `trailing` (badge, button, meta) slots. Set `interactive` on items that are clickable; for navigation render the item as a link (`as="a"`) or put a link inside. Variants: `plain` (no dividers; for short lists inside another surface), `divided` (hairline dividers; the default), `card` (each row is its own bordered card, for selectable/sortable entries), `interactive` (divided rows that are all hoverable, focusable and keyboard-activatable), `with-avatar` (roomier rows with an unmuted leading slot for an `Avatar`, medium-weight title). `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets row padding and text size for every row; `gap` (`none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`) spaces rows in `plain` and `card` lists (divided variants are separated by their rule and ignore it). For tabular data with columns use `Table`/`DataTable`; for chronological events use `Timeline`.

import { List, ListItem } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- as: string | Component = 'ul' - Element to render (`ol` for ordered).
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.
- variant: 'plain' | 'divided' | 'card' | 'interactive' | 'with-avatar' - Row presentation, shared with every `ListItem` inside. When omitted the `divided` prop decides (dividers by default); unknown values behave as omitted.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Row padding and text size, shared with every `ListItem`: `sm` 12px text, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px with roomier rows. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- gap: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Space between rows (0, 4px, 8px, 16px). Only `plain` and `card` lists use it; `card` rows keep 8px when it is not set. Divided variants ignore it. Unknown values behave as unset.
- marker: 'none' | 'disc' | 'decimal' = 'none' - Real list markers for hand-authored bulleted or numbered text (legal text, feature bullets). The list becomes a plain block with logical start padding and muted markers; `variant`, `divided` and `gap` do not apply and rows drop their flex layout. `decimal` renders an `ol` unless `as` is set. Unknown values behave as `none`.
- divided: boolean = true - Dividers between items. Only used when `variant` is not set.
- bordered: boolean = false - Rounded border around the list.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- ListItem - One row. Slots: `leading`, default, `description`, `trailing`.
    - as: string | Component = 'li' - Element to render.
    - asChild: boolean = false - Render the slot child; leading/trailing layout is skipped.
    - interactive: boolean = false - Hover/focus styles, tabindex=0 and Enter/Space activation (non-native elements). Defaults to true inside `<List variant="interactive">`; `:interactive="false"` opts a row out.
    - selected: boolean = false - Highlight and set aria-current.
    - disabled: boolean = false - Dim and block clicks/keys.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - `ListItem` children.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `ListItem` is rendered outside a `List` (a plain `ul`, `ol` or `role="list"` parent also counts).

Rules:
- Use `marker="disc"` or `"decimal"` for prose-like bulleted or numbered text; leave it unset for rows with slots and dividers.
- Use `leading`/`trailing` slots instead of custom flex wrappers inside ListItem.
- Choose the look with `variant` on List (not per row): `card` for separated entries, `with-avatar` for people lists, `interactive` when every row is clickable.
- Set `size` and `gap` on List, not per row; `gap` only affects `plain` and `card`.
- Make an item interactive only if it does something; navigation should be a link.
- Do not place block-level layout (cards) inside ListItem; use Card grid instead.

Accessibility:
- Explicit `role="list"` is set so lists keep list semantics in Safari even with list-style removed.
- Interactive non-native items get `tabindex=0` and respond to Enter/Space; prefer `as="a"`/`as="button"` for real navigation/actions.
- `selected` sets `aria-current`; `disabled` sets `aria-disabled`.
- Rows are flat: no accent stripe or hover movement. Selection is a background plus `aria-current`, not colour alone. Slot text inherits a muted colour: give a Button inside `trailing` its own `text-foreground` on selected rows.
- `size` and `gap` change spacing and text only. Interactive rows keep at least a 28px height at `sm`, above the 24px minimum target.
- Keyboard: Tab reaches interactive rows (and links or buttons inside them); Enter or Space activates a non-native row. Dividers and rows reflow at any width.

Example: Bulleted and numbered text
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-8">
  <List marker="disc" class="max-w-xs">
    <ListItem>Sample feature one</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Sample feature two</ListItem>
  </List>
  <List marker="decimal" class="max-w-xs">
    <ListItem>Sample first step</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Sample second step</ListItem>
  </List>
</div>
```

Example: Simple list
```vue

  <ListItem>Overview</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Settings</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Members</ListItem>
</List>
```

Example: Leading, description, trailing and interactive
```vue

  <ListItem interactive>
    <template #leading><Icon :icon="faFolder" /></template>
    src
    <template #description>12 files</template>
    <template #trailing><Badge variant="secondary">Dir</Badge></template>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem interactive selected>
    <template #leading><Icon :icon="faFile" /></template>

    <template #description>Updated today</template>
```

# Timeline
group: data-display / Lists
Vertical sequence of events with status-toned markers, times and a connector line.

Use `Timeline` + `TimelineItem` for chronological activity: deploy history, audit trails, order status. Each item has a marker (status tone, optional FontAwesome icon), title, time and free-form body. The connector line is drawn between items and hidden after the last. Layouts: `vertical` (default; activity feeds, audit logs), `horizontal` (a few steps in a row, e.g. order progress; scrolls when it overflows), `alternating` (events left and right of a centre line from `md` up, plain vertical below; for history/roadmap pages). `size` is `compact` (smaller markers and spacing for dense side panels), `default` or `large` (bigger markers, spacing and text). `variant` styles the markers: `default` (tinted), `outline` (a ring in the status tone, plain centre) or `solid` (filled with the tone); the status is also spoken in every variant. For non-chronological rows use `List`.

import { Timeline, TimelineItem } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- layout: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' | 'alternating' = 'vertical' - Orientation / arrangement of the events, shared with every `TimelineItem`. Unknown values fall back to `vertical`.
- size: 'default' | 'compact' | 'large' = 'default' - `compact` = smaller marker (16px), tighter spacing, xs body text; `large` = 32px marker, roomier spacing, larger text. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'solid' = 'default' - Marker look shared with every item: `default` tinted bubble, `outline` ring in the status tone with a plain centre, `solid` marker filled with the status tone. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the list (`aria-label`). Required for `horizontal` (a focusable scroll region); recommended otherwise.
- as: 'ol' | 'ul' = 'ol' - List element; `ol` when order matters.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- TimelineItem - One event. Slots: `icon`, `title`, `time`, default (body).
    - status: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'neutral' - Marker tone.
    - title: string - Event title. An item needs a `title` or a `time` (or the matching slot).
    - time: string - Human-readable time text.
    - datetime: string - Machine-readable value for `<time datetime>`.
    - icon: IconDefinition - FontAwesome icon inside the marker; a dot is used when omitted.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - `TimelineItem` children.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `TimelineItem` has neither a `title` nor a `time` (or the matching slot).
- Throws a ContractError when a `layout="horizontal"` timeline, which is a focusable scroll region, has no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Newest-first or oldest-first is up to you; keep it consistent and say which in surrounding copy.
- Put status words in the title/body too, colour alone is not enough.
- Pick the layout on Timeline (children adapt): `horizontal` for 3-5 short steps, `alternating` for history pages, `compact` for sidebars.
- Use `variant="outline"` or `"solid"` for stronger markers and `size="large"` for roomy history pages; they combine with every layout.
- Use `datetime` whenever `time` is relative text.

Accessibility:
- Rendered as an ordered list with `role="list"`; markers and connector are `aria-hidden`. Name it with `label`.
- Times use `<time>` with tabular figures; pass `datetime` for machine-readable values.
- Status is spoken as well as coloured: non-neutral statuses add a visually hidden "Success.", "Warning.", "Error." or "Info." before the title.
- `variant` and `size` change markers and spacing only. Every variant keeps the visually hidden status word, so `outline` and `solid` markers do not rely on tone alone; the marker glyph is foreground on the ring and on-tone text on the solid fill (the pairs the contrast tests cover). The `outline` ring uses stroke tokens that are at least 3:1 against the page and card backgrounds in every theme, light and dark (WCAG 1.4.11; `warning` uses `warning-foreground` in light mode and `warning` in dark mode), and `contrast.test.ts` pins every status.
- The `horizontal` layout becomes a focusable scroll region (`tabindex="0"`, shared focus ring) so keyboard users can scroll it. Spacing and placement use logical properties, so RTL mirrors them. `alternating` is a plain vertical list below `md`.

Example: Basic
```vue
<Timeline class="max-w-md" label="Sample data: order steps">
  <TimelineItem title="Order placed" time="Mon 09:12">Payment received.</TimelineItem>
  <TimelineItem title="Packed" time="Mon 14:03" />
  <TimelineItem title="Shipped" time="Tue 08:40" />
</Timeline>
```

Example: Status tones and icons
```vue
<Timeline class="max-w-md" label="Sample data: build log">
  <TimelineItem status="success" :icon="faCheck" title="Build passed" time="2 min ago" datetime="2026-03-01T10:00:00Z" />
  <TimelineItem status="warning" :icon="faTriangleExclamation" title="Slow step" time="1 min ago">Took 48s, limit 30s.</TimelineItem>
  <TimelineItem status="primary" :icon="faRocket" title="Deploying" time="now" />
</Timeline>
```

# VirtualList
group: data-display / Lists
Fixed-row-height windowed list that renders only the visible rows, for 10 000+ items.

Use `VirtualList` when a plain `v-for` would create thousands of DOM nodes (logs, long pickers, big result sets). Every row must have the same `itemHeight` (px); rows are absolutely positioned inside a spacer of the full height, so scrolling stays native. Give the list a height with `height` or a class (`h-96`). `overscan` rows are rendered beyond the viewport to avoid blank flashes. Scroll handling is throttled to one update per animation frame. For variable row heights or table semantics use `DataTable`; for short lists use `List`. Browsers cap element height (about 33 million px, less in Firefox), which limits very tall lists.

import { VirtualList } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items*: readonly T[] - All items. Null is treated as an empty list.
- itemHeight*: number - Row height in px. Must be a positive finite number; otherwise a ContractError is thrown (rendering falls back to 32 when strict mode is off).
- height: number | string - Viewport height (px number or CSS length). Without it, size the element with a height class (`h-96`, `max-h-*`, `size-*`, `flex-1`, `grow`) or an inline height; one of the two is required. Use `height="100%"` when a parent sizes the list.
- overscan: number = 4 - Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport. Negative / NaN mean 0.
- itemKey: string | ((item: T, index: number) => string | number) - Stable key: property name or function. Defaults to the row index.
- variant: 'plain' | 'bordered' | 'divided' | 'striped' = 'plain' - `plain` is the unframed list, `bordered` adds a rounded border, `divided` draws a rule under each row and `striped` tints every second row (by index, so the stripes stay put while scrolling). Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the list. Required: set `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ item: T; index: number }) - Row content; the row box is `itemHeight` tall and clips overflow.
- empty - Shown when `items` is empty (default "No items").

Events:
- scroll [scrollTop: number] - Scroll offset in px, at most once per animation frame.
- range [range: { start: number; end: number }] - Rendered index range (end exclusive, overscan included) whenever it changes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `itemHeight` is not a positive finite number.
- Throws a ContractError when the list has no bounded height: set `height`, a height class (`h-*`, `max-h-*`, `size-*`, `flex-1`, `grow`) or an inline height. Use `height="100%"` when a parent sizes it.
- Throws a ContractError when the list has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Every row must have the same height: set `item-height` to it and keep row content within that box.
- Always give the list a height (`height` prop or a `h-*` class); without one it grows to full size and nothing is windowed.
- Use `scrollToIndex(index, align)` through a template ref (`start | center | end | auto`).
- Pass `item-key` when items can be reordered or filtered so row state is preserved.

Accessibility:
- Root is `role="list"` and focusable (`tabindex=0`, shared focus ring) so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys, Page Up / Page Down, Home and End; rows are `role="listitem"` with `aria-setsize` (total) and `aria-posinset` (1-based position), so assistive tech reports the real position even though most rows are not in the DOM.
- With no items the root becomes `role="group"` (an empty `role="list"` is invalid ARIA) and drops out of the tab order, because nothing scrolls.
- Give the list an accessible name with `label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Interactive rows (buttons, links) only exist while rendered; keep roving focus logic outside the list or call `scrollToIndex` before focusing.

Example: 10 000 rows
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const rows = Array.from({ length: 10000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, name: 'Row ' + (i + 1) }))
</script>

<VirtualList :items="rows" :item-height="36" :height="240" label="Rows" class="rounded-md border">
  <template #default="{ item, index }">
    <div class="flex h-full items-center justify-between px-3 text-sm">
      <span>{{ item.name }}</span>
      <span class="text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">#{{ index + 1 }}</span>
    </div>
  </template>
</VirtualList>
```

Example: Jump to a row and read the range
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const rows = Array.from({ length: 10000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, name: 'Row ' + (i + 1) }))
const list = ref(null)
const range = ref({ start: 0, end: 0 })
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <div class="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline" @click="list.scrollToIndex(5000, 'center')">Go to row 5001</Button>
    <span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Rendered {{ range.start }} - {{ range.end }}</span>
  </div>
  <VirtualList ref="list" :items="rows" :item-height="32" :height="192" item-key="id" label="Jump list" class="rounded-md border" @range="range = $event">
    <template #default="{ item }"><div class="flex h-full items-center px-3 text-sm">{{ item.name }}</div></template>
  </VirtualList>
</div>
```

Example: Variants
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const rows = Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, name: 'Row ' + (i + 1) }))
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <VirtualList :items="rows" :item-height="32" :height="96" label="Bordered rows" variant="bordered" item-key="id"><template #default="{ item }"><span class="px-3 text-sm leading-8">{{ item.name }}</span></template></VirtualList>
  <VirtualList :items="rows" :item-height="32" :height="96" label="Divided rows" variant="divided" item-key="id"><template #default="{ item }"><span class="px-3 text-sm leading-8">{{ item.name }}</span></template></VirtualList>
  <VirtualList :items="rows" :item-height="32" :height="96" label="Striped rows" variant="striped" item-key="id"><template #default="{ item }"><span class="px-3 text-sm leading-8">{{ item.name }}</span></template></VirtualList>
</div>
```

Example: Empty state
```vue
<VirtualList :items="[]" :item-height="32" :height="80" label="Empty list" class="rounded-md border">
  <template #empty>Nothing to show</template>
</VirtualList>
```

# Carousel
group: data-display / Media
Scroll-snap carousel with previous / next buttons, dots, keyboard control, optional loop and accessible autoplay.

Use `Carousel` for a small set of equal-weight slides (image galleries, feature tours, testimonials). It is built on native CSS scroll-snap: touch and trackpad swiping, momentum and snapping come from the browser, the component adds an index (`v-model`), buttons, dots, keyboard keys and autoplay. Compose `CarouselContent` (the scroller) with `CarouselItem` slides, and optionally `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselNext`, `CarouselDots` and `CarouselCounter`. Slides are `basis-full` by default; override with a class (`basis-1/3`) to show several at once. Autoplay is off by default, pauses while the pointer is over the carousel or focus is inside, shows a pause/play button (WCAG 2.2.2) and is disabled entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`. `loop` wraps around (rewind), it does not clone slides. Do not use a carousel for critical content or long lists: prefer a grid or `VirtualList`.

import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext, CarouselDots, CarouselPlayPause, CarouselCounter } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- modelValue: number = 0 - Active slide index (v-model; also works uncontrolled). Out-of-range, negative and NaN values are clamped.
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - Scroll axis; invalid values fall back to horizontal.
- loop: boolean = false - Wrap from last to first and first to last (buttons never disable).
- autoplay: boolean = false - Advance automatically. Ignored under prefers-reduced-motion; stops on the last slide unless `loop`.
- interval: number = 5000 - Autoplay delay in ms; non-finite or <= 0 falls back to 5000.
- pauseOnHover: boolean = true - Pause autoplay while hovered. Focus inside the carousel always pauses.
- live: 'auto' | 'off' | 'polite' | 'assertive' = 'auto' - `aria-live` of the track. `auto` is off while autoplay runs (no chatter) and polite otherwise.
- label: string - Accessible name of the carousel region. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); there is no default, so several carousels on a page can be told apart.
- pauseButton: boolean = true - Render the built-in pause/play button while `autoplay` is on.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- CarouselContent - The scroll-snap track: focusable `role="group"` named "Slides", aria-live region. Give it a fixed height for vertical carousels.
    - label: string = 'Slides' - Accessible name of the track.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- CarouselItem - One slide: `role="group"`, `aria-roledescription="slide"`, labelled "n of N". Registers itself with the carousel.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last; use `basis-*` for multi-slide views.
- CarouselPrevious - Previous button, positioned over the carousel; disabled at the start unless `loop`.
    - label: string = 'Previous slide' - Accessible name.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- CarouselNext - Next button, positioned over the carousel; disabled at the end unless `loop`.
    - label: string = 'Next slide' - Accessible name.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- CarouselDots - One button per slide (`aria-current` marks the active one). Each button is a 24px target (44px on touch) around a 10px dot; the active dot is filled, the others are outlined. Scoped `dot` slot: `{ index, active, select }`.
    - label: string = 'Choose slide' - Accessible name of the dot group.
    - dotLabel: (position: number, total: number) => string - Builds each dot name (default "Go to slide n").
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- CarouselPlayPause - Pause / start button for autoplay. `Carousel` renders it automatically while `autoplay` is on; set `pauseButton` to false to place it yourself.
    - pauseLabel: string = 'Pause automatic slide show' - Accessible name while running.
    - playLabel: string = 'Start automatic slide show' - Accessible name while paused.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- CarouselCounter - Visible "2 / 4" position text with tabular figures. Scoped default slot: `{ index, count }`.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.

Slots:
- default ({ index: number; count: number; goTo: (i: number) => void; next: () => void; prev: () => void }) - Carousel parts and any custom controls.

Events:
- update:modelValue [index: number] - The active slide changed (button, dot, key, swipe or autoplay).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `Carousel` has no `CarouselContent`, or `CarouselContent` has no `CarouselItem`.
- Throws a ContractError when `Carousel` has no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`); there is no generic default name.

Rules:
- Always compose Carousel > CarouselContent > CarouselItem; add CarouselPrevious / CarouselNext / CarouselDots as siblings of CarouselContent.
- Set `label` so the region has a meaningful accessible name.
- Use `basis-1/2`, `basis-1/3` on CarouselItem for multiple slides per view; vertical carousels need a fixed height class on CarouselContent.
- Keep autoplay off unless content is non-essential; never rely on it to reveal important information. Autoplay always renders a pause button: do not hide it.
- Slides register in DOM order; keep CarouselItem keys stable when reordering.

Accessibility:
- Root is `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and an `aria-label` (set `label`). The track is a focusable `role="group"` named "Slides"; each slide is `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and an "n of N" label.
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the track, buttons and dots. On the track ArrowLeft / ArrowRight (ArrowUp / ArrowDown when vertical) move one slide and Home / End jump to the first / last. Arrow keys typed on links, buttons and form fields inside a slide keep their own behaviour. The focused track also scrolls natively and snaps to a slide.
- Dots are real buttons: 24px targets (44px on touch), `aria-current="true"` on the active one, and the active dot differs by fill, not only by colour. Previous and next sit at the logical start and end, so they mirror in RTL.
- The track is `aria-live="off"` while autoplay runs and `polite` otherwise (`live` overrides), so slide changes are announced only when the user caused them. `CarouselCounter` shows the position with tabular figures.
- Autoplay never runs under prefers-reduced-motion (scrolling is then instant instead of smooth), stops while the pointer is over the carousel or focus is inside, and always comes with a pause / start button (WCAG 2.2.2) that is the first control in tab order.
- Previous and next disable at the ends unless `loop`.

Example: Basic carousel
```vue
<Carousel class="mx-auto max-w-md" label="Highlights">
  <CarouselContent class="rounded-lg border">
    <CarouselItem v-for="n in 4" :key="n">
      <div class="flex h-40 items-center justify-center bg-muted text-xl font-semibold">Slide {{ n }}</div>
    </CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselPrevious />
  <CarouselNext />
  <CarouselDots />
  <CarouselCounter class="pt-2 text-center" />
</Carousel>
```

Example: v-model, loop and autoplay
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const index = ref(0)
const tips = ['Press the arrow keys to move.', 'Hover to pause the rotation.', 'Home and End jump to the ends.']
</script>

<div class="mx-auto flex max-w-md flex-col gap-3">
  <Carousel v-model="index" loop autoplay :interval="4000" label="Rotating tips">
    <CarouselContent class="rounded-lg border">
      <CarouselItem v-for="tip in tips" :key="tip">
        <p class="flex h-28 items-center justify-center px-6 text-center text-sm">{{ tip }}</p>
      </CarouselItem>
    </CarouselContent>
    <CarouselDots />
  </Carousel>
  <p class="text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">Slide {{ index + 1 }} of {{ tips.length }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Several slides per view
```vue
<Carousel class="mx-auto max-w-lg px-12" label="Cards">
  <CarouselContent class="gap-2">
    <CarouselItem v-for="n in 6" :key="n" class="basis-1/3">
      <div class="flex h-24 items-center justify-center rounded-md border bg-card">{{ n }}</div>
    </CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselPrevious />
  <CarouselNext />
</Carousel>
```

Example: Vertical
```vue
<Carousel orientation="vertical" class="mx-auto max-w-xs" label="Vertical slides">
  <CarouselContent class="h-40 rounded-lg border">
    <CarouselItem v-for="n in 3" :key="n">
      <div class="flex h-full items-center justify-center bg-muted">Slide {{ n }}</div>
    </CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselPrevious />
  <CarouselNext />
</Carousel>
```

# StatBar
group: data-display / Meters
Label + value + proportional bar for usage vs limit (quota, disk, budget).

Use `StatBar` to show how much of a limit is consumed. It renders a caption row (label left, value text right) and a track with a `role="meter"` fill. Use `tone="auto"` to turn the bar warning/danger as it fills. Ratios are clamped to 0..100% so overflowing values never break layout; show the real numbers via `valueText`. For task progress (something completing over time) use a Progress component instead.

import { StatBar } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- label*: string - Caption and accessible name of the meter.
- value*: number - Current value. Non-finite or negative values render as empty.
- max: number = 100 - Value that fills the bar. Must be finite and > 0, otherwise the bar is empty.
- valueText: string - Right-hand text and aria-valuetext. Defaults to the rounded percentage.
- tone: 'auto' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - `auto` escalates to warning at `warnAt` and danger at `dangerAt`.
- warnAt: number = 0.75 - Ratio (0..1) at which `auto` turns warning.
- dangerAt: number = 0.9 - Ratio (0..1) at which `auto` turns danger.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Bar thickness: 6px, 10px or 16px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- layout: 'stacked' | 'inline' = 'stacked' - `stacked` shows the caption row above the bar. `inline` puts label, bar and value on one row (the bar takes the free width). `hideLabel` always renders the bar alone. Unknown values fall back to `stacked`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - End caps of the track and fill: pill (default) or square. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- hideLabel: boolean = false - Hide the caption row (keep it when the surrounding UI already labels the bar).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `label` is blank.
- Throws a ContractError when `value` is not a finite number (show a skeleton or hide the bar while it loads).
- Throws a ContractError when `max` is not a finite number above 0.

Rules:
- Always pass `valueText` with the real "used / limit" numbers.
- Use `tone="auto"` for quotas; fixed tones only for categorical meaning.
- Do not use StatBar for loading progress.

Accessibility:
- Uses `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` 100, `aria-valuenow` (clamped 0..100), `aria-valuetext` and the label as accessible name.
- Colour is never the only signal: always provide `valueText` with the real numbers. The value text uses `tabular-nums`, so stacked bars line up.
- `layout="inline"` keeps the DOM order (label, value, then the meter) but shows the meter between them visually; the meter keeps its own `aria-label`, so the name does not depend on the row. `size`, `layout` and `shape` change geometry only.
- The fill animates its width only when reduced motion is not requested. The bar is fluid and the caption row wraps its content, so nothing overflows at 320px.

Example: Basic
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm"><StatBar label="Storage" :value="42" /></div>
```

Example: Sizes, layouts and shapes
```vue
<div class="flex max-w-md flex-col gap-4">
  <StatBar size="sm" label="Small" :value="30" />
  <StatBar size="md" label="Medium" :value="50" />
  <StatBar size="lg" label="Large" :value="70" />
  <StatBar layout="inline" label="Inline" :value="45" />
  <StatBar shape="square" size="lg" label="Square" :value="60" />
</div>
```

Example: Usage against limits with auto tone
```vue
<div class="flex max-w-sm flex-col gap-4">
  <StatBar label="Requests / day" :value="420" :max="1000" value-text="420 / 1,000" tone="auto" />
  <StatBar label="Budget / month" :value="82" tone="auto" value-text="82 / 100 units" />
  <StatBar label="Seats" :value="19" :max="20" tone="auto" value-text="19 / 20" size="sm" />
</div>
```

# Leaderboard
group: data-display / Rankings
Ranked entries as a list, a table or a podium, with ties, deltas, proportional bars and a highlighted entry.

Use `Leaderboard` to show who or what is ahead on one number: sales by region, tickets closed by team, tests passed by suite. Each entry is `{ id, label, value, rank?, delta?, avatar? }`. Entries are sorted (`sort`), ranked (`ties`) and formatted (`valueFormat`, `locale`) for you.

`variant="list"` is an ordered list of ruled rows. `variant="table"` is a real table (rank, name, value, change) inside a focusable, named scroll region. `variant="podium"` shows the top three as steps in the visual order 2-1-3 while the DOM stays in rank order, with the remaining entries in a list below.

Ranks: `competition` (default) gives equal values the same rank and skips the next (1, 2, 2, 4); `dense` does not skip (1, 2, 2, 3); `none` ranks by position. An entry `rank` always wins. Values that are not finite numbers render the fallback text, sort last and have no rank. `sort="asc"` makes the lowest value rank 1 (times, costs); `sort="none"` keeps the order you pass.

A delta is shown as an arrow icon and a signed number, never as colour alone. `highlight` marks one entry with `aria-current`, a tinted surface and the visible text from `highlightLabel`. Bars are decorative: the number is always the text. For a single quota against a limit use StatBar; for a full data grid use DataTable.

import { Leaderboard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- entries: LeaderboardEntry[] = [] - The entries: `{ id, label, value, rank?, delta?, avatar? }`. `id` is a unique non-empty string or number. `avatar` is an image source string (an inline data URI works) or `{ src?, fallback? }`; without an image the initials of the label (or `fallback`) are shown. An empty or missing array shows the empty state.
- label: string - Accessible name of the leaderboard and the hidden table caption. Required, or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.
- variant: 'list' | 'table' | 'podium' = 'list' - `list` ruled rows, `table` a real table in a scroll region, `podium` the top three as 2-1-3 steps and the rest in a list. Unknown values fall back to `list`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text and avatar size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- density: 'comfortable' | 'compact' = 'comfortable' - Row spacing. Unknown values fall back to `comfortable`.
- showRank: boolean = true - Show the rank of each entry (a column in the table).
- highlight: string | number - Id of the entry to mark: `aria-current="true"`, a tinted surface and the visible `highlightLabel`.
- highlightLabel: string = 'Selected' - Visible text on the highlighted entry. Change it to match the meaning, for example "Your team".
- bars: boolean = false - Draw a bar under each entry, proportional to the largest value (negative values draw an empty bar). Decorative: hidden from assistive technology.
- valueFormat: LeaderboardValueFormat - Number format of values and deltas: `{ format, currency, unit, notation, minimumFractionDigits, maximumFractionDigits, signDisplay }`, the same options as FormattedNumber (`format` is `decimal`, `percent`, `currency`, `unit` or `compact`). Deltas always show a sign.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for numbers (`de-DE`). Defaults to `en`, not the browser locale, so server and client agree.
- ties: 'competition' | 'dense' | 'none' = 'competition' - How equal values rank: 1 2 2 4, 1 2 2 3, or by position. Unknown values fall back to `competition`.
- sort: 'desc' | 'asc' | 'none' = 'desc' - Highest first, lowest first (the lowest is rank 1), or keep the given order (ranks still follow the highest value). The sort is stable. Unknown values fall back to `desc`.
- columnLabels: LeaderboardColumnLabels - Texts of the table headers and the hidden word before each rank: `{ rank, name, value, delta }`. Defaults: Rank, Name, Value, Change.
- emptyText: string = 'No entries yet.' - Text shown when there are no entries and no `empty` slot.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- entry ({ entry: LeaderboardEntry, rank: number | null, index: number, highlighted: boolean }) - Replaces the name of an entry (the label text). The avatar, rank, highlight text and value stay.
- value ({ entry: LeaderboardEntry, rank: number | null, index: number, formatted: string }) - Replaces the formatted value of an entry.
- empty - Content shown when there are no entries (replaces `emptyText`).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when two entries share the same `id`.
- Throws a ContractError when an entry has no valid `id` (a non-empty string or a finite number).
- Throws a ContractError when an entry has a blank `label`.

Rules:
- Entry avatars blur when a surrounding `ConfigProvider` sets `blurMedia` (privacy, not decoration); there is no prop on this component.
- Always pass `label` (or `aria-label`) and give every entry a unique `id`.
- Pass raw numbers in `value` and set `valueFormat` (and `locale`) instead of pre-formatting strings.
- Use `highlight` plus `highlightLabel` to mark the current user or team; never mark it with colour only.
- Use `ties="dense"` when the next rank must not skip; use `sort="asc"` when lower is better.
- Do not use Leaderboard for one value against a limit (StatBar) or for sortable, filterable data (DataTable).

Accessibility:
- The list variant is an ordered list (`ol` and `li`); the table variant is a real `table` with a hidden caption, `th scope="col"` headers and `th scope="row"` names inside a focusable region with the same name, so it scrolls by keyboard at 320px; the podium is an ordered list of the top three in rank order (CSS only reorders them visually to 2-1-3) followed by a list of the rest.
- Each rank is text, with a visually hidden "Rank" before it. The highlighted entry has `aria-current="true"` and visible text from `highlightLabel`, so it never relies on colour. A delta is an arrow icon plus a signed number.
- Bars and avatars are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the label and the number are always text. Long labels truncate with a `title` and `min-w-0`, hostile text is rendered as text, and logical properties make it work right-to-left.
- Numbers use tabular figures and bidi isolation (FormattedNumber), so a sign or digit never reorders in right-to-left text. The leaderboard is not interactive, so it has no keyboard map beyond the scroll region of the table.

Example: List
```vue
<div class="max-w-md"><Leaderboard label="Tickets closed by team (sample)" :entries="[
    { id: 'a', label: 'Team A', value: 128 },
    { id: 'b', label: 'Team B', value: 117 },
    { id: 'c', label: 'Team C', value: 96 },
    { id: 'd', label: 'Team D', value: 74 },
    { id: 'e', label: 'Team E', value: 52 },
  ]" /></div>
```

# Gauge
group: data-display / Statistics
SVG gauge (semicircle, three-quarter arc or linear bar) for a value within a range, with threshold tones, a label and role=meter semantics.

Use `Gauge` to show one measurement against a known range (CPU load, disk usage, score). `thresholds` map value bands to tones (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, ...): the highest threshold whose `value` is <= the current value wins. Values are clamped to the range, reversed `min` / `max` are swapped and `null` / `NaN` render an empty gauge reading `–`. The arc sweeps in on mount and on change unless the user prefers reduced motion. `variant` picks the shape: `semicircle` (default half-dial), `arc` (three-quarter dial with the value inside) or `linear` (a horizontal bar with caption and value on one line); all three keep the same meter semantics, name and value text. Use `StatBar` for linear usage bars and `Progress` for task completion; a gauge is for a live reading, not progress.

import { Gauge } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- value: number | null - Current value. null / NaN / Infinity mean "no data".
- min: number = 0 - Range start. Non-finite values fall back to 0.
- max: number = 100 - Range end. Non-finite values fall back to 100.
- thresholds: GaugeThreshold[] - Tone bands: `{ value, tone }`, applied when the value is >= `value`.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - Tone below all thresholds (or when there are none).
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Rendered width (w-24, w-40, w-56) and text size.
- variant: 'semicircle' | 'arc' | 'linear' = 'semicircle' - `semicircle` half-dial with the value at its foot, `arc` a three-quarter dial with the value centred, `linear` a horizontal bar (caption left, value right, same width as the dial). Same `role="meter"`, name and `aria-valuetext` in all three.
- label: string - Caption under the value; also the accessible name. Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- valueText: string - Replaces the formatted value inside the gauge and `aria-valuetext` (e.g. "3.2 of 4 GB").
- animated: boolean = true - Animate the arc; always off under prefers-reduced-motion.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; use it to set the size (`w-64`).

Slots:
- default ({ value: number; percent: number; tone: GaugeTone; text: string }) - Replace the centre value (e.g. add a unit).
- label - Replace the caption under the value.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Always give a Gauge a `label` or aria-label.
- List thresholds ascending, starting at the range minimum, so the tone below the first band is explicit.
- Use `variant="linear"` where a row or card needs a gauge to line up with text (give it `class="w-full"`); use `arc` when the value is the focus and `semicircle` for the compact dial.
- Use `valueText` for units; the default text is just the rounded number.
- Use the tone `danger` (not `destructive`) for the red state.

Accessibility:
- Root has `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`; the label becomes `aria-label` (falls back to "Gauge"; pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` when there is no visible label).
- With no data the root switches to `role="img"` with the label "<label>: No data", because `role="meter"` requires `aria-valuenow`. Min, max and valuetext are omitted then.
- `variant` does not change the semantics: every shape is `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` and the same name; without data all three are `role="img"` labelled "<label>: No data". The arc, the bar and their track are `aria-hidden`; the value and caption stay real text.
- The value uses `tabular-nums`; the caption is 12px text. The width follows `size` or `class` and never exceeds the container needs at 320px (`w-56` is the widest).
- The arc animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; the SVG itself is aria-hidden.
- Tone is also exposed as `data-tone`; do not rely on colour alone: add `valueText` such as "Critical: 96%" when the state matters.

Example: Basic gauge
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-6">
  <Gauge :value="42" label="CPU" size="sm" />
  <Gauge :value="68" label="Memory" />
  <Gauge :value="91" label="Disk" size="lg" />
</div>
```

Example: Variant: semicircle, arc, linear
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-8">
  <Gauge variant="semicircle" :value="68" label="Memory" />
  <Gauge variant="arc" :value="68" label="Memory" />
  <Gauge variant="linear" :value="68" label="Memory" tone="info" />
</div>
```

Example: Linear sizes and thresholds
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-md gap-4">
  <Gauge variant="linear" size="sm" :value="35" label="Queue" value-text="35% normal" :thresholds="[{ value: 0, tone: 'success' }, { value: 70, tone: 'warning' }, { value: 90, tone: 'danger' }]" class="w-full" />
  <Gauge variant="linear" size="md" :value="78" label="Queue" value-text="78% raised" :thresholds="[{ value: 0, tone: 'success' }, { value: 70, tone: 'warning' }, { value: 90, tone: 'danger' }]" class="w-full" />
  <Gauge variant="linear" size="lg" :value="96" label="Queue" value-text="96% high" :thresholds="[{ value: 0, tone: 'success' }, { value: 70, tone: 'warning' }, { value: 90, tone: 'danger' }]" class="w-full" />
</div>
```

Example: Threshold tones
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const thresholds = [
  { value: 0, tone: 'success' },
  { value: 70, tone: 'warning' },
  { value: 90, tone: 'danger' },
]
</script>

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-6">
  <Gauge v-for="v in [35, 78, 96]" :key="v" :value="v" :label="'Load ' + v" :value-text="v + '% ' + (v >= 90 ? 'high' : v >= 70 ? 'raised' : 'normal')" :thresholds="thresholds" />
</div>
```

Example: Custom range and slot
```vue

<Gauge :value="72" label="Battery" :animated="false">
  <template #default="{ value }">{{ value }}%</template>
</Gauge>
```

Example: No data
```vue

  <Gauge :value="null" label="Throughput" />
  <Gauge variant="arc" :value="null" label="Throughput" />
  <Gauge variant="linear" :value="null" label="Throughput" />
</div>
```

# KpiTile
group: data-display / Statistics
Headline metric tile: label, value, trend delta with good/bad colouring, hint, icon and loading skeleton.

Use `KpiTile` for dashboard headline numbers. `trend` (`up`/`down`/`flat`) picks the arrow; `goodWhen` says which direction is desirable so colour reflects meaning (error rate going down is good). Group tiles with `StatGroup`. Numbers are formatted for you (`12345.6` shows `12,345.6`); pass a string for pre-formatted values such as `99.9%` or `1.2 MB`. Values, deltas and the sparkline use tabular figures so columns of tiles line up. Variations: `size="compact"` for dense dashboards; `variant="inverted"` for one high-contrast hero tile; `sparkline` (array of numbers, or the `sparkline` slot) for a mini trend line; `progress` (0-100) for a bar showing usage against a target. All still accept the Card surfaces (`outline`, `elevated`, `interactive`, `ghost`, ...). For usage against a hard limit with labels use `StatBar`.

import { KpiTile } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- label*: string - Metric name.
- value: string | number | null - Headline value; numbers are formatted, null / NaN / Infinity show `–`.
- delta: string | number - Change text; numbers get a sign and formatting.
- trend: 'up' | 'down' | 'flat' = 'flat' - Direction of the change (arrow icon).
- goodWhen: 'up' | 'down' | 'none' = 'up' - Which direction is good. `none` always uses the neutral colour.
- hint: string - Supporting text, e.g. "vs last 7 days".
- icon: IconDefinition - FontAwesome icon shown top-right.
- loading: boolean = false - Shows a skeleton instead of value/delta and sets aria-busy.
- variant: 'default' | 'outline' | 'elevated' | 'interactive' | 'ghost' | 'filled' | 'with-image-header' | 'inverted' = 'default' - Card surface, or `inverted` = foreground background with light text. The old `accent` edge stripe was removed; a stale `accent` value renders the plain default tile.
- size: 'default' | 'compact' | 'lg' = 'default' - `compact` = `p-3 gap-1`, smaller label and value; `lg` = `p-6 gap-3` with a 36px value. Unknown values behave like `default`.
- layout: 'stacked' | 'split' | 'centered' = 'stacked' - `stacked` is the default column. `split` puts the label at the start and the value at the end of one row (delta, sparkline and progress span the full width below). `centered` centres every row. Unknown values behave like `stacked`.
- tone: 'neutral' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' = 'primary' - Colour of the progress bar and sparkline. Unknown values fall back to `primary`.
- sparklineVariant: 'area' | 'line' = 'area' - `area` fills under the built-in sparkline; `line` draws the line only. Unknown values behave like `area`.
- sparkline: number[] - Values for a mini area sparkline under the delta (non-finite entries become gaps). Hidden while `loading` or when empty.
- progress: number | null - Percentage 0-100 (clamped) rendered as `role="progressbar"`; null / NaN / Infinity hide it.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element to render (e.g. `a` for a linking tile).
- asChild: boolean = false - Render the single slot child instead of a wrapper.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- value - Replace the value text.
- delta - Replace the delta text (arrow and colour remain).
- hint - Replace the hint (e.g. with a Sparkline).
- icon - Custom icon content.
- sparkline - Replace the built-in sparkline (e.g. a custom chart); rendered below the delta row.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `label` is blank.

Rules:
- Set `good-when="down"` for cost, latency, error rate metrics so decreases are green.
- Wrap tiles in StatGroup, not a hand-written grid.
- Pass pre-formatted strings for currency/percent; numbers only get generic grouping.
- Use `size="compact"` in dense grids and `variant="inverted"` for at most one hero tile per view. There is no accent stripe or gradient variant.
- Pass `sparkline` / `progress` props rather than custom children; use the `sparkline` slot only for a different chart.
- Use `loading` instead of rendering a zero while data is fetching.

Accessibility:
- The delta includes visually-hidden text ("Increase:", "Decrease:", "No change:") so direction is not conveyed by colour/arrow alone.
- `progress` renders `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` and the label "<label> progress"; the sparkline has an `aria-label` ("<label> trend"). Neither replaces the textual value.
- Colour is never the only signal: tone and sentiment colours accompany an arrow icon and hidden text. Numbers use `tabular-nums`.
- `layout` and `size` only rearrange and rescale the same elements in the same reading order (label, value, delta, sparkline, progress); the colour pairs are unchanged. `split` is a two-column grid whose label column shrinks and wraps, so a long label never overflows at 320px.
- Loading sets `aria-busy` and announces "Loading" via a status region.
- Render with `as="a"` (or `as-child`) when the tile navigates; a plain tile is not interactive.

Example: Basic tiles
```vue
<StatGroup aria-label="Sample data: basic tiles">
  <KpiTile label="Requests" :value="1284" delta="+8.2%" trend="up" hint="vs previous period" />
  <KpiTile label="Error rate" value="0.4%" delta="-0.1pt" trend="down" good-when="down" />
  <KpiTile label="Queue depth" :value="37" delta="0" trend="flat" />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: Icons, sparkline and loading
```vue
<StatGroup :columns="3" aria-label="Sample data: icons and loading">
  <KpiTile label="Traffic" value="48.2k" delta="+12%" trend="up" :icon="faDollarSign">
    <template #hint><Sparkline :data="[3, 5, 4, 7, 9, 8, 12]" area label="Traffic trend, sample data" /></template>
  </KpiTile>
  <KpiTile label="Servers" :value="12" :icon="faServer" hint="2 draining" />
  <KpiTile label="Latency p95" loading />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: Compact
```vue
<StatGroup :columns="3" aria-label="Sample data: compact tiles">
  <KpiTile size="compact" label="Requests" :value="98213" delta="+4%" trend="up" />
  <KpiTile size="compact" label="Errors" :value="12" delta="-2" trend="down" good-when="down" />
  <KpiTile size="compact" label="Latency" value="142 ms" />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: With sparkline
```vue

  <KpiTile label="Throughput" value="48.2k" delta="+12%" trend="up" :sparkline="[3, 5, 4, 7, 9, 8, 12]" tone="success" />
  <KpiTile label="Retries" :value="320" :sparkline="[9, 7, 8, 5, 6, 4, 3]" />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: Line-only sparkline
```vue

  <KpiTile label="Latency" value="142 ms" sparkline-variant="line" :sparkline="[3, 5, 4, 7, 9, 8, 12]" />
  <KpiTile label="Retries" :value="320" sparkline-variant="line" :sparkline="[9, 7, 8, 5, 6, 4, 3]" tone="warning" />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: With progress
```vue

  <KpiTile label="Storage" value="64 GB" hint="of 100 GB" :progress="64" />
  <KpiTile label="Quota used" value="92%" hint="Nearly exhausted" :progress="92" tone="danger" />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: Sizes and layouts
```vue
<StatGroup :columns="3" aria-label="Sample data: sizes and layouts">
  <KpiTile size="lg" label="Requests" :value="98213" delta="+4%" trend="up" />
  <KpiTile layout="split" label="Queue depth" :value="37" delta="-3" trend="down" good-when="down" hint="vs yesterday" :progress="37" />
  <KpiTile layout="centered" label="Success rate" value="99.2%" delta="+0.1pt" trend="up" :sparkline="[4, 5, 5, 6, 7]" />

```

Example: Inverted
```vue

  <KpiTile variant="inverted" label="Total requests" value="1.2M" delta="+8.4%" trend="up" hint="vs previous period" :progress="72" />
  <KpiTile variant="inverted" label="Failure rate" value="2.1%" delta="-0.3pt" trend="down" good-when="down" :sparkline="[5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2]" />
</StatGroup>
```

# StatGroup
group: data-display / Statistics
Responsive grid wrapper for KpiTile (or any tile) rows.

Use `StatGroup` to lay out a row of `KpiTile`s. The default `auto` mode fits as many tiles of at least 12rem per row as the container allows; pass `columns` for a fixed number at the `lg` breakpoint (collapsing to 2 then 1 column on small screens). Layouts: `grid` (default; separate tiles with gaps, best for card-style `KpiTile`s), `inline` (wrapping flex row, tiles grow from 10rem; best for a handful of compact tiles in a toolbar/header, `columns` is ignored), `divided` (one bordered surface with hairline dividers; the tiles lose their own border, radius and shadow; choose `columns` that divide the tile count evenly so no empty divider-coloured cell shows).

import { StatGroup } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- layout: 'grid' | 'inline' | 'divided' = 'grid' - Arrangement of the tiles; unknown values fall back to `grid`.
- gap: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between tiles of the `grid` and `inline` layouts: 0, 0.5rem, 1rem, 1.5rem. `divided` ignores it (its rules are hairlines). Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- columns: 'auto' | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 'auto' - Column count at the largest breakpoint; invalid values fall back to `auto`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Tiles.

Rules:
- Use `layout="divided"` for a single framed stats strip (columns must divide the tile count), `inline` for a few compact tiles, `grid` otherwise.
- Use `columns` only when you need an exact count; prefer `auto`.
- Always add aria-label when the group is not introduced by a heading.

Accessibility:
- Rendered with `role="group"`; give it an `aria-label` describing the metrics.
- Tiles keep their reading order in every layout and wrap or stack on a phone (`auto` fits 12rem columns, fixed counts collapse to 1 or 2 columns), so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px. Values and deltas inside the tiles use tabular figures.

Example: Auto layout
```vue
<StatGroup aria-label="Sample data: auto layout">
  <KpiTile label="Requests" :value="98213" />
  <KpiTile label="Errors" :value="12" />
  <KpiTile label="Latency" value="142 ms" />
</StatGroup>
```

Example: Fixed four columns with aria-label

```vue
<StatGroup :columns="4" aria-label="Key metrics">

  <KpiTile label="B" :value="2" />
  <KpiTile label="C" :value="3" />
  <KpiTile label="D" :value="4" />
</StatGroup>
```

```vue
<StatGroup layout="inline" aria-label="Summary">

  <KpiTile size="compact" label="In review" :value="7" />
```

# TrendBadge
group: data-display / Statistics
Compact up / down / flat change indicator with good-or-bad colouring, Intl formatting and screen-reader text.

Use `TrendBadge` next to a metric to show how it moved. `direction` picks the arrow (or is derived from the sign of `value`); `goodWhen` (or `inverse`) says which direction is desirable, so a drop in latency is green and a drop in revenue is red. The magnitude is printed without sign because the arrow carries the direction. Formatting goes through `Intl.NumberFormat` (`number`, `percent`, `compact`, `currency`). `null`, `NaN` and `Infinity` render an en dash and announce "No data". Use `KpiTile` when you need the whole tile; use this badge inside tables, lists and headings.

import { TrendBadge } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- direction: 'up' | 'down' | 'flat' - Arrow direction. Derived from the sign of `value` when omitted; invalid values are ignored.
- value: number | null - Magnitude of the change (sign is not printed). Omit for an arrow-only badge; null / NaN / Infinity show `–`.
- goodWhen: 'up' | 'down' | 'none' = 'up' - Which direction is good. `none` always uses the neutral colour.
- inverse: boolean = false - Shorthand for `goodWhen="down"` (cost, latency, error rate).
- format: 'number' | 'percent' | 'compact' | 'currency' = 'number' - `percent` appends % to the value as-is (12 becomes 12%).
- currency: string - ISO 4217 code for `format="currency"`; invalid codes fall back to a plain number.
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale. Unset uses the ConfigProvider locale, then `en`; invalid values fall back to `en`.
- fractionDigits: number = 1 - Maximum fraction digits (clamped to 0-20).
- variant: 'soft' | 'solid' | 'ghost' | 'outline' = 'soft' - Tinted background, solid fill, text only, or bordered text. Unknown values fall back to `soft`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corner radius: 6px, fully round, or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Badge size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default ({ text: string; direction: TrendDirection; tone: "good" | "bad" | "neutral" }) - Replace the visible value text (the screen-reader text keeps the formatted value).

Rules:
- Pass the absolute magnitude or a signed number; the sign is never printed, the arrow is.
- Set `inverse` (or good-when="down") for cost, latency and error-rate metrics.
- Use `format="percent"` with percentage points (12 means 12%), not fractions.
- Do not pass pre-formatted strings as `value`; use the default slot for custom text.

Accessibility:
- The arrow is decorative (aria-hidden); a visually-hidden text states the change: "Increase of 12.4", "Decrease of 3.2", "No change" or "No data".
- Colour is never the only signal: direction is conveyed by the arrow and the hidden text, meaning by the text.
- `outline` keeps the 1px border in forced-colors mode and uses the same text tokens as `ghost`; `shape` changes only the radius.
- Colours come from theme tokens (success / destructive / muted) and keep contrast in light and dark mode. The number uses `tabular-nums`, and the badge never wraps (`whitespace-nowrap`).

Example: Up, down and flat
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <TrendBadge :value="12.4" format="percent" />
  <TrendBadge :value="-3.2" format="percent" />
  <TrendBadge :value="0" format="percent" />
</div>
```

Example: Down can be good
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <TrendBadge :value="-120" inverse><template #default="{ text }">{{ text }} ms</template></TrendBadge>
  <TrendBadge :value="8" good-when="down" format="percent" />
  <TrendBadge direction="up" :value="5" good-when="none" />
</div>
```

Example: Variants and sizes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <TrendBadge variant="soft" size="sm" :value="4" />
  <TrendBadge variant="solid" :value="-4" />
  <TrendBadge variant="ghost" size="lg" :value="1500" format="compact" />
</div>
```

Example: Outline and shapes
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <TrendBadge variant="outline" :value="6" />
  <TrendBadge variant="outline" :value="-6" />
  <TrendBadge variant="soft" shape="pill" :value="6" />
  <TrendBadge variant="solid" shape="square" :value="-2" />
</div>
```

Example: Currency and missing data
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <TrendBadge :value="1234.5" format="currency" currency="USD" locale="en-US" :fraction-digits="2" />
  <TrendBadge :value="null" />
  <TrendBadge direction="down" />
</div>
```

# UptimeBar
group: data-display / Status
Row of segments, one per check or period, each marked up, degraded, down or unknown, for status pages.

Use `UptimeBar` to show the history of one service as a strip: one segment per check (or per day), oldest first. Each segment is `up` (success), `degraded` (warning), `down` (destructive) or `unknown` (muted track). Segments share the width, with a 1px minimum, so 90 days or 200 checks fit a phone; above 100 segments the gap between them is dropped. The strip is one image with a text alternative: "API: 28 checks: 26 up, 1 degraded, 1 down", and the same counts show as a visible summary line, so state never relies on colour alone. Each segment has a native tooltip with its `label` and state name. Pass `summary` (or the `summary` slot) for your own line, such as an uptime percentage you computed. Not a chart for numeric values (use `Sparkline` or `BarChart`) and not a single indicator (use `StatusDot`).

import { UptimeBar } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- segments*: { state: 'up' | 'degraded' | 'down' | 'unknown'; label?: string }[] - One entry per check or period, oldest first. Unknown states are drawn as `unknown`. An empty array shows `emptyText`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the image, e.g. "API checks, last 28 days". Required (or pass `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- stateLabels: Partial<Record<'up' | 'degraded' | 'down' | 'unknown', string>> - Replaces the state names in tooltips and the summary. English defaults: up, degraded, down, unknown. Blank values are ignored.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Segment height: 16px, 32px or 48px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- summary: string - Replaces the generated summary in the visible line and the accessible name.
- hideSummary: boolean = false - Hide the visible summary line; the accessible name still carries it.
- emptyText: string = 'No checks yet' - Shown when there are no segments.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge onto the root element.

Slots:
- summary ({ total: number; counts: Record<state, number>; text: string }) - Replaces the visible summary line. The accessible name is unchanged; use `summary` to change both.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `label` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `segments` is not an array. An empty array is valid and shows `emptyText`.

Rules:
- Pass `segments` oldest first, one per check or period; add `label` (time or day) so tooltips are useful.
- Always set `label`; compute figures such as an uptime percentage yourself and pass them as `summary`.
- Translate state names with `stateLabels`; use `StatusDot` for one current state instead.
- Do not invent uptime numbers in examples; label sample data as sample.

Accessibility:
- The strip is a `role="img"` named "<label>: <summary>", so a screen reader gets the counts without 200 separate stops. Segments are not focusable.
- State never relies on colour alone: the summary line shows the counts as text and each segment has a native tooltip with its label and state name. Touch and keyboard users read the summary.
- The success, warning and destructive fills and the muted track are semantic tokens, checked in every theme. No animation.
- Direction-neutral: the row follows the document direction, so right-to-left shows the oldest segment on the right.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<UptimeBar label="Sample service, last 6 checks" :segments="[{ state: 'up' }, { state: 'up' }, { state: 'degraded' }, { state: 'up' }, { state: 'down' }, { state: 'up' }]" />
```

Example: Status page row (28 days)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const days = Array.from({ length: 28 }, (_, i) => ({ state: i === 9 ? 'down' : i === 17 || i === 18 ? 'degraded' : 'up', label: 'Day ' + (i + 1) }))
</script>

<div class="flex max-w-xl flex-col gap-2">
  <div class="flex items-baseline justify-between text-sm"><span class="font-medium">Sample API</span><span class="text-muted-foreground">Sample data</span></div>
  <UptimeBar label="Sample API, last 28 days" :segments="days" />
</div>
```

Example: Sizes, 200 segments and translated states
```vue
<div class="flex max-w-xl flex-col gap-4">
  <UptimeBar size="sm" label="Sample data: 200 checks" :segments="Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => ({ state: i % 50 === 7 ? 'down' : 'up' }))" />
  <UptimeBar size="lg" label="Beispieldaten" :state-labels="{ up: 'in Betrieb', degraded: 'eingeschränkt', down: 'ausgefallen', unknown: 'unbekannt' }" :segments="[{ state: 'up' }, { state: 'degraded' }, { state: 'down' }, { state: 'unknown' }]" empty-text="Noch keine Prüfungen" />
</div>
```

Example: Empty
```vue
<UptimeBar label="Sample service" :segments="[]" />
```
