# DataGrid
group: data-display / Tables
Spreadsheet-like data grid: keyboard navigation over cells, inline editing with validation, sorting, resizable and pinned columns, row selection, copy as TSV and a windowed render for 10,000 rows.

Use `DataGrid` when people work in the cells: move with the arrow keys, press Enter or F2 to edit, copy a block into a spreadsheet. Use `DataTable` for read-only tables with paging and `Table` for static markup. The grid follows the ARIA grid pattern: `role="grid"` with one tab stop (roving tabindex), so Tab enters and leaves it. Give `columns` (`{ key, label, type, editable, width, pinned, sortable, align }`) and `rows`; bind `v-model:rows` to receive edits (the grid never mutates the array it was given, it emits a new array with a new row object). `v-model:sort` and `v-model:selected` work controlled or uncontrolled.

Rows have a fixed height (set by `density`), cell text is truncated with an ellipsis, and above 200 rows (or with `virtual`) only the visible window is mounted, so 10,000 rows cost about 30 rows of DOM. The row with the focus stays mounted when it scrolls out of view. Cell values are always rendered as text, never as HTML.

Known limits: no merged cells, no column reorder or grouping, no row grouping or tree rows, no fill handle, no undo or redo, no paste, no type-to-edit (press Enter or F2 first), no mouse drag selection of cells (use Shift+Arrow or Shift+click), no horizontal virtualization (every column is rendered), no variable row height, no server paging (use the `rows` you have). After you edit a sorted column the row keeps its place until the next sort. Column widths are in pixels and the grid does not stretch to fill a wider container. Change the data by replacing `rows` with a new array; mutating a row in place is not detected. Text direction is read when the grid mounts and when `dir` changes.

import { DataGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- columns*: DataGridColumn<T>[] - `{ key, label, type?, editable?, width?, minWidth?, maxWidth?, pinned?, sortable?, resizable?, align?, options?, formatter? }`. `type` is `text` (default), `number` or `select` and picks the editor. `pinned` is `start` or `end`: pinned columns stick to that edge while the grid scrolls sideways and are moved to the edges in the order given. `width` is in px (default 160, resize limits 48 to 1000). `align` is `start`, `center` or `end` (numbers default to `end`). `options` are values or `{ value, label }` for a `select` column. `formatter(value, row)` returns the text shown and copied.
- rows*: T[] - v-model:rows. Plain objects. An edit emits a new array holding a new object for the edited row; the input is never mutated. Replace the array to change the data.
- rowKey: keyof T | ((row: T, index: number) => string | number) = 'id' - Row property or function giving a unique id, used for selection. A row without a string or number id falls back to its index; with `selectable` a missing or repeated id throws a ContractError.
- label: string - Accessible name of the grid. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- sort: { key: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" } | null = null - v-model:sort. Header click, Enter or Space cycles ascending, descending, none. Stable; numbers compare as numbers, text naturally; empty values go last in both directions.
- selectable: boolean = false - Adds a pinned checkbox column, `aria-selected` on rows and Space (Shift+Space for a range) on any cell to toggle the row.
- selected: (string | number)[] = [] - v-model:selected: ids of the selected rows. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- validate: (value: unknown, context: DataGridValidateContext<T>) => string | null | undefined | void - Called before an edit is applied with the parsed value (a number for `number`, the option value for `select`). Return error text to reject it: the editor stays open with `aria-invalid`, the text is shown next to the cell, linked with `aria-describedby`, and announced. Escape cancels.
- height: number | string - Height of the scroll area: px number or any CSS length. Virtual grids default to 480px; other grids grow with their rows unless you set it (the header and pinned columns stay in view only inside a bounded height).
- virtual: boolean | 'auto' = 'auto' - `auto` windows the rows above 200; `true` always, `false` never.
- overscan: number = 6 - Rows mounted above and below the visible window.
- density: 'compact' | 'default' | 'comfortable' = 'default' - Row height (28px, 36px, 48px) and cell padding. Touch devices get at least 44px rows. Unknown values fall back to default.
- variant: 'bordered' | 'striped' | 'borderless' = 'bordered' - `bordered` frames the grid and rules the columns; `striped` frames it and tints every second row; `borderless` drops the frame and column rules. Unknown values fall back to bordered.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size: 12px, 14px, 16px. Editors are 16px below the `md` breakpoint so phones do not zoom.
- loading: boolean = false - Shows placeholder rows, sets `aria-busy` and announces the change once.
- emptyText: string = 'No rows' - Message when there are no rows (use the `empty` slot for rich content).
- nullText: string = '' - Shown for null and undefined cells (copied as empty).
- dir: 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'auto' = 'auto' - Text direction. `auto` reads the nearest `dir` attribute or the computed direction when the grid mounts. Arrow keys, sticky edges, resize and alignment follow it.
- neutralizeFormulas: boolean = true - In copied text, prefix text cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or carriage return with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet shows them as text instead of running them. Numbers are left alone. Turn off only when the clipboard must hold the exact text.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root (`data-slot="data-grid"`). `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` go to the grid element; every other attribute goes to the root.

Slots:
- cell-<key> ({ row: T, value: unknown, column: DataGridColumn<T>, rowIndex: number }) - Custom (display) content for the cells of that column; `rowIndex` is the index in the source `rows`. The editor still opens on Enter. Keep the content short: rows have a fixed height.
- header-<key> ({ column: DataGridColumn<T> }) - Custom header label for that column. The visible text must still contain the column label.
- empty - Replaces the empty-state message.

Events:
- update:rows [rows: T[]] - A new array after a committed edit.
- update:sort [sort: SortState | null] - Sort changed from a header.
- update:selected [ids: (string | number)[]] - Row selection changed.
- cell-edit [edit: { row, rowKey, rowIndex, column, value, previousValue }] - A value was committed and changed. `rowIndex` is the index in the source rows.
- column-resize [resize: { key: string; width: number }] - A drag ended, or one keyboard step was applied.
- copy [copy: { text: string; cells: number }] - Cells were copied with Ctrl or Cmd+C (the text is the TSV that was written).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the grid has no accessible name (`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Throws a ContractError when `columns` is empty, when a column has no non-empty `key`, when two columns share a `key`, or when a column has no `label`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `select` column has no `options`.
- Throws a ContractError when `selectable` is set and a row has no string or number id, or two rows have the same id (they would be selected together).

Rules:
- Always set `label` and give every column a unique `key` and a `label`.
- Bind `v-model:rows`; the grid never mutates the rows you pass, it emits a new array. React to `cell-edit` for saving, and use `validate` (return error text) instead of validating in the event.
- Mark columns `editable: true` to edit them (default is read-only); use `type: "number"` or `type: "select"` with `options` for typed editors.
- For many rows set a `height` and leave `virtual` on auto; rows have a fixed height and text is truncated, so do not put tall content in cells.
- With `selectable`, every row needs a unique string or number `id` (or pass `rowKey`).
- Cell values render as text; format with `formatter` or a `cell-<key>` slot, never with HTML strings.
- Do not use it for read-only report tables: use `DataTable` (paging, cards on phones) or `Table`.

Accessibility:
- ARIA grid pattern: `role="grid"` with rowgroups, rows, `columnheader` and `gridcell`, `aria-rowcount` and `aria-colcount` for the whole data set and `aria-rowindex` on every mounted row, so a windowed grid still reports the true position (the header is row 1).
- One tab stop (roving tabindex): Tab enters the grid on its current cell and the next Tab leaves it. Arrow keys move one cell (they swap in right-to-left), Home and End go to the first and last column, Ctrl or Cmd+Home and +End to the first and last cell, PageUp and PageDown move by the visible rows. The header is row 0 of the navigation.
- Editing: Enter or F2 (or double click) opens the editor, Enter saves and returns focus to the cell, Escape cancels, Tab saves and continues to the next tab stop. Enter and Escape are ignored while an IME composition is open. A rejected value keeps the editor open with `aria-invalid="true"`, the error text visible next to the cell and referenced by `aria-describedby`, and announced in the status region.
- Sorting: the sorted header carries `aria-sort`; Enter or Space on a header cell, or a click on its button, cycles the direction. The change is announced ("Sorted by Name, ascending").
- Resizing: each header has a visible 24px `role="separator"` handle with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. Drag it, or Tab from the header cell onto it: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft change the width by 10px (Shift: 50px, reversed in right-to-left), Home and End jump to the limits, Escape returns to the header cell. The handle is a tab stop only while its header cell is the current cell.
- Selection: rows carry `aria-selected`, the header checkbox is named "Select all rows" and is indeterminate for a partial selection, each row checkbox is "Select row n". Space toggles the row from any cell, Shift+Space or Shift+click selects a range. Cells in a Shift+Arrow block carry `aria-selected="true"`.
- One polite `role="status"` region announces sorting, edits, validation errors, resizing, loading and copying. It is never used for every keystroke or scroll.
- Focus is a visible 2px outline inside the cell (kept in forced-colors mode). Rows are at least 28px (44px on touch devices) and the resize handle is 24px wide. State is never colour only: errors have an icon and text, sorting has an arrow icon plus `aria-sort`, selection has a checkbox.
- Cell values are text only. Hostile or very long text is truncated inside its fixed-height cell; the full value is in the editor and the copied text.

Example: Editable cells with validation
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [
  { key: 'item', label: 'Item', editable: true, sortable: true, width: 200 },
  { key: 'qty', label: 'Quantity', type: 'number', editable: true, sortable: true, width: 120 },
  { key: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'select', editable: true, sortable: true, width: 140,
    options: [{ value: 'open', label: 'Open' }, { value: 'packed', label: 'Packed' }, { value: 'sent', label: 'Sent' }] },
  { key: 'note', label: 'Note', width: 200 },
]
const rows = ref([
  { id: 1, item: 'Sample crate A', qty: 12, status: 'open', note: 'Sample note' },
  { id: 2, item: 'Sample crate B', qty: 40, status: 'packed', note: '' },
  { id: 3, item: 'Sample crate C', qty: 3, status: 'sent', note: 'Fragile sample' },
  { id: 4, item: 'Sample crate D', qty: 18, status: 'open', note: '' },
])
const lastEdit = ref('No edits yet')
function validate(value, { column }) {
  if (column.key === 'qty' && value !== null && value >= 100) return 'Quantity must be under 100'
}
function onEdit(edit) { lastEdit.value = edit.column.label + ' of row ' + edit.rowKey + ' is now ' + edit.value }
</script>

<div class="space-y-3">
  <DataGrid v-model:rows="rows" :columns="columns" label="Sample crates, editable" :validate="validate" @cell-edit="onEdit" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground" role="status">{{ lastEdit }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Sorting and resizing columns
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [
  { key: 'item', label: 'Item', editable: true, sortable: true, width: 200 },
  { key: 'qty', label: 'Quantity', type: 'number', editable: true, sortable: true, width: 120 },
  { key: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'select', editable: true, sortable: true, width: 140,
    options: [{ value: 'open', label: 'Open' }, { value: 'packed', label: 'Packed' }, { value: 'sent', label: 'Sent' }] },
  { key: 'note', label: 'Note', width: 200 },
]
const rows = ref([
  { id: 1, item: 'Sample crate A', qty: 12, status: 'open', note: 'Sample note' },
  { id: 2, item: 'Sample crate B', qty: 40, status: 'packed', note: '' },
  { id: 3, item: 'Sample crate C', qty: 3, status: 'sent', note: 'Fragile sample' },
  { id: 4, item: 'Sample crate D', qty: 18, status: 'open', note: '' },
])
const sort = ref({ key: 'qty', direction: 'desc' })
</script>

<div class="space-y-3">
  <DataGrid v-model:rows="rows" v-model:sort="sort" :columns="columns" label="Sample crates, sortable" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Sorted by {{ sort ? sort.key + ' (' + sort.direction + ')' : 'nothing' }}</p>
</div>
```

Example: Pinned columns in a wide grid
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [
  { key: 'item', label: 'Item', width: 180, pinned: 'start' },
  { key: 'site', label: 'Site', width: 160 },
  { key: 'owner', label: 'Owner', width: 160 },
  { key: 'qty', label: 'Quantity', type: 'number', width: 140 },
  { key: 'status', label: 'Status', width: 140 },

  { id: 2, item: 'Sample crate B', site: 'Site 2', owner: 'Owner B', qty: 40, status: 'Packed', note: 'Another sample note', total: 400 },
  { id: 3, item: 'Sample crate C', site: 'Site 3', owner: 'Owner C', qty: 3, status: 'Sent', note: 'Fragile sample', total: 30 },
]
</script>

<DataGrid :rows="rows" :columns="columns" label="Sample crates, wide" class="max-w-full" :height="260" />
```

Example: 10,000 rows, windowed
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [
  { key: 'id', label: 'Number', type: 'number', width: 110, sortable: true, pinned: 'start' },
  { key: 'item', label: 'Item', width: 220, sortable: true },
  { key: 'qty', label: 'Quantity', type: 'number', width: 120, sortable: true, editable: true },
  { key: 'site', label: 'Site', width: 180, sortable: true },
]
const rows = ref(Array.from({ length: 10000 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: i + 1, item: 'Sample item ' + (i + 1), qty: (i * 7) % 100, site: 'Site ' + ((i % 12) + 1),
})))
</script>

<DataGrid v-model:rows="rows" :columns="columns" label="Sample items, 10,000 rows" :height="320" density="compact" />
```

---

# DataTable
group: data-display / Tables
Data-array table with client-side sorting, row selection, pagination, loading and empty states.

Give `columns` and `rows`; the table renders them with `Table` parts. Sorting cycles none → asc → desc → none (stable; null/NaN/Invalid Date always last), selection is per page (header checkbox selects the visible page and keeps other pages), pagination is a built-in simple pager. `v-model:sort`, `v-model:selected` and `v-model:page` work controlled or uncontrolled. All work is client-side: for server-side paging/sorting use `Table` parts or pass pre-sorted rows without `sortable`. Without `selectable`, duplicate or missing row keys are tolerated (rendering uses a unique internal key). With `selectable`, selection stores the id from `rowKey`, so every row needs a unique string or number id: a missing or repeated one throws a ContractError, because those rows would be selected together. Name the table with `caption` or `label`. Look props (all combinable): `density`, `size`, `variant`, `striped`, `bordered`, `stickyHeader`; `layout="cards"` turns rows into cards on narrow screens. The header row is hidden visually there, so below 640px a visible control bar appears above the cards: a "Sort by" select with a direction button for the sortable columns, and a "Select all" checkbox when `selectable` is set. It writes the same `v-model:sort` and `v-model:selected` values as the header (one source of truth). Relabel it with `sortByLabel`, `sortDirectionLabel`, `sortDefaultLabel`, `sortAscendingLabel`, `sortDescendingLabel` and `selectAllLabel`, or hide it with `:card-controls="false"`.

import { DataTable, SortHeaderButton, TableCardControls } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- columns*: DataTableColumn<T>[] - `{ key, header, sortable?, align?, numeric?, rowHeader?, actions?, width?, accessor?, class? }`. `accessor(row)` defaults to `row[key]`; `width` is an inline CSS width; `numeric` right-aligns with tabular figures; `rowHeader` renders the column as `<th scope="row">` and names the row checkbox; `actions` marks a row-actions column, which in `layout="cards"` has no "Actions:" label and closes the card at the end with a rule.
- rows*: T[] - Source rows (never mutated).
- rowKey: keyof T | ((row: T, index: number) => string | number) = 'id' - Row property name or function giving a unique string or number id, used for selection. Required to resolve for every row when `selectable` is set; otherwise missing ids fall back to the row index.
- sort: { key: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" } | null = null - v-model:sort. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- selectable: boolean = false - Adds a leading checkbox column.
- selected: (string | number)[] = [] - v-model:selected: selected row ids. Controlled or uncontrolled.
- page: number = 1 - v-model:page (1-based). Out-of-range values are clamped and `update:page` is emitted with the clamped value.
- pageSize: number - Rows per page. Undefined, 0, negative, NaN or Infinity disable pagination; fractions are floored.
- loading: boolean = false - Shows skeleton rows, sets aria-busy and hides data rows and the pager.
- loadingRows: number - Number of skeleton rows. Defaults to the page size, else 5.
- emptyText: string = 'No results' - Message when there are no rows (use the `empty` slot for rich content).
- locale: string - BCP 47 locale for Date cells. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `en`, never the browser locale, so server and client agree.
- timeZone: string - IANA time zone for Date cells. Falls back to `ConfigProvider`, then `UTC`.
- nullText: string = '–' - Shown for null/undefined (and Invalid Date, function and unserialisable) cells. Plain objects and arrays render as JSON truncated to 80 characters; use the `cell` slot for anything richer.
- rowClickable: boolean = false - Rows get tabindex=0, a pointer cursor and emit `row-click` on click / Enter / Space. Clicks from links, buttons, inputs, selects, textareas, labels and `[data-no-row-click]` are ignored.
- density: 'default' | 'compact' | 'comfortable' = 'default' - Cell padding scale: `compact` (8px cells), `default` (12px) or `comfortable` (16px). Unknown values fall back to default.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size of headers and cells: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px. Independent of `density`.
- variant: 'default' | 'borderless' | 'filled' = 'default' - `default` has a rule under every row; `borderless` drops the body row rules; `filled` gives the header a muted band. Combines with `striped` and `bordered`. Unknown values fall back to default.
- striped: boolean = false - Tint every second body row. Hover and selected styling still win.
- bordered: boolean = false - Outer frame plus column rules.
- layout: 'table' | 'cards' = 'table' - `cards`: below the `sm` breakpoint (640px) each row becomes a stacked card of label and value pairs (the labels are the column headers) and the header row is hidden visually. Sorting, selection, paging, loading and empty states keep working.
- stickyHeader: boolean = false - Pin the header; set a height on `containerClass` (e.g. `max-h-96`).
- cardControls: boolean = true - With `layout="cards"`, show the sort select, direction button and "Select all" checkbox below 640px (where the header row is hidden). It appears only when a column is `sortable` or `selectable` is set. Set `false` to hide it and offer your own.
- cardSortControl: 'select' | 'combobox' = 'select' - Cards-layout sort control. `combobox` swaps the native select for a filterable Combobox (type to narrow the sortable columns, clear to restore the default order). Same label, direction button and `v-model:sort` value. Unknown values use the select.
- sortByLabel: string = 'Sort by' - Visible label of the cards-layout sort select.
- sortDirectionLabel: string = 'Sort direction' - Start of the accessible name of the direction button ("Sort direction: Ascending"); its visible text is the current direction.
- sortDefaultLabel: string = 'Default order' - Select option that clears the sort.
- sortAscendingLabel: string = 'Ascending' - Text for the ascending direction.
- sortDescendingLabel: string = 'Descending' - Text for the descending direction.
- selectAllLabel: string = 'Select all' - Visible label of the cards-layout "Select all" checkbox.
- containerClass: string | object | array - Classes for the scroll container.
- tableClass: string | object | array - Classes for the inner <table>.
- caption: string - Visually hidden <caption> for assistive tech. Set `caption` or `label`: one of them is required.
- label: string - aria-label for the <table>; also names the scroll region. Set `caption` or `label`: one of them is required.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root wrapper (`data-slot="data-table"`). Other attributes also fall through to it.

Parts:
- SortHeaderButton - Button for a sortable <th>: label slot + decorative sort icon. Reusable in custom tables built from Table parts.
    - direction: 'asc' | 'desc' | null = null - Current direction; changes the icon.
    - align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' = 'left' - Aligns label + icon in the header cell.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.
- TableCardControls - The control bar `DataTable` shows above a `layout="cards"` table below 640px (`sm:hidden`): a labelled native select of the sortable columns, a direction button and a "Select all" checkbox, with 44px targets on coarse pointers. Reusable with a hand-written `Table` that uses `layout="cards"`: bind `v-model:sort`, pass the sortable columns as `options`, and handle `select-all` yourself.
    - options: { key: string; label: string }[] = [] - Sortable columns in header order. With none, the sort select and button are not rendered.
    - sort: { key: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" } | null = null - v-model:sort, the same value as `DataTable`.
    - selectable: boolean = false - Show the "Select all" checkbox.
    - allSelected: boolean = false - Checks the box (every row of the page is selected).
    - someSelected: boolean = false - Indeterminate box (some, not all, rows are selected).
    - selectDisabled: boolean = false - Disables the checkbox (no rows).
    - sortControl: 'select' | 'combobox' = 'select' - `combobox` renders a filterable Combobox (clearable, placeholder = `sortDefaultLabel`) instead of the native select. Unknown values use the select.
    - sortByLabel: string = 'Sort by' - Visible label of the select.
    - sortDirectionLabel: string = 'Sort direction' - Accessible name prefix of the direction button.
    - sortDefaultLabel: string = 'Default order' - Option that clears the sort.
    - sortAscendingLabel: string = 'Ascending' - Ascending text.
    - sortDescendingLabel: string = 'Descending' - Descending text.
    - selectAllLabel: string = 'Select all' - Visible label of the checkbox.
    - announce: boolean = true - Render a polite live region that says "Sort by Name, Ascending". `DataTable` turns it off because it has its own.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last on the bar.

Slots:
- cell-<key> ({ row: T, value: unknown, column: DataTableColumn<T>, index: number }) - Custom cell content for the column with that key. `index` is the position in the source `rows`.
- cell ({ row, value, column, index }) - Fallback custom cell content for every column without a `cell-<key>` slot.
- header-<key> ({ column: DataTableColumn<T> }) - Custom header label (rendered inside the sort button for sortable columns).
- empty - Replaces the empty-state message.
- footer - Content of <tfoot>; provide your own <tr><td colspan>…</td></tr>.

Events:
- update:sort [value: SortState | null] - Sort changed by a header click or by the cards-layout sort select or direction button.
- update:selected [value: (string | number)[]] - Selection changed (row checkbox, header checkbox or the cards-layout "Select all").
- update:page [value: number] - Page changed by the pager or clamped into range.
- row-click [row: T, event: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent] - A clickable row was activated.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when neither `caption` nor `label` names the table.
- Throws a ContractError when `columns` is empty, when a column has no non-empty `key`, when two columns share a `key`, or when a column has neither a `header` text nor a `header-<key>` slot.
- Throws a ContractError when `rowKey` is neither a property name nor a function.
- Throws a ContractError when `selectable` is set and a row has no string or number id, or two rows have the same id (they would be selected together). Without `selectable`, duplicate or missing ids are tolerated.

Rules:
- Give `columns` stable unique `key`s and rows a unique `id` (or pass rowKey) when using selectable.
- Use v-model:sort / v-model:selected / v-model:page; do not mutate props.
- Use `cell-<key>` slots for badges/actions; put buttons inside cells (clicks on them do not trigger row-click).
- Always set `caption` or `label`.
- Look props: `density` padding, `size` text, `variant` rules and header band, `striped`, `bordered`; `layout="cards"` for phones: below 640px it shows its own "Sort by" select, direction button and "Select all" checkbox (same `v-model:sort` / `v-model:selected` state as the header; relabel with `sortByLabel`, `sortDirectionLabel`, `sortDefaultLabel`, `sortAscendingLabel`, `sortDescendingLabel`, `selectAllLabel`; hide with `:card-controls="false"`).
- Sorting and paging are client-side only; for server data, handle sorting yourself and omit `sortable`.

Accessibility:
- Native table semantics; sortable headers are buttons inside <th scope="col">. Only the sorted column carries `aria-sort` (ascending or descending); unsorted columns have no `aria-sort`. Focus stays on the header button after a sort, and a visually hidden `role="status"` announces "Sorted by Name, ascending".
- Mark the identifying column `rowHeader: true` so its cells are `<th scope="row">`.
- Loading sets aria-busy on the table.
- Selection checkboxes are labelled "Select all rows" (header, indeterminate when partially selected) and "Select <row header text>" (or "Select row n" without a row header column). They are 20px targets with 12px cell padding around them.
- The scroll container is a focusable `role="region"` named by `label` or `caption`, so a wide table scrolls with the arrow keys; `stickyHeader` pins the header inside a height-bounded container.
- The pager is a <nav aria-label="Pagination">; Previous/Next are disabled at the ends and the "Page n of m" text is a polite live region with tabular figures.
- Clickable rows are focusable (tabindex=0) and activate on Enter/Space.
- `layout="cards"` keeps the table markup: below `sm` the elements get explicit `table`, `rowgroup`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader` and `cell` roles so `display` changes do not drop table semantics, and the visual column labels are `aria-hidden` (the column header names each cell). The header row is hidden visually below `sm`; its sort buttons and select-all checkbox stay in the accessibility tree and appear when a keyboard user focuses them.
- Cards layout control bar (`data-slot="table-card-controls"`, visible only below `sm`, so touch users can sort and select all without the header row): the sort select is a native `<select>` wrapped in a visible "Sort by" `<label>` (16px text, 44px high on coarse pointers); the direction button shows the current direction as text plus an arrow icon (never colour alone), is named "Sort direction: Ascending", and is disabled while no column is sorted; "Select all" is a native checkbox inside its label (a 44px target on coarse pointers) with the same indeterminate state as the header box. Everything is keyboard operable (Tab, arrow keys on the select, Space on the checkbox, Enter or Space on the button). The bar writes the same `sort` and `selected` values as the header, so `aria-sort` on the sorted `<th>` and the polite "Sorted by Name, ascending" announcement are identical whichever control sorted. Without sortable columns and without `selectable` the bar is not rendered; `:card-controls="false"` removes it.
- Numeric and right-aligned columns use `tabular-nums`. Pass `caption` or `label` so the table has an accessible name.

Example: Basic sortable
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, rowHeader: true },
  { key: 'plan', header: 'Plan', sortable: true },
  { key: 'seats', header: 'Seats', sortable: true, numeric: true },
]
const rows = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Item A', plan: 'Plan 1', seats: 12 },
  { id: 2, name: 'Item B', plan: 'Plan 2', seats: 40 },
  { id: 3, name: 'Item C', plan: 'Plan 3', seats: 3 },
  { id: 4, name: 'Item D', plan: 'Plan 1', seats: null },
]
</script>

<DataTable :columns="columns" :rows="rows" caption="Sample data: items and plans" />
```

---

# Table
group: data-display / Tables
Styled, responsive native <table> with compound parts for hand-written tabular markup.

Use `Table` + parts when you write the rows yourself (static data, custom layouts, footers with totals). The wrapper scrolls horizontally on small screens. For data arrays with sorting, selection or pagination use `DataTable`. Do not use tables for layout. Variations (all props on `Table`, combinable): `density` (`compact`, `default`, `comfortable`) for padding; `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) for the type scale; `variant` (`default`, `borderless`, `filled`) for the row rules and header band; `layout="cards"` to turn rows into stacked cards on narrow screens (the header row is hidden there; place `TableCardControls` above the table to give touch users a visible "Sort by" select, direction button and "Select all" checkbox that drive your own sort and selection state; `DataTable` does this for you); `stickyHeader` for long scrolling tables; `striped` zebra rows to track long rows across wide tables; `bordered` outer frame + column rules for spreadsheet-like data; `:hoverable="false"` for read-only/report tables where rows are not interactive; `selectedTone="accent"` for a stronger selected-row look (primary tint + leading bar) next to `TableRow selected`. `density`, `size`, `variant`, `layout` and `stickyHeader` reach cells through `group/table` data attributes and provide/inject; `striped`, `hoverable` and `selectedTone` reach `TableRow` the same way, so rows and cells must be inside a `Table`. On cells, `valign` sets the vertical alignment and `label` names the cell in the cards layout.

import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableCaption, TableEmpty } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- density: 'default' | 'compact' | 'comfortable' = 'default' - Cell padding scale: `compact` (8px cells, 32px header), `default` (12px, 40px) or `comfortable` (16px, 48px). Unknown values fall back to default.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size of header and body cells: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px, `lg` 16px. Independent of `density`. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- variant: 'default' | 'borderless' | 'filled' = 'default' - `default` has a rule under every row; `borderless` drops the body row rules (the header keeps its rule; forced-colors mode still draws them); `filled` gives the header row a muted band. Combines with `striped` and `bordered`. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- layout: 'table' | 'cards' = 'table' - `cards`: below the `sm` breakpoint (640px) each body row becomes a bordered card of label and value pairs and the header row is hidden visually. Add `label` to every `TableCell`. Unknown values fall back to `table`.
- stickyHeader: boolean = false - Pin header cells to the top of the scroll container. The container needs a bounded height, e.g. `containerClass="max-h-96"`.
- striped: boolean = false - Tint every second body row (zebra). Header/footer rows are not striped; hover and selected styling still win.
- bordered: boolean = false - Rounded outer border on the scroll container plus vertical rules between columns.
- hoverable: boolean = true - Tint rows on hover. `false` removes the hover tint (selected styling is kept).
- selectedTone: 'muted' | 'accent' = 'muted' - Emphasis for selected rows: neutral `muted` background or `accent` (primary tint). Unknown values fall back to `muted`.
- label: string - Accessible name of the scroll region (`role="region"`, focusable). Defaults to the table `aria-label`, else the `TableCaption` text. The table needs one of these names (`label`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a `TableCaption`).
- containerClass: string | object | array - Classes for the scroll wrapper div (`data-slot="table-container"`).
- class: string | object | array - Applied to the inner <table>, merged last. Other attributes (id, aria-*, data-*) also go to the <table>.

Parts:
- TableHeader - <thead>.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableBody - <tbody>; last row has no bottom border.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableFooter - <tfoot> with muted background.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableRow - <tr> with hover, stripe (from `Table striped`) and selected styling.
    - selected: boolean = false - Sets data-state="selected" and the selected background. Does not add aria-selected: pass it yourself for grid/treegrid tables.
    - selectedTone: 'muted' | 'accent' - Selected emphasis for this row; defaults to the Table `selectedTone`.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableHead - <th>. Defaults to scope="col"; pass aria-sort for sortable headers.
    - align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' = 'left' - Text alignment (logical: `left` is the start edge, `right` the end edge, so RTL mirrors).
    - scope: 'col' | 'row' | 'colgroup' | 'rowgroup' = 'col' - Header scope.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableCell - <td>.
    - align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' = 'left' - Text alignment.
    - numeric: boolean = false - Right-aligns (unless align is set) and uses tabular numerals.
    - valign: 'top' | 'middle' | 'bottom' = 'middle' - Vertical alignment inside the row. Use `top` when neighbouring cells wrap onto several lines.
    - label: string - Column name shown before the value when the Table uses `layout="cards"` below `sm`. Visual only (`aria-hidden`): the column header already names the cell for assistive tech. Ignored in the default layout.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableCaption - <caption>.
    - hidden: boolean = false - Visually hide but keep for assistive tech (sr-only).
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.
- TableEmpty - A <tr> with one <td> spanning the table; centred muted message. Default text "No results".
    - colspan: number = 1 - Columns to span. Invalid values fall back to 1.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the table has no accessible name: add a `TableCaption`, or set `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `TableHead` is not inside a `TableRow`, or when a `scope="col"` (or `colgroup`) `TableHead` is not inside `TableHeader`. Row headers use `scope="row"` and may sit in `TableBody`.
- Throws a ContractError when a `TableRow` is rendered outside a `Table`.

Rules:
- Use Table parts for static markup; use DataTable for arrays of rows.
- Always render TableHead cells inside TableHeader > TableRow.
- Use `numeric` on TableCell for numbers so columns align.
- Use `density` for padding, `size` for text, `variant` for rules and header band; do not set `class` to change them. Use `layout="cards"` with a `label` on every TableCell when the table must work on phones, and add `TableCardControls` above it when phones need sorting or select-all.
- Choose Table props by need: `striped` for wide tables, `bordered` for spreadsheet-like data, `density="compact"` for dense views, `:hoverable="false"` for read-only tables.
- Use `selected` on TableRow for selected rows and `selectedTone="accent"` on Table for a stronger look; add aria-selected yourself only for grid tables.
- TableRow striping, hover and selection tone only apply inside a Table (provide/inject).
- Sticky header requires a bounded container height (containerClass="max-h-96").
- Do not use tables for layout.

Accessibility:
- Native table semantics (caption, thead/tbody/tfoot, th scope). Use `<TableHead scope="row">` for the cell that names a row.
- The scroll container is `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can scroll a wide table with the arrow keys, and is a `role="region"` named by `label`, the table `aria-label` or the caption when one exists. It shows the shared focus ring.
- Stripes, borders and selection tint are visual only: selection must also be exposed non-visually (a checkbox or aria-selected on grid rows).
- Give every table a caption (use `hidden` for sr-only) or an aria-label.
- Put aria-sort on the sortable TableHead that is currently sorted; do not set `aria-sort="none"` on the others.
- Numeric cells use `tabular-nums` and align to the end edge. `left` and `right` alignment are logical, so RTL mirrors them.
- `layout="cards"` keeps real table markup: below `sm` the table, row groups, rows and cells get explicit `table`, `rowgroup`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader` and `cell` roles so screen readers still announce a table after `display` changes. The cell `label` is `aria-hidden` (the column header already names the cell). The header row is hidden visually below `sm` (it stays in the accessibility tree and appears when a keyboard user tabs into it), so touch users cannot reach sort buttons or a select-all checkbox in it: render `TableCardControls` (visible only below `sm`) above the table, bind its `v-model:sort`, and apply the same state to your rows and your `aria-sort`, so the bar and the header stay one source of truth. It is a labelled native select, a direction button with text and an icon, and a "Select all" checkbox, with 44px targets on coarse pointers.
- `variant="borderless"` keeps row rules in forced-colors mode (they are transparent borders); `filled` is a header band, not a state.
- Responsive: the table keeps its natural width and scrolls inside its region instead of widening the page; `stickyHeader` keeps the header visible inside a height-bounded container.

Example: Basic
```vue
<Table>
  <TableCaption>Sample data: members and seats</TableCaption>
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
      <TableHead>Role</TableHead>
      <TableHead align="right">Seats</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead scope="row" class="h-auto p-3 font-medium text-foreground">Member A</TableHead>
      <TableCell><Badge variant="secondary">Admin</Badge></TableCell>
      <TableCell numeric>12</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
    <TableRow selected>
      <TableHead scope="row" class="h-auto p-3 font-medium text-foreground">Member B</TableHead>
      <TableCell>Member</TableCell>
      <TableCell numeric>3</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableBody>
  <TableFooter>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell colspan="2">Total</TableCell>
      <TableCell numeric>15</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableFooter>
</Table>
```

Example: Row selection
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const picked = ref(['b'])
const rows = [{ id: 'a', name: 'Item A' }, { id: 'b', name: 'Item B' }, { id: 'c', name: 'Item C' }]
function toggle(id) {
  picked.value = picked.value.includes(id) ? picked.value.filter((x) => x !== id) : [...picked.value, id]
}
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <Table selected-tone="accent" aria-label="Sample data: selectable items">
    <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Name</TableHead><TableHead align="right">Selected</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow v-for="r in rows" :key="r.id" :selected="picked.includes(r.id)">
        <TableCell>{{ r.name }}</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="right"><input type="checkbox" class="relative inline-grid size-5 shrink-0 cursor-pointer appearance-none place-content-center rounded border border-input bg-background align-middle checked:border-primary checked:bg-primary indeterminate:border-primary indeterminate:bg-primary disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 after:hidden after:content-[''] after:h-2.5 after:w-1.5 after:rotate-45 after:border-b-2 after:border-e-2 after:border-primary-foreground checked:after:block indeterminate:after:block indeterminate:after:h-0 indeterminate:after:w-2.5 indeterminate:after:rotate-0 indeterminate:after:border-e-0 outline-hidden focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/40" :aria-label="'Select ' + r.name" :checked="picked.includes(r.id)" @change="toggle(r.id)" /></TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">{{ picked.length }} selected</p>
</div>
```

Example: Cards layout with sort and select-all controls
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const sort = ref(null)
const picked = ref([])
const data = [{ id: 'a', name: 'Item A', seats: 12 }, { id: 'b', name: 'Item B', seats: 40 }, { id: 'c', name: 'Item C', seats: 3 }]
const options = [{ key: 'name', label: 'Item' }, { key: 'seats', label: 'Seats' }]
const rows = computed(() => {
  const s = sort.value
  if (!s) return data
  return data.toSorted((x, y) => (x[s.key] > y[s.key] ? 1 : -1) * (s.direction === 'asc' ? 1 : -1))
})
const ariaSort = (key) => (sort.value?.key === key ? (sort.value.direction === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending') : undefined)
function toggleAll() {
  picked.value = picked.value.length === data.length ? [] : data.map((r) => r.id)
}
function toggle(id) {
  picked.value = picked.value.includes(id) ? picked.value.filter((x) => x !== id) : [...picked.value, id]
}
</script>

<div class="space-y-3">
  <TableCardControls v-model:sort="sort" :options="options" selectable :all-selected="picked.length === data.length" :some-selected="picked.length > 0 && picked.length < data.length" @select-all="toggleAll" />
  <Table layout="cards" aria-label="Sample data: cards layout with controls">
    <TableHeader>
      <TableRow>
        <TableHead>Select</TableHead>
        <TableHead :aria-sort="ariaSort('name')">Item</TableHead>
        <TableHead align="right" :aria-sort="ariaSort('seats')">Seats</TableHead>
      </TableRow>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow v-for="r in rows" :key="r.id" :selected="picked.includes(r.id)">
        <TableCell label="Select"><input type="checkbox" class="relative inline-grid size-5 shrink-0 cursor-pointer appearance-none place-content-center rounded border border-input bg-background align-middle checked:border-primary checked:bg-primary indeterminate:border-primary indeterminate:bg-primary disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 after:hidden after:content-[''] after:h-2.5 after:w-1.5 after:rotate-45 after:border-b-2 after:border-e-2 after:border-primary-foreground checked:after:block indeterminate:after:block indeterminate:after:h-0 indeterminate:after:w-2.5 indeterminate:after:rotate-0 indeterminate:after:border-e-0 outline-hidden focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/40" :aria-label="'Select ' + r.name" :checked="picked.includes(r.id)" @change="toggle(r.id)" /></TableCell>
        <TableCell label="Item">{{ r.name }}</TableCell>
        <TableCell label="Seats" numeric>{{ r.seats }}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>
</div>
```

# BlogCard
group: marketing / Blog
Article teaser card: cover image, category badge, title link, excerpt and author/date/read-time meta.

Use in blog indexes, "latest posts" strips and related-article lists. Renders a semantic `<article>`; the title is a link stretched over the whole card (the card is one tab stop and one click target), so do not nest other links in it. A valid ISO `date` renders `<time datetime>`; any other string is shown as plain text. `vertical` stacks image over text, `horizontal` places a fixed-width image beside the text from `sm`, `featured` is a large hero card (image 60% from `lg`, bigger title). For several cards use `BlogGrid`.

import { BlogCard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- title*: string - Post title; becomes the link text when `href` is set. Must not be empty.
- excerpt: string - Short summary (the default slot overrides it).
- href: string - Post URL. When set the title is a link stretched over the whole card; otherwise the title is plain text.
- image: string - Cover image URL. A missing or broken image leaves a neutral placeholder (or no image block when unset).
- imageAlt: string - Alt text of the cover. Required with `image`; an empty string marks it decorative (the title is adjacent text).
- category: string - Category shown as a Badge.
- author: string - Author name in the meta line.
- date: string - ISO 8601 date (`2024-03-01`, `2024-03-01T10:00:00Z`). Valid: `<time datetime>` with a formatted label. Invalid (`"Last Tuesday"`, `2024-02-31`): shown as plain text in a span, no `datetime`.
- readTime: string | number - A number means minutes (`5` -> "5 min read"; zero, negative and non-finite render nothing); a string is shown as given.
- variant: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' | 'featured' = 'vertical' - Layout; unknown values fall back to `vertical`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gaps, title and text scale. `sm` is compact (16px padding, `text-base` title), `md` is the original, `lg` is roomy (24px padding, `text-xl` title, 16px excerpt). The featured layout scales the same way. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners: `rounded` is the original 8px radius, `square` has none (the cover image is clipped to the same shape). Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- appearance: 'card' | 'plain' | 'filled' = 'card' - `card` is the original bordered surface. `plain` has no fill and a transparent border (the content sits straight on the page; the border appears in forced-colors mode). `filled` uses the secondary surface with secondary-foreground text and no visible border. Unknown values fall back to `card`.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading element level of the title; invalid values fall back to 3.
- locale: string = 'en-US' - BCP 47 locale used to format a valid `date` (always in UTC, so server and client agree). Unsupported locales fall back to `en-US`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- image - Replaces the cover `<img>` (e.g. a responsive `<picture>` or NuxtImg). The image block renders when this slot is used.
- default - Replaces the excerpt text.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `title` is missing or blank.
- Throws a ContractError when `image` is set without an `imageAlt` string (and no `image` slot). An empty string marks the cover decorative.

Rules:
- The cover image blur when a surrounding `ConfigProvider` sets `blurMedia` (privacy, not decoration); there is no prop on this component.
- Pass dates as ISO strings (`2024-03-01`) so `<time datetime>` is emitted.
- Do not nest interactive elements in the card: the title link is stretched over it.
- Use `vertical` in grids, `horizontal` for list-style indexes, `featured` once at the top of an index.
- Set `level` to fit the page outline (default 3 under an h2 section heading).
- Use `appearance="plain"` for dense indexes on a page background and `filled` for related-post strips on a card surface; keep `card` for general use. Keep one `size` per list.
- Use BlogGrid for several posts instead of hand-building a grid.

Accessibility:
- Root is an `<article>`; the title is a heading (`level`, default 3: set it to fit the page outline) containing the only link, stretched over the card with a pseudo-element so the whole card is one focus target (well above 24px, and the card is one tab stop).
- Keyboard: Tab focuses the title link, Enter follows it. The focus ring surrounds the whole card; in forced-colors mode an outline replaces the ring.
- The cover image is decorative by default (`imageAlt=""`); give it alt text only when it carries information.
- Valid dates use `<time datetime>`; the visible text is formatted for the `locale`. Separator dots in the meta line are aria-hidden.
- `size`, `shape` and `appearance` change padding, corners and surface only; the title link, heading level and focus handling are the same in every combination. `plain` and `filled` keep a transparent 1px border, so the focus ring (and the forced-colors outline) still surrounds the whole card, and the box does not shift between appearances. Text colours use token pairs checked for contrast: foreground on background (plain), card-foreground on card, secondary-foreground on secondary (filled).
- Layouts reflow to one column on a 320px screen (`horizontal` and `featured` only go side by side from `sm` / `lg`); long words wrap (`overflow-wrap:anywhere`). Nothing animates on hover.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<div class="max-w-sm"><BlogCard title="Sample post title" excerpt="One or two sentences that summarise the article." href="/guides/getting-started" /></div>
```

Example: Vertical variant
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const post = { title: 'Install the package and import the theme', excerpt: '...', href: '/guides/getting-started', image: '/cover.jpg', imageAlt: '', category: 'Guide', author: 'Author name', date: '2024-03-01', readTime: 6 }
</script>

<div class="max-w-sm"><BlogCard variant="vertical" v-bind="post" /></div>
```

Example: Horizontal variant
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const post = { ... }
</script>

<BlogCard variant="horizontal" v-bind="post" />
```

Example: Featured variant
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const post = { ... }
</script>

<BlogCard variant="featured" :level="2" v-bind="post" />
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid items-start gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <BlogCard v-for="s in ['sm', 'md', 'lg']" :key="s" :size="s" :title="'Size ' + s" excerpt="Sample teaser text for the size gallery." category="Sample" author="Author name" date="2024-03-01" :read-time="3" href="/guides/getting-started" />
</div>
```

Example: Shapes
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const cover = '/cover.svg'
</script>

<div class="grid gap-6 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <BlogCard v-for="s in ['rounded', 'square']" :key="s" :shape="s" :image="cover" image-alt="" :title="'Shape ' + s" excerpt="Sample teaser text for the shape gallery." href="/guides/getting-started" />
</div>
```

Example: Appearances
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3">
  <BlogCard v-for="a in ['card', 'plain', 'filled']" :key="a" :appearance="a" :title="'Appearance ' + a" excerpt="Sample teaser text for the appearance gallery." category="Sample" author="Author name" date="2024-03-01" :read-time="3" href="/guides/getting-started" />
</div>
```

Example: Combined: square, filled, large, horizontal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const post = { ... }
</script>

<BlogCard variant="horizontal" size="lg" shape="square" appearance="filled" v-bind="post" />
```

Example: Realistic: meta variations and fallbacks
```vue
<div class="grid gap-6 sm:grid-cols-3">
  <BlogCard title="Numeric read time" category="Guide" author="Author name" date="2024-05-17T09:30:00Z" :read-time="4" href="/guides/customisation" />
  <BlogCard title="Free-form date" author="Author name" date="Last Tuesday" read-time="a quick read" href="/guides/migration" />
  <BlogCard title="No link, no image" excerpt="Plain card without href." category="Note" />
</div>
```

# BlogGrid
group: marketing / Blog
Responsive 1-4 column grid of BlogCards from a posts array, with an optional featured first post.

Use for blog indexes and "latest posts" sections. Pass `items` for the common case, or place your own `BlogCard`s (or any element) in the default slot. One column on mobile, two from `sm`, then `columns` from `lg`. `variant` is forwarded to every card. `layout="featured"` renders the first post as a full-width `featured` card and the remaining posts in the grid with `variant`. An empty `items` array renders an empty container; use the `empty` slot for an "no posts" message.

import { BlogGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Columns on large screens; invalid values (0, 5, strings) fall back to 3.
- variant: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' | 'featured' = 'vertical' - BlogCard variant forwarded to every generated card; unknown values fall back to `vertical`.
- layout: 'grid' | 'featured' = 'grid' - `featured`: first post is a full-width featured card. Unknown values fall back to `grid`.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between cards: `sm` 16px, `md` 24px (the original), `lg` 32px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - BlogCard `size` forwarded to every generated card (padding and title scale). A post in `items` can carry its own `size`, which wins. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Cards placed in the default slot keep their own props.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - BlogCard `shape` forwarded to every generated card; a post's own `shape` wins. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- appearance: 'card' | 'plain' | 'filled' = 'card' - BlogCard `appearance` forwarded to every generated card; a post's own `appearance` wins. Unknown values fall back to `card`.
- items: BlogGridItem[] = [] - Posts: `{ title, excerpt?, href?, image?, imageAlt?, category?, author?, date?, readTime?, size?, shape?, appearance? }`. `title` is required and `imageAlt` is required with `image` (empty string for a decorative cover). Non-array values and null entries are ignored.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level used by the generated cards.
- locale: string = 'en-US' - Locale forwarded to the cards for date formatting.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Custom cards; replaces `items` rendering (and the list role).
- empty - Shown when `items` is empty and there is no default slot.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a post in `items` has no non-empty `title`, or has an `image` without an `imageAlt` string (the message names the first failing index). An empty `imageAlt` marks the cover decorative.

Rules:
- Use `items` unless cards need custom content.
- Use `layout="featured"` when the newest post deserves emphasis; otherwise leave `layout` as `grid`.
- Pick `columns` 3 for 3/6/9 posts, 2 for 2/4, 1 with `variant="horizontal"` for list-style indexes.
- Provide an `empty` slot so an empty array does not leave a blank section.
- Pass dates as ISO strings so cards emit `<time datetime>`.
- Pair with SectionHeading above it.

Accessibility:
- In `items` mode the root is a real `<ul>` and every card sits in an `<li>`; with the default slot or no posts the root is a plain `<div>` (wrap your own cards in `<li>` inside a `<ul>` if you want list semantics).
- Cards are `<article>` elements with a single stretched title link; heading levels come from `level` (set it so the titles sit one level below the section heading).
- `gap`, `size`, `shape` and `appearance` change spacing and surfaces only; list semantics, headings and links are identical in every combination.
- One column at 320px, two from `sm`, `columns` from `lg`; cards have no hover motion.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<BlogGrid :columns="2" :items="[{ title: 'Sample post title', excerpt: 'Short summary of the post.', href: '/guides/getting-started' }, { title: 'Second sample post', href: '/guides/customisation' }]" />
```

Example: Vertical cards, three columns
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const posts = [{ title: '...', excerpt: '...', href: '/guides/getting-started', image: '/x.jpg', imageAlt: '', category: 'Guide', author: 'Author name', date: '2024-03-01', readTime: 6 }, ...]
</script>

<BlogGrid variant="vertical" :columns="3" :items="posts" />
```

Example: Horizontal cards, one column
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const posts = [...]
</script>

<BlogGrid variant="horizontal" :columns="1" :items="posts" />
```

Example: Featured layout
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const posts = [...]
</script>

<BlogGrid layout="featured" :columns="3" :items="posts" :level="2" />
```

Example: Gap
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const posts = [...]
</script>

<div class="grid gap-10">
  <BlogGrid v-for="g in ['sm', 'md', 'lg']" :key="g" :gap="g" :columns="2" :items="posts.slice(2, 4)" />
</div>
```

Example: Size, shape and appearance
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const mixed = [{ title: 'Follows the grid', excerpt: 'Square, plain, small.', href: '/guides/getting-started' }, { title: 'Own appearance', excerpt: 'This post asks for filled.', href: '/guides/customisation', appearance: 'filled' }]
</script>

<BlogGrid size="sm" shape="square" appearance="plain" :columns="2" :items="mixed" />
```

Example: Realistic: heading, empty state and slot cards
```vue
<section class="space-y-8">
  <SectionHeading title="Four guides cover installation, theming, migration and tests" />
  <BlogGrid :items="[]" :columns="2">
    <template #empty><p class="rounded-lg border border-dashed p-8 text-center text-muted-foreground">No posts published yet.</p></template>
  </BlogGrid>
  <BlogGrid :columns="2">
    <BlogCard title="Hand-built card" excerpt="Any BlogCard works in the slot." href="/guides/getting-started" category="Slot" />
    <BlogCard title="Another one" variant="horizontal" date="2024-06-01" />
  </BlogGrid>
</section>
```

# ScrollProgress
group: marketing / Chrome
Thin reading-progress bar pinned to the top or bottom of the viewport.

Use on long-form pages (articles, docs, case studies). It reads window scroll position and document height, never throws on pages that do not scroll (stays at 0) and removes its listeners on unmount. The bar is non-interactive (`pointer-events-none`) and its transition is disabled for reduced-motion users. Render it once per page, e.g. next to `SiteHeader`.

import { ScrollProgress } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- position: 'top' | 'bottom' = 'top' - Viewport edge to pin to. Unknown values fall back to `top`.
- variant: 'bar' | 'rounded' | 'inset' = 'bar' - `bar` is a flush strip, `rounded` rounds both ends of the fill, `inset` floats a rounded track 0.5rem from the edge and 1rem from the viewport sides. Unknown values fall back to `bar`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Thickness: 2px, 4px or 6px. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'neutral' | 'success' | 'info' = 'primary' - Fill colour: `primary`, `neutral` (the foreground colour), `success` or `info`. Unknown values fall back to `primary`. Reflected as `data-tone`.
- label: string = 'Reading progress' - Accessible name (localise here).
- target: string | HTMLElement | null - Follow this scroll container (an element or a CSS selector) instead of the page. A selector that matches nothing falls back to the page.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes. Pass `static` to render the strip in the page flow, as the galleries below do.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the progress bar has no accessible name (`label` emptied and no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`).

Rules:
- Mount once per page, not per section.
- Do not use for form or upload progress; use Progress from feedback.
- It tracks the whole document unless `target` names an inner scroll container.

Accessibility:
- role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin/max (0-100), aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext ("42%") and an aria-label (`label`, default "Reading progress"). It is not focusable, has no keyboard map and never takes pointer events.
- `size`, `tone` and `variant` change looks only: the role, name and value text are the same in every combination. `tone` is colour only, so the percentage in `aria-valuetext` stays the signal.
- The bar is smoothed with `motion-safe:transition-transform`, so reduced-motion users get position updates without animation. Nothing flashes or loops.
- In forced-colors mode the fill is drawn as a 4px bottom border in the text colour, because background colours are overridden there.
- The bar fills from the start edge, so it mirrors in right-to-left pages (`rtl:origin-right`).
- It is a 4px bar fixed to the viewport edge (2px to 6px with `size`; `inset` sits 0.5rem from the edge), so it never affects reflow at 320px and does not cover content that scrolls into view (it is thinner than any focus indicator).

Example: Tracking a scroll box
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <ScrollProgress target="#sp-basic" class="static bg-muted" label="Progress through the sample article" />
  <div id="sp-basic" role="region" aria-label="Sample article (sp-basic)" tabindex="0" :ref="(el) => { if (el && !el.scrollTop) el.scrollTop = 90 }" class="h-32 overflow-auto rounded-md border p-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground"><p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="py-1">Sample paragraph {{ n }}.</p></div>
</div>
```

Example: Size gallery: sm, md, lg
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <ScrollProgress size="sm" target="#sp-size" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, small" />
  <ScrollProgress size="md" target="#sp-size" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, medium" />
  <ScrollProgress size="lg" target="#sp-size" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, large" />
  <div id="sp-size" role="region" aria-label="Sample article (sp-size)" tabindex="0" :ref="(el) => { if (el && !el.scrollTop) el.scrollTop = 90 }" class="h-32 overflow-auto rounded-md border p-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground"><p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="py-1">Sample paragraph {{ n }}.</p></div>
</div>
```

Example: Tone gallery: primary, neutral, success, info
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <ScrollProgress tone="primary" size="lg" target="#sp-tone" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, primary" />
  <ScrollProgress tone="neutral" size="lg" target="#sp-tone" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, neutral" />
  <ScrollProgress tone="success" size="lg" target="#sp-tone" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, success" />
  <ScrollProgress tone="info" size="lg" target="#sp-tone" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, info" />
  <div id="sp-tone" role="region" aria-label="Sample article (sp-tone)" tabindex="0" :ref="(el) => { if (el && !el.scrollTop) el.scrollTop = 90 }" class="h-32 overflow-auto rounded-md border p-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground"><p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="py-1">Sample paragraph {{ n }}.</p></div>
</div>
```

Example: Variant gallery: bar, rounded, inset
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <ScrollProgress variant="bar" size="lg" target="#sp-variant" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, bar" />
  <ScrollProgress variant="rounded" size="lg" target="#sp-variant" class="static bg-muted" label="Reading progress, rounded" />
  <ScrollProgress variant="inset" size="lg" target="#sp-variant" class="static" label="Reading progress, inset" />
  <div id="sp-variant" role="region" aria-label="Sample article (sp-variant)" tabindex="0" :ref="(el) => { if (el && !el.scrollTop) el.scrollTop = 90 }" class="h-32 overflow-auto rounded-md border p-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground"><p v-for="n in 12" :key="n" class="py-1">Sample paragraph {{ n }}.</p></div>
</div>
```

Example: Page-level bar, bottom edge
```vue
<ScrollProgress position="bottom" variant="inset" tone="neutral" label="Progress through the article" />
```

# ContactLink
group: marketing / Contact
mailto: or tel: link with a leading icon, as an inline link, a button (filled, outline or ghost) or a card.

Use for email addresses and phone numbers in headers, footers and contact sections. For `tel` the display text keeps your formatting while the href is reduced to dialable characters. A missing value renders plain text instead of a dead link. `variant` picks the look: `inline` (text link), `button` (filled button), `outline` (bordered button), `ghost` (borderless button with a fill on hover) or `card` (bordered block with a bare icon, the `label` as headline and the raw `value` beneath it); `size` scales text, icon and padding; `tone` picks the colour (primary, neutral or muted) and `shape` the corners (rounded, pill or square). Tone and shape never change the accessible name or the `mailto:` / `tel:` target.

import { ContactLink } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- type: 'email' | 'tel' = 'email' - Link scheme. Unknown values behave as email.
- value: string - Address or number. Empty renders a non-link span.
- label: string - Visible text; defaults to `value`. In the `card` variant it is the headline and `value` is shown as the secondary line when they differ.
- subject: string - mailto subject (email only), URL-encoded automatically.
- icon: IconDefinition - Override the default envelope/phone icon.
- noIcon: boolean = false - Hide the icon (and the icon tile in `card`).
- variant: 'inline' | 'button' | 'outline' | 'ghost' | 'card' = 'inline' - Look. `button` is filled, `outline` has a border and a hover fill, `ghost` has no border and a hover fill (a border appears in forced-colors mode). Unknown values fall back to `inline`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'neutral' | 'muted' = 'primary' - Colour. `inline` and `ghost`: text in primary, foreground or muted-foreground. `button`: primary fill, foreground fill with background text, or secondary fill. `outline`: border and text in primary, foreground (input border) or muted-foreground. `card`: icon colour. Neutral and muted inline links are underlined so colour is not the only cue. Applies to real links only; a non-link span keeps the surrounding colour. Unknown values fall back to `primary`. Reflected as `data-tone`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners: the original radius of the variant (`rounded-sm` inline, `rounded-md` buttons, `rounded-lg` card), `rounded-full`, or none. Also shapes the focus ring. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text, icon and padding scale (button minimum heights 2 / 2.25 / 2.75rem). Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces the visible text (the headline in the `card` variant).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the link has no text: no `value`, no `label` and no default slot content.

Rules:
- Choose `variant`: inline inside text or footers, button for a primary contact call to action, outline or ghost for a secondary one next to it, card for a contact section with several channels (give each a `label` such as "Email us").
- Keep `tone="primary"` unless the page already has a stronger accent; `neutral` and `muted` suit footers. Use `shape="pill"` only when the neighbouring buttons are pills too.
- Use ContactLink instead of hand-writing mailto:/tel: anchors.
- Never embed unvalidated user input as `value`.
- Use only addresses and numbers that exist; the docs samples are placeholders.
- Do not set `href` yourself; it is derived from `value`.

Accessibility:
- A real anchor (`mailto:` or `tel:`) whose name is its visible text; the icon is decorative (aria-hidden). Use `label` when the raw value is not meaningful to read aloud; keep the visible text inside the accessible name.
- `variant`, `tone` and `shape` change the look only: the element, the `href`, the visible text (the accessible name) and the aria-hidden icon are identical in every combination. Text colours use checked pairs: primary, foreground and muted-foreground on the page background, primary-foreground on primary, background on foreground, secondary-foreground on secondary, accent-foreground on the hover fill. `ghost` and `outline` keep a border in forced-colors mode so the target stays visible.
- Keyboard: Tab to focus, Enter to follow. Visible focus ring. A missing value renders a plain span, not a dead link.
- Targets are at least 24px tall (button and card more) and 44px on coarse pointers; the button grows with its text instead of clipping at 200% zoom, and long labels wrap (`break-words`) so the card reflows at 320px.

Example: Basic: email
```vue
<ContactLink value="hello@example.com" subject="Question about pricing" />
```

Example: Realistic: phone with label
```vue
<ContactLink type="tel" value="+1 555 0100" label="Call us: 555 0100" />
```

Example: Inline variant, small
```vue
<ContactLink variant="inline" size="sm" value="support@example.com" />
```

Example: Button variant
```vue
<ContactLink variant="button" value="sales@example.com" label="Email sales" subject="Pricing question" />
```

Example: Button variant, large phone
```vue
<ContactLink variant="button" size="lg" type="tel" value="+1 555 0100" label="Call +1 555 0100" />
```

Example: Card variant
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-2xl gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <ContactLink variant="card" value="hello@example.com" label="Email us" />
  <ContactLink variant="card" type="tel" value="+1 555 0100" label="Call us" />
</div>
```

Example: Card variant, large without icon
```vue
<ContactLink variant="card" size="lg" no-icon class="max-w-sm" value="press@example.com" label="Press enquiries" />
```

Example: Outline and ghost variants
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
  <ContactLink variant="outline" value="sales@example.com" label="Email sales" />
  <ContactLink variant="ghost" value="support@example.com" label="Email support" />

```

# ContactSection
group: marketing / Contact
Contact page section: heading plus a `form` slot and a `details` slot in split, centered, card or inline layouts.

Layout shell for contact pages. It owns the heading and arrangement only; put your own form (Field/Input/Textarea/Button) in the `form` slot and addresses, phone numbers or ContactLinks in the `details` slot. It does no validation and no network access. `split` shows heading and details beside the form on large screens, `centered` stacks heading, form and details in one column, `card` is `split` inside a bordered surface, `inline` is a compact one-row strip (heading and description left, form and details right) for a short form such as a single question. `size` scales gaps and surface padding, `tone="muted"` gives the section a secondary surface and `align="center"` centres the text of `split` and `card`. Works with any subset of slots.

import { ContactSection } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'split' | 'centered' | 'card' | 'inline' = 'split' - Layout. `inline` is compact: heading and description on the left, form and details in one block on the right from `lg` (one column below). Unknown values fall back to `split`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Gaps, padding of a surface (`card` or a muted tone), heading scale and details text. `md` is the original. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' = 'default' - `default` has no fill (`card` keeps `bg-card`). `muted` gives every layout a bordered secondary surface with secondary-foreground text. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - `center` centres the heading and details of `split` and `card`. `centered` is always centred and `inline` always start-aligned. Unknown values fall back to `start`. Reflected as `data-align`.
- eyebrow: string - Short label above the title. Plain text; use only when it adds information the title lacks.
- title: string - Section title. State what the section is for ("Ask about the library"), not a generic "Contact".
- description: string - Supporting paragraph under the title.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Heading element level of the title; invalid values fall back to 2.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- form - The contact form (any content).
- details - Contact details: addresses, phone, email, hours, ContactLink/SocialLinks. Sits under the heading (split, card) or below the form (centered).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a `<form>` inside the component has no submit handler (`@submit` / `@submit.prevent`) and no `action`, because it would submit nowhere.

Rules:
- Put the form in the `form` slot and contact info in the `details` slot; this component does not validate or submit.
- Use `split` by default, `centered` for short forms, `card` when the page background is plain and the block needs a surface.
- Use `inline` for a one-question strip, `tone="muted"` when the section needs to stand out from the page, `size="sm"` in dense pages and `align="center"` only for short headings with few details.
- Use NewsletterSignup, not this, for a single email field.
- A form with no `@submit` handler submits nowhere; always wire one or remove the form.
- Wrap form fields in `Field`.

Accessibility:
- Renders a plain `<section>` with no landmark name: labelling every section would make each a `region` landmark, which dilutes navigation and fails landmark-unique when repeated. Add your own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` only if the section deserves to be a landmark.
- The title renders at `level` (default h2); keep heading levels sequential on the page.
- The form is yours: give every field a visible label (use `Field`), `autocomplete` tokens, `aria-invalid` plus a described error, and a live status for the result. The component does no validation and no network access.
- Every layout, `size`, `tone` and `align` keeps the same DOM order (heading, form, details) so the reading order and tab order do not change; `inline` only places the form and the details in one block on the right. A muted surface carries a border so it is still outlined in forced-colors mode. Text on it uses secondary-foreground (and muted-foreground for the description) on the secondary surface.
- Reflows at 320px: the grid is one column below `lg`, content uses `min-w-0`, and the layouts use no left/right offsets, so RTL mirrors.

Example: Minimal (heading only, no slots)
```vue
<ContactSection title="Ask about the library" description="Add your own contact details in the details slot." />
```

Example: Split layout
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
async function onSubmit(event) {
  await fetch('/api/contact', { method: 'POST', body: new FormData(event.target) })
}
</script>

<ContactSection variant="split" title="Ask about the library" description="Write to the maintainers with a question about a component.">
  <template #details>
    <ContactLink type="email" value="name@example.com" />
    <ContactLink type="tel" value="+15550100" label="+1 555 0100" />
  </template>
  <template #form>
    <form class="space-y-4" @submit.prevent="onSubmit">
      <Field label="Name"><Input name="name" autocomplete="name" /></Field>
      <Field label="Email"><Input name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" /></Field>
      <Field label="Message"><Textarea name="message" /></Field>
      <Button type="submit">Send message</Button>
    </form>
  </template>
</ContactSection>
```
