# SocialLinks
group: marketing / Contact
Row or column of icon-only links to social/profile pages in plain, outline, filled or ghost styles, each with an aria-label.

Use in footers, author boxes and contact sections. Pass FontAwesome `IconDefinition`s (brand icons require `@fortawesome/free-brands-svg-icons` in your app; the library itself only ships solid icons). Entries without a label or href are skipped because icon-only links without a name are inaccessible. `variant` picks the look (`ghost` is the original style), `size` the hit area, `align` the position along the main axis and `orientation` row or column.

import { SocialLinks } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- links: SocialLink[] = [] - `{ label, href, icon }`; label becomes the aria-label. Entries without a `label` or `href` are a contract violation, not skipped silently.
- variant: 'ghost' | 'plain' | 'outline' | 'filled' = 'ghost' - Look. `ghost`: muted icon with an accent background on hover (the original style). `plain`: no background, colour change only. `outline`: bordered square with rounded corners. `filled`: solid primary. Unknown values fall back to `ghost`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Hit area (2 / 2.5 / 3rem, at least 2.75rem on coarse pointers) and icon size; unknown falls back to md.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'start' - Position along the main axis (justify in a row, items in a column). Unknown values fall back to `start`.
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - `horizontal` wraps in a row, `vertical` stacks in a column. Unknown values fall back to `horizontal`. Reflected as `data-orientation`.
- newTab: boolean = true - target="_blank" with rel="noopener noreferrer".
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root `<ul>`; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `links` has no non-empty `label` (the link is icon-only) or no non-empty `href`. The message names the first failing index.

Rules:
- Choose `variant`: ghost or plain in footers, outline on light content sections, filled for a prominent block. Use `orientation="vertical"` only for rails/sidebars.
- Always provide a human label ("GitHub"), never rely on the icon alone.
- Only link profiles that exist; an icon with no target is a dead end.
- Install a brand icon package in the app for brand icons.

Accessibility:
- A native `ul` of links. Each link is named by its `label` (aria-label) because it is icon-only; icons are aria-hidden. Entries without a label or href are skipped.
- Keyboard: Tab / Shift+Tab through the links, Enter to follow. Visible focus ring that also shows as an outline in forced-colors mode.
- Hit areas are 32/40/48px, raised to at least 44px on coarse pointers, and the row wraps so it reflows at 320px.
- Links open in a new tab by default (`target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`); set `newTab` to false for same-tab navigation.

Example: Basic: icon links
```vue
<SocialLinks :links="links" />
```

Example: Realistic: large, same tab
```vue
<SocialLinks size="lg" :new-tab="false" :links="links" />
```

Example: Ghost variant (default)
```vue
<SocialLinks variant="ghost" :links="links" />
```

Example: Plain variant
```vue
<SocialLinks variant="plain" size="sm" :links="links" />
```

Example: Outline variant
```vue
<SocialLinks variant="outline" :links="links" />
```

Example: Filled variant, large
```vue
<SocialLinks variant="filled" size="lg" :links="links" />
```

Example: Centered row
```vue
<SocialLinks variant="outline" align="center" :links="links" />
```

Example: Vertical column, aligned to the end
```vue
<SocialLinks orientation="vertical" align="end" variant="filled" size="sm" class="w-12" :links="links" />
```

# FaqList
group: marketing / Content
Accessible FAQ accordion built on native <details>/<summary> in six layouts.

Use for real support questions on landing and pricing pages. It uses native `<details>`, so it works without JavaScript, is keyboard accessible and findable with in-page search. `single` keeps one answer open at a time. Variants: `bordered` (default rules between items), `separated` (each item a card), `plain` (no chrome), `two-column` (balanced two-column list on `md`+), `with-categories` (group by `category` under headings or switch with tabs), `numbered` (1., 2. ... before each question; only for answers you refer to by number). For app navigation accordions use the navigation Accordion instead.

import { FaqList } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: FaqItem[] = [] - Questions and answers: `{ q: string, a: string, category?: string }`.
- variant: 'bordered' | 'separated' | 'plain' | 'two-column' | 'with-categories' | 'numbered' = 'bordered' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `bordered` (the original look).
- categoryMode: 'headings' | 'tabs' = 'headings' - `with-categories` only: category headings (`h3` by default, see `headingLevel`) or a tab per category. Unknown values fall back to `headings`.
- categoriesLabel: string = 'Question categories' - `with-categories` + `tabs`: accessible name of the tab list.
- defaultCategory: string - `with-categories` + `tabs`: category selected first. Unknown values select the first category.
- uncategorizedLabel: string = 'Other' - `with-categories`: heading/tab for items without a `category` when other items have one.
- headingLevel: number = 3 - `with-categories` + `headings`: heading level of the category titles, 2 to 6. Other values fall back to 3.
- single: boolean = false - Only one answer open at a time (across categories too).
- defaultOpen: number[] = [] - Item indexes (position in `items`) open initially. Invalid indexes are ignored.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- answer ({ item: FaqItem, index: number }) - Replaces the answer text (rich content). `index` is the position in `items`, also when items are grouped.

Events:
- toggle [{ index: number, open: boolean }] - An item was opened or closed. `index` is the position in `items`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an item has an empty `q`, or an empty `a` while the `answer` slot is not used (the first one is named by index).

Rules:
- Answers are plain strings; use the `answer` slot for links/markup.
- Use `single` for long lists.
- Pair with FAQPage JSON-LD in the app if SEO matters.
- Choose `with-categories` only when items carry a `category`; use `categoryMode="tabs"` for more than ~3 categories.
- `two-column` suits 6+ short questions; `separated` suits tinted or dark sections; `numbered` suits step-like or ordered FAQs.

Accessibility:
- Native details/summary semantics: Tab focuses a question, Enter or Space toggles it, the open state is exposed by the browser (no ARIA needed). Questions are at least 24px tall and `pointer-coarse:min-h-11` on touch; focus uses the shared ring (an outline in forced-colors mode).
- Chevron and the decorative number in `numbered` are aria-hidden; the chevron rotation is skipped under reduced motion.
- Category headings are h3 labelling a `role="group"` (not a region landmark per category). Tabs mode uses the library Tabs: role=tablist (named by `categoriesLabel`) / tab / tabpanel, Left/Right (Up/Down) arrows move between tabs with roving tabindex, Home/End jump to the first/last tab.
- Text wraps and the layouts collapse to one column at 320px; alignment uses logical properties for RTL.

Example: Minimal (bordered, default)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [{ q: 'How do I turn on dark mode?', a: 'Add class="dark" to the html element.' }, ...]
</script>

<FaqList :items="items" />
```

Example: Realistic: single-open with a default and toggle events
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const last = ref(null)
</script>

<FaqList single :default-open="[0]" :items="items" @toggle="last = $event" />
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Last: {{ last ?? 'none yet' }}</p>
```

Example: Variant bordered
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<FaqList variant="bordered" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant separated (cards)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<FaqList variant="separated" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant plain
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<FaqList variant="plain" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant two-column
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<FaqList variant="two-column" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant numbered
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<FaqList variant="numbered" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant with-categories (headings)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<FaqList variant="with-categories" :items="categorised" />
```

# InstallTabs
group: marketing / Content
Tabbed install/code snippets with a copy button.

Use for package-manager install commands or short multi-variant snippets (npm / pnpm / yarn, curl / brew). Standalone WAI-ARIA tabs with automatic activation (selection follows focus) and a clipboard copy button that copies the active snippet. The snippet is a focusable, scrollable region, so long commands stay reachable by keyboard at 320px. For long code or syntax highlighting use a dedicated code block; for general tabs use the navigation Tabs.

import { InstallTabs } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- tabs: InstallTab[] = [] - `{ label, code, language? }`.
- variant: 'default' | 'minimal' | 'contained' = 'default' - Look. `default` bordered card with a muted header; `minimal` no frame, underlined tabs; `contained` muted tray with pill tabs and a raised code panel. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text and padding scale of tabs, copy button and code. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- modelValue: number - v-model: selected tab index (clamped). Uncontrolled when omitted.
- copyLabel: string = 'Copy' - Copy button text.
- copiedLabel: string = 'Copied' - Text after copying; also announced via a status region.
- copyErrorLabel: string = 'Copy failed' - Text shown and announced when the clipboard write fails (also emits `copy-error`).
- label: string = 'Install commands' - Accessible name of the tablist.
- resetAfter: number = 2000 - Milliseconds before the copied / failed message resets.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:modelValue [index: number] - Selected tab changed.
- copy [text: string] - Snippet copied to the clipboard.
- copy-error [error: unknown] - Clipboard unavailable or write rejected. The button and a live region also say "Copy failed".

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `tabs` is empty.
- Throws a ContractError when a tab has an empty `label` or `code` (the first one is named by index).
- Throws a ContractError when `label` (the name of the tab list) is empty.

Rules:
- Choose `variant`: default inside content sections, minimal inside docs prose or a hero, contained over images or tinted backgrounds. Use `size="lg"` for hero commands and `sm` for sidebars.
- Keep snippets short (one command per tab).
- Listen to `copy-error` if you need a fallback UI; copying needs a secure context (HTTPS).
- Use unique tab labels.

Accessibility:
- role=tablist/tab/tabpanel. The tablist has an accessible name (`label`), the selected tab has aria-selected="true" and a roving tabindex (only it is in the Tab order), and the panel is named by its tab with aria-labelledby. There is no aria-controls, because the inactive panels are not rendered.
- Keyboard: ArrowRight / ArrowLeft move to the next / previous tab and wrap (the arrows swap in a right-to-left page), Home and End jump to the first and last tab, selection follows focus, and Tab moves on to the panel and then the copy button.
- The panel is `tabindex="0"` and scrolls horizontally (`overflow-x-auto`), so long commands are reachable by keyboard; its focus outline is drawn inset (2px, `outline-solid`, using the shared `insetFocus` helper) so the frame never clips it.
- The copy button is a real button with the visible name "Copy" (WCAG 2.5.3: the visible text is the name). Its result, "Copied" or "Copy failed", replaces the button text and is announced through a persistent `role="status"` region outside the button.
- Tabs and the copy button are at least 24px tall and 44px on coarse pointers. In forced-colors mode the active tab is underlined because backgrounds and rings are overridden.

Example: Basic: package managers
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const tabs = [{ label: 'pnpm', code: 'pnpm add @perfect-design/ui' }, ...]
</script>

<InstallTabs :tabs="tabs" />
```

Example: Realistic: controlled with localised labels
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const active = ref(1)
</script>

<InstallTabs v-model="active" label="Installationsbefehle" copy-label="Kopieren" copied-label="Kopiert" copy-error-label="Kopieren fehlgeschlagen" :tabs="tabs" />
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Selected: {{ tabs[active].label }}</p>
```

Example: Minimal variant
```vue
<InstallTabs variant="minimal" :tabs="tabs" />
```

Example: Contained variant
```vue
<InstallTabs variant="contained" :tabs="tabs" />
```

Example: Small size
```vue
<InstallTabs size="sm" :tabs="tabs" />
```

Example: Large size, contained
```vue
<InstallTabs size="lg" variant="contained" :tabs="tabs" />
```

# NumberedSteps
group: marketing / Content
Numbered steps for how-it-works and onboarding sequences: cards, timeline, horizontal, minimal or with media.

Use to explain a short ordered process (3-6 steps). Renders a semantic `<ol>` in every variant. Numbers are kept because the steps are an ordered sequence; do not use it for lists that have no order. `variant` picks the layout: `default` (bordered card with the number beside the text), `cards` (number above the text), `timeline` (single column with a vertical connector line), `horizontal` (one row from `sm` upward with a connector between numbers), `minimal` (no boxes, large bare numbers and divider lines) and `with-media` (text next to an image per step, alternating sides on `md`+). `columns` applies to `default`, `cards` and `minimal`; the other variants are single-column or flow by step count. Show the real steps in the real product where you can (`with-media`). For feature lists without order use `FeatureGrid`; for interactive wizards use a stepper from the navigation group.

import { NumberedSteps } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- steps: Step[] = [] - `{ title: string, description?: string, media?: string, mediaAlt?: string }`. `media`/`mediaAlt` are used by the `with-media` variant only.
- variant: 'default' | 'cards' | 'timeline' | 'horizontal' | 'minimal' | 'with-media' = 'default' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Marker size (32, 40 or 48px), title and description scale, item padding and gaps. Timeline and horizontal connector lines move with the marker. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- tone: 'primary' | 'neutral' | 'success' | 'info' = 'primary' - Marker colour. Filled markers use `primary` / `primary-foreground`, `foreground` / `background` (neutral), `success` / `success-foreground` or `info` / `info-foreground`. The outlined timeline marker and the bare `minimal` number use the tone colour on the page background. Unknown values fall back to `primary`. Use `success` and `info` only when the colour means something; the number carries the order.
- shape: 'circle' | 'rounded' | 'square' = 'circle' - Marker shape: `circle` (the original), `rounded` (6px radius) or `square`. The bare number of `minimal` has no box and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `circle`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - `center` centres the marker against the text in row layouts (`default`, `minimal`, `with-media`) and centres the whole step in `cards`. `timeline` and `horizontal` always start-align because their connector lines begin at the marker. Unknown values fall back to `start`. Reflected as `data-align`.
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Columns on large screens for `default`, `cards` and `minimal`; ignored by `timeline`, `horizontal` and `with-media`. Invalid falls back to 3.
- pad: boolean = false - Two-digit numbers (01, 02...).
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of step titles; invalid falls back to 3.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root `<ol>`; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- step ({ step: Step, index: number, number: string }) - Replaces a whole step's content (number, text and media) inside the `<li>`; the variant's item styling stays.
- media ({ step: Step, index: number }) - Custom media for the `with-media` variant (video, illustration, component). Takes precedence over `step.media`; ignored by other variants.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a step has an empty `title` and the `step` slot is not used (the first one is named by index).

Rules:
- Use only for a real ordered sequence. Keep to 3-6 steps with short titles, and prefer showing the actual steps with `with-media`.
- Choose `variant`: default or cards for 3-4 equal steps, timeline for long or detailed sequences, horizontal for 3-5 very short steps on wide layouts, minimal for editorial pages, with-media when each step has a screenshot.
- Use `columns` equal to the step count up to 4 (default, cards, minimal only).
- Keep `tone` as `primary` unless the colour carries meaning (for example `success` for finished steps); use `neutral` on pages that already have a strong accent. Use one `size` per list.
- Use the `step` slot only when you need custom markup; you then own accessibility of the number.
- Prefer `step.media` for images and the `media` slot only for non-image media.

Accessibility:
- Ordered list semantics in every variant; the visual number is aria-hidden and the title includes a screen-reader-only "N." prefix.
- `size`, `tone`, `shape` and `align` change the look only: the order, the screen-reader numbers and the aria-hidden marker are identical in every combination. `tone` never replaces the number, so colour is not the only carrier of order. Marker colours use checked token pairs (primary-foreground on primary, background on foreground, success-foreground on success, info-foreground on info; tone text on the page background for the outlined and bare markers). Marker sizes are decorative (the sequence is announced by the list), so the 24px target rule does not apply.
- Connector lines and marker circles are purely decorative (CSS only). They are positioned with logical offsets (`start`/`end`), so RTL mirrors them.
- Columns collapse to one on phones; every variant reflows at 320px. Item surfaces use a border, not a shadow.
- Give `mediaAlt` a real description when the image carries information; it is empty (decorative) when omitted. Custom `media` slot content owns its own accessibility.

Example: Basic: how it works
```vue
<NumberedSteps :steps="steps" />
```

Example: Default: vertical, padded numbers, custom step
```vue
<NumberedSteps :columns="1" pad :steps="steps">
  <template #step="{ step, number }"><div class="flex items-baseline gap-3"><span class="font-semibold tabular-nums text-primary">{{ number }}</span><span>{{ step.title }}</span></div></template>
</NumberedSteps>
```

Example: Cards variant, four columns
```vue
<NumberedSteps variant="cards" :columns="4" pad :steps="steps" />
```

Example: Timeline variant
```vue
<NumberedSteps variant="timeline" class="max-w-xl" :steps="steps" />
```

Example: Horizontal variant
```vue
<NumberedSteps variant="horizontal" :steps="steps" />
```

Example: Minimal variant (no boxes)
```vue
<NumberedSteps variant="minimal" :columns="3" pad :steps="steps" />
```

Example: With-media variant
```vue

```

Example: With-media variant using the media slot
```vue

  <template #media="{ step, index }">
    <img :src="scene" :alt="'Sample image for step ' + (index + 1)" class="aspect-video w-full object-cover" />
  </template>
</NumberedSteps>
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-8 md:grid-cols-3">
  <NumberedSteps v-for="s in ['sm', 'md', 'lg']" :key="s" variant="timeline" :size="s" :steps="short" />
```


Example: Combined: small, success, square, minimal


# FeatureCard
group: marketing / Features
Card that presents one feature: icon, title, description and optional link, in eight variants.

Use inside `FeatureGrid` (or any grid) to describe a feature. Pick the look with `variant`, scale it with `size`, paint it with `tone` and choose corners with `shape`. Variants: `card` (default: border, no shadow, bare accent icon), `bordered` (heavier outline), `flat` (muted surface, no border), `icon-left` (row layout), `icon-top` (icon above the text), `icon-badge` (borderless with a tinted icon tile; opt-in, because a tinted square above every title is a stock look), `minimal` (no box) and `highlight` (primary border for the one feature that matters). `align="center"` centres the content. The card has no hover effect because it is not interactive; only its link is. Icons are optional: leave them out unless they depict the specific feature. For numbered processes use `NumberedSteps`.

import { FeatureCard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- icon: IconDefinition - FontAwesome-shaped icon definition, drawn in the accent colour. Choose one that depicts the feature; omit it otherwise.
- title*: string - Feature name and card heading. Required unless the `title` slot is used.
- description: string - Short explanation.
- href: string - Renders a link at the bottom when set.
- linkLabel: string - Link text. Defaults to `Read about <title>` (or `Read more` without a title). Name what happens, not a generic invitation.
- external: boolean = false - Open link in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer"; adds an external-link icon and a screen reader note.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of the title; invalid falls back to 3. Keep it one level below the section heading.
- variant: 'card' | 'bordered' | 'flat' | 'icon-left' | 'icon-top' | 'icon-badge' | 'minimal' | 'highlight' = 'card' - Visual style. Unknown values fall back to `card`. Exposed as `data-variant`.
- align: 'left' | 'center' = 'left' - Content alignment. With `icon-left` the icon stays beside the text and the text stays at the start. Unknown values fall back to `left`. Exposed as `data-align`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and type scale: `sm` = p-4 with a 16px title, `md` = p-6 with an 18px title (the original look), `lg` = p-8 with a 20px title and 16px description. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' | 'inverted' = 'default' - Surface colour. `default` keeps the variant's own surface; `muted` paints the muted surface, `primary` the primary colour and `inverted` the foreground colour, with matching text, icon and link colours. `minimal` and `icon-badge` get padding and rounded corners when a tone is set. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Exposed as `data-tone`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - `square` removes the corner radius of the card and of the `icon-badge` tile. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- icon - Replaces the icon (any element); still wrapped in the variant icon wrapper.
- title - Replaces the title text.
- default - Replaces the description text.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is neither a non-empty `title` nor a `title` slot.

Rules:
- Always give `title`; keep descriptions under about 140 characters.
- Pass FontAwesome IconDefinition objects, not names, and only icons that depict the feature. Skip the icon when none fits.
- Name the link action in `linkLabel` ("Open the data table docs"). Never a generic invitation.
- Use `external` for off-site links.
- Choose `card` as the safe default, `flat` or `minimal` for dense sections, `bordered` on tinted backgrounds, `icon-left` for stacked lists and `highlight` for one key feature. `icon-badge` is available but is a stock look: use it sparingly.
- Use `align="center"` for short centred sections; do not centre long descriptions.
- Use `size` for density (`sm` in dense grids, `lg` for a lone feature), `tone="primary"` or `"inverted"` on one card per section, and `shape="square"` only when the surrounding layout has square corners.
- Inside FeatureGrid prefer its `variant` prop over styling each card.

Accessibility:
- Icons are decorative (aria-hidden). The title is a heading chosen by `level` (default h3); keep the heading order valid under the section heading.
- The DOM order (icon, title, description, link) is the same in every variant. Cards are not interactive; only the link is focusable, with a visible focus ring and a 24px minimum height (44px on coarse pointers).
- Link text is descriptive (`Read about <title>` by default). External links add an icon and a screen-reader note that they open in a new tab.
- Text wraps and the card uses `min-w-0`, so it reflows at 320px; alignment uses logical values so RTL works.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<FeatureCard :icon="faTable" title="Tables that sort and filter" description="Column definitions, sorting and paging are props." />
```

Example: With link

```vue
  <FeatureCard :icon="faPalette" title="One theme file" description="Colour, radius and type come from tokens, so a rebrand edits one place." href="/foundations/colors" link-label="Read about the colour tokens" />
</div>
```


# FeatureGrid
group: marketing / Features
Feature section in six layouts (grid, list, alternating, bento, centered, with-heading) built from an items array or slot content.

Use to show 3-12 product features. Pass `items` for the common case, or place your own `FeatureCard`s (or any element) in the default slot. `layout` chooses the arrangement: `grid` (default, 1 column on mobile, 2 from `sm`, then `columns` from `lg`), `list` (stacked icon-left rows), `alternating` (text next to an image, flipping sides every row), `bento` (tiles of mixed width via `span`), `centered` (centred, unboxed cards) and `with-heading` (a built-in SectionHeading above a grid; any of `eyebrow`/`title`/`description` also adds the heading in other layouts). `variant` is passed to every generated card; without it each layout picks a default (`grid`: card, `list`: icon-left, `alternating`: minimal, `bento`: card, `centered`: minimal). Generated items render as a real `ul` with `li` children. When a heading is present the root is a wrapper and the list is the inner `feature-grid-items`. Content placed in the default slot renders in a plain grid `div` without list semantics, so any element is valid there. Give the feature that matters more extra weight (`span`, `variant: "highlight"`) instead of repeating identical cards.

import { FeatureGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- layout: 'grid' | 'list' | 'alternating' | 'bento' | 'centered' | 'with-heading' = 'grid' - Arrangement of the items. Unknown values fall back to `grid`. Exposed as `data-layout`.
- columns: 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Columns on large screens for `grid`, `bento`, `centered` and `with-heading`; invalid falls back to 3. Ignored by `list` and `alternating`.
- items: FeatureItem[] = [] - Cards to render: `{ icon?, title, description?, href?, linkLabel?, external?, span?, image?, imageAlt?, variant? }`. `span` (1-4, clamped to `columns`) is used by `bento`; `image`/`imageAlt` by `alternating`; `variant` overrides the grid variant for that item.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level for generated cards.
- variant: 'card' | 'bordered' | 'flat' | 'icon-left' | 'icon-top' | 'icon-badge' | 'minimal' | 'highlight' - FeatureCard variant for generated cards. Omitted = the layout default. Unknown values fall back to `card`. The resolved value is exposed as `data-variant` on the root, also when the cards come from the slot.
- align: 'left' | 'center' = 'left' - Alignment of card content and of the built-in heading. `centered` layout always centres.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Spacing between items. `md` keeps each layout's own spacing; `sm` tightens and `lg` loosens it. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-gap`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - FeatureCard `size` for generated cards (padding and type scale). Cards placed in the slot keep their own props. Exposed as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' | 'inverted' = 'default' - FeatureCard `tone` for generated cards. Exposed as `data-tone`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - FeatureCard `shape` for generated cards. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- eyebrow: string - Built-in SectionHeading eyebrow.
- title: string - Built-in SectionHeading title.
- description: string - Built-in SectionHeading description.
- headingLevel: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Element level of the built-in heading title (cards use `level`).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; lands on the root (the wrapper when a heading is shown).

Slots:
- default - Custom cards; replaces `items` rendering (in every layout).
- heading - Replaces the built-in SectionHeading and forces the heading wrapper.
- media ({ item: FeatureItem, index: number }) - `alternating` layout: media for each row instead of `item.image`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `items` has no non-empty `title` (the message names the first failing index).
- Throws a ContractError when, in the `alternating` layout, an entry of `items` has an `image` but no `imageAlt` string and there is no `media` slot. An empty string marks the image decorative.

Rules:
- Use `items` unless cards need custom content.
- Give the feature that matters more extra room with `span` or `variant: "highlight"` instead of repeating identical cards, or use the `list` layout.
- Give `alternating` images an `imageAlt` that describes the real screenshot.
- Pick `columns` 3 for 3/6/9 items, 4 for 4/8, 2 for 2/4.
- Use `layout="with-heading"` (or just set `title`) instead of stacking SectionHeading + FeatureGrid by hand.
- Choose `grid` for 3-12 equal features, `list` for narrow columns, `alternating` for 2-4 features that deserve a screenshot each, `bento` for one or two hero features among small ones (give those `span: 2`), `centered` for short icon+title+text rows.
- Pass `variant` on the grid, not on each item, unless one item must stand out (`variant: "highlight"`).
- Do not set `span`/`image` outside `bento`/`alternating`; they are ignored.

Accessibility:
- Generated items are a native `ul` with `li` children (cards, or rows in `alternating`), so axe `aria-required-children` and `aria-allowed-role` pass. Slot content is a plain grid `div` with no list role; wrap items in your own list element if you need list semantics.
- Alternating images need a meaningful `imageAlt`; an empty alt marks the image decorative. Text comes first in DOM order, so reading order does not change when rows flip.
- Layout is 1 column on phones, 2 from `sm` and `columns` from `lg`, so it reflows at 320px. Cards use `min-w-0` and logical alignment for RTL. Heading levels are configurable: `headingLevel` for the section heading and `level` for the cards.

Example: Minimal: from items
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [{ icon: faPalette, title: 'Tokens', description: 'One theme file.' }, ...]
</script>

<FeatureGrid :columns="3" :items="items" />
```

Example: Slot with links, four columns
```vue
<FeatureGrid :columns="4">
  <FeatureCard :icon="faCircleHalfStroke" title="Themes" description="Accent presets and dark mode." href="/foundations/themes" link-label="Read about the themes" />
  <FeatureCard :icon="faPalette" title="Tokens" description="One theme file." />
</FeatureGrid>
```

Example: Layout: grid with two columns and a card variant
```vue
<FeatureGrid layout="grid" :columns="2" variant="bordered" :items="items" />
```

Example: Layout: list
```vue
<FeatureGrid class="max-w-xl" layout="list" :items="items" />
```

Example: Layout: alternating
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const rows = [{ title: 'Design', description: '...', image: '/screens/tokens.png', imageAlt: 'Token reference page' }, ...]
</script>

<FeatureGrid layout="alternating" :items="rows" />
```

Example: Layout: alternating with the media slot
```vue
<FeatureGrid layout="alternating" :items="items">
  <template #media="{ item, index }"><div class="grid aspect-video place-items-center text-muted-foreground">Media {{ index + 1 }}: {{ item.title }}</div></template>
</FeatureGrid>
```

Example: Layout: bento
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<FeatureGrid layout="bento" :columns="3" :items="tiles" />
```

Example: Layout: centered
```vue

```

Example: Layout: with-heading
```vue

```

Example: Gap, size, tone and shape
```vue
<div class="grid gap-8">
  <FeatureGrid :columns="2" gap="sm" size="sm" tone="muted" :items="items" />
  <FeatureGrid :columns="2" gap="lg" size="lg" shape="square" :items="items" />
</div>
```

Example: Custom heading slot
```vue
<FeatureGrid layout="with-heading" :items="items">
  <template #heading><h2 class="text-2xl font-semibold">What the library ships</h2></template>
</FeatureGrid>
```

Example: Realistic: six features with a highlighted item
```vue

```

# NewsletterSignup
group: marketing / Forms
Single-field email signup with validation; the parent performs the request and drives `status`.

Presentational newsletter form. It validates the address (simple pattern), emits `subscribe` with the trimmed email and renders whatever `status` the parent sets: `loading` disables the button (aria-busy) and ignores further submits, `success` shows `successMessage`, `error` shows `errorMessage`. It never makes a network call itself: the form submits nowhere until you handle `subscribe`, so always wire the event or remove the component. `inline` puts input and button in a row from `sm`, `stacked` is a centred narrow column, `card` is a stacked form on a bordered surface, `split` puts the copy on the left and the form on the right from `lg` (one column below). `size` scales the controls, title and spacing, and `shape` rounds the field and the button as rounded, pill or square. For multi-field forms use `ContactSection` with your own form.

import { NewsletterSignup } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'inline' | 'stacked' | 'card' | 'split' = 'inline' - Layout. `split` places the title and description on the left and the form and its messages on the right from `lg`; below `lg` it is one column in reading order. Without a title or description the form is not pushed to the right column. Unknown values fall back to `inline`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Controls, title, description and spacing. `sm`: 36px controls, `md`: the original 44px, `lg`: 48px controls and a larger title. Touch pointers keep a 44px minimum height and the field keeps 16px text on small screens at every size. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'pill' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of the email field and the button: 6px (the original), fully round (the field gets extra inline padding) or none. The field keeps its border and focus ring. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`.
- status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error' = 'idle' - Controlled by the parent after handling `subscribe`; unknown values fall back to `idle`.
- modelValue: string - Email value for `v-model`. Optional: without it the component keeps its own value.
- title: string - Heading text (or use the `title` slot).
- description: string - Supporting text under the title (or use the `description` slot).
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Heading element level of the title; invalid values fall back to 2.
- placeholder: string = 'Enter your email' - Input placeholder.
- buttonLabel: string = 'Subscribe' - Submit button text.
- label: string = 'Email address' - Visually hidden label of the input (accessible name).
- successMessage: string = 'Thanks for subscribing!' - Shown (role="status") while `status` is `success`.
- errorMessage: string = 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' - Shown (role="alert") while `status` is `error`.
- invalidMessage: string = 'Enter a valid email address.' - Shown (role="alert") when the typed email fails validation; also sets aria-invalid on the input and moves focus to it.
- resetOnSuccess: boolean = false - Clear the input (and emit `update:modelValue` with `""`) when `status` becomes `success`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes. Attributes fall through to the root element.

Slots:
- title - Rich title content; replaces the `title` prop.
- description - Rich description content; replaces the `description` prop.

Events:
- subscribe [email: string] - Fired on a valid submit with the trimmed email. Not fired for invalid emails, nor while `status` is `loading`.
- update:modelValue [value: string] - Fired on every input and on reset after success.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no `@subscribe` listener: the form only emits `subscribe`, so without one it submits nowhere.
- Throws a ContractError when `label` or `buttonLabel` is an empty string (the input and the button need accessible names).

Rules:
- The form submits nowhere on its own: always handle `@subscribe`.
- Handle `@subscribe`, set `status="loading"` immediately, then `success` or `error` when your request finishes; the component does no network I/O.
- Never set `status` to `loading` without a pending request; the button stays disabled until you change it.
- Use `split` for a wide band with a heading and the form side by side; give it a title or description so the form sits in the right column. Keep one `size` and one `shape` per page, matching the neighbouring buttons.
- Choose `inline` for wide bands, `stacked` for footers/narrow columns, `card` for sidebars or plain backgrounds.
- Use `v-model` plus `reset-on-success` to clear the field after success.
- The `subscribe` payload is the trimmed email string, already validated.

Accessibility:
- The input has a visually hidden `<label>` (`label` prop) and `type="email"` with `autocomplete="email"`. Keyboard: Tab to the input and the button, Enter submits. The row stacks below `sm`, so it reflows at 320px, and the input text uses `text-start` for RTL.
- Invalid input sets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the error message (`role="alert"`), and moves focus to the input (native validation is off with `novalidate`, so the component does it). The input shows the invalid state with a border, not colour alone, and clears it as soon as the value becomes valid.
- A server error (`status="error"`) is announced via `role="alert"` and linked with `aria-describedby`; success uses a persistent `role="status"` live region.
- While loading the button is disabled with `aria-busy="true"`, the form has `aria-busy`, and the input is read-only so typing is not lost.
- `variant`, `size` and `shape` change layout, scale and corners only. The label, the `type="email"` field, the submit button, the alert and status regions and the `aria-busy` handling are identical in every combination. Controls keep a 44px minimum on touch pointers and 16px text below `md`; the pill field gets extra inline padding so the text stays off the curve, and the border and focus ring follow the shape (a `Highlight` outline replaces the ring in forced-colors mode).
- The form is named by the title (`aria-labelledby`) when one is set, which makes it a form landmark: give every newsletter form on a page a different title (or none). Native browser validation is disabled (`novalidate`) so messages are consistent.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const status = ref('idle')
const email = ref('')
async function onSubscribe(value) {
  status.value = 'loading'
  try {
    await fetch('/api/subscribe', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ email: value }) })
    status.value = 'success'
  } catch {
    status.value = 'error'
  }
}
</script>

<NewsletterSignup :status="status" @subscribe="onSubscribe" />
```

# BeforeAfter
group: marketing / Media
Image comparison slider, horizontal or vertical: drag or use the keyboard to reveal the before and after images.

Use to compare two images with identical framing (renovations, retouching, UI redesigns). `orientation="horizontal"` (default) splits left/right; `orientation="vertical"` stacks before on top of after and the divider moves up/down. The divider is a real ARIA slider: pointer drag on either axis, arrow keys (step, Shift = 5x), PageUp/PageDown, Home/End. Position is a percentage of the width (height when vertical) showing "before" (0 = all "after", 100 = all "before") and is clamped; non-numeric values fall back to 50. Supports `v-model` or uncontrolled via `start`.

import { BeforeAfter } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- before: string - Image URL on the left (top when vertical). Missing = neutral placeholder.
- after: string - Image URL on the right (bottom when vertical). Missing = accent placeholder.
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' = 'horizontal' - Divider axis. Unknown values fall back to `horizontal`. Reflected as `data-orientation` and `aria-orientation`.
- showLabels: boolean = true - Show the decorative labels. `false` is the same as `variant="none"`. The slider's `aria-valuetext` always names both sides.
- variant: 'overlay' | 'bar' | 'none' = 'overlay' - Label placement. `overlay` puts a chip in the corner of each image, `bar` docks one opaque caption strip along the bottom edge, `none` shows no labels. Unknown values fall back to `overlay`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Handle and label size. Hit area 2rem, 2.5rem or 3rem wide; knob 1.75rem, 2.25rem or 2.75rem. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Frame corners (and label chips): `rounded-lg` or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`.
- tone: 'default' | 'primary' | 'neutral' = 'default' - Colour of the divider line and grip: the background colour, the primary colour (grip text uses primary-foreground) or the foreground colour (grip text uses background). Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-tone`.
- appearance: 'knob' | 'bar' | 'line' = 'knob' - Handle style. `knob` is a line with a round grip and two arrows, `bar` a line with a short rounded grip, `line` a thicker line only. Unknown values fall back to `knob`. Reflected as `data-appearance`.
- beforeAlt: string - Alt text for the before image. Required with `before`; an empty string marks it decorative.
- afterAlt: string - Alt text for the after image. Required with `after`; an empty string marks it decorative.
- beforeLabel: string = 'Before' - Corner label and slider text.
- afterLabel: string = 'After' - Corner label and slider text.
- modelValue: number - Divider position 0-100 (v-model): % of the width (height when vertical) showing "before". Clamped.
- start: number = 50 - Initial position when uncontrolled.
- step: number = 2 - Keyboard step in percent; invalid falls back to 2.
- aspect: string = '16 / 9' - CSS aspect ratio "w / h"; invalid falls back to 16 / 9.
- label: string = 'Image comparison slider' - Accessible name of the slider.
- blurred: boolean - Privacy blur on both images; the labels and the slider stay sharp. v-model:blurred. Wins over `ConfigProvider blurMedia`, true or false; undefined inherits, then false.
- defaultBlurred: boolean - Starting blur when `blurred` is not bound.
- revealable: boolean = false - When blurred, show a button that unblurs, then a toggle that blurs again. The button is an action whose name says what it does next ("Show image", "Hide image"), with a 24px minimum target (44px on coarse pointers) and does not appear while the media was never blurred.
- revealLabel: string = 'Show image' - Name of the reveal button (translate it).
- hideLabel: string = 'Hide image' - Name of the button that blurs again (translate it).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:blurred [value: boolean] - The reveal button changed the blur.
- update:modelValue [value: number] - Position changed by pointer or keyboard.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `before` is set without a `beforeAlt` string, or `after` without an `afterAlt` string. An empty string marks the image decorative.
- Throws a ContractError when `label` is an empty string: the slider needs an accessible name.

Rules:
- Use `blurred` for privacy, not decoration.
- Use `orientation="vertical"` for portrait/tall images or narrow columns; keep horizontal for landscape images.
- Both images must share the same crop/aspect ratio.
- Always set beforeAlt/afterAlt describing the content.
- Do not rely on drag only; the slider is keyboard operable by design.

Accessibility:
- Blur is visual only: alt text and names are unchanged and nothing is hidden from assistive technology; the root gets `data-blurred`. The reveal button is a real button whose name changes with the action (`revealLabel` while blurred, `hideLabel` once shown); it has no `aria-pressed`, because a toggle must not also change its label. Blur is a CSS filter on the media only, so it needs no colour and survives forced-colors mode; its transition runs only under `motion-safe:`.
- The divider handle is role="slider" (tabindex 0) with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext ("40% Before, 60% After") and an aria-label (`label`).
- Keyboard map: ArrowRight/ArrowUp/PageUp add "before" and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown/PageDown remove it (horizontal); vertical follows the arrow (Down/Right/PageDown move the divider down). Shift multiplies the step by 5; PageUp/PageDown always move 5 steps; Home = 0, End = 100.
- Focus is shown as an inset outline around the whole handle and as a ring on the round knob (and, in forced-colors mode, an outline). The handle hit area is 40px wide (a 36px knob) so it exceeds the 24px target size; the page can still scroll over the image on the cross axis (`touch-pan-y` / `touch-pan-x`).
- `size`, `shape`, `tone`, `appearance` and `variant` change looks only. The role, name, value text, keyboard map and alt contract are identical in every combination. In every appearance, focus is an inset 2px outline in the ring colour around the whole handle hit area (also visible in forced-colors mode), plus the ring on the grip when there is one; `appearance="line"` has no grip, so the outline is its only indicator. With `tone` primary or neutral the grip border follows the tone.
- `variant="bar"` is an opaque caption strip (no blur, no translucency) docked along the bottom edge with the labels in physical order (before left, after right) in right-to-left pages too; it is aria-hidden like the chips.
- `aria-orientation` follows `orientation`. Corner labels are decorative (aria-hidden), opaque, and can be hidden with `showLabels`; the slider text always names both sides.
- Provide meaningful beforeAlt/afterAlt: both images stay in the accessibility tree. The divider axis is physical (left/right or top/bottom) and is not mirrored in RTL because the images are not mirrored either. Nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no special handling.

Example: Basic: uncontrolled placeholders
```vue
<BeforeAfter class="max-w-xl" aspect="4 / 3" before-label="Before" after-label="After" />
```

Example: Realistic: images, alt text and v-model
```vue

const after = '/screenshots/after.png'
</script>

  <BeforeAfter v-model="pos" :before="before" :after="after" before-alt="Sample image showing the previous layout" after-alt="Sample image showing the new layout" />
  <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Position: {{ Math.round(pos) }}%</p>
</div>
```



# ImageGrid
group: marketing / Media
Image gallery as a uniform grid, masonry or featured layout that opens a Lightbox on click.

Use for galleries and screenshot collections. `variant` selects the layout: `grid` (uniform tiles, default), `masonry` (CSS columns with natural image heights, so mixed portrait/landscape photos pack tightly) and `featured` (the first image spans 2x2 beside smaller tiles). `gap` sets the spacing, `aspect` the tile ratio (`ratio` still works as a legacy alias) and `shape` the tile corners. Each thumbnail is a button labelled "View image: <alt>" that opens the built-in `Lightbox` at that image (state is internal; listen to `open` if you need to know). Set `lightbox=false` for a static grid. Broken thumbnails fall back to their alt text.

import { ImageGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- images: GridImage[] = [] - `{ src, alt, caption?, thumb? }`. `alt` is required (an empty string marks the image decorative; with `lightbox` a `caption` also counts). `thumb` is a smaller image for the grid.
- variant: 'grid' | 'masonry' | 'featured' = 'grid' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `grid`. Reflected as `data-variant`.
- columns: 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Columns from `sm` upward; invalid falls back to 3. Always 2 on mobile.
- gap: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between tiles (0 / 0.375rem / 0.75rem / 1.5rem); invalid falls back to `md`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Tile corners: `rounded-lg` or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`. There is no circle: tiles are photos with their own aspect ratio, and a circle would crop them into ovals (use `Avatar` for round images).
- aspect: 'square' | 'video' | 'portrait' | 'landscape' | 'auto' - Tile shape (1:1, 16:9, 3:4, 4:3, natural height). Wins over `ratio`; invalid values are ignored. Default `square`, or `auto` for masonry.
- ratio: 'square' | 'video' | 'auto' - Legacy alias of `aspect` kept for compatibility; used when `aspect` is not set. Default `square` (`auto` for masonry).
- lightbox: boolean = true - Open a Lightbox on click.
- viewLabel: string = 'View image' - Prefix of each button's accessible name (localise here).
- blurred: boolean - Privacy blur on every image, also inside the Lightbox. Wins over `ConfigProvider blurMedia`, true or false; undefined inherits, then false. Changing it clears the per-image reveals.
- revealable: boolean = false - Offer a reveal button per image (and inside the Lightbox). Revealing one image leaves the others blurred; a revealed image gets a hide toggle. Buttons are actions whose names say what they do next ("Show image", "Hide image"), with a 24px minimum target (44px on coarse pointers).
- revealLabel: string = 'Show image' - Name of the reveal button (translate it).
- hideLabel: string = 'Hide image' - Name of the button that blurs an image again (translate it).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- reveal [index: number, revealed: boolean] - An image was revealed or blurred again, from the grid or from the Lightbox.
- open [index: number] - A thumbnail was activated.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `images` has no `alt` string (with `lightbox` on, a non-empty `caption` also satisfies it). The message names the first failing index. The internal Lightbox is bound to `open`, so its own contract holds.

Rules:
- Use `blurred` for privacy, not decoration. With `revealable` each image has its own button; the grid-wide `blurred` is the default for all of them.
- Always provide meaningful `alt` (it becomes the button label); never remote placeholder URLs in examples.
- Provide `thumb` for large originals.
- Choose `variant`: grid for uniform screenshots, masonry for mixed-orientation photography, featured to spotlight one hero image among 4-7 others.
- Use `aspect` (not `ratio`) in new code; use `aspect="auto"` only with masonry or when images share a shape.
- Use `shape="square"` for flush galleries; do not try to make tiles circular (use Avatar for round images).
- Do not nest ImageGrid inside a link.

Accessibility:
- Blur is visual only: alt text and names are unchanged and nothing is hidden from assistive technology; the root gets `data-blurred`. The reveal button is a real button whose name changes with the action (`revealLabel` while blurred, `hideLabel` once shown); it has no `aria-pressed`, because a toggle must not also change its label. Blur is a CSS filter on the media only, so it needs no colour and survives forced-colors mode; its transition runs only under `motion-safe:`.
- The root is a native `<ul>` and each tile an `<li>`. With the lightbox on, a tile is a `<button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog">` named "View image: <alt>" (the alt text, else the caption, else the position); its image is decorative so the name is not announced twice. Tiles are at least 44px tall (`min-h-11`) even before the image loads, which keeps lazy images above the 24px target size.
- Keyboard: Tab moves through the thumbnails, Enter or Space opens the Lightbox (see Lightbox: Esc closes, Left/Right arrows and Home/End navigate, focus returns to the thumbnail). With `lightbox=false` the tiles are plain images with their `alt`.
- Masonry fills column by column, so the visual order differs from the DOM and tab order across columns; use it for galleries whose order does not matter.
- `shape` changes the corners only: the tile is still a bordered, named button, so `square` tiles stay visible in forced-colors mode and keep the focus ring.
- Two columns on a 320px screen, `columns` from `sm`; there is no hover zoom, so nothing moves under reduced motion. Tiles have a border (visible in forced-colors mode).

Example: Basic: gallery with lightbox
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const images = [{ src: '/a.jpg', alt: 'Describe what the photo shows' }, ...]
</script>

<ImageGrid :images="images" :columns="3" />
```

Example: Static 16:9 grid
```vue
<ImageGrid :lightbox="false" aspect="video" :columns="2" :images="images" />
```

Example: Grid variant: portrait tiles, large gap
```vue
<ImageGrid variant="grid" aspect="portrait" gap="lg" :columns="4" :images="images" />
```

Example: Masonry variant
```vue
<ImageGrid variant="masonry" :columns="3" gap="sm" :images="images" />
```

Example: Featured variant
```vue
<ImageGrid variant="featured" :columns="3" :images="images" />
```

Example: Tight gallery without gaps
```vue
<ImageGrid gap="none" aspect="landscape" :columns="4" :images="images" class="overflow-hidden rounded-lg" />
```

Example: Shape gallery: rounded, square
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-6">
  <ImageGrid shape="rounded" :columns="3" :images="images" />
  <ImageGrid shape="square" :columns="3" :images="images" />
</div>
```

Example: Square tiles in a featured layout
```vue
<ImageGrid variant="featured" shape="square" gap="sm" :columns="3" :images="images" />
```

Example: Blurred, reveal per image
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const last = ref(null)
</script>

<ImageGrid blurred revealable :images="images" :columns="3" @reveal="(i, on) => (last = { i, on })" />
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground" role="status">{{ last ? 'Image ' + (last.i + 1) + (last.on ? ' revealed' : ' blurred again') : 'All images blurred' }}</p>
```

# Lightbox
group: marketing / Media
Full-screen image viewer dialog with previous/next, Esc, focus containment and scroll lock.

Use to enlarge images from a gallery or screenshot. Controlled with `v-model:open` (and optionally `v-model:index`); it is teleported to `<body>`. Opening moves focus to the close button, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, arrow keys navigate, and focus returns to the opener on close. `ImageGrid` wires this up for you. For arbitrary modal content use the overlays Dialog instead.

import { Lightbox } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- open*: boolean - v-model:open. Required: the viewer never opens itself, so bind it (`false` is fine). Renders nothing when false or when `images` is empty.
- index: number - v-model:index, the visible image; clamped to the valid range.
- images: LightboxImage[] = [] - `{ src, alt, caption? }`. `alt` is required (an empty string marks the image decorative); a non-empty `caption` also satisfies it.
- loop: boolean = true - Wrap around at the ends; false disables prev/next at the ends.
- closeOnBackdrop: boolean = true - Close on backdrop click.
- label: string = 'Image viewer' - Accessible name of the dialog.
- closeLabel: string = 'Close' - aria-label of the close button.
- prevLabel: string = 'Previous image' - aria-label of the previous button.
- nextLabel: string = 'Next image' - aria-label of the next button.
- blurred: boolean - Privacy blur on the open image. v-model:blurred. Wins over `ConfigProvider blurMedia`, true or false; undefined inherits, then false. The reveal button sits in the header, never over the picture.
- defaultBlurred: boolean - Starting blur when `blurred` is not bound.
- revealable: boolean = false - When blurred, show a button that unblurs, then a toggle that blurs again. The button is an action whose name says what it does next ("Show image", "Hide image"), with a 24px minimum target (44px on coarse pointers) and does not appear while the media was never blurred.
- revealLabel: string = 'Show image' - Name of the reveal button (translate it).
- hideLabel: string = 'Hide image' - Name of the button that blurs again (translate it).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the overlay; wins over internal classes.

Events:
- update:blurred [value: boolean] - The reveal button changed the blur.
- update:open [open: boolean] - Requested open state change.
- update:index [index: number] - Visible image changed.
- close - Closed by Esc, close button or backdrop.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the `open` prop is not provided (undefined). `false` is fine: bind `v-model:open`.
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `images` has no `alt` string and no non-empty `caption`. The message names the first failing index.

Rules:
- Use `blurred` for privacy, not decoration. `revealable` puts the button in the header; ImageGrid passes its own blur state down.
- Always bind `v-model:open`; the component never opens itself.
- Supply `alt` for each image.
- Prefer ImageGrid unless you need a custom trigger.

Accessibility:
- Blur is visual only: alt text and names are unchanged and nothing is hidden from assistive technology; the root gets `data-blurred`. The reveal button is a real button whose name changes with the action (`revealLabel` while blurred, `hideLabel` once shown); it has no `aria-pressed`, because a toggle must not also change its label. Blur is a CSS filter on the media only, so it needs no colour and survives forced-colors mode; its transition runs only under `motion-safe:`.
- role="dialog" aria-modal="true" with an aria-label (`label`); focus moves to Close on open and is restored to the opener on close.
- Keyboard map: Tab/Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog (no trap escape); Escape closes; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move to the previous/next image (swapped in RTL); Home/End jump to the first/last image. Close, previous and next are real buttons with accessible names (`closeLabel`, `prevLabel`, `nextLabel`). At the ends with `loop=false` they use aria-disabled so a focused button keeps focus.
- The counter ("2 / 5") is a polite live region. Body scroll is locked while open and restored afterwards (including on unmount).
- Layout: the overlay is `h-dvh`, controls sit in header and footer bars (never over the picture), the image shrinks to the space left, so nothing is clipped at 320px or behind mobile browser bars. Controls are 40px (48px on coarse pointers) and the chevrons mirror in RTL. Nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no special handling.
- Give every image meaningful `alt` (it falls back to the caption).

Example: Basic
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
const images = [{ src: '/a.jpg', alt: 'A', caption: 'First' }, ...]
</script>

<Button @click="open = true">Open viewer</Button>
<Lightbox v-model:open="open" :images="images" />
```

Example: Controlled index, no looping
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
const index = ref(2)
</script>

<Button variant="outline" @click="open = true">Start at third</Button>
<Lightbox v-model:open="open" v-model:index="index" :loop="false" :images="images" />
```

Example: Blurred, revealable
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const open = ref(false)
</script>

<Button variant="outline" @click="open = true">Open blurred viewer</Button>
<Lightbox v-model:open="open" revealable default-blurred :images="images" />
```

# Marquee
group: marketing / Motion
Infinite CSS ticker (horizontal or vertical) for logos or short text, paused on hover and focus.

Use for decorative, repeating strips: partner names, tech stack, announcements. Content is duplicated once (the copy is aria-hidden) and translated with a pure CSS animation. `direction` is `left`, `right` (horizontal) or `up`, `down` (vertical, needs a height: `h-64` by default, override with `class`). A visible pause/resume button (`pausable`, on by default) lets anyone stop it (WCAG 2.2.2); it also pauses on hover and focus-within and fades at the edges (`fade`). For users who prefer reduced motion it stops animating, hides the duplicate and the button, and becomes a focusable, named, manually scrollable row. Do not use for important content that must be read; a moving target fails many users, so use `LogoCloud` for static display.

import { Marquee } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: string[] = [] - Simple text items (ignored when the default slot is used).
- duration: number = 30 - Seconds per loop; invalid or <= 0 is ignored (then `speed` applies, else 30); clamped to 0.1-86400. Wins over `speed`.
- speed: 'slow' | 'normal' | 'fast' - Preset for `duration`: slow = 60s, normal = 30s, fast = 15s per loop. Alias for quick tuning; an explicit valid `duration` always wins. Unknown values are ignored.
- direction: 'left' | 'right' | 'up' | 'down' = 'left' - Scroll direction. `up`/`down` make a vertical strip (set its height via `class`, default `h-64`). Unknown values fall back to `left`.
- pauseOnHover: boolean = true - Pause while hovered or focused within.
- gap: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between items (0 / 1 / 2 / 3 rem); unknown values fall back to `md`.
- fade: boolean = true - Fade both ends of the strip with a CSS mask (horizontal or vertical to match the axis).
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size of `items` (text-sm / text-lg / text-2xl). Slot content is not affected. Unknown values fall back to `md`. The resolved value is exposed as `data-size` on the root, also when slot content replaces `items`.
- label: string - Optional accessible name; sets role="group".
- pausable: boolean = true - Render the pause/resume button below the strip. Keep it on: moving content that lasts longer than 5 seconds needs a pause mechanism (WCAG 2.2.2).
- paused: boolean - `v-model:paused`. Leave undefined for uncontrolled use.
- pauseLabel: string = 'Pause scrolling' - Button text while the strip moves (localise here).
- playLabel: string = 'Resume scrolling' - Button text while the strip is paused.
- scrollLabel: string = 'Scrollable content' - Accessible name of the strip when it becomes a scrollable row under prefers-reduced-motion.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the root; wins over internal classes (e.g. `h-96` for vertical strips).

Slots:
- default - Rich items (logos, badges). Rendered twice; do not attach unique ids inside.

Events:
- update:paused [paused: boolean] - The pause button was used.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `pausable` is false while the strip moves (no reduced-motion preference, items present) and `paused` is not bound to your own control (WCAG 2.2.2).

Rules:
- Use only for decorative strips.
- Prefer `speed` (slow/normal/fast) for tuning; use `duration` only for an exact loop time.
- Use `direction="up"`/`"down"` only in a container with a fixed height (set `class="h-48"` etc.). Horizontal is the default for logo and tech-stack rows.
- Set `:fade="false"` when the strip sits edge-to-edge or on a tinted section.
- No interactive elements with unique ids in the slot (it renders twice).
- Give a `label` if the strip carries meaning.
- Keep `pausable` on; WCAG 2.2.2 requires a way to stop moving content.

Accessibility:
- Pause mechanism (WCAG 2.2.2): a real "Pause scrolling" / "Resume scrolling" button (Tab to it, Enter or Space) stops and restarts the animation; the label changes with the state. It is at least 24px tall and 44px on coarse pointers, sits outside the faded edges and has the shared focus ring. The strip also pauses on hover and while focus is inside it.
- prefers-reduced-motion: the animation never runs, the duplicate and the button are hidden, and the strip becomes a scrollable row (or column) that is focusable (`tabindex="0"`), named (`scrollLabel`) and operable with the arrow keys.
- The duplicate copy is aria-hidden so content is announced once; `label` names the group.
- Treat as decorative: do not place the only copy of critical information here. Gaps use logical padding so RTL works; the strip clips inside its own box, so 320px screens never scroll sideways.

Example: Basic: text items
```vue
<Marquee :items="['Vue 3', 'Tailwind 4', 'TypeScript', 'Vitest', 'Pinia']" />
```

Example: Realistic: slot content, reversed and slower
```vue
<Marquee direction="right" :duration="45" label="Technologies">
  <Badge variant="secondary">Accessible</Badge>
  <Badge variant="secondary">Themeable</Badge>
  <Badge variant="secondary">Typed</Badge>
</Marquee>
```

Example: Left direction with speed preset
```vue
<Marquee speed="fast" :items="['Typed', 'Tested', 'Themeable', 'Accessible']" />
```

Example: Right direction without edge fade
```vue
<Marquee direction="right" :fade="false" gap="lg" size="lg" :items="['Alpha', 'Beta', 'Gamma', 'Delta']" />
```

Example: Vertical: up
```vue
<Marquee direction="up" class="h-40 max-w-xs" size="sm" gap="sm" :items="['First sample item', 'Second sample item', 'Third sample item', 'Fourth sample item']" />
```

Example: Vertical: down, no pause on hover
```vue
<Marquee direction="down" :pause-on-hover="false" :duration="20" class="h-48 max-w-xs" size="sm" gap="sm" :items="['One sample item', 'Two sample item', 'Three sample item', 'Four sample item']" />
```

Example: Custom duration beats speed
```vue
<Marquee speed="slow" :duration="10" :items="['Quick', 'Brown', 'Fox']" />
```

# SectionReveal
group: marketing / Motion
Opt-in wrapper that fades its content in (rising, dropping or sliding sideways) when scrolled into view. Does nothing unless `enabled`.

Off by default: without `enabled` it renders a plain element, with no classes, no observer and no hidden state. Turn it on for at most one orchestrated moment on a page (for example the first below-the-fold section), never on every section, because the same fade-up on every block is a stock look. When enabled it uses IntersectionObserver. Content is visible by default for server rendering, no-JS and browsers without IntersectionObserver; it is hidden only after mount, and only when it starts below the viewport. Users who prefer reduced motion never see the hidden state. Use `delay` to stagger siblings. Do not wrap above-the-fold content. `effect`, `distance` and `speed` only change the hidden state and the transition length: only `opacity` and `translate` animate, so the box never moves in the layout. A sideways effect moves the wrapper itself, so put it inside a container that clips horizontally (`overflow-x-clip`, or a `Container` with side padding at least as large as `distance`) when it spans the full viewport width, otherwise the hidden state can add a horizontal scrollbar.

import { SectionReveal } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- enabled: boolean = false - Turn the reveal on. When false the component is a plain wrapper (no-op).
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Element or component to render.
- once: boolean = true - Reveal once; false re-hides when scrolled out.
- threshold: number = 0.15 - Visible fraction (0-1) that triggers the reveal; invalid falls back to 0.15.
- rootMargin: string = '0px 0px -8% 0px' - IntersectionObserver rootMargin.
- delay: number = 0 - transition-delay in ms for staggering; invalid falls back to 0.
- effect: 'fade-up' | 'fade' | 'fade-down' | 'slide-left' | 'slide-right' = 'fade-up' - `fade-up` fades in while rising, `fade-down` while dropping, `fade` only fades, `slide-left` and `slide-right` fade in from the left or right. The sides are physical and are not mirrored in right-to-left pages. Unknown values fall back to `fade-up`. Reflected as `data-effect` while enabled.
- distance: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - How far the hidden state is offset: 0.5rem, 1rem or 2rem. Ignored by `fade`. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-distance` while enabled.
- speed: 'fast' | 'normal' | 'slow' = 'normal' - Transition length: 300ms, 700ms or 1000ms. Unknown values fall back to `normal`. Reflected as `data-speed` while enabled.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Content to reveal.

Events:
- reveal - Content became visible (each time when `once` is false). Never emitted while `enabled` is false.

Rules:
- Default is a no-op. Add `enabled` for one orchestrated moment, not on every section.
- Never wrap the Hero or other above-the-fold content.
- Keep the whole moment short: `duration-150` to `duration-300` via `class`, and `delay` steps of 40 to 100ms, not long chains.
- Prefer `effect="fade"` for large containers to avoid layout-looking jumps.
- Put `slide-left` and `slide-right` inside an `overflow-x-clip` container; keep `distance` at `sm` or `md` and `speed` at `fast` or `normal` for a calm page.

Accessibility:
- The new effects change only `opacity` and `translate`; text is never scaled or rotated, so it stays readable at 200% zoom, and nothing moves in the layout. Sideways effects can extend past the right edge while hidden: wrap them in `overflow-x-clip` so no horizontal scrollbar appears at 320px.
- Content is never removed from the accessibility tree or `display`-hidden, only made transparent, so assistive technology reads it in order. Without JavaScript or IntersectionObserver it stays fully visible.
- prefers-reduced-motion: content is shown immediately and no observer is created; transitions also carry `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- No focusable element is moved or hidden by the transition, and the wrapper adds no role or tab stop.

Example: Default (no-op)
```vue
<SectionReveal><p class="rounded-lg border p-6">Rendered as is: no animation, no hidden state.</p></SectionReveal>
```

Example: Enabled
```vue
<SectionReveal enabled><p class="rounded-lg border p-6">I fade in when I scroll into view.</p></SectionReveal>
```

Example: One staggered moment
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
  <SectionReveal v-for="(n, i) in [1, 2, 3]" :key="n" enabled :delay="i * 40" effect="fade" class="duration-150">
    <div class="rounded-lg border p-6">Sample card {{ n }}</div>
  </SectionReveal>
</div>
```

Example: Effect gallery: fade-up, fade-down, fade, slide-left, slide-right
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 overflow-x-clip sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="fade-up"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">fade-up (default)</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="fade-down"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">fade-down</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="fade"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">fade</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="slide-left"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">slide-left</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="slide-right"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">slide-right</div></SectionReveal>
</div>
```

Example: Distance gallery: sm, md, lg
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 overflow-x-clip sm:grid-cols-3">
  <SectionReveal enabled distance="sm"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">distance sm</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled distance="md"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">distance md</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled distance="lg"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">distance lg</div></SectionReveal>
</div>
```

Example: Speed gallery: fast, normal, slow
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 overflow-x-clip sm:grid-cols-3">
  <SectionReveal enabled speed="fast"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">speed fast</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled speed="normal"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">speed normal</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled speed="slow"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">speed slow</div></SectionReveal>
</div>
```

Example: Slide in from the sides
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 overflow-x-clip sm:grid-cols-2">
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="slide-left" speed="fast"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">Sample column that enters from the left</div></SectionReveal>
  <SectionReveal enabled effect="slide-right" speed="fast" :delay="60"><div class="rounded-lg border p-6">Sample column that enters from the right</div></SectionReveal>
</div>
```
