# CookieConsent
group: marketing / Notices
Cookie notice with per-category toggles and equally prominent accept and reject buttons; it stores nothing and emits `change`.

Presentational consent notice. It shows a title, an explanation, a policy link (`policy` slot) and one toggle per category. Necessary categories are on, locked and labelled "Always on"; every optional category starts off. "Reject all" and "Accept all" are the same button: same variant, size, weight and width, rejecting comes first in the reading order, and neither needs a second step. "Save choices" sends the toggles as they are. The component remembers nothing: handle `change`, store the result yourself (the optional `readConsent` / `writeConsent` / `clearConsent` helpers do that in `localStorage` and are safe on the server) and load scripts only for categories that are `true`. `banner` is a full-width bar (categories sit behind "Choose categories"; place it with `class`, for example `fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0`), `inline` is a card with the categories always visible, and `modal` is a dialog with a focus trap. In the modal, Escape and the close button hide it and emit `dismiss` without a choice, and a click outside does nothing. Wording is plain: no guilt copy, no pre-ticked boxes, no hidden reject.

import { CookieConsent } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'banner' | 'modal' | 'inline' = 'banner' - Look. `banner`: full-width bar with the categories behind a button. `inline`: bordered card with all categories shown. `modal`: dialog with a focus trap and a close button. Unknown values fall back to `banner`.
- categories: ConsentCategory[] = [] - Entries `{ id, label, description?, necessary? }`. Entries without a non-blank string `id` and repeated ids are dropped; a missing label falls back to the id. With no categories only the three-choice notice is shown (no toggles, no "Save choices").
- modelValue: Record<string, boolean> - Toggle state by id (`v-model`). Only `true` turns an optional category on. A necessary category stays on whatever this holds. Unknown keys are ignored.
- open: boolean - Whether the notice is shown (`v-model:open`). Omit it and the component hides itself after a choice or a dismissal.
- title: string = 'Cookie preferences' - Heading text and accessible name of the region or dialog. Required: an empty title needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The `title` slot replaces it.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Heading level of the title. Invalid values fall back to 2.
- description: string = 'We use cookies to run this site. Optional categories stay off until you turn them on.' - Explanation under the title. The `description` slot replaces it.
- acceptLabel: string = 'Accept all' - Text of the accept button.
- rejectLabel: string = 'Reject all' - Text of the reject button.
- saveLabel: string = 'Save choices' - Text of the button that sends the current toggles. Shown only while the categories are visible.
- manageLabel: string = 'Choose categories' - Text of the button that shows and hides the categories in the `banner` variant (aria-expanded).
- alwaysOnLabel: string = 'Always on' - Text added to the description of a necessary category, so the locked state is not only a dimmed switch.
- categoriesLabel: string = 'Cookie categories' - Accessible name of the list of categories.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes. Attributes fall through to the root (the section, or the dialog content in `modal`).

Slots:
- title - Rich title content; replaces the `title` prop.
- description - Rich explanation; replaces the `description` prop.
- policy - Link to the cookie or privacy policy, shown under the explanation. The component renders no link of its own.

Events:
- change [choice: { action: "accept-all" | "reject-all" | "save", categories: Record<string, boolean> }] - The user pressed Accept all, Reject all or Save choices. `categories` has one boolean per id and necessary ones are always `true`. Never emitted by Escape or the close button.
- update:modelValue [value: Record<string, boolean>] - A toggle moved, or a button set the state.
- update:open [value: boolean] - Emitted with `false` after a choice or a dismissal.
- dismiss - `modal` only: closed with Escape or the close button, without a choice.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is no accessible name: an empty `title` (and no `title` slot) without `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. In `modal` the Dialog also throws when no title is rendered.

Rules:
- The component stores nothing: handle `@change`, persist the result (`writeConsent` helps) and only load scripts for categories whose value is `true`.
- Never pre-tick an optional category, never style accept and reject differently, never hide reject behind a second screen, and never write guilt copy; the defaults already avoid all four.
- Show it again only when no saved choice exists, or when the user opens a "Cookie settings" link (use `v-model:open`).
- Mark categories `necessary: true` only for cookies the site cannot work without; those cannot be switched off.
- Give a policy link through the `policy` slot; the component does not know your URL.
- Use `banner` with a fixed-position `class` for the first visit, `inline` on a settings page and `modal` when the choice must interrupt.

Accessibility:
- The banner and the inline card are a `section` named by the title (`aria-labelledby`), so they are a region landmark: give each one on a page a different title (or `aria-label`). The modal is a reka Dialog: focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes it and focus returns to what had it before. The dialog title is required (the Dialog contract).
- Every toggle is a switch with a visible label and a description linked with `aria-describedby`. A necessary category is a disabled switch that is on; the words "Always on" in its description carry the locked state, so it is not conveyed by dimming alone.
- Accept all and Reject all share one variant, size and class set, so they look and behave the same. Both are reachable with Tab in a fixed order (reject, accept, save, choose categories). The categories button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- Buttons are at least 36px high and 44px on touch pointers, stack to full width below `sm` and wrap, so the notice reflows at 320px. Long labels and descriptions wrap (`break-words`). Logical properties keep it correct in right-to-left layouts.
- The modal does not close on an outside click, so a stray tap is never treated as a decision; Escape and the close button emit `dismiss` and never `change`.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const last = ref('No choice yet')
const categories = [
  { id: 'necessary', label: 'Strictly necessary', description: 'Keeps you signed in and remembers this choice.', necessary: true },
  { id: 'analytics', label: 'Analytics', description: 'Counts visits so the site owner can see which pages are read.' },
  { id: 'preferences', label: 'Preferences', description: 'Remembers language and layout settings.' },
]
function onChange(choice) {
  // choice: { action: 'accept-all' | 'reject-all' | 'save', categories: { necessary: true, analytics: false, ... } }
  last.value = choice.action
}
</script>

<CookieConsent title="Cookie notice without categories" class="max-w-3xl" @change="onChange" />
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ last }}</p>
```

Example: Banner variant
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const last = ref('No choice yet')
const categories = [
  { id: 'necessary', label: 'Strictly necessary', description: 'Keeps you signed in and remembers this choice.', necessary: true },
  { id: 'analytics', label: 'Analytics', description: 'Counts visits so the site owner can see which pages are read.' },
  { id: 'preferences', label: 'Preferences', description: 'Remembers language and layout settings.' },
]
function onChange(choice) {
  // choice: { action: 'accept-all' | 'reject-all' | 'save', categories: { necessary: true, analytics: false, ... } }
  last.value = choice.action
}
</script>

<CookieConsent variant="banner" title="Cookie notice as a banner" :categories="categories" @change="onChange">
  <template #policy><a href="/cookies" class="underline underline-offset-4">Cookie policy</a></template>
</CookieConsent>
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">{{ last }}</p>
```

# ComparisonTable
group: marketing / Pricing
Generic feature matrix: a real table of columns x features with check, cross, text and empty cells, grouping, a highlighted column and sticky options.

Use to compare plans, products or editions feature by feature. `columns` define the headers (one may be `highlighted`), `rows` are features (`{ label, description?, values[] }`) or `{ group }` headings that open a new section. Cell values: `true` = check, `false` = cross, text/number = shown as-is, `null`/`undefined`/missing/empty = dash. Every check and cross carries screen-reader text. The table scrolls horizontally inside a focusable region on small screens (`stickyFirstColumn` is on by default, so feature names stay visible; pass `false` to let the whole table scroll). `stickyHeader` keeps the header visible while the region scrolls vertically, so give the root a max height (`class="max-h-96"`). For plan headers with prices and CTAs use `PricingTable` (built on this component). For a handful of plans with long feature lists use `PricingGrid` instead.

import { ComparisonTable } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- columns: ComparisonColumn[] = [] - Headers: `{ key?, title, subtitle?, badge?, highlighted? }`. Malformed entries are skipped.
- rows: ComparisonRow[] = [] - Feature rows `{ label, description?, values: (boolean | string | number | null | undefined)[] }` and group headings `{ group: string }`. Malformed entries are skipped; `values` may be shorter than `columns`.
- variant: 'default' | 'striped' | 'bordered' | 'minimal' = 'default' - `default` framed, `striped` alternating row shading, `bordered` borders on every cell, `minimal` no outer frame. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Cell density. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- caption: string - Required (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`). Accessible name: used for the sr-only `<caption>` and the `aria-label` of the scroll region. Give each table on a page a different caption: identical region names fail the landmark-unique rule.
- stickyHeader: boolean = false - Pin the header row while the region scrolls vertically (needs a max height on the root).
- stickyFirstColumn: boolean = true - Pin the feature-name column while the region scrolls horizontally. On by default so row labels never scroll out of view; pass `false` to let the whole table scroll.
- cornerLabel: string = 'Features' - Text of the top-left header cell.
- includedLabel: string = 'Included' - Screen-reader text for a check.
- excludedLabel: string = 'Not included' - Screen-reader text for a cross.
- unavailableLabel: string = 'Not available' - Screen-reader text for an empty cell.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the scroll region (root).

Slots:
- corner - Replaces the top-left header cell content.
- column-header ({ column: ComparisonColumn, index: number }) - Replaces the content of a column header.
- column-footer ({ column: ComparisonColumn, index: number }) - Adds a footer row; one cell per column (e.g. CTA buttons).
- cell ({ value, row, column, rowIndex, columnIndex }) - Replaces the default check/cross/text rendering of a cell.
- row-label ({ row: ComparisonFeature }) - Replaces the feature name cell content.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the table has no name: set `caption` (also the sr-only `<caption>`), `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Throws a ContractError when a column has an empty `title` and no `column-header` slot replaces the header (the first one is named by index).

Rules:
- One value per column, in column order; use `true`/`false` for yes/no and strings for specifics ("10 GB").
- Mark at most one column `highlighted`, and give it a `badge`.
- Use `{ group: "..." }` rows to section long matrices instead of several tables.
- Use `stickyHeader` only with a max-height class on the root; `stickyFirstColumn` is on by default, turn it off only for two- or three-column tables with short labels.
- Pick `striped` for long tables, `bordered` for spec sheets, `minimal` on plain pages, `default` otherwise.
- For priced plans with CTAs use PricingTable; do not rebuild headers by hand.

Accessibility:
- A real `<table>` with `<caption>` (sr-only), `scope="col"` column headers, `scope="row"` feature headers and `scope="rowgroup"` group headings (each group is its own `<tbody>`).
- Checks, crosses and dashes are icons with screen-reader text ("Included", "Not included", "Not available"); localise with the label props.
- The scroll region has `role="region"`, an accessible name (`caption`, make it unique per page) and `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys; focus shows a ring (an outline in forced-colors mode).
- The highlighted column is marked with `data-highlighted` and an opaque tinted header; add a `badge` so the emphasis is not colour-only.
- Reflow: the table keeps a 36rem minimum width and scrolls horizontally inside its own region at 320px, so the page never scrolls sideways; `stickyFirstColumn` (on by default) keeps feature names visible. Alignment uses logical properties (`text-start`, `start-0`) so RTL works.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [{ title: 'Plan A' }, { title: 'Plan B', highlighted: true }]
const rows = [{ label: 'Projects', values: ['1', '10'] }, { label: 'SSO', values: [false, true] }]
</script>

<ComparisonTable caption="Minimal comparison" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Realistic: grouped features with a highlighted plan
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Grouped feature comparison" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Variant: default
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Variant: default" variant="default" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Variant: striped
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Variant: striped" variant="striped" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Variant: bordered
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Variant: bordered" variant="bordered" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Variant: minimal
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Variant: minimal" variant="minimal" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Size: sm
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Size: sm" size="sm" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Size: lg
```vue
<ComparisonTable caption="Size: lg" size="lg" :columns="columns" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Sticky header
```vue

```

Example: Sticky first column (default)
```vue

```

Example: Footer row (column-footer slot)
```vue

  <template #column-footer="{ column }"><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Choose {{ column.title }}</Button></template>
</ComparisonTable>
```

Example: Custom cells (cell slot) and localised labels
```vue

  <template #cell="{ value }"><Badge v-if="typeof value === 'string'" variant="secondary">{{ value }}</Badge><template v-else>{{ value === true ? 'Ja' : value === false ? 'Nein' : '-' }}</template></template>
</ComparisonTable>
```

# PricingCard
group: marketing / Pricing
Single pricing plan: name, monthly/yearly price, feature checklist, badge and CTA slot, in five variants.

Use one card per plan, usually inside `PricingGrid`. `variant` picks the look: `default`, `highlighted` (recommended plan; same as `highlighted`), `outline` (transparent, 2px border), `minimal` (no frame, for plan lists on plain backgrounds) and `compact` (smaller padding and type, for sidebars or 4+ plans). Features are strings or `{ label, included }`; excluded features get an X icon, strike-through and a screen-reader "Not included" note. Provide prices already formatted ("Free", "Custom" or your own currency format). For yearly billing give `yearlyPrice` (+ optional `yearlyPeriod`, `yearlyNote`) and set `billing="yearly"`; PricingGrid and PricingTable do that from their billing toggle. Plans without `yearlyPrice` (Free, Custom) keep `price` in both modes.

import { PricingCard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- name: string - Plan name. Required unless the `name` slot is used.
- price: string | number - Displayed (monthly / default) price text, formatted by you ("$XX" in these samples). Required unless the `price` slot is used: use text such as "Free" or "Custom" when there is no number. `0` is shown.
- period: string - Suffix such as "/month".
- yearlyPrice: string | number - Price shown instead of `price` while `billing` is `yearly`. Plans without it keep `price`.
- yearlyPeriod: string - Suffix for the yearly price (e.g. "/month, billed yearly" or "/year"). Falls back to `period`.
- yearlyNote: string - Small note under the price while the yearly price is shown (e.g. "Billed yearly").
- billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' = 'monthly' - Which price to display. Unknown values mean `monthly`. Exposed as `data-billing` on the price block.
- description: string - One-line plan summary.
- features: (string | { label: string; included?: boolean })[] = [] - Checklist entries. Empty/malformed entries are skipped.
- highlighted: boolean = false - Emphasise as the recommended plan; works with every variant. Equivalent to `variant="highlighted"`.
- variant: 'default' | 'highlighted' | 'outline' | 'minimal' | 'compact' = 'default' - Visual style. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Exposed as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding, gap and price scale of every variant; `md` is the original spacing. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - `square` removes the corner radius. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- badge: string - Small badge above the name.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of the plan name.
- excludedLabel: string = 'Not included' - Screen-reader text for excluded features (localise here).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- name - Replaces the plan name text.
- price ({ price: string | number | undefined, period: string | undefined, billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly', yearly: boolean }) - Replaces the whole price line (amount + period + note).
- default - Extra content between features and the CTA.
- cta - Call-to-action button(s), pinned to the bottom of the card.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `name` is empty and the `name` slot is not used.
- Throws a ContractError when `price` is empty (undefined, an empty string, NaN) and the `price` slot is not used. `0` and text such as "Free" are valid.

Rules:
- Provide pre-formatted price strings.
- One `highlighted` plan per grid.
- Put exactly one Button per card in the `cta` slot; use the default variant only on the highlighted plan.
- For monthly/yearly pricing set `price` + `yearlyPrice` on each plan and let PricingGrid/PricingTable own the `billing` state; do not set `billing` on cards inside a grid.
- Use `outline` on coloured backgrounds, `compact` for 4+ plans or narrow columns, `minimal` only on plain backgrounds.
- Free/Custom plans: omit `yearlyPrice` so they stay unchanged.

Accessibility:
- Rendered as an `<article>` with a heading (`level`, default 3: set it to follow the section heading, e.g. `:level="2"` under an h1); features are a `<ul>`; excluded items are announced as "Not included" and the check/cross icons are decorative.
- Highlighting is not conveyed by colour alone: it uses a solid border (kept in forced-colors mode) and you should add `badge` text for the recommended plan. Text on the card uses card tokens, so contrast holds in light and dark mode.
- The card has no interactive parts of its own; Tab reaches the buttons you put in `cta`. Inside PricingGrid the card is wrapped in an `<li>`; do not put `role="listitem"` on it (an article cannot take that role).
- Variants only change styling, never the DOM order or semantics. The card stacks to one column at 320px and nothing animates.

Example: Basic plan
```vue
<PricingCard class="max-w-sm" name="Sample plan" price="$XX" period="/month" description="One line on who the plan is for" :features="['First sample feature', 'Second sample feature']">
  <template #cta><Button variant="outline">Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

Example: Highlighted with excluded features
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const features = ['First sample feature', 'Second sample feature', { label: 'Excluded sample feature', included: false }]
</script>

<PricingCard class="max-w-sm" highlighted badge="Recommended" name="Sample plan" price="$XX" period="/month" :features="features">
  <template #cta><Button>Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

Example: Variant: default
```vue
<PricingCard class="max-w-sm" variant="default" name="Sample plan" price="$XX" period="/month" description="One line on who the plan is for" :features="['First sample feature', 'Second sample feature', { label: 'Excluded sample feature', included: false }]">
  <template #cta><Button variant="outline">Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

Example: Variant: highlighted
```vue

  <template #cta><Button>Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

Example: Variant: outline
```vue

  <template #cta><Button variant="outline">Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

```vue
  <template #cta><Button variant="outline">Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

```vue
  <template #cta><Button variant="outline">Choose this plan</Button></template>
</PricingCard>
```

Example: Sizes and square corners
```vue

  <PricingCard size="sm" name="Small plan" price="$XX" period="/month" :features="['Sample feature']" />
  <PricingCard size="md" name="Medium plan" price="$XX" period="/month" :features="['Sample feature']" />
  <PricingCard size="lg" shape="square" name="Large square plan" price="$XX" period="/month" :features="['Sample feature']" />

```

Example: Yearly price (billing="yearly")
```vue
<div class="grid max-w-2xl gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <PricingCard name="Sample plan, monthly" price="$XX" period="/month" yearly-price="$YY" yearly-period="/month, billed yearly" yearly-note="Billed yearly" billing="monthly" />
  <PricingCard name="Sample plan, yearly" price="$XX" period="/month" yearly-price="$YY" yearly-period="/month, billed yearly" yearly-note="Billed yearly" billing="yearly" />
</div>
```

Example: Custom price slot
```vue

  <template #price="{ price, yearly }"><span class="text-3xl font-bold">{{ price }}</span><span v-if="yearly" class="text-xs text-muted-foreground">billed yearly</span></template>
</PricingCard>
```

# PricingGrid
group: marketing / Pricing
Responsive grid of PricingCards from a plans array, with a per-plan CTA slot and an optional monthly/yearly billing toggle.

Use to lay out 1-4 plans side by side. Pass `plans` (PricingCard props) and a scoped `cta` slot, or put your own `PricingCard`s in the default slot. When at least one plan has a `yearlyPrice` a billing toggle appears above the grid (force it with `showToggle`); the selected `billing` is passed to every generated card so prices switch together. `v-model:billing` controls the state; without it the grid keeps its own state (`defaultBilling` sets the start value). `variant` is passed to generated cards (a plan's own `variant` wins). When the toggle is visible the root is a wrapper (`pricing-grid`) and the list element is the inner `pricing-grid-items`. For a feature-by-plan matrix use `PricingTable`.

import { PricingGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- plans: PricingPlan[] = [] - Plan objects with the same fields as PricingCard props (name, price, period, yearlyPrice, yearlyPeriod, yearlyNote, description, features, highlighted, variant, badge, level, excludedLabel). `billing` is controlled by the grid.
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Columns on large screens; invalid falls back to 3.
- billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' - `v-model:billing`. Leave undefined for uncontrolled use. Unknown values mean `monthly`.
- defaultBilling: 'monthly' | 'yearly' = 'monthly' - Initial period when uncontrolled.
- showToggle: boolean - Force the toggle on or off. Default (unset): visible when at least one plan has a `yearlyPrice`.
- yearlyDiscountLabel: string - Badge next to the yearly option. State a fact you can back up.
- monthlyLabel: string = 'Monthly' - Label of the monthly option.
- yearlyLabel: string = 'Yearly' - Label of the yearly option.
- billingLabel: string = 'Billing period' - Accessible name of the toggle group.
- variant: 'default' | 'highlighted' | 'outline' | 'minimal' | 'compact' - PricingCard variant for generated cards; a plan's own `variant` wins. Unknown values fall back to `default`. The resolved value is exposed as `data-variant` on the root, also when the cards come from the slot.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - PricingCard `size` for generated cards (a plan's own `size` wins). Exposed as `data-size`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - PricingCard `shape` for generated cards (a plan's own `shape` wins). Exposed as `data-shape`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; lands on the root (the wrapper when the toggle is visible).

Slots:
- default ({ billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' }) - Custom cards; replaces `plans` rendering. Receives the active billing so you can pass it to your cards.
- cta ({ plan: PricingPlan, index: number, billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' }) - Per-plan call to action when using `plans`.

Events:
- update:billing [value: 'monthly' | 'yearly'] - The user picked a different billing period (not emitted when the active option is clicked again).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `plans` is empty and no cards are placed in the default slot.
- Throws a ContractError when `billing` or `defaultBilling` is not `monthly` or `yearly`.
- Throws a ContractError when `billing` is set, the toggle is visible and nothing listens to `update:billing` (use `v-model:billing`).
- Throws a ContractError when the visible toggle has an empty `billingLabel`, `monthlyLabel` or `yearlyLabel`.

Rules:
- Use `plans` + `cta` slot for the common case.
- Exactly one plan should be `highlighted`.
- Use columns equal to the number of plans (max 4).
- For monthly/yearly pricing add `yearlyPrice` to paid plans; the toggle appears by itself. Use `v-model:billing` only if something else on the page needs the value.
- Do not pass `billing` inside `plans`; the grid owns it.
- With custom default-slot cards use the slot prop `billing` to pass the period to your PricingCards; do not add role="listitem" to them.

Accessibility:
- With `plans` the plans form a native `<ul>` of `<li>` elements, each containing an `<article>` PricingCard (a role on the article itself is not allowed). With the default slot (or no plans) the container is a plain `<div>`: put any markup in it.
- The toggle is a `radiogroup` (named by `billingLabel`) with two `radio` buttons; one is in the tab order (roving tabindex); Arrow keys change and focus the option, Home/End jump to monthly/yearly. Options are at least 24px tall (44px on coarse pointers) and the checked option keeps a border, so the state shows in forced-colors mode as well as by colour.
- The discount badge is part of the yearly option text, so it is announced with it; it uses the `success` / `success-foreground` token pair so the 12px text keeps 4.5:1 contrast in light and dark mode.
- One column at 320px, two from `md`, then `columns`; cards stretch to equal height. Use `level` so plan names continue the page heading outline.

Example: From plans
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const plans = [{ name: 'Sample plan A', price: 'Free', features: ['First sample feature'] }, ...]
</script>

<PricingGrid :plans="plans">
  <template #cta="{ plan }"><Button :variant="plan.highlighted ? 'default' : 'outline'">Choose {{ plan.name }}</Button></template>
</PricingGrid>
```

Example: Two custom cards
```vue
<PricingGrid :columns="2">
  <PricingCard name="Sample monthly plan" price="$XX" period="/mo" :features="['First sample feature']"><template #cta><Button variant="outline">Pick monthly</Button></template></PricingCard>
  <PricingCard name="Sample yearly plan" price="$YY" period="/yr" highlighted badge="Recommended" :features="['First sample feature']"><template #cta><Button>Pick yearly</Button></template></PricingCard>
</PricingGrid>
```

Example: Billing toggle (uncontrolled)
```vue
<PricingGrid :plans="plans" yearly-discount-label="Yearly saves money">
  <template #cta="{ plan }"><Button :variant="plan.highlighted ? 'default' : 'outline'">Choose {{ plan.name }}</Button></template>
</PricingGrid>
```

Example: Billing toggle with v-model:billing
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const billing = ref('yearly')
</script>

<PricingGrid v-model:billing="billing" :plans="plans" yearly-discount-label="Yearly saves money" />
<p class="mt-4 text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground">Showing {{ billing }} prices</p>
```

Example: Billing toggle with localised labels
```vue
<PricingGrid :plans="plans" monthly-label="Monat" yearly-label="Jahr" billing-label="Abrechnungszeitraum" yearly-discount-label="Spart Geld" :columns="3" />
```

Example: Card variant: compact, four columns
```vue
<PricingGrid :columns="4" variant="compact" :plans="plans" />
```

Example: Card variant: outline
```vue
<PricingGrid variant="outline" :plans="plans" />
```

# PricingTable
group: marketing / Pricing
Pricing comparison table: plans as columns (price, badge, CTA), features as rows with check/cross/text cells and an optional billing toggle.

Use when visitors need to compare many features across plans; for a short card-per-plan layout use `PricingGrid`. `plans` define the columns (price, optional `yearlyPrice`, `badge`, `highlighted`), `rows` the features and `{ group }` headings (same shape as `ComparisonTable`). Cell values: `true` check, `false` cross, text/number as-is, `null`/missing dash. A monthly/yearly toggle appears when a plan has a `yearlyPrice` (`v-model:billing`, or uncontrolled with `defaultBilling`). Put CTA buttons in the `cta` slot (under each price; `repeatCta` repeats them in a footer row). The table is a real `<table>`; table-level options (`variant`, `size`, `stickyHeader`, `stickyFirstColumn`) match `ComparisonTable`, which this component wraps.

import { PricingTable } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- plans: PricingTablePlan[] = [] - Columns: `{ id?, name, price?, period?, yearlyPrice?, yearlyPeriod?, yearlyNote?, description?, highlighted?, badge? }`. Malformed entries are skipped.
- rows: ComparisonRow[] = [] - Feature rows `{ label, description?, values[] }` (one value per plan) and `{ group }` headings.
- billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' - `v-model:billing`. Leave undefined for uncontrolled use. Unknown values mean `monthly`.
- defaultBilling: 'monthly' | 'yearly' = 'monthly' - Initial period when uncontrolled.
- showToggle: boolean - Force the toggle on or off. Default (unset): visible when at least one plan has a `yearlyPrice`.
- yearlyDiscountLabel: string - Badge next to the yearly option. State a fact you can back up.
- monthlyLabel: string = 'Monthly' - Label of the monthly option.
- yearlyLabel: string = 'Yearly' - Label of the yearly option.
- billingLabel: string = 'Billing period' - Accessible name of the toggle group.
- variant: 'default' | 'striped' | 'bordered' | 'minimal' = 'default' - Table surface style (see ComparisonTable). Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Cell density. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- caption: string - Required (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`). Accessible name of the table and its scroll region. Make it unique when a page has several tables (identical region names fail the landmark-unique rule).
- tableClass: string - Extra classes merged onto the table scroll region (e.g. `max-h-96`); `class` goes on the root instead.
- stickyHeader: boolean = false - Pin plan headers while the table scrolls vertically; pair with `tableClass="max-h-96"` so the table has a height to scroll within.
- stickyFirstColumn: boolean = true - Pin the feature-name column while scrolling horizontally. On by default; pass `false` to let the whole table scroll.
- cornerLabel: string = 'Features' - Top-left header cell text.
- repeatCta: boolean = false - Also render the `cta` slot in a footer row.
- includedLabel: string = 'Included' - Screen-reader text for a check.
- excludedLabel: string = 'Not included' - Screen-reader text for a cross.
- unavailableLabel: string = 'Not available' - Screen-reader text for an empty cell.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last onto the root (toggle + table).

Slots:
- cta ({ plan: PricingTablePlan, index: number, billing: 'monthly' | 'yearly' }) - Call to action under each plan price.
- corner - Replaces the top-left header cell content.
- cell ({ value, row, column, rowIndex, columnIndex }) - Replaces the default check/cross/text rendering of a cell.
- row-label ({ row: ComparisonFeature }) - Replaces the feature name cell content.

Events:
- update:billing [value: 'monthly' | 'yearly'] - The user picked a different billing period.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the table has no name: set `caption`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (the last two land on the table region, not the wrapper).
- Throws a ContractError when a plan has an empty `name` (the first one is named by index).
- Throws a ContractError when `billing` or `defaultBilling` is not `monthly` or `yearly`.
- Throws a ContractError when `billing` is set, the toggle is visible and nothing listens to `update:billing` (use `v-model:billing`).
- Throws a ContractError when the visible toggle has an empty `billingLabel`, `monthlyLabel` or `yearlyLabel`.

Rules:
- One `values` entry per plan, in plan order.
- Add `yearlyPrice` to paid plans to get the toggle; Free/Custom plans keep their `price`.
- Mark at most one plan `highlighted` with a `badge`.
- Put one Button per plan in `cta`; the default variant only on the highlighted plan.
- Use PricingTable for 5+ features compared across plans; use PricingGrid for a short checklist per plan.

Accessibility:
- Real `<table>` with sr-only caption, `scope="col"` plan headers, `scope="row"` feature headers and `scope="rowgroup"` group headings.
- Checks and crosses are icons with screen-reader text; localise with `includedLabel`, `excludedLabel` and `unavailableLabel`.
- The billing toggle is a `radiogroup` of two `radio` buttons with roving tabindex and Arrow/Home/End keys; the 12px discount badge uses the success / success-foreground pair for 4.5:1 contrast.
- The table sits in a focusable, named scroll region (`tabindex="0"`, name from `caption`: give each table on a page a different caption) and keeps a 36rem minimum width, so it scrolls inside itself at 320px instead of the page scrolling sideways.
- The highlighted plan is marked with `data-highlighted` and an opaque tinted header; add a `badge` so emphasis is not colour-only.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const plans = [{ name: 'Plan A', price: 'Free' }, { name: 'Plan B', price: '$XX', highlighted: true }]
const rows = [{ label: 'Projects', values: ['1', '10'] }, { label: 'SSO', values: [false, true] }]
</script>

<PricingTable caption="Minimal plan comparison" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Realistic: grouped features, CTA and billing toggle
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Plan comparison with billing toggle" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" yearly-discount-label="Yearly saves money">
  <template #cta="{ plan }"><Button :variant="plan.highlighted ? 'default' : 'outline'" size="sm">Choose {{ plan.name }}</Button></template>
</PricingTable>
```

Example: Billing toggle with v-model:billing
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const billing = ref('yearly')
</script>

<PricingTable caption="Plan comparison bound to billing" v-model:billing="billing" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
<p class="mt-3 text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground">Showing {{ billing }} prices</p>
```

Example: Without a toggle (single price per plan)
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Plan comparison without a toggle" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Footer CTA row (repeatCta)
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Plan comparison with footer actions" repeat-cta :plans="plans" :rows="rows">
  <template #cta="{ plan }"><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Choose {{ plan.name }}</Button></template>
</PricingTable>
```

Example: Table variant: striped, size sm
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Striped small plan comparison" variant="striped" size="sm" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Table variant: bordered
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Bordered plan comparison" variant="bordered" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Sticky header
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Plan comparison with sticky header" sticky-header table-class="max-h-64" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
```

Example: Sticky first column (default)
```vue
<PricingTable caption="Plan comparison with sticky first column" class="max-w-md" :plans="plans" :rows="rows" />
```

# RateCard
group: marketing / Pricing
A dense, metered price list: one row per billable unit with its rate, what is included and what happens beyond it.

Use `RateCard` for developer and infrastructure products that bill by usage, where a grid of plan cards would hide the numbers. Each item has a name, the unit the rate is per, and a rate. A numeric `rate` is formatted with `Price` (small rates such as 0.0004 keep the digits they need); a string rate ("Custom") is shown as written. `included` and `overage` columns appear only when at least one item has them.

`variant="table"` (default) is a semantic table inside a focusable, named scroll region, so at 375px it scrolls sideways instead of overflowing the page. `variant="list"` stacks every rate as a definition row and reflows with no horizontal scroll. `size` sets the density.

Group rows: give items a `group` name and optionally list `groups` to set the order and add a description. Ungrouped items come first without a heading; groups without items are skipped.

Pass a `caption` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`): the list must have a name. Sample rates in these docs are labelled samples, not offers. For plan comparison use `PricingTable` or `ComparisonTable`; for graduated or volume tiers use `TieredPricing`.

import { RateCard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items*: RateCardItem[] - Rates: `{ id?, name, description?, unit, rate, included?, overage?, badge?, group? }`. `rate` is a number (formatted as a price) or text. Items without a name or a rate are skipped.
- currency: string = 'USD' - ISO 4217 code. An invalid code renders plain numbers.
- locale: string = ConfigProvider locale, else 'en-US' - BCP 47 tag such as `de-DE`.
- caption: string - Accessible name of the table or list. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- variant: 'table' | 'list' = 'table' - `table` is a semantic table in a scroll region; `list` stacks the rates. Unknown values fall back to `table`. Exposed as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size and row padding. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- groups: { group: string; description?: string }[] - Heading rows and their order. Items join a group through `item.group`; other group names follow in order of first appearance.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when none of `caption`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names the rate list.

Rules:
- Always pass `caption`; the list needs a name.
- Pass numeric rates as numbers in major units (0.0004), not formatted strings; use a string only for text such as "Custom".
- Put the unit in `unit` ("per 1,000 requests"), not in the name.
- Use `variant="list"` where a wide table would scroll in a narrow column.
- Use `group` on items for heading rows; do not render several RateCards to fake groups.
- Only invented, labelled sample rates in examples ("Sample requests"); never real prices or real company names.

Accessibility:
- The table variant is a real `<table>` with a `<caption>`, column headers (`scope="col"`), row headers (`scope="row"`) and group headers (`scope="rowgroup"`), wrapped in a `role="region"` scroll area that is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) and named, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys.
- At 375px the table scrolls inside its region and the page never scrolls sideways. The list variant has no horizontal scroll at 320px.
- The list variant is a `role="group"` of definition lists; each group heading names its list. The included and overage text carries hidden "Included" and "Beyond included" labels for screen readers.
- Badges are text, never colour alone. Rates use `Price` with tabular figures.
- Use a `caption` that names what the rates are for; when several rate lists share a page the names must differ.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<RateCard caption="Sample usage rates" :items="[
  { name: 'Sample requests', unit: 'per 1,000 requests', rate: 0.4, included: 'First 10,000 free' },
  { name: 'Sample storage', unit: 'per GB-month', rate: 0.02, included: 'First 5 GB free' },
  { name: 'Sample egress', unit: 'per GB', rate: 0.1, included: 'First 10 GB free' },
]" />
```

Example: Grouped with overage
```vue
<RateCard
  caption="Kestrel Freight sample rates"
  :groups="[{ group: 'Compute', description: 'Sample rates' }, { group: 'Data' }]"
  :items="[
    { name: 'Sample workers', description: 'Sample unit', unit: 'per 1,000 requests', rate: 0.5, included: 'First 100,000 free', overage: 'Billed at the rate shown', group: 'Compute', badge: 'Sample' },
    { name: 'Sample queues', unit: 'per 1,000 messages', rate: 0.0004, included: 'First 1,000,000 free', overage: 'Billed at the rate shown', group: 'Compute' },
    { name: 'Sample storage', unit: 'per GB-month', rate: 0.02, included: 'First 5 GB free', overage: 'Billed at the rate shown', group: 'Data' },
    { name: 'Sample support', unit: 'per month', rate: 'Custom', group: 'Data' },
  ]"
/>
```

Example: Variant: list
```vue
<RateCard variant="list" caption="Sample usage rates (list)" :items="[
  { name: 'Sample requests', unit: 'per 1,000 requests', rate: 0.4, included: 'First 10,000 free' },
  { name: 'Sample storage', unit: 'per GB-month', rate: 0.02, included: 'First 5 GB free' },
  { name: 'Sample egress', unit: 'per GB', rate: 0.1, included: 'First 10 GB free' },
]" />
```

Example: Size
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-6">
  <RateCard size="sm" caption="Sample rates, small" :items="[
  { name: 'Sample requests', unit: 'per 1,000 requests', rate: 0.4, included: 'First 10,000 free' },
  { name: 'Sample storage', unit: 'per GB-month', rate: 0.02, included: 'First 5 GB free' },
  { name: 'Sample egress', unit: 'per GB', rate: 0.1, included: 'First 10 GB free' },
]" />
  <RateCard size="lg" caption="Sample rates, large" :items="[
  { name: 'Sample requests', unit: 'per 1,000 requests', rate: 0.4, included: 'First 10,000 free' },
  { name: 'Sample storage', unit: 'per GB-month', rate: 0.02, included: 'First 5 GB free' },
  { name: 'Sample egress', unit: 'per GB', rate: 0.1, included: 'First 10 GB free' },
]" />
</div>
```

Example: Currency and locale
```vue
<RateCard currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" caption="Sample rates in euro" :items="[{ name: 'Sample requests', unit: 'per 1.000 Anfragen', rate: 0.4 }, { name: 'Sample storage', unit: 'pro GB-Monat', rate: 0.02 }]" />
```

# TieredPricing
group: marketing / Pricing
Graduated or volume price tiers with an optional usage marker and a computed total.

Use `TieredPricing` to explain how a per-unit rate falls as usage grows. Each tier is `{ upTo, rate, flat? }`; `upTo: null` means "and above" and `upTo` is inclusive. Tiers can come in any order and invalid ones are skipped.

`mode="graduated"` (default) prices the units inside each tier at that tier's rate. `mode="volume"` prices every unit at the rate of the tier the total reaches. A visible note states which one applies. A `flat` fee is charged once when the tier applies (graduated: when it holds any units; volume: for the tier reached).

Pass `usage` to mark the tier(s) it reaches with a "Your usage" marker (icon plus text) and to show the computed total in one polite status region, so a changing usage value is announced. Usage above the last tier continues at the last tier's rate; 0 and negative usage cost nothing; a non-finite usage shows nothing. The same arithmetic is exported as `tierTotal(tiers, usage, mode)`.

`variant="table"` (default) is a semantic table in a focusable, named scroll region. `variant="steps"` is a ladder that runs side by side from `sm` and stacks below it. Pass a `caption` (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`). Examples use labelled sample rates, not offers.

import { TieredPricing } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- tiers*: PricingTier[] - `{ upTo: number | null; rate: number; flat?: number }`. `upTo` is inclusive; `null` means and above. Any order; tiers with a non-finite rate or a bad `upTo` are skipped.
- mode: 'graduated' | 'volume' = 'graduated' - `graduated`: each tier prices its own units. `volume`: all units use the rate of the tier reached. Unknown values mean `graduated`. Exposed as `data-mode`.
- usage: number - Units to price. Marks the tier(s) reached and shows the total. Negative counts as 0; NaN and Infinity show nothing.
- unit: string - Plural unit name such as "requests", used in the column header, marker and total.
- currency: string = 'USD' - ISO 4217 code. An invalid code renders plain numbers.
- locale: string = ConfigProvider locale, else 'en-US' - BCP 47 tag such as `de-DE`.
- caption: string - Accessible name of the table or list. Required unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.
- variant: 'table' | 'steps' = 'table' - `table` is a semantic table; `steps` is a ladder that stacks below `sm`. Unknown values fall back to `table`. Exposed as `data-variant`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Text size and spacing. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last with tailwind-merge; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when none of `caption`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names the tiers.

Rules:
- Always pass `caption`; the tiers need a name.
- Set `mode` on purpose: `graduated` prices each tier's own units, `volume` prices all units at the tier reached.
- `upTo` is inclusive and `null` means and above; do not pass a huge number for the last tier.
- Use `tierTotal(tiers, usage, mode)` when you need the number outside the component.
- Pass `usage` to get the marker and total; do not render your own total next to the component.
- Only invented, labelled sample rates in examples; never real prices.

Accessibility:
- The table variant is a real `<table>` with a `<caption>`, column headers and row headers, inside a `role="region"` scroll area that is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) and named, so it scrolls with the keyboard and never overflows the page at 375px.
- The steps variant is an ordered list named by `caption`; below `sm` the steps stack vertically.
- The tier(s) a usage reaches carry a "Your usage" marker with a check icon and text, plus `data-active`; the highlight colour is never the only signal.
- One polite `role="status"` region holds the computed total, so changing `usage` announces the new total once. There are no other live regions.
- The mode note ("Each tier prices only the units that fall inside it.") is visible text above the tiers.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<TieredPricing caption="Sample request tiers" unit="requests" :tiers="[
  { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
  { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
]" />
```

Example: Usage and total
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const usage = ref('12500')
</script>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3">
  <Field label="Sample usage (requests)">
    <Input v-model="usage" type="number" min="0" />
  </Field>
  <TieredPricing caption="Sample request tiers with usage" unit="requests" :usage="Number(usage)" :tiers="[
    { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
    { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
    { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
  ]" />
</div>
```

Example: Mode: volume
```vue
<TieredPricing mode="volume" caption="Sample volume tiers" unit="requests" :usage="12500" :tiers="[
  { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
  { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
]" />
```

Example: Flat fees
```vue
<TieredPricing caption="Sample tiers with flat fees" unit="seats" :usage="30" :tiers="[
  { upTo: 10, rate: 5, flat: 20 },
  { upTo: 50, rate: 4, flat: 20 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 3, flat: 20 },
]" />
```

Example: Variant: steps
```vue
<TieredPricing variant="steps" caption="Sample request tiers (steps)" unit="requests" :usage="5000" :tiers="[
  { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
  { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
]" />
```

Example: Size
```vue
<div class="flex flex-col gap-6">
  <TieredPricing size="sm" caption="Sample tiers, small" :tiers="[
  { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
  { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
]" />
  <TieredPricing size="lg" caption="Sample tiers, large" :tiers="[
  { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
  { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
]" />
</div>
```

Example: Currency and locale
```vue

  { upTo: 1000, rate: 0.5 },
  { upTo: 10000, rate: 0.4 },
  { upTo: null, rate: 0.3 },
]" />
```

# CtaBand
group: marketing / Sections
Call-to-action section in 5 layouts (band, card, split, inline, newsletter) and 3 flat tones.

Use near the end of a landing page, or between sections, to push one action. Pick a `variant` for the layout and a `tone` for the colour. Keep to one clear action and label it with what happens; do not stack several CtaBands. Unknown `variant` falls back to `card`; unknown `tone` falls back to `primary`.

Variants and when to use them:
- `card` (default): rounded centred block inside the page container. The closing CTA.
- `band`: full-width square band with centred copy. Use when the CTA spans edge to edge between full-width sections.
- `split`: copy on one side, `media` or `form` on the other. Use when a real screenshot or a sign-up form supports the pitch.
- `inline`: compact one-liner (headline, optional subtext, buttons at the end). Use mid-page or inside articles and docs.
- `newsletter`: centred copy with an email `form` slot. Use for subscriptions.

Tones: `primary` (brand fill with `primary-foreground`), `muted` (quiet panel) and `inverted` (`foreground` fill with `background` text). All are flat fills; the gradient tone was removed, and text is never faded with opacity so contrast is the tested token pair.

import { CtaBand } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'band' | 'card' | 'split' | 'inline' | 'newsletter' = 'card' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `card`.
- headline: string - Main call to action text. A heading is required: this, the `headline` slot, a heading in another slot or an `aria-label`. A claim or a plain statement of what happens, not a generic invitation.
- subtext: string - Supporting sentence.
- tone: 'primary' | 'muted' | 'inverted' = 'primary' - Flat colour treatment. Unknown values (including the removed `gradient`) fall back to `primary`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Padding and headline scale of every layout; `md` is the original spacing. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - `square` removes the corner radius of the boxed layouts (`band` has none). Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Heading level; invalid falls back to 2.
- as: string | Component = 'section' - Root element.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- headline - Replaces the headline text.
- subtext - Replaces the subtext.
- actions - Buttons row. On `primary` use `variant="secondary"` Buttons, on `inverted` use a default Button with `class="bg-background text-foreground hover:bg-background/90"`, on `muted` the default Button.
- form - `newsletter`: email form under the subtext. `split`: form shown beside the copy. Ignored by other variants.
- media - `split` only: real screenshot beside the copy.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the band has no heading: set `headline` (or the `headline` slot), put a heading in another slot, or set `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- One main CtaBand per page, placed before the footer; `inline` may be used additionally mid-page.
- Choose by content: card = default, band = full-bleed layouts, split = needs a real screenshot or form, inline = small nudge, newsletter = email capture.
- Label the action with what happens ("Open the catalogue"), never a generic invitation.
- On `primary` use a `secondary` Button (a default Button would blend in); on `inverted` use a default Button with `bg-background text-foreground` (an `outline` Button turns grey on the light panel in dark mode).
- There is no gradient tone. Do not fade text with opacity utilities inside the band.
- The `form` slot renders only in `newsletter` and `split`; `media` only in `split`.
- Do not invent customer counts or claims in the headline or subtext.

Accessibility:
- The headline is a heading chosen by `level` (default 2); keep the order valid on the page. Actions are normal focusable buttons or links.
- Give every control in the `form` slot a label or aria-label, and report errors with aria-invalid plus a described message.
- Each tone pairs a fill with its matching foreground token and the subtext is not faded with opacity, so text meets 4.5:1 in light and dark.
- Reflows at 320px: actions wrap, headlines break long words, layouts stack below `sm`/`lg`. Logical properties (`text-start`) keep RTL correct.

Example: Card (default)
```vue
<CtaBand headline="Browse the catalogue before you build" subtext="Every component page has live examples and copyable code.">
  <template #actions><Button variant="secondary" size="lg">Open the catalogue</Button></template>
</CtaBand>
```

Example: Band (full width)
```vue
<CtaBand variant="band" headline="Edge-to-edge between full-width sections" subtext="Use when the surrounding sections also run full width.">
```

# Hero
group: marketing / Sections
Page-top hero with 14 layouts, 4 backgrounds, 3 sizes, media frames, stats, logos, a form slot and bento tiles.

Use once at the top of a landing, docs or product page. Pick a `variant`, a `size` and optionally a `background`; everything else is slots. The default `variant` is `left`: left-aligned text with a headline that says what the product does. The title is an h1 by default; raise `level` to 2 when the page already has an h1. Unknown `variant`, `size` and `background` values fall back to `left`, `md` and none. Entrance fades use `motion-safe:` so they stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

Variants and when to use them:
- `left` (default): left-aligned text, optional media below. Docs, product and editorial pages.
- `centered`: short display line, centred. Use only when the headline is a few words; centred long text is hard to read.
- `split`: text on one side, media on the other. Use when one real screenshot carries the argument.
- `split-reverse`: media first on large screens.
- `minimal`: compact heading. Inner pages and changelogs.
- `stacked-media`: large media below the text in a browser frame. For a real dashboard screenshot.
- `announcement`: a bordered notice above the title. Only for real news with a link; leave it out otherwise.
- `with-stats`: stat row below the text (`stats` prop or slot). Only numbers you can source.
- `with-logos`: logo strip below the text. Only logos you have permission to show.
- `with-form`: `form` slot under the subtitle, for example an email field.
- `terminal`: text beside a window frame with command output (`code` prop or media slot).
- `code`: text beside a window frame with source code.
- `full-bleed`: cover `image` behind a solid text panel, so contrast never depends on the picture. Without an image it falls back to the primary colour with `primary-foreground` text.
- `bento`: text plus a grid of tiles in the `bento` slot. Only when tile sizes reflect importance.

Backgrounds: `none` (default), `grid` and `dots` (aria-hidden SVG patterns, hidden in forced-colors mode) and `image` (cover photo, needs `image`). `gradient`, `glow` and `spotlight` were removed and now render nothing. `decoration` is the old name of `background` and still works.

Actions: put one primary action in `actions`, labelled with what happens ("Open the catalogue"), not a generic invitation.

import { Hero } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'left' | 'centered' | 'split' | 'split-reverse' | 'minimal' | 'stacked-media' | 'announcement' | 'with-stats' | 'with-logos' | 'with-form' | 'terminal' | 'code' | 'full-bleed' | 'bento' = 'left' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `left`. Slots and props specific to a variant are ignored by the others.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Vertical padding and type scale. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- background: 'none' | 'grid' | 'dots' | 'image' = 'none' - Built-in aria-hidden background. `image` renders `image` behind a scrim and puts the text on a solid panel. `gradient`, `glow` and `spotlight` were removed and render nothing.
- decoration: 'none' | 'grid' | 'dots' | 'image' - Deprecated alias of `background`; `background` wins when both are set.
- image: string - Cover image URL for `background="image"` and `variant="full-bleed"`. Decorative (empty alt).
- eyebrow: string - Plain label above the title. Use only when it adds information the title lacks.
- title: string - Main heading text. A heading is required: `title`, the `title` slot, a heading in the default slot or an `aria-label`.
- subtitle: string - Supporting paragraph.
- reverse: boolean = false - Split, terminal and code: media before text on large screens.
- mediaFrame: 'browser' | 'window' | 'phone' | 'plain' | 'none' - MediaFrame chrome around the media slot. Default: `browser` for stacked-media, `window` for terminal/code, else `none`.
- mediaTitle: string - Chrome bar text of the media frame (URL or file name). Also names the code block.
- code: string - Code or terminal text rendered in a focusable, scrollable `pre` when the `media` slot is empty.
- codeLabel: string - Accessible name of the code block. Defaults to `<mediaTitle> code`, then `Code sample`.
- announcement: string - `announcement` variant: notice text. Use only for real news.
- announcementHref: string - `announcement` variant: makes the notice a link with an arrow.
- stats: { value: string | number; label: string }[] = [] - `with-stats` variant: stat list. Malformed entries are skipped.
- logosLabel: string - `with-logos` variant: caption above the strip.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 1 - Heading level of the title; invalid falls back to 1.
- as: string | Component = 'section' - Root element.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- eyebrow - Replaces the eyebrow text.
- title - Replaces the title text (inline content).
- subtitle - Replaces the subtitle text.
- actions - Action row. One primary action.
- media - Real screenshot or code block. Below the text in non-split variants, beside it in split/terminal/code. Wrapped in a MediaFrame when `mediaFrame` is not `none`. A scrolling `pre` needs `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and `aria-label`.
- announcement - `announcement` variant: replaces the notice text.
- form - `with-form` variant: form under the subtitle. Give every field a label.
- stats - `with-stats` variant: replaces the built-in stat list.
- logos - `with-logos` variant: logo images or text (images are h-8 by default; give each an alt).
- bento - `bento` variant: tiles placed in a 1/2/3-column grid; use `lg:col-span-*` on tiles.
- decoration - Custom background; replaces the built-in `background` pattern.
- default - Extra content below the actions.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when the hero has no heading: set `title` (or the `title` slot), put a heading in the default slot, or set `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.

Rules:
- One Hero per page; its title is the only h1. Pass `level` 2 when the page already has one.
- Default is the left-aligned variant. Use `centered` only for a short display line.
- Choose the variant by content: split/split-reverse = one real image, stacked-media = real app screenshot, terminal/code = developer tools, with-form = email capture, with-stats/with-logos = only real numbers and logos, announcement = real news with a link, bento = tiles of unequal importance, full-bleed = photo-led page.
- Put one primary Button in `actions`, labelled with what happens. Never a generic invitation, and never two generic buttons.
- Do not invent stats, logos, customers or quotes. Use real facts or mark the gap with TODO(content).
- Use the `background` prop (none, grid, dots, image) instead of custom absolute divs. Gradient, glow and spotlight no longer exist.
- Use `mediaFrame`/`mediaTitle` instead of wrapping the media slot in MediaFrame yourself.
- Variant-specific props and slots (stats, logos, form, bento, announcement) only render in their own variant.
- On full-bleed with an image use default Buttons (text sits on a solid panel); without an image the surface is primary, so use `secondary` Buttons.
- Give images an alt that describes them; the cover `image` is decorative by design.

Accessibility:
- The title is an h1 by default. Set `level` so the heading order stays valid; docs examples use 3.
- Backgrounds, the cover image and the scrim are aria-hidden and pointer-events-none. The grid and dots patterns are hidden in forced-colors mode.
- Full-bleed puts text on a solid `bg-background` panel (or on `bg-primary` with `text-primary-foreground` when there is no image), so contrast is the tested token pair in light and dark, never the picture.
- The `code` prop renders a focusable (`tabindex="0"`), labelled (`role="region"`, `aria-label`) scrollable `pre`. A custom `media` slot with scrolling content must do the same.
- Stats use a description list (dt label, dd value, `tabular-nums`). The announcement is a real link when `announcementHref` is set, with a visible inset focus outline (2px, `outline-solid`; the code panel uses the same shared `insetFocus` helper).
- Entrance fades use `motion-safe:` and stop under prefers-reduced-motion. There is no blinking caret or looping animation. Text wraps (`break-words`) and the layout reflows at 320px; logical properties keep RTL correct.

```vue
</Hero>
```

# MediaFrame
group: marketing / Sections
Browser, window, phone or plain frame around a real screenshot or code block.

Wrap real screenshots of the product, or a code block, in a frame. Do not use it to draw a fake dashboard: the content must be an actual capture or actual code. Variants: `browser` (three dots and an address pill; web screenshots), `window` (dots and a centred file name; terminal and code), `phone` (rounded bezel with a notch; mobile screenshots) and `plain` (bordered panel, no chrome). Hero uses it through its `mediaFrame` prop. Content comes from the default slot or the `src` shortcut. The frame is flat: no shadow unless `elevated` is set. `size` scales the chrome (and the phone width), `shape` squares the corners and `appearance` drops the outline.

import { MediaFrame } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'browser' | 'window' | 'phone' | 'plain' = 'browser' - Chrome style. Unknown values fall back to `browser`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Chrome bar padding, dots and text, phone notch and phone width (14rem, 18rem, 20rem). `plain` has no chrome, so `size` only affects the phone there. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners: `rounded-lg` (`rounded-xl` for the phone bezel) or none. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Reflected as `data-shape`.
- appearance: 'bordered' | 'borderless' = 'bordered' - Outline of the browser, window and plain frames. `borderless` removes it (a border returns in forced-colors mode). The phone keeps its bezel: it is the device. Unknown values fall back to `bordered`. Reflected as `data-appearance`.
- title: string - Chrome bar text: URL (browser) or file name (window). Ignored by phone and plain.
- src: string - Image shortcut used when the default slot is empty. Pair it with a meaningful `alt`.
- alt: string - Alt text for `src`. Required with `src` (and no default slot). Describe what the screenshot shows. An empty string marks the image decorative; only do that when the caption already says it.
- elevated: boolean = false - Neutral `shadow-md` under the frame. Off by default because only floating surfaces cast shadows.
- contentClass: string | object | array - Classes for the content area (padding, background, font).
- blurred: boolean - Privacy blur on the content area (the image or whatever is in the slot); the chrome bar stays sharp. v-model:blurred. Wins over `ConfigProvider blurMedia`, true or false; undefined inherits, then false.
- defaultBlurred: boolean - Starting blur when `blurred` is not bound.
- revealable: boolean = false - When blurred, show a button that unblurs, then a toggle that blurs again. The button is an action whose name says what it does next ("Show image", "Hide image"), with a 24px minimum target (44px on coarse pointers) and does not appear while the media was never blurred.
- revealLabel: string = 'Show image' - Name of the reveal button (translate it).
- hideLabel: string = 'Hide image' - Name of the button that blurs again (translate it).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last on the frame root; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Frame content (image, video, code). Overrides `src`. Wide code needs its own scroll container (see the code example).

Events:
- update:blurred [value: boolean] - The reveal button changed the blur.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `src` is set without an `alt` string (and no default slot content). An empty string marks the image decorative.

Rules:
- Use `blurred` for privacy (screen sharing, demos, sensitive uploads), never as decoration. Add `revealable` when the viewer may look.
- Wrap real screenshots only. Never recreate a dashboard in markup inside a frame.
- Use `size` for chrome density, `shape="square"` and `appearance="borderless"` for flush layouts; never add chrome with custom classes.
- Use `browser` for web screenshots, `window` for terminal and code, `phone` for mobile screens, `plain` for no chrome.
- Always set `alt` on `src` images to describe the capture.
- Never put interactive controls inside the chrome; only the content area is a slot.
- Give wide code a focusable, labelled scroll container.
- In Hero prefer the `mediaFrame` prop instead of wrapping the media slot by hand.

Accessibility:
- Blur is visual only: alt text and names are unchanged and nothing is hidden from assistive technology; the root gets `data-blurred`. The reveal button is a real button whose name changes with the action (`revealLabel` while blurred, `hideLabel` once shown); it has no `aria-pressed`, because a toggle must not also change its label. Blur is a CSS filter on the media only, so it needs no colour and survives forced-colors mode; its transition runs only under `motion-safe:`.
- The frame is a `figure`. Add `aria-label` or a `figcaption` when the capture needs a name; the chrome dots and notch are aria-hidden decoration and the address bar text is plain text.
- Give `src` images a meaningful `alt`. Empty alt is for decoration only.
- Scrollable code inside the frame must be focusable and labelled: `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and `aria-label` on the scrolling element (Hero does this for its `code` prop).
- `size`, `shape` and `appearance` change looks only: the figure, the alt contract and the aria-hidden chrome are the same. A borderless frame keeps a border in forced-colors mode so its edge stays visible.
- Reflows at 320px: the frame is `min-w-0` and the phone variant is capped at `max-w-56`, `max-w-72` or `max-w-80` by `size` (and by its container). Logical properties only, so RTL needs no changes.

Example: Browser around a screenshot
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<MediaFrame variant="browser" title="localhost:5173/dashboard" :src="shot" alt="Dashboard with a sidebar and a table of components" />
```

```vue
  <pre tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Install command" class="overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre">pnpm add @perfect-design/ui</pre>
</MediaFrame>
```

Example: Phone
```vue

```

# SectionHeading
group: marketing / Sections
Optional eyebrow, title, description and actions that introduce a page section, in 3 alignments, 4 sizes and 2 eyebrow styles.

Use at the top of a landing or docs section so headings, spacing and alignment stay consistent. The title should state the section's claim, not label it ("Every part has a keyboard map", not "Features"). `level` controls the heading element for a correct outline; `size` scales the type and the max width. Not for page titles inside a Hero (Hero has its own title). Unknown `align`/`size`/`eyebrowStyle` values fall back to `left` / `md` / `text`.

Options and when to use them:
- `align="left"` (default): section titles above left-aligned content such as feature lists or docs.
- `align="center"`: classic landing sections above centred grids (features, pricing, testimonials).
- `align="right"`: end-aligned block (follows the writing direction); rare.
- `size="sm"` compact subsection or sidebar heading; `md` default; `lg` hero-like section opener; `full` removes the width limit (use with a side-by-side layout).
- `eyebrowStyle="text"` plain accent label in sentence case; `eyebrowStyle="pill"` bordered badge. Use an eyebrow only when it adds information the title lacks; most sections need none.
- `divider` adds a short accent rule between title and description, good on text-heavy pages.
- `actions` slot (or the default slot) adds buttons or links below the description.

import { SectionHeading } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- eyebrow: string - Short label above the title. Plain sentence-case text; leave it out unless it adds information the title lacks.
- title: string - Heading text. Required unless the `title` slot is used.
- description: string - Supporting paragraph.
- align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' = 'left' - Text alignment; center/right also position the block and actions. Unknown falls back to `left`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' = 'md' - Max width (xl / 2xl / 3xl / none) and type scale. Unknown falls back to `md`.
- eyebrowStyle: 'text' | 'pill' = 'text' - Eyebrow look. Unknown falls back to `text`.
- divider: boolean = false - Accent rule between title and description (aria-hidden).
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Heading element level. Invalid values fall back to 2.
- as: string | Component = 'div' - Root element.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- eyebrow - Replaces the eyebrow text.
- title - Replaces the title text (keep it inline content).
- description - Replaces the description text.
- actions - Actions row rendered below the description (buttons, links).
- default - Same row as `actions` (kept for backward compatibility); rendered after it.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `title` is empty and the `title` slot is not used.

Rules:
- Use one SectionHeading per section; set `level` to match the page outline (usually 2).
- Put buttons in the `actions` slot, not in the description.
- Use `align="center"` for centred layouts instead of wrapping in text-center.
- Skip the eyebrow unless it adds information the title lacks. Use `eyebrowStyle="pill"` for status markers, `text` for category labels.
- Write the title as a claim about the section, not a generic label such as "Features".
- Use `size="lg"` for the first section after a Hero and `sm` for nested subsections.

Accessibility:
- Renders a real h1-h6 chosen by `level` (default h2); keep the document outline sequential. Examples on this page use `level` 3 where an h2 would skip a level.
- The divider is aria-hidden decoration. Titles wrap long words and the block reflows at 320px; alignment uses logical values (`text-start`, `text-end`, `ms-auto`) so RTL mirrors correctly.

Example: Minimal (left)
```vue
<SectionHeading title="Every part has a documented keyboard map" description="Each component page lists the keys it responds to and the roles it exposes." />
```

Example: Centered with actions

```vue
  <template #actions>
    <Button>Open the catalogue</Button>
    <Button variant="outline">Read the theming guide</Button>
  </template>
</SectionHeading>
```

Example: Right aligned
```vue

```

Example: Small
```vue

```

Example: Large
```vue

```

Example: Pill eyebrow
```vue

```

Example: Text eyebrow



Example: Full width
```vue

```
