# SiteFooter
group: marketing / Site chrome
Marketing footer in 7 variants (columns, simple, centered, minimal, newsletter, mega, split) with sizes, alignment and default, muted or dark tones.

Use at the bottom of marketing and docs sites. Columns are `{ title, links }` groups rendered as a labelled navigation landmark with one heading and list per column. The bottom row combines legal text and legal links. Put social icon links (see `SocialLinks`) in the `social` slot. Unknown `variant` falls back to `columns`; unknown `tone` to `default`.

Variants and when to use them:
- `columns` (default): brand block left, 2-4 link columns right. Most marketing sites.
- `simple`: one row with brand, a flat list of links and social icons, then the legal row. Small sites with 4-8 links. Flat links come from `links` or, by default, every link in `columns`.
- `centered`: everything stacked and centred. Personal, portfolio and brand-led sites.
- `minimal`: only the legal row (optionally brand and social inline). Apps, checkout and focused landing pages.
- `newsletter`: brand, link columns and an extra newsletter column (`newsletterTitle`, `newsletterDescription`, `newsletter` slot for the form). Content and community sites that grow a mailing list.
- `mega`: large brand block plus four link columns and a spaced legal row. Big sites with many pages.
- `split`: brand block on one half, link columns (up to three per row) on the other, then the legal row. Sites with a longer tagline and a few link groups.

Link only pages that exist; a four-column footer of dead links is a stock look. Compute the copyright year (`new Date().getFullYear()`) instead of hard-coding it.

Tone: `tone="dark"` inverts the footer (`bg-foreground` with `text-background`) and works with every variant. Use it to anchor a light page or to contrast with a light CtaBand above. `tone="muted"` uses the muted surface with the usual text colours: a quieter separation from the page than the border alone.

Size: `size` sets vertical padding (`sm`, `md`, `lg`; `md` is the original) and the text size of links, titles, descriptions and legal text (`lg` is 16px, `sm` and `md` stay at 14px).

Align: `align` (`start`, `center`, `end`) sets text and item alignment in every variant. Unset keeps the variant default (`centered` centres, the others start). On `simple`, centred or end-aligned content stacks instead of spreading across one row.

import { SiteFooter } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'columns' | 'simple' | 'centered' | 'minimal' | 'newsletter' | 'mega' | 'split' = 'columns' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `columns`.
- tone: 'default' | 'dark' | 'muted' = 'default' - Colour treatment: the page surface, the inverted `dark` footer, or the `muted` surface. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-tone`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Vertical padding and text size of links, titles and legal text (`lg` is 16px). Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' - Text and item alignment. Unset keeps the variant default. Unknown values are ignored. Reflected as `data-align`.
- columns: FooterColumn[] = [] - `{ title, links: { label, href, external? }[] }`. Used by columns, newsletter and mega; simple/centered flatten them. Malformed columns are skipped.
- links: FooterLink[] - Flat links for `simple` and `centered`. Defaults to all links of `columns`; an empty array hides the nav.
- legal: string - Copyright or legal text. Compute the year.
- legalLinks: FooterLink[] = [] - Links in the bottom row (Privacy, Terms).
- description: string - Short brand tagline under the brand slot (not shown in `minimal`).
- newsletterTitle: string - `newsletter` variant: heading of the form column.
- newsletterDescription: string - `newsletter` variant: text above the form.
- navLabel: string = 'Footer' - Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Give each footer on a page a distinct name.
- headingLevel: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 - Heading level of the column and newsletter titles; invalid falls back to 2.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- brand - Logo/brand block (top-left; inline in the legal row for `minimal`).
- social - Social links: under the brand (columns, newsletter, mega), beside the links (simple, centered) or in the legal row (minimal).
- newsletter - `newsletter` variant: the subscribe form.
- legal - Replaces the legal text.
- default - Extra content between the main area and the legal row.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a column has an empty `title`, or a link in `columns`, `links` or `legalLinks` has an empty `label` or `href` (the first one is named by location).
- Throws a ContractError when a footer navigation is shown and `navLabel` is empty.

Rules:
- One SiteFooter per page; if several appear (docs, demos) give each a distinct `nav-label`.
- Link only pages that exist, and compute the copyright year.
- Pick by size: minimal (no navigation), simple/centered (under ~8 links), columns (2-4 columns), newsletter (columns + mailing list), mega (4 columns, many pages).
- Keep columns to 2-4 with 3-7 links each.
- Put icon-only social links in the `social` slot with aria-labels (use SocialLinks).
- Use `tone="dark"` or `tone="muted"` instead of overriding colours with class.
- Use `size="sm"` for dense app footers, `size="lg"` for brand-led pages, `align` instead of text classes, and `variant="split"` when the tagline is long.
- Newsletter props and slot render only in the `newsletter` variant; `links` only in `simple`/`centered`.

Accessibility:
- The root is a `footer` (contentinfo) with a labelled `nav` (`navLabel`). Several footers on one page need distinct `navLabel`s, or axe reports landmark-unique. Each column is a heading (level set by `headingLevel`, default 2) plus a native list named by that heading.
- Keyboard: Tab / Shift+Tab through links in DOM order; Enter activates. There are no widgets to operate.
- External links use `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Links are at least 24px tall and 44px on coarse pointers.
- `size`, `align`, the `muted` tone and the `split` variant change looks and layout only: landmark, heading levels, list names and the contract stay the same. `align="end"` uses logical alignment, so it mirrors in right-to-left pages. The muted tone keeps `muted-foreground` for links and legal text (a tested pair on the muted surface).
- Dark tone uses the `background` token at 70% for links and text on the `foreground` fill; that pair keeps at least 4.5:1. Keep legal text at that tone or stronger.
- Columns stack to two on phones and three from `sm`, so it reflows at 320px. Logical properties and no left/right offsets, so RTL needs no changes.

Example: Columns and legal row

```vue
const columns = [{ title: 'Reference', links: [{ label: 'Components', href: '/components' }] }, ...]

  <template #brand><span class="text-lg font-semibold">Perfect Design</span></template>
</SiteFooter>
```

# SiteHeader
group: marketing / Site chrome
Marketing header in 7 variants (default, centered, minimal, transparent, floating, with-announcement, stacked) with sizes, tones, borders, link groups and a mobile menu.

Use at the top of marketing, docs and product sites. Links are plain anchors (`href`) so it works with any router: listen to `navigate` or place RouterLinks in the `links` slot. Below `md` the links collapse behind a menu button; Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button. The active link gets `aria-current="page"` and an underline, so the state is not colour alone. This is not the app shell top bar; use navigation components for in-app chrome. Unknown `variant` values fall back to `default`.

All surfaces are opaque: no backdrop blur, no translucent fills, no shadows. The bar is separated from the page by a border.

Variants and when to use them:
- `default`: logo left, links, actions right, sticky bar. Works everywhere.
- `centered`: logo in the middle, links left, actions right. Brand-led sites with few links.
- `minimal`: slim bar, links always behind the menu button. Landing pages and checkout flows with few distractions.
- `transparent`: overlays the top of the page (fixed, or absolute when `sticky` is false) with no fill, and becomes opaque after scrolling more than 8px or when the menu opens. Only place it over a hero whose surface keeps the link text at 4.5:1 (the default Hero surface does); over a photo use `default` instead.
- `floating`: a bordered `rounded-lg` panel inset from the edges (`w-11/12`, `max-w-5xl`). Product sites that want a detached bar.
- `with-announcement`: default bar plus a primary-colour top bar (`announcement` + optional `announcementHref`, or the `announcement` slot). Only for real news.
- `stacked`: brand and actions on the first row, the navigation on a second row under a rule (links from `md`; below that the menu button opens the usual panel). Sites with many links.

Look dimensions, all independent of the variant:
- `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`): minimum bar height 3rem, 4rem or 5rem (`minimal` and `floating` are one step slimmer), brand text and link text. Targets stay at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers).
- `tone` (`default`, `muted`, `inverted`): page surface, muted surface, or the ink surface with page-coloured text. The `transparent` variant stays transparent over the page until it turns solid, then takes the tone.
- `appearance` (`bordered`, `flat`, `elevated`): the original hairline, no border, or a 2px stronger border. Nothing casts a shadow.

Simple link groups: pass `linkGroups` (`{ title, links }[]`) for sectioned navigation without dropdowns. Groups sit inline on desktop (separated by a rule, labelled for assistive tech) and appear as headed sections in the mobile menu.

Sticky behaviour: while `sticky`, the component keeps the page `scroll-padding-top` equal to the header height (restored on unmount) so a focused element is never scrolled underneath it (WCAG 2.4.11). Link only pages that exist; a generic Features/Pricing/Blog row with dead targets is a stock look.

import { SiteHeader } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- variant: 'default' | 'centered' | 'minimal' | 'transparent' | 'floating' | 'with-announcement' | 'stacked' = 'default' - Look and layout. Unknown values fall back to `default`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Bar minimum height (3rem, 4rem, 5rem; `minimal` and `floating` one step slimmer), brand text and link text. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'inverted' = 'default' - Surface: the page, the muted surface, or the foreground colour with page-coloured text. `transparent` applies it only once solid. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-tone`.
- appearance: 'bordered' | 'flat' | 'elevated' = 'bordered' - Edge: hairline border (default), no border, or a stronger 2px border. No shadow in any value. Unknown values fall back to `bordered`. Reflected as `data-appearance`.
- brand: string - Brand text link, used when the `logo` slot is empty.
- brandHref: string = '/' - Brand link target.
- links: SiteLink[] = [] - `{ label, href, active?, external? }`.
- linkGroups: SiteLinkGroup[] = [] - `{ title, links }` groups shown after `links`; no dropdowns. Malformed or empty groups are skipped.
- activeHref: string - Current path; matching link gets aria-current="page".
- sticky: boolean = true - Stay in view while scrolling. `transparent`: fixed (true) or absolute (false). While true the page `scroll-padding-top` follows the header height.
- announcement: string - `with-announcement`: top bar text.
- announcementHref: string - `with-announcement`: makes the top bar text a link.
- modelValue: boolean - v-model for the mobile menu (uncontrolled when omitted).
- navLabel: string = 'Main' - Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Give each header on a page a distinct name (the mobile list is named `<navLabel> (mobile)`).
- menuLabel: string = 'Menu' - Name of the mobile menu button. Constant while open or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state (localise here).
- openLabel: string - Optional. Name while closed. Setting it or `closeLabel` switches back to a name that changes with state; prefer `menuLabel`.
- closeLabel: string - Optional. Name while open. See `openLabel`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- logo - Brand/logo; replaces `brand` text.
- links - Custom nav items (e.g. RouterLinks). Rendered in both desktop and mobile navs; replaces `links` and `linkGroups`.
- cta - Right-aligned actions (buttons). Shown in the bar from `sm` and inside the mobile panel below `sm`; when there are no links it is always shown in the bar.
- announcement - `with-announcement`: replaces the top bar text.

Events:
- update:modelValue [open: boolean] - Mobile menu opened or closed.
- navigate [link: SiteLink] - A built-in link was clicked.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a link has an empty `label` or `href`, or a link group has an empty `title` (the first one is named by location).
- Throws a ContractError when the navigation is shown and `navLabel` is empty.
- Throws a ContractError when the navigation is shown and the menu button has no name (`menuLabel` emptied; not checked while `openLabel` / `closeLabel` are in use).

Rules:
- Use one SiteHeader per page. If a page shows several (docs, demos), give each a distinct `nav-label`.
- Pick by need: default for most sites, centered for brand-led, minimal for focused flows, transparent over a plain Hero, floating for a detached bar, with-announcement for real news, stacked for many links.
- Use `size` for density, `tone="inverted"` for a dark bar on a light page, `appearance="flat"` only with a tone that differs from the page surface.
- Use `transparent` only directly above full-width hero content with a solid surface; keep `sticky` true in real pages (fixed) and add top padding to the Hero. There is no blur variant.
- Link only pages that exist.
- Pass router paths as `href` and set `active-href` from the current route.
- Put at most one primary Button in `cta`.
- Use the `links` slot with RouterLink when client-side routing is required; use `linkGroups` for sectioned links instead of building dropdowns.
- The announcement props/slot only render in `with-announcement`.

Accessibility:
- The root is a `header` (banner) with a labelled `nav` (`navLabel`). Several headers on one page need distinct `navLabel`s, or axe reports landmark-unique.
- The menu button is a real button with a constant name (`menuLabel`, default "Menu"), `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the panel. Focus stays on the button when the panel opens, so the next Tab enters the panel. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the button.
- Keyboard: Tab / Shift+Tab move through links and actions in DOM order; Enter activates links; there is no arrow-key menu model because this is site navigation, not an application menu.
- The current page uses `aria-current="page"` and an underline (not colour alone, and visible in forced-colors mode). External links use `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Link groups are `role="group"` named by the group title (desktop) with a visible heading (mobile).
- Sticky header: `scroll-padding-top` follows the header height so focus is not obscured (WCAG 2.4.11).
- Targets are at least 24px (44px on coarse pointers). The bar has a minimum, not fixed, height and the desktop nav wraps, so it reflows at 320px and with 200% text. Logical properties (`ms-`, `ps-`, `border-s`) keep RTL correct.
- `size`, `tone`, `appearance` and the `stacked` variant change looks and layout only: landmark, names, keyboard map, `aria-expanded` and Escape behave the same. The inverted tone draws focus as a 2px outline in the page colour (the shared ring colour is too close to the ink surface); the current page stays underlined in every tone. `stacked` keeps DOM order brand, links, actions, so Tab order is unchanged.
- All surfaces are opaque (no blur), so text contrast is the tested token pair. The only scroll listener is passive and toggles a colour; nothing animates beyond a short colour transition that stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

Example: Default
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const links = [{ label: 'Components', href: '/components' }, { label: 'Guides', href: '/guides/getting-started' }, ...]
</script>

<SiteHeader brand="Perfect Design" nav-label="Default header" active-href="/components" :sticky="false" :links="links">
  <template #cta><Button size="sm">Open the catalogue</Button></template>
</SiteHeader>
```

Example: Controlled menu with custom logo

```vue
const links = [{ label: 'Components', href: '/components' }, { label: 'Source notes', href: '/guides/getting-started', external: true }]
</script>

<SiteHeader v-model="open" nav-label="Controlled header" :sticky="false" :links="links">
  <template #logo><span class="text-lg font-semibold">Perfect Design <Badge variant="secondary">beta</Badge></span></template>
</SiteHeader>
<p class="mt-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Menu open: {{ open }}</p>
```

```vue
  <template #cta><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Open the catalogue</Button></template>

```

```vue

</script>

  <template #cta><Button size="sm">Open the catalogue</Button></template>
</SiteHeader>
```

# LogoCloud
group: marketing / Social proof
Logos (or names) as a grid, inline row, marquee, split, centered or card strip, in grayscale, muted or colour, with optional bordered tiles.

Use for strips of customers, partners or source projects, only with real, permitted names. Each entry has a `name` (alt text and text fallback), optional `src` image and optional `href`. Broken images fall back to the name. Layouts: `grid` (default), `inline` (centred wrapping row, best for 3-6 logos), `marquee` (continuous scroll using `Marquee`, for 10+ logos; logos are not links there), `with-title` (small caption on the left, logos in a grid on the right from `lg`), `split` (headline-size title on the left third, wrapping logos on the rest, from `lg`), `centered` (headline-size centred title above a centred wrapping row) and `card` (title and grid inside a bordered panel). `tone` picks grayscale-until-hover, always-muted or full colour (only the image is dimmed, text names keep full contrast); `size` sets logo height; `shape` draws each logo in a bordered tile (`rounded`, `square`, `pill`); `gap` sets the spacing between logos.

import { LogoCloud } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- logos: LogoItem[] = [] - `{ name: string, src?: string, href?: string }`. `name` is always required, even with `src` (it is the alt text). `href` is ignored by the `marquee` layout.
- title: string - Caption: above the logos, or beside them in `with-title`. In `marquee` it also labels the scrolling group for assistive tech.
- layout: 'grid' | 'inline' | 'marquee' | 'with-title' | 'split' | 'centered' | 'card' = 'grid' - Arrangement. `split` and `centered` use a headline-size title; `grid`, `inline`, `with-title` (smaller) and `card` use the caption size. `grid`, `with-title` and `card` use `columns`; `split` and `centered` wrap like `inline`. Unknown values fall back to `grid`. Reflected as `data-layout`.
- tone: 'grayscale' | 'color' | 'muted' - `grayscale` dims images until hover/focus; `color` shows them as is; `muted` keeps them dimmed and gives no hover or focus reveal. Only the image is dimmed, never the text. When unset, the `grayscale` prop decides. Invalid values are ignored.
- shape: 'plain' | 'rounded' | 'square' | 'pill' = 'plain' - Logo tile. `plain` is the original borderless logo; `rounded`, `square` and `pill` draw a bordered tile on the card surface. Unknown values fall back to `plain`. Reflected as `data-shape`.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between logos (grid: 1rem/2rem/3rem columns, 1rem/1.5rem/2rem rows; row layouts: 1.5rem/2.5rem/4rem columns). In `marquee` `sm` uses the medium strip gap and `md` and `lg` the large one. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Reflected as `data-gap`.
- grayscale: boolean = true - Backwards-compatible switch for grayscale-until-hover. Only used when `tone` is not set.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Logo height: 2rem, 3rem, 4rem. Invalid values fall back to `md`.
- columns: 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 5 - Columns from `md` up in `grid` and `with-title`; invalid falls back to 5. Always 2 on mobile, 3 on `sm`. Ignored by `inline` and `marquee`.
- duration: number - `marquee` only: seconds for one loop. Unset uses the Marquee default (30); invalid values also fall back to it.
- direction: 'left' | 'right' - `marquee` only: scroll direction (Marquee default `left`).
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `logos` has no non-empty `name`, even if it has a `src`. The message names the first failing index.

Rules:
- Always give `name`, even when `src` is set (alt text).
- Prefer SVG logos in the same visual height. Only list names you may show.
- Use `layout="marquee"` for more than ~10 logos; use `inline` for a short hero strip; use `with-title` when the headline should sit beside the logos.
- Use `layout="split"` or `"centered"` when the title is a real claim, `"card"` to set the strip apart, `shape` only when the logos need a tile, and `tone="muted"` for logos that are not links.
- Use `tone="color"` on brand-coloured sections and `grayscale` on neutral ones; never pass both `tone` and `grayscale`.
- Do not rely on `href` in the marquee layout.

Accessibility:
- grid, inline, with-title, split, centered and card render a native list; images use the name as alt (the text fallback is the name itself); linked logos are focusable with the shared focus ring and reveal colour on focus.
- Contrast: only the image is dimmed in the grayscale tone. The text fallback is never faded (no opacity on text), so names keep the 4.5:1 ratio in light and dark mode.
- marquee: the group is labelled by `title`; the duplicated copy is aria-hidden; logos there are not focusable links. It inherits Marquee's pause button (Tab, Enter/Space) and stops moving under prefers-reduced-motion.
- `shape` tiles have a border, so they stay visible in forced-colors mode; the muted tone dims only the image, and text names keep the muted-foreground on card contrast pair. `card` is a plain bordered container, not a landmark. `split` and `centered` wrap instead of using columns.
- Reflow: two columns at 320px, three from `sm`, then `columns` from `md`; names wrap instead of overflowing.

Example: Minimal (names only)
```vue
<LogoCloud title="Sample logos" :columns="4" :logos="[{ name: 'Kestrel Freight' }, { name: 'Orchard Mill' }, { name: 'Tallow and Finch' }, { name: 'Brightwater Co' }]" />
```

Example: Realistic: links, colour, large
```vue

```

# Testimonial
group: marketing / Social proof
Customer quote with author, role, avatar and optional star rating in six layouts.

Use for customer or user quotes. Semantic `<figure>` + `<blockquote>` + `<figcaption>`. If the avatar image is missing or fails to load, initials from the author name are shown. Pick a `variant` for the context: `card` for walls of love, `quote` for one big pull quote, `inline` inside prose or sidebars, `with-rating` for review-style proof, `avatar-left` for a roomy row layout, `featured` to highlight the best quote in a grid. Several testimonials in a layout: use `TestimonialGrid` or `TestimonialSlider`.

import { Testimonial } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- quote*: string - Required unless the default slot is used. The quote text (curly quotes are added automatically).
- author*: string - Person name. Required unless the `author` slot is used.
- role: string - Job title / company.
- avatar: string - Image URL; falls back to initials when missing or broken.
- avatarAlt: string = '' - Alt text of the avatar (empty = decorative, since the name is adjacent).
- variant: 'card' | 'quote' | 'inline' | 'with-rating' | 'avatar-left' | 'featured' = 'card' - Layout. `avatar-left` needs an avatar (image, author name or avatar slot) and otherwise renders like `card`. Unknown values fall back to `card`.
- rating: number - Star rating from 0 to 5, rounded to the nearest half. Out-of-range values are clamped (7 -> 5, -1 -> 0); NaN, Infinity and non-numbers render no stars. Stars show in any variant; `with-rating` is the card style meant for it.
- as: string | Component = 'figure' - Root element.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Quote text and padding scale. `md` is the original look. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' | 'inverted' = 'default' - Surface colour. `default` keeps the variant's own surface; `muted`, `primary` and `inverted` paint a filled surface and recolour the text, role line, stars and avatar to match. `quote` and `inline` gain a padded rounded box when a tone is set. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Exposed as `data-tone`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - `square` removes the radius of the card and of the avatar. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces the quote text (no curly quotes added).
- avatar - Replaces the avatar.
- author - Replaces name and role.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when there is neither a non-empty `quote` nor default slot content.
- Throws a ContractError when there is neither a non-empty `author` nor an `author` slot.

Rules:
- The avatar blur when a surrounding `ConfigProvider` sets `blurMedia` (privacy, not decoration); there is no prop on this component.
- Pass `quote` without surrounding quotation marks.
- Use real names, roles and ratings only; never fabricate testimonials. Examples use visibly sample text.
- Leave `avatarAlt` empty unless the image conveys extra information.
- Choose `quote` for a single hero quote, `inline` for compact use, `featured` for one highlighted card among cards.
- Pass `rating` as a number 0-5; never as a string.

Accessibility:
- Semantic `<figure>` + `<blockquote>` + `<figcaption>` relate the quote to its author; the initials avatar is aria-hidden and an image avatar is decorative unless you pass `avatarAlt`.
- Stars are one role="img" element with aria-label such as "4.5 out of 5"; individual stars are aria-hidden. Filled stars use the foreground colour (not the warning colour) so they stay clearly visible against the empty ones in light and dark mode; the value is never colour-only.
- No interactive parts, so there is no keyboard map. Text wraps (`text-pretty` / `text-balance`) and the card needs no horizontal space beyond its container, so it reflows at 320px; the quote rule of `inline` uses a logical `border-s-2` for RTL.
- The `featured` variant is a solid primary border on the card surface (visible in forced-colors mode); no shadow or glow is used for emphasis in any variant.

Example: Minimal (initials avatar)
```vue
<Testimonial quote="Sample quote." author="Customer name" role="Role, Company" />
```

Example: Variant card (default), image avatar in a grid
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <Testimonial variant="card" quote="Short sample quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" :avatar="portrait" avatar-alt="Sample portrait placeholder" />
  <Testimonial variant="card" quote="Medium-length sample quote." author="Second customer" role="Role" />
</div>
```

Example: Variant quote (large pull quote)
```vue
<Testimonial variant="quote" quote="Sample pull quote, set large." author="Customer name" role="Role, Company" />
```

Example: Variant inline (compact)
```vue
<Testimonial variant="inline" quote="Sample inline quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
```

Example: Variant with-rating (stars)
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
  <Testimonial variant="with-rating" :rating="4.5" quote="Sample quote with a rating." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial variant="with-rating" :rating="3" quote="Second sample quote with a rating." author="Second customer" role="Role" />
</div>
```

Example: Variant avatar-left
```vue
<Testimonial variant="avatar-left" quote="Sample quote for the avatar-left layout." author="Customer name" role="Role, Company" :avatar="portrait" avatar-alt="Sample portrait placeholder" />
```

Example: Variant featured (highlighted)
```vue
<Testimonial variant="featured" quote="Sample featured quote, the one to highlight." author="Customer name" role="Role, Company" />
```

Example: Sizes
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-3">
  <Testimonial size="sm" quote="Sample small quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial size="md" quote="Sample medium quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial size="lg" quote="Sample large quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
</div>
```

Example: Tones
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
  <Testimonial tone="default" :rating="4" quote="Sample quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial tone="muted" :rating="4" quote="Sample quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial tone="primary" :rating="4" quote="Sample quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial tone="inverted" :rating="4" quote="Sample quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
</div>
```

Example: Shape and tone on a pull quote
```vue

  <Testimonial variant="quote" tone="muted" shape="square" quote="Sample pull quote in a square muted box." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial variant="inline" tone="muted" quote="Sample inline quote in a muted box." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
</div>
```

Example: Realistic: custom slots
```vue

  <template #default>Sample quote with <strong>inline emphasis</strong>.</template>
  <template #avatar><span class="flex size-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-muted text-sm">CN</span></template>
</Testimonial>
```

# TestimonialGrid
group: marketing / Social proof
Wall of testimonials in a grid, masonry or side-by-side columns layout.

Lays out several `Testimonial`s. Pass `items` for the common case or fill the default slot with your own `Testimonial`s. `layout="grid"` gives equal-height rows, `masonry` flows cards by natural height (best when quote lengths differ), `columns` puts 2-4 testimonials side by side on `md`+ and stacks them on mobile. The `variant` is passed to every generated `Testimonial`. For a swipeable single row use `TestimonialSlider`.

import { TestimonialGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: TestimonialItem[] = [] - `{ quote?, author?, role?, avatar?, avatarAlt?, rating? }` per testimonial. Ignored when the default slot is used.
- layout: 'grid' | 'masonry' | 'columns' = 'grid' - Arrangement. Unknown values fall back to `grid`.
- columns: 1 | 2 | 3 = 3 - Max columns on large screens for `grid` and `masonry` (always 1 on mobile, 2 from `sm`). Ignored by `columns`. Invalid values fall back to 3.
- variant: 'card' | 'quote' | 'inline' | 'with-rating' | 'avatar-left' | 'featured' = 'card' - Testimonial variant for generated items. Unknown values fall back to `card`.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Spacing between testimonials: `md` is the original spacing (`gap-6`), `sm` tightens and `lg` loosens it, in every layout. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-gap`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Testimonial `size` for generated items (quote and padding scale). Exposed as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' | 'inverted' = 'default' - Testimonial `tone` for generated items. Exposed as `data-tone`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Testimonial `shape` for generated items. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces `items`; place `Testimonial` components (the grid does not wrap them).

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `items` has no non-empty `quote` or no non-empty `author` (the message names the first failing index).

Rules:
- Use `masonry` when quote lengths vary a lot, `grid` for uniform cards, `columns` for 2-3 headline quotes.
- Use `columns` prop only with `grid`/`masonry`.
- Give every item `author`; omit fabricated ratings.
- Use the default slot to mix a `featured` Testimonial with normal ones.

Accessibility:
- Each generated Testimonial is a `<figure>` with blockquote and figcaption, so every quote stays tied to its author. With `items` the grid is a native `<ul>` of `<li>` (a screen reader announces "list, 4 items"); with the default slot or no items it is a plain `<div>` and adds no ARIA roles (`role` is a Testimonial prop, the job title).
- No interactive parts, so there is no keyboard map. One column at 320px, two from `sm`, `columns` from `lg` (`columns` layout stacks below `md`); cards wrap long text.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<TestimonialGrid :columns="2" :items="[{ quote: 'First sample.', author: 'Customer name' }, { quote: 'Second sample.', author: 'Second customer' }]" />
```

Example: Layout grid (equal-height rows)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialGrid layout="grid" :columns="2" :items="items" />
```

Example: Layout masonry (CSS columns)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialGrid layout="masonry" :columns="2" :items="items" />
```

Example: Layout columns (side by side)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialGrid layout="columns" :items="items.slice(0, 3)" />
```

Example: Variant with-rating
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialGrid variant="with-rating" :columns="2" :items="items.slice(0, 2)" />
```

Example: Variant inline, one column
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialGrid variant="inline" :columns="1" :items="items.slice(0, 3)" />
```

Example: Gap, size, tone and shape
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<div class="grid gap-8">
  <TestimonialGrid :columns="2" gap="sm" size="sm" tone="muted" :items="items.slice(0, 2)" />
  <TestimonialGrid :columns="2" gap="lg" size="lg" shape="square" :items="items.slice(0, 2)" />
</div>
```

Example: Realistic: featured quote plus slot content
```vue

  <Testimonial variant="featured" quote="Sample featured quote." author="Customer name" role="Role" />
  <Testimonial quote="Short sample." author="Second customer" role="Role" />
</TestimonialGrid>
```

# TestimonialSlider
group: marketing / Social proof
Swipeable testimonial carousel built on CSS scroll-snap, no JavaScript carousel engine.

A horizontally scrolling, snap-aligned row of testimonials with optional previous/next buttons. Touch swiping, trackpad scrolling and keyboard (focus the track, then Left/Right arrows) all work. There is no autoplay by design. Use `perView` to show 2-3 slides on large screens. For a static wall use `TestimonialGrid`.

import { TestimonialSlider } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: TestimonialItem[] = [] - `{ quote?, author?, role?, avatar?, avatarAlt?, rating? }` per slide. Ignored when the default slot is used.
- variant: 'card' | 'quote' | 'inline' | 'with-rating' | 'avatar-left' | 'featured' = 'card' - Testimonial variant for generated slides. Unknown values fall back to `card`. The resolved value is exposed as `data-variant` on the root, also when the slides come from the slot.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Testimonial `size` for generated slides (quote and padding scale). Exposed as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'muted' | 'primary' | 'inverted' = 'default' - Testimonial `tone` for generated slides. Exposed as `data-tone`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Testimonial `shape` for generated slides. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' = 'end' - Where the previous and next buttons sit under the track. Unknown values fall back to `end`. Exposed as `data-align`.
- perView: 1 | 2 | 3 = 1 - Slides visible at once on large screens (always 1 on mobile, 2 from `md` for 3). Invalid values fall back to 1.
- controls: boolean = true - Show previous/next buttons. At the ends (or when everything fits) they are aria-disabled, not disabled, so a focused button keeps focus.
- label: string = 'Testimonials' - Accessible name of the carousel region. Make it unique when a page has several carousels (identical region names fail the landmark-unique rule).
- slidesLabel: string = 'Slides' - Accessible name of the focusable, scrollable track (a group inside the region).
- slideLabel: string = '{n} of {total}' - Name of each generated slide; `{n}` and `{total}` are replaced (position in the original sequence).
- statusLabel: string = 'Slide {n} of {total}' - Text announced in the polite live region once scrolling settles on a different slide. Silent on load.
- prevLabel: string = 'Previous testimonial' - aria-label of the previous button.
- nextLabel: string = 'Next testimonial' - aria-label of the next button.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Slots:
- default - Replaces `items`. Each child should be a slide, e.g. `<div class="snap-start shrink-0 basis-full">`.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `label` is an empty string (the carousel region needs a name), or, with `controls`, when `prevLabel` or `nextLabel` is empty.
- Throws a ContractError when an entry of `items` has no non-empty `quote` or no non-empty `author` (the message names the first failing index).

Rules:
- Prefer TestimonialGrid when all quotes can be shown at once; use the slider when vertical space is tight.
- Always set a meaningful `label` when the page has more than one carousel.
- In custom slot content every slide needs `snap-start shrink-0` plus a basis class.

Accessibility:
- The wrapper is role="region" with aria-roledescription="carousel" and an accessible name from `label` (give each carousel on a page a different `label`). The track is a focusable `role="group"` named by `slidesLabel`; generated slides are role="group" aria-roledescription="slide" labelled "n of N".
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches the track, then Left/Right arrows scroll one page (visual direction, also in RTL); Tab continues to the Previous and Next buttons (Enter or Space). Arrow keys pressed inside a link or button in a slide are left alone. At the ends the buttons stay focusable (aria-disabled) and do nothing.
- A visually hidden polite status region announces "Slide N of M" after scrolling settles on a different slide (scrollend, or a 150ms debounce); it is silent on load. The buttons are 36px (44px on coarse pointers) with the shared focus ring; chevrons mirror in RTL.
- No autoplay, so there is nothing to pause. Smooth scrolling is replaced by instant scrolling under prefers-reduced-motion. One slide per view at 320px; the track scrolls inside itself, never the page.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<TestimonialSlider label="Minimal testimonial slider" :items="[{ quote: 'First sample.', author: 'Customer name' }, { quote: 'Second sample.', author: 'Second customer' }]" />
```

Example: Realistic: with-rating cards, 2 per view
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialSlider variant="with-rating" :per-view="2" label="Sample reviews" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant quote without controls
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialSlider variant="quote" :controls="false" label="Pull quotes without buttons" :items="items" />
```

Example: Size, tone, shape and centred controls
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const items = [...]
</script>

<TestimonialSlider size="lg" tone="muted" shape="square" align="center" label="Sample large slides" :items="items" />
```

Example: Custom slides
```vue
<TestimonialSlider label="Custom slides example">
  <div class="snap-start shrink-0 basis-full"><Testimonial quote="One." author="Customer name" /></div>
  <div class="snap-start shrink-0 basis-full"><Testimonial quote="Two." author="Second customer" /></div>
</TestimonialSlider>
```

# StatCounter
group: marketing / Stats
Inline number with prefix, suffix, locale formatting and tabular figures. Static: it does not count up.

Use for a figure you can source, next to the claim it supports. It renders the final value immediately, formatted with `Intl` (`locale`, `decimals`) and set in tabular figures so columns of numbers line up. Non-finite values render `fallback` instead of "NaN". The count-up animation and its `animate` and `duration` props were removed (a count-up on statistics is a stock effect and moves text that people are trying to read); both props are still accepted and ignored. Used by `StatGrid`. `size`, `tone` and `align` are optional looks: unset, the figure is an inline span that inherits the surrounding size and colour.

import { StatCounter } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- value*: number - Number to show. NaN/Infinity render `fallback`.
- prefix: string = '' - Text before the number, e.g. "$".
- suffix: string = '' - Text after the number, e.g. "%".
- decimals: number = 0 - Fraction digits, clamped to 0-6.
- locale: string = 'en-US' - Locale for grouping/decimal separators. Invalid locales fall back to plain digits.
- fallback: string = 'n/a' - Shown when `value` is not a finite number.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' - Figure size, semibold: `sm` 24px, `md` 36px, `lg` 60px. Unset inherits the surrounding type size (the original behaviour, and what `StatGrid` relies on). Unknown values are ignored. Reflected as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'primary' | 'muted' | 'success' | 'info' | 'danger' = 'default' - Figure colour. `default` inherits the surrounding colour; the others use the `text-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `text-success`, `text-info` and `text-destructive` tokens. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Reflected as `data-tone`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' - Text alignment. Setting it makes the figure a block (`block text-start|center|end`); unset it stays inline. Logical values, so they mirror in right-to-left pages. Unknown values are ignored. Reflected as `data-align`.
- duration: number - Deprecated no-op. The count-up animation was removed.
- animate: boolean - Deprecated no-op. The number is always static.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when `value` is not a finite number (NaN, Infinity, undefined), unless an explicit `fallback` text is set for the unavailable state.

Rules:
- Pass numbers, never user-supplied strings.
- Use `suffix` and `prefix` for units instead of concatenating outside.
- Only show figures you can source. Do not invent metrics.
- Do not pass `animate` or `duration`; they are ignored.
- Leave `size` unset inside a heading or `StatGrid`; set it for a standalone figure. Use `tone` sparingly and always with a visible label.

Accessibility:
- A plain text node: screen readers read the formatted number once. There is no aria-hidden copy, no live region and no animation to pause or to reduce.
- `tabular-nums` keeps digits the same width so numbers do not shift or misalign.
- `size`, `tone` and `align` change looks only; the text node is the same. A tone is colour only and never the signal (a red number still needs its label); the tone tokens are tested against the page and card surfaces. `align` uses logical values and mirrors in right-to-left pages. The largest size is 60px semibold; it stays inside its container because the figure is text that wraps.
- Give the number a visible label (StatGrid uses a description list); the number alone carries no meaning.

Example: Static value
```vue
<StatCounter :value="170" class="text-4xl font-semibold" />
```

Example: Decimals, prefix and fallback
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-x-8 gap-y-2 text-3xl font-semibold">
  <StatCounter :value="12.5" :decimals="1" suffix="%" />
  <StatCounter :value="49" prefix="$" />
  <StatCounter :value="missing" fallback="not reported" />
</div>
```

Example: Locale formatting
```vue
<StatCounter :value="1234.5" :decimals="2" locale="de-DE" class="text-3xl font-semibold" />
```

Example: Size gallery: sm, md, lg
```vue
<div class="flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-8">
  <StatCounter :value="1200" size="sm" suffix="+" />
  <StatCounter :value="1200" size="md" suffix="+" />
  <StatCounter :value="1200" size="lg" suffix="+" />
</div>
```

Example: Tone gallery: default, primary, muted, success, info, danger
```vue
<dl class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
  <div><dt class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Default tone (sample)</dt><dd><StatCounter :value="42" size="md" tone="default" /></dd></div>
  <div><dt class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Primary tone (sample)</dt><dd><StatCounter :value="42" size="md" tone="primary" /></dd></div>
  <div><dt class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Muted tone (sample)</dt><dd><StatCounter :value="42" size="md" tone="muted" /></dd></div>
  <div><dt class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Success tone, passing checks (sample)</dt><dd><StatCounter :value="42" size="md" tone="success" /></dd></div>
  <div><dt class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Info tone, notices (sample)</dt><dd><StatCounter :value="42" size="md" tone="info" /></dd></div>
  <div><dt class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Danger tone, failing checks (sample)</dt><dd><StatCounter :value="42" size="md" tone="danger" /></dd></div>
</dl>
```

Example: Align gallery: start, center, end
```vue
<div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
  <div class="rounded-lg border p-4"><StatCounter :value="2048" size="md" align="start" /></div>
  <div class="rounded-lg border p-4"><StatCounter :value="2048" size="md" align="center" /></div>
  <div class="rounded-lg border p-4"><StatCounter :value="2048" size="md" align="end" /></div>
</div>
```

# StatGrid
group: marketing / Stats
Headline numbers with labels in five layouts, optional icons and trend indicators. Numbers are static.

Use to show 2-4 numbers you can source, next to the claim they support. A banner of big numbers with no source is a stock look, so only list figures you can reproduce. Numeric values render through `StatCounter` (static, tabular figures); string values (for example "24/7") are shown as-is. Uses a `<dl>` so labels and values are programmatically related. Variants: `plain` (default: bare numbers, no boxes), `cards` (bordered cards), `divided` (one panel with hairline dividers), `inline` (compact single row), `with-icons` (bare icon above each number). Any item can carry a `trend` and `change` for dashboards. The count-up animation was removed; the `animate` prop is accepted and ignored.

import { StatGrid } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- items: StatItem[] = [] - `{ value: number | string, label, prefix?, suffix?, decimals?, description?, icon?, trend?: "up" | "down" | "flat", change?: string }`.
- variant: 'plain' | 'cards' | 'divided' | 'inline' | 'with-icons' = 'plain' - Layout. Unknown values fall back to `plain`.
- columns: 2 | 3 | 4 = 4 - Columns from `sm` up (4 uses 2 on `sm`, 4 on `lg`). Invalid falls back to 4. Ignored by `inline`.
- align: 'left' | 'center' - Text alignment. Default depends on the variant: `left` for `cards` and `with-icons`, otherwise `center`. Invalid values use that default.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Figure size (`text-2xl`, `text-4xl`, `text-5xl`; `inline` uses `text-xl`, `text-2xl`, `text-3xl`). `cards` and `divided` scale their padding too. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-size`.
- tone: 'default' | 'primary' = 'default' - Figure colour: foreground, or the accent. Unknown values fall back to `default`. Exposed as `data-tone`.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Spacing between stats. `md` keeps each variant's own spacing. `divided` draws its cell borders with a 1px gap and ignores it. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Exposed as `data-gap`.
- shape: 'rounded' | 'square' = 'rounded' - Corners of `cards` and `divided`. Unknown values fall back to `rounded`. Exposed as `data-shape`.
- animate: boolean - Deprecated no-op. The count-up animation was removed; numbers are always static.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when an item has an empty `label`, or a `value` that is not a finite number or a non-empty string (the first one is named by index).

Rules:
- Only list numbers you can source or reproduce. Do not invent metrics.
- Use numbers for formatted values, strings for pre-formatted ones.
- Keep 2-4 items and place them next to the claim they support.
- Do not pass `animate`; the count-up was removed.
- Default `plain` has no boxes. Pick `cards` or `divided` on tinted backgrounds, `inline` for a one-line strip, `with-icons` when each stat has a clear symbol.
- Pass `icon` as an IconDefinition object; it only renders in `with-icons`.
- Use `trend` with `change` text; never encode direction by colour alone (the component already adds sr-only text).

Accessibility:
- Renders dl/dt/dd, so each label is programmatically tied to its value. Numbers are plain text with `tabular-nums`; there is no animation, live region or aria-hidden duplicate.
- Trend arrows and icons are aria-hidden; the trend direction is announced through sr-only text ("Up", "Down", "No change") before the change text, and colour is never the only signal.
- Columns collapse to one on phones (`grid-cols-1`), so it reflows at 320px. Alignment uses `text-start`, so RTL mirrors.

Example: Plain (default)
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const short = [{ value: 170, label: 'Components' }, ...]
</script>

<StatGrid :columns="3" :items="short" />
```

Example: With descriptions
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<StatGrid :columns="3" :items="items" />
```

Example: Variant cards
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const short = [...]
</script>

<StatGrid variant="cards" :columns="3" :items="short" />
```

Example: Variant divided
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<StatGrid variant="divided" :columns="3" :items="short" />
```

Example: Variant inline
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const short = [...]
</script>

<StatGrid variant="inline" :items="short" />
```

Example: Variant with-icons
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const iconItems = [{ value: 170, label: 'Components', icon: faUsers }, ...]
</script>

<StatGrid variant="with-icons" :columns="3" :items="iconItems" />
```

Example: Trend indicators on cards
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

</script>

<StatGrid variant="cards" :columns="3" :items="trendItems" />
```

```vue
  <StatGrid variant="cards" size="sm" :columns="3" :items="short" />
```

# TeamGrid
group: marketing / Team
Responsive 2/3/4-column grid of team member cards with avatar or initials, role, bio and links.

Use on About/Team pages to introduce people. Pass `items` for the common case, or place your own `TeamMemberCard`s (or any element) in the default slot. One column on mobile, two from `sm`, then `columns` from `lg`. `variant` picks the card layout: `card` (bordered surface), `minimal` (no surface), `centered` (stacked and centred), `horizontal` (avatar beside the text). Do not use for a handful of testimonials (use Testimonial) or for people lists with data columns (use a table).

import { TeamGrid, TeamMemberCard } from '@perfect-design/ui'

Props:
- columns: 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 - Columns on large screens; invalid values fall back to 3.
- variant: 'card' | 'minimal' | 'centered' | 'horizontal' = 'card' - Card layout forwarded to every generated card; unknown values fall back to `card`.
- gap: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Space between members: `sm` 16px, `md` 24px (the original), `lg` 40px. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - TeamMemberCard `size` forwarded to every generated card (spacing, avatar and type scale). A member in `items` can carry its own `size`, which wins. Unknown values fall back to `md`. Cards placed in the default slot keep their own props.
- shape: 'circle' | 'rounded' | 'square' = 'circle' - Avatar shape forwarded to every generated card: `circle`, `rounded` (12px radius) or `square` (6px radius). A member's own `shape` wins. Unknown values fall back to `circle`.
- align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - Text alignment forwarded to the generated `card` and `minimal` cards; a member's own `align` wins. `centered` is always centred and `horizontal` always start-aligned. Unknown values fall back to `start`.
- items: TeamGridItem[] = [] - Members: `{ name, role?, bio?, avatar?, avatarAlt?, links?: { label, href, icon?, external? }[], size?, shape?, align? }`. Non-array values and null entries are ignored. `name` is required and every link needs a `label` and an `href`.
- level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of member names; invalid values fall back to 3.
- blurred: boolean - Privacy blur on every generated member photo (and the initials). Names, roles, bios and links stay readable. Wins over `ConfigProvider blurMedia`, true or false. Cards in the default slot keep their own props.
- class: string | object | array - Merged last; wins over internal classes.

Parts:
- TeamMemberCard - A single member card. Used by TeamGrid; use it directly inside the default slot. Do not put `role="listitem"` on it: `role` is the member job title prop.
    - name: string - Display name. Also the avatar label and the source of fallback initials.
    - role: string - Job title or role.
    - bio: string - Short biography (the default slot overrides it).
    - avatar: string - Image URL; a missing or broken image falls back to initials.
    - avatarAlt: string = name - Alt text of the avatar image.
    - links: TeamMemberLink[] = [] - Links; every entry needs a non-empty `href` and `label` (a contract violation otherwise). With `icon` the link is icon-only and `label` becomes its aria-label.
    - variant: 'card' | 'minimal' | 'centered' | 'horizontal' = 'card' - Layout; unknown values fall back to `card`.
    - size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' = 'md' - Spacing, avatar size (card 64, 80 or 112px; minimal and centered 80, 96 or 128px; horizontal 48, 64 or 80px), name and text scale, card padding. Unknown values fall back to `md`.
    - shape: 'circle' | 'rounded' | 'square' = 'circle' - Avatar shape, forwarded to Avatar. The `name` and `avatarAlt` contract is the same in every shape. Unknown values fall back to `circle`.
    - align: 'start' | 'center' = 'start' - `center` centres the avatar, text and links of the `card` and `minimal` layouts. Ignored by `centered` (already centred) and `horizontal`. Unknown values fall back to `start`.
    - level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3 - Heading level of the name.
    - blurred: boolean - Privacy blur on the photo and the initials; text stays readable. Wins over `ConfigProvider blurMedia`, true or false.
    - class: string | object | array - Merged last.

Slots:
- default - TeamGrid: custom cards, replaces `items` rendering. TeamMemberCard: replaces the bio text.
- avatar - TeamMemberCard only: replaces the Avatar.

Enforced requirements (a ContractError is thrown when missing):
- Throws a ContractError when a member has no non-empty `name`, or a link has no non-empty `label` (the accessible name of an icon-only link) or `href`. Applies to `items` (the message names the first failing index) and to `TeamMemberCard`.

Rules:
- Use `blurred` for privacy, not decoration; text stays readable.
- Use `items` unless cards need custom content; pass icons as FontAwesome IconDefinition objects.
- Use real names only with permission; never invent people. Pick `variant="card"` by default, `centered` for leadership with big photos, `minimal` on already-carded pages, `horizontal` with `columns=2` and long bios.
- Keep one `size` and one `shape` per grid. `align="center"` only moves `card` and `minimal`.
- Pick `columns` 3 for 3/6/9 people, 4 for 4/8, 2 for 2/4.
- Every icon-only link needs a `label`; it becomes the accessible name.
- Pair with SectionHeading above it.

Accessibility:
- Blur is visual only: names, roles and the avatar alt text are unchanged; the avatar root gets `data-blurred`.
- With `items` the root is a native `<ul>` and each member an `<li>` (role="listitem" is never put on the card: `role` is the job-title prop). With the default slot, or when empty, the root is a plain `<div>`; wrap your cards in `<li>` inside your own `<ul>` for list semantics.
- Names render as headings (`level`, default 3); keep levels consistent with the surrounding section.
- Icon-only links use `label` as aria-label; the avatar is labelled with `avatarAlt` or the name (initials fallback is exposed as an image with the name). Every link is at least 24px square and 44px on coarse pointers, with the shared focus ring.
- `size`, `shape`, `align` and `gap` change spacing and alignment only. The avatar keeps its label (`avatarAlt` or the name) in every shape, names stay headings, and link targets keep their 24px (44px coarse) minimum at every size.
- Links with `external` open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer". One column at 320px, two from `sm`; long names and bios wrap.

Example: Minimal
```vue
<TeamGrid :items="[{ name: 'Sample person A', role: 'Role title' }, { name: 'Sample person B', role: 'Role title' }]" :columns="2" />
```

```vue
</script>

<TeamGrid variant="card" :columns="3" :items="team" />
```
